# kanok-ui (@purpurabog/ui 1.4.3): the full documentation

> Carbon Design System components for any web app: Lit web components (`<ui-button>`, any framework), React wrappers, unstyled React parts (headless) and React + Tailwind components you copy in with shadcn. Themes white / g10 / g90 / g100, layers, Thai and English. npm package `@purpurabog/ui`; shadcn registry namespace `@kanok-ui`.

Rules for writing code with it: use these components instead of raw HTML controls; colour and space with the `--ui-*` tokens (never hard-coded colours); restyle with `::part()` and tokens, not the shadow DOM; nest `<ui-layer>` (or React `Layer`) for surfaces on surfaces. Each page below has an Installation section (npm and shadcn commands) and an API section (attributes, properties, events, slots, parts). The design tokens and rules are in [DESIGN.md](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/DESIGN.md) (also in the package: `node_modules/@purpurabog/ui/DESIGN.md`). Thai versions of every page are under `th/`.

# @purpurabog/ui

Components that follow IBM's Carbon Design System, made for forms in Thai and English: fields, lists, dates (Buddhist era), overlays, data tables and the UI shell. This site is built with them.

The same components come in three forms. Pick the one that fits your app:

| You build with | Use | You get |
|---|---|---|
| Any framework, or plain HTML | Lit web components (`<ui-date-picker>`) | Carbon's look and behaviour, styled with tokens and `::part()` |
| React + Tailwind | Components copied into your app with shadcn (`npx shadcn add`) | Carbon's look as Tailwind classes you can edit line by line |
| React, your own design | [Unstyled parts](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless/) (`@purpurabog/ui/headless`) | Carbon's keyboard, focus and ARIA with no classes at all |

All three share one core, so the behaviour is the same everywhere: every component is tested against Carbon in Chrome and WebKit, with axe and with the keyboard.

## Try it

```html
<ui-date-picker label="Contract start" helper-text="dd/mm/yyyy"></ui-date-picker>
```

Change the theme or the language in the settings at the top right: the components follow the page's `data-theme` and `lang`.

## What next

- [Install the package](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/) or copy components with shadcn.
- Browse every element, its attributes, slots, parts and events in the Storybook.


---

# Installation

The package is public on npm. Pick the way that fits your app; you can mix them.

## Choose a style

The components come in two styles. Both use the same JavaScript: a style is only a stylesheet.

| Style | Load | On the page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Carbon** (the default) | `tokens.css` | nothing to add |
| **Kanok** (our own design) | `tokens.css`, then `kanok.css` | `data-design="kanok"` on `<html>` or on your app's root element |
| **Both**, switchable | the same two files | set or remove `data-design` at run time |

```html
<html data-design="kanok">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/@purpurabog/ui/dist/tokens.css" />
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/@purpurabog/ui/dist/kanok.css" />
```

Kanok uses the Bai Jamjuree font (Thai and Latin, SIL Open Font License). Install it with `npm i @fontsource/bai-jamjuree`, then import the weights 400, 500, 600 and 700 (`import '@fontsource/bai-jamjuree/400.css';` and so on).

To see the whole site in Kanok, open **Settings** (the gear in the header) and choose **Kanok** under Style, or share a link ending in `?design=kanok`. More in [Kanok design](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/kanok/).

## Web components (any framework)

```bash
npm i @purpurabog/ui lit
```

Load the design tokens once per page, then the components you use:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/@purpurabog/ui/dist/tokens.css" />
<script type="module">
  import '@purpurabog/ui';              // every component
  // or only what you use: import '@purpurabog/ui/date-picker';
</script>
```

### React

React wrappers with typed props and events come with the package. They need `@lit/react` too (an optional peer dependency, only for `@purpurabog/ui/react`):

```bash
npm i @purpurabog/ui lit @lit/react
```

Load the tokens once (`import '@purpurabog/ui/tokens.css';`), then import the wrappers you use from `@purpurabog/ui/react`.

## React + Tailwind with shadcn

Copy a component into your app and edit its classes. Its behaviour (keyboard, focus, ARIA) comes from `@purpurabog/ui/headless`, which the CLI installs for you.

1. Your app needs Tailwind v4 and a `components.json`. If you already use shadcn, add only the `registries` part:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://ui.shadcn.com/schema.json",
  "style": "new-york",
  "rsc": false,
  "tsx": true,
  "tailwind": { "config": "", "css": "src/index.css", "baseColor": "neutral", "cssVariables": true, "prefix": "" },
  "aliases": { "components": "@/components", "utils": "@/lib/utils", "ui": "@/components/ui", "lib": "@/lib", "hooks": "@/hooks" },
  "registries": {
    "@kanok-ui": { "url": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@latest/registry/{name}.json" }
  }
}
```

Pin the version in the URL (`@purpurabog/ui@0.82.0` instead of `@latest`) so every copy in your app comes from the same release.

2. Add components:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-select @kanok-ui/tw-button
```

3. Import the tokens and the theme after Tailwind in your main CSS:

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import './components/ui/primitives/tokens.css';
@import './components/ui/react-tw/theme.css';
```

The files land in `components/ui/` (under `src/` when your app has one).

## Unstyled React (headless)

For your own design system: the behaviour without a single class.

```bash
npm i @purpurabog/ui react react-dom
```

State shows as `data-*` attributes (`data-open`, `data-selected`, `data-highlighted` …) to style on. The parts have their own section: start at [Headless](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless/).

## Use your first component

The same dropdown as a web component, with the React wrapper and with React + Tailwind. Every example on this site comes in these tabs: pick yours once and the other pages follow. The headless version is in [Headless](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless/#your-first-component).


HTML:

```html
<html lang="th">
<ui-dropdown label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type">
  <option value="sale">Sale</option>
  <option value="lease">Lease</option>
</ui-dropdown>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiDropdown } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiDropdown label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type">
  <option value="sale">Sale</option>
  <option value="lease">Lease</option>
</UiDropdown>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-dropdown
import { Dropdown } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/dropdown';

const types = [
  { value: 'sale', label: 'Sale' },
  { value: 'lease', label: 'Lease' },
];

<Dropdown label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type" items={types} />
```

`lang` on the element or any ancestor sets the language of the built-in text of the web components and the React wrappers (Thai and English are included).


---

# Migrating to 1.0

1.0 replaces the data-driven web component `<ui-data-table>` with a family of elements that follow Carbon web components (`cds-table`): `<ui-table>`, `<ui-table-head>`, `<ui-table-header-row>`, `<ui-table-header-cell>`, `<ui-table-body>`, `<ui-table-row>`, `<ui-table-cell>` and the toolbar, batch-action and skeleton elements around them. This page lists what to change.

## What changed and why

- **Markup instead of data.** `<ui-data-table>` took `headers` and `rows` as properties and drew the table itself. `<ui-table>` is written as elements, as Carbon's `cds-table` is: each header, row and cell is an element you write or render. What a cell shows is whatever you put in it, so `renderCell` is gone.
- **Carbon web components names.** Attributes, events, slots and parts now follow `cds-table`: `is-sortable`, `is-selectable`, `use-zebra-styles`, `ui-table-header-cell-sort`, `ui-table-row-selected` and so on. Features Carbon doesn't have (paging, column settings, pinned and resized columns, CSV, inline editing, loading and empty states) keep working with the same behaviour and get names in the same style.
- **The toolbar is elements too.** The search, the batch actions, the Columns button and the Export CSV button are `<ui-table-toolbar-search>`, `<ui-table-batch-actions>`, `<ui-table-column-settings>` and `<ui-table-csv-export>` inside a `<ui-table-toolbar>`, instead of switches on the table.
- **New entry point.** Import `@purpurabog/ui/table` instead of `@purpurabog/ui/data-table`.

**Unchanged:** the React + Tailwind `DataTable` (`tw-data-table`, data-driven with `headers` and `rows`, including `DataTableSkeleton`) and the headless `useDataTable` hook and its parts. Code that uses them needs no change.

## Before and after


Before:

```html
<ui-data-table id="contracts" heading="Contracts" sortable selectable searchable csv-export>
  <ui-button slot="batch-actions">Archive</ui-button>
</ui-data-table>

<script type="module">
  import '@purpurabog/ui/data-table';

  const table = document.getElementById('contracts');
  table.headers = [
    { key: 'name', header: 'Contract' },
    { key: 'amount', header: 'Amount (THB)' },
  ];
  table.rows = [
    { id: '1', name: 'Service agreement', amount: 1250000 },
    { id: '2', name: 'NDA', amount: 0 },
  ];
  table.renderCell = (row, header) => (header.key === 'amount' ? row.amount.toLocaleString('th-TH') : row[header.key]);
  table.addEventListener('ui-select', (event) => console.log(event.detail.selected));
</script>
```

After:

```html
<ui-table id="contracts" aria-label="Contracts" is-sortable is-selectable>
  <ui-table-header-title slot="title">Contracts</ui-table-header-title>
  <ui-table-toolbar slot="toolbar">
    <ui-table-batch-actions>
      <ui-button>Archive</ui-button>
    </ui-table-batch-actions>
    <ui-table-toolbar-content>
      <ui-table-toolbar-search></ui-table-toolbar-search>
      <ui-table-csv-export></ui-table-csv-export>
    </ui-table-toolbar-content>
  </ui-table-toolbar>
  <ui-table-head>
    <ui-table-header-row>
      <ui-table-header-cell column="name">Contract</ui-table-header-cell>
      <ui-table-header-cell column="amount">Amount (THB)</ui-table-header-cell>
    </ui-table-header-row>
  </ui-table-head>
  <ui-table-body>
    <ui-table-row data-id="1">
      <ui-table-cell>Service agreement</ui-table-cell>
      <ui-table-cell sort-value="1250000" csv-value="1250000">1,250,000</ui-table-cell>
    </ui-table-row>
    <ui-table-row data-id="2">
      <ui-table-cell>NDA</ui-table-cell>
      <ui-table-cell sort-value="0" csv-value="0">0</ui-table-cell>
    </ui-table-row>
  </ui-table-body>
</ui-table>

<script type="module">
  import '@purpurabog/ui/table';

  const table = document.getElementById('contracts');
  table.addEventListener('ui-table-row-selected', (event) => console.log(event.detail.selectedRows.map((row) => row.dataset.id)));
</script>
```

## Attributes and properties

| `<ui-data-table>` | 1.0 |
|---|---|
| `headers` (`{ key, header }[]`) | `<ui-table-header-cell>`s in a `<ui-table-head>` › `<ui-table-header-row>`; `key` → `column`, `header` → the cell's content |
| `rows` (`{ id, … }[]`) | `<ui-table-row>`s of `<ui-table-cell>`s in a `<ui-table-body>`; keep the id yourself (`data-id`, a React `key`) |
| `renderCell(row, header)` | Write the content into the `<ui-table-cell>` |
| `size` | `size` (unchanged) |
| `zebra` | `use-zebra-styles` |
| `static-width` | `use-static-width` |
| `sortable` | `is-sortable` on the table (every header) or on single headers |
| `sort-key` + `sort-direction` | `sort-direction` on that `<ui-table-header-cell>` |
| `manual-sorting` | `preventDefault()` on `ui-table-header-cell-sort`, then sort the data and set `sort-direction` |
| `sortRow(a, b, context)` | `sort-value` on cells; `customSortRow(lhs, rhs, collator)` on the table compares two cells' values |
| `heading` | `<ui-table-header-title slot="title">` |
| `description` | `<ui-table-header-description slot="description">` |
| `label` | `aria-label` on `<ui-table>` |
| `selectable` | `is-selectable` |
| `radio` | `radio` (unchanged) |
| `selectedIds` | `selected` on `<ui-table-row>`; `selectedRows` (the row elements) on the table |
| `searchable` | `<ui-table-toolbar-search>` in `<ui-table-toolbar-content>` |
| `search-persistent` | `persistent` on `<ui-table-toolbar-search>` |
| `search-label`, `search-placeholder` | `label`, `placeholder` on `<ui-table-toolbar-search>` |
| `filter-text` | No attribute: set the search's `value` and dispatch an `input` event from it |
| `filterRows(row, text, headers)` (true keeps the row) | `filterRows(rowText, searchString)` on the table — **true now leaves the row out**, as in Carbon |
| `manual-filtering` | `filterRows = () => false`, and listen for `input` on the search |
| `renderExpandedRow(row)` | `expandable` on the table and a `<ui-table-expanded-row>` right after the row |
| `expandedIds` | `expanded` on `<ui-table-row>` |
| `expand-all` | `batch-expansion` (with `expandable`) |
| `sticky-header` | `sticky-header` (unchanged) |
| `resizable` | `resizable` on the table (every header) or on single headers |
| `columnWidths` | `width` on each header; `columnWidths` on the table is now read-only |
| `loading`, `loading-rows` | Unchanged |
| `page-size`, `page`, `page-sizes` | Unchanged |
| `total-selected` | `selected-rows-count` on `<ui-table-batch-actions>` (set it in your `ui-table-row-selected` listener) |
| `total-count` | `total-rows-count` on `<ui-table-batch-actions>` |
| `column-settings` | `<ui-table-column-settings>` in `<ui-table-toolbar-content>` |
| `hiddenColumns` | `column-hidden` on headers, `setColumnHidden(column, hidden)` and `resetColumns()`; `hiddenColumns` on the table is now read-only |
| `csv-export` | `<ui-table-csv-export>` in `<ui-table-toolbar-content>` |
| `csv-file-name` | `file-name` on `<ui-table-csv-export>` |
| Host `data-has-selection` | `selected` on `<ui-table-header-row>` while any row is chosen (`ui-table:has(ui-table-header-row[selected])`) |

Header fields:

| `DataTableHeader` | `<ui-table-header-cell>` |
|---|---|
| `key` | `column` |
| `header` | The cell's content |
| `sortable: false` | Leave `is-sortable` off the table and put it on the headers that sort |
| `align` | No attribute: style the cells, e.g. `style="text-align: end"` on `<ui-table-cell>` |
| `editable`, `options` | `editable`, `options` (a property, or JSON in the attribute) |
| `validate(value, row)` | `validate(value, cell)` (a property) |
| `resizable: false` | Leave `resizable` off the table and put it on the headers that resize |
| `width`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth` | `width`, `min-width`, `max-width` |
| `hideable: false` | `hideable="false"` |
| `hidden: true` | `column-hidden` |
| `pinned` | `pinned` |

Row fields: `id` is yours to keep (`data-id`); `disabled: true` → `disabled` on `<ui-table-row>`.

## Methods

| `<ui-data-table>` | 1.0 |
|---|---|
| `toCsv({ scope })`, `downloadCsv({ scope, fileName })` | Unchanged on `<ui-table>` |
| `focus()` | Unchanged |
| `selectedRows` | `selectedRows` returns the `<ui-table-row>` elements |
| `sortBy(key, direction)` | None: click the header, or sort the data yourself and set `sort-direction` |
| `filteredRows`, `visibleRows`, `shownRows` | None: `table.querySelectorAll('ui-table-row:not([filtered])')`; rows on other pages also have `paged-out` |
| `pageCount` | None: `Math.ceil(rows / pageSize)` |
| `visibleHeaders` | `table.columns.filter((header) => !header.columnHidden)` |

## Events

| `<ui-data-table>` | 1.0 |
|---|---|
| `ui-sort` `{ key, direction }` | `ui-table-header-cell-sort` `{ oldSortDirection, sortDirection }` from the header, cancelable, before the rows move; `ui-table-sorted` `{ sortedHeader }` after |
| `ui-select` `{ selected, rows }` | `ui-table-row-selected` `{ selectedRow, selectedRows }`; `ui-table-row-all-selected` `{ selectedRows }` after select-all or Cancel |
| `ui-filter` `{ value }` | `ui-table-filtered` `{ unfilteredRows }`; `input` on `<ui-table-toolbar-search>` for the text |
| `ui-cell-edit` `{ rowId, key, value, previous, row }`, after the save | `ui-table-cell-edit` `{ row, cell, column, value, previous }` from the cell, cancelable, before the value is written |
| `ui-page-change` | `ui-table-page-change` (same detail) |
| `ui-select-all` `{ totalCount }` | `ui-table-batch-actions-select-all-clicked` from `<ui-table-batch-actions>` |
| `ui-column-resize` `{ key, width, widths }` | `ui-table-column-resize` `{ column, width }` from the header; read `columnWidths` on the table for all |
| `ui-expand` `{ expandedIds, expanded, id }` | `ui-table-row-expando-toggled` `{ expanded }` from the row (cancelable `ui-table-row-expando-beingtoggled` before) |
| `ui-csv-export` `{ csv, rows, fileName }` | `ui-table-csv-export` `{ csv, rows, fileName }` from `<ui-table-csv-export>`, cancelable; `rows` are now the row elements |
| `ui-columns-change` `{ hiddenColumns, key, hidden }` | `ui-table-columns-change` `{ hiddenColumns, column, hidden }` |

## Slots

| `<ui-data-table>` | 1.0 |
|---|---|
| `toolbar` | Your controls go in `<ui-table-toolbar-content>`, inside `<ui-table-toolbar slot="toolbar">` |
| `batch-actions` | The children of `<ui-table-batch-actions>` |
| `empty`, `no-results` | Unchanged |
| — | New: `title`, `description` |

## CSS parts and custom property

| `<ui-data-table>` | 1.0 |
|---|---|
| `base` | None: style `ui-table` |
| `header`, `content`, `table`, `pagination`, `empty` | Unchanged on `ui-table` |
| `title`, `description` | Style `ui-table-header-title`, `ui-table-header-description` |
| `toolbar`, `toolbar-content`, `search` | Style `ui-table-toolbar`, `ui-table-toolbar-content`, `ui-table-toolbar-search` |
| `batch-actions` | Style `ui-table-batch-actions` |
| `batch-summary`, `cancel-button`, `select-all-button` | `ui-table-batch-actions::part(…)`, same names |
| `sort-button`, `resizer` | `ui-table-header-cell::part(sort-button)`, `::part(resizer)` |
| `columns-button`, `columns-panel` | `ui-table-column-settings::part(button)`, `::part(panel)` |
| `export-button` | `ui-table-csv-export::part(button)` |
| `expand-button` | `ui-table-row::part(expand-button)` (`ui-table-header-row` for expand-all) |
| `expanded-row` | `ui-table-expanded-row::part(cell)` |
| `--ui-data-table-max-height` | `--ui-table-max-height` |

React + Tailwind's `DataTable` still reads `--ui-data-table-max-height`.

## Skeleton

`<ui-data-table-skeleton>` (`UiDataTableSkeleton`) becomes `<ui-table-skeleton>` (`UiTableSkeleton`), as Carbon's `cds-table-skeleton`: `headers` is a list of strings instead of `{ header }` objects, `hide-header` becomes `show-header="false"` and `hide-toolbar` becomes `show-toolbar="false"`. `row-count`, `column-count` and `zebra` are unchanged; there is no `size`.

## Screen reader announcements

`<ui-data-table>` said "Sorted by Contract, ascending" after a sort and "3 of 12 rows" when typing paused. `<ui-table>` says only "Loading data" while `loading`, as Carbon's table says nothing; the batch bar's count is still a status. The React + Tailwind `DataTable` keeps both announcements.

## React

`UiDataTable` and `UiDataTableSkeleton` are gone from `@purpurabog/ui/react`. Pick one of:

- **The `UiTable*` wrappers** (`UiTable`, `UiTableHead`, `UiTableHeaderRow`, `UiTableHeaderCell`, `UiTableBody`, `UiTableRow`, `UiTableCell`, `UiTableExpandedRow`, `UiTableHeaderTitle`, `UiTableHeaderDescription`, `UiTableToolbar`, `UiTableToolbarContent`, `UiTableToolbarSearch`, `UiTableBatchActions`, `UiTableColumnSettings`, `UiTableCsvExport`, `UiTableSkeleton`): map your data into them. Events are `onUiTable…` props, such as `onUiTableRowSelected`.
- **The React + Tailwind `DataTable`**: still data-driven with `headers` and `rows`, closest to the old `UiDataTable` props.

The table sorts by moving its rows in the DOM, and saves an edit by writing into the cell. Rows React renders belong to React, so sort and save through your state:

```tsx
<UiTable
  onUiTableCellEdit={(e) => {
    e.preventDefault(); // React writes the value
    const { row, column, value } = e.detail;
    setRows((all) => all.map((r) => (r.id === row.dataset.id ? { ...r, [column]: value } : r)));
  }}
>
  <UiTableHead>
    <UiTableHeaderRow>
      {headers.map((h) => (
        <UiTableHeaderCell
          key={h.key}
          column={h.key}
          editable={h.editable}
          sortDirection={sort.column === h.key ? sort.direction : 'none'}
          onUiTableHeaderCellSort={(e) => {
            e.preventDefault(); // React orders the rows
            setSort({ column: h.key, direction: e.detail.sortDirection });
          }}
        >
          {h.header}
        </UiTableHeaderCell>
      ))}
    </UiTableHeaderRow>
  </UiTableHead>
  <UiTableBody>
    {sortRows(rows, sort).map((row) => (
      <UiTableRow key={row.id} data-id={row.id}>
        {headers.map((h) => <UiTableCell key={h.key}>{row[h.key]}</UiTableCell>)}
      </UiTableRow>
    ))}
  </UiTableBody>
</UiTable>
```

The same goes for Vue, Angular and any framework that renders the rows. See [Data table](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/data-table/) for every feature in HTML and React.

## Types

The `DataTable…` types of the web component (`DataTableHeader`, `DataTableRow`, `DataTableSortDetail` …) are gone from `@purpurabog/ui`; the new ones are `UiTable`, `UiTableRow`, `UiTableHeaderCell` …, `TableSortDirection` and the event details (`TableSortedDetail`, `TableRowSelectedDetail`, `TableCellEditDetail` …). React + Tailwind's own types (`DataTableSort` …) are unchanged.


---

# Themes and layers

Every color comes from Carbon's four themes, generated from `@carbon/themes` into `tokens.css`. You pick a theme with one attribute, `data-theme`, on the whole page or on any part of it. Inside a theme, `<ui-layer>` moves fields and menus one step along Carbon's layering model so they stay visible on the surface below them.

| Theme | Look |
|---|---|
| `white` | Light, white background (the default) |
| `g10` | Light, gray 10 background |
| `g90` | Dark, gray 90 background |
| `g100` | Dark, gray 100 background |

`data-theme` and the tokens work the same for the web components, the React wrappers and React + Tailwind, whose classes read the same tokens. Headless parts have no colors of their own.

## Switch the theme of the page

Put `data-theme` on `<html>`. Without it the page is `white`.

```html
<html data-theme="g100">
```

The dark themes (`g90`, `g100`) also set `color-scheme: dark`, so scrollbars and the browser's own controls turn dark too.

## Make a zone dark

`data-theme` works on any element: everything inside it uses that theme, the rest of the page doesn't. Zones can nest.

A zone only changes the tokens. To paint the zone itself, give it the theme's background and text color:


HTML:

```html
<div data-theme="g100" style="padding: 16px; background: var(--ui-canvas); color: var(--ui-ink)">
  <ui-text-input label="Name (field-01 of g100)"></ui-text-input>
  <ui-layer level="1" with-background style="padding: 16px; margin-top: 16px">
    <ui-text-input label="On the next layer (field-02)"></ui-text-input>
  </ui-layer>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<div data-theme="g100" style={{ padding: 16, background: 'var(--ui-canvas)', color: 'var(--ui-ink)' }}>
  <UiTextInput label="Name (field-01 of g100)" />
  <UiLayer level={1} withBackground style={{ padding: 16, marginTop: 16 }}>
    <UiTextInput label="On the next layer (field-02)" />
  </UiLayer>
</div>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<div data-theme="g100" className="bg-canvas p-4 text-ink">
  <TextInput label="Name (field-01 of g100)" />
  <Layer withBackground className="mt-4 p-4">
    <TextInput label="On the next layer (field-02)" />
  </Layer>
</div>
```

The field inside the layer uses the next layer's color, so it still stands out from the surface it sits on.

## Follow the system setting

`data-theme="auto"` shows `white`, or `g100` when the system asks for dark (`prefers-color-scheme: dark`). It's opt-in: Carbon itself never switches on its own.

```html
<html data-theme="auto">
```

`auto` works on `<html>` or on a zone: an `auto` zone inside another theme still shows `white` or `g100` by the system setting.

## Let people pick light, dark or system

`<ui-theme-switcher>` is an icon content switcher with three choices: light, dark and system. It has no Carbon counterpart. The one under Settings at the top right of this site is this element.


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/theme-switcher';</script>

<ui-theme-switcher></ui-theme-switcher>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiThemeSwitcher } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiThemeSwitcher />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-theme-switcher
import { ThemeSwitcher } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/theme-switcher';

<ThemeSwitcher />
```

To draw your own control in React with no styles, use the `useThemeMode` hook: see [Headless](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless/#build-your-own-theme-switcher).

What it does:

- **Shows the choice on `<html data-theme>`.** Light becomes `light-theme` (`white` by default), dark becomes `dark-theme` (`g100` by default), and system follows the OS, also while it changes.
- **Remembers it** in `localStorage` under `storage-key` (`ui-theme` by default; `storage-key=""` doesn't remember).
- **Starts on** the remembered choice, else `value`, else what `<html data-theme>` already shows, else light.
- **Keeps every switcher in step**: all switchers on the page (Lit and React) and in other tabs follow each other.

| Attribute | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `light`, `dark`, `system` | the remembered choice |
| `light-theme` | `white`, `g10` | `white` |
| `dark-theme` | `g90`, `g100` | `g100` |
| `storage-key` | any key; `""` = don't remember | `ui-theme` |
| `size` | `sm`, `md`, `lg` | `md` |
| `low-contrast` | boolean | off |
| `tooltip-placement` | where the icon tooltips show | `top` |
| `label` | names the group | "Theme", translated |

In React and React + Tailwind the props are camelCase (`lightTheme`, `darkTheme`, `storageKey`, `lowContrast`, `tooltipPlacement`), and the Tailwind switcher takes `aria-label` instead of `label`.

On the web component, its parts are `switcher` (the content switcher) and `item` (each choice).

### Save the choice to a user's profile

Picking a choice fires `ui-theme-change` with `{ mode, theme }` (`onUiThemeChange` on the React wrapper, `onChange` on the React + Tailwind switcher). Store the mode on your server, and set `value` when the profile loads: the switcher shows it and remembers it.


HTML:

```js
const switcher = document.querySelector('ui-theme-switcher');

switcher.addEventListener('ui-theme-change', (event) => {
  const { mode, theme } = event.detail; // e.g. 'dark', 'g100'
  saveProfile({ theme: mode }); // your own function
});

// when the profile arrives
switcher.value = profile.theme;
```

React:

```tsx
// profile comes from your server; saveProfile is your own function
<UiThemeSwitcher value={profile.theme} onUiThemeChange={(e) => saveProfile({ theme: e.detail.mode })} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// with value, the switcher shows what you pass: saveProfile also updates profile.theme
<ThemeSwitcher value={profile.theme} onChange={({ mode }) => saveProfile({ theme: mode })} />
```

### Paint the remembered theme on the first frame

The switcher only runs once its script has loaded, so on a reload the page would first paint the default theme and then switch. `themeScript()` returns a small script for `<head>` that sets the remembered theme before anything is painted. Render it on the server, or write it into `index.html` in a build step:

```js
import { themeScript } from '@purpurabog/ui/core';

const head = `<script>${themeScript({ storageKey: 'ui-theme', lightTheme: 'white', darkTheme: 'g100' })}</script>`;
```

Give it the same `storageKey`, `lightTheme` and `darkTheme` as your switcher, whichever of the four it is. When nothing is remembered it does nothing, so your own `<html data-theme>` stays the default. On the server `useThemeMode`, and so the React + Tailwind switcher, returns `defaultValue` (or `light`), so add `themeScript()` to `<head>` there too.

## Put fields on a tile: `<ui-layer>`

Carbon colors surfaces in layers: a field on a gray tile must not be the same gray as the tile. `<ui-layer>` is Carbon's Layer. Inside it, components use the theme's next layer set:

- field, tile and menu backgrounds, and selected rows
- borders and dividers
- hover and active fills

| `level` | Uses |
|---|---|
| `0` | The page's own set, as outside any layer |
| `1` | The second set |
| `2` | The third set (the deepest) |

Without `level`, a layer works it out like Carbon's `cds-layer`: a layer outside any other is level `0`, and a nested one is its parent's level + 1, up to `2`. Set `level` to choose one yourself. `with-background` paints the layer with Carbon's layer background, the color its content sits on.


HTML:

```html
<ui-layer level="1" with-background>
  <ui-text-input label="Field on a tile"></ui-text-input>
  <ui-layer with-background>
    <ui-text-input label="One level deeper"></ui-text-input>
  </ui-layer>
</ui-layer>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiLayer, UiTextInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiLayer level={1} withBackground>
  <UiTextInput label="Field on a tile" />
  <UiLayer withBackground>
    <UiTextInput label="One level deeper" />
  </UiLayer>
</UiLayer>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Layer } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/layer';
import { TextInput } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/text-input';

<Layer withBackground className="p-4">
  <TextInput label="Field on a tile" />
  <Layer withBackground className="p-4">
    <TextInput label="One level deeper" />
  </Layer>
</Layer>
```

Carbon React's `<Layer>` starts at level 1, not 0. The React + Tailwind `Layer` follows Carbon React, so it needs no `level` here. The React wrapper renders `<ui-layer>` and starts at 0 like the element: write `level="1"` (`level={1}`) for the same result.

## Use themes inside a shadow root (micro apps)

This section is for the web components in a Lit app; for a React + Tailwind app in a shadow root, see [Frameworks](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/frameworks/#run-inside-a-shadow-root-micro-app).

Tokens are CSS custom properties, which inherit through shadow roots: a theme on `<html>` reaches every component, wherever it is.

The `[data-theme]` rules, though, live in `tokens.css` at document level. If your app renders inside a shadow root of its own and puts `data-theme` on an element in there, load `tokens.css` into that shadow root too. The file also names `:host`, so `data-theme` on your app's host element works like it does on `<html>`:

```ts
import { LitElement, html, unsafeCSS } from 'lit';
import tokens from '@purpurabog/ui/tokens.css?inline'; // Vite: the CSS as text
import '@purpurabog/ui/text-input';

class ContractsApp extends LitElement {
  static styles = unsafeCSS(tokens);

  render() {
    return html`<ui-text-input label="Contract name"></ui-text-input>`;
  }
}
customElements.define('contracts-app', ContractsApp);
```

```html
<contracts-app data-theme="g90"></contracts-app>
```

The theme switcher only changes `<html>`. In a micro app, set `data-theme` on your own host instead. `<ui-layer>` needs nothing extra: its rules are part of the element, so it works in any shadow root.

## What next

- [Customize the look](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/customizing/): tokens, `::part()`, states and slots.

# Kanok design

Kanok (กนก, after the flame-like Thai motif *lai kanok*) is the library's own style, next to Carbon. It is meant for internal business tools: clean and calm, surfaces set apart by their fill rather than lines, with a Thai-craft identity in its colours and one recurring detail. Every component keeps the same HTML, JavaScript and accessibility; only the stylesheet changes.

## What it looks like

- **Colour.** Khram indigo for actions (`#3341a8`, dark: `#5563db`), chad vermilion for danger, cool near-neutral greys on white (theme `paper`) and a violet-warm black (theme `lacquer`). Every colour is generated and checked against WCAG 2.2 contrast when the package is built.
- **You are here.** An indigo line marks the selected tab, the current page in the header and a chosen table row (`--ui-border-interactive`: the primary on paper, a lighter indigo on lacquer so it stays visible); in the side nav, a tree and vertical tabs the chosen row is tinted, with no bar.
- **No lines where a fill will do.** Cards and tiles have no border: a soft grey sets them apart from the page, one step off whatever they sit on, in a layer too. Notifications and toasts have no coloured bar; the icon tells the kind.
- **Focus.** One light ring everywhere: solid indigo, 1.5px, with rounded corners, shown for the keyboard only. A click on a button, a checkbox or a toggle shows none; Tab does, 2px outside a control and inside a highlighted row. An input box (a text field, a dropdown, a select) shows its focus either way, on its own border (Carbon: 2px, square, a click too).
- **Shape.** Pill-shaped buttons; 6px corners on fields, outlined on every side; 12px on cards, tiles and dialogs (a card's footer buttons sit 8px in) (a card clips its image to them); 8px on menus, notifications and code snippets. Tags have small 4px corners, so a status never reads as a button.
- **No ink blocks.** Secondary buttons are a soft grey fill with no border. Chosen things are indigo, never black: a selected tag, a chosen tile, the slider, the multi-select count.
- **Density.** Buttons and fields 40px tall by default (`sm` 32px, `lg` 48px, as Carbon's fields), so a button lines up with the field beside it; menu rows 32px, table rows 40px. The large button sizes stay pills: `xl` is 48px and `2xl` 56px, label centred (Carbon's 64 / 80px with the label at the top).
- **Select.** A native select, as in Carbon: it opens the browser's own list, and a phone's own picker. For a list in the menu look, use a dropdown (or set `--ui-select-appearance: base-select` for Chrome 135+'s customizable select).
- **Type.** Bai Jamjuree for Thai and Latin, semibold labels and headings, and taller lines so stacked Thai vowels and tone marks never collide.

## Use it

Load `kanok.css` after `tokens.css` (see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/)), then mark where Kanok applies:

```html
<html data-design="kanok" data-theme="paper">
```

`data-design` works on any element, not only `<html>`. An app that runs inside another product's frame (a portal with its own header and side bar) puts it on its own root element, so the host page is left alone:

```html
<div id="contracts-app" data-design="kanok" data-theme="paper">…</div>
```

### React + Tailwind

The React + Tailwind components read the same settings, so they follow Kanok too. Copy `kanok.css` next to the tokens (`npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/kanok`) and import it after them:

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import './components/ui/primitives/tokens.css';
@import './components/ui/primitives/kanok.css';
@import './components/ui/react-tw/theme.css';
```

Then set `data-design` as above. In a micro app (React in a shadow root) put `data-design` and `data-theme` on the host element.

## Light and dark

Kanok has two themes: `paper` (light) and `lacquer` (dark). `data-theme="auto"` follows the system setting. You don't need to change anything for `<ui-theme-switcher>` or `useThemeMode`: on a Kanok page their light / dark choice becomes paper / lacquer. The core functions are in `@purpurabog/ui/core`:

| Function | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `applyDesign('kanok')` | sets `data-design` on `<html>` and moves the theme to the same mode in Kanok |
| `designScript()` | a `<head>` script that paints the remembered style (or `?design=` from the URL) on the first frame; put it before `themeScript()` |
| `themeIn('kanok', 'g100')` | the theme a design shows for a mode: `lacquer` |

## Adjust it

Kanok is a set of values for public CSS custom properties: colours (`--ui-primary`, `--ui-border-interactive`, …) and shape settings (`--ui-button-radius`, `--ui-field-border`, `--ui-card-radius`, `--ui-menu-item-radius`, …). Override any of them on a zone, as in [Customizing](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/customizing/). Each element's settings are listed in its API reference.

## Status

Kanok is new. These components have their Kanok shape: button, the form fields (text input, text area, number, select, search, dropdown, combobox, multi-select, date and time pickers), checkbox, radio, toggle, tags, tabs, tiles, cards, tables (with a mark on a chosen row), menus, notifications, modals, button sets, code snippets, contained tabs (as a segmented control), the calendar, the header, the side nav, the content switcher, pagination, the slider, the file uploader, tooltips, popovers, toggletips, overflow menus, side panels and tearsheets. Every other component already takes Kanok's colours, font and sizes, and gets its shape in the next releases. The React + Tailwind components follow Kanok as well.


---

# Customize the look

Start from the shallowest layer and go deeper only when it isn't enough:

1. **Design tokens** (`--ui-*`) for sizes and colors
2. **Theme zones** (`data-theme`, see [Themes and layers](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/themes/))
3. **`::part()`** for one piece of an element
4. **Slots** for markup in labels and help text
5. **A derived class** as the last resort

The shallower layers survive upgrades better, because they don't depend on how an element is built inside. Attributes, properties, events, slots, parts and `--ui-*` tokens listed in [api.md](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@latest/docs/api.md) are not removed or renamed before the next major version. Selectors inside the shadow DOM are not part of that promise.

## Change sizes and colors with tokens

Every component reads CSS custom properties named `--ui-*` from `tokens.css` (loaded once per page). Set them on `:root` to change the whole app, or on any element to change only what's inside it. You don't touch the shadow DOM:


HTML:

```html
<style>
  .compact {
    --ui-field-height-md: 32px;
    --ui-menu-max-rows: 3;
  }
</style>
<div class="compact">
  <ui-text-input label="32px field"></ui-text-input>
  <ui-dropdown label="Menu shows 3 rows" placeholder="Choose">
    <option value="1">One</option>
    <option value="2">Two</option>
    <option value="3">Three</option>
    <option value="4">Four</option>
  </ui-dropdown>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
// .compact is the same CSS rule as in the HTML tab
<div className="compact">
  <UiTextInput label="32px field" />
  <UiDropdown label="Menu shows 3 rows" placeholder="Choose">
    <option value="1">One</option>
    <option value="2">Two</option>
    <option value="3">Three</option>
    <option value="4">Four</option>
  </UiDropdown>
</div>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const numbers = [
  { value: '1', label: 'One' },
  { value: '2', label: 'Two' },
  { value: '3', label: 'Three' },
  { value: '4', label: 'Four' },
];

<div className="[--ui-field-height-md:32px] [--ui-menu-max-rows:3]">
  <TextInput label="32px field" />
  <Dropdown label="Menu shows 3 rows" placeholder="Choose" items={numbers} />
</div>
```

The React + Tailwind classes read the same tokens (see below), so a token set on a wrapper changes them too. Headless parts have no look, so tokens don't apply to them.

The public tokens that components read:

| Token | Changes |
|---|---|
| `--ui-field-height-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` | Field height per `size` (32 / 40 / 48px): text input, select, dropdown, combobox, multi-select, date picker, button |
| `--ui-menu-max-rows` | Rows a dropdown, combobox or multi-select menu shows before it scrolls (5.5) |
| `--ui-calendar-width` | Width of the date picker's calendar (288px) |
| `--ui-sheet-radius` | Top corners of the date picker's bottom sheet on phones (the menu radius) |
| `--ui-available-height`, `--ui-available-width` | Written on an open list or menu while it is open: the room left beside its field. Its max-height takes it, so a long list scrolls inside the screen. Read it in your own popup's CSS; don't set it |
| `--ui-highlight` | Color of the selected days in a range picker |
| `--ui-surface-1`, `--ui-surface-2`, `--ui-hairline`, `--ui-ink-subtle`, `--ui-ghost-hover`, `--ui-ghost-active` | Layer tokens: they point at the current layer's set, and `<ui-layer>` moves them |
| `--ui-primary`, `--ui-ink`, `--ui-canvas`, `--ui-focus`, … | Theme colors, each made from the Carbon token named at the end of its line in `tokens.css` |

Each element's own list is under "Design tokens" in [api.md](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@latest/docs/api.md) and in the CSS custom properties table of its Storybook page.

## Change one piece of an element with `::part()`

`::part(name)` styles a piece an element exposes. Part names are the same words across components: `base`, `label`, `input`, `menu`, `option`, `helper-text`, `error-text`, … The date picker passes on the parts of the fields inside it; in range mode they get `start-` and `end-` in front:


HTML:

```html
<style>
  ui-dropdown.bold::part(input) {
    font-weight: 600;
  }
  ui-date-picker.split::part(end-input) {
    text-align: end;
  }
</style>
<ui-dropdown class="bold" label="Bold" placeholder="Choose">
  <option value="1">One</option>
</ui-dropdown>
<ui-date-picker class="split" range label="Start" end-label="End"></ui-date-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
// the same CSS as in the HTML tab: the wrappers render <ui-dropdown> and <ui-date-picker>
<UiDropdown className="bold" label="Bold" placeholder="Choose">
  <option value="1">One</option>
</UiDropdown>
<UiDatePicker className="split" range label="Start" endLabel="End" />
```

Every element's parts are listed in [api.md](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@latest/docs/api.md). `::part()` is for the web components and the React wrappers, which render them. React + Tailwind and headless have no shadow DOM: give the pieces classes instead (the last two sections).

A few elements have no pieces inside: `ui-toaster`, `ui-fluid-form`, `ui-button-set`, `ui-badge-indicator` and `ui-stack` are the box you see. Style them with plain CSS on the element, e.g. `ui-stack { row-gap: 24px; }` or `ui-badge-indicator { background: var(--ui-info); }`: page CSS wins over their own. `ui-button-set` also has the part `button-set` (as in Carbon), but its layout is on the element.

## Style by state

You can read every state that changes the look from the element itself, and combine it with `::part()`:

- **Properties you or the user change** are reflected as attributes: `open`, `checked`, `selected`, `expanded`, `invalid`, `warn`, `size`, `kind`, …
- **States the element works out itself** are set as `data-*` attributes on the element:

| Attribute | Means | On |
|---|---|---|
| `data-open` | The list or calendar is open | `ui-dropdown`, `ui-combobox`, `ui-multi-select`, `ui-date-picker` |
| `data-show-error`, `data-show-warn` | The error or warning is actually showing (an error replaces a warning) | every form field |
| `data-has-value` | There is text or a selection | `ui-combobox`, `ui-multi-select`, `ui-search` |
| `data-placeholder` | The placeholder is showing | `ui-dropdown`, `ui-select` |
| `data-password-visible` | The password is shown | `ui-text-input type="password"` |
| `data-editing` | In edit mode | `ui-edit-in-place` |
| `data-drag-over` | A file is dragged over the drop zone | `ui-file-uploader` |
| `data-shown` | The spinner or overlay really shows (after `delay`) | `ui-loading` |
| `data-overflowing` | The text is cut off | `ui-truncated-text` |

Each of these is also a custom state, as on native and Web Awesome elements: `ui-dropdown:state(open)` matches exactly when `ui-dropdown[data-open]` does (`:state(show-error)`, `:state(has-value)`, …). Use whichever you prefer; the attribute works in older browsers too. Each element's states are listed in its API reference.

Click into the email field and leave it empty, then open the dropdown:


HTML:

```html
<style>
  ui-text-input[data-show-error]::part(label) {
    color: var(--ui-error-text);
  }
  ui-dropdown[data-open]::part(label) {
    font-weight: 600;
  }
</style>
<ui-text-input label="Email" required></ui-text-input>
<ui-dropdown label="Fruit" placeholder="Choose">
  <option value="1">Apple</option>
</ui-dropdown>
```

React:

```tsx
// the same CSS as in the HTML tab: the states are set on the elements the wrappers render
<UiTextInput label="Email" required />
<UiDropdown label="Fruit" placeholder="Choose">
  <option value="1">Apple</option>
</UiDropdown>
```

Use `[data-show-error]` rather than `[invalid]` to style the error the user actually sees. `invalid` is the value you set: it stays on a disabled field, which shows no error, and it doesn't include errors from the user's own input.

The `data-*` states are set after the first render in the browser, so HTML rendered on a server doesn't have them yet. The headless parts show their state with `data-*` attributes of their own: see [Headless](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless/#style-on-data-attributes).

## Put markup in labels and help text with slots

When text needs a link, bold text or an icon, use a slot instead of the attribute of the same name. The attribute still works as plain-text fallback.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input>
  <span slot="label">Email <em>(required)</em></span>
  <span slot="helper-text">Use your work email. See the <a href="#policy">policy</a>.</span>
</ui-text-input>
<ui-dropdown label="Country" placeholder="Choose">
  <option value="th" data-description="UTC+7">Thailand</option>
  <option value="jp" data-description="UTC+9">Japan</option>
</ui-dropdown>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput>
  <span slot="label">Email <em>(required)</em></span>
  <span slot="helper-text">Use your work email. See the <a href="#policy">policy</a>.</span>
</UiTextInput>
<UiDropdown label="Country" placeholder="Choose">
  <option value="th" data-description="UTC+7">Thailand</option>
  <option value="jp" data-description="UTC+9">Japan</option>
</UiDropdown>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const countries = [
  { value: 'th', label: 'Thailand', description: 'UTC+7' },
  { value: 'jp', label: 'Japan', description: 'UTC+9' },
];

<TextInput
  label={<>Email <em>(required)</em></>}
  helperText={<>Use your work email. See the <a href="#policy">policy</a>.</>}
/>
<Dropdown label="Country" placeholder="Choose" items={countries} />
```

Every field takes the `label`, `helper-text`, `warn-text` and `invalid-text` slots. `data-description` on an `<option>` adds a second line in a dropdown, combobox or multi-select. Other elements have their own, such as `header-actions` on `ui-modal` and `end` on `ui-tabs`; [api.md](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@latest/docs/api.md) lists them all. React + Tailwind has no slots: `label`, `helperText`, `warnText` and `invalidText` take markup, and an item's `description` is its second line.

## Change the shape with a derived class

The last resort, for what tokens, parts and slots can't do, and only for the web components. Extend the element's class and add your styles after its own. You keep all its behavior (forms, keyboard, accessibility):

```ts
import { css } from 'lit';
import { UiButton } from '@purpurabog/ui/button';

export class BrandButton extends UiButton {
    static override readonly styles = [
        ...UiButton.styles,
        css`
            [part='base'] {
                border-radius: var(--ui-radius-pill);
            }
        `,
    ];
}

customElements.define('brand-button', BrandButton);

declare global {
    interface HTMLElementTagNameMap {
        'brand-button': BrandButton;
    }
}
```

Internal selectors are not public API. Select by `[part=…]`, as above: it survives upgrades better than internal class names.

## React + Tailwind: edit the copied classes

With shadcn the component's source is copied into your app, so you change its look where it is written. Each file keeps its classes in plain Tailwind (`cva` variants for kinds and sizes). For example, in `components/ui/react-tw/button.tsx`:

```tsx
// before
'rounded-none border border-solid border-transparent',
// after: pill-shaped buttons everywhere
'rounded-pill border border-solid border-transparent',
```

For one place only, pass `className`. Classes are merged with `tailwind-merge`, so the ones you pass win:

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/button';

<Button className="w-full">Save</Button>
```

The classes (`bg-primary`, `text-ink`, `h-field-md`, `rounded-pill`, …) come from `theme.css`, which maps the `--ui-*` tokens into Tailwind's theme. Tokens and `data-theme` zones therefore work here exactly as for the web components. The behavior (keyboard, focus, ARIA) comes from `@purpurabog/ui/headless` and keeps updating with the package.

## Headless

The headless parts render no classes and read no tokens: you style them on their `data-*` state attributes. See [Headless](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless/#style-on-data-attributes).


---

# Icons

The components don't ship icons; they take yours in a slot or an `icon` prop and size and color them. Use Carbon's icons, the set this design system is drawn with: browse them in the [IBM UI icon library](https://www.ibm.com/design/language/iconography/ui-icons/library/) and install the package for your stack.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button kind="primary">Add
    <svg slot="suffix" viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M17 15 17 8 15 8 15 15 8 15 8 17 15 17 15 24 17 24 17 17 24 17 24 15z"/></svg>
  </ui-button>
  <ui-icon-button label="Edit">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M2 26H30V28H2z"/><path d="M25.4,9c0.8-0.8,0.8-2,0-2.8l-3.6-3.6c-0.8-0.8-2-0.8-2.8,0l-15,15V24h6.4L25.4,9z M20.4,4L24,7.6l-3,3L17.4,7L20.4,4z M6,22v-3.6l10-10l3.6,3.6l-10,10H6z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
  <ui-icon-button label="Delete">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M12 12H14V24H12z"/><path d="M18 12H20V24H18z"/><path d="M4,6V8H6V28a2,2,0,0,0,2,2H24a2,2,0,0,0,2-2V8h2V6ZM8,28V8H24V28Z"/><path d="M12 2H20V4H12z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
  <ui-icon-button label="Notifications" badge-count="3">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M14.4,10.1L13,8.8V6.5c0-2.6-1.9-4.7-4.5-5v-1h-1v1C5,1.8,3,3.9,3,6.5v2.3l-1.4,1.3c-0.1,0.1-0.2,0.2-0.1,0.4V12c0,0.3,0.2,0.5,0.4,0.5h3.6C5.5,13.9,6.6,15,8,15s2.5-1.1,2.5-2.5H14c0.3,0,0.5-0.2,0.5-0.5v-1.5C14.5,10.4,14.4,10.2,14.4,10.1z M8,14c-0.8,0-1.5-0.7-1.5-1.5h3C9.5,13.3,8.8,14,8,14z M13.5,11.5h-11v-0.8l1.3-1.4C3.9,9.3,4,9.1,4,9V6.5c0-2.2,1.8-4,4-4s4,1.8,4,4V9c0,0.1,0.1,0.3,0.1,0.4l1.4,1.3V11.5z"/></svg>

```

React:

```tsx
import { UiButton, UiIconButton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';
import { Add, Edit, Notification, TrashCan } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<UiButton kind="primary">Add<Add slot="suffix" /></UiButton>
<UiIconButton label="Edit"><Edit /></UiIconButton>
<UiIconButton label="Delete"><TrashCan /></UiIconButton>

```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/button';
import { IconButton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/icon-button';

<Button kind="primary" icon={<Add />}>Add</Button>
```

## Install

Carbon publishes the icons as two packages, both under the Apache-2.0 license. Install the one for your stack; `@purpurabog/ui` doesn't depend on either.


React:

```bash
npm install @carbon/icons-react
```

HTML, Lit and other frameworks:

```bash
npm install @carbon/icons @carbon/icon-helpers
```

## Find an icon's name

The library shows each icon's name in lowercase with hyphens, such as `trash-can`. Each package spells it its own way:

| In the library | React (`@carbon/icons-react`) | Others (`@carbon/icons`) |
|---|---|---|
| `add` | `Add` | `@carbon/icons/es/add/16.js` |
| `trash-can` | `TrashCan` | `@carbon/icons/es/trash-can/16.js` |
| `overflow-menu--horizontal` | `OverflowMenuHorizontal` | `@carbon/icons/es/overflow-menu--horizontal/16.js` |
| `chevron--right` | `ChevronRight` | `@carbon/icons/es/chevron--right/16.js` |

`@carbon/icons` has a file for each size: `16.js`, `20.js`, `24.js` and `32.js`. Some icons are drawn differently at 16px, so pick the size the component shows (see [Size and color](#size-and-color)).

## Put an icon in a component

In React, an icon is a component that renders an `<svg>` and passes other props, such as `slot`, to it. Without a bundler or in another framework, turn the icon's data into an `<svg>` with `toString` from `@carbon/icon-helpers`. For a static HTML page, use **Download SVG** in the library and paste the `<svg>`, as the HTML examples on this site do.


Lit:

```js
import { html } from 'lit';
import { unsafeHTML } from 'lit/directives/unsafe-html.js';
import { toString } from '@carbon/icon-helpers';
import Add16 from '@carbon/icons/es/add/16.js';
import TrashCan16 from '@carbon/icons/es/trash-can/16.js';

/** A Carbon icon as markup, with extra attributes such as `slot`. */
const icon = (descriptor, attrs = {}) => unsafeHTML(toString({ ...descriptor, attrs: { ...descriptor.attrs, ...attrs } }));

html`
  <ui-button kind="primary">Add ${icon(Add16, { slot: 'suffix' })}</ui-button>
  <ui-icon-button label="Delete">${icon(TrashCan16)}</ui-icon-button>
`;
```

JavaScript:

```js
import { toString } from '@carbon/icon-helpers';
import Add16 from '@carbon/icons/es/add/16.js';

const button = document.querySelector('ui-button');
button.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', toString({ ...Add16, attrs: { ...Add16.attrs, slot: 'suffix' } }));
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiMenuItem, UiOverflowMenu } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';
import { Copy, Edit } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<UiOverflowMenu label="Document options">
  <UiMenuItem label="Edit"><Edit slot="icon" /></UiMenuItem>
  <UiMenuItem label="Duplicate"><Copy slot="icon" /></UiMenuItem>
</UiOverflowMenu>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { MenuItem, OverflowMenu } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/menu';
import { Copy, Edit } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<OverflowMenu label="Document options">
  <MenuItem label="Edit" icon={<Edit />} />
  <MenuItem label="Duplicate" icon={<Copy />} />
</OverflowMenu>
```

### Where the components take an icon

| Component | Web component / React wrapper | React + Tailwind |
|---|---|---|
| [Button](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/button/) | `prefix` or `suffix` slot | `icon` (after the text) |
| [Icon button](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/button/#icon-only-buttons) | the default slot | children |
| [Menu](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/menu/) item | `icon` slot | `icon` |
| [Overflow menu](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/menu/) trigger | `icon` slot (in place of ⋮) | `icon` |
| [Tabs](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tabs/) | `icon` slot of `ui-tab` | `icon` |
| [Content switcher](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/content-switcher/) | `icon` slot | `icon` |
| [Tag](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tag/) | `icon` slot | `icon` |
| [Link](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/link/) | `icon` slot | `icon` |
| [Tile](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tile/) | `icon` slot of a linked tile | `icon` |
| [Contained list](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/contained-list/) item | `icon` slot | `icon` |
| [Tree view](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tree-view/) node | `icon` slot | `icon` |
| [User avatar](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/user-avatar/) | `icon` slot | `icon` |
| [Toggletip](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/toggletip/) trigger | `trigger` slot (in place of ⓘ) | `icon` |
| [UI shell](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/ui-shell/) | header global action: the default slot; side nav link and menu: `icon` slot | children / `icon` |
| [Page header](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/page-header/) | `icon` slot of the breadcrumb bar and of the content | `icon` |

## Size and color

The component sets the icon's size: 16px in buttons, menus, tags and the side nav, 20px in the header and in large icon-only tabs, 32px before a page header's title. The `width` and `height` an icon comes with don't matter there. Use the icon's own size (`size={20}` in React, `20.js` in `@carbon/icons`) when the component shows it at 20px or more, so you get the drawing made for that size.

Carbon's icons fill with `currentColor`, so they take the component's text color, also on hover, when disabled and in every theme. Don't set a `fill` of your own.

## Accessibility

An icon inside a control is decoration: both packages add `aria-hidden="true"` to an icon without an `aria-label`. The control carries the name, such as the `label` of an icon button, which is also its tooltip. Don't give the icon a label as well, or screen readers read the name twice.

An icon that stands alone and means something (a status, for example) needs its own name: pass `aria-label` (React) or add it to `attrs`; the icon then gets `role="img"`. For status, the [status indicator](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/status-indicator/) already has the right icons and names.

## Names that clash

Some icon names are also component names, such as `Search`, `Notification` or `Copy`. Rename the icon when you import it. The examples on this site use an `Icon` suffix:

```tsx
import { Search as SearchIcon, Notification as NotificationIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';
```


---

# Forms and validation

Every field is a form-associated custom element: it takes part in a plain `<form>` the way `<input>` does. You get submit, `FormData`, reset and the browser's constraint validation without any glue code.

The React wrappers from `@purpurabog/ui/react` render the same elements, so everything on this page applies to them too. The React + Tailwind components copied with shadcn work like Carbon React: validation is your app's, and they show what you pass in `invalid` and `invalidText` (going over `maxCount` is still an error by itself). For the wrappers, events and the rest of the setup, see [Using it with frameworks](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/frameworks/).


HTML:

```html
<form method="dialog">
  <ui-stack gap="6">
    <ui-text-input label="Full name" name="name" required invalid-text="Enter your full name"></ui-text-input>
    <ui-date-picker label="Contract start" name="start" required></ui-date-picker>
    <ui-dropdown label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type" required>
      <option value="sale">Sale</option>
      <option value="lease">Lease</option>
    </ui-dropdown>
    <ui-button-set>
      <ui-button kind="secondary" type="reset">Reset</ui-button>
      <ui-button type="submit">Submit</ui-button>
    </ui-button-set>
  </ui-stack>
</form>
```

React:

```tsx
<form method="dialog">
  <UiStack gap="6">
    <UiTextInput label="Full name" name="name" required invalidText="Enter your full name" />
    <UiDatePicker label="Contract start" name="start" required />
    <UiDropdown label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type" required>
      <option value="sale">Sale</option>
      <option value="lease">Lease</option>
    </UiDropdown>
    <UiButtonSet>
      <UiButton kind="secondary" type="reset">Reset</UiButton>
      <UiButton type="submit">Submit</UiButton>
    </UiButtonSet>
  </UiStack>
</form>
```

Press Submit with the fields empty: each one shows its error and the first gets focus. (`method="dialog"` only keeps this demo on the page; your form posts as usual.)

## Submit with a form

Give each field a `name`. Fields submit under that name, so `FormData` reads them like native inputs:


HTML:

```html
<form id="contract">
  <ui-text-input label="Full name" name="name" required></ui-text-input>
  <ui-date-picker label="Contract start" name="start" required></ui-date-picker>
  <ui-button type="submit">Save</ui-button>
</form>

<script type="module">
  const form = document.querySelector('#contract');
  form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const data = Object.fromEntries(new FormData(form));
    // { name: 'Somchai', start: '2026-10-10' }
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<form
  onSubmit={(event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const data = Object.fromEntries(new FormData(event.currentTarget));
    // { name: 'Somchai', start: '2026-10-10' }
  }}
>
  <UiTextInput label="Full name" name="name" required />
  <UiDatePicker label="Contract start" name="start" required />
  <UiButton type="submit">Save</UiButton>
</form>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// checking the values is your app's: see "Show an error from your validator"
<form
  onSubmit={(event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const data = Object.fromEntries(new FormData(event.currentTarget));
    // { name: 'Somchai', start: '2026-10-10' }
  }}
>
  <TextInput label="Full name" name="name" />
  <DatePicker label="Contract start" name="start" />
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</form>
```

- `<ui-button type="submit">` submits the form it sits in, and `type="reset"` resets it. The default `type` is `button`, which does neither.
- Enter in a text box submits the form as a native text input does: through the form's first submit button, and not at all while that button is disabled. A form without a submit button submits on Enter only when it has a single text field.
- A `<fieldset disabled>` or `<ui-form-group disabled>` disables every field and `<ui-button>` inside it: they are not submitted, don't block the form and can't submit it.
- A field without a `label` of its own is named by an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on it, or by a `<label for>` that points at it, as a native control is.
- `submit` only fires when every field is valid.
- Reset puts each field back to the value it started with and hides its error again.

## Mark a field as required

Add `required`. The form won't submit while the field is empty.

Every field brings its own message, translated to the page language (Thai and English are built in):

| Field | Message when empty |
|---|---|
| `ui-dropdown`, `ui-combobox`, `ui-multi-select` | Built in: "Please select an option." |
| `ui-radio-group` | Built in: "Please select an option." (`required-text` to change it) |
| `ui-checkbox-group` | Built in: "Select at least one option." (`required-text` to change it) |
| `ui-date-picker` | Built in: "Please enter a date.", plus messages for a wrong format, an impossible date and dates outside `min` / `max` |
| `ui-file-uploader` | Built in: "Add at least one file." (`required-text` to change it) |
| `ui-text-input`, `ui-text-area`, `ui-number-input` | Built in: "Fill out this field." |
| `ui-select` | Built in: "Please select an option." |

Other browser checks, such as a wrong email address or a `pattern`, still use the browser's message, in the browser's language. On every field in this table except the file uploader, `invalid-text` replaces the built-in or browser message, whatever made the field invalid. Set it when you want your own words, or one language everywhere:


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input label="Full name" name="name" required invalid-text="Enter your full name"></ui-text-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput label="Full name" name="name" required invalidText="Enter your full name" />
```

## When errors show

Errors wait until the user is done with the field. Nobody sees "required" while they're still typing.

- A field shows its error after the user leaves it.
- Trying to submit shows the error on every invalid field at once and moves focus to the first one. The browser's own bubble doesn't appear. `reportValidity()` (the form's or a field's) does the same.
- `checkValidity()` stays silent, as on native controls: an app that checks the form on every keystroke (to enable its Save button, say) shows no errors and doesn't move the focus.
- Going over a `max-count` limit, and `invalid` set by your code, show right away.
- A disabled or read-only field shows no error.

## Show an error from your validator

Set `invalid` and `invalid-text` for errors only your app or server knows about. The error shows right away. When your form library owns validation, pass its result to `invalid` and `invalidText`:


HTML:

```js
const email = document.querySelector('ui-text-input[name="email"]');

const response = await fetch('/api/contracts', { method: 'POST', body: new FormData(form) });
if (response.status === 409) {
  email.invalidText = 'This email is already registered';
  email.invalid = true;
}

// clear it once the user changes the value
email.addEventListener('input', () => {
  email.invalid = false;
});
```

React:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { UiButton, UiTextInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

export function NameForm() {
  const [error, setError] = useState('');
  return (
    <form
      onSubmit={(event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        const name = String(new FormData(event.currentTarget).get('name') ?? '');
        setError(name.trim().length < 2 ? 'Enter at least 2 characters' : '');
      }}
    >
      <UiTextInput label="Full name" name="name" invalid={error !== ''} invalidText={error} onInput={() => setError('')} />
      <UiButton type="submit">Save</UiButton>
    </form>
  );
}
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { useForm } from 'react-hook-form';
import { TextInput } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/text-input';

type Values = { name: string };

export function NameForm({ onSave }: { onSave: (values: Values) => void }) {
  const { register, handleSubmit, formState: { errors } } = useForm<Values>();
  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit(onSave)}>
      <TextInput label="Full name" {...register('name', { required: 'Enter your full name' })} invalid={!!errors.name} invalidText={errors.name?.message} />
    </form>
  );
}
```

On the web component and its React wrapper, `invalid` also makes the field invalid for the form, so the form won't submit again until you clear it. The React + Tailwind example uses React Hook Form; add `zodResolver` from `@hookform/resolvers` for a Zod schema.

## Check a rule with custom validity

`setCustomValidity()` works like on `<input>`: a message makes the field invalid, and `''` clears it. Unlike `invalid`, the message waits for the user to leave the field, like the built-in checks:

```js
const password = document.querySelector('ui-text-input[name="password"]');
const confirm = document.querySelector('ui-text-input[name="confirm"]');

confirm.addEventListener('input', () => {
  confirm.setCustomValidity(confirm.value === password.value ? '' : 'The passwords don’t match');
});
```

Fields also have `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`, `validity`, `validationMessage`, `willValidate` and `form`, as native controls do. These are methods of the elements: in React, call them on the wrapper's `ref`. In React + Tailwind, such a rule is part of your own validation.

## Add helper text and warnings

- `helper-text` is a hint under the field.
- `warn` with `warn-text` is a warning that doesn't block submit.
- One line shows at a time: an error beats a warning, and a warning beats helper text.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input label="Phone" name="phone" helper-text="We only call about this contract"></ui-text-input>
<ui-number-input label="Deposit" name="deposit" warn warn-text="Higher than usual for this contract type"></ui-number-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput label="Phone" name="phone" helperText="We only call about this contract" />
<UiNumberInput label="Deposit" name="deposit" warn warnText="Higher than usual for this contract type" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput label="Phone" name="phone" helperText="We only call about this contract" />
<NumberInput label="Deposit" name="deposit" warn warnText="Higher than usual for this contract type" />
```

To put a link or bold text in a message, use the slot of the same name (`helper-text`, `warn-text`, `invalid-text`). In React + Tailwind, pass the markup to `helperText`, `warnText` or `invalidText`:


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input label="Tax ID" name="taxId">
  <span slot="helper-text">Where to find it: <a href="/help/tax-id">help</a></span>
</ui-text-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput label="Tax ID" name="taxId">
  <span slot="helper-text">Where to find it: <a href="/help/tax-id">help</a></span>
</UiTextInput>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput label="Tax ID" name="taxId" helperText={<>Where to find it: <a href="/help/tax-id">help</a></>} />
```

## Style a field that shows an error

While the error line is showing, the field has `data-show-error` on itself (`data-show-warn` for a warning). Unlike `invalid`, which you set, this attribute follows what the user actually sees. It is on the web components, so it works with the React wrappers too:

```css
ui-text-input[data-show-error]::part(label) {
  color: var(--ui-error);
}

form:has([data-show-error]) .error-summary {
  display: block;
}
```

## Disable a field or a group

- `disabled` greys the field out. A disabled field isn't submitted and isn't validated, as natively.
- `readonly` shows the value and submits it, but the user can't change it.
- A disabled `<fieldset>` disables every field inside. So does `<ui-form-group disabled>`, Carbon's fieldset with a label as its legend:


HTML:

```html
<ui-form-group legend="Billing address" disabled>
  <ui-text-input label="Street" name="street"></ui-text-input>
  <ui-text-input label="Postcode" name="postcode"></ui-text-input>
</ui-form-group>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiFormGroup legend="Billing address" disabled>
  <UiTextInput label="Street" name="street" />
  <UiTextInput label="Postcode" name="postcode" />
</UiFormGroup>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<FormGroup legend="Billing address" disabled>
  <TextInput label="Street" name="street" />
  <TextInput label="Postcode" name="postcode" />
</FormGroup>
```

## Dates: what users see and what you get

The date picker shows dates the way the reader expects. Your code always gets the same ISO date:

| | Page in Thai (`lang="th"`) | Page in English |
|---|---|---|
| The user sees and types | 10/10/2569 (พ.ศ.) | 10/10/2026 |
| `value` and the submitted form | `2026-10-10` | `2026-10-10` |

- `value`, `min` and `max` are always `yyyy-mm-dd` in the Gregorian year (ค.ศ.).
- Thai pages show and take years in พ.ศ. Set `era="ce"` to use ค.ศ. instead.
- Users may type Thai digits (๐–๙). They become 0–9.
- In พ.ศ., a year typed before 2400 (say 2026) gets a message asking for the พ.ศ. year. Nothing is converted behind the user's back.
- `format` sets the order: `dd/mm/yyyy` (default), `mm/dd/yyyy` or `yyyy-mm-dd`. The format shows as helper text until you set your own.
- The language comes from `lang` on the element or the closest ancestor. Set `locale` to override it for the date picker alone.


HTML:

```html
<ui-date-picker label="Contract start" name="start" value="2026-10-10" min="2026-01-01" required></ui-date-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDatePicker label="Contract start" name="start" value="2026-10-10" min="2026-01-01" required />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<DatePicker label="Contract start" name="start" defaultValue="2026-10-10" min="2026-01-01" required />
```

A range picker submits two entries, `name` and `end-name`:


HTML:

```html
<ui-date-picker range label="Start" end-label="End" name="from" end-name="to"></ui-date-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDatePicker range label="Start" endLabel="End" name="from" endName="to" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<DatePicker range label="Start" endLabel="End" name="from" endName="to" />
```

To refuse single days (weekends, holidays), set `isDateDisabled`: a function that returns `true`, or a string to use as the message. On the web component it's a property, so set it in JavaScript; in React and React + Tailwind it's a prop:


HTML:

```js
const picker = document.querySelector('ui-date-picker[name="start"]');
picker.isDateDisabled = (date) => (date.getDay() === 0 ? 'No deliveries on Sundays' : false);
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDatePicker label="Contract start" name="start" isDateDisabled={(date) => (date.getDay() === 0 ? 'No deliveries on Sundays' : false)} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<DatePicker label="Contract start" name="start" isDateDisabled={(date) => (date.getDay() === 0 ? 'No deliveries on Sundays' : false)} />
```

## Count characters and words

`max-count` adds a counter to `ui-text-input` and `ui-text-area`. It's a soft limit: users can paste and then trim. Going over turns the counter red, shows an error and blocks submit. Screen readers hear when the limit is near.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-area label="Notes" name="notes" max-count="200"></ui-text-area>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextArea label="Notes" name="notes" maxCount={200} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextArea label="Notes" name="notes" maxCount={200} />
```

On `ui-text-area`, `counter-mode="word"` counts words instead. Thai has no spaces between words, so the count uses the browser's word segmenter for the field's language. "สวัสดีครับ ผมชื่อสมชาย" counts as 5 words.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-area label="Summary" name="summary" max-count="50" counter-mode="word"></ui-text-area>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextArea label="Summary" name="summary" maxCount={50} counterMode="word" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextArea label="Summary" name="summary" maxCount={50} counterMode="word" />
```

Change the messages with `too-long-text` (`{max}` becomes the limit) and `near-limit-text`. For a hard limit that stops typing, use `maxlength` instead.

## Use a fluid form

Inside `<ui-fluid-form>`, fields render as Carbon fluid fields: the label sits inside a 64px box and errors show inside the box. Fluid fields have no helper line. `ui-fluid-form` is not a form, so wrap it in your own `<form>`:


HTML:

```html
<form method="dialog">
  <ui-fluid-form>
    <ui-text-input label="First name" name="first" required></ui-text-input>
    <ui-text-input label="Last name" name="last" required></ui-text-input>
    <ui-date-picker label="Date of birth" name="birth"></ui-date-picker>
  </ui-fluid-form>
</form>
```

React:

```tsx
<form method="dialog">
  <UiFluidForm>
    <UiTextInput label="First name" name="first" required />
    <UiTextInput label="Last name" name="last" required />
    <UiDatePicker label="Date of birth" name="birth" />
  </UiFluidForm>
</form>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { FluidForm } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/field';

<form>
  <FluidForm>
    <TextInput label="First name" name="first" />
    <TextInput label="Last name" name="last" />
    <DatePicker label="Date of birth" name="birth" />
  </FluidForm>
</form>
```

To make one field fluid on its own, give it the `fluid` attribute (the `fluid` prop in React and React + Tailwind).
