# Button

A button starts an action: save, submit, open a dialog. For going to another page, give it an `href` and it becomes a real link.

Every example below comes in three versions: the web component (HTML, any framework), the React wrapper (`@purpurabog/ui/react`) and the React + Tailwind copy (shadcn). Pick a tab once and the whole site follows.

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/button
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-button
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/button.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/button/button-skeleton.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/button/button.styles.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/button/button.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-button, shared-element, shared-field, shared-form-control, shared-localize, shared-navigate, shared-skeleton, shared-slots, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install class-variance-authority@0.7.1
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-button.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/button.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-button, tw-i18n, tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/button';</script>

<ui-button kind="primary" type="submit">Save</ui-button>
```

React:

```tsx
// npm i @purpurabog/ui lit @lit/react
import { UiButton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiButton kind="primary" type="submit">Save</UiButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/button';

<Button kind="primary" type="submit">Save</Button>
```

## Pick a kind


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button>Save</ui-button>
  <ui-button kind="secondary">Cancel</ui-button>
  <ui-button kind="tertiary">Export</ui-button>
  <ui-button kind="ghost">Learn more</ui-button>
  <ui-button kind="danger">Delete</ui-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiButton>Save</UiButton>
<UiButton kind="secondary">Cancel</UiButton>
<UiButton kind="tertiary">Export</UiButton>
<UiButton kind="ghost">Learn more</UiButton>
<UiButton kind="danger">Delete</UiButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Button>Save</Button>
<Button kind="secondary">Cancel</Button>
<Button kind="tertiary">Export</Button>
<Button kind="ghost">Learn more</Button>
<Button kind="danger">Delete</Button>
```

| Kind | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `primary` | The one main action of a page or dialog |
| `secondary` | The action next to the primary one (Cancel, Back) |
| `tertiary` | A less important action that still needs a visible border |
| `ghost` | Quiet actions in toolbars, tables and next to other content |
| `danger`, `danger-tertiary`, `danger-ghost` | Actions that delete or can't be undone |

Use one primary button per area. `kind` is Carbon's name; `variant` works as an alias on the web component.

## Danger buttons

Use a danger kind for an action that deletes something or can't be undone: `danger` for the main action of a confirm dialog, `danger-tertiary` and `danger-ghost` next to other content. Add a danger description: screen readers hear it after the name, so the warning isn't carried by the red colour alone.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button kind="danger" danger-description="Deletes the contract for good">Delete contract</ui-button>
  <ui-button kind="danger-tertiary" danger-description="This can't be undone">End the lease</ui-button>
  <ui-button kind="danger-ghost" danger-description="This can't be undone">Remove signer</ui-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiButton kind="danger" dangerDescription="Deletes the contract for good">Delete contract</UiButton>
<UiButton kind="danger-tertiary" dangerDescription="This can't be undone">End the lease</UiButton>
<UiButton kind="danger-ghost" dangerDescription="This can't be undone">Remove signer</UiButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Button kind="danger" dangerDescription="Deletes the contract for good">Delete contract</Button>
<Button kind="danger-tertiary" dangerDescription="This can't be undone">End the lease</Button>
<Button kind="danger-ghost" dangerDescription="This can't be undone">Remove signer</Button>
```

## Sizes

`size`: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px, `lg` 48px (the default), `xl` 64px, `2xl` 80px. In forms, match the field height (`md` for 40px fields). On `xl` and `2xl` the label stays at the top, as in Carbon.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button size="sm">Small</ui-button>
  <ui-button size="md">Medium</ui-button>
  <ui-button>Large</ui-button>
  <ui-button size="xl">Extra large</ui-button>
  <ui-button size="2xl">2X large</ui-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiButton size="sm">Small</UiButton>
<UiButton size="md">Medium</UiButton>
<UiButton>Large</UiButton>
<UiButton size="xl">Extra large</UiButton>
<UiButton size="2xl">2X large</UiButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Button size="sm">Small</Button>
<Button size="md">Medium</Button>
<Button>Large</Button>
<Button size="xl">Extra large</Button>
<Button size="2xl">2X large</Button>
```

## Full width

`full-width` stretches the button to the width of its container. Use it for the only action at the foot of a narrow form or a phone screen.


HTML:

```html
<ui-button full-width>Send for approval</ui-button>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiButton fullWidth>Send for approval</UiButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Button fullWidth>Send for approval</Button>
```

## Button set

`<ui-button-set>` puts buttons side by side, each up to 196px wide, with a thin line between them: Carbon's footer of a form or side panel. Put the secondary button first. `stacked` gives each button its own row, for a narrow panel.


HTML:

```html
<ui-button-set>
  <ui-button kind="secondary">Cancel</ui-button>
  <ui-button>Save</ui-button>
</ui-button-set>
<div style="max-width: 196px">
  <ui-button-set stacked>
    <ui-button>Approve</ui-button>
    <ui-button kind="secondary">Request changes</ui-button>
  </ui-button-set>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiButton, UiButtonSet } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiButtonSet>
  <UiButton kind="secondary">Cancel</UiButton>
  <UiButton>Save</UiButton>
</UiButtonSet>
<UiButtonSet stacked>
  <UiButton>Approve</UiButton>
  <UiButton kind="secondary">Request changes</UiButton>
</UiButtonSet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-button-set
import { ButtonSet } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/button-set';

<ButtonSet>
  <Button kind="secondary">Cancel</Button>
  <Button>Save</Button>
</ButtonSet>
<ButtonSet stacked>
  <Button>Approve</Button>
  <Button kind="secondary">Request changes</Button>
</ButtonSet>
```

## Icons

The web component takes an icon in its `prefix` or `suffix` slot; the React + Tailwind button takes a trailing `icon` only. Carbon puts the icon at the end, and a ghost button that moves on to more detail often ends in a chevron. For a button with only an icon, see [icon-only buttons](#icon-only-buttons).


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button kind="primary">Add
    <svg slot="suffix" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M8.5 7.5V3h-1v4.5H3v1h4.5V13h1V8.5H13v-1z"/></svg>
  </ui-button>
  <ui-button kind="ghost">Details
    <svg slot="suffix" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="m11 8-5 5-.7-.7L9.6 8 5.3 3.7 6 3z"/></svg>
  </ui-button>
  <ui-button kind="tertiary">
    <svg slot="prefix" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M13 2H3a1 1 0 0 0-1 1v10a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h10a1 1 0 0 0 1-1V5zm-7 1h4v2H6zm7 10H3V3h2v3h6V3.4l2 2z"/></svg>
    Save draft
  </ui-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
import { Add as AddIcon, ChevronRight as ChevronRightIcon, Save as SaveIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<UiButton kind="primary">
  Add
  <AddIcon slot="suffix" />
</UiButton>
<UiButton kind="ghost">
  Details
  <ChevronRightIcon slot="suffix" />
</UiButton>
<UiButton kind="tertiary">
  <SaveIcon slot="prefix" />
  Save draft
</UiButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Add as AddIcon, ChevronRight as ChevronRightIcon, Save as SaveIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<Button kind="primary" icon={<AddIcon />}>Add</Button>
<Button kind="ghost" icon={<ChevronRightIcon />}>Details</Button>
{/* no leading icon here: it goes at the end */}
<Button kind="tertiary" icon={<SaveIcon />}>Save draft</Button>
```

## Icon-only buttons

For a button that shows only an icon, use `<ui-icon-button>` (Carbon's `IconButton`). Its `label` is both its name and its tooltip, so the meaning shows on hover and on focus. It's `ghost` by default; `tooltip-placement` moves the tooltip (below by default). `<ui-button icon-only label="…">` also makes a square button, but without the tooltip.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-icon-button label="Edit contract">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="m13.7 4.3-2-2a1 1 0 0 0-1.4 0L2 10.6V14h3.4l8.3-8.3a1 1 0 0 0 0-1.4ZM5 13H3v-2l6-6 2 2Zm7-7-2-2 1-1 2 2Z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
  <ui-icon-button label="Add signer" kind="primary">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M8.5 7.5V3h-1v4.5H3v1h4.5V13h1V8.5H13v-1z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
  <ui-icon-button label="Edit terms" kind="tertiary" tooltip-placement="right">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="m13.7 4.3-2-2a1 1 0 0 0-1.4 0L2 10.6V14h3.4l8.3-8.3a1 1 0 0 0 0-1.4ZM5 13H3v-2l6-6 2 2Zm7-7-2-2 1-1 2 2Z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiIconButton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';
import { Add as AddIcon, Edit as EditIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<UiIconButton label="Edit contract"><EditIcon /></UiIconButton>
<UiIconButton label="Add signer" kind="primary"><AddIcon /></UiIconButton>
<UiIconButton label="Edit terms" kind="tertiary" tooltipPlacement="right"><EditIcon /></UiIconButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Add as AddIcon, Edit as EditIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

// npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-icon-button
import { IconButton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/icon-button';

<IconButton label="Edit contract"><EditIcon /></IconButton>
<IconButton label="Add signer" kind="primary"><AddIcon /></IconButton>
<IconButton label="Edit terms" kind="tertiary" tooltipPlacement="right"><EditIcon /></IconButton>
```

## Notification badge

`badge-count` puts Carbon's badge indicator in the corner of a ghost icon button: a number shows a count, and 0 shows a dot. Screen readers hear the count as the button's description. Use it for things waiting for the user, such as approvals.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-icon-button label="Approvals" badge-count="4">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M28.7 19.3 26 16.6V13a10 10 0 0 0-9-10v-2h-2v2a10 10 0 0 0-9 10v3.6l-2.7 2.7A1 1 0 0 0 3 20v3a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h7v.8a5 5 0 0 0 10 0V24h7a1 1 0 0 0 1-1v-3a1 1 0 0 0-.3-.7ZM19 24.8a3 3 0 0 1-6 0V24h6ZM27 22H5v-1.6l2.7-2.7A1 1 0 0 0 8 17v-4a8 8 0 0 1 16 0v4a1 1 0 0 0 .3.7l2.7 2.7Z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
  <ui-icon-button label="Notifications, new" badge-count="0">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M28.7 19.3 26 16.6V13a10 10 0 0 0-9-10v-2h-2v2a10 10 0 0 0-9 10v3.6l-2.7 2.7A1 1 0 0 0 3 20v3a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h7v.8a5 5 0 0 0 10 0V24h7a1 1 0 0 0 1-1v-3a1 1 0 0 0-.3-.7ZM19 24.8a3 3 0 0 1-6 0V24h6ZM27 22H5v-1.6l2.7-2.7A1 1 0 0 0 8 17v-4a8 8 0 0 1 16 0v4a1 1 0 0 0 .3.7l2.7 2.7Z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
import { Notification as NotificationIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<UiIconButton label="Approvals" badgeCount={4}><NotificationIcon /></UiIconButton>
<UiIconButton label="Notifications, new" badgeCount={0}><NotificationIcon /></UiIconButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Notification as NotificationIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<IconButton label="Approvals" badgeCount={4}><NotificationIcon /></IconButton>
<IconButton label="Notifications, new" badgeCount={0}><NotificationIcon /></IconButton>
```

## Toggle buttons

`pressed` makes a button that stays on or off, such as pinning a contract to the dashboard. Screen readers hear "pressed" or "not pressed". Flip it in your click handler; leave it unset on an ordinary button. It works on `<ui-button>` and `<ui-icon-button>`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-icon-button id="button-pin" label="Pin to dashboard" pressed>
  <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M10 1 9 2l1 1-3 3-3-.5L3.5 6 6 8.5 2 12.5V14h1.5L7.5 10l2.5 2.5.5-.5-.5-3 3-3 1 1 1-1z"/></svg>
</ui-icon-button>
<p>Pinned: <output id="button-pin-out">yes</output></p>
<script type="module">
  const pin = document.getElementById('button-pin');
  pin.addEventListener('click', () => {
    pin.pressed = !pin.pressed;
    document.getElementById('button-pin-out').textContent = pin.pressed ? 'yes' : 'no';
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
import { Pin as PinIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<UiIconButton label="Pin to dashboard" pressed={pinned} onClick={() => setPinned(!pinned)}>
  <PinIcon />
</UiIconButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Pin as PinIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<IconButton label="Pin to dashboard" aria-pressed={pinned} onClick={() => setPinned(!pinned)}>
  <PinIcon />
</IconButton>
```

## Loading

`loading` shows Carbon's small spinner, ignores clicks and keeps focus on the button, so keyboard users don't lose their place. The loading text replaces the label while it loads; the loading label is what screen readers hear.

`loading-position` moves the spinner: `end` (the default) where a trailing icon goes, `start` in the label's place, `center` in the middle of the button.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button loading loading-text="Saving…">Save</ui-button>
  <ui-button kind="secondary" loading loading-position="start" loading-text="Sending…">Send</ui-button>
  <ui-button kind="tertiary" loading loading-position="center">Export</ui-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiButton loading={saving} loadingText="Saving…">Save</UiButton>
<UiButton kind="secondary" loading={sending} loadingPosition="start" loadingText="Sending…">Send</UiButton>
<UiButton kind="tertiary" loading={exporting} loadingPosition="center">Export</UiButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Button loading={saving} loadingText="Saving…">Save</Button>
<Button kind="secondary" loading={sending} loadingPosition="start" loadingText="Sending…">Send</Button>
<Button kind="tertiary" loading={exporting} loadingPosition="center">Export</Button>
```

## Skeleton

While the data behind a page loads, `<ui-button-skeleton>` keeps the button's place: a 150px bar at the button's `size`. Screen readers skip it, so say "loading" on the area around it (for example `aria-busy="true"`).


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button-skeleton></ui-button-skeleton>
  <ui-button-skeleton size="md"></ui-button-skeleton>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiButtonSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiButtonSkeleton />
<UiButtonSkeleton size="md" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { ButtonSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/button';

<ButtonSkeleton />
<ButtonSkeleton size="md" />
```

## Disabled, or disabled with a reason

`disabled` removes the button from the Tab order, as Carbon does. If people need to learn why they can't use it, use disabled-focusable instead: it looks disabled and ignores clicks, but keyboard users can still reach it and read a tooltip.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button disabled>Approve</ui-button>
  <ui-tooltip text="Only approvers can approve contracts">
    <ui-button disabled-focusable>Approve</ui-button>
  </ui-tooltip>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiButton disabled>Approve</UiButton>
<UiTooltip text="Only approvers can approve contracts">
  <UiButton disabledFocusable>Approve</UiButton>
</UiTooltip>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Button disabled>Approve</Button>
<Tooltip text="Only approvers can approve contracts">
  <Button disabledFocusable>Approve</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

## Links that look like buttons

With `href` the button renders an `<a>` and screen readers announce a link. On the web component a plain click fires a cancelable `ui-navigate` event, so a SPA router can take over (see [Frameworks](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/frameworks/)). In this preview the event is cancelled and its `href` shown instead.


HTML:

```html
<ui-button id="button-new-contract" kind="tertiary" href="/contracts/new">New contract</ui-button>
<p>Router got: <output id="button-new-contract-out"></output></p>
<script type="module">
  document.getElementById('button-new-contract').addEventListener('ui-navigate', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    document.getElementById('button-new-contract-out').textContent = event.detail.href;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiButton kind="tertiary" href="/contracts/new" onUiNavigate={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); navigate(e.detail.href); }}>
  New contract
</UiButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Button kind="tertiary" href="/contracts/new">New contract</Button>
```

## Submit a form

In a `<form>`, `type="submit"` submits it and `type="reset"` resets it, as a native button does. The default `type` is `button`, so other buttons never submit by accident. Set `loading` while the request runs, so nobody sends it twice.


HTML:

```html
<form id="button-form" method="dialog" style="display: grid; gap: 16px">
  <ui-text-input label="Department" name="department" value="Legal" required></ui-text-input>
  <ui-button-set>
    <ui-button kind="secondary" type="reset">Reset</ui-button>
    <ui-button id="button-form-submit" type="submit" loading-text="Saving…">Save</ui-button>
  </ui-button-set>
</form>
<p>Sent: <output id="button-form-out"></output></p>
<script type="module">
  const form = document.getElementById('button-form');
  const submit = document.getElementById('button-form-submit');
  form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    submit.loading = true;
    setTimeout(() => {
      submit.loading = false;
      document.getElementById('button-form-out').textContent = [...new FormData(form)].map(([key, value]) => `${key}=${value}`).join(', ');
    }, 1500);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={async (e) => { e.preventDefault(); setSaving(true); await save(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); setSaving(false); }}>
  <UiTextInput label="Department" name="department" value="Legal" required />
  <UiButtonSet>
    <UiButton kind="secondary" type="reset">Reset</UiButton>
    <UiButton type="submit" loading={saving} loadingText="Saving…">Save</UiButton>
  </UiButtonSet>
</form>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={async (e) => { e.preventDefault(); setSaving(true); await save(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); setSaving(false); }}>
  <TextInput label="Department" name="department" defaultValue="Legal" required />
  <ButtonSet>
    <Button kind="secondary" type="reset">Reset</Button>
    <Button type="submit" loading={saving} loadingText="Saving…">Save</Button>
  </ButtonSet>
</form>
```

## Accessibility

- It renders a native `<button>`: Enter and Space press it, and `type="submit"` / `type="reset"` work in a `<form>`.
- Name icon-only buttons: `label` on the web component (an `aria-label` on the element does not reach the inner button), `aria-label` on the Tailwind button.
- `pressed` makes it a toggle button (`aria-pressed`); `haspopup` and `expanded` describe a button that opens a menu or dialog.
- Danger kinds can add a danger description, read after the name ("Deletes the contract for good").

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-button>` · React `UiButton`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` |  |  |  | Same as `kind`, kept for teams used to `variant` (shadcn, MUI); `kind` is Carbon's name and the one in the docs |
| `kind` | `kind` | `ButtonKind` | `'primary'` | Carbon `kind`: primary, secondary, tertiary, ghost, danger, danger-tertiary, danger-ghost. |
| `size` | `size` | `ButtonSize` | `'lg'` |  |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `disabled-focusable` | `disabledFocusable` | `boolean` | `false` | Disabled, but still focusable: aria-disabled, ignores clicks — so a tooltip can explain why. |
| `type` | `type` | `'button' \| 'submit' \| 'reset'` | `'button'` |  |
| `full-width` | `fullWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | Stretch to the container width. |
| `icon-only` | `iconOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Square button (as wide as it is tall, no padding) with its content centred: put the icon in the `prefix` slot and leave the label empty — nothing is hidden for you. Set `label` for its name; it shows no tooltip (use `<ui-icon-button>` for one). |
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name; required when the button shows only an icon. |
| `description` | `description` | `string` | `''` | Accessible description (set by ui-tooltip). |
| `danger-description` | `dangerDescription` | `string` | `''` | Carbon `dangerDescription`: read after the name of a danger kind (danger, danger-tertiary, danger-ghost), e.g. "Deletes the contract for good". Empty by default, as Carbon v11 (React `ButtonBase`, WC `cds-button`). |
| `href` | `href` | `string` | `''` | Render as a link. |
| `target` | `target` | `'_self' \| '_blank'` | `'_self'` |  |
| `loading` | `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Busy: looks disabled with a spinner, ignores clicks, keeps focus, announces `loading-label`. |
| `loading-label` | `loadingLabel` | `string` | `''` | What `loading` announces (default: `loading-text`, else the translation's "Loading"). |
| `loading-position` | `loadingPosition` | `ButtonLoadingPosition` | `'end'` | Where the spinner goes (MUI `loadingPosition`): `end` (Carbon ActionSet), `start`, `center`. |
| `loading-text` | `loadingText` | `string` | `''` | Shown in the label's place while loading, e.g. "Saving…" (Carbon Modal `loadingDescription`). |
| `pressed` | `pressed` | `boolean \| undefined` |  | Toggle-button state; leave unset for a normal button. |
| `haspopup` | `haspopup` | `string` | `''` | The button opens a popup: rendered as `aria-haspopup` (e.g. `menu`, `listbox`, `dialog`). |
| `expanded` | `expanded` | `boolean \| undefined` |  | Whether the popup / disclosed content is open (`aria-expanded`); left unset, only a `haspopup` button reports it. |

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `variant` | `ButtonKind` | Same as `kind` (permanent alias for teams used to `variant`); a `variant` attribute works too. |
| `form` |  | (read-only) The `<form>` the button submits or resets, as a native button's `form`. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-navigate` | none (use a ref) | detail: { href } (cancelable) on a plain click of the link; cancel it to route client-side (README: SPA router) |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | Label |
| `prefix` | Leading icon |
| `suffix` | Trailing icon (e.g. the ghost-button chevron) |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The native button or link |
| `prefix` | The leading icon slot |
| `suffix` | The trailing icon slot |
| `loading` | The spinner's place: at the end, the start or the centre (`loading` only; not when it takes the label's place) |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-button-align` |  | `align-items` of the content (ui-modal sets `flex-start` for its 64px footer buttons) |
| `--ui-button-padding-top` |  | Top padding of the content (ui-modal footer: 14px) |
| `--ui-button-padding-start` |  | Start padding (default 15px; ui-table-batch-actions: 16px) |
| `--ui-button-padding-end` |  | End padding (default 63px, Carbon's room for an icon; ui-table-batch-actions: 16px) |
| `--ui-button-height-lg` |  | Height of `size="lg"`, the default (default: `--ui-field-height-lg`, 48px; Kanok: 32px) |
| `--ui-button-radius` |  | Corner radius (default 0; Kanok: 6px) |
| `--ui-button-justify` |  | `justify-content` of label and icon (default `space-between`, Carbon's label-start / icon-end; Kanok: `center`) |
| `--ui-button-gap` |  | Gap between label and icon (default 32px; Kanok: 8px) |
| `--ui-button-ghost-justify` |  | `justify-content` of the ghost kinds (default `flex-start`) |
| `--ui-button-ghost-padding-end` |  | End padding of the ghost kinds (default 15px) |
| `--ui-button-secondary` |  | Fill of `kind="secondary"` (default `--ui-secondary`); also `--ui-button-secondary-hover`, `--ui-button-secondary-active` |
| `--ui-on-button-secondary` |  | Text of `kind="secondary"` (default `--ui-on-primary`) |
| `--ui-button-secondary-border` |  | Border colour of `kind="secondary"` (default transparent) |
| `--ui-button-height-xl` |  | Height of `size="xl"` (default 64px; Kanok: 40px); also `--ui-button-height-2xl` (80px; Kanok: 48px) |
| `--ui-button-padding-xl` |  | Start and end padding of `size="xl"` (default: the button's own); also `--ui-button-padding-2xl` |
| `--ui-button-tall-align` |  | `align-items` of xl / 2xl content (default `flex-start`, Carbon's label at the top; Kanok: `center`) |
| `--ui-button-tall-padding-top` |  | Top padding of xl / 2xl content (default 14px; Kanok: 0px); also `--ui-button-tall-icon-offset` (1px) |
| `--ui-focus-offset` |  | `outline-offset` of the focus ring (default -2px, inside; Kanok: 2px, outside) |
| `--ui-focus-inset-width` |  | Width of the inner focus-inset line (default 2px; Kanok: 0) |
| `--ui-button-tertiary-hover` |  | / --ui-button-tertiary-active / --ui-button-tertiary-focus - Tertiary fills (default primary, its hover and active; Kanok: an indigo tint) |
| `--ui-button-tertiary-state-ink` |  | / --ui-button-tertiary-active-border - Tertiary text on those fills and the pressed border (default text-on-color, the button's border) |




---

# Text input

A text input takes one line of text: a name, an email, a password, an ID number. For several lines, use a [text area](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/text-area/); for amounts, a [number input](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/number-input/).


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input label="Full name" name="name" helper-text="As it appears on your ID card"></ui-text-input>
<ui-text-input label="Password" name="password" type="password"></ui-text-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput label="Full name" name="name" helperText="As it appears on your ID card" />
<UiTextInput label="Password" name="password" type="password" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput label="Full name" name="name" helperText="As it appears on your ID card" />
<TextInput label="Password" name="password" type="password" />
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/text-input
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-text-input
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/text-input.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/text-input/text-input-skeleton.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/text-input/text-input.styles.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/text-input/text-input.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-field, core-mask, shared-affixes, shared-element, shared-field, shared-form-control, shared-localize, shared-skeleton, shared-slots, tooltip, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install class-variance-authority@0.7.1 @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-text-input.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/text-input.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    tw-affix, tw-field, tw-skeleton, tw-theme, tw-tooltip, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/text-input';</script>

<ui-text-input label="Full name" name="name"></ui-text-input>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiTextInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiTextInput label="Full name" name="name" onInput={(e) => setName((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value)} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { TextInput } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/text-input';

<TextInput label="Full name" name="name" value={name} onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)} />
```

- The element fires native `input` on every keystroke and `change` when the user commits the value, so the React wrapper has `onInput` and `onChange`.
- The React + Tailwind `onChange` is React's own (every keystroke). Its second argument is the value without a mask's separators.

## Sizes

`size`: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (the default), `lg` 48px.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input label="Small" size="sm"></ui-text-input>
<ui-text-input label="Medium"></ui-text-input>
<ui-text-input label="Large" size="lg"></ui-text-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput label="Small" size="sm" />
<UiTextInput label="Medium" />
<UiTextInput label="Large" size="lg" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput label="Small" size="sm" />
<TextInput label="Medium" />
<TextInput label="Large" size="lg" />
```

## Passwords

`type="password"` adds Carbon's show / hide button at the end of the field. Its tooltip is also its name and says what a press does next: "Show password", then "Hide password". Change the words with `show-password-label` and `hide-password-label`. Each press fires `ui-toggle` with `detail.visible`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input id="text-input-password" label="Password" name="password" type="password" autocomplete="current-password"></ui-text-input>
<ui-text-input label="PIN" name="pin" type="password" inputmode="numeric" show-password-label="Show PIN" hide-password-label="Hide PIN"></ui-text-input>
<p>Password shown: <output id="text-input-password-out">no</output></p>
<script type="module">
  document.getElementById('text-input-password').addEventListener('ui-toggle', (event) => {
    document.getElementById('text-input-password-out').textContent = event.detail.visible ? 'yes' : 'no';
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput label="Password" name="password" type="password" autocomplete="current-password" onUiToggle={(e) => track(e.detail.visible)} />
<UiTextInput label="PIN" name="pin" type="password" inputmode="numeric" showPasswordLabel="Show PIN" hidePasswordLabel="Hide PIN" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput label="Password" name="password" type="password" autoComplete="current-password" onTogglePasswordVisibility={(e, visible) => track(visible)} />
<TextInput label="PIN" name="pin" type="password" inputMode="numeric" showPasswordLabel="Show PIN" hidePasswordLabel="Hide PIN" />
```

## Email, phone and web addresses

`type` also takes `email`, `tel`, `url`, `search` and `number`, as on `<input>`. For the virtual keyboard alone, set `inputmode` (and `enterkeyhint` for its Enter key).

Add `autocomplete` so the browser can fill the field in. The browser checks an email address; a mask keeps a phone number readable.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input label="Work email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email"></ui-text-input>
<ui-text-input label="Mobile" name="mobile" type="tel" autocomplete="tel" mask="000-000-0000" helper-text="Format: 000-000-0000"></ui-text-input>
<ui-text-input label="Company website" name="website" type="url" placeholder="https://"></ui-text-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput label="Work email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" />
<UiTextInput label="Mobile" name="mobile" type="tel" autocomplete="tel" mask="000-000-0000" helperText="Format: 000-000-0000" />
<UiTextInput label="Company website" name="website" type="url" placeholder="https://" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput label="Work email" name="email" type="email" autoComplete="email" />
<TextInput label="Mobile" name="mobile" type="tel" autoComplete="tel" mask="000-000-0000" helperText="Format: 000-000-0000" />
<TextInput label="Company website" name="website" type="url" placeholder="https://" />
```

## Currency, units and masks

`prefix-text` and `suffix-text` put text inside the field, before or after the value: a currency, a unit. They aren't part of the value, and screen readers hear them as part of the field's description.

`mask` formats the value as the user types: `0` is a digit, `a` a letter, `*` either, and any other character is a separator the field adds by itself. A mask of digits only brings up the numeric keyboard. Put the format in the helper text too, so people know it before they type.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input label="Weight" name="weight" suffix-text="kg"></ui-text-input>
<ui-text-input label="Citizen ID" name="citizenId" mask="0-0000-00000-00-0" helper-text="13 digits: 0-0000-00000-00-0"></ui-text-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput label="Weight" name="weight" suffixText="kg" />
<UiTextInput label="Citizen ID" name="citizenId" mask="0-0000-00000-00-0" helperText="13 digits: 0-0000-00000-00-0" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput label="Weight" name="weight" suffixText="kg" />
<TextInput label="Citizen ID" name="citizenId" mask="0-0000-00000-00-0" helperText="13 digits: 0-0000-00000-00-0" onChange={(e, raw) => setCitizenId(raw)} />
```

- The element's `value` and the submitted form get the formatted text (`1-2345-67890-12-3`). Its `rawValue` property gives what was typed, without separators (`1234567890123`). In React + Tailwind, `onChange` gets that as its second argument.
- A value your code sets, raw or formatted, shows formatted.
- None of these has a Carbon counterpart (Carbon puts the unit or the format in the label or helper text); they follow USWDS.

## Read the value

Listen to `input` to react on every keystroke, or to `change` once the user is done. With a mask, `value` is what the field shows and `rawValue` is what was typed.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input id="text-input-tax" label="Tax ID" name="taxId" mask="0-0000-00000-00-0" helper-text="13 digits"></ui-text-input>
<p>value: <output id="text-input-tax-value"></output><br>rawValue: <output id="text-input-tax-raw"></output></p>
<script type="module">
  const tax = document.getElementById('text-input-tax');
  tax.addEventListener('input', () => {
    document.getElementById('text-input-tax-value').textContent = tax.value;
    document.getElementById('text-input-tax-raw').textContent = tax.rawValue;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
import type { UiTextInput as UiTextInputElement } from '@purpurabog/ui/text-input';

<UiTextInput label="Tax ID" name="taxId" mask="0-0000-00000-00-0" helperText="13 digits" onInput={(e) => setTaxId((e.target as UiTextInputElement).rawValue)} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput label="Tax ID" name="taxId" mask="0-0000-00000-00-0" helperText="13 digits" onChange={(e, raw) => setTaxId(raw)} />
```

## Character counter

`max-count` shows a counter above the field. It's a soft limit: people can paste a long text and then trim it. Going over turns the counter red, shows an error at once and blocks the form. Screen readers hear when the limit is near, not on every keystroke.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input label="Contract title" name="title" max-count="40" value="Lease of the warehouse on Rama IV Road"></ui-text-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput label="Contract title" name="title" maxCount={40} value="Lease of the warehouse on Rama IV Road" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput label="Contract title" name="title" maxCount={40} defaultValue="Lease of the warehouse on Rama IV Road" />
```

Change the messages with `too-long-text` (`{max}` becomes the limit) and `near-limit-text`. For a hard limit that stops typing, use `maxlength`. More in [Forms and validation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/#count-characters-and-words).

## Helper text, warnings and errors

One line shows under the field at a time: an error beats a warning, and a warning beats the helper text.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input label="Phone" name="phone" helper-text="We only call about this contract"></ui-text-input>
<ui-text-input label="Email" name="email" value="somchai@gmial.com" warn warn-text="Check the spelling of the domain"></ui-text-input>
<ui-text-input label="Tax ID" name="taxId" value="12345" invalid invalid-text="A tax ID has 13 digits"></ui-text-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput label="Phone" name="phone" helperText="We only call about this contract" />
<UiTextInput label="Email" name="email" value="somchai@gmial.com" warn warnText="Check the spelling of the domain" />
<UiTextInput label="Tax ID" name="taxId" value="12345" invalid invalidText="A tax ID has 13 digits" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput label="Phone" name="phone" helperText="We only call about this contract" />
<TextInput label="Email" name="email" defaultValue="somchai@gmial.com" warn warnText="Check the spelling of the domain" />
<TextInput label="Tax ID" name="taxId" defaultValue="12345" invalid invalidText="A tax ID has 13 digits" />
```

- On the element, `required`, `pattern`, `minlength` and the browser's checks work as on `<input>`, and their errors wait until the user leaves the field. The React + Tailwind field shows what you pass in `invalid` and `invalidText`; validation is your app's, as in Carbon React.
- To put a link in a message, use the slot of the same name (`helper-text`, `warn-text`, `invalid-text`). In React + Tailwind, pass the markup to `helperText`, `warnText` or `invalidText`.
- When errors show, custom validity and server errors: [Forms and validation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/).

## Label and helper text with markup

For a label or a message with markup, such as a link or an emphasis, use the `label` and `helper-text` slots (`warn-text` and `invalid-text` work the same way). The React + Tailwind field takes the markup in `label` and `helperText`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input name="signerEmail" type="email" required>
  <span slot="label">Signer's email <em>(required)</em></span>
  <span slot="helper-text">We send the contract here. <a href="/en/forms/">How fields are checked</a></span>
</ui-text-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput name="signerEmail" type="email" required>
  <span slot="label">Signer's email <em>(required)</em></span>
  <span slot="helper-text">We send the contract here. <a href="/forms">How fields are checked</a></span>
</UiTextInput>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput
  name="signerEmail"
  type="email"
  required
  label={<>Signer's email <em>(required)</em></>}
  helperText={<>We send the contract here. <a href="/forms">How fields are checked</a></>}
/>
```

## Label position, read-only and disabled

- `hide-label` keeps the label for screen readers but doesn't show it. Use it only where something else on screen names the field.
- `inline` puts the label before the field and the message after it, in one row (Carbon's inline text input).
- `fluid`, or a fluid form around the field, puts the label inside a 64px box ([fluid forms](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/#use-a-fluid-form)).
- `readonly` shows and submits the value, but the user can't change it. `disabled` greys the field out; it isn't submitted.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input label="Contract no." value="C-2026-0142" inline></ui-text-input>
<ui-text-input label="Contract no." value="C-2026-0142" readonly></ui-text-input>
<ui-text-input label="Branch" value="Bangkok" disabled></ui-text-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput label="Contract no." value="C-2026-0142" inline />
<UiTextInput label="Contract no." value="C-2026-0142" readonly />
<UiTextInput label="Branch" value="Bangkok" disabled />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput label="Contract no." defaultValue="C-2026-0142" inline />
<TextInput label="Contract no." defaultValue="C-2026-0142" readOnly />
<TextInput label="Branch" defaultValue="Bangkok" disabled />
```

## Fluid fields

A fluid field puts its label inside a 64px box, and an error or a warning shows inside the box below a line; there is no helper text. Set `fluid` on a field, or put the fields in a `<ui-fluid-form>` (see [fluid forms](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/#use-a-fluid-form)).


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input label="Contract value" name="amount" prefix-text="฿" suffix-text="THB" value="500,000" fluid></ui-text-input>
<ui-text-input label="Password" name="password" type="password" fluid></ui-text-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput label="Contract value" name="amount" prefixText="฿" suffixText="THB" value="500,000" fluid />
<UiTextInput label="Password" name="password" type="password" fluid />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput label="Contract value" name="amount" prefixText="฿" suffixText="THB" defaultValue="500,000" fluid />
<TextInput label="Password" name="password" type="password" fluid />
```

## Check it in a form

In a `<form>`, the element checks `required`, `type`, `pattern`, `minlength` and the counter, as a native input does. A submit with a problem is blocked, every field with a problem shows its error, and the first one gets focus. Try sending this form empty.


HTML:

```html
<form id="text-input-form" method="dialog" style="display: grid; gap: 16px">
  <ui-text-input label="Supplier name" name="supplier" required></ui-text-input>
  <ui-text-input label="Email" name="email" type="email" required></ui-text-input>
  <div><ui-button type="submit" size="md">Add supplier</ui-button></div>
</form>
<p>Sent: <output id="text-input-form-out"></output></p>
<script type="module">
  const form = document.getElementById('text-input-form');
  form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    document.getElementById('text-input-form-out').textContent = [...new FormData(form)].map(([key, value]) => `${key}=${value}`).join(', ');
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); addSupplier(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }}>
  <UiTextInput label="Supplier name" name="supplier" required />
  <UiTextInput label="Email" name="email" type="email" required />
  <UiButton type="submit" size="md">Add supplier</UiButton>
</form>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// your validation fills `errors`, as in Carbon React
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); addSupplier(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }} noValidate>
  <TextInput label="Supplier name" name="supplier" invalid={!!errors.supplier} invalidText={errors.supplier} />
  <TextInput label="Email" name="email" type="email" invalid={!!errors.email} invalidText={errors.email} />
  <Button type="submit" size="md">Add supplier</Button>
</form>
```

## Errors from your own checks

`setCustomValidity(message)` makes the field invalid with your message, as on `<input>`. Use it for a check the browser can't do, such as a contract number that is already in use. The error shows once the user leaves the field; `setCustomValidity('')` clears it. More in [Forms and validation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/#check-a-rule-with-custom-validity).


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input id="text-input-contract" label="Contract no." name="contractNo" helper-text="C-2026-0142 is already in use: try it"></ui-text-input>
<script type="module">
  const contract = document.getElementById('text-input-contract');
  contract.addEventListener('change', () => {
    contract.setCustomValidity(contract.value.trim() === 'C-2026-0142' ? 'This contract number is already in use' : '');
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput
  label="Contract no."
  name="contractNo"
  onChange={(e) => {
    const field = e.target as UiTextInputElement;
    field.setCustomValidity(isTaken(field.value) ? 'This contract number is already in use' : '');
  }}
/>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput
  label="Contract no."
  name="contractNo"
  invalid={taken}
  invalidText="This contract number is already in use"
  onBlur={(e) => setTaken(isTaken(e.target.value))}
/>
```

## Skeleton

While the data of a form loads, `<ui-text-input-skeleton>` keeps the field's place: a label bar and a field bar at its `size`, or a fluid box with `fluid`. Screen readers skip it, so say "loading" on the form (for example `aria-busy="true"`).


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input-skeleton></ui-text-input-skeleton>
<ui-text-input-skeleton fluid></ui-text-input-skeleton>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiTextInputSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiTextInputSkeleton />
<UiTextInputSkeleton fluid />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { TextInputSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/text-input';

<TextInputSkeleton />
<TextInputSkeleton fluid />
```

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| Enter | Submits the form the field sits in, as a native text input does |
| Enter or Space on the password button | Shows or hides the password |

## Accessibility

- The label is a real `<label>` for the inner `<input>`, and the message line is its `aria-describedby`. `aria-label` on the element does not reach the input; use `label` (with `hide-label` if it must not show).
- An error sets `aria-invalid` on the input. On the element it waits until the user leaves the field, so nobody hears "required" while still typing.
- The password button has no `aria-pressed`: its name changes with what it does next, as in Carbon.
- The prefix and suffix are read as part of the field's description, so "฿" or "kg" isn't lost to screen reader users.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Text input](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-text-input/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-text-input>` · React `UiTextInput`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | Visible label text; the `label` slot replaces it when markup is needed. |
| `hide-label` | `hideLabel` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep the label for screen readers but don't show it. |
| `helper-text` | `helperText` | `string` | `''` | Helper text under the field, shown while there is no error or warning. |
| `invalid-text` | `invalidText` | `string` | `''` | Message shown when invalid. Falls back to the browser's validation message. |
| `invalid` | `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Force the error state (e.g. a server-side error). |
| `warn` | `warn` | `boolean` | `false` | Non-blocking warning; shown when there is no error. |
| `warn-text` | `warnText` | `string` | `''` | Text of the warning shown while `warn`. |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `''` | Reflected: form-associated elements submit under the `name` attribute. |
| `type` | `type` | `TextInputType` | `'text'` |  |
| `size` | `size` | `TextInputSize` | `'md'` | Field height: sm 32px, md 40px, lg 48px (tokens `--ui-field-height-*`). |
| `placeholder` | `placeholder` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `autocomplete` | `autocomplete` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `inputmode` | `inputmode` | `string` | `''` | Passed to the text box: the virtual keyboard to show (`numeric`, `decimal`, `email`, `tel`, `url`, `search`…). |
| `enterkeyhint` | `enterkeyhint` | `string` | `''` | Passed to the text box: the label of the virtual keyboard's Enter key (`search`, `send`, `next`, `done`…). |
| `pattern` | `pattern` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `prefix-text` | `prefixText` | `string` | `''` | Text inside the field before the value, e.g. a currency (`฿`). Part of the field's description for screen readers. |
| `suffix-text` | `suffixText` | `string` | `''` | Text inside the field after the value, e.g. a unit (`kg`). Part of the field's description for screen readers. |
| `mask` | `mask` | `string` | `''` | Formats the value as the user types: `0` a digit, `a` a letter, `*` either; any other character is a separator added for the user (`\` makes a pattern character one). E.g. `0-0000-00000-00-0` (Thai citizen ID), `000-000-0000`. `value` and the form get the formatted text, `rawValue` what was typed. Put the format in the helper text too (Carbon). |
| `minlength` | `minlength` | `number \| undefined` |  |  |
| `maxlength` | `maxlength` | `number \| undefined` |  |  |
| `max-count` | `maxCount` | `number \| undefined` |  | Soft limit with a visible counter (unlike maxlength, extra text isn't blocked). |
| `too-long-text` | `tooLongText` | `string` | `''` | Error when over `max-count`; `{max}` is replaced with the limit. |
| `near-limit-text` | `nearLimitText` | `string` | `''` | Announced once when the remaining characters drop to 10% or less. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the control; a disabled `<fieldset>` ancestor does the same. |
| `readonly` | `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows and submits the value but blocks changes. |
| `fluid` | `fluid` | `boolean` | `false` | Carbon `FluidTextInput`: the label inside a 64px box, an error / warning inside it. `<ui-fluid-form>` sets it for every field inside. |
| `required` | `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Blocks form submission while the field is empty. |
| `show-password-label` | `showPasswordLabel` | `string` | `''` | The password toggle's name and tooltip while the password is hidden (Carbon `showPasswordLabel`; default: the translation's "Show password"). |
| `hide-password-label` | `hidePasswordLabel` | `string` | `''` | The password toggle's name and tooltip while the password shows (Carbon `hidePasswordLabel`; default: the translation's "Hide password"). |
| `inline` | `inline` | `boolean` | `false` | Carbon `inline`: the label before the field, the helper / error text after it (ignored while fluid). |

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `rawValue` |  | (read-only) The characters typed, without the mask's separators (`value` when there is no mask). |
| `willValidate` |  | (read-only) Whether the field takes part in constraint validation (not while disabled), as natively. |
| `labels` |  | (read-only) The `<label>`s that point at this field. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `setCustomValidity(message)` | Like `<input>.setCustomValidity()`: a non-empty message makes the field invalid (and is shown as its error once touched) until cleared with ''. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `change` | `onChange` | Re-dispatched from the native input (native change is not composed) |
| `ui-toggle` | `onUiToggle` | detail: { visible } when the password toggle shows or hides the password (Carbon `onTogglePasswordVisibility`) |
| `input` | `onInput` | Native input event (already composed, so it reaches the host) |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| `label` | Label content with markup; the `label` attribute is the plain-text fallback |
| `helper-text` | Helper text with markup (links, bold); overrides `helper-text` |
| `warn-text` | Warning text shown while `warn`; overrides `warn-text` |
| `invalid-text` | Error text shown while invalid; overrides `invalid-text` |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The field box around the input |
| `label` | The label |
| `input` | The native input |
| `prefix` | The text before the value |
| `suffix` | The text after the value |
| `password-toggle` | The show / hide password button |
| `password-tooltip` | The `<ui-tooltip>` around it (its name) |
| `counter` | The character counter |
| `status-icon` | The error / warning icon |
| `helper-text` | The helper line |
| `warning-text` | The warning line |
| `warn-text` | Same line as `warning-text` (named after the `warn-text` attribute / slot) |
| `error-text` | The error line |
| `invalid-text` | Same line as `error-text` (named after the `invalid-text` attribute / slot) |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-field-border` |  | Border on every side of the box (default none: Carbon's underline only; Kanok: a 1px outline) |
| `--ui-field-disabled-border-color` |  | Border colour when disabled (default: the underline transparent) |
| `--ui-field-readonly-border-color` |  | Border colour when read-only (default: a hairline underline) |
| `--ui-field-radius` |  | Corner radius of the box (default 0; Kanok: 6px) |
| `--ui-field-background` |  | Fill of the box (default `--ui-surface-1`; Kanok: transparent) |
| `--ui-label-font` |  | Font of the label (default `--ui-font-caption`; Kanok: 14px semibold) |
| `--ui-label-color` |  | Colour of the label (default `--ui-ink-muted`; Kanok: `--ui-ink`) |
| `--ui-field-readonly-background` |  | The box's fill when read-only (default transparent; Kanok: a faint ink tint, so read-only reads as set and never weaker than disabled) |
| `--ui-fluid-background` |  | / --ui-fluid-gap - A fluid box's fill and the space under it (default the layer's fill, 0: boxes that touch; Kanok: transparent, 8px) |
| `--ui-icon-control-radius` |  | Corners of its small icon buttons, their hover fill and ring (default 0; Kanok: round) |




---

# Text area

A text area takes text that runs over several lines: notes, a description, a reason. It has the same label, helper text and error line as the [text input](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/text-input/), plus a character or word counter and a field that can grow with its text.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-area label="Notes" name="notes" helper-text="Anything the legal team should know"></ui-text-area>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextArea label="Notes" name="notes" helperText="Anything the legal team should know" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextArea label="Notes" name="notes" helperText="Anything the legal team should know" />
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/text-area
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-text-area
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/text-area.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/text-area/text-area-skeleton.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/text-area/text-area.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-auto-grow, core-field, shared-element, shared-field, shared-form-control, shared-localize, shared-skeleton, shared-slots, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install class-variance-authority@0.7.1 @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-text-area.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/text-area.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-field, tw-field, tw-skeleton, tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/text-area';</script>

<ui-text-area label="Notes" name="notes"></ui-text-area>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiTextArea } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiTextArea label="Notes" name="notes" onInput={(e) => setNotes((e.target as HTMLTextAreaElement).value)} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { TextArea } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/text-area';

<TextArea label="Notes" name="notes" value={notes} onChange={(e) => setNotes(e.target.value)} />
```

- The element fires native `input` on every keystroke and `change` when the user leaves the field, so the React wrapper has `onInput` and `onChange`. The React + Tailwind `onChange` is React's own (every keystroke).

## Height

`rows` sets the starting height in lines, 4 by default as in Carbon. The user can drag the corner to make it taller (`resize: vertical`); a disabled field can't be resized.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-area label="Reason for the change" name="reason" rows="2"></ui-text-area>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextArea label="Reason for the change" name="reason" rows={2} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextArea label="Reason for the change" name="reason" rows={2} />
```

## Grow with the text

`auto-grow` starts at `rows` and grows a line at a time as the user types, with no resize handle. `max-rows` caps it; past that, the field scrolls. Carbon has no auto-grow.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-area label="Description" name="description" rows="2" auto-grow max-rows="6"></ui-text-area>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextArea label="Description" name="description" rows={2} autoGrow maxRows={6} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextArea label="Description" name="description" rows={2} autoGrow maxRows={6} />
```

## Count characters or words

`max-count` shows a counter above the field. As on the text input, it's a soft limit: going over turns the counter red, shows an error at once and blocks the form, but nothing is cut. Screen readers hear when the limit is near.

`counter-mode="word"` counts words instead (Carbon's `counterMode`). Thai has no spaces between words, so the field asks the browser's word segmenter for its language (`lang` on the field or the page): "สวัสดีครับ ผมชื่อสมชาย" is 5 words, where Carbon's count splits Thai at every vowel and tone mark. Numbers don't count as words.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-area label="Notes" name="notes" max-count="200"></ui-text-area>
<ui-text-area label="Summary" name="summary" max-count="50" counter-mode="word"></ui-text-area>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextArea label="Notes" name="notes" maxCount={200} />
<UiTextArea label="Summary" name="summary" maxCount={50} counterMode="word" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextArea label="Notes" name="notes" maxCount={200} />
<TextArea label="Summary" name="summary" maxCount={50} counterMode="word" />
```

Change the messages with `too-long-text` (`{max}` becomes the limit) and `near-limit-text`. For a hard limit that stops typing, use `maxlength`. More in [Forms and validation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/#count-characters-and-words).

## Your own counter messages

`too-long-text` is the error once the text is over the limit, and `near-limit-text` is what screen readers hear once when 10% or less is left. Write them for the field, so people know what to cut. This text is already too long, so the error shows at once.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-area label="Reason for rejection" name="rejectReason" rows="2" max-count="60" too-long-text="Keep the reason under {max} characters for the approval email" near-limit-text="Almost at the length the approval email allows" value="The rent is higher than the budget that finance approved for this year."></ui-text-area>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextArea
  label="Reason for rejection"
  name="rejectReason"
  rows={2}
  maxCount={60}
  tooLongText="Keep the reason under {max} characters for the approval email"
  nearLimitText="Almost at the length the approval email allows"
/>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextArea
  label="Reason for rejection"
  name="rejectReason"
  rows={2}
  maxCount={60}
  tooLongText="Keep the reason under {max} characters for the approval email"
  nearLimitText="Almost at the length the approval email allows"
/>
```

## Helper text, warnings and errors

Same as the text input: one line under the field, an error beats a warning, and a warning beats the helper text. The error and warning icons sit in the top-right corner of the field.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-area label="Delivery address" name="address" value="99/1 Rama IV Rd" warn warn-text="Add the district and postcode"></ui-text-area>
<ui-text-area label="Reason" name="reason" invalid invalid-text="Tell us why the contract ends early"></ui-text-area>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextArea label="Delivery address" name="address" value="99/1 Rama IV Rd" warn warnText="Add the district and postcode" />
<UiTextArea label="Reason" name="reason" invalid invalidText="Tell us why the contract ends early" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextArea label="Delivery address" name="address" defaultValue="99/1 Rama IV Rd" warn warnText="Add the district and postcode" />
<TextArea label="Reason" name="reason" invalid invalidText="Tell us why the contract ends early" />
```

`required`, `minlength` and `maxlength` work on the element as on `<textarea>`. In React + Tailwind, validation is your app's: pass `invalid` and `invalidText`. Everything else about errors: [Forms and validation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/).

## Label and helper text with markup

For a label or a message with markup, use the `label` and `helper-text` slots (`warn-text` and `invalid-text` work the same way). The React + Tailwind field takes the markup in `label` and `helperText`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-area name="scope" rows="3">
  <span slot="label">Scope of work <em>(part of the contract)</em></span>
  <span slot="helper-text">Put each service on <strong>its own line</strong></span>
</ui-text-area>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextArea name="scope" rows={3}>
  <span slot="label">Scope of work <em>(part of the contract)</em></span>
  <span slot="helper-text">Put each service on <strong>its own line</strong></span>
</UiTextArea>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextArea
  name="scope"
  rows={3}
  label={<>Scope of work <em>(part of the contract)</em></>}
  helperText={<>Put each service on <strong>its own line</strong></>}
/>
```

## Read-only, disabled and fluid

- `readonly` shows and submits the text, but the user can't change it. `disabled` greys it out; it isn't submitted.
- `fluid`, or a fluid form around it, puts the label inside the box (Carbon's `FluidTextArea`, see [fluid forms](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/#use-a-fluid-form)).


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-area label="Terms" value="Rent is paid on the first working day of each month." readonly></ui-text-area>
<ui-text-area label="Notes from legal" value="Reviewed on 2 October." rows="2" disabled></ui-text-area>
<ui-text-area label="Notes" name="notes" fluid></ui-text-area>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextArea label="Terms" value="Rent is paid on the first working day of each month." readonly />
<UiTextArea label="Notes from legal" value="Reviewed on 2 October." rows={2} disabled />
<UiTextArea label="Notes" name="notes" fluid />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextArea label="Terms" defaultValue="Rent is paid on the first working day of each month." readOnly />
<TextArea label="Notes from legal" defaultValue="Reviewed on 2 October." rows={2} disabled />
<TextArea label="Notes" name="notes" fluid />
```

## Check it in a form

In a `<form>`, `required` and `minlength` block the submit until the text is long enough, and the field shows its error. Try sending this form with a short reason.


HTML:

```html
<form id="text-area-form" method="dialog" style="display: grid; gap: 16px">
  <ui-text-area label="Reason for the change" name="reason" rows="3" required minlength="20" helper-text="At least 20 characters"></ui-text-area>
  <div><ui-button type="submit" size="md">Send for approval</ui-button></div>
</form>
<p>Sent: <output id="text-area-form-out"></output></p>
<script type="module">
  const form = document.getElementById('text-area-form');
  form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    document.getElementById('text-area-form-out').textContent = [...new FormData(form)].map(([key, value]) => `${key}=${value}`).join(', ');
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); sendForApproval(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }}>
  <UiTextArea label="Reason for the change" name="reason" rows={3} required minlength={20} helperText="At least 20 characters" />
  <UiButton type="submit" size="md">Send for approval</UiButton>
</form>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// your validation sets `reasonError`, as in Carbon React
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); sendForApproval(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }} noValidate>
  <TextArea label="Reason for the change" name="reason" rows={3} helperText="At least 20 characters" invalid={!!reasonError} invalidText={reasonError} />
  <Button type="submit" size="md">Send for approval</Button>
</form>
```

## Save a draft when the user leaves

`change` fires once the user leaves the field after changing it, so it is the moment to save a draft without a request on every keystroke.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-area id="text-area-draft" label="Meeting notes" name="minutes" rows="3"></ui-text-area>
<p>Draft: <output id="text-area-draft-out">not saved yet</output></p>
<script type="module">
  const minutes = document.getElementById('text-area-draft');
  minutes.addEventListener('change', () => {
    const time = new Date().toLocaleTimeString('en', { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });
    document.getElementById('text-area-draft-out').textContent = `saved at ${time}, ${minutes.value.length} characters`;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextArea label="Meeting notes" name="minutes" rows={3} onChange={(e) => saveDraft((e.target as HTMLTextAreaElement).value)} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// onChange runs on every keystroke here: save when the field loses focus
<TextArea label="Meeting notes" name="minutes" rows={3} onBlur={(e) => saveDraft(e.target.value)} />
```

## Skeleton

While the data of a form loads, `<ui-text-area-skeleton>` keeps the field's place: a label bar and a 100px field bar, or a fluid box with `fluid`. Screen readers skip it, so say "loading" on the form (for example `aria-busy="true"`).


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-area-skeleton></ui-text-area-skeleton>
<ui-text-area-skeleton fluid></ui-text-area-skeleton>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiTextAreaSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiTextAreaSkeleton />
<UiTextAreaSkeleton fluid />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { TextAreaSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/text-area';

<TextAreaSkeleton />
<TextAreaSkeleton fluid />
```

## Accessibility

- The label is a real `<label>` for the inner `<textarea>`, and the message line is its `aria-describedby`. `aria-label` on the element does not reach the textarea; use `label` (with `hide-label` if it must not show).
- Enter types a new line, as in any text area; it never submits the form.
- The counter is not read on every keystroke. Screen readers hear once when the limit is near and when it's passed.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Text area](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-text-area/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-text-area>` · React `UiTextArea`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | Visible label text; the `label` slot replaces it when markup is needed. |
| `hide-label` | `hideLabel` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep the label for screen readers but don't show it. |
| `helper-text` | `helperText` | `string` | `''` | Helper text under the field, shown while there is no error or warning. |
| `invalid-text` | `invalidText` | `string` | `''` | Error text shown while `invalid` or while the field fails validation. |
| `invalid` | `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Forces the error state, e.g. after server-side validation. |
| `warn` | `warn` | `boolean` | `false` | Non-blocking warning; shown when there is no error. |
| `warn-text` | `warnText` | `string` | `''` | Text of the warning shown while `warn`. |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `''` | Reflected: form-associated elements submit under the `name` attribute. |
| `placeholder` | `placeholder` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `rows` | `rows` | `number` | `4` | Initial number of text rows (Carbon default 4); the user can still resize. |
| `minlength` | `minlength` | `number \| undefined` |  |  |
| `maxlength` | `maxlength` | `number \| undefined` |  |  |
| `autocomplete` | `autocomplete` | `string` | `''` | Passed to the textarea (`off`, or an autofill token). |
| `inputmode` | `inputmode` | `string` | `''` | Passed to the text box: the virtual keyboard to show (`numeric`, `decimal`, `email`, `tel`, `url`, `search`…). |
| `enterkeyhint` | `enterkeyhint` | `string` | `''` | Passed to the text box: the label of the virtual keyboard's Enter key (`search`, `send`, `next`, `done`…). |
| `max-count` | `maxCount` | `number \| undefined` |  | Soft limit with a visible counter (unlike maxlength, extra text isn't blocked). |
| `counter-mode` | `counterMode` | `CounterMode` | `'character'` | What `max-count` counts: `character` (default) or `word` (Carbon `counterMode`). |
| `auto-grow` | `autoGrow` | `boolean` | `false` | Grows with the text from `rows` (no Carbon counterpart); `max-rows` caps it, then it scrolls. |
| `max-rows` | `maxRows` | `number \| undefined` |  | The most lines `auto-grow` shows before scrolling (default: no cap). |
| `too-long-text` | `tooLongText` | `string` | `''` | Error when over `max-count`; `{max}` is replaced with the limit (default: the translation's, for characters or words). |
| `near-limit-text` | `nearLimitText` | `string` | `''` | Announced once when what is left of the limit drops to 10% or less. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the control; a disabled `<fieldset>` ancestor does the same. |
| `readonly` | `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows and submits the value but blocks changes. |
| `fluid` | `fluid` | `boolean` | `false` | Carbon `FluidTextArea`: the label inside a 64px box, an error / warning inside it. `<ui-fluid-form>` sets it for every field inside. |
| `required` | `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Blocks form submission while the field is empty. |

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `willValidate` |  | (read-only) Whether the field takes part in constraint validation (not while disabled), as natively. |
| `labels` |  | (read-only) The `<label>`s that point at this field. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `setCustomValidity(message)` | Like `<input>.setCustomValidity()`: a non-empty message makes the field invalid (and is shown as its error once touched) until cleared with ''. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `change` | `onChange` | Re-dispatched from the native textarea (native change is not composed) |

#### CSS custom properties
