| `--ui-field-background` |  | Fill of the box (default `--ui-surface-1`; Kanok: transparent) |
| `--ui-label-font` |  | Font of the label (default `--ui-font-caption`; Kanok: 14px semibold) |
| `--ui-label-color` |  | Colour of the label (default `--ui-ink-muted`; Kanok: `--ui-ink`) |
| `--ui-field-readonly-background` |  | The box's fill when read-only (default transparent; Kanok: a faint ink tint, so read-only reads as set and never weaker than disabled) |
| `--ui-fluid-background` |  | / --ui-fluid-gap - A fluid box's fill and the space under it (default the layer's fill, 0: boxes that touch; Kanok: transparent, 8px) |




---

# Number input

A number input takes a number: a quantity, an amount, a percentage. Carbon's − and + buttons sit at the end of the field, and ↑ / ↓ step from the keyboard.


HTML:

```html
<ui-number-input label="Number of units" name="units" value="1" min="1" max="20"></ui-number-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNumberInput label="Number of units" name="units" value="1" min={1} max={20} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<NumberInput label="Number of units" name="units" defaultValue={1} min={1} max={20} />
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/number-input
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-number-input
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/number-input.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/number-input/number-input-skeleton.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/number-input/number-input.styles.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/number-input/number-input.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-number-format, shared-affixes, shared-element, shared-field, shared-form-control, shared-localize, shared-skeleton, shared-slots, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-number-input.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/number-input.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-field, tw-affix, tw-field, tw-i18n, tw-refs, tw-skeleton, tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/number-input';</script>

<ui-number-input label="Number of units" name="units" min="1" max="20"></ui-number-input>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiNumberInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiNumberInput label="Number of units" name="units" min={1} max={20} onChange={(e) => setUnits((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value)} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { NumberInput } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/number-input';

<NumberInput label="Number of units" name="units" min={1} max={20} value={units} onChange={setUnits} />
```

- The value is text, so the field can be empty: `"12"`, `"0.5"`, or `""`. The element's `valueAsNumber` gives the number (`NaN` while empty).
- The element fires `input` on every keystroke or step, and `change` when the value is committed (leaving the field, Enter, a step). The React wrapper has `onInput` and `onChange`.
- The React + Tailwind `onChange` gets the new value as text, not an event.

## Step, minimum and maximum

`step` (1 by default) is how far − / + and ↑ / ↓ move. A step stays within `min` and `max`, and the button at the end of the range turns off. A value typed outside the range is an error.

From an empty field, the first step goes to `step-start-value` if you set one; otherwise to `min` when only a minimum is set, else to 1 or −1, as in Carbon.


HTML:

```html
<ui-number-input label="Rent increase" name="increase" value="3" min="0" max="10" step="0.5" suffix-text="%"></ui-number-input>
<ui-number-input label="Floor" name="floor" min="1" step-start-value="10"></ui-number-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNumberInput label="Rent increase" name="increase" value="3" min={0} max={10} step={0.5} suffixText="%" />
<UiNumberInput label="Floor" name="floor" min={1} stepStartValue={10} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<NumberInput label="Rent increase" name="increase" defaultValue={3} min={0} max={10} step={0.5} suffixText="%" />
<NumberInput label="Floor" name="floor" min={1} stepStartValue={10} />
```

## Decimals

A step rounds to the decimals of the value or of `step`, whichever has more, so 0.1 + 0.2 shows `0.3`, not `0.30000000000000004`. With the default `type="number"`, `step` is also the precision the browser accepts: with `step="0.01"`, `12.345` is an error.


HTML:

```html
<ui-number-input label="Interest rate" name="rate" value="2.75" step="0.01" min="0" suffix-text="% a year"></ui-number-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNumberInput label="Interest rate" name="rate" value="2.75" step={0.01} min={0} suffixText="% a year" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<NumberInput label="Interest rate" name="rate" defaultValue="2.75" step={0.01} min={0} suffixText="% a year" />
```

## Currency, units and number formats

`prefix-text` and `suffix-text` put text inside the field, before or after the number: `฿`, `kg`, `baht a month`. They stay in view while the user types and aren't part of the value. They have no Carbon counterpart.

For Carbon's formatted field, set `type="text"` with `format-options`, which takes any `Intl.NumberFormat` options: thousands separators, currency, percent, units. The text is free while the user types and is formatted when they leave. The value stays a plain number: `฿1,234.50` submits `1234.5`, and a percent style gives the fraction (`0.5` for 50%). The locale is the page language, or `locale`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-number-input label="Deposit" name="deposit" value="45000" min="0" prefix-text="฿"></ui-number-input>
<ui-number-input label="Monthly rent" name="rent" type="text" value="18500" format-options='{"style":"currency","currency":"THB"}'></ui-number-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNumberInput label="Deposit" name="deposit" value="45000" min={0} prefixText="฿" />
<UiNumberInput label="Monthly rent" name="rent" type="text" value="18500" formatOptions={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'THB' }} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<NumberInput label="Deposit" name="deposit" defaultValue={45000} min={0} prefixText="฿" />
<NumberInput label="Monthly rent" name="rent" type="text" defaultValue={18500} formatOptions={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'THB' }} />
```

## Percent and units

With `format-options`, the percent sign or the unit is part of the formatted text, which is Carbon's way. A percent style stores the fraction: 7.5% is `0.075`, so give `step`, `min` and `max` as fractions too. `locale` picks the number format when it must not follow the page.


HTML:

```html
<ui-number-input label="Discount" name="discount" type="text" value="0.075" step="0.005" min="0" max="1" format-options='{"style":"percent","maximumFractionDigits":1}' helper-text="7.5% submits 0.075"></ui-number-input>
<ui-number-input label="Cargo weight" name="weight" type="text" value="1250.5" step="0.5" min="0" format-options='{"style":"unit","unit":"kilogram"}'></ui-number-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNumberInput label="Discount" name="discount" type="text" value="0.075" step={0.005} min={0} max={1} formatOptions={{ style: 'percent', maximumFractionDigits: 1 }} helperText="7.5% submits 0.075" />
<UiNumberInput label="Cargo weight" name="weight" type="text" value="1250.5" step={0.5} min={0} formatOptions={{ style: 'unit', unit: 'kilogram' }} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<NumberInput label="Discount" name="discount" type="text" defaultValue={0.075} step={0.005} min={0} max={1} formatOptions={{ style: 'percent', maximumFractionDigits: 1 }} helperText="7.5% submits 0.075" />
<NumberInput label="Cargo weight" name="weight" type="text" defaultValue={1250.5} step={0.5} min={0} formatOptions={{ style: 'unit', unit: 'kilogram' }} />
```

## Empty fields

As in Carbon, an empty number input counts as missing, even without `required`: the form won't submit until there is a number. Set `allow-empty` on a field that may stay empty.


HTML:

```html
<ui-number-input label="Parking spaces (optional)" name="parking" min="0" allow-empty></ui-number-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNumberInput label="Parking spaces (optional)" name="parking" min={0} allowEmpty />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<NumberInput label="Parking spaces (optional)" name="parking" min={0} allowEmpty />
```

## Steppers and the mouse wheel

- `hide-steppers` removes the − / + buttons; ↑ / ↓ still step.
- `disable-wheel` stops the mouse wheel from changing a focused field, which is easy to do by accident while scrolling a long form.
- `decrement-label` and `increment-label` rename the buttons for screen readers ("Decrement number" and "Increment number" by default, translated).


HTML:

```html
<ui-number-input label="Year built" name="year" value="2019" min="1900" max="2026" hide-steppers disable-wheel></ui-number-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNumberInput label="Year built" name="year" value="2019" min={1900} max={2026} hideSteppers disableWheel />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<NumberInput label="Year built" name="year" defaultValue={2019} min={1900} max={2026} hideSteppers disableWheel />
```

## Sizes, messages, read-only and disabled

- `size`: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (the default), `lg` 48px.
- `helper-text`, `warn` + `warn-text` and `invalid` + `invalid-text` work as on the [text input](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/text-input/#helper-text-warnings-and-errors). A value outside `min` / `max` gets the browser's or the built-in message unless you set `invalid-text`. More in [Forms and validation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/).
- `readonly` shows and submits the number, and the steppers turn off. `disabled` greys it out; it isn't submitted.


HTML:

```html
<ui-number-input label="Guests" name="guests" value="12" warn warn-text="The room seats 10"></ui-number-input>
<ui-number-input label="Team size" name="team" value="42" min="1" max="30" invalid invalid-text="At most 30 people"></ui-number-input>
<ui-number-input label="Contract length" name="months" value="24" suffix-text="months" readonly></ui-number-input>
<ui-number-input label="Floors" name="floors" value="3" size="sm" disabled></ui-number-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNumberInput label="Guests" name="guests" value="12" warn warnText="The room seats 10" />
<UiNumberInput label="Team size" name="team" value="42" min={1} max={30} invalid invalidText="At most 30 people" />
<UiNumberInput label="Contract length" name="months" value="24" suffixText="months" readonly />
<UiNumberInput label="Floors" name="floors" value="3" size="sm" disabled />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<NumberInput label="Guests" name="guests" defaultValue={12} warn warnText="The room seats 10" />
<NumberInput label="Team size" name="team" defaultValue={42} min={1} max={30} invalid invalidText="At most 30 people" />
<NumberInput label="Contract length" name="months" defaultValue={24} suffixText="months" readOnly />
<NumberInput label="Floors" name="floors" defaultValue={3} size="sm" disabled />
```

## Fluid

`fluid` (Carbon's `FluidNumberInput`), or a `<ui-fluid-form>` around the field, puts the label inside a 64px box; an error or a warning shows inside the box, and there is no helper text. See [fluid forms](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/#use-a-fluid-form).


HTML:

```html
<ui-number-input label="Monthly rent" name="rent" value="18500" min="0" step="500" prefix-text="฿" fluid></ui-number-input>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNumberInput label="Monthly rent" name="rent" value="18500" min={0} step={500} prefixText="฿" fluid />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<NumberInput label="Monthly rent" name="rent" defaultValue={18500} min={0} step={500} prefixText="฿" fluid />
```

## Work out a total

Listen to `input` to update a total on every keystroke and every step. `valueAsNumber` gives the number, or `NaN` while the field is empty.


HTML:

```html
<ui-number-input id="number-input-qty" label="Units" name="qty" value="2" min="1" max="50"></ui-number-input>
<ui-number-input id="number-input-price" label="Price per unit" name="price" value="1500" min="0" step="100" prefix-text="฿"></ui-number-input>
<p>Total: <output id="number-input-total"></output></p>
<script type="module">
  const qty = document.getElementById('number-input-qty');
  const price = document.getElementById('number-input-price');
  const baht = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { style: 'currency', currency: 'THB' });
  const update = () => {
    const total = qty.valueAsNumber * price.valueAsNumber;
    document.getElementById('number-input-total').textContent = Number.isNaN(total) ? '–' : baht.format(total);
  };
  qty.addEventListener('input', update);
  price.addEventListener('input', update);
  update();
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNumberInput label="Units" name="qty" value={qty} min={1} max={50} onInput={(e) => setQty((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value)} />
<UiNumberInput label="Price per unit" name="price" value={price} min={0} step={100} prefixText="฿" onInput={(e) => setPrice((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value)} />
<p>Total: {baht.format(Number(qty) * Number(price))}</p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<NumberInput label="Units" name="qty" value={qty} min={1} max={50} onChange={setQty} />
<NumberInput label="Price per unit" name="price" value={price} min={0} step={100} prefixText="฿" onChange={setPrice} />
<p>Total: {baht.format(Number(qty) * Number(price))}</p>
```

## In a form

With a `name`, the field submits a plain number: the formatted rent `฿18,500.00` below submits `18500`. A value outside `min` / `max`, or an empty field without `allow-empty`, blocks the submit and shows its error. Try 72 months.


HTML:

```html
<form id="number-input-form" method="dialog" style="display: grid; gap: 16px">
  <ui-number-input label="Monthly rent" name="rent" type="text" value="18500" min="0" format-options='{"style":"currency","currency":"THB"}'></ui-number-input>
  <ui-number-input label="Contract length" name="months" value="12" min="1" max="60" suffix-text="months"></ui-number-input>
  <div><ui-button type="submit" size="md">Save terms</ui-button></div>
</form>
<p>Sent: <output id="number-input-form-out"></output></p>
<script type="module">
  const form = document.getElementById('number-input-form');
  form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    document.getElementById('number-input-form-out').textContent = [...new FormData(form)].map(([key, value]) => `${key}=${value}`).join(', ');
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); saveTerms(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }}>
  <UiNumberInput label="Monthly rent" name="rent" type="text" value="18500" min={0} formatOptions={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'THB' }} />
  <UiNumberInput label="Contract length" name="months" value="12" min={1} max={60} suffixText="months" />
  <UiButton type="submit" size="md">Save terms</UiButton>
</form>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); saveTerms(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }}>
  <NumberInput label="Monthly rent" name="rent" type="text" defaultValue={18500} min={0} formatOptions={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'THB' }} />
  <NumberInput label="Contract length" name="months" defaultValue={12} min={1} max={60} suffixText="months" />
  <Button type="submit" size="md">Save terms</Button>
</form>
```

## Skeleton

While the data of a form loads, `<ui-number-input-skeleton>` keeps the field's place: a label bar and a field bar at its `size`, or a fluid box with `fluid`. Screen readers skip it, so say "loading" on the form (for example `aria-busy="true"`).


HTML:

```html
<ui-number-input-skeleton></ui-number-input-skeleton>
<ui-number-input-skeleton fluid></ui-number-input-skeleton>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiNumberInputSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiNumberInputSkeleton />
<UiNumberInputSkeleton fluid />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { NumberInputSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/number-input';

<NumberInputSkeleton />
<NumberInputSkeleton fluid />
```

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| ↑ / ↓ | One step up or down, within `min` / `max` |
| Enter | Commits the value and submits the form the field sits in |

The − / + buttons are out of the Tab order, as in Carbon: the arrow keys do the same from the field.

## Accessibility

- The label is a real `<label>` for the inner `<input>`; the prefix, the suffix and the message line are its description.
- The − / + buttons have names ("Decrement number", "Increment number") and turn off at the end of the range.
- `inputmode="decimal"` brings up a keyboard with a decimal point on phones.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Number input](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-number-input/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-number-input>` · React `UiNumberInput`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | Visible label text; the `label` slot replaces it when markup is needed. |
| `hide-label` | `hideLabel` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep the label for screen readers but don't show it. |
| `helper-text` | `helperText` | `string` | `''` | Helper text under the field, shown while there is no error or warning. |
| `invalid-text` | `invalidText` | `string` | `''` | Error text shown while `invalid` or while the field fails validation. |
| `invalid` | `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Forces the error state, e.g. after server-side validation. |
| `warn` | `warn` | `boolean` | `false` | Non-blocking warning; shown when there is no error. |
| `warn-text` | `warnText` | `string` | `''` | Text of the warning shown while `warn`. |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` | The field text; `valueAsNumber` gives the parsed number (NaN while empty or invalid). |
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `''` | Reflected: form-associated elements submit under the `name` attribute. |
| `placeholder` | `placeholder` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `prefix-text` | `prefixText` | `string` | `''` | Text inside the field before the value, e.g. a currency (`฿`); not part of `value`. Part of the field's description for screen readers. |
| `suffix-text` | `suffixText` | `string` | `''` | Text inside the field after the value, e.g. a unit (`kg`); not part of `value`. Part of the field's description for screen readers. |
| `min` | `min` | `number \| undefined` |  |  |
| `max` | `max` | `number \| undefined` |  |  |
| `step` | `step` | `number` | `1` | Step of the ± buttons and ↑ / ↓; with `type="number"` also the allowed precision. |
| `step-start-value` | `stepStartValue` | `number` | `0` | Where the steppers start from an empty field (Carbon `stepStartValue`); 0 = Carbon's rule: ±1, or `min` when only a minimum is set. |
| `type` | `type` | `NumberInputType` | `'number'` | `number`: a native number field. `text`: a text field formatted for `locale` with `format-options` (Carbon `type="text"`). |
| `locale` | `locale` | `string` | `''` | BCP 47 locale of the formatting with `type="text"`; empty = the page language (`lang` on the element, an ancestor or `<html>`), as `ui-date-picker`. |
| `format-options` | `formatOptions` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` | `{}` | `Intl.NumberFormat` options with `type="text"`, e.g. `{"style":"currency","currency":"THB"}` or `{"maximumFractionDigits":2}`. |
| `allow-empty` | `allowEmpty` | `boolean` | `false` | An empty field is valid (Carbon `allowEmpty`); otherwise empty counts as missing. |
| `hide-steppers` | `hideSteppers` | `boolean` | `false` | Remove the − / + buttons (keyboard stepping still works). |
| `disable-wheel` | `disableWheel` | `boolean` | `false` | Ignore mouse-wheel changes while focused (Carbon `disableWheel`). |
| `size` | `size` | `NumberInputSize` | `'md'` | Field height: sm 32px, md 40px, lg 48px (tokens `--ui-field-height-*`). |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the control; a disabled `<fieldset>` ancestor does the same. |
| `readonly` | `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows and submits the value but blocks changes. |
| `fluid` | `fluid` | `boolean` | `false` | Carbon `FluidNumberInput`: the label inside a 64px box, an error / warning inside it. `<ui-fluid-form>` sets it for every field inside. |
| `required` | `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Blocks form submission while the field is empty. |
| `decrement-label` | `decrementLabel` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name of the − button. |
| `increment-label` | `incrementLabel` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name of the + button. |

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `valueAsNumber` |  | (read-only) The parsed value, NaN while empty or not a number. |
| `willValidate` |  | (read-only) Whether the field takes part in constraint validation (not while disabled), as natively. |
| `labels` |  | (read-only) The `<label>`s that point at this field. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `setCustomValidity(message)` | Like `<input>.setCustomValidity()`: a non-empty message makes the field invalid (and is shown as its error once touched) until cleared with ''. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `change` | `onChange` | After a committed change (blur / Enter / stepper; with `type="text"`, on blur when the number changed) |
| `input` | `onInput` | On every keystroke or stepper click |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| `label` | Label content with markup; the `label` attribute is the plain-text fallback |
| `helper-text` | Helper text with markup (links, bold); overrides `helper-text` |
| `warn-text` | Warning text shown while `warn`; overrides `warn-text` |
| `invalid-text` | Error text shown while invalid; overrides `invalid-text` |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The field box |
| `label` | The label |
| `input` | The native input |
| `prefix` | The text before the value |
| `suffix` | The text after the value |
| `controls` | The stepper group |
| `decrement-button` | The − button |
| `increment-button` | The + button |
| `status-icon` | The error / warning icon |
| `helper-text` | The helper line |
| `warning-text` | The warning line |
| `warn-text` | Same line as `warning-text` (named after the `warn-text` attribute / slot) |
| `error-text` | The error line |
| `invalid-text` | Same line as `error-text` (named after the `invalid-text` attribute / slot) |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-field-border` |  | Border on every side of the box (default none: Carbon's underline only; Kanok: a 1px outline) |
| `--ui-field-disabled-border-color` |  | Border colour when disabled (default: the underline transparent) |
| `--ui-field-readonly-border-color` |  | Border colour when read-only (default: a hairline underline) |
| `--ui-field-radius` |  | Corner radius of the box (default 0; Kanok: 6px) |
| `--ui-field-background` |  | Fill of the box (default `--ui-surface-1`; Kanok: transparent) |
| `--ui-label-font` |  | Font of the label (default `--ui-font-caption`; Kanok: 14px semibold) |
| `--ui-label-color` |  | Colour of the label (default `--ui-ink-muted`; Kanok: `--ui-ink`) |
| `--ui-field-readonly-background` |  | The box's fill when read-only (default transparent; Kanok: a faint ink tint, so read-only reads as set and never weaker than disabled) |
| `--ui-fluid-background` |  | / --ui-fluid-gap - A fluid box's fill and the space under it (default the layer's fill, 0: boxes that touch; Kanok: transparent, 8px) |
| `--ui-icon-control-radius` |  | Corners of its small icon buttons, their hover fill and ring (default 0; Kanok: round) |




---

# Search

A search field lets people find or filter content by typing. Carbon hides its label and shows a magnifier instead; a clear button appears once there is text.


HTML:

```html
<ui-search label="Search contracts" placeholder="Search by name or number"></ui-search>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSearch label="Search contracts" placeholder="Search by name or number" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Search label="Search contracts" placeholder="Search by name or number" />
```

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui

```

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/search';</script>

<ui-search label="Search contracts" name="q"></ui-search>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiSearch } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiSearch label="Search contracts" name="q" onInput={(e) => setQuery((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value)} onUiClear={() => setQuery('')} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Search } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/search';

<Search label="Search contracts" name="q" value={query} onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)} />
```

- The element fires `input` on every keystroke, `change` when the value is committed (leaving the field, Enter) or cleared, and `ui-clear` after the clear button or Esc emptied it.
- In React + Tailwind, clearing empties the field with a real `input` event, so your `onChange` sees it; `onClear` runs after.
- Always give it a `label`, even though it doesn't show: it names the search landmark and the field ("Search" when you leave it out).

## Sizes

`size`: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (the default), `lg` 48px. Match the height of what sits next to it, such as a table toolbar or a button.


HTML:

```html
<ui-search label="Search" size="sm" placeholder="Small"></ui-search>
<ui-search label="Search" placeholder="Medium"></ui-search>
<ui-search label="Search" size="lg" placeholder="Large"></ui-search>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSearch label="Search" size="sm" placeholder="Small" />
<UiSearch label="Search" placeholder="Medium" />
<UiSearch label="Search" size="lg" placeholder="Large" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Search label="Search" size="sm" placeholder="Small" />
<Search label="Search" placeholder="Medium" />
<Search label="Search" size="lg" placeholder="Large" />
```

## Clear the text

The × button appears once there is text and empties the field, keeping focus in it. Esc does the same from the keyboard. On an empty field Esc does nothing, so a dialog around the search can still close on Esc. `clear-label` renames the button ("Clear search input" by default, translated).


HTML:

```html
<ui-search label="Search tenants" value="Somchai" clear-label="Clear tenant search"></ui-search>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSearch label="Search tenants" value="Somchai" clearLabel="Clear tenant search" onUiClear={() => resetResults()} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Search label="Search tenants" defaultValue="Somchai" clearLabel="Clear tenant search" onClear={() => resetResults()} />
```

## Filter a list as you type

For a short list that is already on the page, filter it on `input`. It fires on every keystroke and when the field is cleared, so one listener keeps the list in step.


HTML:

```html
<ui-search id="search-departments" label="Filter departments" placeholder="Filter departments"></ui-search>
<ul id="search-departments-list">
  <li>Legal</li>
  <li>Finance</li>
  <li>Procurement</li>
  <li>Human resources</li>
  <li>Facilities</li>
</ul>
<p>Showing <output id="search-departments-out">5</output> of 5</p>
<script type="module">
  const search = document.getElementById('search-departments');
  const items = [...document.querySelectorAll('#search-departments-list li')];
  search.addEventListener('input', () => {
    const query = search.value.trim().toLowerCase();
    let shown = 0;
    for (const item of items) {
      item.hidden = !item.textContent.toLowerCase().includes(query);
      if (!item.hidden) shown += 1;
    }
    document.getElementById('search-departments-out').textContent = shown;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const shown = departments.filter((name) => name.toLowerCase().includes(query.trim().toLowerCase()));

<UiSearch label="Filter departments" placeholder="Filter departments" onInput={(e) => setQuery((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value)} />
<ul>{shown.map((name) => <li key={name}>{name}</li>)}</ul>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const shown = departments.filter((name) => name.toLowerCase().includes(query.trim().toLowerCase()));

<Search label="Filter departments" placeholder="Filter departments" value={query} onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)} />
<ul>{shown.map((name) => <li key={name}>{name}</li>)}</ul>
```

## Expandable search

`expandable` (Carbon's `ExpandableSearch`) shows only the magnifier until someone clicks it or presses Enter or Space; then it opens to its full width with focus in the field. Leaving it empty, or Esc on an empty field, closes it again. `expanded` is the state: set it to open the search from your code. Each open or close fires `ui-toggle` with `detail.expanded`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-search label="Search the table" expandable></ui-search>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSearch label="Search the table" expandable onUiToggle={(e) => setOpen(e.detail.expanded)} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// or <Search expandable … />
<ExpandableSearch label="Search the table" onExpandedChange={setOpen} />
```

The magnifier is a button named by the `label`, with the label as its tooltip. `ExpandableSearch` comes with the same `tw-search` file.

## Open with an earlier search

An expandable search with text stays open: it closes only when it's empty. Set `expanded` and `value` together to show a search the user ran before, such as a table filter kept in the address. Clear it and leave the field, and it closes.


HTML:

```html
<ui-search id="search-table" label="Search the table" expandable expanded value="lease"></ui-search>
<p>Open: <output id="search-table-out">yes</output></p>
<script type="module">
  document.getElementById('search-table').addEventListener('ui-toggle', (event) => {
    document.getElementById('search-table-out').textContent = event.detail.expanded ? 'yes' : 'no';
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSearch label="Search the table" expandable expanded={open} value={query} onUiToggle={(e) => setOpen(e.detail.expanded)} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ExpandableSearch label="Search the table" defaultExpanded defaultValue="lease" onExpandedChange={setOpen} />
```

## Fluid

`fluid` (Carbon's `FluidSearch`), or a `<ui-fluid-form>` around it, shows the label inside a 64px box, so the search lines up with the other fluid fields of a form.


HTML:

```html
<ui-search label="Search suppliers" name="supplier" placeholder="Name or tax ID" fluid></ui-search>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSearch label="Search suppliers" name="supplier" placeholder="Name or tax ID" fluid />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Search label="Search suppliers" name="supplier" placeholder="Name or tax ID" fluid />
```

## Read-only and disabled

`readonly` keeps the text, still submits it and hides the clear button: use it to show the search behind a saved report. `disabled` greys the field out, for a search that can't be used yet.


HTML:

```html
<ui-search label="Search contracts" name="q" value="lease" readonly></ui-search>
<ui-search label="Search archived contracts" value="2019" disabled></ui-search>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSearch label="Search contracts" name="q" value="lease" readonly />
<UiSearch label="Search archived contracts" value="2019" disabled />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Search label="Search contracts" name="q" defaultValue="lease" readOnly />
<Search label="Search archived contracts" defaultValue="2019" disabled />
```

## In a form

- Give it a `name` and it submits like `<input type="search">`. Enter submits the form it sits in.
- `required`, `pattern`, `minlength` and `maxlength` work as on a native search input. Carbon's search has no error line, so a failed check shows the browser's bubble.
- `readonly` keeps the text and hides the clear button. `disabled` greys the field out.
- `fluid`, or a fluid form around it, shows the label inside a 64px box (Carbon's `FluidSearch`).

Type at least two characters and press Enter.


HTML:

```html
<form id="search-form" method="dialog">
  <ui-search label="Search contracts" name="q" minlength="2" placeholder="Contract name or number"></ui-search>
</form>
<p>Searched for: <output id="search-form-out"></output></p>
<script type="module">
  const form = document.getElementById('search-form');
  form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    document.getElementById('search-form-out').textContent = new FormData(form).get('q');
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); runSearch(new FormData(e.currentTarget).get('q')); }}>
  <UiSearch label="Search contracts" name="q" minlength={2} placeholder="Contract name or number" />
</form>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); runSearch(new FormData(e.currentTarget).get('q')); }}>
  <Search label="Search contracts" name="q" minLength={2} placeholder="Contract name or number" />
</form>
```

## Skeleton

While the results load, `<ui-search-skeleton>` keeps the search's place: one bar at its `size`, or a fluid box with `fluid`. Screen readers skip it, so say "loading" on the area around it (for example `aria-busy="true"`).


HTML:

```html
<ui-search-skeleton></ui-search-skeleton>
<ui-search-skeleton fluid></ui-search-skeleton>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiSearchSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiSearchSkeleton />
<UiSearchSkeleton fluid />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { SearchSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/search';

<SearchSkeleton />
<SearchSkeleton fluid />
```

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| Esc | Clears the text and keeps focus in the field; on an empty expandable search, closes it and focuses the magnifier |
| Enter | Commits the value and submits the form the search sits in |
| Enter or Space on the magnifier | Opens an expandable search |
| Tab | Moves to the clear button while there is text (it's skipped when there is nothing to clear) |

## Accessibility

- It's a `role="search"` landmark named by its label, so screen reader users can jump to it.
- The label is hidden on screen, as in Carbon, but the field and the landmark use it. `aria-label` on the element doesn't reach the inner input; use `label`.
- Pressing the clear button keeps focus in the field, so keyboard users can type again right away.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Search](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-search/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-search>` · React `UiSearch`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name of the field (visually hidden, as in Carbon). |
| `placeholder` | `placeholder` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `''` | Reflected: form-associated elements submit under the `name` attribute. |
| `size` | `size` | `SearchSize` | `'md'` | Field height: sm 32px, md 40px, lg 48px (tokens `--ui-field-height-*`). |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the control; a disabled `<fieldset>` ancestor does the same. |
| `autocomplete` | `autocomplete` | `string` | `'off'` |  |
| `inputmode` | `inputmode` | `string` | `''` | Passed to the text box: the virtual keyboard to show (`numeric`, `decimal`, `email`, `tel`, `url`, `search`…). |
| `enterkeyhint` | `enterkeyhint` | `string` | `''` | Passed to the text box: the label of the virtual keyboard's Enter key (`search`, `send`, `next`, `done`…). |
| `clear-label` | `clearLabel` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name of the clear button. |
| `required` | `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Constraint validation like `<input type="search">`: blocks submit and reports in the browser's bubble (Carbon Search has no error line). |
| `pattern` | `pattern` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `minlength` | `minlength` | `number \| undefined` |  |  |
| `maxlength` | `maxlength` | `number \| undefined` |  |  |
| `readonly` | `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | Value can be selected and submitted but not changed; no clear button. |
| `fluid` | `fluid` | `boolean` | `false` | Carbon `FluidSearch`: the label inside a 64px box. `<ui-fluid-form>` sets it for every field inside. |
| `expandable` | `expandable` | `boolean` | `false` | Carbon `ExpandableSearch`: collapsed to its magnifier until opened. |
| `expanded` | `expanded` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether an expandable search is open. |

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `willValidate` |  | (read-only) Whether the field takes part in constraint validation (not while disabled), as natively. |
| `labels` |  | (read-only) The `<label>`s that point at this field. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `setCustomValidity(message)` | Like `<input>.setCustomValidity()`: a non-empty message makes the field invalid until cleared with ''. |
| `clear()` | Empties the field, keeps focus in it and announces the change (`input`, `change`, `ui-clear`). |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `change` | `onChange` | When the value is committed (blur / Enter) or cleared |
| `ui-toggle` | `onUiToggle` | detail: { expanded } when an expandable search opens or collapses |
| `input` | `onInput` | On every keystroke |
| `ui-clear` | `onUiClear` | After the clear button or Esc emptied the field |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The role=search wrapper |
| `input` | The native search input |
| `label` | The label (visually hidden, as in Carbon; shown inside the box when `fluid`) |
| `magnifier` | The search icon |
| `clear-button` | The clear button |
| `magnifier-button` | The magnifier of an expandable search |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-field-border` |  | Border on every side of the box (default none: Carbon's underline only; Kanok: a 1px outline) |
| `--ui-field-disabled-border-color` |  | Border colour when disabled (default: the underline transparent) |
| `--ui-field-readonly-border-color` |  | Border colour when read-only (default: a hairline underline) |
| `--ui-field-radius` |  | Corner radius of the box (default 0; Kanok: 6px) |
| `--ui-field-background` |  | Fill of the box (default `--ui-surface-1`; Kanok: transparent) |
| `--ui-label-font` |  | Font of the label (default `--ui-font-caption`; Kanok: 14px semibold) |
| `--ui-label-color` |  | Colour of the label (default `--ui-ink-muted`; Kanok: `--ui-ink`) |
| `--ui-icon-control-radius` |  | Corners of its small icon buttons, their hover fill and ring (default 0; Kanok: round) |

# Select

A select picks one option from a list. It wraps the browser's own `<select>`, so phones open their native picker and screen readers know it well.


HTML:

```html
<ui-select label="Department" name="department" placeholder="Choose a department" helper-text="Where the contract is filed">
  <option value="sales">Sales</option>
  <option value="legal">Legal</option>
  <option value="finance">Finance</option>
</ui-select>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSelect label="Department" name="department" placeholder="Choose a department" helperText="Where the contract is filed">
  <option value="sales">Sales</option>
  <option value="legal">Legal</option>
  <option value="finance">Finance</option>
</UiSelect>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Select label="Department" name="department" placeholder="Choose a department" helperText="Where the contract is filed">
  <option value="sales">Sales</option>
  <option value="legal">Legal</option>
  <option value="finance">Finance</option>
</Select>
```

## Select, Dropdown, Combobox or MultiSelect?

| Component | Use it when |
|---|---|
| [Select](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/select/) | A plain form field. The browser draws the list: the native picker on phones, the most familiar control for screen readers. Options are one line of text. |
| [Dropdown](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/dropdown/) | The list must look the same in every browser, or options need a second line (`data-description`). |
| [Combobox](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/combobox/) | The list is long and typing is faster than scrolling, the options come from a server search, or free text is allowed. |
| [Multi-select](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/multi-select/) | The user picks several values. |

For two to five options that should all stay visible, use a [radio group](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/radio/) (one choice) or [checkboxes](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/checkbox/) (several).

## Placeholder and starting value

`placeholder` adds an empty first choice in a muted colour. With `required`, the user has to pick something else before the form submits.

Without a placeholder, the select starts on `value`, else on the `<option selected>`, else on the first option, as a native select does. Reset goes back to that starting value. `change` fires when the user picks an option.


HTML:

```html
<ui-select id="select-currency" label="Currency" name="currency" value="thb">
  <option value="usd">US dollar</option>
  <option value="thb">Thai baht</option>
  <option value="eur">Euro</option>
</ui-select>
<p>Value: <output id="select-currency-out"></output></p>

<script type="module">
  const currency = document.getElementById('select-currency');
  const out = document.getElementById('select-currency-out');
  out.value = currency.value;
  currency.addEventListener('change', () => (out.value = currency.value));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
import type { UiSelect as SelectElement } from '@purpurabog/ui';

const [currency, setCurrency] = useState('thb');

<UiSelect label="Currency" name="currency" value={currency} onChange={(e) => setCurrency((e.target as SelectElement).value)}>
  <option value="usd">US dollar</option>
  <option value="thb">Thai baht</option>
  <option value="eur">Euro</option>
</UiSelect>
<p>Value: <output>{currency}</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [currency, setCurrency] = useState('thb');

<Select label="Currency" name="currency" value={currency} onChange={(e) => setCurrency(e.target.value)}>
  <option value="usd">US dollar</option>
  <option value="thb">Thai baht</option>
  <option value="eur">Euro</option>
</Select>
<p>Value: <output>{currency}</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind renders a native `<select>`, so its `onChange` is React's own and it also takes `defaultValue`.

## Groups and disabled options

Put options in `<optgroup label>` to group them. `disabled` on an option or an `<optgroup>` shows it but blocks it. The web component watches its children, so you can add or remove `<option>`s at any time.


HTML:

```html
<ui-select label="Office" name="office" placeholder="Choose an office">
  <optgroup label="Bangkok">
    <option value="silom">Silom</option>
    <option value="asok">Asok</option>
  </optgroup>
  <optgroup label="North">
    <option value="chiangmai">Chiang Mai</option>
    <option value="lampang" disabled>Lampang (closed)</option>
  </optgroup>
</ui-select>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSelect label="Office" name="office" placeholder="Choose an office">
  <optgroup label="Bangkok">
    <option value="silom">Silom</option>
    <option value="asok">Asok</option>
  </optgroup>
  <optgroup label="North">
    <option value="chiangmai">Chiang Mai</option>
    <option value="lampang" disabled>Lampang (closed)</option>
  </optgroup>
</UiSelect>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Select label="Office" name="office" placeholder="Choose an office">
  <optgroup label="Bangkok">
    <option value="silom">Silom</option>
    <option value="asok">Asok</option>
  </optgroup>
  <optgroup label="North">
    <option value="chiangmai">Chiang Mai</option>
    <option value="lampang" disabled>Lampang (closed)</option>
  </optgroup>
</Select>
```

## Options that depend on another field

An address form fills the district list from the chosen province. Replace the options when the first select changes: the web component picks up the new children by itself. Keep the second select disabled until there is something to choose.


HTML:

```html
<ui-select id="select-province" label="Province" name="province" placeholder="Choose a province">
  <option value="bkk">Bangkok</option>
  <option value="cnx">Chiang Mai</option>
</ui-select>
<ui-select id="select-district" label="District" name="district" placeholder="Choose a district" disabled></ui-select>

<script type="module">
  const districts = {
    bkk: [['bangrak', 'Bang Rak'], ['pathumwan', 'Pathum Wan'], ['chatuchak', 'Chatuchak']],
    cnx: [['mueang', 'Mueang Chiang Mai'], ['hangdong', 'Hang Dong'], ['sansai', 'San Sai']],
  };
  const province = document.getElementById('select-province');
  const district = document.getElementById('select-district');
  province.addEventListener('change', () => {
    district.replaceChildren(...districts[province.value].map(([value, label]) => new Option(label, value)));
    district.value = '';
    district.disabled = false;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const districts: Record<string, [string, string][]> = {
  bkk: [['bangrak', 'Bang Rak'], ['pathumwan', 'Pathum Wan'], ['chatuchak', 'Chatuchak']],
  cnx: [['mueang', 'Mueang Chiang Mai'], ['hangdong', 'Hang Dong'], ['sansai', 'San Sai']],
};
const [province, setProvince] = useState('');
const [district, setDistrict] = useState('');

<UiSelect label="Province" name="province" placeholder="Choose a province" value={province} onChange={(e) => { setProvince((e.target as SelectElement).value); setDistrict(''); }}>
  <option value="bkk">Bangkok</option>
  <option value="cnx">Chiang Mai</option>
</UiSelect>
<UiSelect label="District" name="district" placeholder="Choose a district" disabled={!province} value={district} onChange={(e) => setDistrict((e.target as SelectElement).value)}>
  {districts[province]?.map(([value, label]) => <option key={value} value={value}>{label}</option>)}
</UiSelect>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Select label="Province" name="province" placeholder="Choose a province" value={province} onChange={(e) => { setProvince(e.target.value); setDistrict(''); }}>
  <option value="bkk">Bangkok</option>
  <option value="cnx">Chiang Mai</option>
</Select>
<Select label="District" name="district" placeholder="Choose a district" disabled={!province} value={district} onChange={(e) => setDistrict(e.target.value)}>
  {districts[province]?.map(([value, label]) => <option key={value} value={value}>{label}</option>)}
</Select>
```

`districts`, `province` and `district` are the same in every React version.

## Sizes

`size`: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (the default, as in Carbon), `lg` 48px.


HTML:

```html
<ui-select label="Small" size="sm">
  <option>Legal</option>
</ui-select>
<ui-select label="Medium">
  <option>Legal</option>
</ui-select>
<ui-select label="Large" size="lg">
  <option>Legal</option>
</ui-select>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSelect label="Small" size="sm"><option>Legal</option></UiSelect>
<UiSelect label="Medium"><option>Legal</option></UiSelect>
<UiSelect label="Large" size="lg"><option>Legal</option></UiSelect>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Select label="Small" size="sm"><option>Legal</option></Select>
<Select label="Medium"><option>Legal</option></Select>
<Select label="Large" size="lg"><option>Legal</option></Select>
```

## Inline

`inline` puts the label beside a compact, borderless select. Use it in toolbars and above tables, not in forms.


HTML:

```html
<ui-select inline label="Items per page" value="25">
  <option value="10">10</option>
  <option value="25">25</option>
  <option value="50">50</option>
</ui-select>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSelect inline label="Items per page" value="25">
  <option value="10">10</option>
  <option value="25">25</option>
  <option value="50">50</option>
</UiSelect>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Select inline label="Items per page" defaultValue="25">
  <option value="10">10</option>
  <option value="25">25</option>
  <option value="50">50</option>
</Select>
```

## Fluid

`fluid` puts the label inside a 64px box (Carbon's `FluidSelect`). A fluid form around the field does the same for every field in it; see [fluid forms](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/#use-a-fluid-form). Fluid fields have no helper line.


HTML:

```html
<ui-select fluid label="Department" name="department" placeholder="Choose a department">
  <option value="sales">Sales</option>
  <option value="legal">Legal</option>
  <option value="finance">Finance</option>
</ui-select>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSelect fluid label="Department" name="department" placeholder="Choose a department">
  <option value="sales">Sales</option>
  <option value="legal">Legal</option>
  <option value="finance">Finance</option>
</UiSelect>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Select fluid label="Department" name="department" placeholder="Choose a department">
  <option value="sales">Sales</option>
  <option value="legal">Legal</option>
  <option value="finance">Finance</option>
</Select>
```

## Helper text, warnings and errors

One line shows under the field at a time: an error beats a warning, and a warning beats the helper text. `warn` is a non-blocking warning; `invalid` forces the error, for example after the server rejected the value.


HTML:

```html
<ui-select label="Approver" name="approver" helper-text="The approver gets the contract next">
  <option value="somchai">Somchai K.</option>
  <option value="malee">Malee S.</option>
</ui-select>
<ui-select label="Approver" name="approver2" value="malee" warn warn-text="Malee is on leave until 20 October">
  <option value="somchai">Somchai K.</option>
  <option value="malee">Malee S.</option>
</ui-select>
<ui-select label="Approver" name="approver3" value="somchai" invalid invalid-text="Somchai drafted this contract and can't approve it">
  <option value="somchai">Somchai K.</option>
  <option value="malee">Malee S.</option>
</ui-select>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSelect label="Approver" name="approver" helperText="The approver gets the contract next">…</UiSelect>
<UiSelect label="Approver" name="approver2" value="malee" warn warnText="Malee is on leave until 20 October">…</UiSelect>
<UiSelect label="Approver" name="approver3" value="somchai" invalid invalidText="Somchai drafted this contract and can't approve it">…</UiSelect>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Select label="Approver" name="approver" helperText="The approver gets the contract next">…</Select>
<Select label="Approver" name="approver2" defaultValue="malee" warn warnText="Malee is on leave until 20 October">…</Select>
<Select label="Approver" name="approver3" defaultValue="somchai" invalid invalidText="Somchai drafted this contract and can't approve it">…</Select>
```

## A link in the helper text

The `helper-text`, `warn-text` and `invalid-text` attributes are plain text. For a link or bold text, put the markup in the slot of the same name. In React + Tailwind, pass the markup to `helperText`, `warnText` or `invalidText`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-select label="Retention period" name="retention" value="10">
  <option value="5">5 years</option>
  <option value="10">10 years</option>
  <option value="forever">Keep forever</option>
  <span slot="helper-text">Follow the <a href="#accessibility">document retention policy</a>.</span>
</ui-select>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSelect label="Retention period" name="retention" value="10">
  <option value="5">5 years</option>
  <option value="10">10 years</option>
  <option value="forever">Keep forever</option>
  <span slot="helper-text">Follow the <a href="/policies/retention">document retention policy</a>.</span>
</UiSelect>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Select label="Retention period" name="retention" defaultValue="10" helperText={<>Follow the <a href="/policies/retention">document retention policy</a>.</>}>
  <option value="5">5 years</option>
  <option value="10">10 years</option>
  <option value="forever">Keep forever</option>
</Select>
```

## Read-only and disabled

- `readonly` (`readOnly` in React + Tailwind) shows the value and submits it, but neither the mouse nor the keyboard can change it. Tab still moves through.
- `disabled` greys the select out. It isn't submitted.


HTML:

```html
<ui-select label="Department" value="legal" readonly>
  <option value="sales">Sales</option>
  <option value="legal">Legal</option>
</ui-select>
<ui-select label="Department" disabled>
  <option value="sales">Sales</option>
  <option value="legal">Legal</option>
</ui-select>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSelect label="Department" value="legal" readonly>…</UiSelect>
<UiSelect label="Department" disabled>…</UiSelect>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Select label="Department" defaultValue="legal" readOnly>…</Select>
<Select label="Department" disabled>…</Select>
```

## Required in a form

With `required` and a `placeholder`, the form won't submit until the user picks an option. Press Submit without a choice to see the error. Without `invalid-text`, the built-in "Please select an option." shows, in the page's language.


HTML:

```html
<form id="select-form" style="display: grid; gap: 16px">
  <ui-select label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type" required invalid-text="Choose the contract type">
    <option value="sale">Sale</option>
    <option value="lease">Lease</option>
    <option value="service">Service</option>
  </ui-select>
  <div><ui-button type="submit">Submit</ui-button></div>
</form>
<p>Submitted: <output id="select-form-out"></output></p>

<script type="module">
  const form = document.getElementById('select-form');
  const out = document.getElementById('select-form-out');
  form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    out.value = [...new FormData(form)].map(([key, value]) => `${key}=${value}`).join(', ');
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const [sent, setSent] = useState('');
const submit = (event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  setSent([...new FormData(event.currentTarget)].map(([key, value]) => `${key}=${value}`).join(', '));
};

<form onSubmit={submit}>
  <UiSelect label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type" required invalidText="Choose the contract type">
    <option value="sale">Sale</option>
    <option value="lease">Lease</option>
    <option value="service">Service</option>
  </UiSelect>
  <UiButton type="submit">Submit</UiButton>
</form>
<p>Submitted: <output>{sent}</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// validation is your app's: `type` is the field's value, `tried` is set on the first submit
<form onSubmit={submit}>
  <Select label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type" value={type} onChange={(e) => setType(e.target.value)} invalid={tried && !type} invalidText="Choose the contract type">
    <option value="sale">Sale</option>
    <option value="lease">Lease</option>
    <option value="service">Service</option>
  </Select>
  <Button type="submit">Submit</Button>
</form>
<p>Submitted: <output>{sent}</output></p>
```

The React + Tailwind select shows what you pass in `invalid` and `invalidText`; checking the value is your app's, as in Carbon React. More in [Forms and validation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/).

## Skeleton

While the options load, show `ui-select-skeleton` in the field's place: a label bar and a field bar at the same `size`. It is hidden from screen readers, so say "loading" on the container (for example `aria-busy`).


HTML:

```html
<ui-select-skeleton></ui-select-skeleton>
<ui-select-skeleton size="sm" hide-label></ui-select-skeleton>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiSelectSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiSelectSkeleton />
<UiSelectSkeleton size="sm" hideLabel />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { SelectSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/select';

<SelectSkeleton />
<SelectSkeleton size="sm" hideLabel />
```

On the web component, import it from `@purpurabog/ui/select-skeleton`.

## Accessibility

- The control is a native `<select>`: the browser's own keys open and change it, and phones show the system picker.
- `label` is tied to the select. Use `hide-label` to keep it for screen readers only when the context already names the field.
- Helper, warning and error text are the select's description, so they are read when it gets focus.
- Options can't hold markup or a second line. If you need that, use a [Dropdown](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/dropdown/).

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Select](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-select/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-select>` · React `UiSelect`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | Visible label text; the `label` slot replaces it when markup is needed. |
| `hide-label` | `hideLabel` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep the label for screen readers but don't show it. |
| `helper-text` | `helperText` | `string` | `''` | Helper text under the field, shown while there is no error or warning. |
| `invalid-text` | `invalidText` | `string` | `''` | Error text shown while `invalid` or while the field fails validation. |
| `invalid` | `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Forces the error state, e.g. after server-side validation. |
| `warn` | `warn` | `boolean` | `false` | Non-blocking warning; shown when there is no error. |
| `warn-text` | `warnText` | `string` | `''` | Text of the warning shown while `warn`. |
| `placeholder` | `placeholder` | `string` | `''` | Shown as an empty first choice; with `required` the user must pick something else. |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `''` | Reflected: form-associated elements submit under the `name` attribute. |
| `size` | `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Field height: sm 32px, md 40px, lg 48px (tokens `--ui-field-height-*`). |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the control; a disabled `<fieldset>` ancestor does the same. |
| `required` | `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Blocks form submission while the field is empty. |
| `readonly` | `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows and submits the value but blocks changes. |
| `fluid` | `fluid` | `boolean` | `false` | Carbon `FluidSelect`: the label inside a 64px box, an error / warning inside it. `<ui-fluid-form>` sets it for every field inside. |
| `inline` | `inline` | `boolean` | `false` | Label beside a compact, borderless select. |

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `willValidate` |  | (read-only) Whether the field takes part in constraint validation (not while disabled), as natively. |
| `labels` |  | (read-only) The `<label>`s that point at this field. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `setCustomValidity(message)` | Like `<input>.setCustomValidity()`: a non-empty message makes the field invalid (and is shown as its error once touched) until cleared with ''. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `change` | none (use a ref) | When the user picks an option |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| `label` | Label content with markup; the `label` attribute is the plain-text fallback |
| `helper-text` | Helper text with markup (links, bold); overrides `helper-text` |
| `warn-text` | Warning text shown while `warn`; overrides `warn-text` |
| `invalid-text` | Error text shown while invalid; overrides `invalid-text` |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The field box |
| `label` | The label |
| `input` | The native select |
| `chevron` | The arrow icon |
| `status-icon` | The error / warning icon |
| `helper-text` | The helper line |
| `warning-text` | The warning line |
| `warn-text` | Same line as `warning-text` (named after the `warn-text` attribute / slot) |
| `error-text` | The error line |
| `invalid-text` | Same line as `error-text` (named after the `invalid-text` attribute / slot) |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-field-border` |  | Border on every side of the box (default none: Carbon's underline only; Kanok: a 1px outline) |
| `--ui-field-disabled-border-color` |  | Border colour when disabled (default: the underline transparent) |
| `--ui-field-readonly-border-color` |  | Border colour when read-only (default: a hairline underline) |
| `--ui-field-inline-border-color` |  | Border colour of the `inline` variant (default: no underline) |
| `--ui-field-radius` |  | Corner radius of the box (default 0; Kanok: 6px) |
| `--ui-select-appearance` |  | `base-select` opens the list in the menu look of the dropdowns (`--ui-menu-*`) where the browser supports a customizable select (Chrome 135+); default `none`, the native list (Kanok: base-select) |
| `--ui-field-background` |  | Fill of the box (default `--ui-surface-1`; Kanok: transparent) |
| `--ui-label-font` |  | Font of the label (default `--ui-font-caption`; Kanok: 14px semibold) |
| `--ui-label-color` |  | Colour of the label (default `--ui-ink-muted`; Kanok: `--ui-ink`) |
| `--ui-field-readonly-background` |  | The box's fill when read-only (default transparent; Kanok: a faint ink tint, so read-only reads as set and never weaker than disabled) |
| `--ui-fluid-background` |  | / --ui-fluid-gap - A fluid box's fill and the space under it (default the layer's fill, 0: boxes that touch; Kanok: transparent, 8px) |




---

# Dropdown

A dropdown picks one option from a list that looks the same in every browser. Options can have a second line and sit in labelled groups.


HTML:

```html
<ui-dropdown label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type">
  <option value="sale" data-description="The buyer owns the property">Sale</option>
  <option value="lease" data-description="Monthly rent, fixed term">Lease</option>
  <option value="mortgage" data-description="Property as security for a loan">Mortgage</option>
</ui-dropdown>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDropdown label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type">
  <option value="sale" data-description="The buyer owns the property">Sale</option>
  <option value="lease" data-description="Monthly rent, fixed term">Lease</option>
  <option value="mortgage" data-description="Property as security for a loan">Mortgage</option>
</UiDropdown>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const types = [
  { value: 'sale', label: 'Sale', description: 'The buyer owns the property' },
  { value: 'lease', label: 'Lease', description: 'Monthly rent, fixed term' },
  { value: 'mortgage', label: 'Mortgage', description: 'Property as security for a loan' },
];

<Dropdown label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type" items={types} />
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/dropdown
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-dropdown
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/dropdown.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/dropdown/dropdown-skeleton.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/dropdown/dropdown.styles.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/dropdown/dropdown.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-dropdown, core-listbox, core-popup, core-typeahead, shared-element, shared-events, shared-field, shared-form-control, shared-listbox, shared-localize, shared-position, shared-skeleton, shared-slots, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-dropdown.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/dropdown.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-field, tw-field, tw-i18n, tw-list, tw-skeleton, tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

```html
<ui-dropdown label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type">
  <option value="sale">Sale</option>
  <option value="lease">Lease</option>
</ui-dropdown>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiDropdown } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiDropdown label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type">
  <option value="sale">Sale</option>
  <option value="lease">Lease</option>
</UiDropdown>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Dropdown } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/dropdown';

const types = [
  { value: 'sale', label: 'Sale' },
  { value: 'lease', label: 'Lease' },
];

<Dropdown label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type" items={types} />
```

## Select, Dropdown, Combobox or MultiSelect?

| Component | Use it when |
|---|---|
| [Select](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/select/) | A plain form field. The browser draws the list: the native picker on phones, the most familiar control for screen readers. |
| [Dropdown](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/dropdown/) | The list must look the same in every browser, or options need a second line. |
| [Combobox](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/combobox/) | The list is long and typing is faster than scrolling, the options come from a server search, or free text is allowed. |
| [Multi-select](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/multi-select/) | The user picks several values. |

## Options, groups and descriptions

The web component takes `<option value>` children, the same markup as [Select](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/select/):

- `<optgroup label>` makes a labelled group in the list.
- `data-description` on an option adds a second line under its label. Typing to jump to an option only searches the label.
- `disabled` shows an option but skips it.

React + Tailwind takes the same as data in `items`: options `{ value, label, description?, disabled? }` and groups `{ label, options }`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-dropdown label="Branch" name="branch" placeholder="Choose a branch">
  <optgroup label="Bangkok">
    <option value="silom" data-description="Mon–Fri, 9:00–17:00">Silom</option>
    <option value="asok" data-description="Every day, 10:00–20:00">Asok</option>
  </optgroup>
  <optgroup label="North">
    <option value="chiangmai">Chiang Mai</option>
    <option value="lampang" disabled>Lampang (closed)</option>
  </optgroup>
</ui-dropdown>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDropdown label="Branch" name="branch" placeholder="Choose a branch">
  <optgroup label="Bangkok">
    <option value="silom" data-description="Mon–Fri, 9:00–17:00">Silom</option>
    <option value="asok" data-description="Every day, 10:00–20:00">Asok</option>
  </optgroup>
  <optgroup label="North">
    <option value="chiangmai">Chiang Mai</option>
    <option value="lampang" disabled>Lampang (closed)</option>
  </optgroup>
</UiDropdown>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const branches = [
  { label: 'Bangkok', options: [
    { value: 'silom', label: 'Silom', description: 'Mon–Fri, 9:00–17:00' },
    { value: 'asok', label: 'Asok', description: 'Every day, 10:00–20:00' },
  ] },
  { label: 'North', options: [
    { value: 'chiangmai', label: 'Chiang Mai' },
    { value: 'lampang', label: 'Lampang (closed)', disabled: true },
  ] },
];

<Dropdown label="Branch" name="branch" placeholder="Choose a branch" items={branches} />
```

## Placeholder and value

`placeholder` is the text in the field while nothing is chosen (Carbon calls it `label`). The starting choice is `value`, else the `<option selected>`. Reset goes back to it. `change` fires when the user picks a different option.


HTML:

```html
<ui-dropdown id="dropdown-type" label="Contract type" name="type" value="lease">
  <option value="sale">Sale</option>
  <option value="lease">Lease</option>
  <option value="service">Service</option>
</ui-dropdown>
<p>Value: <output id="dropdown-type-out"></output></p>

<script type="module">
  const type = document.getElementById('dropdown-type');
  const out = document.getElementById('dropdown-type-out');
  out.value = type.value;
  type.addEventListener('change', () => (out.value = type.value));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
import type { UiDropdown as DropdownElement } from '@purpurabog/ui';

const [type, setType] = useState('lease');

<UiDropdown label="Contract type" name="type" value={type} onChange={(e) => setType((e.target as DropdownElement).value)}>
  <option value="sale">Sale</option>
  <option value="lease">Lease</option>
  <option value="service">Service</option>
</UiDropdown>
<p>Value: <output>{type}</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [type, setType] = useState('lease');

<Dropdown label="Contract type" name="type" items={types} value={type} onChange={setType} />
<p>Value: <output>{type}</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind also takes `defaultValue` when you don't need to hold the value yourself.

## Sizes and direction

`size`: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (the default), `lg` 48px. The list opens below the field. `direction="top"` prefers above; either way it flips when there is no room.


HTML:

```html
<ui-dropdown label="Small" size="sm" value="lease">
  <option value="sale">Sale</option>
  <option value="lease">Lease</option>
</ui-dropdown>
<ui-dropdown label="Medium" value="lease">
  <option value="sale">Sale</option>
  <option value="lease">Lease</option>
</ui-dropdown>
<ui-dropdown label="Large, opens above" size="lg" direction="top" value="lease">
  <option value="sale">Sale</option>
  <option value="lease">Lease</option>
</ui-dropdown>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDropdown label="Small" size="sm" value="lease">…</UiDropdown>
<UiDropdown label="Medium" value="lease">…</UiDropdown>
<UiDropdown label="Large, opens above" size="lg" direction="top" value="lease">…</UiDropdown>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Dropdown label="Small" items={types} size="sm" defaultValue="lease" />
<Dropdown label="Medium" items={types} defaultValue="lease" />
<Dropdown label="Large, opens above" items={types} size="lg" direction="top" defaultValue="lease" />
```

## Inline

`inline` puts the label, a borderless field and any error or warning in one row, with no helper line. Use it in toolbars and above tables.


HTML:

```html
<ui-dropdown inline label="Status" value="all">
  <option value="all">All</option>
  <option value="draft">Draft</option>
  <option value="signed">Signed</option>
</ui-dropdown>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDropdown inline label="Status" value="all">
  <option value="all">All</option>
  <option value="draft">Draft</option>
  <option value="signed">Signed</option>
</UiDropdown>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const statuses = [
  { value: 'all', label: 'All' },
  { value: 'draft', label: 'Draft' },
  { value: 'signed', label: 'Signed' },
];

<Dropdown inline label="Status" items={statuses} defaultValue="all" />
```

## Inline with an error or a warning

An inline dropdown shows its error or warning beside the field, in the same row, so a toolbar keeps its height.


HTML:

```html
<ui-dropdown inline label="Status" placeholder="Choose" invalid invalid-text="Choose a status">
  <option value="draft">Draft</option>
  <option value="signed">Signed</option>
</ui-dropdown>
```


React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Dropdown inline label="Status" items={statuses} placeholder="Choose" invalid invalidText="Choose a status" />
<Dropdown inline label="Owner" items={owners} defaultValue="ananya" warn warnText="Owner is on leave" />
```

## Fluid

`fluid` puts the label inside a 64px box (Carbon's `FluidDropdown`); the open list keeps the usual row height. A fluid form around the field does the same for every field in it; see [fluid forms](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/#use-a-fluid-form).


HTML:

```html
<ui-dropdown fluid label="Contract type" name="type" placeholder="Choose a type">
  <option value="sale">Sale</option>
  <option value="lease">Lease</option>
  <option value="mortgage">Mortgage</option>
</ui-dropdown>
```

React:
