The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/date-picker';</script>

<ui-date-picker label="Contract start" name="start"></ui-date-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiDatePicker } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';
import type { UiDatePicker as DatePickerElement } from '@purpurabog/ui';

<UiDatePicker label="Contract start" name="start" value={start}
  onChange={(e) => setStart((e.target as DatePickerElement).value)} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { DatePicker } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/date-picker';

<DatePicker label="Contract start" name="start" value={start} onChange={setStart} />
```

`UiDatePicker` fires a native `change`, so its React prop is `onChange` (there is no `onUiChange`). The Tailwind `DatePicker` hands `onChange` the ISO string itself.

## What users see, what you get

Users see and type the date in the page's language and era. Your code reads the same ISO date in every language. The two pickers below share one value: change either one.


HTML:

```html
<ui-date-picker id="date-picker-seen-en" label="Signed on" value="2026-10-10"></ui-date-picker>
<ui-date-picker id="date-picker-seen-th" lang="th" label="วันที่ลงนาม" value="2026-10-10"></ui-date-picker>
<p>value: <output id="date-picker-seen-out">2026-10-10</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const en = document.getElementById('date-picker-seen-en');
  const th = document.getElementById('date-picker-seen-th');
  for (const [from, to] of [[en, th], [th, en]]) {
    from.addEventListener('change', () => {
      to.value = from.value;
      document.getElementById('date-picker-seen-out').textContent = from.value || '(empty)';
    });
  }
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const [signed, setSigned] = useState('2026-10-10');
const onChange = (e: Event) => setSigned((e.target as DatePickerElement).value);

<UiDatePicker label="Signed on" value={signed} onChange={onChange} />
<UiDatePicker lang="th" label="วันที่ลงนาม" value={signed} onChange={onChange} />
<p>value: <output>{signed || '(empty)'}</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [signed, setSigned] = useState('2026-10-10');

<DatePicker label="Signed on" value={signed} onChange={setSigned} />
<DatePicker locale="th" label="วันที่ลงนาม" value={signed} onChange={setSigned} />
<p>value: <output>{signed || '(empty)'}</output></p>
```


| | Page in Thai | Page in English |
|---|---|---|
| The user sees and types | 10/10/2569 | 10/10/2026 |
| `value`, `change`, the submitted form | `2026-10-10` | `2026-10-10` |

- `value`, `min` and `max` are always `yyyy-mm-dd` in the Gregorian year. A `value` that isn't a real date of that form becomes `''`, as with `<input type="date">`.
- The element fires `change` when a value is committed: on leaving the field, on Enter, on a pick from the calendar and on clear. Read `event.target.value` (and `endValue` in a range).
- An empty field still submits `name=`, as a native date input does. A disabled picker submits nothing.

## Type it or pick it

The calendar opens when the text box gets focus, by a click or by Tab, and focus stays in the box so users can keep typing. The calendar follows what they type.

- Text that already reads as a full date in the field's format, such as `10/10/2026`, becomes the value at once; `change` fires when it is committed (blur, Enter), not while typing.
- Anything else is read on blur or Enter. The numbers are pulled out of what was typed, so `s10/12/2026x` becomes 10/12/2026.
- Nothing is guessed. An incomplete date (`10/12`), an impossible one (`31/04/2026`) or text with no date in it stays in the field with a message saying what's wrong, and `value` becomes `''`.
- A full date outside `min` / `max`, or one `isDateDisabled` refuses, is kept and committed with its own message. The form won't submit until it's fixed.

Try it: type a date that doesn't exist, or one outside the year, then leave the field.


HTML:

```html
<ui-date-picker label="Contract end" helper-text="Type 31/04/2026, then leave the field"></ui-date-picker>
<ui-date-picker label="Invoice date" min="2026-01-01" max="2026-12-31" helper-text="Only dates in 2026. Type one in 2025, then leave the field"></ui-date-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDatePicker label="Contract end" helperText="Type 31/04/2026, then leave the field" />
<UiDatePicker label="Invoice date" min="2026-01-01" max="2026-12-31" helperText="Only dates in 2026. Type one in 2025, then leave the field" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<DatePicker label="Contract end" helperText="Type 31/04/2026, then leave the field" />
<DatePicker label="Invoice date" min="2026-01-01" max="2026-12-31" helperText="Only dates in 2026. Type one in 2025, then leave the field" />
```

The messages come built in, in Thai and English. How and when errors show, and how to add your own, is in [Forms and validation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/).

## Buddhist era and Thai

The language comes from `lang` on the element or the closest ancestor, else `<html lang>`. A Thai language gives Thai labels and messages, Thai month names, and years in พ.ศ. (ค.ศ. + 543). `locale` overrides the language for this picker alone.


HTML:

```html
<ui-date-picker lang="th" label="วันที่เริ่มสัญญา" value="2026-10-10"></ui-date-picker>
<ui-date-picker lang="th" era="ce" label="วันที่เริ่มสัญญา (ค.ศ.)" value="2026-10-10"></ui-date-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDatePicker lang="th" label="วันที่เริ่มสัญญา" value="2026-10-10" />
<UiDatePicker lang="th" era="ce" label="วันที่เริ่มสัญญา (ค.ศ.)" value="2026-10-10" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<DatePicker locale="th" label="วันที่เริ่มสัญญา" defaultValue="2026-10-10" />
<DatePicker locale="th" era="ce" label="วันที่เริ่มสัญญา (ค.ศ.)" defaultValue="2026-10-10" />
```

- `era` sets the year users see and type: `be` (พ.ศ., the default for Thai) or `ce` (ค.ศ., the default otherwise). Any language can use either.
- Typed years follow the same era. In พ.ศ., a year before 2400 (say 2026) gets a message asking for the พ.ศ. year; nothing is converted behind the user's back.
- Users may type Thai digits (๐–๙). They become 0–9 as they type.
- The placeholder and the default helper line show the format in the page's language: `วว/ดด/ปปปป` in Thai.
- React + Tailwind reads `<html lang>`, or its `locale` prop.

## Formats

`format` sets the order of day, month and year: `dd/mm/yyyy` (the default), `mm/dd/yyyy` or `yyyy-mm-dd`. Only what users see changes; `value` stays ISO.


HTML:

```html
<ui-date-picker label="Due date" format="yyyy-mm-dd" value="2026-10-10"></ui-date-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDatePicker label="Due date" format="yyyy-mm-dd" value="2026-10-10" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<DatePicker label="Due date" format="yyyy-mm-dd" defaultValue="2026-10-10" />
```

The format shows as helper text until you set `helper-text` (`helperText` in React + Tailwind). Screen readers still hear it after that.

## Pick a range

`range` gives two fields sharing one calendar: `value` / `name` / `label` for the start, `end-value` / `end-name` / `end-label` for the end. With both names the form gets two entries. Without `end-name`, `ui-date-picker` submits one `name` entry, `start/end` (`2026-10-01/2026-10-05`), as Carbon's `cds-date-picker` does; the React + Tailwind `DatePicker` submits the end only under `endName`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-date-picker range label="Check-in" end-label="Check-out" name="from" end-name="to"
  value="2026-10-10" end-value="2026-10-14"></ui-date-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDatePicker range label="Check-in" endLabel="Check-out" name="from" endName="to"
  value="2026-10-10" endValue="2026-10-14" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<DatePicker range label="Check-in" endLabel="Check-out" name="from" endName="to"
  value={from} onChange={setFrom} endValue={to} onEndChange={setTo} />
```

- A pick from the start field keeps the calendar open for the end. The days in between are highlighted with a continuous ribbon, with a preview while the end is chosen.
- Picking an end before the start swaps the two.
- A typed end before the start is kept and reported, not swapped.

### Two-month range view

Set `months="2"` to display two side-by-side months in the calendar, ideal for flight/hotel booking and long booking ranges:


HTML:

```html
<ui-date-picker range months="2" label="Depart" end-label="Return" name="depart" end-name="return"
  value="2026-10-15" end-value="2026-11-05"></ui-date-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDatePicker range months={2} label="Depart" endLabel="Return" name="depart" endName="return"
  value="2026-10-15" endValue="2026-11-05" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<DatePicker range months={2} label="Depart" endLabel="Return" name="depart" endName="return"
  value={depart} onChange={setDepart} endValue={ret} onEndChange={setRet} />
```

## Limit the dates

`min` and `max` take ISO dates. Days outside them are greyed out, and the month buttons stop at them.

To refuse single days (weekends, holidays), set `isDateDisabled`: a function that returns `true`, or a string to show as the message. On the web component it's a property, so set it in JavaScript:


HTML:

```html
<ui-date-picker id="date-picker-delivery" label="Delivery date" min="2026-01-01" max="2026-12-31"></ui-date-picker>

<script type="module">
  document.getElementById('date-picker-delivery').isDateDisabled = (date) =>
    date.getDay() === 0 || date.getDay() === 6 ? 'We don’t deliver at the weekend.' : false;
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const weekend = (date: Date) =>
  date.getDay() === 0 || date.getDay() === 6 ? 'We don’t deliver at the weekend.' : false;

<UiDatePicker label="Delivery date" min="2026-01-01" max="2026-12-31" isDateDisabled={weekend} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const weekend = (date: Date) =>
  date.getDay() === 0 || date.getDay() === 6 ? 'We don’t deliver at the weekend.' : false;

<DatePicker label="Delivery date" min="2026-01-01" max="2026-12-31" isDateDisabled={weekend} />
```

## Clear button and Today

`clearable` adds a × inside the field while it has text. `show-today` adds a Today button under the calendar (Carbon has none; this one is opt-in). `first-day` sets the first day of the week, from `0` (Sunday, the default) to `6`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-date-picker label="Meeting date" clearable show-today first-day="1"></ui-date-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDatePicker label="Meeting date" clearable showToday firstDay={1} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<DatePicker label="Meeting date" clearable showToday firstDay={1} />
```

## Sizes and fluid

`size`: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (the default, as in Carbon), `lg` 48px, the same scale as the text input. `fluid`, or a fluid form around it (`<ui-fluid-form>`, `FluidForm` in React + Tailwind), gives Carbon's fluid field: a 64px box with the label inside. Both props have the same names in React and React + Tailwind.


HTML:

```html
<ui-date-picker size="sm" label="Posted on (sm)" value="2026-10-10"></ui-date-picker>
<ui-date-picker size="lg" label="Posted on (lg)" value="2026-10-10"></ui-date-picker>
<ui-date-picker fluid range label="Lease start" end-label="Lease end" value="2026-11-01" end-value="2027-10-31"></ui-date-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDatePicker size="sm" label="Posted on (sm)" value="2026-10-10" />
<UiDatePicker size="lg" label="Posted on (lg)" value="2026-10-10" />
<UiDatePicker fluid range label="Lease start" endLabel="Lease end" value="2026-11-01" endValue="2027-10-31" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<DatePicker size="sm" label="Posted on (sm)" defaultValue="2026-10-10" />
<DatePicker size="lg" label="Posted on (lg)" defaultValue="2026-10-10" />
<DatePicker fluid range label="Lease start" endLabel="Lease end" defaultValue="2026-11-01" defaultEndValue="2027-10-31" />
```

## Helper text, errors and warnings

`helper-text` says what the date is for (the `helper-text` slot takes markup). `warn` with `warn-text` flags a date that is allowed but unusual; it doesn't block submit. `invalid` with `invalid-text` shows an error from your own check, such as one made on the server. In a range, the warning shows under the start field.


HTML:

```html
<ui-date-picker label="Effective date" helper-text="The day the new rate starts"></ui-date-picker>
<ui-date-picker label="Payment due" value="2026-10-03" warn warn-text="This is a Saturday. The bank pays on Monday."></ui-date-picker>
<ui-date-picker label="Contract end" value="2026-09-30" invalid invalid-text="The end must be after the start, 01/10/2026."></ui-date-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDatePicker label="Effective date" helperText="The day the new rate starts" />
<UiDatePicker label="Payment due" value="2026-10-03" warn warnText="This is a Saturday. The bank pays on Monday." />
<UiDatePicker label="Contract end" value="2026-09-30" invalid invalidText="The end must be after the start, 01/10/2026." />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<DatePicker label="Effective date" helperText="The day the new rate starts" />
<DatePicker label="Payment due" defaultValue="2026-10-03" warn warnText="This is a Saturday. The bank pays on Monday." />
<DatePicker label="Contract end" defaultValue="2026-09-30" invalid invalidText="The end must be after the start, 01/10/2026." />
```

## Read-only and disabled

`readonly` shows and submits the value but blocks typing and the calendar. `disabled` greys the field out; it isn't submitted or validated. A disabled `<fieldset>` around it does the same.


HTML:

```html
<ui-date-picker label="Signed on" value="2026-10-10" readonly></ui-date-picker>
<ui-date-picker label="Signed on" value="2026-10-10" disabled></ui-date-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiDatePicker label="Signed on" value="2026-10-10" readonly />
<UiDatePicker label="Signed on" value="2026-10-10" disabled />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<DatePicker label="Signed on" defaultValue="2026-10-10" readOnly />
<DatePicker label="Signed on" defaultValue="2026-10-10" disabled />
```

The web component and its React wrapper spell it `readonly`; React + Tailwind uses `readOnly`.

## In a form

With `required`, the form won't submit until the date is filled in; in a range, both dates are required. The form gets ISO dates under `name` (and `end-name`). Submit the empty form below to see the messages.


HTML:

```html
<form id="date-picker-form" method="dialog" style="display: grid; gap: 16px">
  <ui-date-picker label="Request date" name="requested" value="2026-10-10" required></ui-date-picker>
  <ui-date-picker range label="Leave from" end-label="Leave until" name="from" end-name="until" required></ui-date-picker>
  <div><ui-button type="submit">Send request</ui-button></div>
</form>
<p>Submitted: <output id="date-picker-form-out">nothing yet</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const form = document.getElementById('date-picker-form');
  form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const entries = [...new FormData(form)].map(([key, value]) => `${key}=${value}`);
    document.getElementById('date-picker-form-out').textContent = entries.join(', ');
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); send(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }}>
  <UiDatePicker label="Request date" name="requested" value="2026-10-10" required />
  <UiDatePicker range label="Leave from" endLabel="Leave until" name="from" endName="until" required />
  <UiButton type="submit">Send request</UiButton>
</form>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); send(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }}>
  <DatePicker label="Request date" name="requested" defaultValue="2026-10-10" required />
  <DatePicker range label="Leave from" endLabel="Leave until" name="from" endName="until" required />
  <Button type="submit">Send request</Button>
</form>
```

`send` stands for your own code.

## Phones and tablets

On a phone (a touch screen narrower than 42rem), `picker="auto"` (the default) opens the calendar in a bottom sheet: a dialog along the bottom edge of the screen, over a dimmed page.

- A tap on the box opens it with a day focused, so no on-screen keyboard comes up over it. Focus alone doesn't open it: after the sheet closes, a tap on the box types.
- Esc, the × button, a swipe down on its top bar or a tap on the dimmed page closes it. Typed text is committed and focus goes back to the box.
- While it is open the page behind can't be reached or scrolled, and the sheet's padding keeps clear of the phone's safe areas (the home indicator, a notch).

On tablets and larger screens the calendar opens under the box as before.

| `picker` | Opens |
|---|---|
| `auto` (default) | The bottom sheet on a phone, the calendar under the box everywhere else |
| `custom` | The calendar under the box on every device |
| `sheet` | The bottom sheet on every device |
| `native` | The OS date picker. It can't grey out `isDateDisabled` days, so its pick is checked like typed text |

```html
<ui-date-picker label="Visit date" picker="sheet"></ui-date-picker>
```

Style the sheet with `::part(sheet)` (its scrim with `::part(sheet)::backdrop`), `::part(sheet-grip)` and `::part(sheet-close)`; `--ui-sheet-radius` rounds its top corners (the menu radius by default). The prop has the same name in every variant.

## The calendar on its own

The calendar inside the picker is its own element, `ui-calendar`, and it comes with the same import. It is a controlled view: it moves its own focus, but you keep the chosen day. Listen to `ui-pick` (detail `{ date }`, a `Date`) and set `value`:


HTML:

```html
<ui-calendar id="date-picker-calendar" style="max-width: 288px" show-today></ui-calendar>

<script type="module">
  const calendarAlone = document.getElementById('date-picker-calendar');
  calendarAlone.addEventListener('ui-pick', (event) => {
    const d = event.detail.date;
    const pad = (n) => String(n).padStart(2, '0');
    calendarAlone.value = `${d.getFullYear()}-${pad(d.getMonth() + 1)}-${pad(d.getDate())}`;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiCalendar } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';
import { toIso } from '@purpurabog/ui/core';

<UiCalendar value={day} showToday onUiPick={(e) => setDay(toIso(e.detail.date))} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-calendar
import { Calendar } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/calendar';
import { toIso } from '@purpurabog/ui/core';

const [focus, setFocus] = useState(() => new Date());

<Calendar value={day} focusDate={focus} onFocusDateChange={setFocus}
  onPick={(date) => setDay(toIso(date))} showToday />
```

The month shown follows the `focusDate` property (a `Date`, today by default). Like the picker, `ui-calendar` follows the page's language (the nearest `lang`) and shows พ.ศ. in Thai; `locale` and `era` override it. It takes `min`, `max`, `isDateDisabled`, `range` with `end-value`, `first-day` and `show-today` as the picker does. The React + Tailwind `Calendar` is controlled too: `focusDate`, `onFocusDateChange` and `onPick` are required.

### Multiple dates (`multi`)

`<ui-calendar multi>` allows selecting multiple arbitrary dates simultaneously (Cally style), toggled into `values`:


HTML:

```html
<ui-calendar multi values='["2026-10-05","2026-10-12","2026-10-19"]'></ui-calendar>
```

### Dual-month calendar (`months="2"`)

`<ui-calendar range months="2">` renders two months side-by-side with a continuous cross-month range ribbon:


HTML:

```html
<ui-calendar range months="2" value="2026-10-10" end-value="2026-11-04"></ui-calendar>
```

## Skeleton

While the page loads its data, show `<ui-date-picker-skeleton>` in the picker's place, as Carbon's `DatePickerSkeleton`; add `range` for two fields. It has its own import, `@purpurabog/ui/date-picker-skeleton`, and is hidden from screen readers.


HTML:

```html
<ui-date-picker-skeleton></ui-date-picker-skeleton>
<ui-date-picker-skeleton range></ui-date-picker-skeleton>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiDatePickerSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiDatePickerSkeleton />
<UiDatePickerSkeleton range />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { DatePickerSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/date-picker';

<DatePickerSkeleton />
<DatePickerSkeleton range />
```

## Keyboard

In the text box:

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Typing | Enters the date; the open calendar follows a full date |
| ↓ | Opens the calendar and moves focus into it |
| Tab | With the calendar open: moves into it (the field's date, else today) |
| Shift + Tab | From the start field: closes the calendar and moves back |
| Enter | Commits the typed text, closes the calendar and submits the form it's in |
| Esc | Closes the calendar |

In the calendar:

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| ← / → | Previous / next day |
| ↑ / ↓ | Same day of the previous / next week |
| Home / End | First / last day of the week |
| Page Up / Page Down | Previous / next month |
| Shift + Page Up / Page Down | Previous / next year |
| Enter, Space | Picks the day; the calendar closes (in a range, after the end) |
| Esc | Closes, focus back in the text box |
| Tab | In a range, from the start: to the end field. Otherwise leaves the picker and closes the calendar. In the bottom sheet, Tab stays in the sheet |
| Shift + Tab | Back to the text box |

With a mouse, click the year in the calendar header to type one, or use its ▲▼ buttons.

## Accessibility

- The text box is a combobox that opens a dialog (`aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded`). The calendar is a dialog named "Choose date" with a grid of day buttons, following the WAI-ARIA date picker dialog pattern.
- Each day is read as a full date ("Saturday, October 10, 2026"). Today has `aria-current="date"`, chosen days `aria-pressed`, refused days `aria-disabled`.
- Month changes are announced through a polite live region.
- The bottom sheet is a modal dialog with the same name: the page behind it is inert until it closes.
- The calendar icon is decorative, as in Carbon: it is not a Tab stop, and a click on it is a click in the text box.
- An error sets `aria-invalid` and is linked to the box with `aria-describedby`, as is the format hint.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Date picker](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-date-picker/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-date-picker>` · React `UiDatePicker`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | Visible label text; the `label` slot replaces it when markup is needed. |
| `hide-label` | `hideLabel` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep the label for screen readers but don't show it. |
| `helper-text` | `helperText` | `string` | `''` | Helper text under the field, shown while there is no error or warning. |
| `invalid-text` | `invalidText` | `string` | `''` | Error text shown while `invalid` or while the field fails validation. |
| `invalid` | `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Forces the error state, e.g. after server-side validation. |
| `warn` | `warn` | `boolean` | `false` | Non-blocking warning; shown when there is no error. |
| `warn-text` | `warnText` | `string` | `''` | Text of the warning shown while `warn`. |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` | ISO yyyy-mm-dd (the start date in `range` mode). |
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `''` | Reflected: form-associated elements submit under the `name` attribute. |
| `range` | `range` | `boolean` | `false` | Two fields sharing one calendar (Carbon `datePickerType="range"`). |
| `end-value` | `endValue` | `string` | `''` | Range mode: the end date, ISO yyyy-mm-dd. |
| `end-name` | `endName` | `string` | `''` | Range mode: form entry name of the end date. Without it the range submits as one `name` entry `start/end`. |
| `end-label` | `endLabel` | `string` | `''` | Range mode: label of the end field. |
| `min` | `min` | `string` | `''` | Earliest selectable date, ISO yyyy-mm-dd. |
| `max` | `max` | `string` | `''` | Latest selectable date, ISO yyyy-mm-dd. |
| `format` | `format` | `DateFormat` | `'dd/mm/yyyy'` |  |
| `locale` | `locale` | `string` | `''` | Locale for names, labels and messages. Defaults to the nearest `lang`: the element's own, an ancestor's, then `<html>`'s, else the browser language. |
| `era` | `era` | `Era \| ''` | `''` | Year era shown and typed: `be` (พ.ศ.) or `ce` (ค.ศ.). Defaults to `be` for Thai locales. |
| `first-day` | `firstDay` | `number` | `0` | 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the control; a disabled `<fieldset>` ancestor does the same. |
| `required` | `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Blocks form submission while the field is empty. |
| `readonly` | `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows and submits the value but blocks changes. |
| `fluid` | `fluid` | `boolean` | `false` | Carbon `FluidDatePicker`: each date box is a 64px box with its label inside. `<ui-fluid-form>` sets it for every field inside. |
| `picker` | `picker` | `'auto' \| 'custom' \| 'sheet' \| 'native'` | `'auto'` | Which picker opens: `auto` (default) = our calendar, in a bottom sheet on a phone; `custom` = our calendar as a popover on every device; `sheet` = in a bottom sheet on every device; `native` = the OS date picker. |
| `clearable` | `clearable` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows a clear button inside the field while it has text. |
| `show-today` | `showToday` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds a "Today" button under the calendar. |
| `months` | `months` | `number` | `1` | Number of months to show side-by-side in the calendar (default 1, e.g. 2 for range picking). |
| `size` | `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Field height, same scale as ui-text-input. |

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `isDateDisabled` | `(date: Date) => boolean \| string \| undefined` | Property only. Return `true` for days that can't be chosen (weekends, holidays…), or a string to show that reason instead of the generic message. |
| `willValidate` |  | (read-only) Whether the field takes part in constraint validation (not while disabled), as natively. |
| `labels` |  | (read-only) The `<label>`s that point at this field. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `setCustomValidity(message)` | Like `<input>.setCustomValidity()`: a non-empty message makes the field invalid (and is shown as its error once touched) until cleared with ''. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `change` | none (use a ref) | When a committed value (start or end) changes: blur, Enter, a calendar pick or clear. A typed date outside min/max is still committed, with the field reporting the range error. |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| `label` | Label content with markup; the `label` attribute is the plain-text fallback |
| `helper-text` | Helper text with markup (links, bold); overrides `helper-text` |
| `warn-text` | Warning text shown while `warn`; overrides `warn-text` |
| `invalid-text` | Error text shown while invalid; overrides `invalid-text` |
| `end-label` | Label of the end field in range mode; overrides `end-label` |

# Time picker

A time picker takes a time as short `hh:mm` text, with optional selects beside it for AM / PM and the time zone.


HTML:

```html
<ui-time-picker label="Start time" name="time">
  <ui-time-picker-select label="AM or PM" name="period">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </ui-time-picker-select>
  <ui-time-picker-select label="Time zone" name="zone">
    <option value="ict">Bangkok (ICT)</option>
    <option value="utc">UTC</option>
  </ui-time-picker-select>
</ui-time-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTimePicker label="Start time" name="time">
  <UiTimePickerSelect label="AM or PM" name="period">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </UiTimePickerSelect>
  <UiTimePickerSelect label="Time zone" name="zone">
    <option value="ict">Bangkok (ICT)</option>
    <option value="utc">UTC</option>
  </UiTimePickerSelect>
</UiTimePicker>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TimePicker label="Start time" name="time">
  <TimePickerSelect label="AM or PM" name="period">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </TimePickerSelect>
  <TimePickerSelect label="Time zone" name="zone">
    <option value="ict">Bangkok (ICT)</option>
    <option value="utc">UTC</option>
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/time-picker
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-time-picker
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/time-picker.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/time-picker/time-picker-select.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/time-picker/time-picker-shared.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/time-picker/time-picker-skeleton.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/time-picker/time-picker.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-date, shared-element, shared-field, shared-form-control, shared-localize, shared-skeleton, shared-slots, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-time-picker.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/time-picker.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    tw-field, tw-i18n, tw-skeleton, tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/time-picker';</script>

<ui-time-picker label="Start time" name="time"></ui-time-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiTimePicker, UiTimePickerSelect } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiTimePicker label="Start time" name="time" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { TimePicker, TimePickerSelect } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/time-picker';

<TimePicker label="Start time" name="time" />
```

## 12-hour or 24-hour

By default the box takes 12-hour time, `h:mm` or `hh:mm` (`9:30`, `09:30`, `12:45`), and at most 5 characters. Carbon's own pattern rejects a leading zero; this one accepts it, so typing what the `hh:mm` placeholder shows works.

For 24-hour time, set your own `pattern` and leave out the AM / PM select:


HTML:

```html
<ui-time-picker label="Departure" name="departure" pattern="([01]?[0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]"></ui-time-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTimePicker label="Departure" name="departure" pattern="([01]?[0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TimePicker label="Departure" name="departure" pattern="([01]?[0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]" />
```

`maxlength` (`maxLength` in React) changes the length limit; `placeholder` the hint.

## Start with a value

To edit a time that is already saved, set `value` on the picker and on each select. A select without `value` starts on its `<option selected>`, else its first option, as a native select does.


HTML:

```html
<ui-time-picker label="Board meeting" value="2:30">
  <ui-time-picker-select label="AM or PM" value="PM">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </ui-time-picker-select>
  <ui-time-picker-select label="Time zone">
    <option value="ict" selected>Bangkok (ICT)</option>
    <option value="sgt">Singapore (SGT)</option>
    <option value="utc">UTC</option>
  </ui-time-picker-select>
</ui-time-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTimePicker label="Board meeting" value="2:30">
  <UiTimePickerSelect label="AM or PM" value="PM">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </UiTimePickerSelect>
  <UiTimePickerSelect label="Time zone" value="ict">
    <option value="ict">Bangkok (ICT)</option>
    <option value="sgt">Singapore (SGT)</option>
    <option value="utc">UTC</option>
  </UiTimePickerSelect>
</UiTimePicker>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TimePicker label="Board meeting" defaultValue="2:30">
  <TimePickerSelect label="AM or PM" defaultValue="PM">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </TimePickerSelect>
  <TimePickerSelect label="Time zone" defaultValue="ict">
    <option value="ict">Bangkok (ICT)</option>
    <option value="sgt">Singapore (SGT)</option>
    <option value="utc">UTC</option>
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>
```

HTML:

```html

  <ui-time-picker-select label="AM or PM">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </ui-time-picker-select>
</ui-time-picker>
<ui-time-picker size="lg" label="Large (lg)" value="9:30">
```

## Fluid

`fluid`, or a fluid form around it (`<ui-fluid-form>`, `FluidForm` in React + Tailwind), gives Carbon's fluid time picker: the box and each select as equal 64px columns with their labels inside. The prop has the same name in React and React + Tailwind.


HTML:

```html

  <ui-time-picker-select label="AM or PM">

    <option value="PM">PM</option>
```

## Errors and warnings

The web component checks the text against `pattern` after the user leaves the box or tries to submit, and shows the error under it. `invalid-text` replaces the browser's own message ("Please match the requested format"). Set `invalid` for an error from your own validation, or `warn` with `warn-text` for a warning that doesn't block submit:


HTML:

```html
<ui-time-picker label="Pick-up" value="13:30" invalid invalid-text="The shop closes at 12:00."></ui-time-picker>
<ui-time-picker label="Site visit" value="7:00" warn warn-text="Before office hours. Someone must open the gate.">
  <ui-time-picker-select label="AM or PM">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </ui-time-picker-select>
</ui-time-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTimePicker label="Pick-up" value="13:30" invalid invalidText="The shop closes at 12:00." />
<UiTimePicker label="Site visit" value="7:00" warn warnText="Before office hours. Someone must open the gate.">
  <UiTimePickerSelect label="AM or PM">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </UiTimePickerSelect>
</UiTimePicker>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TimePicker label="Pick-up" defaultValue="13:30" invalid invalidText="The shop closes at 12:00." />
<TimePicker label="Site visit" defaultValue="7:00" warn warnText="Before office hours. Someone must open the gate.">
  <TimePickerSelect label="AM or PM">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>
```

React + Tailwind follows Carbon React: `pattern` still takes part in the form's validation, but no message shows by itself. Set `invalid` and `invalidText` when your check fails. More in [Forms and validation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/).

## Read-only and disabled

`readonly` keeps every value and submits it: the box can't be edited, and a select still takes focus but doesn't open or change. `disabled` disables the box and every select inside.


HTML:

```html
<ui-time-picker label="Start time" value="9:30" readonly>
  <ui-time-picker-select label="AM or PM">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </ui-time-picker-select>
</ui-time-picker>
<ui-time-picker label="Start time" value="9:30" disabled>
  <ui-time-picker-select label="AM or PM">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </ui-time-picker-select>
</ui-time-picker>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTimePicker label="Start time" value="9:30" readonly>
  <UiTimePickerSelect label="AM or PM">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </UiTimePickerSelect>
</UiTimePicker>
<UiTimePicker label="Start time" value="9:30" disabled>
  <UiTimePickerSelect label="AM or PM">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </UiTimePickerSelect>
</UiTimePicker>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TimePicker label="Start time" defaultValue="9:30" readOnly>
  <TimePickerSelect label="AM or PM">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>
<TimePicker label="Start time" defaultValue="9:30" disabled>
  <TimePickerSelect label="AM or PM">
    <option value="AM">AM</option>
    <option value="PM">PM</option>
  </TimePickerSelect>
</TimePicker>
```

The web component and its React wrapper spell it `readonly`; React + Tailwind uses `readOnly`.

## What the form gets

Each part submits on its own: the time box under its `name` and each select under its own `name`. The time is the text as typed (`9:30` or `09:30`), and the select values are your `<option>` values. Nothing is converted: the time zone select is a plain choice, with no time zone arithmetic behind it. `required` blocks the submit while the box is empty.


HTML:

```html
<form id="time-picker-form" method="dialog" style="display: grid; gap: 16px">
  <ui-time-picker label="Signing deadline" name="time" required>
    <ui-time-picker-select label="AM or PM" name="period">
      <option value="AM">AM</option>
      <option value="PM">PM</option>
    </ui-time-picker-select>
    <ui-time-picker-select label="Time zone" name="zone">
      <option value="ict">Bangkok (ICT)</option>
      <option value="utc">UTC</option>
    </ui-time-picker-select>
  </ui-time-picker>
  <div><ui-button type="submit">Save</ui-button></div>
</form>
<p>Submitted: <output id="time-picker-form-out">nothing yet</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const form = document.getElementById('time-picker-form');
  form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const entries = [...new FormData(form)].map(([key, value]) => `${key}=${value}`);
    document.getElementById('time-picker-form-out').textContent = entries.join(', ');
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); save(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }}>
  <UiTimePicker label="Signing deadline" name="time" required>
    <UiTimePickerSelect label="AM or PM" name="period">
      <option value="AM">AM</option>
      <option value="PM">PM</option>
    </UiTimePickerSelect>
    <UiTimePickerSelect label="Time zone" name="zone">
      <option value="ict">Bangkok (ICT)</option>
      <option value="utc">UTC</option>
    </UiTimePickerSelect>
  </UiTimePicker>
  <UiButton type="submit">Save</UiButton>
</form>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); save(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }}>
  <TimePicker label="Signing deadline" name="time" required>
    <TimePickerSelect label="AM or PM" name="period">
      <option value="AM">AM</option>
      <option value="PM">PM</option>
    </TimePickerSelect>
    <TimePickerSelect label="Time zone" name="zone">
      <option value="ict">Bangkok (ICT)</option>
      <option value="utc">UTC</option>
    </TimePickerSelect>
  </TimePicker>
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</form>
```

`save` stands for your own code.

## Events

The web component fires `input` while typing and `change` on commit; each select fires `change`. In React the wrapper props are `onInput` / `onChange`; the Tailwind `TimePicker` passes `onChange` to its `<input>`, as React does.


HTML:

```html
<ui-time-picker id="time-picker-events" label="Reminder at"></ui-time-picker>
<p>input: <output id="time-picker-events-input">–</output>, change: <output id="time-picker-events-change">–</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const reminder = document.getElementById('time-picker-events');
  reminder.addEventListener('input', () => {
    document.getElementById('time-picker-events-input').textContent = reminder.value;
  });
  reminder.addEventListener('change', () => {
    document.getElementById('time-picker-events-change').textContent = reminder.value;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
import type { UiTimePicker as TimePickerElement } from '@purpurabog/ui';

<UiTimePicker label="Reminder at"
  onInput={(e) => setTyped((e.target as TimePickerElement).value)}
  onChange={(e) => setCommitted((e.target as TimePickerElement).value)} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// React's onChange runs on every keystroke; onBlur is the commit
<TimePicker label="Reminder at"
  onChange={(e) => setTyped(e.target.value)}
  onBlur={(e) => setCommitted(e.target.value)} />
```

## Check a time against another

Your own rules, such as a closing time after the opening time, go through `invalid` and `invalid-text`: check on `change` and set them. Here both boxes take 24-hour time.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: flex-start">
  <ui-time-picker id="time-picker-opens" label="Branch opens" value="08:30" pattern="([01]?[0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]"></ui-time-picker>
  <ui-time-picker id="time-picker-closes" label="Branch closes" value="17:30" pattern="([01]?[0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]"></ui-time-picker>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const opens = document.getElementById('time-picker-opens');
  const closes = document.getElementById('time-picker-closes');
  const minutes = (text) => {
    const [h, m] = text.split(':').map(Number);
    return h * 60 + m;
  };
  const check = () => {
    const wrong = minutes(closes.value) <= minutes(opens.value);
    closes.invalid = wrong;
    closes.invalidText = wrong ? 'Must be after the opening time.' : '';
  };
  opens.addEventListener('change', check);
  closes.addEventListener('change', check);
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const H24 = '([01]?[0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]';
const minutes = (text: string) => {
  const [h, m] = text.split(':').map(Number);
  return h * 60 + m;
};
const wrong = minutes(closes) <= minutes(opens);

<UiTimePicker label="Branch opens" value={opens} pattern={H24}
  onChange={(e) => setOpens((e.target as TimePickerElement).value)} />
<UiTimePicker label="Branch closes" value={closes} pattern={H24}
  onChange={(e) => setCloses((e.target as TimePickerElement).value)}
  invalid={wrong} invalidText={wrong ? 'Must be after the opening time.' : ''} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// H24 and minutes as in the React tab
const wrong = minutes(closes) <= minutes(opens);

<TimePicker label="Branch opens" value={opens} pattern={H24} onChange={(e) => setOpens(e.target.value)} />
<TimePicker label="Branch closes" value={closes} pattern={H24} onChange={(e) => setCloses(e.target.value)}
  invalid={wrong} invalidText={wrong ? 'Must be after the opening time.' : ''} />
```

## Skeleton

While the page loads its data, show `<ui-time-picker-skeleton>` in the picker's place. Carbon has only the fluid time picker skeleton, so this is that one: the box, the AM / PM select and the time zone select. `is-only-two` (`isOnlyTwo` in React + Tailwind) draws two equal parts instead. It has its own import, `@purpurabog/ui/time-picker-skeleton`, and is hidden from screen readers.


HTML:

```html
<ui-time-picker-skeleton></ui-time-picker-skeleton>
<ui-time-picker-skeleton is-only-two></ui-time-picker-skeleton>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiTimePickerSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiTimePickerSkeleton />
<UiTimePickerSkeleton isOnlyTwo />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { TimePickerSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/time-picker';

<TimePickerSkeleton />
<TimePickerSkeleton isOnlyTwo />
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Enter (in the time box) | Submits the form it's in, as a native input does |
| ↑ / ↓, Space (on a select) | The browser's own select keys; ignored while read-only |

## Accessibility

- The box is a native text input with a `<label>`; the selects are native `<select>` elements.
- Name each select with `label`. Without one, the web component and React + Tailwind fall back to "Open list of options", as Carbon does.
- An error sets `aria-invalid` on the box and is linked to it with `aria-describedby`.
- A read-only select has `aria-readonly`.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Time picker](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-time-picker/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-time-picker>` · React `UiTimePicker`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max-length` |  |  |  | Deprecated: use `maxlength` |
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `hide-label` | `hideLabel` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `placeholder` | `placeholder` | `string` | `'hh:mm'` |  |
| `pattern` | `pattern` |  | `` String.raw`(1[012]\|0?[1-9]):[0-5][0-9](\s)?` `` | 12-hour time with an optional trailing space. Carbon's default rejects a leading zero, so "09:30" typed as the `hh:mm` placeholder shows would fail; this one accepts "9:30" and "09:30". |
| `maxlength` | `maxLength` | `number` | `5` | Like `<input maxlength>` (Carbon `maxLength`); the `max-length` attribute of 0.8 and earlier is still read. |
| `size` | `size` | `TimePickerSize` | `'md'` |  |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `readonly` | `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `fluid` | `fluid` | `boolean` | `false` | Carbon `FluidTimePicker`: equal 64px columns with labels inside, an error / warning inside the box. `<ui-fluid-form>` sets it for every field inside. |
| `required` | `required` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `invalid` | `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `invalid-text` | `invalidText` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `warn` | `warn` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `warn-text` | `warnText` | `string` | `''` |  |

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `willValidate` |  | (read-only) Whether the field takes part in constraint validation (not while disabled), as natively. |
| `labels` |  | (read-only) The `<label>`s that point at this field. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `setCustomValidity(message)` | Like `<input>.setCustomValidity()`: a non-empty message makes the field invalid (and is shown as its error once touched) until cleared with ''. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `change` | `onChange` |  |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | `<ui-time-picker-select>` elements |
| `label` | Rich label |
| `invalid-text` | Rich error text |
| `warn-text` | Rich warning text |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `label` | The label |
| `base` | Row with the input and the selects |
| `input` | The text input |
| `error-text` | Error text |
| `invalid-text` | Same line as `error-text` (named after the `invalid-text` attribute / slot) |
| `warning-text` | Warning text |
| `warn-text` | Same line as `warning-text` (named after the `warn-text` attribute / slot) |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-field-border` |  | Border on every side of the box (default none: Carbon's underline only; Kanok: a 1px outline) |
| `--ui-field-disabled-border-color` |  | Border colour when disabled (default: the underline transparent) |
| `--ui-field-readonly-border-color` |  | Border colour when read-only (default: a hairline underline) |
| `--ui-field-radius` |  | Corner radius of the box (default 0; Kanok: 6px) |
| `--ui-field-background` |  | Fill of the box (default `--ui-surface-1`; Kanok: transparent) |
| `--ui-label-font` |  | Font of the label (default `--ui-font-caption`; Kanok: 14px semibold) |
| `--ui-label-color` |  | Colour of the label (default `--ui-ink-muted`; Kanok: `--ui-ink`) |
| `--ui-field-readonly-background` |  | The box's fill when read-only (default transparent; Kanok: a faint ink tint, so read-only reads as set and never weaker than disabled) |

# Slider

A slider picks a number, or a range between two numbers, from a scale. A number box beside the track lets users type the exact value.


HTML:

```html
<ui-slider label="Volume" name="volume" value="40"></ui-slider>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSlider label="Volume" name="volume" value={40} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Slider label="Volume" name="volume" defaultValue={40} />
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/slider
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-slider
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/slider.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/slider/slider-skeleton.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/slider/slider.styles.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/slider/slider.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-slider, shared-element, shared-field, shared-form-control, shared-localize, shared-row-wrap, shared-skeleton, shared-slots, tooltip, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-slider.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/slider.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-field, core-slider, tw-field, tw-i18n, tw-theme, tw-tooltip, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/slider';</script>

<ui-slider label="Volume" name="volume" value="40"></ui-slider>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiSlider } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';
import type { UiSlider as SliderElement } from '@purpurabog/ui';

<UiSlider label="Volume" name="volume" value={volume}
  onChange={(e) => setVolume((e.target as SliderElement).value)} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Slider } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/slider';

<Slider label="Volume" name="volume" value={volume} onChange={setVolume} />
```

The web component fires `input` while the value moves (dragging, keys, typing) and `change` when it is committed: the pointer released, a key handled, the number box left. In React those are `onInput` / `onChange` on `UiSlider`. The Tailwind `Slider` calls `onChange(value)` on every change and `onRelease(value)` on commits.

## Scale and step

`min` and `max` set the ends (0 and 100 by default) and `step` the increment (1). Arrow keys move one step; with Shift they move `step-multiplier` steps (4 by default). `min-label` and `max-label` add a unit after the end numbers.


HTML:

```html
<ui-slider label="Discount" min="0" max="50" step="5" value="10" min-label="%" max-label="%"></ui-slider>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSlider label="Discount" min={0} max={50} step={5} value={10} minLabel="%" maxLabel="%" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Slider label="Discount" min={0} max={50} step={5} defaultValue={10} minLabel="%" maxLabel="%" />
```

## Format the labels

For more control, the `formatLabel` property (a function `(value, label) => string`) formats the end labels and the value screen readers hear. It is a property on the web component and a prop in both React versions. With `hide-text-input`, the tooltip on the thumb uses it too, so money reads as money.


HTML:

```html
<ui-slider id="slider-budget" label="Training budget" min="0" max="10000" step="100" value="2500" hide-text-input></ui-slider>
<ui-slider id="slider-rent" label="Rent per month" min="0" max="50000" step="500" value="8000" value-upper="20000" hide-text-input></ui-slider>

<script type="module">
  const baht = (value) => `฿${value.toLocaleString('th-TH')}`;
  document.getElementById('slider-budget').formatLabel = baht;
  document.getElementById('slider-rent').formatLabel = baht;
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const baht = (value: number) => `฿${value.toLocaleString('th-TH')}`;

<UiSlider label="Training budget" min={0} max={10000} step={100} value={2500} hideTextInput formatLabel={baht} />
<UiSlider label="Rent per month" min={0} max={50000} step={500} value={8000} valueUpper={20000} hideTextInput formatLabel={baht} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const baht = (value: number) => `฿${value.toLocaleString('th-TH')}`;

<Slider label="Training budget" min={0} max={10000} step={100} defaultValue={2500} hideTextInput formatLabel={baht} />
<Slider label="Rent per month" min={0} max={50000} step={500} defaultValue={8000} defaultValueUpper={20000} hideTextInput formatLabel={baht} />
```

## Two handles: a range

Set `value-upper` and the slider picks a range from `value` to `value-upper`. The two thumbs never pass each other, a press on the track moves the nearer one, and each has its own number box: the lower one before the track, the upper one after.


HTML:

```html
<ui-slider id="slider-price" label="Price" min="0" max="1000" step="10" value="200" value-upper="600"
  name="min-price" name-upper="max-price"></ui-slider>
<p>Search from <output id="slider-price-out">200 to 600</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const price = document.getElementById('slider-price');
  price.addEventListener('change', () => {
    document.getElementById('slider-price-out').textContent = `${price.value} to ${price.valueUpper}`;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSlider label="Price" min={0} max={1000} step={10} value={200} valueUpper={600}
  name="min-price" nameUpper="max-price"
  onChange={(e) => {
    const slider = e.target as SliderElement;
    search(slider.value, slider.valueUpper);
  }} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Slider label="Price" min={0} max={1000} step={10} defaultValue={200} defaultValueUpper={600}
  name="min-price" nameUpper="max-price" onRelease={(low, high) => search(low, high)} />
```

The form gets both values: under `name-upper` for the upper one, or both under `name` when you leave `name-upper` out. The thumbs are named "Lower bound" and "Upper bound" after the slider's label; `input-label` and `upper-input-label` rename the number boxes.

## The number box

The box mirrors the value, and typing changes it:

- A number in range applies at once, snapped to the nearest step.
- On blur or Enter, a number outside `min` / `max` is clamped to the nearest end. Screen readers hear that it was corrected (`corrected-text` changes the words; `{value}` is the typed number).
- A box that holds no number (cleared, say) shows the error "Enter a number" and blocks submit until it is fixed.

`hide-text-input` removes the box and shows the value in a tooltip on the thumb instead:


HTML:

```html
<ui-slider label="Brightness" value="70" hide-text-input></ui-slider>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSlider label="Brightness" value={70} hideTextInput />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Slider label="Brightness" defaultValue={70} hideTextInput />
```

## Errors and warnings

`invalid` with `invalid-text` shows an error from your own validation and blocks submit; `warn` with `warn-text` shows a warning that doesn't. The slider has no helper line.


HTML:

```html
<ui-slider label="Team size" min="1" max="20" value="18" warn warn-text="Rooms hold 15 people."></ui-slider>
<ui-slider label="Retention period" min="0" max="120" value="6" max-label=" months" invalid invalid-text="Keep records for at least 12 months."></ui-slider>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSlider label="Team size" min={1} max={20} value={18} warn warnText="Rooms hold 15 people." />
<UiSlider label="Retention period" min={0} max={120} value={6} maxLabel=" months" invalid invalidText="Keep records for at least 12 months." />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Slider label="Team size" min={1} max={20} defaultValue={18} warn warnText="Rooms hold 15 people." />
<Slider label="Retention period" min={0} max={120} defaultValue={6} maxLabel=" months" invalid invalidText="Keep records for at least 12 months." />
```

How errors show across fields: [Forms and validation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/forms/).

## Read-only and disabled

`readonly` keeps the value and submits it; the thumb can't be moved and the number box can't be edited. A read-only thumb leaves the Tab order unless the box is hidden, so users still reach the value. `disabled` greys everything out and nothing is submitted.


HTML:

```html
<ui-slider label="Limit" value="30" readonly></ui-slider>
<ui-slider label="Limit" value="30" disabled></ui-slider>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSlider label="Limit" value={30} readonly />
<UiSlider label="Limit" value={30} disabled />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Slider label="Limit" defaultValue={30} readOnly />
<Slider label="Limit" defaultValue={30} disabled />
```

The web component and its React wrapper spell it `readonly`; React + Tailwind uses `readOnly`.

## Show the value as it moves

Use `input` to update what depends on the value while the thumb moves, and `change` to save once it settles. In React + Tailwind those are `onChange` and `onRelease`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-slider id="slider-down" label="Down payment" min="0" max="50" step="5" value="20" min-label="%" max-label="%"></ui-slider>
<p>On a ฿1,200,000 vehicle: <output id="slider-down-out">฿240,000</output>. Saved: <output id="slider-down-saved">20%</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const down = document.getElementById('slider-down');
  down.addEventListener('input', () => {
    document.getElementById('slider-down-out').textContent = `฿${(12000 * down.value).toLocaleString('th-TH')}`;
  });
  down.addEventListener('change', () => {
    document.getElementById('slider-down-saved').textContent = `${down.value}%`;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const [percent, setPercent] = useState(20);

<UiSlider label="Down payment" min={0} max={50} step={5} value={percent} minLabel="%" maxLabel="%"
  onInput={(e) => setPercent((e.target as SliderElement).value)}
  onChange={(e) => save((e.target as SliderElement).value)} />
<p>On a ฿1,200,000 vehicle: <output>฿{(12000 * percent).toLocaleString('th-TH')}</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [percent, setPercent] = useState(20);

<Slider label="Down payment" min={0} max={50} step={5} value={percent} minLabel="%" maxLabel="%"
  onChange={setPercent} onRelease={save} />
<p>On a ฿1,200,000 vehicle: <output>฿{(12000 * percent).toLocaleString('th-TH')}</output></p>
```

`save` stands for your own code.

## In a form

With a `name`, the slider submits its value with the form; a range also submits `name-upper`. Form reset puts the thumbs back where they started.


HTML:

```html
<form id="slider-form" method="dialog" style="display: grid; gap: 16px">
  <ui-slider label="Retention period" name="retention" min="0" max="120" value="36" max-label=" months"></ui-slider>
  <ui-slider label="Approval limit (฿)" name="limitFrom" name-upper="limitTo" min="0" max="500000" step="10000" value="50000" value-upper="200000"></ui-slider>
  <div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
    <ui-button type="submit">Save policy</ui-button>
    <ui-button type="reset" kind="secondary">Reset</ui-button>
  </div>
</form>
<p>Submitted: <output id="slider-form-out">nothing yet</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const form = document.getElementById('slider-form');
  form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const entries = [...new FormData(form)].map(([key, value]) => `${key}=${value}`);
    document.getElementById('slider-form-out').textContent = entries.join(', ');
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); save(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }}>
  <UiSlider label="Retention period" name="retention" min={0} max={120} value={36} maxLabel=" months" />
  <UiSlider label="Approval limit (฿)" name="limitFrom" nameUpper="limitTo" min={0} max={500000} step={10000} value={50000} valueUpper={200000} />
  <UiButton type="submit">Save policy</UiButton>
  <UiButton type="reset" kind="secondary">Reset</UiButton>
</form>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); save(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }}>
  <Slider label="Retention period" name="retention" min={0} max={120} defaultValue={36} maxLabel=" months" />
  <Slider label="Approval limit (฿)" name="limitFrom" nameUpper="limitTo" min={0} max={500000} step={10000} defaultValue={50000} defaultValueUpper={200000} />
  <Button type="submit">Save policy</Button>
  <Button type="reset" kind="secondary">Reset</Button>
</form>
```

## Skeleton

While the page loads its data, show `<ui-slider-skeleton>` in the slider's place, as Carbon's `SliderSkeleton`. `two-handles` (`twoHandles` in React + Tailwind) draws a range and `hide-label` leaves out the label bar. It has its own import, `@purpurabog/ui/slider-skeleton`, and is hidden from screen readers.


HTML:

```html
<ui-slider-skeleton></ui-slider-skeleton>
<ui-slider-skeleton two-handles></ui-slider-skeleton>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiSliderSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiSliderSkeleton />
<UiSliderSkeleton twoHandles />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { SliderSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/slider';

<SliderSkeleton />
<SliderSkeleton twoHandles />
```

## Keyboard

On a thumb:

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| ← / ↓ | One step down |
| → / ↑ | One step up |
| Shift + arrow | `step-multiplier` steps (4 by default) |
| Home / End | To `min` / `max` (in a range, as far as the other thumb allows) |

In the number box, Enter commits the typed number.

## Accessibility

- Each thumb is a `role="slider"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext`, named by the label. In a range each thumb's bounds stop at the other thumb.
- A click on the label focuses the thumb, as a label focuses a native range input.
- The number box is a native number input with its own name ("Slider number input", or "Lower bound" / "Upper bound"; `input-label` and `upper-input-label` change them).
- An error sets `aria-invalid` and is linked with `aria-describedby`. A clamped number is announced in a polite live region.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Slider](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-slider/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-slider>` · React `UiSlider`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `hide-label` | `hideLabel` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `value` | `value` | `number` | `0` |  |
| `value-upper` | `valueUpper` | `number \| null` | `null` | A second thumb: the slider picks the range `value`…`value-upper` (Carbon `unstable_valueUpper`). |
| `name-upper` | `nameUpper` | `string` | `''` | The name the upper value is submitted under (default: `name`, so the form gets both under one name). |
| `upper-input-label` | `upperInputLabel` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name of the upper number box (Carbon `unstable_ariaLabelInputUpper`; default "Upper bound"). |
| `min` | `min` | `number` | `0` |  |
| `max` | `max` | `number` | `100` |  |
| `step` | `step` | `number` | `1` |  |
| `step-multiplier` | `stepMultiplier` | `number` | `4` | Shift + arrow moves by `step × step-multiplier`. |
| `min-label` | `minLabel` | `string` | `''` | Appended to the min / max numbers, e.g. "%" (Carbon `minLabel` / `maxLabel`). |
| `max-label` | `maxLabel` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `input-label` | `inputLabel` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name of the number input (Carbon `ariaLabelInput`). |
| `hide-text-input` | `hideTextInput` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `readonly` | `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `required` | `required` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `invalid` | `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `invalid-text` | `invalidText` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `warn` | `warn` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `warn-text` | `warnText` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `corrected-text` | `correctedText` | `string` | `''` | Announcement after an out-of-range number is clamped; `{value}` is the typed number (Carbon auto-correct message). |

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `formatLabel` | `SliderFormatLabel` | Formats min / max labels and the value tooltip (Carbon `formatLabel`). |
| `willValidate` |  | (read-only) Whether the field takes part in constraint validation (not while disabled), as natively. |
| `labels` |  | (read-only) The `<label>`s that point at this field. |
| `isRange` |  | (read-only) Two thumbs (`value-upper` set). |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `setCustomValidity(message)` | Like `<input>.setCustomValidity()`: a non-empty message makes the field invalid (and is shown as its error once touched) until cleared with ''. |
| `focus(options)` | Focus the handle. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `input` | `onInput` |  |
| `change` | `onChange` |  |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| `label` | Rich label (overrides `label`) |
| `invalid-text` | Rich error text |
| `warn-text` | Rich warning text |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `label` | The label |
| `base` | Row with labels, track and input |
| `min-label` | Minimum label |
| `max-label` | Maximum label |
| `track` | The 2px track |
| `filled-track` | The filled part |
| `thumb` | The handle (`role=slider`) |
| `thumb-lower` | With `value-upper`: the lower handle (also `thumb`) |
| `thumb-upper` | With `value-upper`: the upper handle (also `thumb`) |
| `input` | The number input |
| `input-lower` | With `value-upper`: the lower bound's input (also `input`) |
| `input-upper` | With `value-upper`: the upper bound's input (also `input`) |
| `error-text` | Error text below |
| `invalid-text` | Same line as `error-text` (named after the `invalid-text` attribute / slot) |
| `warning-text` | Warning text below |
| `warn-text` | Same line as `warning-text` (named after the `warn-text` attribute / slot) |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-field-border` |  | / --ui-field-radius / --ui-field-background - The number box, as the other fields |
| `--ui-slider-fill` |  | The thumb, the filled track and the range handles (default `--ui-layer-selected-inverse`; Kanok: indigo) |
| `--ui-slider-handle-hover` |  | A range handle under the pointer (default `--ui-ink-muted`) |
| `--ui-slider-tick` |  | `display` of the mark at the middle of the track (default inline-block; Kanok: none) |
| `--ui-slider-range-handle-width` |  | / --ui-slider-range-handle-height / --ui-slider-range-lower-offset / --ui-slider-range-upper-offset - A range's handle box and where it sits on its value (default 16 × 24px, beside the value: Carbon's flags) |
| `--ui-slider-range-thumb` |  | / --ui-slider-range-thumb-hover / --ui-slider-range-thumb-inset / --ui-slider-range-thumb-radius / --ui-slider-range-focus-ring - A range thumb drawn in the handle (default none: the flag icons only; Kanok: a round dot) |
| `--ui-slider-range-gap` |  | / --ui-slider-range-icon-opacity - The gap where a flag meets the track and the flags' opacity (default the page colour, 1) |
