## Ask before closing

×, Esc and a click on the overlay fire `ui-request-close`, cancelable, with the `reason`: `close-button`, `escape` or `overlay`. Call `preventDefault()` to keep the panel open. `requestClose(reason)` asks the same way from your own button; setting `open` to false closes without asking. The panel below only closes with its Done button.


HTML:

```html
<div style="transform: translateZ(0); position: relative; height: 300px; overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid var(--ui-hairline); --ui-side-panel-top: 0px">
  <div style="padding: 16px">
    <ui-button id="side-panel-guard-open" kind="tertiary">Open checklist</ui-button>
    <p>Asked to close by: <output id="side-panel-guard-out"></output></p>
  </div>
  <ui-side-panel id="side-panel-guard" heading="Signing checklist" size="sm" include-overlay>
    <p>Tick every item, then press Done.</p>
    <ui-button slot="actions" id="side-panel-guard-done">Done</ui-button>
  </ui-side-panel>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const panel = document.getElementById('side-panel-guard');
  document.getElementById('side-panel-guard-open').addEventListener('click', () => (panel.open = true));
  document.getElementById('side-panel-guard-done').addEventListener('click', () => (panel.open = false));
  panel.addEventListener('ui-request-close', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    document.getElementById('side-panel-guard-out').value = event.detail.reason;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSidePanel open={open} heading="Signing checklist" includeOverlay onUiRequestClose={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); setReason(e.detail.reason); }} onUiClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
  <p>Tick every item, then press Done.</p>
  <UiButton slot="actions" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Done</UiButton>
</UiSidePanel>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// onRequestClose only reports: the panel stays open until you set open to false
<SidePanel open={open} onRequestClose={setReason} heading="Signing checklist" includeOverlay actions={[{ label: 'Done', onClick: () => setOpen(false) }]}>
  <p>Tick every item, then press Done.</p>
</SidePanel>
```

`ui-request-close` and `ui-close` bubble, so a notification inside fires them on the panel too: check that `event.target` is the panel. React's `UiSidePanel` does that for you: `onUiRequestClose` and `onUiClose` get only the panel's own events.

`hide-close-button` removes ×; then give the panel another way to close.

## Keyboard

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the panel's controls and wraps around inside it (not with `slide-in`) |
| Esc | Asks to close (`escape`; not with `slide-in`); focus goes back to what opened it |

## Accessibility

- The panel is a `complementary` landmark named by its `heading`.
- × is named "Close" and the back button "Back", in the page language, with a tooltip; `close-icon-description` and `navigation-back-icon-description` change them.
- A slide-over panel keeps Tab inside, but the page behind it is not inert: screen reader users can still reach it with their reading keys. Use a [Modal](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/modal/) when the page must be out of reach.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Side panel](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-side-panel/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-side-panel>` · React `UiSidePanel`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `open` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `placement` | `placement` | `'right' \| 'left'` | `'right'` |  |
| `size` | `size` | `SidePanelSize` | `'md'` | xs 16rem, sm 20rem, md 30rem, lg 40rem, xl 65rem, 2xl 80rem. |
| `heading` | `heading` | `string` | `''` | The heading (Carbon `title`); also the panel's accessible name. |
| `label-text` | `labelText` | `string` | `''` | A small label above the heading. |
| `slide-in` | `slideIn` | `boolean` | `false` | Push the page aside (`selector-page-content`) instead of covering it; no focus trap, no Esc. |
| `include-overlay` | `includeOverlay` | `boolean` | `false` | Dim the page; a click on it closes the panel (unless `prevent-close-on-click-outside`). |
| `prevent-close-on-click-outside` | `preventCloseOnClickOutside` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `selector-initial-focus` | `selectorInitialFocus` | `string` | `''` | What takes focus on open (a selector in the content), else the first control. |
| `selector-page-content` | `selectorPageContent` | `string` | `''` | The page element a slide-in panel pushes aside. |
| `hide-close-button` | `hideCloseButton` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `close-icon-description` | `closeIconDescription` | `string` | `''` | The × button's name and tooltip (default "Close", translated). |
| `close-icon-tooltip-alignment` | `closeIconTooltipAlignment` | `Placement` | `'left'` |  |
| `navigation-back-icon-description` | `navigationBackIconDescription` | `string` | `''` | The back button's name and tooltip (default "Back", translated). |
| `current-step` | `currentStep` | `number` | `0` | Above 0 shows the back button (a panel with steps). |
| `condensed-actions` | `condensedActions` | `boolean` | `false` | 48px action buttons instead of 64px. |
| `animate-title` | `animateTitle` | `boolean` | `true` | Shrink the heading as the content scrolls (Carbon's default). |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `requestClose(reason)` | Asks to close (cancelable `ui-request-close`), then closes. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-close` | `onUiClose` | After it closed |
| `ui-navigate-back` | `onUiNavigateBack` | The back button (`current-step` > 0) was pressed |
| `ui-request-close` | `onUiRequestClose` | Cancelable; detail: { reason: 'escape' \| 'close-button' \| 'overlay' } |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | The content |
| `subtitle` | Text under the heading |
| `above-title` | Content above the label and heading |
| `below-title` | Content under the subtitle |
| `action-toolbar` | Small buttons under the header (the first one with its label) |
| `actions` | The action buttons |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `panel` | The panel |
| `overlay` | The overlay of `include-overlay` |
| `header` | The header |
| `heading` | The heading |
| `body` | The content's box |
| `actions` | The row of action buttons |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-side-panel-top` |  | Where the panel starts (default 3rem, under the UI shell header) |
| `--ui-side-panel-radius` |  | Corner radius of the edge facing the page (default 0; Kanok: 12px) |
| `--ui-actions-gap` |  | / --ui-actions-padding - Gap between the action buttons and padding round them (default none: full-bleed buttons that touch; Kanok: 8px / 16px 20px) |
| `--ui-actions-button-flex` |  | `flex` of each action button (default: Carbon's widths by count; Kanok: their own width) |
| `--ui-actions-button-align` |  | / --ui-actions-button-padding-top - Where a button's label sits (default: at the top, 16px in) |
| `--ui-actions-stacked-direction` |  | / --ui-actions-stacked-wrap / --ui-actions-stacked-width - Where Carbon stacks the actions (narrow): `flex-direction`, `flex-wrap` and each button's width (default column-reverse, nowrap, 100%; Kanok: one row that wraps) |




---

# Tearsheet

A tearsheet is a large modal that rises from the bottom of the screen over the dimmed page. Use it for a task that needs room but keeps the user in the same place: creating a record, a form in several sections, a review with a side pane. It is Carbon for IBM Products' `Tearsheet`. For a short decision, use a [Modal](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/modal/); to keep the page in view, a [Side panel](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/side-panel/).


HTML:

```html
<ui-button id="tearsheet-open">New contract</ui-button>
<ui-tearsheet id="tearsheet-create" width="wide" heading="New contract" label="Legal" description="Fill in the parties and the term. You can add clauses after the contract is created." selector-initial-focus="#tearsheet-create-name">
  <div style="display: grid; gap: 16px; padding: 16px 32px">
    <ui-text-input id="tearsheet-create-name" label="Contract name"></ui-text-input>
    <ui-text-input label="Counterparty"></ui-text-input>
    <ui-date-picker label="Start date"></ui-date-picker>
  </div>
  <ui-button slot="actions" kind="ghost">Cancel</ui-button>
  <ui-button slot="actions" kind="secondary">Save draft</ui-button>
  <ui-button slot="actions">Create</ui-button>
</ui-tearsheet>

<script type="module">
  const sheet = document.getElementById('tearsheet-create');
  document.getElementById('tearsheet-open').addEventListener('click', () => (sheet.open = true));
  for (const button of sheet.querySelectorAll('[slot="actions"]')) button.addEventListener('click', () => (sheet.open = false));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<UiButton onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>New contract</UiButton>
<UiTearsheet open={open} width="wide" heading="New contract" label="Legal" description="Fill in the parties and the term. You can add clauses after the contract is created." selectorInitialFocus="#contract-name" onUiClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
  <UiTextInput id="contract-name" label="Contract name" />
  <UiTextInput label="Counterparty" />
  <UiDatePicker label="Start date" />
  <UiButton slot="actions" kind="ghost" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</UiButton>
  <UiButton slot="actions" kind="secondary" onClick={saveDraft}>Save draft</UiButton>
  <UiButton slot="actions" onClick={create}>Create</UiButton>
</UiTearsheet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>New contract</Button>
<Tearsheet
  open={open}
  onRequestClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  width="wide"
  heading="New contract"
  label="Legal"
  description="Fill in the parties and the term. You can add clauses after the contract is created."
  selectorInitialFocus="#contract-name"
  actions={[
    { label: 'Cancel', kind: 'ghost', onClick: () => setOpen(false) },
    { label: 'Save draft', kind: 'secondary', onClick: saveDraft },
    { label: 'Create', onClick: create },
  ]}
>
  <TextInput id="contract-name" label="Contract name" />
  <TextInput label="Counterparty" />
  <DatePicker label="Start date" />
</Tearsheet>
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tearsheet
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-tearsheet
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tearsheet.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/tearsheet/tearsheet.styles.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/tearsheet/tearsheet.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-modal, core-motion, core-overlay, layer, shared-action-set, shared-element, shared-events, shared-focus-ring, shared-localize, shared-quiet-focus, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-tearsheet.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/tearsheet.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-action-set, tw-action-set, tw-i18n, tw-layer, tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/tearsheet';</script>

<ui-button onclick="document.getElementById('new-contract').open = true">New contract</ui-button>
<ui-tearsheet id="new-contract" width="wide" heading="New contract">
  …
  <ui-button slot="actions">Create</ui-button>
</ui-tearsheet>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiTearsheet } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiTearsheet open={open} width="wide" heading="New contract" onUiClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
  …
  <UiButton slot="actions" onClick={create}>Create</UiButton>
</UiTearsheet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Tearsheet } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/tearsheet';

<Tearsheet open={open} onRequestClose={() => setOpen(false)} width="wide" heading="New contract" actions={[{ label: 'Create', onClick: create }]}>
  …
</Tearsheet>
```

Set `open` to show it and back to false to hide it. It is a native modal `<dialog>`: the page behind is inert and doesn't scroll, and Tab stays inside the sheet. On open, focus goes to `selector-initial-focus` (a selector inside the sheet), else to ×, else to the first control; on close it goes back to what had it. `ui-close` fires after the sheet has sunk back.

The content has no padding of its own: put your own around it, as in these examples. React + Tailwind is controlled: `onRequestClose(reason)` reports ×, Esc and a click outside, and you set `open` to false.

## Narrow

`width="narrow"` (the default) is Carbon's small modal width: 60%, 42% or 36% of the screen from medium, large and extra-large screens up. It starts 130px from the top; `vertical-position="normal"` moves it up to 90px, as a wide one. The heading is a size smaller, and the content sits on the layer instead of the background. React + Tailwind also has `TearsheetNarrow`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-button id="tearsheet-narrow-open" kind="tertiary">Rename department</ui-button>
<ui-tearsheet id="tearsheet-narrow" heading="Rename department" description="The new name shows on every contract the department owns.">
  <div style="padding: 16px">
    <ui-text-input label="Department name" value="Legal"></ui-text-input>
  </div>
  <ui-button slot="actions" kind="secondary">Cancel</ui-button>
  <ui-button slot="actions">Rename</ui-button>
</ui-tearsheet>

<script type="module">
  const sheet = document.getElementById('tearsheet-narrow');
  document.getElementById('tearsheet-narrow-open').addEventListener('click', () => (sheet.open = true));
  for (const button of sheet.querySelectorAll('[slot="actions"]')) button.addEventListener('click', () => (sheet.open = false));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTearsheet open={open} heading="Rename department" description="The new name shows on every contract the department owns." onUiClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
  <UiTextInput label="Department name" value="Legal" />
  <UiButton slot="actions" kind="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</UiButton>
  <UiButton slot="actions" onClick={rename}>Rename</UiButton>
</UiTearsheet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { TearsheetNarrow } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/tearsheet';

<TearsheetNarrow
  open={open}
  onRequestClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  heading="Rename department"
  description="The new name shows on every contract the department owns."
  actions={[
    { label: 'Cancel', kind: 'secondary', onClick: () => setOpen(false) },
    { label: 'Rename', onClick: rename },
  ]}
>
  <TextInput label="Department name" defaultValue="Legal" />
</TearsheetNarrow>
```

## Header actions and tabs

A wide tearsheet can carry small buttons in the header (`slot="header-actions"`) and tabs under the header text (`slot="header-navigation"`). Switch the content yourself on the tabs' `ui-tab-change`. React + Tailwind takes them in `headerActions` and `navigation`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-button id="tearsheet-tabs-open" kind="tertiary">Open contract</ui-button>
<ui-tearsheet id="tearsheet-tabs" width="wide" heading="CT-2026-0142" description="Office lease, 3rd floor." has-close-icon>
  <ui-button slot="header-actions" kind="secondary" size="sm">Export PDF</ui-button>
  <ui-tabs slot="header-navigation" id="tearsheet-tabs-nav" label="Contract sections">
    <ui-tab panel="parties">Parties</ui-tab>
    <ui-tab panel="terms">Terms</ui-tab>
    <ui-tab panel="history">History</ui-tab>
  </ui-tabs>
  <div style="padding: 16px 32px">
    <p data-section="parties">Siam Logistics Co., Ltd. and the company.</p>
    <p data-section="terms" hidden>24 months from 1 November 2026, 45,000 baht a month.</p>
    <p data-section="history" hidden>Signed by both parties on 9 October 2026.</p>
  </div>
  <ui-button slot="actions">Done</ui-button>
</ui-tearsheet>

<script type="module">
  const sheet = document.getElementById('tearsheet-tabs');
  document.getElementById('tearsheet-tabs-open').addEventListener('click', () => (sheet.open = true));
  sheet.querySelector('[slot="actions"]').addEventListener('click', () => (sheet.open = false));
  document.getElementById('tearsheet-tabs-nav').addEventListener('ui-tab-change', (event) => {
    for (const section of sheet.querySelectorAll('[data-section]')) section.hidden = section.dataset.section !== event.detail.name;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTearsheet open={open} width="wide" heading="CT-2026-0142" description="Office lease, 3rd floor." hasCloseIcon onUiClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
  <UiButton slot="header-actions" kind="secondary" size="sm">Export PDF</UiButton>
  <UiTabs slot="header-navigation" label="Contract sections" onUiTabChange={(e) => setSection(e.detail.name)}>
    <UiTab panel="parties">Parties</UiTab>
    <UiTab panel="terms">Terms</UiTab>
    <UiTab panel="history">History</UiTab>
  </UiTabs>
  <Section name={section} />
  <UiButton slot="actions" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Done</UiButton>
</UiTearsheet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Tearsheet
  open={open}
  onRequestClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  width="wide"
  heading="CT-2026-0142"
  description="Office lease, 3rd floor."
  hasCloseIcon
  headerActions={<Button kind="secondary" size="sm">Export PDF</Button>}
  navigation={
    <Tabs value={section} onValueChange={setSection}>
      <TabList label="Contract sections">
        <Tab value="parties">Parties</Tab>
        <Tab value="terms">Terms</Tab>
        <Tab value="history">History</Tab>
      </TabList>
    </Tabs>
  }
  actions={[{ label: 'Done', onClick: () => setOpen(false) }]}
>
  <Section name={section} />
</Tearsheet>
```

Both slots show only in a wide tearsheet.

## A side pane

`slot="influencer"` adds a pane beside the content of a wide tearsheet: a summary, the steps of a flow, a preview. It sits on the right; `influencer-placement="left"` moves it. `influencer-width` is `narrow` (256px, the default) or `wide` (320px). It scrolls on its own.


HTML:

```html
<ui-button id="tearsheet-pane-open" kind="tertiary">Review request</ui-button>
<ui-tearsheet id="tearsheet-pane" width="wide" heading="Review purchase request" influencer-placement="left">
  <div slot="influencer" style="display: grid; gap: 8px; padding: 16px">
    <strong>PR-2026-0318</strong>
    <span>IT department</span>
    <span>128,500 baht</span>
  </div>
  <div style="display: grid; gap: 16px; padding: 16px 32px">
    <ui-text-area label="Comment for the requester"></ui-text-area>
  </div>
  <ui-button slot="actions" kind="secondary">Return</ui-button>
  <ui-button slot="actions">Approve</ui-button>
</ui-tearsheet>

<script type="module">
  const sheet = document.getElementById('tearsheet-pane');
  document.getElementById('tearsheet-pane-open').addEventListener('click', () => (sheet.open = true));
  for (const button of sheet.querySelectorAll('[slot="actions"]')) button.addEventListener('click', () => (sheet.open = false));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTearsheet open={open} width="wide" heading="Review purchase request" influencerPlacement="left" onUiClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
  <div slot="influencer">
    <strong>PR-2026-0318</strong> …
  </div>
  <UiTextArea label="Comment for the requester" />
  <UiButton slot="actions" kind="secondary" onClick={sendBack}>Return</UiButton>
  <UiButton slot="actions" onClick={approve}>Approve</UiButton>
</UiTearsheet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Tearsheet
  open={open}
  onRequestClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  width="wide"
  heading="Review purchase request"
  influencer={<div><strong>PR-2026-0318</strong> …</div>}
  influencerPosition="left"
  actions={[
    { label: 'Return', kind: 'secondary', onClick: sendBack },
    { label: 'Approve', onClick: approve },
  ]}
>
  <TextArea label="Comment for the requester" />
</Tearsheet>
```

React + Tailwind calls the placement `influencerPosition`.

## Actions and the close button

Up to four `<ui-button slot="actions">` sit at the foot, laid out as Carbon's ActionSet (64px tall; 80px in a wide tearsheet); any more are hidden. With actions, there is no × unless you set `has-close-icon`. With no actions, × always shows, so a sheet that only shows information still closes.


HTML:

```html
<ui-button id="tearsheet-info-open" kind="tertiary">Signing log</ui-button>
<ui-tearsheet id="tearsheet-info" heading="Signing log" description="Who signed CT-2026-0142, and when.">
  <ul style="margin: 0; padding: 16px 32px">
    <li>Ananya P. signed on 8 October 2026, 10:42.</li>
    <li>Boonmee S. signed on 9 October 2026, 14:05.</li>
  </ul>
</ui-tearsheet>

<script type="module">
  const sheet = document.getElementById('tearsheet-info');
  document.getElementById('tearsheet-info-open').addEventListener('click', () => (sheet.open = true));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTearsheet open={open} heading="Signing log" description="Who signed CT-2026-0142, and when." onUiClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
  <ul>…</ul>
</UiTearsheet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Tearsheet open={open} onRequestClose={() => setOpen(false)} heading="Signing log" description="Who signed CT-2026-0142, and when.">
  <ul>…</ul>
</Tearsheet>
```

× is named "Close" in the page language; `close-icon-description` changes it.

## Rich label and description

`label` and `description` take plain text. For markup, use `slot="label"` and `slot="description"` instead, for example a link in the description.


HTML:

```html
<ui-button id="tearsheet-rich-open" kind="tertiary">Data request</ui-button>
<ui-tearsheet id="tearsheet-rich" heading="Personal data request">
  <span slot="label">PDPA · <strong>Due in 3 days</strong></span>
  <span slot="description">Answer within 30 days of the request. <ui-link href="#tearsheet-rich-open">Read the policy</ui-link></span>
  <div style="padding: 16px">
    <ui-text-area label="Answer to the data subject"></ui-text-area>
  </div>
  <ui-button slot="actions">Send answer</ui-button>
</ui-tearsheet>

<script type="module">
  const sheet = document.getElementById('tearsheet-rich');
  document.getElementById('tearsheet-rich-open').addEventListener('click', () => (sheet.open = true));
  sheet.querySelector('[slot="actions"]').addEventListener('click', () => (sheet.open = false));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTearsheet open={open} heading="Personal data request" onUiClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
  <span slot="label">PDPA · <strong>Due in 3 days</strong></span>
  <span slot="description">Answer within 30 days of the request. <UiLink href="/policy">Read the policy</UiLink></span>
  …
</UiTearsheet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Tearsheet
  open={open}
  onRequestClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  heading="Personal data request"
  label={<>PDPA · <strong>Due in 3 days</strong></>}
  description={<>Answer within 30 days of the request. <Link href="/policy">Read the policy</Link></>}
  actions={[{ label: 'Send answer', onClick: send }]}
>
  …
</Tearsheet>
```

## Stacked tearsheets

A tearsheet can open another one over it. The one underneath scales back (to 95%, then 90%) and the page dims less, up to three deep. Each closes on its own, newest first.


HTML:

```html
<ui-button id="tearsheet-stack-open" kind="tertiary">Open the contract</ui-button>
<ui-tearsheet id="tearsheet-stack-1" width="wide" heading="CT-2026-0142" description="Step 1 of a nested flow.">
  <div style="padding: 16px 32px"><ui-button data-next="tearsheet-stack-2" kind="tertiary">Add a party</ui-button></div>
  <ui-button slot="actions">Done</ui-button>
</ui-tearsheet>
<ui-tearsheet id="tearsheet-stack-2" width="wide" heading="Add a party" description="Step 2: over the contract.">
  <div style="padding: 16px 32px"><ui-button data-next="tearsheet-stack-3" kind="tertiary">Add a new company</ui-button></div>
  <ui-button slot="actions">Add</ui-button>
</ui-tearsheet>
<ui-tearsheet id="tearsheet-stack-3" width="wide" heading="New company" description="Step 3: the top one.">
  <div style="padding: 16px 32px"><ui-text-input label="Company name"></ui-text-input></div>
  <ui-button slot="actions">Save</ui-button>
</ui-tearsheet>

<script type="module">
  document.getElementById('tearsheet-stack-open').addEventListener('click', () => (document.getElementById('tearsheet-stack-1').open = true));
  for (const n of [1, 2, 3]) {
    const sheet = document.getElementById(`tearsheet-stack-${n}`);
    sheet.querySelector('[slot="actions"]').addEventListener('click', () => (sheet.open = false));
    sheet.querySelector('[data-next]')?.addEventListener('click', (event) => (document.getElementById(event.currentTarget.dataset.next).open = true));
  }
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTearsheet open={contractOpen} width="wide" heading="CT-2026-0142" onUiClose={() => setContractOpen(false)}>
  <UiButton kind="tertiary" onClick={() => setPartyOpen(true)}>Add a party</UiButton>
  …
</UiTearsheet>
<UiTearsheet open={partyOpen} width="wide" heading="Add a party" onUiClose={() => setPartyOpen(false)}>…</UiTearsheet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Tearsheet open={contractOpen} onRequestClose={() => setContractOpen(false)} width="wide" heading="CT-2026-0142">
  <Button kind="tertiary" onClick={() => setPartyOpen(true)}>Add a party</Button>
</Tearsheet>
<Tearsheet open={partyOpen} onRequestClose={() => setPartyOpen(false)} width="wide" heading="Add a party">…</Tearsheet>
```

## Ask before closing

×, Esc and a click outside the sheet fire `ui-request-close`, cancelable, with the `reason`: `close-button`, `escape` or `outside`. Call `preventDefault()` to keep it open. `prevent-close-on-click-outside` turns the outside click off altogether, which suits a form people type into. Type something below, then press Esc.


HTML:

```html
<ui-button id="tearsheet-guard-open" kind="tertiary">Write a memo</ui-button>
<ui-tearsheet id="tearsheet-guard" heading="New memo" has-close-icon prevent-close-on-click-outside>
  <div style="display: grid; gap: 16px; padding: 16px">
    <ui-notification id="tearsheet-guard-warning" kind="warning" low-contrast open="false" heading="The memo isn't saved" subtitle="Close again to discard it."></ui-notification>
    <ui-text-area id="tearsheet-guard-text" label="Memo"></ui-text-area>
  </div>
  <ui-button slot="actions" id="tearsheet-guard-save">Save</ui-button>
</ui-tearsheet>
<p>Asked to close by: <output id="tearsheet-guard-out"></output></p>

<script type="module">
  const sheet = document.getElementById('tearsheet-guard');
  const text = document.getElementById('tearsheet-guard-text');
  const warning = document.getElementById('tearsheet-guard-warning');
  document.getElementById('tearsheet-guard-open').addEventListener('click', () => {
    text.value = '';
    warning.open = false;
    sheet.open = true;
  });
  document.getElementById('tearsheet-guard-save').addEventListener('click', () => (sheet.open = false));
  sheet.addEventListener('ui-request-close', (event) => {
    if (event.target !== sheet) return; // the notification inside asks too
    document.getElementById('tearsheet-guard-out').value = event.detail.reason;
    if (text.value && !warning.open) {
      event.preventDefault();
      warning.open = true;
    }
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTearsheet
  open={open}
  heading="New memo"
  hasCloseIcon
  preventCloseOnClickOutside
  onUiRequestClose={(e) => { if (dirty && !warned) { e.preventDefault(); setWarned(true); } }}
  onUiClose={() => setOpen(false)}
>
  <UiNotification kind="warning" lowContrast open={warned} heading="The memo isn't saved" subtitle="Close again to discard it." />
  <UiTextArea label="Memo" />
  <UiButton slot="actions" onClick={save}>Save</UiButton>
</UiTearsheet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// onRequestClose only reports: the sheet stays open until you set open to false
<Tearsheet
  open={open}
  onRequestClose={() => { if (dirty && !warned) setWarned(true); else setOpen(false); }}
  heading="New memo"
  hasCloseIcon
  preventCloseOnClickOutside
  actions={[{ label: 'Save', onClick: save }]}
>
  <Notification kind="warning" lowContrast open={warned} title="The memo isn't saved" subtitle="Close again to discard it." />
  <TextArea label="Memo" />
</Tearsheet>
```

`ui-request-close` and `ui-close` bubble, so a notification inside fires them on the tearsheet too: check that `event.target` is the tearsheet. React's `UiTearsheet` does that for you: `onUiRequestClose` and `onUiClose` get only the tearsheet's own events. `requestClose(reason)` asks from your own button; setting `open` to false closes without asking.

## Keyboard

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the sheet's controls and wraps around inside it |
| Esc | Asks to close (`escape`); focus goes back to what opened it |

## Accessibility

- It is a native modal `<dialog>`, named by its `heading`: the page behind it is inert for the mouse, the keyboard and screen readers.
- Give every tearsheet a `heading`; without one the dialog has no name.
- × is named "Close" in the page language; `close-icon-description` changes it.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Tearsheet](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-tearsheet/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-tearsheet>` · React `UiTearsheet`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `open` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `width` | `width` | `'narrow' \| 'wide'` | `'narrow'` | narrow: Carbon's small modal; wide: the whole screen but 64px each side. |
| `vertical-position` | `verticalPosition` | `'normal' \| 'lower' \| undefined` |  | How far from the top the sheet starts: normal 90px, lower 130px (default lower for a narrow one). |
| `heading` | `heading` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | A small label above the heading. |
| `description` | `description` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `influencer-placement` | `influencerPlacement` | `'left' \| 'right'` | `'right'` |  |
| `influencer-width` | `influencerWidth` | `'narrow' \| 'wide'` | `'narrow'` |  |
| `has-close-icon` | `hasCloseIcon` | `boolean` | `false` | Show the × even with actions (it always shows without them). |
| `close-icon-description` | `closeIconDescription` | `string` | `''` | The ×'s name (default "Close", translated). |
| `prevent-close-on-click-outside` | `preventCloseOnClickOutside` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `selector-initial-focus` | `selectorInitialFocus` | `string` | `''` | What takes focus on open (a selector in the content), else × or the first control. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `placeInStack(position, depth)` | Called by the stack: this sheet's place among the open ones (position 1 = oldest) and how many show. |
| `requestClose(reason)` | Asks to close (cancelable `ui-request-close`), then closes. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-close` | `onUiClose` | After it closed |
| `ui-request-close` | `onUiRequestClose` | Cancelable; detail: { reason: 'escape' \| 'close-button' \| 'outside' } |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | The content |
| `label` | Rich label (instead of `label`) |
| `description` | Rich description (instead of `description`), e.g. a `<ui-truncated-text>` |
| `header-actions` | Small buttons in the header (wide) |
| `header-navigation` | Tabs under the header text (wide) |
| `influencer` | A side pane beside the content (wide) |
| `actions` | Up to four action buttons |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `dialog` | The full-screen dialog |
| `container` | The sheet |
| `header` | The header |
| `heading` | The heading |
| `close-button` | The × |
| `influencer` | The side pane |
| `content` | The content's box |
| `actions` | The row of action buttons |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-tearsheet-radius` |  | Corner radius of the top corners (default 0; Kanok: 12px) |
| `--ui-actions-gap` |  | / --ui-actions-padding - Gap between the action buttons and padding round them (default none: full-bleed buttons that touch; Kanok: 8px / 16px 20px) |
| `--ui-actions-button-flex` |  | `flex` of each action button (default: Carbon's widths by count; Kanok: their own width) |
| `--ui-actions-button-align` |  | / --ui-actions-button-padding-top - Where a button's label sits (default: at the top, 16px in) |
| `--ui-actions-stacked-direction` |  | / --ui-actions-stacked-wrap / --ui-actions-stacked-width - Where Carbon stacks the actions (narrow): `flex-direction`, `flex-wrap` and each button's width (default column-reverse, nowrap, 100%; Kanok: one row that wraps) |
| `--ui-close-size` |  | Size of the × button (default 48px; Kanok: 32px) |
| `--ui-close-inset` |  | Margin that sets the × in from the corner (default 0; Kanok: 8px) |
| `--ui-icon-control-radius` |  | Corners of the ×, its hover fill and its ring (default 0; Kanok: round) |
| `--ui-focus-offset` |  | `outline-offset` of the ×'s focus ring (default -2px: inside; Kanok: 2px outside) |




---

# Notification

A notification tells the user about a change or a problem: a file that failed to upload, a draft that was restored, a policy that applies to the page. One element covers Carbon's inline, actionable, toast and callout notifications. For toasts that stack in the corner of the screen, see [Toast](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/toast/).


HTML:

```html
<ui-notification kind="error" heading="Upload failed" subtitle="contract.pdf is larger than 25 MB."></ui-notification>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNotification kind="error" heading="Upload failed" subtitle="contract.pdf is larger than 25 MB." />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Notification kind="error" title="Upload failed" subtitle="contract.pdf is larger than 25 MB." />
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/notification
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-notification
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/notification.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/notification/notification.styles.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/notification/notification.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-notification, shared-element, shared-events, shared-field, shared-localize, shared-slots, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-notification.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/notification.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-notification, tw-i18n, tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/notification';</script>

<ui-notification kind="success" heading="Contract sent" subtitle="3 signers were notified."></ui-notification>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiNotification } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiNotification kind="success" heading="Contract sent" subtitle="3 signers were notified." />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Notification } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/notification';

<Notification kind="success" title="Contract sent" subtitle="3 signers were notified." />
```

`heading` is the bold title (`title` in React + Tailwind) and `subtitle` the text after it. The default `kind` is `error`, so always set it. An inline notification is 288px to 832px wide, depending on the screen.

## Kinds

`kind` sets the colour and the icon: `error`, `success`, `info`, `info-square`, `warning` and `warning-alt`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-notification kind="error" heading="Payment failed" subtitle="The bank declined the transfer."></ui-notification>
<ui-notification kind="success" heading="Contract signed" subtitle="All parties have signed."></ui-notification>
<ui-notification kind="info" heading="New template" subtitle="Lease 2026 is ready to use."></ui-notification>
<ui-notification kind="info-square" heading="Read only" subtitle="This contract is archived."></ui-notification>
<ui-notification kind="warning" heading="Stamp duty unpaid" subtitle="Pay it before the contract is filed."></ui-notification>
<ui-notification kind="warning-alt" heading="Expires soon" subtitle="The lease ends on 31 October 2026."></ui-notification>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNotification kind="error" heading="Payment failed" subtitle="The bank declined the transfer." />
<UiNotification kind="success" heading="Contract signed" subtitle="All parties have signed." />
<UiNotification kind="info" heading="New template" subtitle="Lease 2026 is ready to use." />
<UiNotification kind="info-square" heading="Read only" subtitle="This contract is archived." />
<UiNotification kind="warning" heading="Stamp duty unpaid" subtitle="Pay it before the contract is filed." />
<UiNotification kind="warning-alt" heading="Expires soon" subtitle="The lease ends on 31 October 2026." />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Notification kind="error" title="Payment failed" subtitle="The bank declined the transfer." />
<Notification kind="success" title="Contract signed" subtitle="All parties have signed." />
<Notification kind="info" title="New template" subtitle="Lease 2026 is ready to use." />
<Notification kind="info-square" title="Read only" subtitle="This contract is archived." />
<Notification kind="warning" title="Stamp duty unpaid" subtitle="Pay it before the contract is filed." />
<Notification kind="warning-alt" title="Expires soon" subtitle="The lease ends on 31 October 2026." />
```

## Low contrast

A notification is dark (the inverse surface) by default. `low-contrast` gives it a light tint of its kind with a thin border instead, which sits more quietly in a form.


HTML:

```html
<ui-notification kind="info" low-contrast heading="Auto-save is on" subtitle="Changes are saved every minute."></ui-notification>
<ui-notification kind="warning" low-contrast heading="Owner on leave" subtitle="Ananya P. is away until 20 October."></ui-notification>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNotification kind="info" lowContrast heading="Auto-save is on" subtitle="Changes are saved every minute." />
<UiNotification kind="warning" lowContrast heading="Owner on leave" subtitle="Ananya P. is away until 20 October." />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Notification kind="info" lowContrast title="Auto-save is on" subtitle="Changes are saved every minute." />
<Notification kind="warning" lowContrast title="Owner on leave" subtitle="Ananya P. is away until 20 October." />
```

## Links and other content

When the title or subtitle needs markup, put it in `slot="title"` or `slot="subtitle"`. Anything without a slot goes after the subtitle: a link, a short list. React + Tailwind takes markup in `title` and `subtitle`, and extra content as children.


HTML:

```html
<ui-notification kind="warning" low-contrast heading="Stamp duty">
  <span slot="subtitle">Not paid yet for <strong>CT-2026-0142</strong>.</span>
  <a href="#notification-pay">Pay now</a>
</ui-notification>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNotification kind="warning" lowContrast heading="Stamp duty">
  <span slot="subtitle">Not paid yet for <strong>CT-2026-0142</strong>.</span>
  <a href="/stamp-duty">Pay now</a>
</UiNotification>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Notification kind="warning" lowContrast title="Stamp duty" subtitle={<>Not paid yet for <strong>CT-2026-0142</strong>.</>}>
  <a href="/stamp-duty">Pay now</a>
</Notification>
```

## With an action

`action-label` adds a button for one quick action, such as Undo or Retry (Carbon's actionable notification). Pressing it fires `ui-action`; it doesn't close the notification. An actionable notification becomes an `alertdialog`: when it appears, focus moves to the action button, Tab goes round its own controls, and Esc closes it while focus is inside it (as Carbon: an Esc meant for something else, such as a modal, leaves it open). Add `no-autofocus` when it is on the page from the start, as here, so it doesn't take focus from the page.


HTML:

```html
<ui-notification id="notification-undo" kind="info" heading="Draft deleted" subtitle="Lease draft for the 3rd floor." action-label="Undo" no-autofocus></ui-notification>
<p>Action: <output id="notification-undo-out"></output></p>

<script type="module">
  const note = document.getElementById('notification-undo');
  note.addEventListener('ui-action', () => {
    document.getElementById('notification-undo-out').value = 'restored';
    note.close();
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNotification kind="info" heading="Draft deleted" subtitle="Lease draft for the 3rd floor." actionLabel="Undo" noAutofocus onUiAction={restore} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(true);

<Notification kind="info" title="Draft deleted" subtitle="Lease draft for the 3rd floor." actionLabel="Undo" noAutofocus onAction={() => { restore(); setOpen(false); }} open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} />
```

`close()` closes it the way × does; it is described under [Closing](#closing).

## Callout

`variant="callout"` is a static box of guidance that belongs to the page, not a message about something that just happened. It has no role, no close button and never takes focus. Its action button is described by the title.


HTML:

```html
<ui-notification variant="callout" kind="info" heading="Signing closes on Friday" subtitle="Two signers have not opened the document yet." action-label="Send reminder"></ui-notification>
<ui-notification variant="callout" kind="warning" low-contrast heading="Retention policy" subtitle="Archived requests are deleted after 10 years."></ui-notification>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNotification variant="callout" kind="info" heading="Signing closes on Friday" subtitle="Two signers have not opened the document yet." actionLabel="Send reminder" onUiAction={remind} />
<UiNotification variant="callout" kind="warning" lowContrast heading="Retention policy" subtitle="Archived requests are deleted after 10 years." />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Notification variant="callout" kind="info" title="Signing closes on Friday" subtitle="Two signers have not opened the document yet." actionLabel="Send reminder" onAction={remind} />
<Notification variant="callout" kind="warning" lowContrast title="Retention policy" subtitle="Archived requests are deleted after 10 years." />
```

## Toast look

`variant="toast"` is the 288px card with a shadow that Carbon uses for toasts: the text stacks, `caption` adds a small line (often the time), and the action becomes a tertiary button under the text. To show toasts in the corner of the screen and stack them, use the toaster: [Toast](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/toast/).


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: flex-start">
  <ui-notification variant="toast" kind="success" heading="Contract sent" subtitle="3 signers were notified." caption="10:42"></ui-notification>
  <ui-notification variant="toast" kind="error" low-contrast heading="Upload failed" subtitle="Try a smaller file." action-label="Retry" no-autofocus></ui-notification>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNotification variant="toast" kind="success" heading="Contract sent" subtitle="3 signers were notified." caption="10:42" />
<UiNotification variant="toast" kind="error" lowContrast heading="Upload failed" subtitle="Try a smaller file." actionLabel="Retry" noAutofocus />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Notification variant="toast" kind="success" title="Contract sent" subtitle="3 signers were notified." caption="10:42" />
<Notification variant="toast" kind="error" lowContrast title="Upload failed" subtitle="Try a smaller file." actionLabel="Retry" noAutofocus />
```

## Close after a time

`timeout` closes the notification by itself after that many milliseconds (reason `timeout`). The countdown pauses while the pointer is over it or focus is inside it, and a notification with an action never closes by itself, so nobody loses a message they are reading. Hover the toast below to hold it.


HTML:

```html
<ui-notification id="notification-timeout" variant="toast" kind="info" heading="Saved" subtitle="This closes after 5 seconds." timeout="5000"></ui-notification>
<ui-button id="notification-timeout-again" kind="tertiary" size="sm">Show again</ui-button>

<script type="module">
  const note = document.getElementById('notification-timeout');
  document.getElementById('notification-timeout-again').addEventListener('click', () => (note.open = true));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNotification variant="toast" kind="info" heading="Saved" subtitle="This closes after 5 seconds." timeout={5000} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Notification variant="toast" kind="info" title="Saved" subtitle="This closes after 5 seconds." timeout={5000} />
```

Setting `open` back to true shows it again and starts the countdown afresh.

## Full width

`full-width` lets an inline notification or a callout fill its container instead of stopping at Carbon's widths: a banner across the top of a page or a card. A toast stays 288px.


HTML:

```html
<ui-notification kind="info" low-contrast full-width heading="Scheduled maintenance" subtitle="The contract system is read-only tonight from 22:00 to 23:00."></ui-notification>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNotification kind="info" lowContrast fullWidth heading="Scheduled maintenance" subtitle="The contract system is read-only tonight from 22:00 to 23:00." />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Notification kind="info" lowContrast fullWidth title="Scheduled maintenance" subtitle="The contract system is read-only tonight from 22:00 to 23:00." />
```

## Closing

×, Esc (on an actionable one) and the timeout fire `ui-request-close`, cancelable, with the `reason`: `close-button`, `escape` or `timeout`. Unless you call `preventDefault()`, the notification sets `open` to false (it stays in the page, hidden) and fires `ui-close`. If focus was inside it, focus goes back to where it was before. `hide-close-button` removes × when the message must stay until the problem is fixed.


HTML:

```html
<ui-notification id="notification-close" kind="success" heading="Approval sent" subtitle="Chaiya R. will get an email."></ui-notification>
<ui-notification kind="error" hide-close-button heading="Bank account missing" subtitle="Add the vendor's account before you pay."></ui-notification>
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button id="notification-close-again" kind="tertiary" size="sm">Show again</ui-button>
  <span>Closed by: <output id="notification-close-out"></output></span>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const note = document.getElementById('notification-close');
  note.addEventListener('ui-close', (event) => (document.getElementById('notification-close-out').value = event.detail.reason));
  document.getElementById('notification-close-again').addEventListener('click', () => (note.open = true));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNotification kind="success" heading="Approval sent" subtitle="Chaiya R. will get an email." open={open} onUiClose={(e) => { setOpen(false); setReason(e.detail.reason); }} />
<UiNotification kind="error" hideCloseButton heading="Bank account missing" subtitle="Add the vendor's account before you pay." />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// return false from onClose to keep it open
<Notification kind="success" title="Approval sent" subtitle="Chaiya R. will get an email." open={open} onClose={(reason) => { setOpen(false); setReason(reason); }} />
<Notification kind="error" hideCloseButton title="Bank account missing" subtitle="Add the vendor's account before you pay." />
```

Without `open`, the React + Tailwind notification hides itself when it closes.

## Errors after a submit

A notification can sum up what blocks a form. It is a polite `status` by default; `role="alert"` makes screen readers announce it at once, for an error the user must deal with now. Press Check below.


HTML:

```html
<ui-notification id="notification-check" kind="error" role="alert" open="false" heading="2 problems" subtitle="Add the counterparty's tax ID and the start date."></ui-notification>
<ui-button id="notification-check-run">Check contract</ui-button>

<script type="module">
  const note = document.getElementById('notification-check');
  document.getElementById('notification-check-run').addEventListener('click', () => (note.open = true));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiNotification kind="error" role="alert" open={errors.length > 0} heading={`${errors.length} problems`} subtitle={errors.join(' ')} />
<UiButton onClick={check}>Check contract</UiButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Notification kind="error" role="alert" open={errors.length > 0} title={`${errors.length} problems`} subtitle={errors.join(' ')} />
<Button onClick={check}>Check contract</Button>
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Reaches the content's links, the action button and × in order; in an actionable notification it goes round them |
| Enter, Space | Press the focused button |
| Esc | Closes an actionable notification while focus is inside it (`close-on-escape="false"` turns it off) |

## Accessibility

- The role is `status` by default (announced politely), none for a callout, and `alertdialog` with an action, named by the title and described by the subtitle. `role` sets another, such as `alert`.
- Screen readers announce changes inside a live region; a notification added to the page together with its text may not be read. The [toaster](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/toast/) keeps one region in the page for its toasts, so every toast is announced.
- The icon is named after the kind ("error icon"); `icon-label` changes it. × is named "Close notification" in the page language; `close-label` changes it.
- Don't put a `timeout` on a message people need to act on.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Notification](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-notification/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-notification>` · React `UiNotification`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` |  |  |  |  |
| `role` |  |  |  |  |
| `variant` | `variant` | `NotificationVariant` | `'inline'` | Inline (default) or toast. |
| `kind` | `kind` | `NotificationKind` | `'error'` | Status kind; sets the colour and the icon. |
| `low-contrast` | `lowContrast` | `boolean` | `false` | Tinted surface with primary text instead of the inverse surface. |
| `heading` | `heading` | `string` | `''` | Bold title; the `title` slot replaces it when markup is needed. (Before 0.5: the `title` attribute, still accepted.) |
| `subtitle` | `subtitle` | `string` | `''` | Body text; the `subtitle` slot replaces it when markup is needed. |
| `caption` | `caption` | `string` | `''` | Toast only: small text under the subtitle, e.g. the time. |
| `action-label` | `actionLabel` | `string` | `''` | Label of the action button; set it to get Carbon's actionable notification. |
| `timeout` | `timeout` | `number` | `0` | Milliseconds after which the notification closes itself (toast); 0 = never. Paused on hover / focus; ignored with `action-label`. |
| `hide-close-button` | `hideCloseButton` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `close-on-escape` | `closeOnEscape` | `boolean` | `true` | Esc closes an actionable notification while focus is inside it (Carbon `closeOnEscape`). |
| `no-autofocus` | `noAutofocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep focus where it is instead of moving it to the action button (Carbon `hasFocus={false}`). |
| `full-width` | `fullWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | Fills its container instead of Carbon's 288–832px cap (inline / callout; a toast stays 288px). |
| `close-label` | `closeLabel` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name of the close button. |
| `icon-label` | `iconLabel` | `string` | `''` | Accessible description of the status icon; defaults to "`kind` icon" (e.g. "error icon") like Carbon. |
| `open` | `open` | `boolean` | `true` | False once closed (reflects `open="false"`); set back to true to show it again. |

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | `NotificationRole \| null` | ARIA role of the notification box; defaults to `status`, or `alertdialog` when there is an action button. A `role` attribute is read and moved inside. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `close(reason)` | Asks to close (`ui-request-close`, cancelable); hides and fires `ui-close` unless prevented. |
| `focus(options)` | Focus the action button, else the close button. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-close` | `onUiClose` | After it closed |
| `ui-action` | `onUiAction` | The action button was pressed |
| `ui-request-close` | `onUiRequestClose` | Cancelable; detail: { reason: 'close-button' \| 'escape' \| 'timeout' } |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | Extra content after the subtitle (links, details) |
| `title` | Title with markup; the `heading` attribute is the plain-text fallback |
| `subtitle` | Subtitle with markup; the `subtitle` attribute is the plain-text fallback |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The notification box |
| `icon` | The status icon |
| `title` | The title |
| `subtitle` | The subtitle |
| `caption` | The toast caption |
| `action-button` | The action button |
| `close-button` | The close button |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-notification-radius` |  | Corner radius (default 0; Kanok: 8px) |
| `--ui-notification-bar-width` |  | Width of the status bar at the start (default 3px; Kanok: 0, the icon tells the kind) |
| `--ui-notification-frame-start` |  | Low contrast: the frame's start side (default 0, the bar is there; Kanok: 1px) |
| `--ui-notification-background` |  | / --ui-notification-ink / --ui-notification-edge - The high-contrast box: fill, text and an extra `box-shadow` (default Carbon's inverse block, none; Kanok: the raised floating surface) |
| `--ui-notification-link` |  | / --ui-notification-hover / --ui-notification-focus - On that box: links and the action, the action's hover and the focus ring (default link-inverse, inverse hover, inverse ink) |
| `--ui-toast-shadow` |  | A toast's shadow (default `0 2px 6px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.2)`) |
| `--ui-close-size` |  | Size of the × button (default 48px; Kanok: 32px) |
| `--ui-close-inset` |  | Margin that sets the × in from the corner (default 0; Kanok: 8px) |
| `--ui-icon-control-radius` |  | Corners of the ×, its hover fill and its ring (default 0; Kanok: round) |
| `--ui-focus-offset` |  | `outline-offset` of the ×'s focus ring (default -2px: inside; Kanok: 2px outside) |




---

# Toast

A toast is a short message that appears in the corner of the screen after something happened elsewhere on the page: a contract saved, an upload that failed in the background. Toasts stack, the newest nearest the corner, and the quiet ones go away by themselves. Carbon has no toast manager; `ui-toaster` and `toast()` are this library's. For a message that belongs in the page, use an inline [Notification](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/notification/).


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button id="toast-save">Save contract</ui-button>
  <ui-toaster></ui-toaster>
</div>

<script type="module">
  // what toast({ kind: 'success', title: 'Contract saved', subtitle: 'CT-2026-0142' }) does
  const toaster = document.querySelector('ui-toaster');
  document.getElementById('toast-save').addEventListener('click', () => {
    const toast = document.createElement('ui-notification');
    Object.assign(toast, { variant: 'toast', role: 'none', kind: 'success', heading: 'Contract saved', subtitle: 'CT-2026-0142', timeout: 5000 });
    toaster.add(toast);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
import { toast } from '@purpurabog/ui/toaster';

<UiButton onClick={() => toast({ kind: 'success', title: 'Contract saved', subtitle: 'CT-2026-0142' })}>Save contract</UiButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { toast } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/toaster';

<Button onClick={() => toast({ kind: 'success', title: 'Contract saved', subtitle: 'CT-2026-0142' })}>Save contract</Button>
```

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { toast } from '@purpurabog/ui/toaster';

  document.getElementById('save').addEventListener('click', () => {
    toast({ kind: 'success', title: 'Contract saved', subtitle: 'CT-2026-0142' });
  });
</script>

<ui-button id="save">Save contract</ui-button>
```

React:

```tsx
import { toast } from '@purpurabog/ui/toaster';

<UiButton onClick={() => toast({ kind: 'success', title: 'Contract saved', subtitle: 'CT-2026-0142' })}>Save contract</UiButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Toaster, toast } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/toaster';

// once, near the root of the app
<Toaster />

<Button onClick={() => toast({ kind: 'success', title: 'Contract saved', subtitle: 'CT-2026-0142' })}>Save contract</Button>
```

`toast(options)` creates a `<ui-notification variant="toast">` and adds it to the page's `<ui-toaster>`, which it creates at the end of `<body>` the first time. It returns `{ element, close }`. The options are `kind`, `title`, `subtitle`, `caption`, `timeout`, `actionLabel`, `onAction`, `lowContrast` and `id`.

The live examples on this page can't import a module, so they do what `toast()` does by hand: create the element and pass it to the toaster's `add()`. In your app, call `toast()`. React + Tailwind has its own `toast()` and a `<Toaster>` you mount once; it returns `{ close }`, and `toast.clear()` removes every toast.

The toaster is one polite live region named "Notifications", in the page before any toast, so screen readers announce each one. It sits in the top layer, 16px from the top end corner, or 16px under a `ui-header`.

## Kinds and how long they stay

`kind` is `info` by default. Info and success toasts close after 5 seconds; error and warning toasts stay until they are closed, because they need reading. `timeout` sets another time in milliseconds, or 0 to stay. The countdown pauses while the pointer is over the toast or focus is inside it.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button kind="tertiary" data-toast-kind="success">Success</ui-button>
  <ui-button kind="tertiary" data-toast-kind="info">Info</ui-button>
  <ui-button kind="tertiary" data-toast-kind="warning">Warning</ui-button>
  <ui-button kind="danger" data-toast-kind="error">Error</ui-button>
  <ui-toaster></ui-toaster>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const toaster = document.querySelector('ui-toaster');
  const texts = {
    success: ['Approval sent', 'Chaiya R. will get an email.'],
    info: ['New template', 'Lease 2026 is ready to use.'],
    warning: ['Stamp duty unpaid', 'Pay it before the contract is filed.'],
    error: ['Could not save', 'The server did not answer.'],
  };
  for (const button of document.querySelectorAll('[data-toast-kind]')) {
    button.addEventListener('click', () => {
      const kind = button.dataset.toastKind;
      const toast = document.createElement('ui-notification');
      // toast() picks the time: 5 s for success and info, 0 (stays) for warning and error
      Object.assign(toast, { variant: 'toast', role: 'none', kind, heading: texts[kind][0], subtitle: texts[kind][1], timeout: kind === 'success' || kind === 'info' ? 5000 : 0 });
      toaster.add(toast);
    });
  }
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
toast({ kind: 'success', title: 'Approval sent', subtitle: 'Chaiya R. will get an email.' });
toast({ title: 'New template', subtitle: 'Lease 2026 is ready to use.' });
toast({ kind: 'warning', title: 'Stamp duty unpaid', subtitle: 'Pay it before the contract is filed.' });
toast({ kind: 'error', title: 'Could not save', subtitle: 'The server did not answer.' });
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
toast({ kind: 'success', title: 'Approval sent', subtitle: 'Chaiya R. will get an email.' });
toast({ title: 'New template', subtitle: 'Lease 2026 is ready to use.' });
toast({ kind: 'warning', title: 'Stamp duty unpaid', subtitle: 'Pay it before the contract is filed.' });
toast({ kind: 'error', title: 'Could not save', subtitle: 'The server did not answer.' });
```

## Caption and low contrast

`caption` adds a small line under the subtitle, usually the time. `lowContrast` gives the toast a light tint instead of the dark surface.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button id="toast-caption" kind="tertiary">Export finished</ui-button>
  <ui-toaster></ui-toaster>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const toaster = document.querySelector('ui-toaster');
  document.getElementById('toast-caption').addEventListener('click', () => {
    const toast = document.createElement('ui-notification');
    const caption = new Date().toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });
    Object.assign(toast, { variant: 'toast', role: 'none', kind: 'success', lowContrast: true, heading: 'Export finished', subtitle: 'contracts-2026.csv', caption, timeout: 5000 });
    toaster.add(toast);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
toast({ kind: 'success', lowContrast: true, title: 'Export finished', subtitle: 'contracts-2026.csv', caption: new Date().toLocaleTimeString() });
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
toast({ kind: 'success', lowContrast: true, title: 'Export finished', subtitle: 'contracts-2026.csv', caption: new Date().toLocaleTimeString() });
```

## With an action

`actionLabel` adds a button for one quick action, and `onAction` runs when it is pressed. An actionable toast never closes by itself, takes focus when it appears and keeps Tab inside it until it is closed (Carbon's actionable notification). Use it only when the action is worth that interruption.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button id="toast-action" kind="tertiary">Upload contract.pdf</ui-button>
  <ui-toaster></ui-toaster>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const toaster = document.querySelector('ui-toaster');
  const show = (options) => {
    const toast = document.createElement('ui-notification');
    Object.assign(toast, { variant: 'toast', ...options });
    toaster.add(toast);
    return toast;
  };
  document.getElementById('toast-action').addEventListener('click', () => {
    // an actionable toast keeps its own role (alertdialog)
    const failed = show({ kind: 'warning', heading: 'Upload failed', subtitle: 'contract.pdf', actionLabel: 'Retry' });
    failed.addEventListener('ui-action', () => {
      failed.close();
      show({ role: 'none', kind: 'info', heading: 'Retrying…', subtitle: 'contract.pdf', timeout: 5000 });
    });
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
toast({
  kind: 'warning',
  title: 'Upload failed',
  subtitle: 'contract.pdf',
  actionLabel: 'Retry',
  onAction: () => upload(file),
});
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
toast({
  kind: 'warning',
  title: 'Upload failed',
  subtitle: 'contract.pdf',
  actionLabel: 'Retry',
  onAction: () => upload(file),
});
```

## Replace a toast

A toast with the same `id` as one that is still open replaces it instead of stacking a second one. Use it for a status that changes: "Syncing…", then "Synced".


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button id="toast-sync" kind="tertiary">Sync contracts</ui-button>
  <ui-toaster></ui-toaster>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const toaster = document.querySelector('ui-toaster');
  // toast({ id: 'sync', … }) removes the open toast with that id first
  const show = (options) => {
    toaster.querySelector('[data-toast-id="sync"]')?.remove();
    const toast = document.createElement('ui-notification');
    Object.assign(toast, { variant: 'toast', role: 'none', ...options });
    toast.dataset.toastId = 'sync';
    toaster.add(toast);
  };
  document.getElementById('toast-sync').addEventListener('click', () => {
    show({ kind: 'info', heading: 'Syncing…', subtitle: '24 contracts' });
    setTimeout(() => show({ kind: 'success', heading: 'Synced', subtitle: '24 contracts are up to date.', timeout: 5000 }), 2000);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
toast({ id: 'sync', title: 'Syncing…', subtitle: '24 contracts', timeout: 0 });
await sync();
toast({ id: 'sync', kind: 'success', title: 'Synced', subtitle: '24 contracts are up to date.' });
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
toast({ id: 'sync', title: 'Syncing…', subtitle: '24 contracts', timeout: 0 });
await sync();
toast({ id: 'sync', kind: 'success', title: 'Synced', subtitle: '24 contracts are up to date.' });
```

## Close from code

`toast()` returns a handle: `close()` closes that toast, for example when the work it talks about is done. On the element, `close()` does the same.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button id="toast-handle" kind="tertiary">Generate report</ui-button>
  <ui-toaster></ui-toaster>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const toaster = document.querySelector('ui-toaster');
  document.getElementById('toast-handle').addEventListener('click', () => {
    const toast = document.createElement('ui-notification');
    Object.assign(toast, { variant: 'toast', role: 'none', kind: 'info', heading: 'Generating the report…', subtitle: 'This takes a few seconds.' });
    toaster.add(toast);
    setTimeout(() => toast.close(), 3000);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const working = toast({ title: 'Generating the report…', subtitle: 'This takes a few seconds.', timeout: 0 });
await generateReport();
working.close();
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const working = toast({ title: 'Generating the report…', subtitle: 'This takes a few seconds.', timeout: 0 });
await generateReport();
working.close();
```

## How many at once

The toaster shows at most `max` toasts (3 by default); a new one closes the oldest. Place a `<ui-toaster>` yourself to change it; `toast()` uses the first one in the page. Press the button a few times.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button id="toast-max" kind="tertiary">Add a signer</ui-button>
  <ui-toaster id="toast-max-toaster" max="2"></ui-toaster>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const toaster = document.getElementById('toast-max-toaster');
  let count = 0;
  document.getElementById('toast-max').addEventListener('click', () => {
    count += 1;
    const toast = document.createElement('ui-notification');
    Object.assign(toast, { variant: 'toast', role: 'none', kind: 'success', heading: `Signer ${count} added`, timeout: 5000 });
    toaster.add(toast);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
// once in the app; toast() then uses it
<UiToaster max={2} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Toaster max={2} />
```

## Bottom corner

`placement="bottom-end"` stacks the toasts in the bottom end corner, the newest at the bottom. `--ui-toaster-offset` sets the distance from the edge (React + Tailwind: `offset`).


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button id="toast-bottom" kind="tertiary">Copy link</ui-button>
  <ui-toaster id="toast-bottom-toaster" placement="bottom-end" style="--ui-toaster-offset: 32px"></ui-toaster>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const toaster = document.getElementById('toast-bottom-toaster');
  document.getElementById('toast-bottom').addEventListener('click', () => {
    const toast = document.createElement('ui-notification');
    Object.assign(toast, { variant: 'toast', role: 'none', kind: 'info', heading: 'Link copied', timeout: 5000 });
    toaster.add(toast);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiToaster placement="bottom-end" style={{ '--ui-toaster-offset': '32px' } as CSSProperties} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Toaster placement="bottom-end" offset="32px" />
```

## Toasts and modals

A toast added while a [Modal](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/modal/) is open is drawn above it, but the page outside a modal is inert: nobody can click it and screen readers can't reach it. Give feedback inside a modal with an inline [Notification](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/notification/) instead (Carbon's guidance).


HTML:

```html
<ui-button id="toast-modal-open" kind="tertiary">Edit department</ui-button>
<ui-modal id="toast-modal" heading="Edit department" size="sm">
  <ui-notification id="toast-modal-saved" kind="success" low-contrast open="false" heading="Saved" subtitle="The new name is in use."></ui-notification>
  <ui-text-input label="Department name" value="Legal"></ui-text-input>
  <ui-button slot="footer" kind="secondary" id="toast-modal-close">Close</ui-button>
  <ui-button slot="footer" id="toast-modal-save">Save</ui-button>
</ui-modal>

<script type="module">
  const modal = document.getElementById('toast-modal');
  document.getElementById('toast-modal-open').addEventListener('click', () => {
    document.getElementById('toast-modal-saved').open = false;
    modal.show();
  });
  document.getElementById('toast-modal-close').addEventListener('click', () => modal.close());
  document.getElementById('toast-modal-save').addEventListener('click', () => (document.getElementById('toast-modal-saved').open = true));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiModal open={open} heading="Edit department" size="sm" onUiClose={(e) => { if (e.target === e.currentTarget) setOpen(false); }}>
  <UiNotification kind="success" lowContrast open={saved} heading="Saved" subtitle="The new name is in use." />
  <UiTextInput label="Department name" value="Legal" />
  <UiButton slot="footer" kind="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Close</UiButton>
  <UiButton slot="footer" onClick={save}>Save</UiButton>
</UiModal>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Modal open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} heading="Edit department" size="sm" footer={…}>
  <Notification kind="success" lowContrast open={saved} title="Saved" subtitle="The new name is in use." />
  <TextInput label="Department name" defaultValue="Legal" />
</Modal>
```

## Accessibility

- Each toast is announced through the toaster's region; the toasts themselves have no live role. An actionable toast keeps the `alertdialog` role and takes focus.
- Closed toasts are removed from the page.
- Keep toasts short, and don't put anything in a toast that the user can only find there: once it is gone, it is gone.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Toast](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-toast/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-toaster>` · React `UiToaster`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `placement` | `placement` | `ToasterPlacement` | `'top-end'` | Corner: newest toast nearest the edge. |
| `max` | `max` | `number` | `3` | Most toasts shown at once; a new one closes the oldest. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `add(toast)` | Adds `toast`, closes the oldest beyond `max`, and lifts the region above anything opened since. |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | `<ui-notification variant="toast">` elements (added by `toast()`) |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-toaster-offset` |  | Distance from the top (or bottom) edge (default 16px; 64px under a ui-header) |

# Tooltip

A tooltip is a short line of plain text about the control it wraps. It opens when the pointer rests on the control or keyboard focus reaches it, and closes when they leave. Use it to name an icon or add a hint, never for content people must read or act on.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-tooltip text="Signed copies are kept for 10 years">
    <ui-button kind="tertiary">Retention policy</ui-button>
  </ui-tooltip>
  <ui-tooltip text="Copy link" as-label>
    <ui-button kind="ghost" icon-only>
      <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M14 5v9H5V5h9m0-1H5a1 1 0 0 0-1 1v9a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h9a1 1 0 0 0 1-1V5a1 1 0 0 0-1-1Z"/><path d="M2 9H1V2a1 1 0 0 1 1-1h7v1H2Z"/></svg>
    </ui-button>
  </ui-tooltip>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
import { Copy as CopyIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<UiTooltip text="Signed copies are kept for 10 years">
  <UiButton kind="tertiary">Retention policy</UiButton>
</UiTooltip>
<UiTooltip text="Copy link" asLabel>
  <UiButton kind="ghost" iconOnly><CopyIcon /></UiButton>
</UiTooltip>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Copy as CopyIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<Tooltip text="Signed copies are kept for 10 years">
  <Button kind="tertiary">Retention policy</Button>
</Tooltip>
<Tooltip text="Copy link" asLabel>
  <Button kind="ghost" iconOnly><CopyIcon /></Button>
</Tooltip>
```
