```html
    <ui-tree-node label="Contracts" value="contracts"></ui-tree-node>
    <ui-tree-node label="Templates" value="templates"></ui-tree-node>
  </ui-tree-view>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTreeView label="Folders" hideLabel>…</UiTreeView>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TreeView label="Folders" hideLabel>…</TreeView>
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves into the tree and out of it: the tree is one Tab stop (the node focused last, else the selected one, else the first) |
| Up / Down | Previous / next visible node |
| Home / End | First / last visible node |
| Right | Opens a closed branch; on an open one, moves to its first child |
| Left | Closes an open branch; on a closed one or a leaf, moves to its parent |
| Enter | Opens or closes a branch, selects the node and follows its link |
| Space | Selects the node; in a `multiselect` tree, adds or removes it |
| Ctrl / ⌘ + A | Selects every node (`multiselect`) |
| A letter | Moves to the next visible node whose label starts with it |

## Accessibility

- The tree is a `role="tree"` of `treeitem`s, with `aria-expanded` on branches and `aria-selected` on every node. Each branch's children are a `group` named by its row.
- `label` names the tree. The caret is hidden from screen readers: the keys above do its job.
- A loading node is `aria-busy` and says "Loading".

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Tree view](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-tree-view/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-tree-view>` · React `UiTreeView`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `hide-label` | `hideLabel` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `size` | `size` | `TreeViewSize` | `'sm'` |  |
| `multiselect` | `multiselect` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `active` | `active` | `string` | `''` | The node that was last activated (4px marker). |

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `selected` | `string[]` | Selected node values. |
| `nodes` | `UiTreeNode[]` | (read-only) Every node, document order. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-select` | `onUiSelect` | detail: { selected: string[], value } after a selection change |
| `ui-activate` | `onUiActivate` | detail: { active } when a node becomes the active one |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | Top-level `<ui-tree-node>`s |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `label` | The tree label |
| `tree` | The `role=tree` container |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-tree-selected` |  | / --ui-tree-mark - The selected row's fill and mark (on `<ui-tree-node>`, with the other --ui-tree-* settings) |

### `<ui-tree-node>` · React `UiTreeNode`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` | Identifies the node in `selected` / `active`; defaults to `label`. |
| `expanded` | `expanded` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `href` | `href` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `lazy` | `lazy` | `boolean` | `false` | A branch whose children aren't loaded yet: it shows a caret and fires `ui-lazy-load` when first expanded. |
| `loading` | `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | The children are being fetched; set by the node when a `lazy` branch opens, cleared when children arrive. |

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `depth` | `number` | Set by the tree. |
| `isBranch` |  | (read-only) Has child nodes, or is `lazy` and will have them. |
| `treeValue` |  | (read-only) What identifies the node in the tree's `selected` / `active`: `value`, else `label`. (Was `nodeValue`, which shadowed DOM `Node.nodeValue`.) |
| `childTreeNodes` | `UiTreeNode[]` | (read-only) Direct child nodes. |
| `parentTreeNode` | `UiTreeNode \| null` | (read-only) The enclosing node, or null at the top level. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `toggle(expanded)` | Expand / collapse (branches only, including `lazy` ones). |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-toggle` | `onUiToggle` | detail: { expanded, value } when the branch opens / closes |
| `ui-lazy-load` | `onUiLazyLoad` | detail: { value } when a `lazy` node is expanded and its children should be fetched |
| `ui-navigate` | `onUiNavigate` | detail: { href } (cancelable) on a plain click of the link; cancel it to route client-side (README: SPA router) |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | Child nodes |
| `icon` | 16px icon before the label |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `label` | The row |
| `toggle` | The caret button (branches) |
| `children` | The `role=group` container |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-tree-background` |  | / --ui-tree-row-radius - Row fill and corners (default the layer, 0; Kanok: transparent, 6px) |
| `--ui-tree-selected` |  | / --ui-tree-selected-hover - The selected row's fill and its hover (default layer-selected, layer-selected-hover; Kanok: the highlight tint) |
| `--ui-tree-mark` |  | / --ui-tree-mark-width / --ui-tree-mark-inset / --ui-tree-mark-radius - The selected row's start mark (default interactive, 4px, full height, square; Kanok: none, the tint alone — forced colours still show it) |
| `--ui-tree-pointer-outline` |  | The ring of a node focused by a click, not the keyboard (default the focus ring, as Carbon; Kanok: none) |




---

# Tabs

Tabs split related content into views on one page. One tab is selected at a time, and only its panel shows. A `disabled` tab stays in the strip but can't be chosen.


HTML:

```html
<ui-tabs label="Contract details">
  <ui-tab panel="overview">Overview</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="parties">Parties</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="history">History</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="archive" disabled>Archive</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab-panel name="overview">Summary of the contract terms.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="parties">Signers and counterparties.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="history">Every change, newest first.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="archive">Archived copies.</ui-tab-panel>
</ui-tabs>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTabs label="Contract details">
  <UiTab panel="overview">Overview</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="parties">Parties</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="history">History</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="archive" disabled>Archive</UiTab>
  <UiTabPanel name="overview">Summary of the contract terms.</UiTabPanel>
  <UiTabPanel name="parties">Signers and counterparties.</UiTabPanel>
  <UiTabPanel name="history">Every change, newest first.</UiTabPanel>
  <UiTabPanel name="archive">Archived copies.</UiTabPanel>
</UiTabs>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Tabs>
  <TabList label="Contract details">
    <Tab value="overview">Overview</Tab>
    <Tab value="parties">Parties</Tab>
    <Tab value="history">History</Tab>
    <Tab value="archive" disabled>Archive</Tab>
  </TabList>
  <TabPanel value="overview">Summary of the contract terms.</TabPanel>
  <TabPanel value="parties">Signers and counterparties.</TabPanel>
  <TabPanel value="history">Every change, newest first.</TabPanel>
  <TabPanel value="archive">Archived copies.</TabPanel>
</Tabs>
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tabs
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-tabs
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tabs.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/tabs/tab-panel.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/tabs/tab.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/tabs/tabs-skeleton.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/tabs/tabs.styles.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/tabs/tabs.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-roving, layer, shared-element, shared-field, shared-localize, shared-skeleton, tooltip, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-tabs.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/tabs.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    tw-i18n, tw-layer, tw-theme, tw-tooltip, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it

Each `<ui-tab panel>` matches the `name` of a `<ui-tab-panel>`. Tabs and panels may come in any order in the markup: the tabs go into the strip by themselves. `label` names the strip for screen readers.


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/tabs';</script>

<ui-tabs label="Contract details">
  <ui-tab panel="overview">Overview</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="parties">Parties</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab-panel name="overview">Summary of the contract terms.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="parties">Signers and counterparties.</ui-tab-panel>
</ui-tabs>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiTabs, UiTab, UiTabPanel } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiTabs label="Contract details">
  <UiTab panel="overview">Overview</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="parties">Parties</UiTab>
  <UiTabPanel name="overview">Summary of the contract terms.</UiTabPanel>
  <UiTabPanel name="parties">Signers and counterparties.</UiTabPanel>
</UiTabs>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/tabs';

<Tabs>
  <TabList label="Contract details">
    <Tab value="overview">Overview</Tab>
    <Tab value="parties">Parties</Tab>
  </TabList>
  <TabPanel value="overview">Summary of the contract terms.</TabPanel>
  <TabPanel value="parties">Signers and counterparties.</TabPanel>
</Tabs>
```

In React + Tailwind, the `Tab`s sit in a `TabList` (it takes `label`), and a `Tab` and its `TabPanel` share a `value`.

## Tabs, content switcher or accordion?

| Component | Use it when |
|---|---|
| Tabs | The views are sections of one item (a contract's terms, parties, history) and the reader looks at one at a time. |
| [Content switcher](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/content-switcher/) | The same content in another form or filter: table or grid, all requests or mine. |
| [Accordion](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/accordion/) | A long page of sections the reader may open several of, or read top to bottom. |

## Starting tab and changes

`value` is the `name` of the panel that shows; left out, the first enabled tab is selected. `ui-tab-change` fires after the user selects another tab, with the panel's name in `detail.name`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-tabs id="tabs-start" label="Approval steps" value="review">
  <ui-tab panel="draft">Draft</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="review">Legal review</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="sign">Signing</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab-panel name="draft">The requester fills in the contract form.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="review">Legal checks the terms and the counterparty.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="sign">Both parties sign, and the contract is filed.</ui-tab-panel>
</ui-tabs>
<p>Selected: <output id="tabs-start-out"></output></p>

<script type="module">
  const tabs = document.getElementById('tabs-start');
  const out = document.getElementById('tabs-start-out');
  out.value = tabs.value;
  tabs.addEventListener('ui-tab-change', (event) => (out.value = event.detail.name));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const [step, setStep] = useState('review');

<UiTabs label="Approval steps" value={step} onUiTabChange={(e) => setStep(e.detail.name)}>
  <UiTab panel="draft">Draft</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="review">Legal review</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="sign">Signing</UiTab>
  <UiTabPanel name="draft">The requester fills in the contract form.</UiTabPanel>
  <UiTabPanel name="review">Legal checks the terms and the counterparty.</UiTabPanel>
  <UiTabPanel name="sign">Both parties sign, and the contract is filed.</UiTabPanel>
</UiTabs>
<p>Selected: <output>{step}</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [step, setStep] = useState('review');

<Tabs value={step} onValueChange={setStep}>
  <TabList label="Approval steps">
    <Tab value="draft">Draft</Tab>
    <Tab value="review">Legal review</Tab>
    <Tab value="sign">Signing</Tab>
  </TabList>
  <TabPanel value="draft">The requester fills in the contract form.</TabPanel>
  <TabPanel value="review">Legal checks the terms and the counterparty.</TabPanel>
  <TabPanel value="sign">Both parties sign, and the contract is filed.</TabPanel>
</Tabs>
<p>Selected: <output>{step}</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind also takes `defaultValue` for an uncontrolled start.

## Contained

`type="contained"` draws 48px tabs on a grey strip with dividers. The selected tab sits on the layer with a blue top edge, and the panels sit on the layer too. Use it where the tabs head a card or a section of their own.


HTML:

```html
<ui-tabs label="Contract details" type="contained">
  <ui-tab panel="overview">Overview</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="parties">Parties</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="history">History</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="archive" disabled>Archive</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab-panel name="overview">Summary of the contract terms.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="parties">Signers and counterparties.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="history">Every change, newest first.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="archive">Archived copies.</ui-tab-panel>
</ui-tabs>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTabs label="Contract details" type="contained">
  <UiTab panel="overview">Overview</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="parties">Parties</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="history">History</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="archive" disabled>Archive</UiTab>
  <UiTabPanel name="overview">Summary of the contract terms.</UiTabPanel>
  …
</UiTabs>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Tabs type="contained">
  <TabList label="Contract details">
    <Tab value="overview">Overview</Tab>
    <Tab value="parties">Parties</Tab>
    <Tab value="history">History</Tab>
    <Tab value="archive" disabled>Archive</Tab>
  </TabList>
  <TabPanel value="overview">Summary of the contract terms.</TabPanel>
  …
</Tabs>
```

## Full width

With `type="contained"`, `full-width` (`fullWidth`) shares the strip in equal columns. A label that doesn't fit ends in an ellipsis.


HTML:

```html
<ui-tabs label="Case sections" type="contained" full-width>
  <ui-tab panel="case">Case details</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="parties">Parties</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="evidence">Attachments and supporting evidence for the hearing</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="history">History</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab-panel name="case">Case number, court and filing date.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="parties">Plaintiffs, defendants and their lawyers.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="evidence">Documents filed with the case.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="history">Every hearing, newest first.</ui-tab-panel>
</ui-tabs>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTabs label="Case sections" type="contained" fullWidth>
  <UiTab panel="case">Case details</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="parties">Parties</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="evidence">Attachments and supporting evidence for the hearing</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="history">History</UiTab>
  …
</UiTabs>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Tabs type="contained" fullWidth>
  <TabList label="Case sections">
    <Tab value="case">Case details</Tab>
    <Tab value="parties">Parties</Tab>
    <Tab value="evidence">Attachments and supporting evidence for the hearing</Tab>
    <Tab value="history">History</Tab>
  </TabList>
  …
</Tabs>
```

## Sizes

`size`: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px (the line default), `lg` 48px (the contained default), `xl` 64px (contained only; line tabs stop at 48px).


HTML:

```html
<ui-tabs label="Small" size="sm">
  <ui-tab panel="a">Overview</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="b">Parties</ui-tab>
</ui-tabs>
<ui-tabs label="Large" size="lg">
  <ui-tab panel="a">Overview</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="b">Parties</ui-tab>
</ui-tabs>
<ui-tabs label="Contained, extra large" type="contained" size="xl">
  <ui-tab panel="a">Overview</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="b">Parties</ui-tab>
</ui-tabs>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTabs label="Small" size="sm">…</UiTabs>
<UiTabs label="Large" size="lg">…</UiTabs>
<UiTabs label="Contained, extra large" type="contained" size="xl">…</UiTabs>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Tabs size="sm">…</Tabs>
<Tabs size="lg">…</Tabs>
<Tabs type="contained" size="xl">…</Tabs>
```

The three strips above have no panels: tabs without a matching panel still select, they just show nothing.

## Icons

Put a 16px icon in a tab's `icon` slot (the `icon` prop in React + Tailwind). It follows the label and takes its colour. The label still names the tab.


HTML:

```html
<ui-tabs label="Contract">
  <ui-tab panel="document">Document <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12.85 4.65l-3.5-3.5A.5.5 0 0 0 9 1H4a1 1 0 0 0-1 1v12a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h8a1 1 0 0 0 1-1V5a.5.5 0 0 0-.15-.35ZM9 2.2 11.8 5H9ZM12 14H4V2h4v3a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h3Z" /></svg></ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="signers">Signers <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M8 2a3 3 0 1 1 0 6 3 3 0 0 1 0-6Zm0-1a4 4 0 1 0 0 8 4 4 0 0 0 0-8Zm5 14h-1v-2.5A2.5 2.5 0 0 0 9.5 10h-3A2.5 2.5 0 0 0 4 12.5V15H3v-2.5A3.5 3.5 0 0 1 6.5 9h3a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 3.5 3.5Z" /></svg></ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="history" disabled>History <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M8 15A7 7 0 1 1 8 1a7 7 0 0 1 0 14ZM8 2a6 6 0 1 0 0 12A6 6 0 0 0 8 2Zm2.3 9L7.5 8.2V4h1v3.8l2.5 2.5Z" /></svg></ui-tab>
  <ui-tab-panel name="document">The signed PDF and its pages.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="signers">Who signed, and when.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="history">Every change, newest first.</ui-tab-panel>
```

React:

```tsx
  <UiTab panel="signers">Signers {userIcon}</UiTab>
```

## Secondary labels

On contained tabs, `secondary-label` (`secondaryLabel`) adds a second, smaller line, such as a count. One secondary label makes every tab in the strip 64px tall.

## Icon only

`icon-only` (`iconOnly`) shows just the icon in a square tab. `label` is then required: it names the tab and shows as its tooltip on hover and on keyboard focus. With `size="lg"` the icons grow to 20px.

## Manual activation

By default the arrow keys select as they move (`activation="automatic"`). With `activation="manual"`, the arrows only move focus, and Enter or Space selects. Use it when a panel is slow to render or loads data.


HTML:

```html
<ui-tabs label="Reports" activation="manual">
  <ui-tab panel="month">This month</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="quarter">This quarter</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="year">This year</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab-panel name="month">Focus a tab, move with the arrow keys, then press Enter or Space.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="quarter">The quarter's report loads only when you choose it.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="year">The year's report loads only when you choose it.</ui-tab-panel>
</ui-tabs>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTabs label="Reports" activation="manual">
  <UiTab panel="month">This month</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="quarter">This quarter</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="year">This year</UiTab>
  …
</UiTabs>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Tabs activation="manual">
  <TabList label="Reports">
    <Tab value="month">This month</Tab>
    <Tab value="quarter">This quarter</Tab>
    <Tab value="year">This year</Tab>
  </TabList>
  …
</Tabs>
```

## An action at the end of the strip

The `end` slot (the `end` prop of `TabList` in React + Tailwind) puts content after the tabs, on the strip's line, for example a ghost button that adds a section.


HTML:

```html
<ui-tabs label="Contract sections">
  <ui-tab panel="terms">Terms</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="payment">Payment</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="annex">Annex</ui-tab>
  <ui-button slot="end" kind="ghost" size="md">Add section</ui-button>
  <ui-tab-panel name="terms">The terms both parties agreed to.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="payment">Instalments and due dates.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="annex">Extra documents.</ui-tab-panel>
</ui-tabs>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTabs label="Contract sections">
  <UiTab panel="terms">Terms</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="payment">Payment</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="annex">Annex</UiTab>
  <UiButton slot="end" kind="ghost" size="md">Add section</UiButton>
  …
</UiTabs>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Tabs>
  <TabList label="Contract sections" end={<Button kind="ghost" size="md">Add section</Button>}>
    <Tab value="terms">Terms</Tab>
    <Tab value="payment">Payment</Tab>
    <Tab value="annex">Annex</Tab>
  </TabList>
  …
</Tabs>
```

## Keep the current tab

`ui-tab-before-change` fires before the selection moves, with `detail.name` (the new tab) and `detail.previous`. Call `preventDefault()` to keep the current tab, for example while a form in it has unsaved changes. In React + Tailwind, keep `value` as it is in `onValueChange`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-checkbox id="tabs-dirty" label="The contract form has unsaved changes" checked></ui-checkbox>
<ui-tabs id="tabs-guard" label="Contract">
  <ui-tab panel="form">Form</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="preview">Preview</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab-panel name="form">Edit the contract here.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="preview">The contract as the counterparty will see it.</ui-tab-panel>
</ui-tabs>
<p><output id="tabs-guard-out"></output></p>

<script type="module">
  const dirty = document.getElementById('tabs-dirty');
  const tabs = document.getElementById('tabs-guard');
  const out = document.getElementById('tabs-guard-out');
  tabs.addEventListener('ui-tab-before-change', (event) => {
    out.value = '';
    if (!dirty.checked) return;
    event.preventDefault();
    out.value = `Save the form before you open "${event.detail.name}".`;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
import type { UiCheckbox as CheckboxElement } from '@purpurabog/ui';

const [dirty, setDirty] = useState(true);
const [message, setMessage] = useState('');

<UiCheckbox label="The contract form has unsaved changes" checked={dirty} onChange={(e) => setDirty((e.target as CheckboxElement).checked)} />
<UiTabs
  label="Contract"
  onUiTabBeforeChange={(e) => {
    setMessage(dirty ? `Save the form before you open "${e.detail.name}".` : '');
    if (dirty) e.preventDefault();
  }}
>
  <UiTab panel="form">Form</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="preview">Preview</UiTab>
  …
</UiTabs>
<p><output>{message}</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// dirty and message as in React
const [tab, setTab] = useState('form');

<Checkbox label="The contract form has unsaved changes" checked={dirty} onChange={(e) => setDirty(e.target.checked)} />
<Tabs
  value={tab}
  onValueChange={(next) => {
    setMessage(dirty ? `Save the form before you open "${next}".` : '');
    if (!dirty) setTab(next);
  }}
>
  <TabList label="Contract">
    <Tab value="form">Form</Tab>
    <Tab value="preview">Preview</Tab>
  </TabList>
  …
</Tabs>
<p><output>{message}</output></p>
```

## Dismissable tabs

`dismissable` gives every tab a close button, and Delete closes the focused tab. The tab first fires a cancelable `ui-request-close` (`detail.name`); unless you prevent it, the tab is hidden and fires `ui-close`. A closed selected tab passes the selection to the first enabled tab, and focus moves to the tab now in its place. Not with `vertical`.

In React + Tailwind, `onTabCloseRequest` gets the tab's `value`: remove that tab from your list to close it.


HTML:

```html
<ui-tabs id="tabs-docs" label="Open documents" dismissable>
  <ui-tab panel="contract">Contract.pdf</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="memo">Memo.docx</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="notes">Notes</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="archive" disabled>Archive</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab-panel name="contract">The × or Delete on the focused tab closes it.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="memo">The legal team's memo.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="notes">Your own notes.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="archive">Archived copies.</ui-tab-panel>
</ui-tabs>
<p>Closed: <output id="tabs-docs-out"></output></p>

<script type="module">
  const tabs = document.getElementById('tabs-docs');
  const out = document.getElementById('tabs-docs-out');
  const closed = [];
  tabs.addEventListener('ui-close', (event) => {
    closed.push(event.detail.name);
    out.value = closed.join(', ');
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const [closed, setClosed] = useState<string[]>([]);

<UiTabs label="Open documents" dismissable onUiClose={(e) => setClosed((list) => [...list, e.detail.name])}>
  <UiTab panel="contract">Contract.pdf</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="memo">Memo.docx</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="notes">Notes</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="archive" disabled>Archive</UiTab>
  …
</UiTabs>
<p>Closed: <output>{closed.join(', ')}</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(['contract', 'memo', 'notes']);
const names: Record<string, string> = { contract: 'Contract.pdf', memo: 'Memo.docx', notes: 'Notes' };

<Tabs dismissable onTabCloseRequest={(value) => setOpen((list) => list.filter((v) => v !== value))}>
  <TabList label="Open documents">
    {open.map((value) => <Tab key={value} value={value}>{names[value]}</Tab>)}
  </TabList>
  {open.map((value) => <TabPanel key={value} value={value}>…</TabPanel>)}
</Tabs>
```

## Vertical tabs

`vertical` puts the tabs in a column beside the panels once the window is wider than 672px (42rem); on a narrower window they become contained tabs in a row. Labels wrap to two lines, then end in an ellipsis. `height` fixes the height: the tab list and the panels then scroll inside it.


HTML:

```html
<ui-tabs label="Settings" vertical height="320px">
  <ui-tab panel="profile">Profile</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="approvals">Approval rules for contracts above the department's limit</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="notifications">Notifications</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="signatures">Signatures</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="retention">Retention</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="audit" disabled>Audit log</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab-panel name="profile"><ui-text-input label="Display name" value="Somchai K."></ui-text-input></ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="approvals">Who approves a contract, by amount.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="notifications">Email and in-app alerts.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="signatures">Your saved signature.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="retention">How long signed copies are kept.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="audit">Who changed what.</ui-tab-panel>
</ui-tabs>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTabs label="Settings" vertical height="320px">
  <UiTab panel="profile">Profile</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="approvals">Approval rules for contracts above the department's limit</UiTab>
  <UiTab panel="notifications">Notifications</UiTab>
  …
  <UiTabPanel name="profile"><UiTextInput label="Display name" value="Somchai K." /></UiTabPanel>
  …
</UiTabs>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Tabs vertical height="320px">
  <TabList label="Settings">
    <Tab value="profile">Profile</Tab>
    <Tab value="approvals">Approval rules for contracts above the department's limit</Tab>
    <Tab value="notifications">Notifications</Tab>
    …
  </TabList>
  <TabPanel value="profile"><TextInput label="Display name" defaultValue="Somchai K." /></TabPanel>
  …
</Tabs>
```

In the column, ↑ and ↓ move between the tabs, and the panels sit one layer up, so their fields keep their contrast.

## Many tabs

When the tabs don't fit, the strip scrolls. Previous and next buttons appear at its ends for the mouse; keyboard users have the arrow keys, so the buttons are no Tab stops and are hidden from screen readers.


HTML:

```html
<ui-tabs label="Months" style="max-width: 480px">
  <ui-tab panel="jan">January</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="feb">February</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="mar">March</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="apr">April</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="may">May</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="jun">June</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="jul">July</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab panel="aug">August</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab-panel name="jan">Contracts signed in January.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="feb">Contracts signed in February.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="mar">Contracts signed in March.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="apr">Contracts signed in April.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="may">Contracts signed in May.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="jun">Contracts signed in June.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="jul">Contracts signed in July.</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel name="aug">Contracts signed in August.</ui-tab-panel>
</ui-tabs>
```

React:

```tsx
// months = [{ value: 'jan', label: 'January' }, …]
<UiTabs label="Months" style={{ maxWidth: 480 }}>
  {months.map((m) => <UiTab key={m.value} panel={m.value}>{m.label}</UiTab>)}
  {months.map((m) => <UiTabPanel key={m.value} name={m.value}>Contracts signed in {m.label}.</UiTabPanel>)}
</UiTabs>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// months = [{ value: 'jan', label: 'January' }, …]
<Tabs className="max-w-[480px]">
  <TabList label="Months">
    {months.map((m) => <Tab key={m.value} value={m.value}>{m.label}</Tab>)}
  </TabList>
  {months.map((m) => <TabPanel key={m.value} value={m.value}>Contracts signed in {m.label}.</TabPanel>)}
</Tabs>
```

## Skeleton

While the page loads, `ui-tabs-skeleton` stands in for the strip: `tabs` bars of 160 × 40px (5 by default). It is hidden from screen readers.


HTML:

```html
<ui-tabs-skeleton tabs="4"></ui-tabs-skeleton>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiTabsSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiTabsSkeleton tabs={4} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { TabsSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/tabs';

<TabsSkeleton tabs={4} />
```

On the web component, import it from `@purpurabog/ui/tabs-skeleton`.

## Accessibility

- The strip is a `tablist` named by `label`; each tab is a `tab` with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`, and each panel a `tabpanel` labelled by its tab.
- One Tab stop: Tab reaches the selected tab, then moves into the panel. ← and → move between tabs and wrap (↑ and ↓ in a vertical column); Home and End jump to the first and last. Disabled tabs are skipped.
- A panel with nothing focusable inside becomes a Tab stop itself, so keyboard users can reach and scroll its text.
- Icon-only tabs need `label`: it is the tab's name and its tooltip.
- In dismissable tabs the close button is hidden from screen readers; each tab announces Delete as its shortcut (`aria-keyshortcuts`).

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Tabs](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-tabs/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-tabs>` · React `UiTabs`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` | Name of the active panel. Defaults to the first enabled tab. |
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name for the tab strip, e.g. "Product details". |
| `activation` | `activation` | `TabsActivation` | `'automatic'` | `automatic` (Carbon's name; `auto` is still accepted) or `manual`. |
| `type` | `type` | `TabsType` | `'line'` | `line` (default) or `contained` (Carbon cds-tabs `type="contained"`). |
| `size` | `size` | `TabsSize \| undefined` |  | Tab height (Carbon `size`): sm 32px, md 40px, lg 48px, xl 64px (contained only); unset = md for line, lg for contained. |
| `full-width` | `fullWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | With `type="contained"`: the tabs share the full width in equal columns (Carbon `full-width` / `fullWidth`). |
| `vertical` | `vertical` | `boolean` | `false` | Carbon `TabsVertical`: the tabs in a column beside the panels from md up (contained tabs in a row below). |
| `height` | `height` | `string` | `''` | A fixed height for vertical tabs (Carbon `height`), e.g. `"400px"`: the tab list and the panels then scroll. |
| `dismissable` | `dismissable` | `boolean` | `false` | A close button on every tab, and Delete closes the focused tab (Carbon `dismissable`); not with `vertical`. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `focus(options)` | Focus the active tab (the tablist's tab stop). |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-tab-change` | `onUiTabChange` | detail: { name } after the user selects a tab |
| `ui-tab-before-change` | `onUiTabBeforeChange` | Cancelable; detail: { name, previous }. preventDefault() keeps the current tab (e.g. unsaved changes). |
| `ui-request-close` | `onUiRequestClose` | From a `<ui-tab>` of dismissable tabs (close button or Delete); cancelable; detail: { name }. preventDefault() keeps the tab. |
| `ui-close` | `onUiClose` | From a `<ui-tab>` after it closed (hidden); detail: { name } |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| `nav` | `<ui-tab>` elements (assigned automatically) |
| (default) | `<ui-tab-panel>` elements |
| `end` | Content at the end of the strip, e.g. an action button |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The strip holding the tab list and scroll buttons |
| `tablist` | The role=tablist container (tabs themselves are light-DOM `<ui-tab>`s: style the element) |
| `scroll-button` | The overflow scroll buttons |
| `end` | Wrapper of the `end` slot |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-tabs-track` |  | `box-shadow` of the tab strip, for one line under every tab (default none; Kanok: a 1px hairline) |
| `--ui-tabs-gap` |  | Gap between line tabs (default 1px; Kanok: 4px) |
| `--ui-tabs-contained-height` |  | Tab height of `type="contained"` (default 48px; Kanok: 32px) |
| `--ui-tabs-contained-track` |  | / --ui-tabs-contained-padding / --ui-tabs-contained-radius / --ui-tabs-contained-gap - The track behind contained tabs (default none: Carbon's full-width strip; Kanok: a grey rounded track) |
| `--ui-tabs-contained-flex` |  | `flex` of the contained strip (default 1, full width; Kanok: hugs the tabs) |
| `--ui-tab-vertical-background` |  | The vertical tab list's fill (default the layer; on `<ui-tab>` with the other --ui-tab-vertical-* settings) |

### `<ui-tab>` · React `UiTab`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hidden` |  |  |  |  |
| `panel` | `panel` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `selected` | `selected` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the control; a disabled `<fieldset>` ancestor does the same. |
| `secondary-label` | `secondaryLabel` | `string` | `''` | A second line under the label (Carbon `secondaryLabel`); contained tabs only. |
| `icon-only` | `iconOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Only the `icon` slot shows (Carbon `IconTab`); `label` names the tab and is its tooltip. |
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name and tooltip of an `icon-only` tab — required with it. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-request-close` | `onUiRequestClose` | Dismissable tabs: its close button or Delete; cancelable; detail: { name } (its `panel`) |
| `ui-close` | `onUiClose` | Dismissable tabs: after it closed (now `hidden`); detail: { name } |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | Tab label |
| `icon` | A 16px icon (20px in icon-only tabs of `size="lg"`), coloured like the label |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `secondary-label` | The second line of a contained tab |
| `close-button` | The close button of a dismissable tab (no tab stop: Delete closes the focused tab) |
| `tooltip` | The `<ui-tooltip>` of an `icon-only` tab |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-tab-line` |  | The underline of every tab (default `2px solid --ui-hairline`; Kanok: transparent, the strip draws one line) |
| `--ui-tab-selected-line` |  | The selected tab's mark (default `--ui-border-interactive`, as in Kanok) |
| `--ui-tab-hover-line` |  | Underline colour on hover (default `--ui-ink-subtle`) |
| `--ui-tab-disabled-line` |  | Underline colour when disabled (default `--ui-hairline`) |
| `--ui-tab-background` |  | Fill of a line tab (default `--ui-canvas`; Kanok: transparent) |
| `--ui-tab-contained-background` |  | / --ui-tab-contained-hover / --ui-tab-contained-selected - Fills of a contained tab at rest, hovered and selected (Carbon: layer-accent, its hover, the layer) |
| `--ui-tab-contained-selected-shadow` |  | `box-shadow` of the selected contained tab (default: a 2px top bar in `--ui-tab-selected-line`) |
| `--ui-tab-contained-radius` |  | Corner radius of a contained tab (default 0; Kanok: 6px) |
| `--ui-tab-contained-divider` |  | The 1px line between contained tabs (default `--ui-hairline-strong`; Kanok: none) |
| `--ui-tab-focus-radius` |  | Corner radius of the focus ring (default 0; Kanok: 6px) |
| `--ui-tab-focus-offset` |  | / --ui-tab-contained-focus-offset - Where the focus ring sits, line and contained tabs (default -2px, over the selected underline; Kanok: -5px, clear of it, and 1px around the chip) |
| `--ui-tab-vertical-background` |  | / --ui-tab-vertical-selected / --ui-tab-vertical-bar / --ui-tab-vertical-hover-bar / --ui-tab-vertical-divider / --ui-tab-vertical-inset / --ui-tab-vertical-radius - Vertical tabs: fill, the chosen tab's fill, the side bars, the rule between tabs, inset and corners (default Carbon's layer fill with bars and rules; Kanok: inset rounded rows, the chosen one tinted) |
| `--ui-tab-vertical-mark` |  | The chosen vertical tab's 3px start bar (default `--ui-tab-selected-line`; Kanok: none, the tint alone) |
| `--ui-icon-control-radius` |  | Corners of its small icon buttons, their hover fill and ring (default 0; Kanok: round) |

### `<ui-tab-panel>` · React `UiTabPanel`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `''` |  |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | Panel content |

### `<ui-tabs-skeleton>` · React `UiTabsSkeleton`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tabs` | `tabs` | `number` | `5` |  |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `tab` | Each tab |

# Breadcrumb

A breadcrumb shows where the current page sits in the site's hierarchy, and links back up to each level above it. Put it at the top of the page, above the title.


HTML:

```html
<ui-breadcrumb no-trailing-slash>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-home">Home</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-contracts">Contracts</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item current>CT-2026-0142</ui-breadcrumb-item>
</ui-breadcrumb>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiBreadcrumb noTrailingSlash>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/contracts">Contracts</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem current>CT-2026-0142</UiBreadcrumbItem>
</UiBreadcrumb>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Breadcrumb noTrailingSlash>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/contracts">Contracts</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem current>CT-2026-0142</BreadcrumbItem>
</Breadcrumb>
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/breadcrumb
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-breadcrumb
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/breadcrumb.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/breadcrumb/breadcrumb-item.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/breadcrumb/breadcrumb-skeleton.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/breadcrumb/breadcrumb.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-overflow, menu, overflow-menu, shared-element, shared-localize, shared-navigate, shared-skeleton, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
# (none)
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-breadcrumb.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/breadcrumb.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-overflow, tw-dom, tw-i18n, tw-menu, tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it

`<ui-breadcrumb>` renders a `<nav>` landmark with an ordered list; each `<ui-breadcrumb-item href>` is one link in it.


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/breadcrumb';</script>

<ui-breadcrumb>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="/">Home</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="/contracts">Contracts</ui-breadcrumb-item>
</ui-breadcrumb>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiBreadcrumb, UiBreadcrumbItem } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiBreadcrumb>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/contracts">Contracts</UiBreadcrumbItem>
</UiBreadcrumb>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb, BreadcrumbItem } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/breadcrumb';

<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/contracts">Contracts</BreadcrumbItem>
</Breadcrumb>
```

## Current page and the trailing slash

Every item is followed by a "/", the last one too, as in Carbon: a trail of links only, with the page title under it, reads as "you are inside Contracts". When the trail ends with the page the user is on, mark that item `current` (plain text with `aria-current="page"`) and drop the last slash with `no-trailing-slash` (`noTrailingSlash`).


HTML:

```html
<ui-breadcrumb>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-home">Home</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-contracts">Contracts</ui-breadcrumb-item>
</ui-breadcrumb>
<ui-breadcrumb no-trailing-slash>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-home">Home</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-contracts">Contracts</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item current>CT-2026-0142</ui-breadcrumb-item>
</ui-breadcrumb>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiBreadcrumb>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/contracts">Contracts</UiBreadcrumbItem>
</UiBreadcrumb>
<UiBreadcrumb noTrailingSlash>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/contracts">Contracts</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem current>CT-2026-0142</UiBreadcrumbItem>
</UiBreadcrumb>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/contracts">Contracts</BreadcrumbItem>
</Breadcrumb>
<Breadcrumb noTrailingSlash>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/contracts">Contracts</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem current>CT-2026-0142</BreadcrumbItem>
</Breadcrumb>
```

## A level without a page

An item without `href` renders as plain text, for a level of the hierarchy that has no page of its own (a group in the menu, say). Unlike `current`, it doesn't claim to be the page the user is on.


HTML:

```html
<ui-breadcrumb no-trailing-slash>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-home">Home</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item>Legal</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-contracts">Contracts</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item current>CT-2026-0142</ui-breadcrumb-item>
</ui-breadcrumb>
```

React:

## Small

`size="sm"` uses the 12px label type and a 4px gap around the slashes. Use it in dense headers and side panels.

```html
<ui-breadcrumb size="sm" no-trailing-slash>
```

## Long trails wrap

A trail that doesn't fit wraps onto the next line; each item stays on one line. To keep it on one line, set the CSS custom property `--ui-breadcrumb-wrap: nowrap`, or collapse it with `overflow` (next section).


HTML:

```html
<ui-breadcrumb no-trailing-slash style="max-width: 320px">
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-home">Home</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-legal">Legal department</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-contracts">Procurement contracts</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-vendor">Siam Office Supplies</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item current>CT-2026-0142</ui-breadcrumb-item>
</ui-breadcrumb>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiBreadcrumb noTrailingSlash style={{ maxWidth: 320 }}>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/legal">Legal department</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/legal/procurement">Procurement contracts</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/vendors/siam-office">Siam Office Supplies</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem current>CT-2026-0142</UiBreadcrumbItem>
</UiBreadcrumb>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Breadcrumb noTrailingSlash className="max-w-[320px]">
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/legal">Legal department</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/legal/procurement">Procurement contracts</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/vendors/siam-office">Siam Office Supplies</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem current>CT-2026-0142</BreadcrumbItem>
</Breadcrumb>
```

## Collapse a long trail

`overflow` keeps the trail on one line: the crumbs that don't fit go, from the end, into a "…" menu just before the last crumb, which always stays. The first crumbs stay as long as they fit. Choosing a crumb in the menu follows its link. `overflow-label` (`overflowLabel`) names the menu button (default "More breadcrumbs"). Make the box narrower or wider to see the menu change.


HTML:

```html
<ui-breadcrumb overflow overflow-label="More levels" no-trailing-slash style="max-width: 420px">
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-home">Home</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-legal">Legal department</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-contracts">Procurement contracts</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-vendor">Siam Office Supplies</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item current>CT-2026-0142</ui-breadcrumb-item>
</ui-breadcrumb>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiBreadcrumb overflow overflowLabel="More levels" noTrailingSlash style={{ maxWidth: 420 }}>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/legal">Legal department</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/legal/procurement">Procurement contracts</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/vendors/siam-office">Siam Office Supplies</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem current>CT-2026-0142</UiBreadcrumbItem>
</UiBreadcrumb>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Breadcrumb overflow overflowLabel="More levels" noTrailingSlash className="max-w-[420px]">
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/legal">Legal department</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/legal/procurement">Procurement contracts</BreadcrumbItem>

  <BreadcrumbItem current>CT-2026-0142</BreadcrumbItem>
</Breadcrumb>
```

## Route in a single-page app

A plain click on an item's link first fires a cancelable `ui-navigate` with `detail.href`, bubbling out of the breadcrumb. Call `preventDefault()` and hand the path to your router; Ctrl-, ⌘- and middle-clicks stay normal links. In React put `onUiNavigate` once on `UiBreadcrumb` (or on a single `UiBreadcrumbItem`). In React + Tailwind the items are plain `<a>`s: route in their `onClick`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-breadcrumb id="breadcrumb-route" no-trailing-slash>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="/">Home</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="/contracts">Contracts</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item current>CT-2026-0142</ui-breadcrumb-item>
</ui-breadcrumb>
<p>Router got: <output id="breadcrumb-route-out"></output></p>

<script type="module">
  const trail = document.getElementById('breadcrumb-route');
  const out = document.getElementById('breadcrumb-route-out');
  trail.addEventListener('ui-navigate', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    out.value = event.detail.href;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
import type { NavigateDetail } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

const navigate = useNavigate(); // your router
const route = (e: CustomEvent<NavigateDetail>) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  navigate(e.detail.href);
};

<UiBreadcrumb noTrailingSlash onUiNavigate={route}>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/">Home</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/contracts">Contracts</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem current>CT-2026-0142</UiBreadcrumbItem>
</UiBreadcrumb>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import type { MouseEvent } from 'react';

const navigate = useNavigate(); // your router
const route = (e: MouseEvent<HTMLAnchorElement>) => {
  if (e.button !== 0 || e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey || e.shiftKey) return;
  e.preventDefault();
  navigate(e.currentTarget.getAttribute('href') ?? '/');
};

<Breadcrumb noTrailingSlash>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/" onClick={route}>Home</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/contracts" onClick={route}>Contracts</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem current>CT-2026-0142</BreadcrumbItem>
</Breadcrumb>
```

## Name the landmark

The `<nav>` is named "Breadcrumb" (translated with the page's language). When a page has two trails, or the default name doesn't fit, set `label`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-breadcrumb label="Contract location" no-trailing-slash>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-archive">Archive</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="#breadcrumb-year">2026</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item current>Box 14</ui-breadcrumb-item>
</ui-breadcrumb>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiBreadcrumb label="Contract location" noTrailingSlash>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/archive">Archive</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem href="/archive/2026">2026</UiBreadcrumbItem>
  <UiBreadcrumbItem current>Box 14</UiBreadcrumbItem>
</UiBreadcrumb>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Breadcrumb label="Contract location" noTrailingSlash>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/archive">Archive</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem href="/archive/2026">2026</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem current>Box 14</BreadcrumbItem>
</Breadcrumb>
```

## Skeleton

While the trail loads, `ui-breadcrumb-skeleton` shows `items` bars of 100 × 16px (3 by default), each followed by a slash. It takes `size` and `no-trailing-slash` like the breadcrumb, and is hidden from screen readers.


HTML:

```html
<ui-breadcrumb-skeleton></ui-breadcrumb-skeleton>
<ui-breadcrumb-skeleton items="4" size="sm" no-trailing-slash></ui-breadcrumb-skeleton>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiBreadcrumbSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiBreadcrumbSkeleton />
<UiBreadcrumbSkeleton items={4} size="sm" noTrailingSlash />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { BreadcrumbSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/breadcrumb';

<BreadcrumbSkeleton />
<BreadcrumbSkeleton items={4} size="sm" noTrailingSlash />
```

On the web component, import it from `@purpurabog/ui/breadcrumb-skeleton`.

## Accessibility

- The trail is a `<nav>` landmark named "Breadcrumb" (or `label`) holding an ordered list, so screen readers announce how many levels it has.
- The current page is text with `aria-current="page"`, not a link to itself.
- The slashes are drawn by CSS and aren't read out.
- Each link is a Tab stop. In a collapsed trail the "…" button is one more; its menu lists the hidden crumbs.

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-breadcrumb>` · React `UiBreadcrumb`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name of the navigation landmark. |
| `no-trailing-slash` | `noTrailingSlash` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `size` | `size` | `BreadcrumbSize` | `'md'` |  |
| `overflow` | `overflow` | `boolean` | `false` | On one line, the crumbs that don't fit go into a "…" menu before the last one. |
| `overflow-label` | `overflowLabel` | `string` | `''` | The overflow menu's name (default: the translation's "More breadcrumbs"). |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `focus(options)` | Focus the first crumb's link. |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | `<ui-breadcrumb-item>` elements |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The `<nav>` |
| `list` | The `<ol>` |
| `overflow` | The "…" item holding the overflow menu (`overflow` only) |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-breadcrumb-wrap` |  | `nowrap` keeps the trail on one line (the page header's bar does) |

### `<ui-breadcrumb-item>` · React `UiBreadcrumbItem`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `href` | `href` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `current` | `current` | `boolean` | `false` | The page the user is on: plain text with `aria-current="page"`. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-navigate` | none (use a ref) | detail: { href } (cancelable) on a plain click of the link; cancel it to route client-side (README: SPA router) |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | The item text |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The link or the current-page text |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-breadcrumb-trailing-slash` |  | `display` of the slash after the last item (default inline; Kanok: none) |

### `<ui-breadcrumb-skeleton>` · React `UiBreadcrumbSkeleton`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `items` | `number` | `3` |  |
| `no-trailing-slash` | `noTrailingSlash` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `size` | `size` | `'sm' \| 'md'` | `'md'` |  |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `item` | Each bar |

# Link

A link takes the user to another page, another place on this page, or a file. It is blue, underlines on hover and focus, and has Carbon's focus ring.


HTML:

```html
<ui-link href="#link-policy">Signing policy</ui-link>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLink href="/policies/signing">Signing policy</UiLink>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Link href="/policies/signing">Signing policy</Link>
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/link
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-link
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/link.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/link/link.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    shared-element, shared-navigate, shared-slots, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install class-variance-authority@0.7.1
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-link.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/link.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/link';</script>

<ui-link href="/policies/signing">Signing policy</ui-link>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiLink } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiLink href="/policies/signing">Signing policy</UiLink>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Link } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/link';

<Link href="/policies/signing">Signing policy</Link>
```

## Link or button?

| Component | Use it when |
|---|---|
| Link | It goes somewhere: a page, a section of this page, a file. The browser's own link features work (open in a new tab, copy the address). |
| [Button](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/button/) | It does something here: submits a form, opens a modal, starts an export. |

When an action must look like a button but go to a page, use a button with `href`; see [Button](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/button/).

## Sizes

`size`: `sm` 12px (helper text), `md` 14px (the default), `lg` 16px. Match the text around the link.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-link href="#link-policy" size="sm">Small link</ui-link>
  <ui-link href="#link-policy">Medium link</ui-link>
  <ui-link href="#link-policy" size="lg">Large link</ui-link>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLink href="/policies/signing" size="sm">Small link</UiLink>
<UiLink href="/policies/signing">Medium link</UiLink>
<UiLink href="/policies/signing" size="lg">Large link</UiLink>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Link href="/policies/signing" size="sm">Small link</Link>
<Link href="/policies/signing">Medium link</Link>
<Link href="/policies/signing" size="lg">Large link</Link>
```

## Inside a sentence

`inline` underlines the link at rest, so it stands out in running text where colour alone isn't enough. An inline link shows no icon.


HTML:

```html
<p>Signed copies are kept for 10 years under the <ui-link href="#link-retention" inline>retention policy</ui-link>. Ask the legal team before you destroy one.</p>
```

React:

```tsx
<p>Signed copies are kept for 10 years under the <UiLink href="/policies/retention" inline>retention policy</UiLink>. Ask the legal team before you destroy one.</p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<p>Signed copies are kept for 10 years under the <Link href="/policies/retention" inline>retention policy</Link>. Ask the legal team before you destroy one.</p>
```

## With an icon

Put a 16px icon in the `icon` slot (the `icon` prop in React + Tailwind): it sits 8px after the text, in the link's colour, and grows to 20px with `size="lg"`. Use it for standalone links, such as "View all" at the end of a list.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-link href="#link-contracts">View all contracts <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M9.3 3.7 13.1 7.5H1v1h12.1l-3.8 3.8.7.7 5-5-5-5z" /></svg></ui-link>
  <ui-link href="#link-contracts" size="lg">View all contracts <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M9.3 3.7 13.1 7.5H1v1h12.1l-3.8 3.8.7.7 5-5-5-5z" /></svg></ui-link>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLink href="/contracts">
  View all contracts
  <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M9.3 3.7 13.1 7.5H1v1h12.1l-3.8 3.8.7.7 5-5-5-5z" /></svg>
</UiLink>
<UiLink href="/contracts" size="lg">View all contracts {arrowIcon}</UiLink>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const arrowIcon = <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M9.3 3.7 13.1 7.5H1v1h12.1l-3.8 3.8.7.7 5-5-5-5z" /></svg>;

<Link href="/contracts" icon={arrowIcon}>View all contracts</Link>
<Link href="/contracts" size="lg" icon={arrowIcon}>View all contracts</Link>
```

## Open in a new tab

`target="_blank"` opens the page in a new tab, and the link adds `rel="noopener noreferrer"` unless you set `rel`. Say so in the text or with Carbon's Launch icon, so the new tab doesn't surprise anyone.


HTML:

```html
<ui-link href="https://carbondesignsystem.com/components/link/usage/" target="_blank">Carbon's link guidelines <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M13 14H3V4h5V3H3a1 1 0 0 0-1 1v10a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h10a1 1 0 0 0 1-1V8h-1z" /><path d="M10 1v1h3.3L7 8.3l.7.7L14 2.7V6h1V1z" /></svg></ui-link>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLink href="https://carbondesignsystem.com/components/link/usage/" target="_blank">
  Carbon's link guidelines {launchIcon}
</UiLink>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Link href="https://carbondesignsystem.com/components/link/usage/" target="_blank" icon={launchIcon}>
  Carbon's link guidelines
</Link>
```

## Download a file

`download` makes the link save its target instead of opening it; its value is the file name. Name the type and size in the text. (The docs site has no such file, so this demo builds one in the browser.)


HTML:

```html
<ui-link id="link-download" href="/files/contract-checklist.txt" download="contract-checklist.txt">Download the contract checklist (TXT, 1 KB)</ui-link>

<script type="module">
  const link = document.getElementById('link-download');
  const text = 'Contract checklist\n- Both parties named\n- Amount and due dates\n- Signatures and witnesses\n';
  link.href = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([text], { type: 'text/plain' }));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLink href="/files/contract-checklist.txt" download="contract-checklist.txt">
  Download the contract checklist (TXT, 1 KB)
</UiLink>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Link href="/files/contract-checklist.txt" download="contract-checklist.txt">
  Download the contract checklist (TXT, 1 KB)
</Link>
```

## Visited links

`visited` turns on Carbon's visited colour (purple) for links the browser has visited. Use it in lists the user works through, such as search results. Click the link, then look at it again.


HTML:

```html
<ui-link href="#link-visited" visited>CT-2026-0142: office supplies</ui-link>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLink href="/contracts/ct-2026-0142" visited>CT-2026-0142: office supplies</UiLink>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Link href="/contracts/ct-2026-0142" visited>CT-2026-0142: office supplies</Link>
```

## Disabled

`disabled` renders grey text with `role="link"` and `aria-disabled="true"`: it isn't a link any more and takes no focus. Prefer leaving the link out, or explain next to it why it is unavailable.


HTML:

```html
<ui-link href="#link-signed" disabled>Download the signed copy</ui-link>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLink href="/contracts/ct-2026-0142/signed.pdf" disabled>Download the signed copy</UiLink>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Link href="/contracts/ct-2026-0142/signed.pdf" disabled>Download the signed copy</Link>
```

## Route in a single-page app

A plain click (main button, no modifier key, same tab, same site, not a download) first fires a cancelable `ui-navigate` with `detail.href`. Call `preventDefault()` and hand the path to your router; the browser then doesn't load the page. Ctrl-, ⌘- and middle-clicks stay normal links. The React + Tailwind `Link` is a plain `<a>`: route in its `onClick`, or wrap your router's link.


HTML:

```html
<ui-link id="link-route" href="/contracts/ct-2026-0142">Open CT-2026-0142</ui-link>
<p>Router got: <output id="link-route-out"></output></p>

<script type="module">
  const link = document.getElementById('link-route');
  const out = document.getElementById('link-route-out');
  link.addEventListener('ui-navigate', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    out.value = event.detail.href;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const navigate = useNavigate(); // your router

<UiLink href="/contracts/ct-2026-0142" onUiNavigate={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); navigate(e.detail.href); }}>
  Open CT-2026-0142
</UiLink>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const navigate = useNavigate(); // your router

<Link
  href="/contracts/ct-2026-0142"
  onClick={(e) => {
    if (e.button !== 0 || e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey || e.shiftKey) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    navigate('/contracts/ct-2026-0142');
  }}
>
  Open CT-2026-0142
</Link>
```

## Accessibility

- The link is a real `<a href>`: Enter follows it, and the browser's menu (open in a new tab, copy the address) works.
- Write text that makes sense on its own ("Download the contract checklist", not "Click here"): screen reader users often move from link to link.
- Icons in the `icon` slot are decoration; give them `aria-hidden="true"` and keep the meaning in the text.
- A disabled link is announced as a dimmed link but takes no focus, so keyboard users never reach it. Say why it is unavailable in nearby text.
- `inline` underlines links inside sentences, so they don't rely on colour alone.

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-link>` · React `UiLink`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `href` | `href` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `target` | `target` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `rel` | `rel` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `download` | `download` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `size` | `size` | `LinkSize` | `'md'` |  |
| `inline` | `inline` | `boolean` | `false` | Underlined at rest, for links inside a sentence. |
| `visited` | `visited` | `boolean` | `false` | Opt into Carbon's visited colour (browser `:visited`). |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders as inert text with `aria-disabled`. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-navigate` | none (use a ref) | detail: { href } (cancelable) on a plain click of the link; cancel it to route client-side (README: SPA router) |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | Link text |
| `icon` | A 16px (lg: 20px) icon after the text (Carbon `renderIcon`; not shown when `inline`) |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The anchor |
| `icon` | The icon wrapper |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-link-focus-radius` |  | Corners of the focus ring (default 0; Kanok: 4px) |

# Pagination nav

Pagination nav moves between numbered pages: Previous, the page numbers, and Next. The pages that don't fit fold into "…" menus at either end. `page` is 0-based, as in Carbon.


HTML:

```html
<ui-pagination-nav total-items="25"></ui-pagination-nav>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiPaginationNav totalItems={25} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<PaginationNav totalItems={25} />
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/pagination-nav
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-pagination-nav
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/pagination-nav.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/pagination-nav/pagination-nav.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-pagination-nav, icon-button, shared-element, shared-field, shared-localize, tooltip, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-pagination-nav.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/pagination-nav.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-i18n, core-pagination-nav, core-position, tw-i18n, tw-icon-button, tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it

`total-items` is the number of pages (Carbon's name).


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/pagination-nav';</script>

<ui-pagination-nav total-items="25"></ui-pagination-nav>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiPaginationNav } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiPaginationNav totalItems={25} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { PaginationNav } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/pagination-nav';

<PaginationNav totalItems={25} />
```

## Pagination or pagination nav?

| Component | Use it when |
|---|---|
| [Pagination](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/pagination/) | Under a data table: the user picks how many rows a page shows and sees "1–10 of 240 items". |
| Pagination nav | Numbered pages of content that reads like a book: search results, a long report, the pages of a scanned contract. |

## Starting page and changes

`page` is the current page, 0-based: `page="3"` shows page 4. `ui-change` fires after the user chose another page, with the 0-based page in `detail.page`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-pagination-nav id="pagination-nav-start" total-items="25" page="3"></ui-pagination-nav>
<p>Page: <output id="pagination-nav-start-out"></output></p>

<script type="module">
  const nav = document.getElementById('pagination-nav-start');
  const out = document.getElementById('pagination-nav-start-out');
  out.value = `${nav.page + 1} of ${nav.totalItems}`;
  nav.addEventListener('ui-change', (event) => (out.value = `${event.detail.page + 1} of ${nav.totalItems}`));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const [page, setPage] = useState(3);

<UiPaginationNav totalItems={25} page={page} onUiChange={(e) => setPage(e.detail.page)} />
<p>Page: <output>{page + 1} of 25</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [page, setPage] = useState(3);

<PaginationNav totalItems={25} page={page} onChange={setPage} />
<p>Page: <output>{page + 1} of 25</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind also takes `defaultPage` for an uncontrolled start.

## Every page fits

With as many pages as `items-shown` or fewer, every number shows and there are no "…" menus.


HTML:

```html
<ui-pagination-nav total-items="5"></ui-pagination-nav>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiPaginationNav totalItems={5} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<PaginationNav totalItems={5} />
```

## How many items show

`items-shown` (`itemsShown`) is how many page items the row holds, the "…" menus included: 10 by default, 4 at least. Lower it where the row has little room.


HTML:

```html
<ui-pagination-nav total-items="25" items-shown="5" page="12"></ui-pagination-nav>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiPaginationNav totalItems={25} itemsShown={5} page={12} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<PaginationNav totalItems={25} itemsShown={5} defaultPage={12} />
```

On a window narrower than 320px, the row falls back to fewer items by itself.

## Wrap around

With `loop`, Previous on the first page goes to the last one, and Next on the last page to the first. Without it, they are disabled at the ends.


HTML:

```html
<ui-pagination-nav total-items="8" loop></ui-pagination-nav>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiPaginationNav totalItems={8} loop />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<PaginationNav totalItems={8} loop />
```

## Turn off the "…" menus

`disable-overflow` (`disableOverflow`) keeps the "…" in the row but stops it from opening. The user then moves with Previous, Next and the numbers shown.


HTML:

```html
<ui-pagination-nav total-items="25" page="12" disable-overflow></ui-pagination-nav>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiPaginationNav totalItems={25} page={12} disableOverflow />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<PaginationNav totalItems={25} defaultPage={12} disableOverflow />
```

## Sizes

`size`: `sm` 32px, `md` 40px, `lg` 48px (the default). Previous and Next follow the same size.


HTML:

```html
<ui-pagination-nav total-items="25" size="sm"></ui-pagination-nav>
<ui-pagination-nav total-items="25" size="md"></ui-pagination-nav>
<ui-pagination-nav total-items="25"></ui-pagination-nav>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiPaginationNav totalItems={25} size="sm" />
<UiPaginationNav totalItems={25} size="md" />
<UiPaginationNav totalItems={25} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<PaginationNav totalItems={25} size="sm" />
<PaginationNav totalItems={25} size="md" />
<PaginationNav totalItems={25} />
```

## Tooltip placement

Previous and Next are icon buttons: their name shows as a tooltip on hover and focus, below them by default. `tooltip-placement` (`tooltipPlacement`) moves it, for example above a row that sits at the bottom of the window.


HTML:

```html
<ui-pagination-nav total-items="25" tooltip-placement="top"></ui-pagination-nav>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiPaginationNav totalItems={25} tooltipPlacement="top" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<PaginationNav totalItems={25} tooltipPlacement="top" />
```

## Page through a list

The component only says which page to show; slicing the content is yours. Here 12 contracts show three per page.


HTML:

```html
<ol id="pagination-nav-list" start="1" style="margin: 0; padding-inline-start: 24px"></ol>
<ui-pagination-nav id="pagination-nav-records" total-items="4" size="md"></ui-pagination-nav>

<script type="module">
  const contracts = [
    'Office supplies', 'Cleaning services', 'Server lease', 'Car rental',
    'Printer maintenance', 'Security guards', 'Catering', 'Software licences',
    'Office lease', 'Legal advice', 'Translation', 'Courier services',
  ];
  const perPage = 3;
  const list = document.getElementById('pagination-nav-list');
  const nav = document.getElementById('pagination-nav-records');
  const show = (page) => {
    list.start = page * perPage + 1;
    list.replaceChildren(...contracts.slice(page * perPage, (page + 1) * perPage).map((name) => Object.assign(document.createElement('li'), { textContent: name })));
  };
  show(nav.page);
  nav.addEventListener('ui-change', (event) => show(event.detail.page));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
// contracts as in the HTML tab
const perPage = 3;
const [page, setPage] = useState(0);

<ol start={page * perPage + 1}>
  {contracts.slice(page * perPage, (page + 1) * perPage).map((name) => <li key={name}>{name}</li>)}
</ol>
<UiPaginationNav totalItems={Math.ceil(contracts.length / perPage)} size="md" page={page} onUiChange={(e) => setPage(e.detail.page)} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ol start={page * perPage + 1}>
  {contracts.slice(page * perPage, (page + 1) * perPage).map((name) => <li key={name}>{name}</li>)}
</ol>
<PaginationNav totalItems={Math.ceil(contracts.length / perPage)} size="md" page={page} onChange={setPage} />
```

## Accessibility

- The row is a `<nav>` landmark named "Pagination" (translated), holding a list.
- Each page is a button that screen readers read as "Page 4"; the current one reads "Active, Page 4" and has `aria-current="page"`.
- Each "…" is a `<select>` named "Select page number": the keyboard and phones open it like any select.
- After a change, a polite live region says "Page 5 of 25".
- Previous and Next are icon buttons named "Previous" and "Next", with tooltips; they are disabled at the ends unless `loop` is on.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Pagination nav](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-pagination-nav/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-pagination-nav>` · React `UiPaginationNav`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | `page` | `number` | `0` | The current page, 0-based (Carbon). |
| `total-items` | `totalItems` | `number` | `1` |  |
| `items-shown` | `itemsShown` | `number` | `10` | Page items in the row (at least 4). |
| `loop` | `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | Previous on the first page goes to the last, Next on the last to the first. |
| `disable-overflow` | `disableOverflow` | `boolean` | `false` | The "…" selects can't be opened. |
| `size` | `size` | `NavSize` | `'lg'` |  |
| `tooltip-placement` | `tooltipPlacement` | `TooltipPlacement` | `'bottom'` | Where Previous / Next show their tooltip. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-change` | `onUiChange` | detail: { page } (0-based) after the user chose a page |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The `<nav>` |
| `page` | Each page button |
| `overflow` | Each "…" select |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-button-radius` |  | Corner radius of the page buttons (the button setting) |
| `--ui-focus-offset` |  | `outline-offset` of its focus ring (default -2px: inside; Kanok: 2px outside) |
| `--ui-pagination-nav-mark-height` |  | Height of the current page's underline (default 4px; Kanok: 2px) |

# Content switcher

A content switcher shows the same content in another way: a filter (all requests or only mine) or a view (table or grid). Exactly one item is selected, and the switch happens at once.


HTML:

```html
<ui-content-switcher aria-label="Requests" style="max-width: 560px">
  <ui-content-switcher-item name="all">All requests</ui-content-switcher-item>
  <ui-content-switcher-item name="mine">Assigned to me</ui-content-switcher-item>
  <ui-content-switcher-item name="archived">Archived</ui-content-switcher-item>
</ui-content-switcher>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiContentSwitcher aria-label="Requests" style={{ maxWidth: 560 }}>
  <UiContentSwitcherItem name="all">All requests</UiContentSwitcherItem>
  <UiContentSwitcherItem name="mine">Assigned to me</UiContentSwitcherItem>
  <UiContentSwitcherItem name="archived">Archived</UiContentSwitcherItem>
</UiContentSwitcher>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ContentSwitcher aria-label="Requests" className="max-w-[560px]">
  <ContentSwitcherItem name="all">All requests</ContentSwitcherItem>
  <ContentSwitcherItem name="mine">Assigned to me</ContentSwitcherItem>
  <ContentSwitcherItem name="archived">Archived</ContentSwitcherItem>
</ContentSwitcher>
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/content-switcher
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash

```

Manual:

```bash

# 2. Copy each file's "content" from

#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/content-switcher/content-switcher-item.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/content-switcher/content-switcher.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-roving, shared-element, shared-field, tooltip, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-content-switcher.json

# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
```
