# Product card

`ui-productive-card` and `ui-expressive-card` are Carbon for IBM Products' `ProductiveCard` and `ExpressiveCard`: cards you configure with attributes, not with parts. They are IBM Products' legacy cards, kept for screens that must match IBM product UIs. **For new work, use [Card](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/card/)**: Carbon's parts-based card, where both Carbon and IBM Products are heading.


HTML:

```html
<ui-productive-card label="Department" heading="Legal" description="6 people" primary-button-text="View team" style="max-width: 360px">
  <ui-icon-button slot="actions" label="Edit"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M1 13h14v1H1zM12.7 4.5 10.5 2.3a1 1 0 0 0-1.4 0L3 8.4V11h2.6l6.1-6.1a1 1 0 0 0 0-1.4zM5.2 10H4V8.8l4-4 1.2 1.2zm4.7-4.7L8.7 4.1l1.1-1.1L11 4.2z" /></svg></ui-icon-button>
  14 contracts in review, 2 overdue.
</ui-productive-card>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProductiveCard label="Department" heading="Legal" description="6 people" primaryButtonText="View team" style={{ maxWidth: 360 }}>
  <UiIconButton slot="actions" label="Edit">{editIcon}</UiIconButton>
  14 contracts in review, 2 overdue.
</UiProductiveCard>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProductiveCard
  label="Department"
  title="Legal"
  description="6 people"
  primaryButtonText="View team"
  actionIcons={[{ id: 'edit', icon: editIcon, iconDescription: 'Edit' }]}
  className="max-w-[360px]"
>
  14 contracts in review, 2 overdue.
</ProductiveCard>
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/product-card
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-product-card
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/product-card.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/product-card/expressive-card.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/product-card/product-card-shared.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/product-card/product-card.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/product-card/productive-card.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    button, core-product-card, icon-button, layer, menu, overflow-menu, shared-element, shared-localize, shared-slots, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-product-card.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/product-card.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-product-card, tw-button, tw-i18n, tw-icon-button, tw-layer, tw-menu, tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it

Both cards load from one module.


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/product-card';</script>

<ui-productive-card heading="Legal" description="6 people">14 contracts in review.</ui-productive-card>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiProductiveCard, UiExpressiveCard } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiProductiveCard heading="Legal" description="6 people">14 contracts in review.</UiProductiveCard>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { ProductiveCard, ExpressiveCard } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/product-card';

<ProductiveCard title="Legal" description="6 people">14 contracts in review.</ProductiveCard>
```

The title is `heading` on the element (`title` is every element's native tooltip) and `title` in React + Tailwind, as in Carbon.

## Productive, expressive or Card?

| Component | Use it when |
|---|---|
| `ui-productive-card` | Dense product screens that copy IBM Products: a compact title, small icon actions or an overflow menu, ghost buttons. |
| `ui-expressive-card` | Content cards that copy IBM Products: media, a pictogram, a larger title, primary and secondary buttons. |
| [Card](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/card/) | Anything new. You build it from parts, and it is where Carbon is going. |

## Action icons

Icon buttons go in the `actions` slot (`actionIcons` in React + Tailwind); give each a `label`. The card makes them ghost buttons and sets their size: small at the top, medium at the bottom. They are separate tab stops.


HTML:

```html
<ui-productive-card id="product-card-icons" heading="Branch renovation" description="Due in 3 days" style="max-width: 360px">
  <ui-icon-button slot="actions" label="Edit"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M1 13h14v1H1zM12.7 4.5 10.5 2.3a1 1 0 0 0-1.4 0L3 8.4V11h2.6l6.1-6.1a1 1 0 0 0 0-1.4zM5.2 10H4V8.8l4-4 1.2 1.2zm4.7-4.7L8.7 4.1l1.1-1.1L11 4.2z" /></svg></ui-icon-button>
  <ui-icon-button slot="actions" label="Delete"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M6 6h1v6H6zm3 0h1v6H9zM2 3v1h1v10a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h8a1 1 0 0 0 1-1V4h1V3zm2 11V4h8v10zM6 1h4v1H6z" /></svg></ui-icon-button>
  Silom branch, second floor. The contractor starts on 1 November.
</ui-productive-card>
<p>Pressed: <output id="product-card-icons-out">nothing yet</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const out = document.getElementById('product-card-icons-out');
  for (const button of document.querySelectorAll('#product-card-icons ui-icon-button')) {
    button.addEventListener('click', () => (out.value = button.label));
  }
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProductiveCard heading="Branch renovation" description="Due in 3 days">
  <UiIconButton slot="actions" label="Edit" onClick={edit}>{editIcon}</UiIconButton>
  <UiIconButton slot="actions" label="Delete" onClick={remove}>{trashIcon}</UiIconButton>
  Silom branch, second floor. The contractor starts on 1 November.
</UiProductiveCard>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProductiveCard
  title="Branch renovation"
  description="Due in 3 days"
  actionIcons={[
    { id: 'edit', icon: editIcon, iconDescription: 'Edit', onClick: edit },
    { id: 'delete', icon: trashIcon, iconDescription: 'Delete', onClick: remove },
  ]}
>
  Silom branch, second floor. The contractor starts on 1 November.
</ProductiveCard>
```

## Overflow menu

A productive card can show its actions in an overflow menu instead: put `ui-menu-item`s in the `overflow` slot (`overflowActions` in React + Tailwind). When there are menu items, they replace the icons. The menu button is named "Options" (translated); `overflow-aria-label` changes it. Choosing an item fires `ui-select`, which bubbles up to the card.


HTML:

```html
<ui-productive-card id="product-card-menu" heading="Supply agreement C-2026-014" description="Chiang Mai plant" overflow-aria-label="Contract actions" style="max-width: 360px">
  <ui-menu-item slot="overflow" label="Duplicate"></ui-menu-item>
  <ui-menu-item slot="overflow" label="Send for signature"></ui-menu-item>
  <ui-menu-item slot="overflow" label="Delete" kind="danger"></ui-menu-item>
  Packaging materials, monthly, until December 2027.
</ui-productive-card>
<p>Chosen: <output id="product-card-menu-out">nothing yet</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const card = document.getElementById('product-card-menu');
  const out = document.getElementById('product-card-menu-out');
  card.addEventListener('ui-select', (event) => (out.value = event.detail.label));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProductiveCard heading="Supply agreement C-2026-014" description="Chiang Mai plant" overflowAriaLabel="Contract actions">
  <UiMenuItem slot="overflow" label="Duplicate" onUiSelect={duplicate} />
  <UiMenuItem slot="overflow" label="Send for signature" onUiSelect={send} />
  <UiMenuItem slot="overflow" label="Delete" kind="danger" onUiSelect={remove} />
  Packaging materials, monthly, until December 2027.
</UiProductiveCard>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProductiveCard
  title="Supply agreement C-2026-014"
  description="Chiang Mai plant"
  overflowAriaLabel="Contract actions"
  overflowActions={[
    { id: 'duplicate', itemText: 'Duplicate', onClick: duplicate },
    { id: 'send', itemText: 'Send for signature', onClick: send },
    { id: 'delete', itemText: 'Delete', kind: 'danger', onClick: remove },
  ]}
>
  Packaging materials, monthly, until December 2027.
</ProductiveCard>
```

## Actions at the bottom

`actions-placement="bottom"` moves the icons (or the menu) into the footer, at medium size. With a primary button there too, the button goes at the start and the icons at the end.


HTML:

```html
<ui-productive-card heading="Monthly contract summary" description="September 2026" actions-placement="bottom" primary-button-text="View report" style="max-width: 360px">
  <ui-icon-button slot="actions" label="Download"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M13 12v2H3v-2H2v2a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h10a1 1 0 0 0 1-1v-2zM13 7l-.7-.7-3.8 3.8V1h-1v9.1L3.7 6.3 3 7l5 5z" /></svg></ui-icon-button>
  48 contracts signed, 5 expiring in the next 30 days.
</ui-productive-card>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProductiveCard heading="Monthly contract summary" description="September 2026" actionsPlacement="bottom" primaryButtonText="View report">
  <UiIconButton slot="actions" label="Download">{downloadIcon}</UiIconButton>
  48 contracts signed, 5 expiring in the next 30 days.
</UiProductiveCard>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProductiveCard
  title="Monthly contract summary"
  description="September 2026"
  actionsPlacement="bottom"
  primaryButtonText="View report"
  actionIcons={[{ id: 'download', icon: downloadIcon, iconDescription: 'Download' }]}
>
  48 contracts signed, 5 expiring in the next 30 days.
</ProductiveCard>
```

## Buttons

`primary-button-text` and `secondary-button-text` add buttons; on a productive card both are ghost buttons. They sit in the footer by default. `primary-button-placement="top"` moves the primary one next to the top actions as a small ghost button; `secondary-button-placement="top"` does the same for the secondary one, but only when there are other top actions, as in Carbon. A press fires `ui-primary-button-click` or `ui-secondary-button-click`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-productive-card id="product-card-buttons" heading="Approval request" description="From Malee S." primary-button-text="Approve" secondary-button-text="Reject" style="max-width: 360px">
  Purchase of 20 laptops for the Finance department, 640,000 baht.
</ui-productive-card>
<ui-productive-card id="product-card-top" heading="Approval request" description="From Somchai K." primary-button-text="Approve" primary-button-placement="top" style="max-width: 360px">
  Renewal of the cleaning contract, 12 months.
</ui-productive-card>
<p>Pressed: <output id="product-card-buttons-out">nothing yet</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const out = document.getElementById('product-card-buttons-out');
  for (const id of ['product-card-buttons', 'product-card-top']) {
    const card = document.getElementById(id);
    card.addEventListener('ui-primary-button-click', () => (out.value = `${card.description}: approve`));
    card.addEventListener('ui-secondary-button-click', () => (out.value = `${card.description}: reject`));
  }
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProductiveCard heading="Approval request" description="From Malee S." primaryButtonText="Approve" secondaryButtonText="Reject" onUiPrimaryButtonClick={approve} onUiSecondaryButtonClick={reject}>
  Purchase of 20 laptops for the Finance department, 640,000 baht.
</UiProductiveCard>
<UiProductiveCard heading="Approval request" description="From Somchai K." primaryButtonText="Approve" primaryButtonPlacement="top" onUiPrimaryButtonClick={approve}>
  Renewal of the cleaning contract, 12 months.
</UiProductiveCard>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProductiveCard title="Approval request" description="From Malee S." primaryButtonText="Approve" secondaryButtonText="Reject" onPrimaryButtonClick={approve} onSecondaryButtonClick={reject}>
  Purchase of 20 laptops for the Finance department, 640,000 baht.
</ProductiveCard>
<ProductiveCard title="Approval request" description="From Somchai K." primaryButtonText="Approve" primaryButtonPlacement="top" onPrimaryButtonClick={approve}>
  Renewal of the cleaning contract, 12 months.
</ProductiveCard>
```

`primary-button-disabled` and `secondary-button-disabled` disable a button.

## Button links and icons

`primary-button-href` and `secondary-button-href` make a footer button a link (a primary button at the top takes no `href`, as in Carbon). A 16px icon after the text goes in the `primary-button-icon` or `secondary-button-icon` slot (`primaryButtonIcon`, `secondaryButtonIcon` in React + Tailwind).


HTML:

```html
<ui-productive-card heading="Procurement policy" description="Version 4, 2026" primary-button-text="Read the policy" primary-button-href="#accessibility" style="max-width: 360px">
  <svg slot="primary-button-icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M9.3 3.7 13.1 7.5H1v1h12.1l-3.8 3.8.7.7 5-5-5-5z" /></svg>
  Who can approve purchases, and up to what amount.
</ui-productive-card>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProductiveCard heading="Procurement policy" description="Version 4, 2026" primaryButtonText="Read the policy" primaryButtonHref="/policies/procurement">
  <svg slot="primary-button-icon" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M9.3 3.7 13.1 7.5H1v1h12.1l-3.8 3.8.7.7 5-5-5-5z" /></svg>
  Who can approve purchases, and up to what amount.
</UiProductiveCard>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProductiveCard
  title="Procurement policy"
  description="Version 4, 2026"
  primaryButtonText="Read the policy"
  primaryButtonHref="/policies/procurement"
  primaryButtonIcon={<svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M9.3 3.7 13.1 7.5H1v1h12.1l-3.8 3.8.7.7 5-5-5-5z" /></svg>}
>
  Who can approve purchases, and up to what amount.
</ProductiveCard>
```

## Title size and heading level

`title-size="large"` sets a productive card's title in heading-03 instead of heading-compact-02. The title is an `<h2>`; set the level that fits your page with `heading-level` (`h1` … `h6`; `headingAs` in React + Tailwind). For markup in the label, title or description, use the `label`, `title` and `description` slots.


HTML:

```html
<ui-productive-card heading="Signed this month" heading-level="h3" title-size="large" style="max-width: 360px">
  <span slot="description">48 contracts, <b>12 more</b> than August</span>
  Sales 21 · Legal 15 · Procurement 12
</ui-productive-card>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProductiveCard heading="Signed this month" headingLevel="h3" titleSize="large">
  <span slot="description">48 contracts, <b>12 more</b> than August</span>
  Sales 21 · Legal 15 · Procurement 12
</UiProductiveCard>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProductiveCard title="Signed this month" headingAs="h3" titleSize="large" description={<>48 contracts, <b>12 more</b> than August</>}>
  Sales 21 · Legal 15 · Procurement 12
</ProductiveCard>
```

## Clickable

`clickable` turns one zone of the card into a button that fires `ui-click` on a click, Enter or Space (in React + Tailwind, passing `onClick` does it). `click-zone` picks the zone: `one` the whole card (default), `two` the header with the body, `three` the body. The zone's button lies under the card's own buttons, which stay separate tab stops and never fire `ui-click`. The title names the button and the description describes it.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(240px, 1fr)); gap: 16px">
  <ui-productive-card id="product-card-zone-one" clickable heading="Zone one" description="The whole card">
    <ui-icon-button slot="actions" label="Edit"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M1 13h14v1H1zM12.7 4.5 10.5 2.3a1 1 0 0 0-1.4 0L3 8.4V11h2.6l6.1-6.1a1 1 0 0 0 0-1.4zM5.2 10H4V8.8l4-4 1.2 1.2zm4.7-4.7L8.7 4.1l1.1-1.1L11 4.2z" /></svg></ui-icon-button>
    Click anywhere but the edit button.
  </ui-productive-card>
  <ui-productive-card id="product-card-zone-three" clickable click-zone="three" heading="Zone three" description="The body only" primary-button-text="Details">
    Only this text is the button.
  </ui-productive-card>
</div>
<p>Last click: <output id="product-card-zone-out">nothing yet</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const out = document.getElementById('product-card-zone-out');
  for (const id of ['product-card-zone-one', 'product-card-zone-three']) {
    const card = document.getElementById(id);
    card.addEventListener('ui-click', () => (out.value = `${card.heading}: ui-click`));
    card.addEventListener('ui-primary-button-click', () => (out.value = `${card.heading}: primary button`));
  }
  document.querySelector('#product-card-zone-one ui-icon-button').addEventListener('click', () => (out.value = 'Zone one: edit button'));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProductiveCard clickable heading="Zone one" description="The whole card" onUiClick={open}>
  <UiIconButton slot="actions" label="Edit" onClick={edit}>{editIcon}</UiIconButton>
  Click anywhere but the edit button.
</UiProductiveCard>
<UiProductiveCard clickable clickZone="three" heading="Zone three" description="The body only" primaryButtonText="Details" onUiClick={open} onUiPrimaryButtonClick={details}>
  Only this text is the button.
</UiProductiveCard>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProductiveCard title="Zone one" description="The whole card" onClick={open} actionIcons={[{ id: 'edit', icon: editIcon, iconDescription: 'Edit', onClick: edit }]}>
  Click anywhere but the edit button.
</ProductiveCard>
<ProductiveCard clickZone="three" title="Zone three" description="The body only" primaryButtonText="Details" onClick={open} onPrimaryButtonClick={details}>
  Only this text is the button.
</ProductiveCard>
```

## Disabled

`disabled` only announces the card as disabled (`aria-disabled`) and stops `ui-click`; it doesn't grey anything out, as in Carbon. Disable the buttons with `primary-button-disabled` and `secondary-button-disabled`, and say in the card why it can't be used.


HTML:

```html
<ui-productive-card clickable disabled heading="Loan contract template" description="Being revised until 15 October" primary-button-text="Use template" primary-button-disabled style="max-width: 360px">
  The legal department is updating the interest clauses.
</ui-productive-card>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProductiveCard clickable disabled heading="Loan contract template" description="Being revised until 15 October" primaryButtonText="Use template" primaryButtonDisabled>
  The legal department is updating the interest clauses.
</UiProductiveCard>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProductiveCard disabled onClick={open} title="Loan contract template" description="Being revised until 15 October" primaryButtonText="Use template" primaryButtonDisabled>
  The legal department is updating the interest clauses.
</ProductiveCard>
```

## Expressive card

`ui-expressive-card` is for content. Media goes across the top (`slot="media"`, at its own size up to the card's width), a pictogram above the title (`slot="pictogram"`), and the buttons in the footer: a primary and a secondary button by default. Action icons (`slot="actions"`) are small and sit at the end of the footer.


HTML:

```html
<ui-expressive-card id="product-card-expressive" label="Guide" heading="Signing a contract online" primary-button-text="Start" secondary-button-text="Later" style="max-width: 360px">
  <img slot="media" alt="" width="360" height="203" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 160 90'%3E%3Crect width='160' height='90' fill='%23d0e2ff'/%3E%3Cpath d='M66 20h22l10 10v40H66z' fill='%23ffffff'/%3E%3Cpath d='M72 42h20M72 50h20M72 58h12' stroke='%230f62fe' stroke-width='2'/%3E%3C/svg%3E" />
  <ui-icon-button slot="actions" label="Save for later"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M12 2v12.2l-3.5-2.6-.5-.4-.5.4L4 14.2V2h8m0-1H4a1 1 0 0 0-1 1v14l5-3.7 5 3.7V2a1 1 0 0 0-1-1Z" /></svg></ui-icon-button>
  Check the parties, sign with your one-time code, and download the signed copy.
</ui-expressive-card>
<p>Pressed: <output id="product-card-expressive-out">nothing yet</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const card = document.getElementById('product-card-expressive');
  const out = document.getElementById('product-card-expressive-out');
  card.addEventListener('ui-primary-button-click', () => (out.value = 'Start'));
  card.addEventListener('ui-secondary-button-click', () => (out.value = 'Later'));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiExpressiveCard label="Guide" heading="Signing a contract online" primaryButtonText="Start" secondaryButtonText="Later" onUiPrimaryButtonClick={start} onUiSecondaryButtonClick={later}>
  <img slot="media" alt="" width={360} height={203} src={guideImage} />
  <UiIconButton slot="actions" label="Save for later">{bookmarkIcon}</UiIconButton>
  Check the parties, sign with your one-time code, and download the signed copy.
</UiExpressiveCard>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ExpressiveCard
  label="Guide"
  title="Signing a contract online"
  primaryButtonText="Start"
  secondaryButtonText="Later"
  onPrimaryButtonClick={start}
  onSecondaryButtonClick={later}
  media={<img alt="" width={360} height={203} src={guideImage} />}
  actionIcons={[{ id: 'save', icon: bookmarkIcon, iconDescription: 'Save for later' }]}
>
  Check the parties, sign with your one-time code, and download the signed copy.
</ExpressiveCard>
```

`primary-button-kind` takes `primary` (default) or `ghost`, `secondary-button-kind` `secondary` (default) or `ghost`.

## Pictogram and media at the start

A pictogram goes above the title, 16px in. `media-position="left"` puts the media at the start, with the content beside it.


HTML:

```html
<ui-expressive-card heading="Non-disclosure agreement" primary-button-text="Use template" primary-button-kind="ghost" style="max-width: 360px">
  <svg slot="pictogram" width="48" height="48" viewBox="0 0 32 32" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M8 3h11l5 5v21H8zM19 3v5h5M12 14h8M12 18h8M12 22h5" /></svg>
  Two-way NDA in Thai and English, approved by the legal department.
</ui-expressive-card>
<ui-expressive-card heading="Asking for an approval" media-position="left" primary-button-text="Read" primary-button-kind="ghost" style="max-width: 560px">
  <img slot="media" alt="" width="180" height="180" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 90 90'%3E%3Crect width='90' height='90' fill='%23d0e2ff'/%3E%3Cpath d='M34 20h18l8 8v42H34z' fill='%23ffffff'/%3E%3Cpath d='M40 42h14M40 50h14M40 58h8' stroke='%230f62fe' stroke-width='2'/%3E%3C/svg%3E" />
  Pick the approvers, add a note, and follow the request from your inbox.
</ui-expressive-card>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiExpressiveCard heading="Non-disclosure agreement" primaryButtonText="Use template" primaryButtonKind="ghost">
  <svg slot="pictogram" width="48" height="48" viewBox="0 0 32 32" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" aria-hidden="true">…</svg>
  Two-way NDA in Thai and English, approved by the legal department.
</UiExpressiveCard>
<UiExpressiveCard heading="Asking for an approval" mediaPosition="left" primaryButtonText="Read" primaryButtonKind="ghost">
  <img slot="media" alt="" width={180} height={180} src={approvalImage} />
  Pick the approvers, add a note, and follow the request from your inbox.
</UiExpressiveCard>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ExpressiveCard title="Non-disclosure agreement" primaryButtonText="Use template" primaryButtonKind="ghost" pictogram={documentPictogram}>
  Two-way NDA in Thai and English, approved by the legal department.
</ExpressiveCard>
<ExpressiveCard title="Asking for an approval" mediaPosition="left" primaryButtonText="Read" primaryButtonKind="ghost" media={<img alt="" width={180} height={180} src={approvalImage} />}>
  Pick the approvers, add a note, and follow the request from your inbox.
</ExpressiveCard>
```

## Clickable expressive card

On an expressive card `clickable` always makes the whole card the button. Its own buttons stay separate.


HTML:

```html
<ui-expressive-card id="product-card-pick" clickable heading="Lease contract" description="Property, rent and term" primary-button-text="Preview" primary-button-kind="ghost" style="max-width: 360px">
  Start a new lease from the approved template.
</ui-expressive-card>
<p>Last press: <output id="product-card-pick-out">nothing yet</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const card = document.getElementById('product-card-pick');
  const out = document.getElementById('product-card-pick-out');
  card.addEventListener('ui-click', () => (out.value = 'card: start a lease'));
  card.addEventListener('ui-primary-button-click', () => (out.value = 'Preview button'));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiExpressiveCard clickable heading="Lease contract" description="Property, rent and term" primaryButtonText="Preview" primaryButtonKind="ghost" onUiClick={start} onUiPrimaryButtonClick={preview}>
  Start a new lease from the approved template.
</UiExpressiveCard>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ExpressiveCard title="Lease contract" description="Property, rent and term" primaryButtonText="Preview" primaryButtonKind="ghost" onClick={start} onPrimaryButtonClick={preview}>
  Start a new lease from the approved template.
</ExpressiveCard>
```

## Decorator and layers

The `decorator` slot puts a small element 16px from the top-end corner, for example an AI label or a tag. Both cards draw themselves in the layer colour they sit on, so inside a `ui-layer` they take the next one.


HTML:

```html
<ui-layer level="1" with-background style="padding: 16px">
  <ui-productive-card heading="Contract summary" description="Generated from 14 pages" style="max-width: 360px">
    <ui-tag slot="decorator" type="purple" size="sm">AI</ui-tag>
    The lease runs for three years with a 5% yearly increase.
  </ui-productive-card>
</ui-layer>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLayer level={1} withBackground style={{ padding: 16 }}>
  <UiProductiveCard heading="Contract summary" description="Generated from 14 pages">
    <UiTag slot="decorator" type="purple" size="sm">AI</UiTag>
    The lease runs for three years with a 5% yearly increase.
  </UiProductiveCard>
</UiLayer>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Layer level={1} withBackground className="p-4">
  <ProductiveCard title="Contract summary" description="Generated from 14 pages" decorator={<Tag type="purple" size="sm">AI</Tag>}>
    The lease runs for three years with a 5% yearly increase.
  </ProductiveCard>
</Layer>
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves through the click zone and the card's own buttons and links, in page order |
| Enter, Space | Presses the click zone or the focused button |

## Accessibility

- The title is a real heading (`<h2>` by default). Set `heading-level` so the page outline stays right.
- The click zone is a `<button>` named by the title (else the label, else the body) and described by the description.
- `disabled` only sets `aria-disabled`: the card looks the same, so say why it can't be used.
- Each action icon needs a `label`; it is the button's name and tooltip.
- The media and pictogram are decorative unless you give them a real `alt` or name.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Product card](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-product-card/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-productive-card>` · React `UiProductiveCard`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `click-zone` | `clickZone` | `ProductCardClickZone` | `'one'` | Which zone `clickable` makes one button: one = the card, two = the header with the body, three = the body. |
| `actions-placement` | `actionsPlacement` | `ProductCardPlacement` | `'top'` | Where the action icons (or the overflow menu) go. |
| `title-size` | `titleSize` | `ProductCardTitleSize` | `'default'` | default: heading-compact-02; large: heading-03. |
| `overflow-aria-label` | `overflowAriaLabel` | `string` | `''` | The overflow menu's name and tooltip (default: the translation's "Options", as Carbon's `iconDescription`). |
| `primary-button-placement` | `primaryButtonPlacement` | `ProductCardPlacement` | `'bottom'` | At the top the primary button joins the top actions (a ghost sm button, without `href`). |
| `secondary-button-placement` | `secondaryButtonPlacement` | `ProductCardPlacement` | `'bottom'` | At the top the secondary button joins the top actions, only when there are other top actions (as Carbon). |
| `heading` | `heading` | `string` | `''` | The title (Carbon `title`; named `heading` because `title` is every element's native tooltip). |
| `heading-level` | `headingLevel` | `string` | `'h2'` | The title's element (h1 … h6; Carbon `Heading` in its `Section`, an `<h2>` at the top of a page). |
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | Text above the title (label-01). |
| `description` | `description` | `string` | `''` | Text below the title (label-01). |
| `clickable` | `clickable` | `boolean` | `false` | Makes the card's click zone one button (Carbon: an `onClick`); listen for `ui-click`. |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Announced as disabled (`aria-disabled`, as Carbon); a clickable zone then fires no `ui-click`. No other change, as Carbon. |
| `primary-button-text` | `primaryButtonText` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `primary-button-href` | `primaryButtonHref` | `string` | `''` | Makes the primary button a link (in the footer; Carbon's button at the top takes no `href`). |
| `primary-button-disabled` | `primaryButtonDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `secondary-button-text` | `secondaryButtonText` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `secondary-button-href` | `secondaryButtonHref` | `string` | `''` | Makes the secondary button a link. |
| `secondary-button-disabled` | `secondaryButtonDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` |  |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-click` | none (use a ref) | The click zone was activated (a click, Enter or Space); not while `disabled` |
| `ui-primary-button-click` | none (use a ref) | The primary button was activated |
| `ui-secondary-button-click` | none (use a ref) | The secondary button was activated |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | The body (body-compact-01) |
| `label` | Replaces `label` |
| `title` | Replaces `heading` |
| `description` | Replaces `description` |
| `actions` | Icon buttons (`<ui-icon-button label="…">`); the card sets their `size` |
| `overflow` | `<ui-menu-item>`s of the overflow menu, shown instead of the action icons |
| `primary-button-icon` | A 16px icon after the primary button's text (Carbon `primaryButtonIcon`) |
| `secondary-button-icon` | A 16px icon after the secondary button's text |
| `decorator` | E.g. an AI label, 16px from the top-end corner |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The card |
| `click-zone` | The clickable zone's button (`clickable` only), covering the zone |
| `content` | The header, body and footer |
| `header` | The header |
| `label` | The label |
| `title` | The title (`<h2>` by default) |
| `description` | The description |
| `actions` | The action icons' (or overflow menu's) box, with the top buttons |
| `overflow` | The `<ui-overflow-menu>` |
| `body` | The body |
| `footer` | The footer |
| `primary-button` | The primary `<ui-button>` |
| `secondary-button` | The secondary `<ui-button>` |
| `decorator` | The decorator's box |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-tile-border-color` |  | Its 1px border, as the selectable tiles (default transparent; Kanok: a hairline) |
| `--ui-card-background` |  | Its fill (default `--ui-surface-1`; Kanok paper: a cool grey that sets it apart from the page, no border) |
| `--ui-card-radius` |  | / --ui-card-overflow - Corners and clipping, as `<ui-card>` (default square, visible; Kanok: 12px, clipped) |

# Code snippet

A code snippet shows code or a command that people copy: an install line, a config file, an ID inside a sentence. It has three types: `single` (one line), `multi` (a block that folds after 15 rows) and `inline` (a chip in running text). Every code sample on this site is a `ui-code-snippet`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-code-snippet>npm install @purpurabog/ui</ui-code-snippet>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiCodeSnippet>npm install @purpurabog/ui</UiCodeSnippet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<CodeSnippet>npm install @purpurabog/ui</CodeSnippet>
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/code-snippet
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-code-snippet
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/code-snippet.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/code-snippet/code-snippet-skeleton.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/code-snippet/code-snippet.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    copy-button, core-code-snippet, shared-align, shared-element, shared-events, shared-field, shared-localize, shared-skeleton, tooltip, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-code-snippet.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/code-snippet.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-position, tw-copy-button, tw-i18n, tw-theme, tw-tooltip, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/code-snippet';</script>

<ui-code-snippet>npm install @purpurabog/ui</ui-code-snippet>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiCodeSnippet } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiCodeSnippet>npm install @purpurabog/ui</UiCodeSnippet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { CodeSnippet } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/code-snippet';

<CodeSnippet>npm install @purpurabog/ui</CodeSnippet>
```

## Single line

`type="single"` (the default) is one 40px line with the copy button at the end. A line longer than the box scrolls sideways; it never wraps. Use it for commands and one-line values.


HTML:

```html
<ui-code-snippet>npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-date-picker @kanok-ui/tw-select @kanok-ui/tw-text-input</ui-code-snippet>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiCodeSnippet>npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-date-picker @kanok-ui/tw-select @kanok-ui/tw-text-input</UiCodeSnippet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<CodeSnippet>npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-date-picker @kanok-ui/tw-select @kanok-ui/tw-text-input</CodeSnippet>
```

## Multi-line

`type="multi"` shows a block with the copy button top-right. Up to 15 rows show at first; longer code gets a "Show more" button that opens the rest. As in `<pre>`, one line break right after the opening tag is dropped, so you can start the code on its own line.


HTML:

```html
<ui-code-snippet type="multi">
{
  "contract": "CT-2026-0142",
  "title": "Office supplies, FY2026",
  "department": "Procurement",
  "vendor": {
    "name": "Siam Office Co., Ltd.",
    "taxId": "0105556012345"
  },
  "amount": 120000,
  "currency": "THB",
  "startDate": "2026-01-01",
  "endDate": "2026-12-31",
  "approvers": [
    { "step": 1, "role": "Department head" },
    { "step": 2, "role": "Finance" },
    { "step": 3, "role": "Legal" }
  ],
  "status": "awaiting-signature",
  "attachments": ["quotation.pdf", "terms.pdf"]
}</ui-code-snippet>
```

React:

```tsx
const contractJson = `{
  "contract": "CT-2026-0142",
  "title": "Office supplies, FY2026",
  …
}`;

<UiCodeSnippet type="multi">{contractJson}</UiCodeSnippet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const contractJson = `{
  "contract": "CT-2026-0142",
  "title": "Office supplies, FY2026",
  …
}`;

<CodeSnippet type="multi">{contractJson}</CodeSnippet>
```

Write `<` as `&lt;` and `&` as `&amp;` when the code goes straight into HTML. In React, pass a string: JSX escapes it for you.

## Wrap long lines

A multi-line snippet scrolls sideways by default, which keeps code aligned. `wrap-text` (`wrapText` in React) wraps long lines instead: use it for prose-like content such as log messages or SQL.


HTML:

```html
<ui-code-snippet type="multi" wrap-text>
2026-03-14 09:12:05 INFO  approval.service  Contract CT-2026-0142 moved from "awaiting-finance" to "awaiting-legal" by somchai.j@example.com after the finance review found no issues with the quotation or the payment terms.
2026-03-14 09:12:06 INFO  notify.service    Sent an email to the legal team (legal@example.com) asking for a review of CT-2026-0142 within 3 working days.</ui-code-snippet>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiCodeSnippet type="multi" wrapText>{approvalLog}</UiCodeSnippet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<CodeSnippet type="multi" wrapText>{approvalLog}</CodeSnippet>
```

## Inline

`type="inline"` is a chip inside a sentence. The chip itself is the copy button: a click copies the code and its tooltip says "Copied!". Its name is the code, so screen readers read what they would copy.


HTML:

```html
<p>Install the package with <ui-code-snippet type="inline">npm install @purpurabog/ui</ui-code-snippet>, then load <ui-code-snippet type="inline">@purpurabog/ui/tokens.css</ui-code-snippet> once per app.</p>
```

React:

```tsx
<p>
  Install the package with <UiCodeSnippet type="inline">npm install @purpurabog/ui</UiCodeSnippet>, then load{' '}
  <UiCodeSnippet type="inline">@purpurabog/ui/tokens.css</UiCodeSnippet> once per app.
</p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<p>
  Install the package with <CodeSnippet type="inline">npm install @purpurabog/ui</CodeSnippet>, then load{' '}
  <CodeSnippet type="inline">@purpurabog/ui/tokens.css</CodeSnippet> once per app.
</p>
```

## Without a copy button

`hide-copy-button` (`hideCopyButton` in React) shows the code only. An inline snippet then becomes a plain code chip that isn't a button. Use it for code people read but shouldn't paste, such as an example of output.


HTML:

```html
<ui-code-snippet hide-copy-button>Status: awaiting-signature (3 of 4 approvals)</ui-code-snippet>
<p>A contract in the <ui-code-snippet type="inline" hide-copy-button>awaiting-signature</ui-code-snippet> state can't be edited.</p>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiCodeSnippet hideCopyButton>Status: awaiting-signature (3 of 4 approvals)</UiCodeSnippet>
<p>A contract in the <UiCodeSnippet type="inline" hideCopyButton>awaiting-signature</UiCodeSnippet> state can't be edited.</p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<CodeSnippet hideCopyButton>Status: awaiting-signature (3 of 4 approvals)</CodeSnippet>
<p>A contract in the <CodeSnippet type="inline" hideCopyButton>awaiting-signature</CodeSnippet> state can't be edited.</p>
```

## Copy something else

`text` is what gets copied instead of the code shown. Show a short or readable form, and copy the full one: here the snippet shows the request command with the token hidden, and copies it with the token.


HTML:

```html
<ui-code-snippet text="curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer 7f3c9a1e5b2d' https://api.example.com/contracts/CT-2026-0142">curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer ••••••' https://api.example.com/contracts/CT-2026-0142</ui-code-snippet>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiCodeSnippet text={`curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${token}' https://api.example.com/contracts/CT-2026-0142`}>
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer ••••••' https://api.example.com/contracts/CT-2026-0142
</UiCodeSnippet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<CodeSnippet text={`curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${token}' https://api.example.com/contracts/CT-2026-0142`}>
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer ••••••' https://api.example.com/contracts/CT-2026-0142
</CodeSnippet>
```

## Copy labels and feedback

- `copy-label` (`copyLabel`): the copy button's tooltip on a single or multi-line snippet (default "Copy to clipboard").
- `label`: the accessible name of the code box (single and multi), or, on an inline chip, its tooltip and description.
- `feedback`: the tooltip after a copy (default "Copied!"), shown for `feedback-timeout` ms (2000).
- `placement` (or Carbon's `align`): the side of the tooltip, `bottom` by default.


HTML:

```html
<ui-code-snippet label="Webhook URL" copy-label="Copy webhook URL" feedback="URL copied" feedback-timeout="3000" placement="top">https://hooks.example.com/approvals/7f3c9a1e</ui-code-snippet>
<p>Ask finance for the code <ui-code-snippet type="inline" label="Copy cost centre" feedback="Cost centre copied" placement="top">CC-4410-PROC</ui-code-snippet> before you submit.</p>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiCodeSnippet label="Webhook URL" copyLabel="Copy webhook URL" feedback="URL copied" feedbackTimeout={3000} placement="top">
  https://hooks.example.com/approvals/7f3c9a1e
</UiCodeSnippet>
<p>Ask finance for the code <UiCodeSnippet type="inline" label="Copy cost centre" feedback="Cost centre copied" placement="top">CC-4410-PROC</UiCodeSnippet> before you submit.</p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<CodeSnippet label="Webhook URL" copyLabel="Copy webhook URL" feedback="URL copied" feedbackTimeout={3000} placement="top">
  https://hooks.example.com/approvals/7f3c9a1e
</CodeSnippet>
<p>Ask finance for the code <CodeSnippet type="inline" label="Copy cost centre" feedback="Cost centre copied" placement="top">CC-4410-PROC</CodeSnippet> before you submit.</p>
```

## Rows shown

On a multi-line snippet, `max-collapsed-rows` (15) is how many 16px rows show before "Show more", and `max-expanded-rows` (0, no limit) caps the open block, which then scrolls. `min-collapsed-rows` (3) and `min-expanded-rows` (16) keep a minimum height. An open snippet whose code is no taller than `min-expanded-rows` folds back when the code is measured again, so lower that too when you lower the collapsed limit.


HTML:

```html
<ui-code-snippet type="multi" max-collapsed-rows="4" max-expanded-rows="8" min-expanded-rows="0">
SELECT c.id, c.title, c.amount, d.name AS department
FROM contracts c
JOIN departments d ON d.id = c.department_id
JOIN vendors v ON v.id = c.vendor_id
WHERE c.status = 'awaiting-signature'
  AND c.amount >= 100000
  AND c.start_date >= DATE '2026-01-01'
  AND d.code IN ('PROC', 'LEGAL', 'FIN')
  AND v.blacklisted = false
GROUP BY c.id, d.name
HAVING count(*) > 0
ORDER BY c.amount DESC
LIMIT 50;</ui-code-snippet>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiCodeSnippet type="multi" maxCollapsedRows={4} maxExpandedRows={8} minExpandedRows={0}>{contractQuery}</UiCodeSnippet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<CodeSnippet type="multi" maxCollapsedRows={4} maxExpandedRows={8} minExpandedRows={0}>{contractQuery}</CodeSnippet>
```

## Open or closed

`expanded` opens a multi-line snippet from the start; the element sets it as the user presses "Show more" and fires `ui-toggle` with `detail.expanded`. `show-more-text` and `show-less-text` change the button's words. In React + Tailwind, use `defaultExpanded`, or `expanded` with `onToggle` to hold the state yourself.


HTML:

```html
<ui-code-snippet id="code-snippet-open" type="multi" expanded show-more-text="Show the whole file" show-less-text="Show the start only">
# .env for the approvals service
APP_NAME=approvals
APP_ENV=production
APP_URL=https://approvals.example.com
APP_TIMEZONE=Asia/Bangkok
APP_LOCALE=th
DB_HOST=db.internal
DB_PORT=5432
DB_NAME=approvals
DB_USER=approvals_app
MAIL_FROM=no-reply@example.com
MAIL_HOST=smtp.example.com
MAIL_PORT=587
NOTIFY_LEGAL=legal@example.com
NOTIFY_FINANCE=finance@example.com
REVIEW_DAYS_LEGAL=3
REVIEW_DAYS_FINANCE=2
MAX_UPLOAD_MB=25
SESSION_MINUTES=30
AUDIT_LOG=true</ui-code-snippet>
<p>Expanded: <output id="code-snippet-open-out">true</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const snippet = document.getElementById('code-snippet-open');
  const out = document.getElementById('code-snippet-open-out');
  snippet.addEventListener('ui-toggle', (event) => {
    out.value = String(event.detail.expanded);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(true);

<UiCodeSnippet
  type="multi"
  expanded={open}
  showMoreText="Show the whole file"
  showLessText="Show the start only"
  onUiToggle={(e) => setOpen(e.detail.expanded)}
>
  {envFile}
</UiCodeSnippet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(true);

<CodeSnippet type="multi" expanded={open} onToggle={setOpen} showMoreText="Show the whole file" showLessText="Show the start only">
  {envFile}
</CodeSnippet>
```

## Handle the copy

Before copying, the snippet fires `ui-copy` with `detail.text` (cancelable). Listen to it to record the copy; call `preventDefault()` to put something else on the clipboard yourself, and the feedback still shows. In React + Tailwind, `onCopy` gets the text; return `false` to copy it yourself.


HTML:

```html
<ui-code-snippet id="code-snippet-copy">docker pull registry.example.com/approvals:2026.3.1</ui-code-snippet>
<p>Last copy: <output id="code-snippet-copy-out">none yet</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const snippet = document.getElementById('code-snippet-copy');
  const out = document.getElementById('code-snippet-copy-out');
  snippet.addEventListener('ui-copy', (event) => {
    out.value = `${event.detail.text} (${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()})`;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiCodeSnippet onUiCopy={(e) => audit('copied image tag', e.detail.text)}>
  docker pull registry.example.com/approvals:2026.3.1
</UiCodeSnippet>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<CodeSnippet onCopy={(text) => audit('copied image tag', text)}>
  docker pull registry.example.com/approvals:2026.3.1
</CodeSnippet>
```

## Disabled

`disabled` greys the code, disables the copy and "Show more" buttons, and takes the code box out of the Tab order. An inline chip stays focusable (`aria-disabled`) but copies nothing.


HTML:

```html
<ui-code-snippet disabled>npm install @purpurabog/ui</ui-code-snippet>
<p>Your plan doesn't include the API, so the key <ui-code-snippet type="inline" disabled>ak_live_••••</ui-code-snippet> can't be copied.</p>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiCodeSnippet disabled>npm install @purpurabog/ui</UiCodeSnippet>
<p>Your plan doesn't include the API, so the key <UiCodeSnippet type="inline" disabled>ak_live_••••</UiCodeSnippet> can't be copied.</p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<CodeSnippet disabled>npm install @purpurabog/ui</CodeSnippet>
<p>Your plan doesn't include the API, so the key <CodeSnippet type="inline" disabled>ak_live_••••</CodeSnippet> can't be copied.</p>
```

## Skeleton

While the code loads, show `ui-code-snippet-skeleton`: a 56px box with one bar (`single`), or 98px with three lines (`type="multi"`). It is hidden from screen readers, so say "loading" on the container (for example `aria-busy`). In React, use the `UiCodeSnippetSkeleton` wrapper. See [Skeleton](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/skeleton/) for the other placeholders.


HTML:

```html
<ui-code-snippet-skeleton></ui-code-snippet-skeleton>
<ui-code-snippet-skeleton type="multi"></ui-code-snippet-skeleton>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiCodeSnippetSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiCodeSnippetSkeleton />
<UiCodeSnippetSkeleton type="multi" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { CodeSnippetSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/code-snippet';

<CodeSnippetSkeleton />
<CodeSnippetSkeleton type="multi" />
```

On the web component, import it from `@purpurabog/ui/code-snippet-skeleton`.

## Keyboard

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves to the code box, then the copy button, then "Show more"; on an inline snippet, to the chip |
| Arrow keys | Scroll the focused code box when the code is wider or taller than it |
| Enter, Space | On the copy button or inline chip: copies. On "Show more": opens or closes the block |

## Accessibility

- The single and multi-line code box is a read-only textbox (`role="textbox"`, `aria-readonly`) that takes focus, so keyboard users can scroll it. Name it with `label` (default "Copy to clipboard"; "Webhook URL" is better).
- The copy button is named by its tooltip (`copy-label`). An inline chip is named by its code, and `label` becomes its description.
- After a copy, a polite live region says the feedback once.
- "Show more" has `aria-expanded`.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Code snippet](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-code-snippet/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-code-snippet>` · React `UiCodeSnippet`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `align` |  |  |  | Carbon's name for `placement` (same values) |
| `type` | `type` | `CodeSnippetType` | `'single'` |  |
| `text` | `text` | `string` | `''` | Text to copy instead of the slotted content. |
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name of the read-only textbox (single / multi); inline: the copy button's tooltip and description (the button is named by its code, WCAG 2.5.3). |
| `copy-label` | `copyLabel` | `string` | `''` | Tooltip of the copy button (single / multi). |
| `feedback` | `feedback` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `feedback-timeout` | `feedbackTimeout` | `number` | `2000` |  |
| `placement` | `placement` | `TooltipPlacement` | `'bottom'` |  |
| `hide-copy-button` | `hideCopyButton` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `wrap-text` | `wrapText` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `expanded` | `expanded` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `show-more-text` | `showMoreText` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `show-less-text` | `showLessText` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `max-collapsed-rows` | `maxCollapsedRows` | `number` | `15` | Rows (16px) visible while collapsed; 0 = no limit. |
| `max-expanded-rows` | `maxExpandedRows` | `number` | `0` | Rows visible while expanded; 0 = no limit. |
| `min-collapsed-rows` | `minCollapsedRows` | `number` | `3` |  |
| `min-expanded-rows` | `minExpandedRows` | `number` | `16` |  |

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `copyText` |  | (read-only) What gets copied: `text`, else the slotted code. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-toggle` | `onUiToggle` | detail: { expanded } when "Show more / less" is used |
| `ui-copy` | `onUiCopy` | detail: { text }; cancelable |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | The code |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `container` | Scrolling container (single) / `<pre>` wrapper (multi) |
| `code` | The `<code>` element |
| `copy-button` | The `<ui-copy-button>` (single / multi) |
| `expand-button` | The "Show more / less" button (multi) |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-code-background` |  | Fill of the snippet (default `--ui-surface-1`; Kanok: a light grey on its white surfaces) |
| `--ui-code-radius` |  | Corners of the single and multi-line snippets (default 0; Kanok: 8px; the inline chip keeps its 4px) |
| `--ui-focus-offset` |  | `outline-offset` of its focus ring (default -2px: inside; Kanok: 2px outside) |

### `<ui-code-snippet-skeleton>` · React `UiCodeSnippetSkeleton`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `type` | `'single' \| 'multi'` | `'single'` |  |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The box |
| `line` | Each bar |

# Copy button

A copy button puts a value on the clipboard: a request number, a link, an API key. It is Carbon's 40px icon button: its tooltip names it ("Copy to clipboard"), and after a copy the tooltip says "Copied!" for two seconds.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px">
  <span>Request RQ-2026-00123</span>
  <ui-copy-button text="RQ-2026-00123" label="Copy request number"></ui-copy-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<span>Request RQ-2026-00123</span>
<UiCopyButton text="RQ-2026-00123" label="Copy request number" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<span>Request RQ-2026-00123</span>
<CopyButton text="RQ-2026-00123" label="Copy request number" />
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/copy-button
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-copy-button
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/copy-button.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/copy-button/copy-button.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    shared-align, shared-element, shared-events, shared-field, shared-localize, tooltip, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-copy-button.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/copy-button.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-position, tw-i18n, tw-theme, tw-tooltip, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Copy button or code snippet?

| Component | Use it when |
|---|---|
| Copy button | The value is shown somewhere else, in your own layout: a field, a table cell, a heading. |
| [Code snippet](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/code-snippet/) | You show code or a command, and the copy button belongs to it. The snippet uses this button inside. |

## Next to the value

Put the button right after the value it copies, so it is clear what it copies. `text` is exactly what goes on the clipboard.

```html
<dl style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: max-content auto; gap: 8px 16px; align-items: center; margin: 0">

</dl>
```

## Label and feedback

`label` is the tooltip at rest and the button's accessible name (default "Copy to clipboard", in the page's language). `feedback` is the tooltip after a copy (default "Copied!"). Say what gets copied when there are several buttons on the screen.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-copy-button text="https://contracts.example.com/CT-2026-0142" label="Copy contract link" feedback="Link copied"></ui-copy-button>
  <ui-copy-button text="finance@example.com" label="Copy finance email" feedback="Email copied"></ui-copy-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiCopyButton text="https://contracts.example.com/CT-2026-0142" label="Copy contract link" feedback="Link copied" />
<UiCopyButton text="finance@example.com" label="Copy finance email" feedback="Email copied" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<CopyButton text="https://contracts.example.com/CT-2026-0142" label="Copy contract link" feedback="Link copied" />
<CopyButton text="finance@example.com" label="Copy finance email" feedback="Email copied" />
```

## Feedback time

`feedback-timeout` (`feedbackTimeout` in React) is how long the feedback shows, in ms (2000 by default). Pressing again starts the time over.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-copy-button text="RQ-2026-00123" feedback-timeout="1000" label="Copy (1 second feedback)"></ui-copy-button>
  <ui-copy-button text="RQ-2026-00123" feedback-timeout="5000" label="Copy (5 second feedback)"></ui-copy-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiCopyButton text="RQ-2026-00123" feedbackTimeout={1000} label="Copy (1 second feedback)" />
<UiCopyButton text="RQ-2026-00123" feedbackTimeout={5000} label="Copy (5 second feedback)" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<CopyButton text="RQ-2026-00123" feedbackTimeout={1000} label="Copy (1 second feedback)" />
<CopyButton text="RQ-2026-00123" feedbackTimeout={5000} label="Copy (5 second feedback)" />
```

## Tooltip side

`placement` puts the tooltip on a side: `top`, `bottom` (the default), `left`, `right`, each with `-start` or `-end`. `align` is Carbon's name for the same attribute. Near the edge of the screen, the tooltip flips to the side with room.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-copy-button text="RQ-2026-00123" placement="top"></ui-copy-button>
  <ui-copy-button text="RQ-2026-00123" placement="right"></ui-copy-button>
  <ui-copy-button text="RQ-2026-00123" placement="bottom-start"></ui-copy-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiCopyButton text="RQ-2026-00123" placement="top" />
<UiCopyButton text="RQ-2026-00123" placement="right" />
<UiCopyButton text="RQ-2026-00123" placement="bottom-start" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<CopyButton text="RQ-2026-00123" placement="top" />
<CopyButton text="RQ-2026-00123" placement="right" />
<CopyButton text="RQ-2026-00123" placement="bottom-start" />
```

## Copy a value that changes

`text` is read at the moment of the press, so set it whenever the value changes. Here the share link follows the expiry the user picks.


HTML:

```html
<ui-select id="copy-button-expiry" label="Link expires in" value="7">
  <option value="1">1 day</option>
  <option value="7">7 days</option>
  <option value="30">30 days</option>
</ui-select>
<div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px">
  <code id="copy-button-link">https://contracts.example.com/s/CT-2026-0142?days=7</code>
  <ui-copy-button id="copy-button-share" text="https://contracts.example.com/s/CT-2026-0142?days=7" label="Copy share link" size="sm"></ui-copy-button>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const expiry = document.getElementById('copy-button-expiry');
  const shown = document.getElementById('copy-button-link');
  const button = document.getElementById('copy-button-share');
  expiry.addEventListener('change', () => {
    const link = `https://contracts.example.com/s/CT-2026-0142?days=${expiry.value}`;
    shown.textContent = link;
    button.text = link;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
import type { UiSelect as SelectElement } from '@purpurabog/ui';

const [days, setDays] = useState('7');
const link = `https://contracts.example.com/s/CT-2026-0142?days=${days}`;

<UiSelect label="Link expires in" value={days} onChange={(e) => setDays((e.target as SelectElement).value)}>
  <option value="1">1 day</option>
  <option value="7">7 days</option>
  <option value="30">30 days</option>
</UiSelect>
<code>{link}</code>
<UiCopyButton text={link} label="Copy share link" size="sm" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [days, setDays] = useState('7');
const link = `https://contracts.example.com/s/CT-2026-0142?days=${days}`;

<Select label="Link expires in" value={days} onChange={(e) => setDays(e.target.value)}>
  <option value="1">1 day</option>
  <option value="7">7 days</option>
  <option value="30">30 days</option>
</Select>
<code>{link}</code>
<CopyButton text={link} label="Copy share link" size="sm" />
```

## Copy it yourself

Before it copies, the button fires `ui-copy` with `detail.text`. Call `preventDefault()` to put something else on the clipboard yourself; the feedback still shows. In React + Tailwind, `onCopy` gets the text; return `false` to copy it yourself. `showFeedback()` on the element shows the feedback at any time, for example after another control copied the value.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px">
  <span>CT-2026-0142</span>
  <ui-copy-button id="copy-button-own" text="CT-2026-0142" label="Copy contract summary" size="sm"></ui-copy-button>
</div>
<p>Copied: <output id="copy-button-own-out"></output></p>

<script type="module">
  const button = document.getElementById('copy-button-own');
  const out = document.getElementById('copy-button-own-out');
  button.addEventListener('ui-copy', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const summary = `${event.detail.text}: Office supplies, 120,000 THB, Procurement`;
    navigator.clipboard?.writeText(summary).catch(() => {});
    out.value = summary;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiCopyButton
  text="CT-2026-0142"
  label="Copy contract summary"
  size="sm"
  onUiCopy={(e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    void navigator.clipboard.writeText(`${e.detail.text}: Office supplies, 120,000 THB, Procurement`);
  }}
/>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<CopyButton
  text="CT-2026-0142"
  label="Copy contract summary"
  size="sm"
  onCopy={(text) => {
    void navigator.clipboard.writeText(`${text}: Office supplies, 120,000 THB, Procurement`);
    return false; // we copied it; the feedback still shows
  }}
/>
```

If the browser refuses the copy (no permission, no secure page and no fallback), the button shows no feedback, so it never says "Copied!" for nothing.

## Disabled

`disabled` greys the icon and takes the button out of the Tab order. Use it while there is nothing to copy yet, for example before a number is issued.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px">
  <span>Request number: pending</span>
  <ui-copy-button text="" label="Copy request number" disabled></ui-copy-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<span>Request number: pending</span>
<UiCopyButton text="" label="Copy request number" disabled />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<span>Request number: pending</span>
<CopyButton text="" label="Copy request number" disabled />
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves to the button; the tooltip shows its label |
| Enter, Space | Copies, and the tooltip shows the feedback |
| Esc | Hides the label tooltip (the feedback stays for its time) |

## Accessibility

- The tooltip text is the button's accessible name, so the icon needs no other label. Give each button its own `label` when there are several ("Copy contract number", "Copy tax ID").
- After a copy, a polite live region (`role="status"`) says the feedback once, so screen reader users hear "Copied!" too.
- Keep the copied value visible next to the button. The clipboard can't be seen, and users want to check what they took.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Copy button](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-copy-button/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-copy-button>` · React `UiCopyButton`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `align` |  |  |  | Carbon's name for `placement` (same values) |
| `text` | `text` | `string` | `''` | What gets copied. |
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name / tooltip at rest. |
| `feedback` | `feedback` | `string` | `''` | Tooltip text after copying. |
| `feedback-timeout` | `feedbackTimeout` | `number` | `2000` |  |
| `placement` | `placement` | `TooltipPlacement` | `'bottom'` |  |
| `size` | `size` | `'sm' \| 'md'` | `'md'` |  |
| `disabled` | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `data-copied` | `copied` | `boolean` | `false` | True while the feedback is showing. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `showFeedback()` | Show the "Copied!" tooltip for `feedback-timeout` ms (Carbon `Copy` fade-in → fade-out). |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-copy` | `onUiCopy` | detail: { text }; cancelable |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `button` | The native button |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-copy-button-background` |  | Its fill at rest (default `--ui-surface-1`; Kanok: transparent); `--ui-copy-button-radius` its corners (default 0; Kanok: 6px) |
| `--ui-focus-offset` |  | `outline-offset` of its focus ring (default -2px: inside; Kanok: 2px outside) |

# User avatar

A user avatar is a round picture of a person: their photo, their initials, or a user icon. It comes from Carbon for IBM Products. Use it next to a name in approval chains, comments, owners of a record, and the header's account button.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-user-avatar name="Thomas J. Watson"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Ada Lovelace" background-color="order-3-green"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar></ui-user-avatar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiUserAvatar name="Thomas J. Watson" />
<UiUserAvatar name="Ada Lovelace" backgroundColor="order-3-green" />
<UiUserAvatar />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<UserAvatar name="Thomas J. Watson" />
<UserAvatar name="Ada Lovelace" backgroundColor="order-3-green" />
<UserAvatar />
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/user-avatar
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-user-avatar
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/user-avatar.json

# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-position, core-user-avatar, shared-element, tooltip, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
# (none)
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-user-avatar.json
#    to its target:

# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):

```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/user-avatar';</script>

<ui-user-avatar name="Thomas J. Watson"></ui-user-avatar>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiUserAvatar } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiUserAvatar name="Thomas J. Watson" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { UserAvatar } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/user-avatar';

```

## What it shows

The avatar shows the first of these it has: the photo (`image`), a custom icon (`slot="icon"`), the initials of `name`, or the user icon.

## Initials

`name` gives the initials, as Carbon counts them: one word gives its first two letters ("Somchai" → "SO"), more words give the first letter of the first and of the last word ("Thomas J. Watson" → "TW"). Letters are upper-cased.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-user-avatar name="Thomas J. Watson"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="somchai jaidee"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Somchai"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Mary Ann de la Cruz"></ui-user-avatar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiUserAvatar name="Thomas J. Watson" />
<UiUserAvatar name="somchai jaidee" />
<UiUserAvatar name="Somchai" />
<UiUserAvatar name="Mary Ann de la Cruz" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<UserAvatar name="Thomas J. Watson" />
<UserAvatar name="somchai jaidee" />
<UserAvatar name="Somchai" />
<UserAvatar name="Mary Ann de la Cruz" />
```

## Thai names

Thai words count their consonants only: a leading vowel (เ แ โ ใ ไ), a vowel or tone mark above or below, and a following vowel are skipped. So two words give the first consonant of each ("สมศรี มั่นคง" → "สม", "เกษม ใจดี" → "กจ"), and one word gives its first two consonants ("สุดา" → "สด"). Pass the full name; you don't need to work out the initials yourself.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-user-avatar name="สมศรี มั่นคง"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="เกษม ใจดี" background-color="order-5-purple"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="สุดา" background-color="order-3-green"></ui-user-avatar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiUserAvatar name="สมศรี มั่นคง" />
<UiUserAvatar name="เกษม ใจดี" backgroundColor="order-5-purple" />
<UiUserAvatar name="สุดา" backgroundColor="order-3-green" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<UserAvatar name="สมศรี มั่นคง" />
<UserAvatar name="เกษม ใจดี" backgroundColor="order-5-purple" />
<UserAvatar name="สุดา" backgroundColor="order-3-green" />
```

## Sizes

`size`: `sm` 24px, `md` 32px (the default), `lg` 48px, `xl` 64px. The initials and the icon grow with it. Use `sm` in tables and lists, `md` next to body text, and `lg` or `xl` on a profile.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-user-avatar name="Thomas Watson" size="sm"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Thomas Watson" size="md"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Thomas Watson" size="lg"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Thomas Watson" size="xl"></ui-user-avatar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiUserAvatar name="Thomas Watson" size="sm" />
<UiUserAvatar name="Thomas Watson" size="md" />
<UiUserAvatar name="Thomas Watson" size="lg" />
<UiUserAvatar name="Thomas Watson" size="xl" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<UserAvatar name="Thomas Watson" size="sm" />
<UserAvatar name="Thomas Watson" size="md" />
<UserAvatar name="Thomas Watson" size="lg" />
<UserAvatar name="Thomas Watson" size="xl" />
```

## No name: the user icon

Without `name`, `image` or an icon, the avatar shows Carbon's user icon: 16px in `sm`, then 20, 24 and 32px. Use it for an account that hasn't set a name yet.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-user-avatar size="sm"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar size="lg"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar size="xl"></ui-user-avatar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiUserAvatar size="sm" />
<UiUserAvatar />
<UiUserAvatar size="lg" />
<UiUserAvatar size="xl" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<UserAvatar size="sm" />
<UserAvatar />
<UserAvatar size="lg" />
<UserAvatar size="xl" />
```

## Photo

`image` is the photo's URL; it fills the circle instead of the initials. `image-description` (`imageDescription`) is its alt text: give the person's name, or leave it empty when the name is already written next to it.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-user-avatar size="lg" image="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 64 64'%3E%3Crect width='64' height='64' fill='%23a6c8ff'/%3E%3Ccircle cx='32' cy='24' r='12' fill='%230f62fe'/%3E%3Cpath d='M10 64c2-14 12-22 22-22s20 8 22 22z' fill='%230f62fe'/%3E%3C/svg%3E" image-description="Thomas J. Watson"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar size="md" image="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 64 64'%3E%3Crect width='64' height='64' fill='%23a6c8ff'/%3E%3Ccircle cx='32' cy='24' r='12' fill='%230f62fe'/%3E%3Cpath d='M10 64c2-14 12-22 22-22s20 8 22 22z' fill='%230f62fe'/%3E%3C/svg%3E" image-description="Thomas J. Watson"></ui-user-avatar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiUserAvatar size="lg" image="/photos/t-watson.jpg" imageDescription="Thomas J. Watson" />

```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx

```

Keep `name` set too: if you remove `image` later (no photo, or it failed to load in your app), the initials come back.

## Custom icon

Put an icon in the `icon` slot (the `icon` prop in React + Tailwind) for something that isn't one person: a service account, a team, a bot. It is sized like the user icon (16 / 20 / 24 / 32px) and drawn in the inverse icon colour.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-user-avatar size="lg" background-color="order-2-gray"><svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 32 32" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M26 4H6a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v20a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h20a2 2 0 0 0 2-2V6a2 2 0 0 0-2-2Zm0 22H6V6h20Z" /><path d="M10 10h12v2H10zm0 5h12v2H10zm0 5h7v2h-7z" /></svg></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar background-color="order-6-teal"><svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 32 32" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 16a5 5 0 1 1 5-5 5 5 0 0 1-5 5Zm0-8a3 3 0 1 0 3 3 3 3 0 0 0-3-3ZM22 30h-2v-5a3 3 0 0 0-3-3H7a3 3 0 0 0-3 3v5H2v-5a5 5 0 0 1 5-5h10a5 5 0 0 1 5 5ZM22 4h2a5 5 0 0 1 0 10h-2v-2h2a3 3 0 0 0 0-6h-2ZM30 30h-2v-5a3 3 0 0 0-2.2-2.9l.6-1.9A5 5 0 0 1 30 25Z" /></svg></ui-user-avatar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiUserAvatar size="lg" backgroundColor="order-2-gray">
  <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 32 32" aria-hidden="true">{/* document icon */}</svg>
</UiUserAvatar>
<UiUserAvatar backgroundColor="order-6-teal">
  <svg slot="icon" viewBox="0 0 32 32" aria-hidden="true">{/* group icon */}</svg>
</UiUserAvatar>
```

