
## Colours

`background-color` (`backgroundColor`) picks one of Carbon's 12 avatar colours, `order-1-cyan` (the default) to `order-12-teal`: 1–6 are the strong grades, 7–12 the deep ones, and dark themes use lighter grades. Give each person a colour that stays the same, for example from their user id, so people learn to spot each other.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; align-items: center">
  <ui-user-avatar name="Anan" background-color="order-1-cyan"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Boonmee" background-color="order-2-gray"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Chanida" background-color="order-3-green"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Darunee" background-color="order-4-magenta"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Ekachai" background-color="order-5-purple"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Fah" background-color="order-6-teal"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Kanya" background-color="order-7-cyan"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Lamai" background-color="order-8-gray"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Manee" background-color="order-9-green"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Nara" background-color="order-10-magenta"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Ornanong" background-color="order-11-purple"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Pim" background-color="order-12-teal"></ui-user-avatar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
const colours = ['order-1-cyan', 'order-2-gray', 'order-3-green', 'order-4-magenta', 'order-5-purple', 'order-6-teal',
  'order-7-cyan', 'order-8-gray', 'order-9-green', 'order-10-magenta', 'order-11-purple', 'order-12-teal'] as const;

{people.map((p) => <UiUserAvatar key={p.id} name={p.name} backgroundColor={colours[p.id % colours.length]} />)}
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const colours = ['order-1-cyan', 'order-2-gray', 'order-3-green', 'order-4-magenta', 'order-5-purple', 'order-6-teal',
  'order-7-cyan', 'order-8-gray', 'order-9-green', 'order-10-magenta', 'order-11-purple', 'order-12-teal'] as const;

{people.map((p) => <UserAvatar key={p.id} name={p.name} backgroundColor={colours[p.id % colours.length]} />)}
```

## With a tooltip

`tooltip-text` (`tooltipText`) turns the avatar into a button named by that text, which shows it in a tooltip on hover and focus and takes a 2px focus ring. `tooltip-alignment` (`tooltipAlignment`) picks the side, `bottom` by default. Start the text with the initials, as Carbon does ("TW, Thomas J. Watson"), so the button's name includes what is seen.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-user-avatar name="Thomas J. Watson" tooltip-text="TW, Thomas J. Watson"></ui-user-avatar>
  <ui-user-avatar name="Somchai Jaidee" background-color="order-3-green" tooltip-text="SJ, Somchai Jaidee, Finance" tooltip-alignment="right"></ui-user-avatar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiUserAvatar name="Thomas J. Watson" tooltipText="TW, Thomas J. Watson" />
<UiUserAvatar name="Somchai Jaidee" backgroundColor="order-3-green" tooltipText="SJ, Somchai Jaidee, Finance" tooltipAlignment="right" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<UserAvatar name="Thomas J. Watson" tooltipText="TW, Thomas J. Watson" />
<UserAvatar name="Somchai Jaidee" backgroundColor="order-3-green" tooltipText="SJ, Somchai Jaidee, Finance" tooltipAlignment="right" />
```

The button does nothing on click by itself. Use the tooltip where only the avatar is shown (a row of reviewers); when the name is written next to it, leave the tooltip out.

## Next to a name

The common layout: the avatar, then the name and a second line. Here, the approvers of a contract. The written name says who it is, so the avatar needs no tooltip.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 12px">
  <div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px">
    <ui-user-avatar name="Somchai Jaidee" background-color="order-3-green"></ui-user-avatar>
    <div><div>Somchai Jaidee</div><div style="color: var(--ui-ink-muted); font: var(--ui-font-caption)">Department head, approved 12 Mar</div></div>
  </div>
  <div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px">
    <ui-user-avatar name="Darunee Srisuk" background-color="order-4-magenta"></ui-user-avatar>
    <div><div>Darunee Srisuk</div><div style="color: var(--ui-ink-muted); font: var(--ui-font-caption)">Finance, reviewing</div></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
{approvers.map((a) => (
  <div key={a.id} style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
    <UiUserAvatar name={a.name} backgroundColor={a.colour} />
    <div>
      <div>{a.name}</div>
      <div style={{ color: 'var(--ui-ink-muted)', font: 'var(--ui-font-caption)' }}>{a.role}, {a.status}</div>
    </div>
  </div>
))}
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
{approvers.map((a) => (
  <div key={a.id} className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <UserAvatar name={a.name} backgroundColor={a.colour} />
    <div>
      <div className="text-ink">{a.name}</div>
      <div className="type-caption text-ink-muted">{a.role}, {a.status}</div>
    </div>
  </div>
))}
```

## Accessibility

- Without a tooltip, the avatar is plain text (the initials) or an image with its `image-description`. Write the person's name next to it; initials alone don't say who it is.
- With `tooltip-text`, it is a button named by that text. Start the text with the initials so voice control users can say what they see.
- The colour carries no meaning, so it never needs a text equivalent.
- The icon slot is decoration: give the svg `aria-hidden="true"`.

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-user-avatar>` · React `UiUserAvatar`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `name` | `string` | `''` | The person's name or initials; the avatar shows the initials. |
| `image` | `image` | `string` | `''` | A photo's URL, shown instead of the initials. |
| `image-description` | `imageDescription` | `string` | `''` | The photo's alt text. |
| `size` | `size` | `UserAvatarSize` | `'md'` |  |
| `background-color` | `backgroundColor` | `UserAvatarColor` | `'order-1-cyan'` | One of Carbon's 12 avatar colours, `order-1-cyan` … `order-12-teal`. |
| `tooltip-text` | `tooltipText` | `string` | `''` | Shown in a tooltip and names the avatar, which becomes a button (e.g. "Thomas J. Watson"). |
| `tooltip-alignment` | `tooltipAlignment` | `Placement` | `'bottom'` |  |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| `icon` | A custom icon in place of the initials / user icon (sized 16 / 20 / 24 / 32px) |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `avatar` | The circle |
| `image` | The photo |
| `trigger` | The button around the avatar when it has a tooltip |

# Truncated text

Truncated text cuts a long text to a few lines with an ellipsis, and only when it doesn't fit, lets the user read the rest: in a tooltip, or with a "View more" toggle. It comes from Carbon for IBM Products. Use it for descriptions and notes in cards, tables and lists, where a long text would push everything else down.


HTML:

```html
<div style="inline-size: 320px; max-inline-size: 100%">
  <ui-truncated-text value="Supply of A4 paper, toner and stationery for the head office and the three regional branches, delivered monthly from January to December 2026, with a price review after six months."></ui-truncated-text>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTruncatedText value="Supply of A4 paper, toner and stationery for the head office and the three regional branches, …" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TruncatedText value="Supply of A4 paper, toner and stationery for the head office and the three regional branches, …" />
```

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/truncated-text';</script>

<ui-truncated-text value="Supply of A4 paper, toner and stationery for the head office …"></ui-truncated-text>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiTruncatedText } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiTruncatedText value="Supply of A4 paper, toner and stationery for the head office …" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { TruncatedText } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/truncated-text';

<TruncatedText value="Supply of A4 paper, toner and stationery for the head office …" />
```

The text goes in `value`, not in the element's content. The element fills its container's width, so the container decides where the lines break.

## Full text in a tooltip

`type="tooltip"` is the default. When the text is cut, it becomes a button that shows the whole text in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus. Use it where there is no room for a toggle, such as table cells.


HTML:

```html
<div style="inline-size: 240px; max-inline-size: 100%">
  <ui-truncated-text lines="1" value="CT-2026-0142: Office supplies for the head office and three regional branches"></ui-truncated-text>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<div style={{ inlineSize: 240 }}>
  <UiTruncatedText lines={1} value="CT-2026-0142: Office supplies for the head office and three regional branches" />
</div>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<div className="w-60">
  <TruncatedText lines={1} value="CT-2026-0142: Office supplies for the head office and three regional branches" />
</div>
```

## View more

`type="expand"` adds a "View more" toggle under a cut text. It opens the rest with a short height animation (none with reduced motion), and becomes "View less". Use it for longer notes that people read in full.


HTML:

```html
<div style="inline-size: 360px; max-inline-size: 100%">
  <ui-truncated-text type="expand" lines="3" value="Finance asks for two changes before signing: the payment term should be 30 days after delivery instead of 15, and the price review after six months needs a cap of 5%. Legal has no further comments. Once the vendor accepts both changes, send the contract to the department head for the final approval, then to the vendor for signature."></ui-truncated-text>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTruncatedText type="expand" lines={3} value={reviewNote} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TruncatedText type="expand" lines={3} value={reviewNote} />
```

## Only when it doesn't fit

The element measures the text. A text that fits shows as it is, with no ellipsis, no tooltip button and no toggle; it measures again when the box resizes or `value` changes.


HTML:

```html
<div style="inline-size: 320px; max-inline-size: 100%; display: grid; gap: 16px">
  <ui-truncated-text type="expand" value="Reviewed by finance. No changes."></ui-truncated-text>
  <ui-truncated-text type="expand" value="Reviewed by finance. The payment term should be 30 days after delivery instead of 15, and the price review after six months needs a cap of 5%."></ui-truncated-text>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTruncatedText type="expand" value="Reviewed by finance. No changes." />
<UiTruncatedText type="expand" value="Reviewed by finance. The payment term should be 30 days after delivery instead of 15, …" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TruncatedText type="expand" value="Reviewed by finance. No changes." />
<TruncatedText type="expand" value="Reviewed by finance. The payment term should be 30 days after delivery instead of 15, …" />
```

## Lines

`lines` is how many lines show before the ellipsis: 2 by default. `0` shows the whole text.


HTML:

```html
<div style="inline-size: 320px; max-inline-size: 100%; display: grid; gap: 16px">
  <ui-truncated-text lines="1" value="Supply of A4 paper, toner and stationery for the head office and the three regional branches, delivered monthly from January to December 2026."></ui-truncated-text>
  <ui-truncated-text lines="3" value="Supply of A4 paper, toner and stationery for the head office and the three regional branches, delivered monthly from January to December 2026, with a price review after six months and a cap of 5% on any increase."></ui-truncated-text>
  <ui-truncated-text lines="0" value="Supply of A4 paper, toner and stationery for the head office and the three regional branches, delivered monthly from January to December 2026."></ui-truncated-text>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTruncatedText lines={1} value={scope} />
<UiTruncatedText lines={3} value={scope} />
<UiTruncatedText lines={0} value={scope} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TruncatedText lines={1} value={scope} />
<TruncatedText lines={3} value={scope} />
<TruncatedText lines={0} value={scope} />
```

## Toggle words

`expand-label` and `collapse-label` (`expandLabel`, `collapseLabel`) replace "View more" and "View less" (which follow the page's language). Keep them short and say what opens.


HTML:

```html
<div style="inline-size: 320px; max-inline-size: 100%">
  <ui-truncated-text type="expand" expand-label="Read the full note" collapse-label="Hide the note" value="Legal: clause 7.2 (late delivery penalty) should refer to working days, not calendar days. Clause 9 (termination) is fine as written. Please send the revised draft by Friday."></ui-truncated-text>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTruncatedText type="expand" expandLabel="Read the full note" collapseLabel="Hide the note" value={legalNote} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TruncatedText type="expand" expandLabel="Read the full note" collapseLabel="Hide the note" value={legalNote} />
```

## Tooltip side

`placement` sets the tooltip's side: `top` (the default), `bottom`, `left`, `right`, each with `-start` or `-end`. `align` is Carbon's name for it.


HTML:

```html
<div style="inline-size: 240px; max-inline-size: 100%">
  <ui-truncated-text lines="1" placement="bottom-start" value="Vendor: Siam Office Supplies and Printing Co., Ltd. (head office)"></ui-truncated-text>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTruncatedText lines={1} placement="bottom-start" value="Vendor: Siam Office Supplies and Printing Co., Ltd. (head office)" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TruncatedText lines={1} placement="bottom-start" value="Vendor: Siam Office Supplies and Printing Co., Ltd. (head office)" />
```

## Open from code

`expanded` shows an expandable text in full; set it to open or close several texts at once. Set from code, it changes without the animation. `ui-toggle` fires with `detail.expanded` when the user presses the toggle. In React + Tailwind, hold it with `expanded` and `onExpandedChange`, or start with `defaultExpanded`.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button id="truncated-text-open-all" kind="tertiary" size="sm">Open all notes</ui-button>
  <ui-button id="truncated-text-close-all" kind="ghost" size="sm">Close all notes</ui-button>
</div>
<div id="truncated-text-notes" style="inline-size: 360px; max-inline-size: 100%; display: grid; gap: 16px">
  <ui-truncated-text type="expand" value="Finance: the payment term should be 30 days after delivery instead of 15, and the price review after six months needs a cap of 5%. Everything else is fine."></ui-truncated-text>
  <ui-truncated-text type="expand" value="Legal: clause 7.2 (late delivery penalty) should refer to working days, not calendar days. Clause 9 (termination) is fine as written."></ui-truncated-text>
</div>
<p>Last toggle: <output id="truncated-text-open-out">none yet</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const notes = document.getElementById('truncated-text-notes').querySelectorAll('ui-truncated-text');
  const out = document.getElementById('truncated-text-open-out');
  const setAll = (open) => notes.forEach((note) => { note.expanded = open; });
  document.getElementById('truncated-text-open-all').addEventListener('click', () => setAll(true));
  document.getElementById('truncated-text-close-all').addEventListener('click', () => setAll(false));
  notes.forEach((note) => note.addEventListener('ui-toggle', (event) => {
    out.value = `expanded: ${event.detail.expanded}`;
  }));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState<Record<string, boolean>>({});
const setAll = (value: boolean) => setOpen(Object.fromEntries(notes.map((n) => [n.id, value])));

<UiButton kind="tertiary" size="sm" onClick={() => setAll(true)}>Open all notes</UiButton>
<UiButton kind="ghost" size="sm" onClick={() => setAll(false)}>Close all notes</UiButton>
{notes.map((note) => (
  <UiTruncatedText
    key={note.id}
    type="expand"
    value={note.text}
    expanded={!!open[note.id]}
    onUiToggle={(e) => setOpen((o) => ({ ...o, [note.id]: e.detail.expanded }))}
  />
))}
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState<Record<string, boolean>>({});
const setAll = (value: boolean) => setOpen(Object.fromEntries(notes.map((n) => [n.id, value])));

<Button kind="tertiary" size="sm" onClick={() => setAll(true)}>Open all notes</Button>
<Button kind="ghost" size="sm" onClick={() => setAll(false)}>Close all notes</Button>
{notes.map((note) => (
  <TruncatedText
    key={note.id}
    type="expand"
    value={note.text}
    expanded={!!open[note.id]}
    onExpandedChange={(value) => setOpen((o) => ({ ...o, [note.id]: value }))}
  />
))}
```

## It follows its box

The text is measured again whenever its box resizes, so the ellipsis, the tooltip button and the toggle come and go with the layout. Drag the corner of the box below to see it.


HTML:

```html
<div style="inline-size: 280px; max-inline-size: 100%; resize: horizontal; overflow: auto; padding: 8px; border: 1px dashed var(--ui-hairline)">
  <ui-truncated-text type="expand" value="Supply of A4 paper, toner and stationery for the head office and the three regional branches, delivered monthly from January to December 2026."></ui-truncated-text>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<div style={{ inlineSize: 280, resize: 'horizontal', overflow: 'auto' }}>
  <UiTruncatedText type="expand" value={scope} />
</div>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<div className="w-70 resize-x overflow-auto">
  <TruncatedText type="expand" value={scope} />
</div>
```

## Style a cut text

While the text doesn't fit its lines, the element has `data-overflowing` (kept while it is open). Style on it, for example to mark notes that have more to read. The text itself is the `content` part. In React + Tailwind the attribute is on the outer `<div>`, so use `data-overflowing:` classes.


HTML:

```html
<style>
  #truncated-text-marked ui-truncated-text[data-overflowing] {
    border-inline-start: 2px solid var(--ui-border-interactive);
    padding-inline-start: 8px;
  }
</style>
<div id="truncated-text-marked" style="inline-size: 320px; max-inline-size: 100%; display: grid; gap: 16px">
  <ui-truncated-text lines="1" value="Approved by the department head."></ui-truncated-text>
  <ui-truncated-text lines="1" value="Approved with a condition: the vendor must send the delivery schedule before the first order."></ui-truncated-text>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
/* CSS: ui-truncated-text[data-overflowing] { border-inline-start: 2px solid var(--ui-border-interactive); padding-inline-start: 8px; } */
<UiTruncatedText lines={1} value="Approved by the department head." />
<UiTruncatedText lines={1} value="Approved with a condition: the vendor must send the delivery schedule before the first order." />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const marked = 'data-overflowing:border-s-2 data-overflowing:border-border-interactive data-overflowing:ps-2';

<TruncatedText lines={1} className={marked} value="Approved by the department head." />
<TruncatedText lines={1} className={marked} value="Approved with a condition: the vendor must send the delivery schedule before the first order." />
```

## It takes the font around it

The text has no font of its own: it uses the font, size and colour of where it sits. Put it inside a heading, a caption or a table cell, and it looks like them.


HTML:

```html
<div style="inline-size: 320px; max-inline-size: 100%; padding: 16px; background: var(--ui-layer-1)">
  <div style="font: var(--ui-font-heading-03)">
    <ui-truncated-text lines="1" value="Office supplies for the head office and regional branches"></ui-truncated-text>
  </div>
  <div style="font: var(--ui-font-caption); color: var(--ui-ink-muted); margin-block-start: 8px">
    <ui-truncated-text lines="2" value="Procurement · 120,000 THB · 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2026 · Siam Office Supplies and Printing Co., Ltd. · awaiting signature"></ui-truncated-text>
  </div>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<div style={{ font: 'var(--ui-font-heading-03)' }}>
  <UiTruncatedText lines={1} value={contract.title} />
</div>
<div style={{ font: 'var(--ui-font-caption)', color: 'var(--ui-ink-muted)' }}>
  <UiTruncatedText value={contract.summary} />
</div>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<div className="type-heading-03">
  <TruncatedText lines={1} value={contract.title} />
</div>
<div className="type-caption text-ink-muted">
  <TruncatedText value={contract.summary} />
</div>
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves to a cut tooltip text (its tooltip shows) or to the toggle |
| Enter, Space | On the toggle: opens or closes the text |
| Esc | Hides the tooltip |

## Accessibility

- A cut tooltip text is a button named by the whole text, so screen readers read all of it, not the cut part.
- The toggle has `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the text.
- A text that fits is plain text: no button, nothing extra to tab through.
- Don't cut text people must read to finish a task (an error, a legal condition they accept). Show it in full.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Truncated text](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-truncated-text/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-truncated-text>` · React `UiTruncatedText`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `align` |  |  |  | Carbon's name for `placement` (the tooltip's side) |
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` | The text. |
| `lines` | `lines` | `number` | `2` | Lines shown before the ellipsis; 0 = all. |
| `type` | `type` | `TruncatedTextType` | `'tooltip'` | What a truncated text offers: the whole text in a tooltip, or a toggle that expands it. |
| `placement` | `placement` | `Placement` | `'top'` | The tooltip's side. |
| `expand-label` | `expandLabel` | `string` | `''` | The expand toggle's text (default "View more", translated). |
| `collapse-label` | `collapseLabel` | `string` | `''` | The collapse toggle's text (default "View less", translated). |
| `expanded` | `expanded` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether an expandable text shows in full. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-toggle` | `onUiToggle` | detail: { expanded } when the toggle opens or closes the text |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `content` | The text |
| `trigger` | The button around the text of a truncated `type="tooltip"` |
| `toggle` | The expand / collapse button |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-focus-offset` |  | `outline-offset` of its focus ring (default -2px: inside; Kanok: 2px outside) |




---

# List

Carbon's lists show related items in running content: steps to follow, conditions, documents to attach. `ui-unordered-list` marks each item with an en dash, `ui-ordered-list` numbers them, and `ui-list-item` is one item. A list inside an item is nested, and the elements notice that for you.


HTML:

```html
<ui-unordered-list>
  <ui-list-item>A copy of the company registration</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>The vendor's quotation</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Bank account details for payment</ui-list-item>
</ui-unordered-list>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiUnorderedList>
  <UiListItem>A copy of the company registration</UiListItem>
  <UiListItem>The vendor's quotation</UiListItem>
  <UiListItem>Bank account details for payment</UiListItem>
</UiUnorderedList>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<UnorderedList>
  <ListItem>A copy of the company registration</ListItem>
  <ListItem>The vendor's quotation</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Bank account details for payment</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
```

## Unordered

Use an unordered list when the order doesn't matter. Each item gets an en dash 16px before the text, and the list is indented 16px.


HTML:

```html
<p>Before you submit the purchase request, attach:</p>
<ui-unordered-list>
  <ui-list-item>The vendor's quotation, signed and dated</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>A comparison of at least three quotations for amounts over 100,000 THB</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>The budget code from your department head</ui-list-item>
</ui-unordered-list>
```

React:

```tsx
<p>Before you submit the purchase request, attach:</p>
<UiUnorderedList>
  <UiListItem>The vendor's quotation, signed and dated</UiListItem>
  <UiListItem>A comparison of at least three quotations for amounts over 100,000 THB</UiListItem>
  <UiListItem>The budget code from your department head</UiListItem>
</UiUnorderedList>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<p>Before you submit the purchase request, attach:</p>
<UnorderedList>
  <ListItem>The vendor's quotation, signed and dated</ListItem>
  <ListItem>A comparison of at least three quotations for amounts over 100,000 THB</ListItem>
  <ListItem>The budget code from your department head</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
```

## Ordered

Use an ordered list for steps that happen in order. The numbers ("1.") sit 24px before the text, outside the list's own box, as in Carbon: leave at least 24px of room on the start side (the demo box has it).


HTML:

```html
<ui-ordered-list>
  <ui-list-item>Fill in the request and attach the quotation.</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Your department head approves it.</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Finance checks the budget code.</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Procurement issues the purchase order.</ui-list-item>
</ui-ordered-list>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiOrderedList>
  <UiListItem>Fill in the request and attach the quotation.</UiListItem>
  <UiListItem>Your department head approves it.</UiListItem>
  <UiListItem>Finance checks the budget code.</UiListItem>
  <UiListItem>Procurement issues the purchase order.</UiListItem>
</UiOrderedList>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<OrderedList>
  <ListItem>Fill in the request and attach the quotation.</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Your department head approves it.</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Finance checks the budget code.</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Procurement issues the purchase order.</ListItem>
</OrderedList>
```

## Nested unordered

Put a list inside an item to nest it. The inner list is 32px in, and its items get a small square (▪) 12px before the text. You don't set `nested`: a list inside a `ui-list-item` (a `ListItem` in React + Tailwind) sets it itself.


HTML:

```html
<ui-unordered-list>
  <ui-list-item>Company documents
    <ui-unordered-list>
      <ui-list-item>Company registration, issued in the last 6 months</ui-list-item>
      <ui-list-item>VAT registration (ภ.พ.20)</ui-list-item>
    </ui-unordered-list>
  </ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Bank details
    <ui-unordered-list>
      <ui-list-item>A copy of the account book's first page</ui-list-item>
    </ui-unordered-list>
  </ui-list-item>
</ui-unordered-list>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiUnorderedList>
  <UiListItem>
    Company documents
    <UiUnorderedList>
      <UiListItem>Company registration, issued in the last 6 months</UiListItem>
      <UiListItem>VAT registration (ภ.พ.20)</UiListItem>
    </UiUnorderedList>
  </UiListItem>
  <UiListItem>
    Bank details
    <UiUnorderedList>
```

## Browser numbers

`native` uses the browser's own decimal numbers instead of Carbon's counter. The browser lines them up on the dot once the list passes 9 items. In React + Tailwind, it also lets the `<ol>` attributes `start` and `reversed` work, which Carbon's counter ignores. Leave room on the start side here too.


HTML:

```html
<ui-ordered-list native>
  <ui-list-item>Request</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Department head</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Finance</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Legal</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Procurement</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Vendor signs</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Company signs</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Filing</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Payment set-up</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>First delivery</ui-list-item>
</ui-ordered-list>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiOrderedList native>
  {steps.map((step) => <UiListItem key={step}>{step}</UiListItem>)}
</UiOrderedList>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<OrderedList native>
  {steps.map((step) => <ListItem key={step}>{step}</ListItem>)}
</OrderedList>
```

## Expressive

`is-expressive` (`isExpressive`) sets the text in body-02 (16px / 24px) instead of body-01 (14px / 20px). Use it on reading pages, such as a policy or a help article. Nested lists take the size of their parent.


HTML:

```html
<ui-unordered-list is-expressive>
  <ui-list-item>Contracts over 1,000,000 THB need two signers.</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Keep signed copies for 10 years.
    <ui-unordered-list>
      <ui-list-item>Paper copies go to the archive room.</ui-list-item>
      <ui-list-item>Scans go to the contract system.</ui-list-item>
    </ui-unordered-list>
  </ui-list-item>
</ui-unordered-list>
```

```tsx
      <UiListItem>Scans go to the contract system.</UiListItem>

</UiUnorderedList>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx

  </ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
```

## Links and code in items

Items take any inline content: [links](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/link/), [inline code](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/code-snippet/#inline), emphasis. Long items wrap under their own text, not under the marker.


HTML:

```html
<ui-unordered-list>
  <ui-list-item>Read the <ui-link href="#list-policy" inline>signing policy</ui-link> before your first contract.</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item>Use the cost centre <ui-code-snippet type="inline">CC-4410-PROC</ui-code-snippet> for office supplies.</ui-list-item>
  <ui-list-item><strong>Don't</strong> sign a contract that legal hasn't reviewed, even when the vendor asks you to hurry because the price is only valid until the end of the week.</ui-list-item>
</ui-unordered-list>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiUnorderedList>
  <UiListItem>Read the <UiLink href="/policies/signing" inline>signing policy</UiLink> before your first contract.</UiListItem>
  <UiListItem>Use the cost centre <UiCodeSnippet type="inline">CC-4410-PROC</UiCodeSnippet> for office supplies.</UiListItem>
  <UiListItem><strong>Don't</strong> sign a contract that legal hasn't reviewed, even when the vendor asks you to hurry …</UiListItem>
</UiUnorderedList>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<UnorderedList>
  <ListItem>Read the <Link href="/policies/signing" inline>signing policy</Link> before your first contract.</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Use the cost centre <CodeSnippet type="inline">CC-4410-PROC</CodeSnippet> for office supplies.</ListItem>
  <ListItem><strong>Don't</strong> sign a contract that legal hasn't reviewed, even when the vendor asks you to hurry …</ListItem>
</UnorderedList>
```

## Accessibility

- Screen readers announce a list and its item count. `ui-list-item` gets `role="listitem"` (unless you set a role), and the list's `<ul>` / `<ol>` sits in the element's shadow root around the items.
- Use an ordered list only when the order matters; the numbers are read out.
- The markers are drawn with CSS, so they aren't read; don't put meaning in them.
- Keep items short and parallel: start each one the same way (all nouns, or all verbs).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-unordered-list>` · React `UiUnorderedList`

|---|---|

| `is-expressive` | `isExpressive` | `boolean` | `false` | Body-02 type (16px) for expressive pages. |

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|

| Part | Description |

# Loading

A loading spinner says that a view or an area is waiting for data. Carbon's spinner is 88px; `small` is 16px with a grey track. It can cover the whole page (`overlay`) or one area (`contained`), and it can wait before it shows, so quick work never flashes a spinner.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 32px; align-items: center">
  <ui-loading></ui-loading>
  <ui-loading small></ui-loading>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLoading />
<UiLoading small />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Loading />
<Loading small />
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/loading
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-loading
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/loading.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/loading/loading.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-spin-delay, shared-element, shared-field, shared-localize, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-loading.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/loading.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-status-indicator, tw-i18n, tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/loading';</script>

<ui-loading></ui-loading>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiLoading } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiLoading />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Loading } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/loading';

<Loading />
```

## Loading, inline loading, progress bar or skeleton?

- Loading: a whole view or one area can't be used until the data arrives.
- [Inline loading](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/inline-loading/): a small status next to the thing that is saving or sending, which ends as "done" or "failed".
- [Progress bar](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/progress-bar/): the work has a known size, such as files uploaded out of five.
- [Skeleton](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/skeleton/): the first load of a page, when you know the shape of the content to come.
- Inside a button, use the button's own `loading`; see [Button](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/button/#loading).

## Small

`small` is the 16px spinner with a grey track, for tight places such as a card header or a table toolbar.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 8px; align-items: center">
  <ui-loading small description="Loading approvals"></ui-loading>
  <span>Loading approvals…</span>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLoading small description="Loading approvals" />
<span>Loading approvals…</span>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Loading small description="Loading approvals" />
<span>Loading approvals…</span>
```

## Description

`description` names the spinner for screen readers and is announced when it shows. It defaults to "Loading", translated to the page language. Say what is loading.


HTML:

```html
<ui-loading description="Loading the contract list"></ui-loading>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLoading description="Loading the contract list" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Loading description="Loading the contract list" />
```

## Start and stop

The spinner is on by default. Set `active` to false to stop and hide it; the element stays in the page, ready for the next time. In HTML, write `active="false"` to start it stopped. While it really shows, the element has a `data-shown` attribute.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button id="loading-toggle" kind="secondary">Stop</ui-button>
  <ui-loading id="loading-toggle-spinner" small description="Loading contracts"></ui-loading>
</div>
<p>Active: <output id="loading-toggle-out">true</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const spinner = document.getElementById('loading-toggle-spinner');
  const button = document.getElementById('loading-toggle');
  button.addEventListener('click', () => {
    spinner.active = !spinner.active;
    button.textContent = spinner.active ? 'Stop' : 'Start';
    document.getElementById('loading-toggle-out').textContent = String(spinner.active);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const [busy, setBusy] = useState(true);

<UiButton kind="secondary" onClick={() => setBusy(!busy)}>{busy ? 'Stop' : 'Start'}</UiButton>
<UiLoading small active={busy} description="Loading contracts" />
<p>Active: <output>{String(busy)}</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [busy, setBusy] = useState(true);

<Button kind="secondary" onClick={() => setBusy(!busy)}>{busy ? 'Stop' : 'Start'}</Button>
<Loading small active={busy} description="Loading contracts" />
<p>Active: <output>{String(busy)}</output></p>
```

## Over one area

`contained` wraps an area, such as a card or a table, instead of the page. While it is active, the overlay covers just that box, and the content under it is inert and `aria-busy`. The rest of the page stays usable. Carbon has no contained loading; this is our addition.


HTML:

```html
<ui-button id="loading-area-run" kind="tertiary">Refresh summary (2 s)</ui-button>
<ui-loading id="loading-area" contained active="false" description="Refreshing the summary">
  <ui-tile>
    <h4 style="margin: 0 0 8px">Contract CT-2026-118</h4>
    <p style="margin: 0">Siam Logistics Co., Ltd. · 1 Nov 2026 – 31 Oct 2027 · ฿1,250,000</p>
  </ui-tile>
</ui-loading>

<script type="module">
  const area = document.getElementById('loading-area');
  document.getElementById('loading-area-run').addEventListener('click', () => {
    area.active = true;
    setTimeout(() => { area.active = false; }, 2000);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiButton kind="tertiary" onClick={refresh}>Refresh summary</UiButton>
<UiLoading contained active={refreshing} description="Refreshing the summary">
  <UiTile>
    <h4>Contract CT-2026-118</h4>
    <p>Siam Logistics Co., Ltd. · 1 Nov 2026 – 31 Oct 2027 · ฿1,250,000</p>
  </UiTile>
</UiLoading>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Button kind="tertiary" onClick={refresh}>Refresh summary</Button>
<Loading contained active={refreshing} description="Refreshing the summary">
  <Tile>
    <h4>Contract CT-2026-118</h4>
    <p>Siam Logistics Co., Ltd. · 1 Nov 2026 – 31 Oct 2027 · ฿1,250,000</p>
  </Tile>
</Loading>
```

`refresh` stands for your own code that sets `refreshing` while it works.

## Saving a form in place

Put the form inside a contained loading while it saves. Focus that was inside the area waits on the spinner, then goes back where it was, so keyboard users keep their place.


HTML:

```html
<ui-loading id="loading-form" contained active="false" description="Saving the department">
  <form id="loading-form-form" method="dialog" style="display: grid; gap: 16px; justify-items: start; padding: 16px; border: 1px solid var(--ui-hairline)">
    <ui-text-input label="Department" name="department" value="Procurement"></ui-text-input>
    <ui-button type="submit">Save</ui-button>
  </form>
</ui-loading>
<p>Saved: <output id="loading-form-out">not yet</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const loading = document.getElementById('loading-form');
  const form = document.getElementById('loading-form-form');
  form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const data = new FormData(form);
    loading.active = true;
    setTimeout(() => {
      loading.active = false;
      document.getElementById('loading-form-out').textContent = `department=${data.get('department')}`;
    }, 1500);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLoading contained active={saving} description="Saving the department">
  <form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); save(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }}>
    <UiTextInput label="Department" name="department" value="Procurement" />
    <UiButton type="submit">Save</UiButton>
  </form>
</UiLoading>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Loading contained active={saving} description="Saving the department">
  <form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); save(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }}>
    <TextInput label="Department" name="department" defaultValue="Procurement" />
    <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
  </form>
</Loading>
```

`save` stands for your own code that sets `saving` while it works.

## Wait before it shows

`delay` (ms) shows the spinner only if the work is still going after that long. `min-duration` (ms, `minDuration` in React) keeps it up at least that long once shown, so it doesn't blink on and off. Both default to 0, as in Carbon. Try the quick check: it ends before the delay, and no spinner shows.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-button id="loading-delay-quick" kind="tertiary">Quick check (0.2 s)</ui-button>
  <ui-button id="loading-delay-slow" kind="tertiary">Full check (2 s)</ui-button>
</div>
<ui-loading id="loading-delay" contained active="false" delay="300" min-duration="500" description="Checking vendor documents">
  <ui-tile>
    <h4 style="margin: 0 0 8px">Vendor documents</h4>
    <p style="margin: 0">Company certificate, VAT registration, bank book.</p>
  </ui-tile>
</ui-loading>
<p>Spinner showing: <output id="loading-delay-out">no</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const loading = document.getElementById('loading-delay');
  const out = document.getElementById('loading-delay-out');
  new MutationObserver(() => {
    out.textContent = loading.hasAttribute('data-shown') ? 'yes' : 'no';
  }).observe(loading, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['data-shown'] });
  const run = (ms) => {
    loading.active = true;
    setTimeout(() => { loading.active = false; }, ms);
  };
  document.getElementById('loading-delay-quick').addEventListener('click', () => run(200));
  document.getElementById('loading-delay-slow').addEventListener('click', () => run(2000));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLoading contained active={checking} delay={300} minDuration={500} description="Checking vendor documents">
  <UiTile>…</UiTile>
</UiLoading>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Loading contained active={checking} delay={300} minDuration={500} description="Checking vendor documents">
  <Tile>…</Tile>
</Loading>
```

`delay` and `min-duration` work with every kind of loading, not only `contained`.

## Over the whole page

`overlay` covers the page in the overlay colour while the spinner shows. It holds focus: Tab and clicks elsewhere come back to it. When it stops, focus goes back where it was. A modal dialog opened above it is left alone. Use it only while the whole view can't be used, and always set `active` from your own state.

The overlay is `position: fixed`. In this demo it sits in a box with a `transform`, so it covers only the box; in your app it covers the window.


HTML:

```html
<div style="transform: translateZ(0); position: relative; height: 240px; overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid var(--ui-hairline)">
  <div style="display: grid; gap: 16px; justify-items: start; padding: 16px">
    <p style="margin: 0">Quarterly purchasing report, 42 pages</p>
    <ui-button id="loading-overlay-open">Generate PDF (3 s)</ui-button>
  </div>
  <ui-loading id="loading-overlay" overlay active="false" description="Generating the PDF"></ui-loading>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const overlay = document.getElementById('loading-overlay');
  document.getElementById('loading-overlay-open').addEventListener('click', () => {
    overlay.active = true;
    setTimeout(() => { overlay.active = false; }, 3000);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiButton onClick={generate}>Generate PDF</UiButton>
<UiLoading overlay active={generating} description="Generating the PDF" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Button onClick={generate}>Generate PDF</Button>
<Loading overlay active={generating} description="Generating the PDF" />
```

`generate` stands for your own code that sets `generating` while it works.

## Keyboard

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab | With `overlay`: stays on the spinner while it shows |

Esc doesn't close the overlay: it goes away when the work ends.

## Accessibility

- The spinner is an image named by `description`, inside an assertive live region while it shows, so screen readers announce it.
- With `overlay`, the spinner is a modal dialog named by `description` and takes focus. Focus goes back to where it was when it stops.
- With `contained`, the content is inert and `aria-busy` while it shows, and the spinner is a group named by `description`. Focus that was inside waits on the spinner, then goes back.
- Write the `description` as what is loading ("Loading the contract list"), not just "Loading".
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, the spinner turns more slowly.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Loading](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-loading/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-loading>` · React `UiLoading`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `active` | `active` | `boolean` | `true` | On by default; `active="false"` stops it. |
| `small` | `small` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `overlay` | `overlay` | `boolean` | `false` | Cover the page and trap focus while active. |
| `description` | `description` | `string` | `''` | Accessible description; defaults to the translation ("Loading"). |
| `contained` | `contained` | `boolean` | `false` | Cover just this element's content (the slot) instead of the page; the content is inert while active (no Carbon counterpart). |
| `delay` | `delay` | `number` | `0` | Milliseconds `active` must last before the spinner shows (default 0, as Carbon). |
| `min-duration` | `minDuration` | `number` | `0` | Once shown, the least milliseconds it stays (default 0). |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | The area `contained` covers |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The spinner wrapper (`aria-live`) |
| `overlay` | The page overlay (`overlay`), or the area's (`contained`) |
| `area` | The covered content (`contained`) |
| `spinner` | The `<svg>` |




---

# Inline loading

Inline loading shows the progress of one action in place, such as saving or sending: a 16px spinner with a short text beside it. It moves from `active` to `finished` (a check mark) or `error`, and screen readers hear each change.


HTML:

```html
<ui-inline-loading>Saving the purchase request…</ui-inline-loading>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiInlineLoading>Saving the purchase request…</UiInlineLoading>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<InlineLoading>Saving the purchase request…</InlineLoading>
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/inline-loading
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash

```

```bash
# React + Tailwind
```

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/inline-loading';</script>

```

```tsx
import { UiInlineLoading } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';
```

```tsx
<InlineLoading>Saving…</InlineLoading>
```

## Inline loading or loading?

Use inline loading next to the control that started the work, when the result ends as done or failed. When a whole view or area can't be used until the data arrives, use [Loading](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/loading/). When the work has a known size, use a [Progress bar](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/progress-bar/). The headless [Loading](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-loading/) parts cover only a spinner with its timing, not these statuses.

## Statuses

`status` is one of:

- `active` (the default): the spinning icon.
- `finished`: a green check mark (it appears at once, as in Carbon).
- `error`: a red error icon.
- `inactive`: only the text. In HTML and React (`UiInlineLoading`) the spinner stops as in Carbon web components: it turns out and fades over 1.4s (at once with reduced motion). React + Tailwind follows Carbon React and shows no icon at once.

The text in the element is the status text (Carbon's `description`). Change it with the status.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 8px; max-width: 320px">
  <ui-inline-loading status="inactive">Not started</ui-inline-loading>
  <ui-inline-loading status="active">Submitting…</ui-inline-loading>
  <ui-inline-loading status="finished">Submitted</ui-inline-loading>
  <ui-inline-loading status="error">Could not submit</ui-inline-loading>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiInlineLoading status="inactive">Not started</UiInlineLoading>
<UiInlineLoading status="active">Submitting…</UiInlineLoading>
<UiInlineLoading status="finished">Submitted</UiInlineLoading>
<UiInlineLoading status="error">Could not submit</UiInlineLoading>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<InlineLoading status="inactive">Not started</InlineLoading>
<InlineLoading status="active">Submitting…</InlineLoading>
<InlineLoading status="finished">Submitted</InlineLoading>
<InlineLoading status="error">Could not submit</InlineLoading>
```

## In place of the submit button

Carbon's pattern: when the user submits, the submit button gives its place to an inline loading. When the work is done, the check mark shows, then `ui-success` puts the button back.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center; min-height: 48px">
  <ui-button kind="secondary">Cancel</ui-button>
  <span id="inline-loading-submit-wrap"><ui-button id="inline-loading-submit">Submit</ui-button></span>
  <div id="inline-loading-flow-wrap" hidden style="width: 200px">
    <ui-inline-loading id="inline-loading-flow"></ui-inline-loading>
  </div>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const submitWrap = document.getElementById('inline-loading-submit-wrap');
  const flowWrap = document.getElementById('inline-loading-flow-wrap');
  const flow = document.getElementById('inline-loading-flow');
  document.getElementById('inline-loading-submit').addEventListener('click', () => {
    submitWrap.hidden = true;
    flowWrap.hidden = false;
    flow.status = 'active';
    flow.textContent = 'Submitting…';
    setTimeout(() => {
      flow.status = 'finished';
      flow.textContent = 'Submitted';
    }, 2000);
  });
  flow.addEventListener('ui-success', () => {
    flowWrap.hidden = true;
    submitWrap.hidden = false;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const [status, setStatus] = useState<'inactive' | 'active' | 'finished'>('inactive');
const submit = async () => {
  setStatus('active');
  await send();
  setStatus('finished');
};

<UiButton kind="secondary">Cancel</UiButton>
{status === 'inactive' ? (
  <UiButton onClick={submit}>Submit</UiButton>
) : (
  <UiInlineLoading status={status} onUiSuccess={() => setStatus('inactive')}>
    {status === 'active' && 'Submitting…'}
    {status === 'finished' && 'Submitted'}
  </UiInlineLoading>
)}
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [status, setStatus] = useState<'inactive' | 'active' | 'finished'>('inactive');
const submit = async () => {
  setStatus('active');
  await send();
  setStatus('finished');
};

<Button kind="secondary">Cancel</Button>
{status === 'inactive' ? (
  <Button onClick={submit}>Submit</Button>
) : (
  <InlineLoading status={status} onSuccess={() => setStatus('inactive')}>
    {status === 'active' && 'Submitting…'}
    {status === 'finished' && 'Submitted'}
  </InlineLoading>
)}
```

`send` stands for your own code.

## After success

`ui-success` fires `success-delay` ms after `status` became `finished` (1500 by default, as Carbon's `successDelay`). Use it to close a dialog, clear the form or put a button back. In React the event prop is `onUiSuccess`; in React + Tailwind it is `onSuccess`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-button id="inline-loading-success-run" kind="tertiary">Send invoice INV-0412</ui-button>
<ui-inline-loading id="inline-loading-success" status="inactive" success-delay="1000">Not sent yet</ui-inline-loading>
<p>ui-success: <output id="inline-loading-success-out">not yet</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const status = document.getElementById('inline-loading-success');
  const out = document.getElementById('inline-loading-success-out');
  document.getElementById('inline-loading-success-run').addEventListener('click', () => {
    status.status = 'active';
    status.textContent = 'Sending…';
    out.textContent = 'waiting';
    setTimeout(() => {
      status.status = 'finished';
      status.textContent = 'Sent to the customer';
    }, 1500);
  });
  status.addEventListener('ui-success', () => {
    out.textContent = `fired at ${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}`;
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiInlineLoading status={status} successDelay={1000} onUiSuccess={() => setLog(`fired at ${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}`)}>
  {text}
</UiInlineLoading>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<InlineLoading status={status} successDelay={1000} onSuccess={() => setLog(`fired at ${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}`)}>
  {text}
</InlineLoading>
```

## Error and try again

On failure, set `status="error"` and say what failed in the text. Put a way to try again right next to it.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <div style="width: 280px">
    <ui-inline-loading id="inline-loading-retry-status" status="error">Could not send to the approver</ui-inline-loading>
  </div>
  <ui-button id="inline-loading-retry" kind="ghost" size="sm">Try again</ui-button>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const status = document.getElementById('inline-loading-retry-status');
  document.getElementById('inline-loading-retry').addEventListener('click', () => {
    status.status = 'active';
    status.textContent = 'Sending…';
    setTimeout(() => {
      status.status = 'finished';
      status.textContent = 'Sent to the approver';
    }, 1500);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiInlineLoading status={status}>{text}</UiInlineLoading>
{status === 'error' && <UiButton kind="ghost" size="sm" onClick={retry}>Try again</UiButton>}
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<InlineLoading status={status}>{text}</InlineLoading>
{status === 'error' && <Button kind="ghost" size="sm" onClick={retry}>Try again</Button>}
```

`retry` stands for your own code.

## Checking a field

Inline loading also fits under a field that the server checks, such as a tax ID. Show it when the check starts, and end with the result.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input id="inline-loading-tax" label="Tax ID" helper-text="13 digits" value="0105556000000"></ui-text-input>
<ui-button id="inline-loading-tax-check" kind="tertiary">Check</ui-button>
<div id="inline-loading-tax-wrap" hidden>
  <ui-inline-loading id="inline-loading-tax-status"></ui-inline-loading>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const input = document.getElementById('inline-loading-tax');
  const wrap = document.getElementById('inline-loading-tax-wrap');
  const status = document.getElementById('inline-loading-tax-status');
  document.getElementById('inline-loading-tax-check').addEventListener('click', () => {
    wrap.hidden = false;
    status.status = 'active';
    status.textContent = 'Checking the tax ID…';
    setTimeout(() => {
      const found = /^\d{13}$/.test(input.value);
      status.status = found ? 'finished' : 'error';
      status.textContent = found ? 'Found: Siam Logistics Co., Ltd.' : 'No company has this tax ID';
    }, 1500);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput label="Tax ID" helperText="13 digits" value={taxId} onInput={(e) => setTaxId((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value)} />
<UiButton kind="tertiary" onClick={check}>Check</UiButton>
{result.status && <UiInlineLoading status={result.status}>{result.text}</UiInlineLoading>}
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput label="Tax ID" helperText="13 digits" value={taxId} onChange={(e) => setTaxId(e.target.value)} />
<Button kind="tertiary" onClick={check}>Check</Button>
{result.status && <InlineLoading status={result.status}>{result.text}</InlineLoading>}
```

`check` stands for your own code that asks the server and sets `result` (the status and the text).

## Icon label

The icon is named by its status: "Loading", "Finished" or "Error", translated to the page language. `icon-label` (`iconLabel` in React) names it yourself when the status text needs a different word.


HTML:

```html
<ui-inline-loading status="finished" icon-label="Saved">Draft saved at 10:42</ui-inline-loading>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiInlineLoading status="finished" iconLabel="Saved">Draft saved at 10:42</UiInlineLoading>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<InlineLoading status="finished" iconLabel="Saved">Draft saved at 10:42</InlineLoading>
```

## Accessibility

- The whole element is a polite live region, so screen readers hear the icon's name and the text each time the status changes.
- Keep the text short and specific: "Submitting…", "Submitted", "Could not submit".
- Inline loading doesn't take focus. When it replaces the button that had focus, move focus somewhere useful afterwards, such as back to the button.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, the spinner stops turning and the check mark shows at once.

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-inline-loading>` · React `UiInlineLoading`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `status` | `InlineLoadingStatus` | `'active'` |  |
| `success-delay` | `successDelay` | `number` | `1500` | Milliseconds after `finished` before `ui-success` fires (Carbon `successDelay`). |
| `icon-label` | `iconLabel` | `string` | `''` | Accessible name of the icon; defaults to the status. |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-success` | `onUiSuccess` | `success-delay` ms after `status` became `finished` |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | The status text (Carbon `description`) |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The row |
| `icon` | The spinner / check / error icon |
| `text` | The description |

# Progress bar

A progress bar shows how far a task has come, such as an upload or an import. The track fills to `value / max`; with no `value` a stripe sweeps across it while the length is unknown. A label names it, and helper text below says the details.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 480px">
  <ui-progress-bar label="Uploading signed copies" helper-text="3 of 5 files" value="60"></ui-progress-bar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProgressBar label="Uploading signed copies" helperText="3 of 5 files" value={60} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProgressBar label="Uploading signed copies" helperText="3 of 5 files" value={60} />
```


shadcn · React + Tailwind:



## Progress bar, progress indicator or loading?

- Progress bar: the system is doing one task and you can say how far it is.
- [Progress indicator](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/progress-indicator/): the user goes through the steps of a form.
- [Loading](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/loading/) or [Inline loading](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/inline-loading/): something is busy and you can't say how far.

## Value and max

`value` is the progress and `max` the whole (100 by default). Use the units of the task when they mean something, such as files. A value below 0 or above `max` is held at the end.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 480px">
  <ui-progress-bar label="Uploading signed copies" helper-text="3 of 5 files" value="3" max="5"></ui-progress-bar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProgressBar label="Uploading signed copies" helperText="3 of 5 files" value={3} max={5} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProgressBar label="Uploading signed copies" helperText="3 of 5 files" value={3} max={5} />
```

## Indeterminate

Leave out `value` while you don't know the length yet. A stripe sweeps across the track until you set a value or a status.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 480px">
  <ui-progress-bar label="Preparing the export" helper-text="Collecting contracts…"></ui-progress-bar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProgressBar label="Preparing the export" helperText="Collecting contracts…" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProgressBar label="Preparing the export" helperText="Collecting contracts…" />
```

## Live progress

Set `value` as the work goes, and `status="finished"` at the end. The track moves smoothly between values.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 480px">
  <ui-progress-bar id="progress-bar-live" label="Uploading signed copies" helper-text="Not started" value="0" max="5"></ui-progress-bar>
</div>
<ui-button id="progress-bar-live-start" kind="tertiary">Upload 5 files</ui-button>

<script type="module">
  const bar = document.getElementById('progress-bar-live');
  let timer;
  document.getElementById('progress-bar-live-start').addEventListener('click', () => {
    clearInterval(timer);
    let files = 0;
    bar.status = 'active';
    bar.value = files;
    bar.helperText = '0 of 5 files';
    timer = setInterval(() => {
      files += 1;
      bar.value = files;
      bar.helperText = `${files} of 5 files`;
      if (files === 5) {
        clearInterval(timer);
        bar.status = 'finished';
        bar.helperText = 'All 5 files uploaded';
      }
    }, 700);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProgressBar
  label="Uploading signed copies"
  value={files}
  max={5}
  status={files === 5 ? 'finished' : 'active'}
  helperText={files === 5 ? 'All 5 files uploaded' : `${files} of 5 files`}
/>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProgressBar
  label="Uploading signed copies"
  value={files}
  max={5}
  status={files === 5 ? 'finished' : 'active'}
  helperText={files === 5 ? 'All 5 files uploaded' : `${files} of 5 files`}
/>
```

## Finished

`status="finished"` fills the track in green and puts a check mark beside the label, whatever the `value`.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 480px">
  <ui-progress-bar label="Uploading signed copies" helper-text="All files uploaded" status="finished"></ui-progress-bar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProgressBar label="Uploading signed copies" helperText="All files uploaded" status="finished" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProgressBar label="Uploading signed copies" helperText="All files uploaded" status="finished" />
```

## Error

`status="error"` turns the track, the icon beside the label and the helper text red. Screen readers hear "Error" after the label. Say in the helper text what went wrong and what to do.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 480px">
  <ui-progress-bar label="Uploading signed copies" helper-text="Upload failed. Check your connection and try again." status="error"></ui-progress-bar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProgressBar label="Uploading signed copies" helperText="Upload failed. Check your connection and try again." status="error" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProgressBar label="Uploading signed copies" helperText="Upload failed. Check your connection and try again." status="error" />
```

## Sizes

`size`: `md` is an 8px track (Carbon's `big`, the default); `sm` is 4px (Carbon's `small`).


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 24px; max-width: 480px">
  <ui-progress-bar label="Medium (8px)" value="40"></ui-progress-bar>
  <ui-progress-bar label="Small (4px)" value="40" size="sm"></ui-progress-bar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProgressBar label="Medium (8px)" value={40} />
<UiProgressBar label="Small (4px)" value={40} size="sm" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProgressBar label="Medium (8px)" value={40} />
<ProgressBar label="Small (4px)" value={40} size="sm" />
```

## Inline

`type="inline"` puts the label and the track on one row, for tight places such as a table cell. The helper text is then read by screen readers only. When it is finished or fails, only the label and the icon show.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 24px; max-width: 480px">
  <ui-progress-bar label="Vendors" helper-text="120 of 300 rows" value="40" type="inline"></ui-progress-bar>
  <ui-progress-bar label="Contracts" helper-text="All rows imported" status="finished" type="inline"></ui-progress-bar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProgressBar label="Vendors" helperText="120 of 300 rows" value={40} type="inline" />
<UiProgressBar label="Contracts" helperText="All rows imported" status="finished" type="inline" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProgressBar label="Vendors" helperText="120 of 300 rows" value={40} type="inline" />
<ProgressBar label="Contracts" helperText="All rows imported" status="finished" type="inline" />
```

## Indented

`type="indented"` moves the label and the helper text 16px in, to line up with indented content such as the text of a tile or a list row. The track stays full width.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 480px">
  <ui-progress-bar label="Importing vendors" helper-text="120 of 300 rows" value="120" max="300" type="indented"></ui-progress-bar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiProgressBar label="Importing vendors" helperText="120 of 300 rows" value={120} max={300} type="indented" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ProgressBar label="Importing vendors" helperText="120 of 300 rows" value={120} max={300} type="indented" />
```

## Hidden label

`hide-label` (`hideLabel` in React) hides the label from view when the text around already says what is progressing. It still names the bar for screen readers, so always write it.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 8px; max-width: 480px">
  <strong>Backup of the finance database</strong>
  <ui-progress-bar label="Backup of the finance database" hide-label value="70"></ui-progress-bar>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<strong>Backup of the finance database</strong>
<UiProgressBar label="Backup of the finance database" hideLabel value={70} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<strong>Backup of the finance database</strong>
<ProgressBar label="Backup of the finance database" hideLabel value={70} />
```

## Accessibility

- The track is a `progressbar` named by the label and described by the helper text. It has `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuenow` when it has a value, and none while indeterminate.
- It is `aria-busy` until it is finished.
- On error, screen readers hear "Error" after the label, translated to the page language.
- Always write a `label`, even with `hide-label`.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, the indeterminate stripe moves more slowly.

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-progress-bar>` · React `UiProgressBar`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | Required. What is progressing; shown above (or beside) the track and read as the bar's name. |
| `hide-label` | `hideLabel` | `boolean` | `false` | Visually hides the label (it still names the bar). |
| `helper-text` | `helperText` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `value` | `value` | `number \| undefined` |  | Current progress; leave unset for an indeterminate bar. |
| `max` | `max` | `number` | `100` |  |
| `size` | `size` | `ProgressBarSize` | `'md'` |  |
| `status` | `status` | `ProgressBarStatus` | `'active'` |  |
| `type` | `type` | `ProgressBarType` | `'default'` |  |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The wrapper |
| `label` | Label row (text + status icon) |
| `track` | The `progressbar` element |
| `bar` | The filled portion |
| `helper-text` | Helper text below the track |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-progress-track` |  | The track's fill (default `--ui-surface-1`; Kanok: a hairline grey); `--ui-progress-radius` its corners (default square; Kanok: round) |




---

# Skeleton

A skeleton is a grey placeholder in the shape of the content to come, shown while a page loads its data for the first time. `<ui-skeleton>` draws text lines, a heading, a field, a button or a block. Most components also have their own skeleton element; see the [index](#every-component-skeleton) at the end.


HTML:

```html
<div aria-busy="true" style="display: grid; gap: 16px; max-width: 480px">
  <ui-skeleton shape="heading"></ui-skeleton>
  <ui-skeleton lines="3"></ui-skeleton>
  <ui-skeleton shape="field"></ui-skeleton>
  <ui-skeleton shape="button"></ui-skeleton>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<div aria-busy="true">
  <UiSkeleton shape="heading" />
  <UiSkeleton lines={3} />
  <UiSkeleton shape="field" />
  <UiSkeleton shape="button" />
</div>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<div aria-busy="true">
  <Skeleton shape="heading" />
  <Skeleton lines={3} />
  <Skeleton shape="field" />
  <Skeleton shape="button" />
</div>
```

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/skeleton';</script>

<ui-skeleton lines="2"></ui-skeleton>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiSkeleton lines={2} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/skeleton';

<Skeleton lines={2} />
```

## Skeleton or loading?

Use a skeleton for the first load of a page, when you know the layout of what is coming: the page appears at once and the content fills in. Use [Loading](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/loading/) or [Inline loading](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/inline-loading/) when the user waits for an action, such as saving, and a skeleton would hide what they were working on.

## Text lines

`shape="text"` (the default) draws `lines` bars, 3 by default. The last of several lines is shorter, so it reads as a paragraph.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 24px; max-width: 480px">
  <ui-skeleton lines="1"></ui-skeleton>
  <ui-skeleton lines="4"></ui-skeleton>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSkeleton lines={1} />
<UiSkeleton lines={4} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Skeleton lines={1} />
<Skeleton lines={4} />
```

## Heading

`shape="heading"` is one 24px bar, half the width by default.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 16px; max-width: 480px">
  <ui-skeleton shape="heading"></ui-skeleton>
  <ui-skeleton lines="2"></ui-skeleton>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSkeleton shape="heading" />
<UiSkeleton lines={2} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Skeleton shape="heading" />
<Skeleton lines={2} />
```

## Field and button

`shape="field"` is a short label bar above a 48px field bar. `shape="button"` is a 48px bar, 120px wide, that sits inline. For a real field or button, prefer its own skeleton element (see the index below), which matches its size.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 16px; max-width: 480px">
  <ui-skeleton shape="field"></ui-skeleton>
  <ui-skeleton shape="field"></ui-skeleton>
  <div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
    <ui-skeleton shape="button"></ui-skeleton>
    <ui-skeleton shape="button"></ui-skeleton>
  </div>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSkeleton shape="field" />
<UiSkeleton shape="field" />
<UiSkeleton shape="button" />
<UiSkeleton shape="button" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Skeleton shape="field" />
<Skeleton shape="field" />
<Skeleton shape="button" />
<Skeleton shape="button" />
```

## Placeholder block

`shape="block"` is one bar, 160px high by default, for an image, a chart or a whole card (Carbon's `SkeletonPlaceholder`). Set the height with the `--ui-skeleton-height` CSS property (`height` in React + Tailwind).


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(160px, 1fr)); gap: 16px; max-width: 520px">
  <ui-skeleton shape="block"></ui-skeleton>
  <ui-skeleton shape="block" style="--ui-skeleton-height: 96px"></ui-skeleton>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSkeleton shape="block" />
<UiSkeleton shape="block" style={{ '--ui-skeleton-height': '96px' } as CSSProperties} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Skeleton shape="block" />
<Skeleton shape="block" height="96px" />
```

## Width

Every shape is full width by default (a heading half, a button 120px). Set the width with the `--ui-skeleton-width` CSS property (`width` in React + Tailwind), so the placeholder looks like the content to come. Give it with its unit (`"200px"`, `"70%"`); `width` and `height` take strings, as Carbon's `SkeletonText` `width`.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 16px; max-width: 480px">
  <ui-skeleton shape="heading" style="--ui-skeleton-width: 200px"></ui-skeleton>
  <ui-skeleton lines="1" style="--ui-skeleton-width: 70%"></ui-skeleton>
  <ui-skeleton shape="button" style="--ui-skeleton-width: 160px"></ui-skeleton>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSkeleton shape="heading" style={{ '--ui-skeleton-width': '200px' } as CSSProperties} />
<UiSkeleton lines={1} style={{ '--ui-skeleton-width': '70%' } as CSSProperties} />
<UiSkeleton shape="button" style={{ '--ui-skeleton-width': '160px' } as CSSProperties} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Skeleton shape="heading" width="200px" />
<Skeleton lines={1} width="70%" />
<Skeleton shape="button" width="160px" />
```

In React + Tailwind, give `width` and `height` with their unit, as strings: they set CSS properties, and a bare number has no unit there.

## Swap it for the content

Skeletons are hidden from screen readers. Tell them about the load on the container instead: `aria-busy="true"` while it loads, and a short status message. When the data arrives, put the content in place and drop both.


HTML:

```html
<div id="skeleton-card" aria-busy="true" style="display: grid; gap: 16px; max-width: 480px; padding: 16px; border: 1px solid var(--ui-hairline)">
  <ui-skeleton shape="heading"></ui-skeleton>
  <ui-skeleton lines="2"></ui-skeleton>
  <ui-skeleton shape="button"></ui-skeleton>
</div>
<p id="skeleton-card-status" role="status">Loading the vendor…</p>
<ui-button id="skeleton-card-reload" kind="tertiary">Load again</ui-button>

<script type="module">
  const card = document.getElementById('skeleton-card');
  const status = document.getElementById('skeleton-card-status');
  const skeleton = card.innerHTML;
  const content = `
    <h4 style="margin: 0">Siam Logistics Co., Ltd.</h4>
    <p style="margin: 0">Tax ID 0105556000000 · 3 active contracts · Paid on time for 24 months.</p>
    <div><ui-button kind="secondary">View contracts</ui-button></div>`;
  let timer;
  const load = () => {
    clearTimeout(timer);
    card.innerHTML = skeleton;
    card.setAttribute('aria-busy', 'true');
    status.textContent = 'Loading the vendor…';
    timer = setTimeout(() => {
      card.innerHTML = content;
      card.removeAttribute('aria-busy');
      status.textContent = 'Vendor loaded';
    }, 2000);
  };
  document.getElementById('skeleton-card-reload').addEventListener('click', load);
  load();
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<div aria-busy={loading || undefined}>
  {loading ? (
    <>
      <UiSkeleton shape="heading" />
      <UiSkeleton lines={2} />
      <UiSkeleton shape="button" />
    </>
  ) : (
    <VendorCard vendor={vendor} />
  )}
</div>
<p role="status">{loading ? 'Loading the vendor…' : 'Vendor loaded'}</p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<div aria-busy={loading || undefined}>
  {loading ? (
    <>
      <Skeleton shape="heading" />
      <Skeleton lines={2} />
      <Skeleton shape="button" />
    </>
  ) : (
    <VendorCard vendor={vendor} />
  )}
</div>
<p role="status">{loading ? 'Loading the vendor…' : 'Vendor loaded'}</p>
```

`VendorCard` stands for your own component.

## Component skeletons

Most components have a skeleton element in their own shape and size, as Carbon's `TextInputSkeleton`, `DropdownSkeleton` and so on. Each has its own import, `@purpurabog/ui/<component>-skeleton`. Each has a React wrapper named after it in `@purpurabog/ui/react` (`UiTextInputSkeleton`, `UiDropdownSkeleton` …). React + Tailwind has a `…Skeleton` component next to each component.


HTML:

```html
<div aria-busy="true" style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(240px, 1fr)); gap: 32px 24px">
  <ui-text-input-skeleton></ui-text-input-skeleton>
  <ui-dropdown-skeleton></ui-dropdown-skeleton>
  <ui-date-picker-skeleton range></ui-date-picker-skeleton>
  <ui-search-skeleton></ui-search-skeleton>
  <ui-slider-skeleton></ui-slider-skeleton>
  <div style="display: flex; gap: 16px; align-items: center"><ui-button-skeleton></ui-button-skeleton><ui-tag-skeleton></ui-tag-skeleton></div>
  <div style="display: grid; gap: 12px"><ui-checkbox-skeleton></ui-checkbox-skeleton><ui-radio-skeleton></ui-radio-skeleton><ui-toggle-skeleton></ui-toggle-skeleton></div>
  <ui-breadcrumb-skeleton></ui-breadcrumb-skeleton>
  <ui-tabs-skeleton tabs="3"></ui-tabs-skeleton>
  <ui-progress-indicator-skeleton steps="3"></ui-progress-indicator-skeleton>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiTextInputSkeleton, UiDropdownSkeleton, UiButtonSkeleton, UiTagSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<div aria-busy="true">
  <UiTextInputSkeleton />
  <UiDropdownSkeleton />
  <UiButtonSkeleton />
  <UiTagSkeleton />
</div>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { TextInputSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/text-input';
import { DropdownSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/dropdown';
import { ButtonSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/button';
import { TagSkeleton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/tag';

<div aria-busy="true">
  <TextInputSkeleton />
  <DropdownSkeleton />
  <ButtonSkeleton />
  <TagSkeleton />
</div>
```

## Fluid field skeletons

The field skeletons take `fluid` for the skeleton of a fluid field: a 64px box with two bars. Inside `<ui-fluid-form>` (`FluidForm` in React + Tailwind) they are fluid without the attribute. The time picker skeleton is always fluid, as Carbon has only that one.


HTML:

```html
<div aria-busy="true" style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(240px, 1fr)); gap: 32px 24px">
  <ui-text-input-skeleton fluid></ui-text-input-skeleton>
  <ui-select-skeleton fluid></ui-select-skeleton>
  <ui-date-picker-skeleton fluid></ui-date-picker-skeleton>
  <ui-time-picker-skeleton></ui-time-picker-skeleton>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiTextInputSkeleton, UiSelectSkeleton, UiDatePickerSkeleton, UiTimePickerSkeleton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiTextInputSkeleton fluid />
<UiSelectSkeleton fluid />
<UiDatePickerSkeleton fluid />
<UiTimePickerSkeleton />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInputSkeleton fluid />
<SelectSkeleton fluid />
<DatePickerSkeleton fluid />
<TimePickerSkeleton />
```

## Every component skeleton

Each component page shows its skeleton with its options. The field skeletons (text input, number input, dropdown, select, date picker) also take `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`), `hide-label` and `fluid`.

| Element | React + Tailwind | Attributes | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ui-accordion-skeleton` | `AccordionSkeleton` | `count`, `open`, `alignment` | [Accordion](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/accordion/#skeleton) |
| `ui-big-number-skeleton` | `BigNumberSkeleton` | `size` | [Big number](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/big-number/) |
