| `ui-date-picker-skeleton` | `DatePickerSkeleton` | `range` | [Date picker](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/date-picker/#skeleton) |
| `ui-dropdown-skeleton` | `DropdownSkeleton` | | [Dropdown](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/dropdown/#skeleton), also for combobox and multi-select |
| `ui-file-uploader-skeleton` | `FileUploaderSkeleton` | | [File uploader](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/file-uploader/#skeleton) |
| `ui-number-input-skeleton` | `NumberInputSkeleton` | | [Number input](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/number-input/#skeleton) |
| `ui-progress-indicator-skeleton` | `ProgressIndicatorSkeleton` | `steps`, `vertical` | [Progress indicator](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/progress-indicator/#skeleton) |
| `ui-radio-skeleton` | `RadioSkeleton` | | [Radio](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/radio/#skeleton) |
| `ui-search-skeleton` | `SearchSkeleton` | `size`, `fluid` | [Search](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/search/#skeleton) |
| `ui-select-skeleton` | `SelectSkeleton` | | [Select](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/select/#skeleton) |
| `ui-slider-skeleton` | `SliderSkeleton` | `hide-label`, `two-handles` | [Slider](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/slider/#skeleton) |
| `ui-structured-list-skeleton` | `StructuredListSkeleton` | `rows` | [Structured list](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/structured-list/#skeleton) |
| `ui-table-skeleton` | `DataTableSkeleton` | `row-count`, `column-count`, `zebra`, `show-header`, `show-toolbar` | [Data table](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/data-table/#empty-loading-and-skeleton) |
| `ui-tabs-skeleton` | `TabsSkeleton` | `tabs` | [Tabs](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tabs/#skeleton) |
| `ui-tag-skeleton` | `TagSkeleton` | `size` | [Tag](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tag/) |
| `ui-text-area-skeleton` | `TextAreaSkeleton` | `hide-label`, `fluid` | [Text area](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/text-area/#skeleton) |
| `ui-text-input-skeleton` | `TextInputSkeleton` | | [Text input](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/text-input/#skeleton) |
| `ui-time-picker-skeleton` | `TimePickerSkeleton` | `is-only-two` | [Time picker](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/time-picker/#skeleton) |
| `ui-toggle-skeleton` | `ToggleSkeleton` | | [Toggle](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/toggle/#skeleton) |

`ui-table-skeleton` comes with `@purpurabog/ui/table`. Every element here has a React wrapper named after it: `ui-accordion-skeleton` is `UiAccordionSkeleton`, `ui-table-skeleton` is `UiTableSkeleton`, and so on; its props are the attributes in camelCase (`hideLabel`, `noTrailingSlash`). In React + Tailwind, import each `…Skeleton` from its component's file, for example `TextInputSkeleton` from `@/components/ui/react-tw/text-input`; `RadioSkeleton` comes from `radio-group`.

## Accessibility

- Every skeleton is hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`) and never takes focus.
- Say "loading" on the container: `aria-busy="true"` and a short status message, such as a `role="status"` "Loading contracts…". Drop both when the content arrives.
- The bars have Carbon's 3-second shimmer; under `prefers-reduced-motion` it stops.

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

# Badge indicator

A badge indicator is the small red mark in the corner of a ghost icon button, for things that wait for the user, such as approvals or new messages. With a count it shows the number; without one it is a dot. It belongs on an [icon button](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/button/#notification-badge): `<ui-icon-button badge-count>` makes one for you.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-icon-button label="Approvals" badge-count="4">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M28.7 19.3 26 16.6V13a10 10 0 0 0-9-10v-2h-2v2a10 10 0 0 0-9 10v3.6l-2.7 2.7A1 1 0 0 0 3 20v3a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h7v.8a5 5 0 0 0 10 0V24h7a1 1 0 0 0 1-1v-3a1 1 0 0 0-.3-.7ZM19 24.8a3 3 0 0 1-6 0V24h6ZM27 22H5v-1.6l2.7-2.7A1 1 0 0 0 8 17v-4a8 8 0 0 1 16 0v4a1 1 0 0 0 .3.7l2.7 2.7Z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
  <ui-icon-button label="Notifications, new" badge-count="0">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M28.7 19.3 26 16.6V13a10 10 0 0 0-9-10v-2h-2v2a10 10 0 0 0-9 10v3.6l-2.7 2.7A1 1 0 0 0 3 20v3a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h7v.8a5 5 0 0 0 10 0V24h7a1 1 0 0 0 1-1v-3a1 1 0 0 0-.3-.7ZM19 24.8a3 3 0 0 1-6 0V24h6ZM27 22H5v-1.6l2.7-2.7A1 1 0 0 0 8 17v-4a8 8 0 0 1 16 0v4a1 1 0 0 0 .3.7l2.7 2.7Z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
import { Notification as NotificationIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<UiIconButton label="Approvals" badgeCount={4}><NotificationIcon /></UiIconButton>
<UiIconButton label="Notifications, new" badgeCount={0}><NotificationIcon /></UiIconButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Notification as NotificationIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<IconButton label="Approvals" badgeCount={4}><NotificationIcon /></IconButton>
<IconButton label="Notifications, new" badgeCount={0}><NotificationIcon /></IconButton>
```

The icons are Carbon's, from `@carbon/icons-react` (see [Icons](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/icons/)).

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/badge-indicator
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-icon-button
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/badge-indicator.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/badge-indicator/badge-indicator.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-badge-indicator, shared-element, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
# (none)
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-icon-button.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/icon-button.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-badge-indicator, core-position, tw-badge-indicator, tw-button, tw-theme, tw-tooltip, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it

`@purpurabog/ui/icon-button` brings the badge indicator with it. Import `@purpurabog/ui/badge-indicator` on its own only when you place `<ui-badge-indicator>` yourself.


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/icon-button';</script>

<ui-icon-button label="Approvals" badge-count="4">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><!-- icon --></svg>
</ui-icon-button>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiIconButton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';
import { Notification as NotificationIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<UiIconButton label="Approvals" badgeCount={4}><NotificationIcon /></UiIconButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Notification as NotificationIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

import { IconButton } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/icon-button';

<IconButton label="Approvals" badgeCount={4}><NotificationIcon /></IconButton>
```

## Count or dot

`badge-count` (`badgeCount` in React) with a number above 0 shows the count in a 16px pill. 0 shows an 8px dot: something is new, but the number doesn't matter. Leave the attribute out for no badge.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-icon-button label="Purchase requests to approve" badge-count="12">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M25.7 9.3l-7-7A.9.9 0 0 0 18 2H8a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v24a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h16a2 2 0 0 0 2-2V10a.9.9 0 0 0-.3-.7ZM18 4.4 23.6 10H18ZM24 28H8V4h8v6a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h6Z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
  <ui-icon-button label="Comments, new" badge-count="0">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M17.7 30 16 29l4-7h6a2 2 0 0 0 2-2V8a2 2 0 0 0-2-2H6a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v12a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h9v2H6a4 4 0 0 1-4-4V8a4 4 0 0 1 4-4h20a4 4 0 0 1 4 4v12a4 4 0 0 1-4 4h-4.8Z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
  <ui-icon-button label="Archive">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M14 19h4a2 2 0 0 0 2-2v-1h-2v1h-4v-1h-2v1a2 2 0 0 0 2 2ZM28 4H4a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v4a2 2 0 0 0 2 2v14a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h20a2 2 0 0 0 2-2V12a2 2 0 0 0 2-2V6a2 2 0 0 0-2-2ZM26 26H6V12h20Zm2-16H4V6h24Z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
import { Archive as ArchiveIcon, Chat as ChatIcon, Document as DocumentIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<UiIconButton label="Purchase requests to approve" badgeCount={12}><DocumentIcon /></UiIconButton>
<UiIconButton label="Comments, new" badgeCount={0}><ChatIcon /></UiIconButton>
<UiIconButton label="Archive"><ArchiveIcon /></UiIconButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Archive as ArchiveIcon, Chat as ChatIcon, Document as DocumentIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<IconButton label="Purchase requests to approve" badgeCount={12}><DocumentIcon /></IconButton>
<IconButton label="Comments, new" badgeCount={0}><ChatIcon /></IconButton>
<IconButton label="Archive"><ArchiveIcon /></IconButton>
```

## Large counts

Past 999 the badge shows "999+", as in Carbon.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-icon-button label="Unread messages" badge-count="85">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M28 6H4a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v16a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h24a2 2 0 0 0 2-2V8a2 2 0 0 0-2-2Zm-2.2 2L16 14.8 6.2 8ZM4 24V8.9l11.4 7.9a1 1 0 0 0 1.1 0L28 8.9V24Z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
  <ui-icon-button label="Unread messages" badge-count="1200">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M28 6H4a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v16a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h24a2 2 0 0 0 2-2V8a2 2 0 0 0-2-2Zm-2.2 2L16 14.8 6.2 8ZM4 24V8.9l11.4 7.9a1 1 0 0 0 1.1 0L28 8.9V24Z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
import { Email as EmailIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<UiIconButton label="Unread messages" badgeCount={85}><EmailIcon /></UiIconButton>
```

## Small buttons

Carbon designs the badge for the large (48px) ghost button. On a small button the dot sits 4px from the corner instead of 8px, so it stays on the button.

## Your own badge element

Instead of `badge-count`, put a `<ui-badge-indicator count="…">` inside the icon button. It takes the button's `badge-indicator` slot by itself, and the button still reads its count to screen readers. In React, `UiBadgeIndicator` works the same way. React + Tailwind has only `badgeCount` on `IconButton` for this; its `BadgeIndicator` is the part that `IconButton` draws.


HTML:

```html
<ui-icon-button label="Contracts to renew">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M25.7 9.3l-7-7A.9.9 0 0 0 18 2H8a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v24a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h16a2 2 0 0 0 2-2V10a.9.9 0 0 0-.3-.7ZM18 4.4 23.6 10H18ZM24 28H8V4h8v6a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h6Z"/></svg>
  <ui-badge-indicator count="7"></ui-badge-indicator>
</ui-icon-button>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiBadgeIndicator, UiIconButton } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';
import { Document as DocumentIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<UiIconButton label="Contracts to renew">
  <DocumentIcon />
  <UiBadgeIndicator count={7} />
</UiIconButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Document as DocumentIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

// no separate badge element in React + Tailwind: IconButton draws it from badgeCount
<IconButton label="Contracts to renew" badgeCount={7}><DocumentIcon /></IconButton>
```

## Update the count

Set `badgeCount` as the number changes. To take the badge away, set the property to `undefined` (`badgeCount={undefined}` in React). Approve the requests one by one below: the last one removes the badge.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-icon-button id="badge-indicator-approvals" label="Purchase requests to approve" badge-count="3">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M25.7 9.3l-7-7A.9.9 0 0 0 18 2H8a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v24a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h16a2 2 0 0 0 2-2V10a.9.9 0 0 0-.3-.7ZM18 4.4 23.6 10H18ZM24 28H8V4h8v6a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h6Z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
  <ui-button id="badge-indicator-approve" kind="tertiary" size="md">Approve one</ui-button>
  <ui-button id="badge-indicator-reset" kind="ghost" size="md">Reset</ui-button>
</div>
<p>Waiting: <output id="badge-indicator-out">3</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const button = document.getElementById('badge-indicator-approvals');
  const out = document.getElementById('badge-indicator-out');
  let waiting = 3;
  const show = () => {
    button.badgeCount = waiting > 0 ? waiting : undefined;
    out.textContent = String(waiting);
  };
  document.getElementById('badge-indicator-approve').addEventListener('click', () => {
    waiting = Math.max(0, waiting - 1);
    show();
  });
  document.getElementById('badge-indicator-reset').addEventListener('click', () => {
    waiting = 3;
    show();
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
import { Document as DocumentIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<UiIconButton label="Purchase requests to approve" badgeCount={waiting > 0 ? waiting : undefined}>
  <DocumentIcon />
</UiIconButton>
<UiButton kind="tertiary" size="md" onClick={() => setWaiting(Math.max(0, waiting - 1))}>Approve one</UiButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Document as DocumentIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<IconButton label="Purchase requests to approve" badgeCount={waiting > 0 ? waiting : undefined}>
  <DocumentIcon />
</IconButton>
<Button kind="tertiary" size="md" onClick={() => setWaiting(Math.max(0, waiting - 1))}>Approve one</Button>
```

## Disabled

A disabled icon button hides its badge, and screen readers no longer hear the count.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; align-items: center">
  <ui-icon-button label="Approvals" badge-count="4" disabled>
    <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32"><path d="M28.7 19.3 26 16.6V13a10 10 0 0 0-9-10v-2h-2v2a10 10 0 0 0-9 10v3.6l-2.7 2.7A1 1 0 0 0 3 20v3a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h7v.8a5 5 0 0 0 10 0V24h7a1 1 0 0 0 1-1v-3a1 1 0 0 0-.3-.7ZM19 24.8a3 3 0 0 1-6 0V24h6ZM27 22H5v-1.6l2.7-2.7A1 1 0 0 0 8 17v-4a8 8 0 0 1 16 0v4a1 1 0 0 0 .3.7l2.7 2.7Z"/></svg>
  </ui-icon-button>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
import { Notification as NotificationIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<UiIconButton label="Approvals" badgeCount={4} disabled><NotificationIcon /></UiIconButton>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Notification as NotificationIcon } from '@carbon/icons-react';

<IconButton label="Approvals" badgeCount={4} disabled><NotificationIcon /></IconButton>
```

## Accessibility

- The badge itself is hidden from screen readers. The icon button reads the count as its description (Carbon's `aria-describedby`), so screen readers hear the count after the button's name.
- A dot has no count to read. Say it in the label instead, such as "Notifications, new".
- The label stays the button's name: write what the button opens ("Approvals"), not the count.
- In forced-colors mode the badge gets a border, so it stays visible.

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-badge-indicator>` · React `UiBadgeIndicator`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | `count` | `number \| undefined` |  | The number shown; unset or 0 = a dot. |




---

# Status indicator

A status indicator shows the state of something with a small coloured icon and a label, such as a job that succeeded or an incident's severity. `<ui-icon-indicator>` uses Carbon's status icons; `<ui-shape-indicator>` uses simple shapes for severity and state. Both follow Carbon's status indicators, which Carbon still marks as preview.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 8px; justify-items: start">
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="succeeded" label="Payment received"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="in-progress" label="Waiting for the second approver"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="failed" label="Bank transfer rejected"></ui-icon-indicator>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiIconIndicator kind="succeeded" label="Payment received" />
<UiIconIndicator kind="in-progress" label="Waiting for the second approver" />
<UiIconIndicator kind="failed" label="Bank transfer rejected" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<IconIndicator kind="succeeded" label="Payment received" />
<IconIndicator kind="in-progress" label="Waiting for the second approver" />
<IconIndicator kind="failed" label="Bank transfer rejected" />
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/status-indicator
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-status-indicator
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/status-indicator.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/status-indicator/icon-indicator.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/status-indicator/shape-indicator.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/status-indicator/status-indicator-shared.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/status-indicator/status-indicator.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-position, core-status-indicator, definition-tooltip, shared-align, shared-element, shared-field, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
# (none)
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-status-indicator.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/status-indicator.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-position, core-status-indicator, tw-definition-tooltip, tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/status-indicator';</script>

<ui-icon-indicator kind="succeeded" label="Approved"></ui-icon-indicator>
<ui-shape-indicator kind="high" label="High"></ui-shape-indicator>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiIconIndicator, UiShapeIndicator } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiIconIndicator kind="succeeded" label="Approved" />
<UiShapeIndicator kind="high" label="High" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { IconIndicator, ShapeIndicator } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/status-indicator';

<IconIndicator kind="succeeded" label="Approved" />
<ShapeIndicator kind="high" label="High" />
```

## Icon or shape?

- Icon indicator: the state of a process or an item, such as a payment, an import or a server.
- Shape indicator: a level, such as the severity of an incident or a risk, and a few states (stable, draft, incomplete).
- For a label the user can click or remove, use a [Tag](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tag/) instead.

Each kind has its own icon and colour, so the state doesn't depend on colour alone. Always write a label.

## Icon indicator kinds

`kind` picks the icon and its colour. There are 12 kinds; a `kind` that isn't one of them renders nothing.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 8px; justify-items: start">
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="failed" label="Failed"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="caution-major" label="Caution major"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="caution-minor" label="Caution minor"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="undefined" label="Undefined"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="succeeded" label="Succeeded"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="normal" label="Normal"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="in-progress" label="In progress"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="incomplete" label="Incomplete"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="not-started" label="Not started"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="pending" label="Pending"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="unknown" label="Unknown"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="informative" label="Informative"></ui-icon-indicator>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiIconIndicator kind="failed" label="Failed" />
<UiIconIndicator kind="caution-major" label="Caution major" />
<UiIconIndicator kind="caution-minor" label="Caution minor" />
{/* … undefined, succeeded, normal, in-progress, incomplete, not-started, pending, unknown, informative */}
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<IconIndicator kind="failed" label="Failed" />
<IconIndicator kind="caution-major" label="Caution major" />
<IconIndicator kind="caution-minor" label="Caution minor" />
{/* … undefined, succeeded, normal, in-progress, incomplete, not-started, pending, unknown, informative */}
```

## Icon size

`size` is 16 (the default, with 14px text) or 20 (with 16px text), for a bigger heading or a dashboard tile.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 12px; justify-items: start">
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="succeeded" label="Backup finished" size="16"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="succeeded" label="Backup finished" size="20"></ui-icon-indicator>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiIconIndicator kind="succeeded" label="Backup finished" size={16} />
<UiIconIndicator kind="succeeded" label="Backup finished" size={20} />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<IconIndicator kind="succeeded" label="Backup finished" size={16} />
<IconIndicator kind="succeeded" label="Backup finished" size={20} />
```

## Shape indicator kinds

`<ui-shape-indicator>` has 11 kinds: the severities (failed, critical, high, medium, low, cautious) and the states (undefined, stable, informative, incomplete, draft). The shape is always 16px.

```html

  <ui-shape-indicator kind="cautious" label="Cautious"></ui-shape-indicator>
  <ui-shape-indicator kind="undefined" label="Undefined"></ui-shape-indicator>

  <ui-shape-indicator kind="informative" label="Informative"></ui-shape-indicator>
```


## Text size

The shape indicator's text is 12px by default. `text-size="14"` (`textSize={14}` in React) makes it 14px, to match body text around it.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 12px; justify-items: start">
  <ui-shape-indicator kind="medium" label="Medium risk"></ui-shape-indicator>
  <ui-shape-indicator kind="medium" label="Medium risk" text-size="14"></ui-shape-indicator>
</div>
```

```tsx

```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ShapeIndicator kind="medium" label="Medium risk" />
<ShapeIndicator kind="medium" label="Medium risk" textSize={14} />
```

## Compact

`compact` shows only the icon or shape. The label moves into a tooltip that opens on hover and on keyboard focus. Screen readers hear the label, or `icon-description` / `shape-description` (`iconDescription` / `shapeDescription` in React) when you set one, for a longer text than the tooltip.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 24px; align-items: center">
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="succeeded" label="Signed" compact></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="pending" label="Pending" compact icon-description="Waiting for the vendor to sign"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-shape-indicator kind="critical" label="Critical" compact shape-description="Critical severity"></ui-shape-indicator>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiIconIndicator kind="succeeded" label="Signed" compact />
<UiIconIndicator kind="pending" label="Pending" compact iconDescription="Waiting for the vendor to sign" />
<UiShapeIndicator kind="critical" label="Critical" compact shapeDescription="Critical severity" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<IconIndicator kind="succeeded" label="Signed" compact />
<IconIndicator kind="pending" label="Pending" compact iconDescription="Waiting for the vendor to sign" />
<ShapeIndicator kind="critical" label="Critical" compact shapeDescription="Critical severity" />
```

## Tooltip placement

`placement` sets where the compact tooltip opens: `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right` (the default), each also with `-start` or `-end`. `align` is Carbon's name for it and takes the same values.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 48px; align-items: center; padding: 32px 64px">
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="caution-major" label="Over budget" compact placement="top"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="caution-minor" label="Close to budget" compact placement="bottom"></ui-icon-indicator>
  <ui-icon-indicator kind="normal" label="Within budget" compact placement="left"></ui-icon-indicator>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiIconIndicator kind="caution-major" label="Over budget" compact placement="top" />
<UiIconIndicator kind="caution-minor" label="Close to budget" compact placement="bottom" />
<UiIconIndicator kind="normal" label="Within budget" compact placement="left" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<IconIndicator kind="caution-major" label="Over budget" compact placement="top" />
<IconIndicator kind="caution-minor" label="Close to budget" compact placement="bottom" />
<IconIndicator kind="normal" label="Within budget" compact placement="left" />
```

## Severity

Use the shape indicator for a level, such as the severity of incidents. Pair the shape with a word, so the order is clear without the colours.


HTML:

```html
<div style="display: grid; gap: 8px; justify-items: start">
  <ui-shape-indicator kind="critical" label="INC-2041 · Critical: invoice export fails for all users" text-size="14"></ui-shape-indicator>
  <ui-shape-indicator kind="high" label="INC-2038 · High: approval emails are late" text-size="14"></ui-shape-indicator>
  <ui-shape-indicator kind="medium" label="INC-2035 · Medium: wrong date format in the PDF" text-size="14"></ui-shape-indicator>
  <ui-shape-indicator kind="low" label="INC-2030 · Low: typo on the vendor form" text-size="14"></ui-shape-indicator>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiShapeIndicator kind="critical" label="INC-2041 · Critical: invoice export fails for all users" textSize={14} />
<UiShapeIndicator kind="high" label="INC-2038 · High: approval emails are late" textSize={14} />
{/* … */}
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<ShapeIndicator kind="critical" label="INC-2041 · Critical: invoice export fails for all users" textSize={14} />
<ShapeIndicator kind="high" label="INC-2038 · High: approval emails are late" textSize={14} />
{/* … */}
```

## Change the status

Set `kind` and `label` as the state changes. The indicator is not a live region: when the change matters to the user, also announce it, for example in a `role="status"` line.


HTML:

```html
<ui-icon-indicator id="status-indicator-job" kind="not-started" label="Import not started"></ui-icon-indicator>
<ui-button id="status-indicator-run" kind="tertiary">Import vendors</ui-button>
<p id="status-indicator-msg" role="status" style="margin: 0"></p>

<script type="module">
  const job = document.getElementById('status-indicator-job');
  const msg = document.getElementById('status-indicator-msg');
  const set = (kind, label) => {
    job.kind = kind;
    job.label = label;
    msg.textContent = label;
  };
  document.getElementById('status-indicator-run').addEventListener('click', () => {
    set('in-progress', 'Importing vendors…');
    setTimeout(() => set('succeeded', 'Import finished: 120 vendors'), 2000);
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiIconIndicator kind={job.kind} label={job.label} />
<p role="status">{job.label}</p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<IconIndicator kind={job.kind} label={job.label} />
<p role="status">{job.label}</p>
```

## Keyboard

Only the compact indicators take focus.

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves to a compact icon and opens its tooltip; leaving closes it |
| Enter, Space | Open or close the tooltip |
| Esc | Closes the tooltip |

## Accessibility

- The icon or shape is hidden from screen readers; the label says the state. Write it as the state ("Signed"), not the colour.
- Compact: the icon is a button that opens a definition tooltip with the label, and screen readers read the label or the description.
- Status changes are not announced by themselves; add a status message when they matter.

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-icon-indicator>` · React `UiIconIndicator`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `align` |  |  |  | Carbon's name for `placement` (same values) |
| `kind` | `kind` | `IconIndicatorKind \| undefined` |  |  |
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `size` | `size` | `16 \| 20` | `16` | 16 (body-compact-01) or 20 (body-compact-02). |
| `compact` | `compact` | `boolean` | `false` | Only the icon; the label in a tooltip. |
| `icon-description` | `iconDescription` | `string \| undefined` |  | Read by screen readers in compact mode instead of the label. |
| `placement` | `placement` | `Placement` | `'right'` | Where the compact tooltip opens. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `icon` | The icon |
| `label` | The label (not compact) |

### `<ui-shape-indicator>` · React `UiShapeIndicator`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `align` |  |  |  | Carbon's name for `placement` (same values) |
| `kind` | `kind` | `ShapeIndicatorKind \| undefined` |  |  |
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `text-size` | `textSize` | `12 \| 14` | `12` | 12 (helper-text-01) or 14 (body-compact-01). |
| `compact` | `compact` | `boolean` | `false` | Only the shape; the label in a tooltip. |
| `shape-description` | `shapeDescription` | `string \| undefined` |  | Read by screen readers in compact mode instead of the label. |
| `placement` | `placement` | `Placement` | `'right'` | Where the compact tooltip opens. |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `icon` | The shape |
| `label` | The label (not compact) |

# Grid

The grid is Carbon's 2x Grid: 4 columns on small screens, 8 from 672px (`md`) and 16 from 1056px (`lg`), with 32px gutters. `<ui-grid>` holds `<ui-column>`s, and each column says how many columns it spans at each size. The tinted boxes on this page only show where the columns are.


HTML:

```html
<style>
  .grid-demo ui-column > p { margin: 0; padding: 8px 0; background: var(--ui-layer-accent-1); font: var(--ui-font-body-sm); }
  .grid-demo ui-column { outline: 1px dashed var(--ui-hairline-strong); }
</style>
<div class="grid-demo">
  <ui-grid>
    <ui-column sm="4" md="4" lg="8"><p>Contract details</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="2" md="2" lg="4"><p>Status</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="2" md="2" lg="4"><p>Owner</p></ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiGrid>
  <UiColumn sm="4" md="4" lg="8"><p>Contract details</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="2" md="2" lg="4"><p>Status</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="2" md="2" lg="4"><p>Owner</p></UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Grid>
  <Column sm={4} md={4} lg={8}><p className="bg-layer-accent-1 py-2 type-body-sm">Contract details</p></Column>
  <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><p className="bg-layer-accent-1 py-2 type-body-sm">Status</p></Column>
  <Column sm={2} md={2} lg={4}><p className="bg-layer-accent-1 py-2 type-body-sm">Owner</p></Column>
</Grid>
```

The sizes follow the width of the window, not of the box the grid sits in, as Carbon's media queries do. On this page the grid sits in a narrow column, so widen or narrow the window to see the columns move.

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/grid
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-css-grid
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/grid.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/grid/column-hang.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/grid/column.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/grid/grid.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-css-grid, shared-element, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
# (none)
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-css-grid.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/css-grid.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-css-grid, tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/grid';</script>

<ui-grid>
  <ui-column sm="4" md="4" lg="8">Main</ui-column>
  <ui-column sm="4" md="4" lg="8">Side</ui-column>
</ui-grid>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiGrid, UiColumn } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiGrid>
  <UiColumn sm="4" md="4" lg="8">Main</UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="4" md="4" lg="8">Side</UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Grid, Column } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/css-grid';

<Grid>
  <Column sm={4} md={4} lg={8}>Main</Column>
  <Column sm={4} md={4} lg={8}>Side</Column>
</Grid>
```

| Size | From | Columns | Grid margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sm` | 0 | 4 | 0 |
| `md` | 672px | 8 | 16px |
| `lg` | 1056px | 16 | 16px |
| `xlg` | 1312px | 16 | 16px |
| `max` | 1584px | 16 | 24px |

The grid is at most 1584px wide and centred. Each column is 16px in from the gutter on both sides, so text in neighbouring columns is 32px apart.

## Spans per size

`sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xlg` and `max` set the span from that size up: `lg="4"` holds at `lg`, `xlg` and `max` until a larger size says otherwise. A column with no span takes one column.


HTML:

```html
<div class="grid-demo">
  <ui-grid>
    <ui-column sm="4" md="2" lg="4"><p>sm 4 · md 2 · lg 4</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="4" md="2" lg="4"><p>sm 4 · md 2 · lg 4</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="4" md="2" lg="4"><p>sm 4 · md 2 · lg 4</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="4" md="2" lg="4"><p>sm 4 · md 2 · lg 4</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="2" md="4" lg="8" xlg="4"><p>sm 2 · md 4 · lg 8 · xlg 4</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="2" md="4" lg="8" xlg="12"><p>sm 2 · md 4 · lg 8 · xlg 12</p></ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiGrid>
  {[1, 2, 3, 4].map((n) => <UiColumn key={n} sm="4" md="2" lg="4"><p>sm 4 · md 2 · lg 4</p></UiColumn>)}
  <UiColumn sm="2" md="4" lg="8" xlg="4"><p>sm 2 · md 4 · lg 8 · xlg 4</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="2" md="4" lg="8" xlg="12"><p>sm 2 · md 4 · lg 8 · xlg 12</p></UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Grid>
  {[1, 2, 3, 4].map((n) => <Column key={n} sm={4} md={2} lg={4}><p>sm 4 · md 2 · lg 4</p></Column>)}
  <Column sm={2} md={4} lg={8} xlg={4}><p>sm 2 · md 4 · lg 8 · xlg 4</p></Column>
  <Column sm={2} md={4} lg={8} xlg={12}><p>sm 2 · md 4 · lg 8 · xlg 12</p></Column>
</Grid>
```

The web component and the React wrapper take the span as text (`"4"`); React + Tailwind takes a number.

## One span for every size

`span` sets the same span at every size. Use it inside a [subgrid](#subgrids), where the parent column already decides the width.


HTML:

```html
<div class="grid-demo">
  <ui-grid>
    <ui-column span="2"><p>span 2</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column span="2"><p>span 2</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column><p>no span: 1</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column><p>no span: 1</p></ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiGrid>
  <UiColumn span="2"><p>span 2</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn span="2"><p>span 2</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn><p>no span: 1</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn><p>no span: 1</p></UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Grid>
  <Column span={2}><p>span 2</p></Column>
  <Column span={2}><p>span 2</p></Column>
  <Column><p>no span: 1</p></Column>
  <Column><p>no span: 1</p></Column>
</Grid>
```

## Hide a column at a size

A span of `0` hides the column from that size up. Here the help panel shows only from `lg`.


HTML:

```html
<div class="grid-demo">
  <ui-grid>
    <ui-column sm="4" md="8" lg="12"><p>Approval form</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="0" lg="4"><p>Help (lg and up)</p></ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiGrid>
  <UiColumn sm="4" md="8" lg="12"><p>Approval form</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="0" lg="4"><p>Help (lg and up)</p></UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Grid>
  <Column sm={4} md={8} lg={12}><p>Approval form</p></Column>
  <Column sm={0} lg={4}><p>Help (lg and up)</p></Column>
</Grid>
```

## Percent spans

`25%`, `50%`, `75%` and `100%` take that share of the grid's columns at each size: `50%` is 2 of 4, 4 of 8 and 8 of 16.


HTML:

```html
<div class="grid-demo">
  <ui-grid>
    <ui-column span="25%"><p>25%</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column span="75%"><p>75%</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column span="50%"><p>50%</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column span="50%"><p>50%</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column span="100%"><p>100%</p></ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiGrid>
  <UiColumn span="25%"><p>25%</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn span="75%"><p>75%</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn span="50%"><p>50%</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn span="50%"><p>50%</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn span="100%"><p>100%</p></UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Grid>
  <Column span="25%"><p>25%</p></Column>
  <Column span="75%"><p>75%</p></Column>
  <Column span="50%"><p>50%</p></Column>
  <Column span="50%"><p>50%</p></Column>
  <Column span="100%"><p>100%</p></Column>
</Grid>
```

## Offset, start and end

Write tokens to place a column: `offset:N` skips N columns, `start:N` and `end:N` are the grid lines it starts and ends at. In React + Tailwind, pass an object.


HTML:

```html
<div class="grid-demo">
  <ui-grid>
    <ui-column sm="span:1 offset:3" md="span:2 offset:6" lg="span:4 offset:12"><p>offset 3 / 6 / 12</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="span:2 offset:2" md="span:4 offset:4" lg="span:8 offset:8"><p>offset 2 / 4 / 8</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="span:3 offset:1" md="span:6 offset:2" lg="span:12 offset:4"><p>offset 1 / 2 / 4</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="span:2 start:2" md="span:4 start:3" lg="span:6 end:17"><p>start 2 / 3, end 17</p></ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiGrid>
  <UiColumn sm="span:1 offset:3" md="span:2 offset:6" lg="span:4 offset:12"><p>offset 3 / 6 / 12</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="span:2 offset:2" md="span:4 offset:4" lg="span:8 offset:8"><p>offset 2 / 4 / 8</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="span:3 offset:1" md="span:6 offset:2" lg="span:12 offset:4"><p>offset 1 / 2 / 4</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="span:2 start:2" md="span:4 start:3" lg="span:6 end:17"><p>start 2 / 3, end 17</p></UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Grid>
  <Column sm={{ span: 1, offset: 3 }} md={{ span: 2, offset: 6 }} lg={{ span: 4, offset: 12 }}><p>offset 3 / 6 / 12</p></Column>
  <Column sm={{ span: 2, offset: 2 }} md={{ span: 4, offset: 4 }} lg={{ span: 8, offset: 8 }}><p>offset 2 / 4 / 8</p></Column>
  <Column sm={{ span: 3, offset: 1 }} md={{ span: 6, offset: 2 }} lg={{ span: 12, offset: 4 }}><p>offset 1 / 2 / 4</p></Column>
  <Column sm={{ span: 2, start: 2 }} md={{ span: 4, start: 3 }} lg={{ span: 6, end: 17 }}><p>start 2 / 3, end 17</p></Column>
</Grid>
```

## Narrow and column hang

`narrow` drops the gutter at the start of each column, so the text hangs on the gutter: Carbon uses it for type-heavy pages. Inside a narrow column, `<ui-column-hang>` pushes content in by 16px, so it lines up with the text of a wide grid above or below.


HTML:

```html
<div class="grid-demo">
  <ui-grid>
    <ui-column sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><p>wide</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><p>wide</p></ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
  <ui-grid narrow>
    <ui-column sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><p>narrow</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><ui-column-hang>narrow, hang</ui-column-hang></ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiGrid>
  <UiColumn sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><p>wide</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><p>wide</p></UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
<UiGrid narrow>
  <UiColumn sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><p>narrow</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><UiColumnHang>narrow, hang</UiColumnHang></UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Grid>
  <Column sm={2} md={4} lg={8}><p>wide</p></Column>
  <Column sm={2} md={4} lg={8}><p>wide</p></Column>
</Grid>
<Grid narrow>
  <Column sm={2} md={4} lg={8}><p>narrow</p></Column>
  <Column sm={2} md={4} lg={8}><ColumnHang>narrow, hang</ColumnHang></Column>
</Grid>
```

## Condensed

`condensed` makes the gutters 1px, for tiles or images that sit edge to edge, such as a dashboard of cards. `<ui-column-hang>` pushes text in by 15.5px here.


HTML:

```html
<div class="grid-demo">

    <ui-column sm="1" md="2" lg="4"><p>Signed</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="1" md="2" lg="4"><p>Pending</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="1" md="2" lg="4"><p>Expired</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="1" md="2" lg="4"><ui-column-hang>Draft</ui-column-hang></ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiGrid condensed>
  <UiColumn sm="1" md="2" lg="4"><p>Signed</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="1" md="2" lg="4"><p>Pending</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="1" md="2" lg="4"><p>Expired</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="1" md="2" lg="4"><UiColumnHang>Draft</UiColumnHang></UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Grid condensed>
  <Column sm={1} md={2} lg={4}><p>Signed</p></Column>
  <Column sm={1} md={2} lg={4}><p>Pending</p></Column>
  <Column sm={1} md={2} lg={4}><p>Expired</p></Column>
  <Column sm={1} md={2} lg={4}><ColumnHang>Draft</ColumnHang></Column>
</Grid>
```

## Space between rows

Columns that wrap to a new row touch by default. `with-row-gap` (`withRowGap`) spaces the rows like the columns: 32px, 16px in a narrow grid, 1px in a condensed one.


HTML:

```html
<div class="grid-demo">
  <ui-grid with-row-gap>
    <ui-column sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><p>Sales</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><p>Legal</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><p>Finance</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><p>Purchasing</p></ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiGrid withRowGap>
  <UiColumn sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><p>Sales</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><p>Legal</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><p>Finance</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="2" md="4" lg="8"><p>Purchasing</p></UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Grid withRowGap>
  <Column sm={2} md={4} lg={8}><p>Sales</p></Column>
  <Column sm={2} md={4} lg={8}><p>Legal</p></Column>
  <Column sm={2} md={4} lg={8}><p>Finance</p></Column>
  <Column sm={2} md={4} lg={8}><p>Purchasing</p></Column>
</Grid>
```

## Full width and alignment

The grid stops at 1584px and centres itself. `full-width` (`fullWidth`) lets it fill any screen; `align="start"` or `align="end"` pins the 1584px grid to one side. On this page the grid is narrower than 1584px, so the preview looks the same; the difference shows on a wide screen.


HTML:

```html
<div class="grid-demo">
  <ui-grid full-width>
    <ui-column sm="4" md="8" lg="16"><p>full-width: no 1584px cap</p></ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
  <ui-grid align="start">
    <ui-column sm="4" md="8" lg="16"><p>align="start": pinned to the start on wide screens</p></ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiGrid fullWidth>
  <UiColumn sm="4" md="8" lg="16"><p>full-width: no 1584px cap</p></UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
<UiGrid align="start">
  <UiColumn sm="4" md="8" lg="16"><p>align="start": pinned to the start on wide screens</p></UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Grid fullWidth>
  <Column sm={4} md={8} lg={16}><p>fullWidth: no 1584px cap</p></Column>
</Grid>
<Grid align="start">
  <Column sm={4} md={8} lg={16}><p>align="start": pinned to the start on wide screens</p></Column>
</Grid>
```

## Subgrids

A `<ui-grid>` inside a `<ui-column>` becomes a subgrid: it has as many columns as its column spans, and its own columns line up with the outer grid. You don't mark it; nesting is enough.


HTML:

```html
<div class="grid-demo">
  <ui-grid>
    <ui-column sm="4" md="2" lg="4"><p>Filters</p></ui-column>
    <ui-column sm="4" md="6" lg="12">
      <p>Results: md 6 · lg 12, with a subgrid</p>
      <ui-grid>
        <ui-column sm="2" md="3" lg="4"><p>Contract A</p></ui-column>
        <ui-column sm="2" md="3" lg="4"><p>Contract B</p></ui-column>
        <ui-column sm="0" md="0" lg="4"><p>Contract C (lg)</p></ui-column>
      </ui-grid>
    </ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiGrid>
  <UiColumn sm="4" md="2" lg="4"><p>Filters</p></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="4" md="6" lg="12">
    <p>Results: md 6 · lg 12, with a subgrid</p>
    <UiGrid>
      <UiColumn sm="2" md="3" lg="4"><p>Contract A</p></UiColumn>
      <UiColumn sm="2" md="3" lg="4"><p>Contract B</p></UiColumn>
      <UiColumn sm="0" md="0" lg="4"><p>Contract C (lg)</p></UiColumn>
    </UiGrid>
  </UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Grid>
  <Column sm={4} md={2} lg={4}><p>Filters</p></Column>
  <Column sm={4} md={6} lg={12}>
    <p>Results: md 6 · lg 12, with a subgrid</p>
    <Grid>
      <Column sm={2} md={3} lg={4}><p>Contract A</p></Column>
      <Column sm={2} md={3} lg={4}><p>Contract B</p></Column>
      <Column sm={0} md={0} lg={4}><p>Contract C (lg)</p></Column>
    </Grid>
  </Column>
</Grid>
```

A subgrid decides once, when it is added to the page, whether it sits in a column. Moving a `<ui-grid>` in or out of a column later doesn't switch it.

## Mix gutter modes

A subgrid can be `narrow` or `condensed` while the outer grid stays wide. Its `<ui-column-hang>`s still line up with the wide text around them.

A percent span counts the columns of the size (4, 8 or 16), not the subgrid's. In a subgrid narrower than the grid, give numbers, as the condensed columns below do.


HTML:

```html
<div class="grid-demo">
  <ui-grid>
    <ui-column span="100%">
      <p>wide</p>
      <ui-grid narrow>
        <ui-column span="25%"><ui-column-hang>narrow</ui-column-hang></ui-column>
        <ui-column span="25%"><ui-column-hang>narrow</ui-column-hang></ui-column>
        <ui-column span="50%">
          <p>wide</p>
          <ui-grid condensed>
            <ui-column sm="1" md="2" lg="4"><ui-column-hang>condensed</ui-column-hang></ui-column>
            <ui-column sm="1" md="2" lg="4"><ui-column-hang>condensed</ui-column-hang></ui-column>
          </ui-grid>
        </ui-column>
      </ui-grid>
    </ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiGrid>
  <UiColumn span="100%">
    <p>wide</p>
    <UiGrid narrow>
      <UiColumn span="25%"><UiColumnHang>narrow</UiColumnHang></UiColumn>
      <UiColumn span="25%"><UiColumnHang>narrow</UiColumnHang></UiColumn>
      <UiColumn span="50%">
        <p>wide</p>
        <UiGrid condensed>
          <UiColumn sm="1" md="2" lg="4"><UiColumnHang>condensed</UiColumnHang></UiColumn>
          <UiColumn sm="1" md="2" lg="4"><UiColumnHang>condensed</UiColumnHang></UiColumn>
        </UiGrid>
      </UiColumn>
    </UiGrid>
  </UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Grid>
  <Column span="100%">
    <p>wide</p>
    <Grid narrow>
      <Column span="25%"><ColumnHang>narrow</ColumnHang></Column>
      <Column span="25%"><ColumnHang>narrow</ColumnHang></Column>
      <Column span="50%">
        <p>wide</p>
        <Grid condensed>
          <Column sm={1} md={2} lg={4}><ColumnHang>condensed</ColumnHang></Column>
          <Column sm={1} md={2} lg={4}><ColumnHang>condensed</ColumnHang></Column>
        </Grid>
      </Column>
    </Grid>
  </Column>
</Grid>
```

## Lay out a form

Fields in columns: two side by side from `md`, one per row on a phone. The grid's 32px gutter separates them, so the fields need no margins of their own.


HTML:

```html
<ui-grid with-row-gap>
  <ui-column sm="4" md="4" lg="8"><ui-text-input label="Contract number" value="CT-2026-0142"></ui-text-input></ui-column>
  <ui-column sm="4" md="4" lg="8"><ui-text-input label="Counterparty" value="Siam Logistics Co., Ltd."></ui-text-input></ui-column>
  <ui-column sm="4" md="8" lg="16"><ui-text-area label="Notes"></ui-text-area></ui-column>
</ui-grid>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiGrid withRowGap>
  <UiColumn sm="4" md="4" lg="8"><UiTextInput label="Contract number" value="CT-2026-0142" /></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="4" md="4" lg="8"><UiTextInput label="Counterparty" value="Siam Logistics Co., Ltd." /></UiColumn>
  <UiColumn sm="4" md="8" lg="16"><UiTextArea label="Notes" /></UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Grid withRowGap>
  <Column sm={4} md={4} lg={8}><TextInput label="Contract number" defaultValue="CT-2026-0142" /></Column>
  <Column sm={4} md={4} lg={8}><TextInput label="Counterparty" defaultValue="Siam Logistics Co., Ltd." /></Column>
  <Column sm={4} md={8} lg={16}><TextArea label="Notes" /></Column>
</Grid>
```

## Other elements as the grid or a column

In React + Tailwind, `as` renders the grid or a column as another element, for example a `<main>` grid with `<section>` columns. The web component is always `<ui-grid>`; put your landmark around it or inside a column.


HTML:

```html
<div class="grid-demo">
  <ui-grid>
    <ui-column sm="4" md="8" lg="16">
      <section aria-label="Summary"><p>A section inside the column</p></section>
    </ui-column>
  </ui-grid>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiGrid>
  <UiColumn sm="4" md="8" lg="16">
    <section aria-label="Summary"><p>A section inside the column</p></section>
  </UiColumn>
</UiGrid>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Grid as="main">
  <Column as="section" aria-label="Summary" sm={4} md={8} lg={16}>
    <p>The column is the section</p>
  </Column>
</Grid>
```

## Accessibility

- The grid only places things. It has no role, and screen readers read the columns in the order they appear in the markup. Keep that order meaningful; don't use offsets to move content before something that comes earlier in the markup.
- A column hidden with a span of `0` is `display: none` at that size, so it is hidden from screen readers too.
- Use [headings](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/heading/) and landmarks for structure; the grid adds none.

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-grid>` · React `UiGrid`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `narrow` | `narrow` | `boolean` | `false` | No start gutter: text hangs on the gutter (Carbon narrow). |
| `condensed` | `condensed` | `boolean` | `false` | 1px gutters (Carbon condensed). |
| `full-width` | `fullWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | No max width. |
| `align` | `align` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end' \| undefined` |  | Pin a max-width grid to a side (centred by default). |
| `with-row-gap` | `withRowGap` | `boolean` | `false` | Rows spaced like columns. |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | `<ui-column>` elements |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `grid` | The grid |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-grid-gutter` |  | The gutter (32px; 1px condensed) |

### `<ui-column>` · React `UiColumn`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sm` | `sm` | `string \| undefined` |  |  |
| `md` | `md` | `string \| undefined` |  |  |
| `lg` | `lg` | `string \| undefined` |  |  |
| `xlg` | `xlg` | `string \| undefined` |  |  |
| `max` | `max` | `string \| undefined` |  |  |
| `span` | `span` | `string \| undefined` |  | The span at every breakpoint (Carbon `span`). |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | The column's content |

### `<ui-column-hang>` · React `UiColumnHang`

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | The content |

# Heading

`<ui-heading>` renders a heading at the right level without you counting: each `<ui-section>` around it goes one level deeper, so the same markup gives an `<h2>` on one page and an `<h4>` inside a nested panel. The type follows Carbon's productive scale for that level.


HTML:

```html
<ui-section level="3">
  <ui-heading>Contract CT-2026-0142</ui-heading>
  <ui-section>
    <ui-heading>Parties</ui-heading>
    <ui-section>
      <ui-heading>Signer</ui-heading>
      <ui-section>
        <ui-heading>Contact details</ui-heading>
      </ui-section>
    </ui-section>
  </ui-section>
</ui-section>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSection level={3}>
  <UiHeading>Contract CT-2026-0142</UiHeading>
  <UiSection>
    <UiHeading>Parties</UiHeading>
    <UiSection>
      <UiHeading>Signer</UiHeading>
      <UiSection>
        <UiHeading>Contact details</UiHeading>
      </UiSection>
    </UiSection>
  </UiSection>
</UiSection>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Section level={3}>
  <Heading>Contract CT-2026-0142</Heading>
  <Section>
    <Heading>Parties</Heading>
    <Section>
      <Heading>Signer</Heading>
      <Section>
        <Heading>Contact details</Heading>
      </Section>
    </Section>
  </Section>
</Section>
```

The previews on this page start at level 3, because the page already has its own `<h1>` and `<h2>`s. The result above is `<h3>`, `<h4>`, `<h5>`, `<h6>`.

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/heading
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-heading
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/heading.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/heading/heading-shared.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/heading/heading.ts
#    components/ui/primitives/heading/section.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    shared-element, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
# (none)
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-heading.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/heading.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it

A `<ui-heading>` outside any section is an `<h1>`. The first section makes its headings `<h2>`, a section inside it `<h3>`, and so on down to `<h6>`.


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/heading';</script>

<ui-heading>Contracts</ui-heading>
<ui-section>
  <ui-heading>Waiting for approval</ui-heading>
</ui-section>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiHeading, UiSection } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiHeading>Contracts</UiHeading>
<UiSection>
  <UiHeading>Waiting for approval</UiHeading>
</UiSection>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Heading, Section } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/heading';

<Heading>Contracts</Heading>
<Section>
  <Heading>Waiting for approval</Heading>
</Section>
```

`<ui-section>` is a plain block with no role. The React + Tailwind `Section` renders a `<section>` element; change it with `as` (for example `as="div"`).

## Set the level

`level` on a section sets the level of its headings, instead of one more than the section around it. Use it where a block starts below a heading that isn't a `<ui-heading>`, such as a page title from your layout. Sections inside it count on from there. Levels stop at 6.


HTML:

```html
<ui-section level="4">
  <ui-heading>Approval history</ui-heading>
  <ui-section>
    <ui-heading>Legal review, 3 October</ui-heading>
  </ui-section>
</ui-section>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiSection level={4}>
  <UiHeading>Approval history</UiHeading>
  <UiSection>
    <UiHeading>Legal review, 3 October</UiHeading>
  </UiSection>
</UiSection>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Section level={4}>
  <Heading>Approval history</Heading>
  <Section>
    <Heading>Legal review, 3 October</Heading>
  </Section>
</Section>
```

## Type for each level

| Level | Carbon type | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `<h1>` | heading-06 | 42px, light |
| `<h2>` | heading-05 | 32px |
| `<h3>` | heading-04 | 28px |
| `<h4>` | heading-03 | 20px |
| `<h5>` | heading-02 | 16px, semibold |
| `<h6>` | heading-01 | 14px, semibold |

Headings have no margins: space them with the layout around them, for example the gap of a flex box or a [grid](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/grid/).

## The same block at any depth

A block you reuse, such as a summary card, can hold a `<ui-heading>` and still be right wherever it goes: inside one section it is an `<h4>`, inside two it is an `<h5>`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-section level="3">
  <ui-heading>Department budget</ui-heading>
  <ui-section>
    <ui-heading>Legal</ui-heading>
    <p>Spent 1.2M of 2.0M baht.</p>
    <ui-section>
      <ui-heading>Outside counsel</ui-heading>
      <p>Spent 400K of 600K baht.</p>
    </ui-section>
  </ui-section>
</ui-section>
```

React:

```tsx
function BudgetCard({ name, spent, children }: { name: string; spent: string; children?: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <UiSection>
      <UiHeading>{name}</UiHeading>
      <p>{spent}</p>
      {children}
    </UiSection>
  );
}

<UiSection level={3}>
  <UiHeading>Department budget</UiHeading>
  <BudgetCard name="Legal" spent="Spent 1.2M of 2.0M baht.">
    <BudgetCard name="Outside counsel" spent="Spent 400K of 600K baht." />
  </BudgetCard>
</UiSection>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
function BudgetCard({ name, spent, children }: { name: string; spent: string; children?: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <Section>
      <Heading>{name}</Heading>
      <p>{spent}</p>
      {children}
    </Section>
  );
}

<Section level={3}>
  <Heading>Department budget</Heading>
  <BudgetCard name="Legal" spent="Spent 1.2M of 2.0M baht.">
    <BudgetCard name="Outside counsel" spent="Spent 400K of 600K baht." />
  </BudgetCard>
</Section>
```

The web component works out its level when it is added to the page. If you move a `<ui-heading>` to another section, it takes the new level then; changing a section's `level` later doesn't renumber the headings already inside.

## Style a heading

The web component shows its `<h1>`…`<h6>` as the `heading` part. In React + Tailwind, pass a `className`.


HTML:

```html
<style>
  .heading-accent::part(heading) { color: var(--ui-link); }
</style>
<ui-section level="4">
  <ui-heading class="heading-accent">Due this week</ui-heading>
</ui-section>
```

React:

```tsx
// .heading-accent::part(heading) { color: var(--ui-link); }
<UiSection level={4}>
  <UiHeading className="heading-accent">Due this week</UiHeading>
</UiSection>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Section level={4}>
  <Heading className="text-link">Due this week</Heading>
</Section>
```

## Accessibility

- Screen reader users jump between headings and list them to find their way. Levels that follow the nesting make that list match the page.
- Keep one `<h1>` per page. Start a block at a deeper `level` when the page title comes from somewhere else.
- `<ui-section>` adds no landmark. If a part of the page needs one, wrap it in your own `<section aria-labelledby>` or `<nav>`.

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-heading>` · React `UiHeading`

#### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `level` | `HeadingLevel` | The level from the `<ui-section>` around it (1 outside any). |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `syncLevel()` | Takes the level of the section around it (also called by a section whose level changed). |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | The heading text |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `heading` | The `<h1>`…`<h6>` |

### `<ui-section>` · React `UiSection`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | `level` | `number \| undefined` |  | The heading level inside, instead of one more than the section around it. |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `getCurrentLevel()` | The level its headings use (Carbon `getCurrentLevel`). |
| `syncLevel()` | Takes its level from `level`, else from the section around it (also called by an ancestor whose level changed). |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | The section's content |

# Layer

`<ui-layer>` is Carbon's Layer: everything inside it uses the theme's next layer set, so a field on a gray tile isn't the same gray as the tile. Fields, menus, borders, dividers and hover fills all follow it. The [Themes and layers](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/themes/#put-fields-on-a-tile-ui-layer) guide explains the layering model; this page shows the element.


HTML:

```html
<ui-text-input label="On the page (field-01)"></ui-text-input>
<ui-layer level="1" with-background style="padding: 16px">
  <ui-text-input label="Inside a layer (field-02)"></ui-text-input>
  <ui-layer with-background style="padding: 16px; margin-top: 16px">
    <ui-dropdown label="One level deeper (field-03)" placeholder="Choose a department">
      <option value="sales">Sales</option>
      <option value="legal">Legal</option>
    </ui-dropdown>
  </ui-layer>
</ui-layer>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTextInput label="On the page (field-01)" />
<UiLayer level={1} withBackground style={{ padding: 16 }}>
  <UiTextInput label="Inside a layer (field-02)" />
  <UiLayer withBackground style={{ padding: 16, marginTop: 16 }}>
    <UiDropdown label="One level deeper (field-03)" placeholder="Choose a department">
      <option value="sales">Sales</option>
      <option value="legal">Legal</option>
    </UiDropdown>
  </UiLayer>
</UiLayer>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<TextInput label="On the page (field-01)" />
<Layer withBackground className="p-4">
  <TextInput label="Inside a layer (field-02)" />
  <Layer withBackground className="mt-4 p-4">
    <Dropdown label="One level deeper (field-03)" placeholder="Choose a department" items={[{ value: 'sales', label: 'Sales' }, { value: 'legal', label: 'Legal' }]} />
  </Layer>
</Layer>
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash

```

## Use it


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/layer';</script>

<ui-layer level="1" with-background>
  <ui-text-input label="Field on a tile"></ui-text-input>
</ui-layer>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiLayer, UiTextInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiLayer level={1} withBackground>
  <UiTextInput label="Field on a tile" />
</UiLayer>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Layer } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/layer';

<Layer withBackground>
  <TextInput label="Field on a tile" />
</Layer>
```

## Levels

`level` is `0`, `1` or `2`. Level `0` is the page's own set, the same as outside any layer; `1` and `2` go deeper. Without `level`, the web component and the React wrapper start at `0` and a nested layer goes one deeper, as Carbon's `cds-layer`. The React + Tailwind `Layer` follows Carbon React instead: it starts at `1`.


HTML:

```html
<ui-layer level="0" with-background style="padding: 16px">
  <ui-text-input label="level 0"></ui-text-input>
</ui-layer>
<ui-layer level="1" with-background style="padding: 16px">
  <ui-text-input label="level 1"></ui-text-input>
</ui-layer>
<ui-layer level="2" with-background style="padding: 16px">
  <ui-text-input label="level 2"></ui-text-input>
</ui-layer>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLayer level={0} withBackground style={{ padding: 16 }}><UiTextInput label="level 0" /></UiLayer>
<UiLayer level={1} withBackground style={{ padding: 16 }}><UiTextInput label="level 1" /></UiLayer>
<UiLayer level={2} withBackground style={{ padding: 16 }}><UiTextInput label="level 2" /></UiLayer>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Layer level={0} withBackground className="p-4"><TextInput label="level 0" /></Layer>
<Layer level={1} withBackground className="p-4"><TextInput label="level 1" /></Layer>
<Layer level={2} withBackground className="p-4"><TextInput label="level 2" /></Layer>
```

Nesting deeper than level 2 stays at 2.

## Fields on a tile

A [tile](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tile/) paints the current layer's color, but it doesn't change the layer of what is inside it. Put the fields in a layer one level up, so they stand out from the tile.


HTML:

```html
<ui-tile>
  <p style="margin: 0 0 16px">Delivery address</p>
  <ui-layer level="1">
    <ui-text-input label="Province" value="Chiang Mai"></ui-text-input>
  </ui-layer>
</ui-tile>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiTile>
  <p>Delivery address</p>
  <UiLayer level={1}>
    <UiTextInput label="Province" value="Chiang Mai" />
  </UiLayer>
</UiTile>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Tile>
  <p className="mb-4">Delivery address</p>
  <Layer>
    <TextInput label="Province" defaultValue="Chiang Mai" />
  </Layer>
</Tile>
```

## With or without a background

A layer on its own only changes the tokens for what is inside it; it paints nothing. `with-background` (`withBackground`) paints it with Carbon's layer background, the surface its content sits on. Leave it off when your own box (a tile, a panel) already paints the surface.


HTML:

```html
<ui-layer level="1" style="padding: 16px; border: 1px dashed var(--ui-hairline-strong)">
  <ui-text-input label="No background: the layer paints nothing"></ui-text-input>
</ui-layer>
<ui-layer level="1" with-background style="padding: 16px">
  <ui-text-input label="with-background"></ui-text-input>
</ui-layer>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLayer level={1} style={{ padding: 16, border: '1px dashed var(--ui-hairline-strong)' }}>
  <UiTextInput label="No background: the layer paints nothing" />
</UiLayer>
<UiLayer level={1} withBackground style={{ padding: 16 }}>
  <UiTextInput label="withBackground" />
</UiLayer>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Layer className="border border-dashed border-hairline-strong p-4">
  <TextInput label="No background: the layer paints nothing" />
</Layer>
<Layer withBackground className="p-4">
  <TextInput label="withBackground" />
</Layer>
```

## Menus, tables and other components

Everything that reads the layer tokens follows the layer: the list of a dropdown, the rows of a table, the dividers of a structured list, the hover fill of a ghost button.


HTML:

```html
<ui-layer level="1" with-background style="padding: 16px">
  <ui-dropdown label="Approver" placeholder="Choose an approver">
    <option value="somchai">Somchai K.</option>
    <option value="malee">Malee S.</option>
  </ui-dropdown>
  <div style="margin-top: 16px"><ui-button kind="ghost">Add another approver</ui-button></div>
</ui-layer>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiLayer level={1} withBackground style={{ padding: 16 }}>
  <UiDropdown label="Approver" placeholder="Choose an approver">
    <option value="somchai">Somchai K.</option>
    <option value="malee">Malee S.</option>
  </UiDropdown>
  <UiButton kind="ghost">Add another approver</UiButton>
</UiLayer>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<Layer withBackground className="p-4">
  <Dropdown label="Approver" placeholder="Choose an approver" items={[{ value: 'somchai', label: 'Somchai K.' }, { value: 'malee', label: 'Malee S.' }]} />
  <Button kind="ghost" className="mt-4">Add another approver</Button>
</Layer>
```

## In a dark zone

A layer works inside any theme zone: it moves along that theme's layer sets. See [Make a zone dark](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/themes/#make-a-zone-dark) for the zone itself.


HTML:

```html
<div data-theme="g90" style="padding: 16px; background: var(--ui-canvas); color: var(--ui-ink)">
  <ui-text-input label="On g90"></ui-text-input>
  <ui-layer level="1" with-background style="padding: 16px; margin-top: 16px">
    <ui-text-input label="On g90, one layer up"></ui-text-input>
  </ui-layer>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<div data-theme="g90" style={{ padding: 16, background: 'var(--ui-canvas)', color: 'var(--ui-ink)' }}>
  <UiTextInput label="On g90" />
  <UiLayer level={1} withBackground style={{ padding: 16, marginTop: 16 }}>
    <UiTextInput label="On g90, one layer up" />
  </UiLayer>
</div>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<div data-theme="g90" className="bg-canvas p-4 text-ink">
  <TextInput label="On g90" />
  <Layer withBackground className="mt-4 p-4">
    <TextInput label="On g90, one layer up" />
  </Layer>
</div>
```

## Read the level

The element's `level` property holds its level, worked out or set. In React + Tailwind, `useLayerLevel()` returns the level of the closest `Layer` (`-1` outside any), for your own components that paint by layer.


HTML:

```html
<ui-layer id="layer-outer" with-background style="padding: 16px">
  <ui-layer id="layer-inner" with-background style="padding: 16px">Nested layer</ui-layer>
</ui-layer>
<p>Levels: <output id="layer-out"></output></p>

<script type="module">
  const outer = document.getElementById('layer-outer');
  const inner = document.getElementById('layer-inner');
  document.getElementById('layer-out').value = `outer ${outer.level}, inner ${inner.level}`;
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
import type { UiLayer as LayerElement } from '@purpurabog/ui';

const inner = useRef<LayerElement>(null);
const [level, setLevel] = useState<number>();
useEffect(() => setLevel(inner.current?.level), []);

<UiLayer withBackground style={{ padding: 16 }}>
  <UiLayer ref={inner} withBackground style={{ padding: 16 }}>Nested layer</UiLayer>
</UiLayer>
<p>Inner level: <output>{level}</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { Layer, useLayerLevel } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/layer';

function LevelBadge() {
  const level = useLayerLevel();
  return <span className="type-caption text-ink-muted">level {level}</span>;
}

<Layer withBackground className="p-4">
  <LevelBadge />
  <Layer withBackground className="mt-4 p-4"><LevelBadge /></Layer>
</Layer>
```

The web component works its level out when it is added to the page, through shadow roots too. Set `level` yourself if you move a layer somewhere else later.

## Accessibility

- A layer is only color. It has no role and adds nothing for screen readers.
- Layers keep fields visible against the surface under them, which helps everyone see where to type. Don't rely on the layer color alone to tell areas apart; use headings and labels too.

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-layer>` · React `UiLayer`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | `level` |  |  | 0, 1 or 2. Computed from the nearest ancestor layer when not set. |
| `with-background` | `withBackground` | `boolean` | `false` | Paint the layer with Carbon's `layer-background` (`withBackground`): the colour its content sits on (white theme, level 1: #f4f4f4 under #ffffff fields). |

#### Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `syncLevel()` | An automatic level follows the layer around it (also called by a layer whose level changed); a set one stays. |

#### Slots

| Slot | Description |
|---|---|
| (default) | Content |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The wrapper |

#### CSS custom properties

| Custom property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-layer-border` |  | / --ui-layer-radius - With `with-background`: its border and corner radius (default none, 0; Kanok: a card's hairline and 12px) |
