# Edit in place

Edit in place shows a value as plain text that people can edit right where it is, without opening a form (Carbon for IBM Products `EditInPlace`). Hovered, it gets the field fill and an "Edit" button. Clicked or tabbed into, it becomes a field with "Cancel" and "Save" buttons. Use it for one value on a page that is mostly read, such as a contract's title or a reference number.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 360px">
  <ui-edit-in-place label="Contract title" value="Warehouse lease, Bang Na"></ui-edit-in-place>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiEditInPlace label="Contract title" value="Warehouse lease, Bang Na" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<EditInPlace label="Contract title" defaultValue="Warehouse lease, Bang Na" />
```

## Installation


npm:

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```

shadcn · Web component:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/edit-in-place
```

shadcn · React + Tailwind:

```bash
npx shadcn@4 add @kanok-ui/tw-edit-in-place
```

Manual:

```bash
# Web component
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install lit@^3.3.0
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/edit-in-place.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/primitives/edit-in-place/edit-in-place.ts
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-edit-in-place, icon-button, popover, shared-element, shared-events, shared-field, shared-localize, shared-position, tokens

# React + Tailwind
# 1. Install the dependencies
npm install @purpurabog/ui@^1.4.3
# 2. Copy each file's "content" from
#    https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@purpurabog/ui@1.4.3/registry/tw-edit-in-place.json
#    to its target:
#    components/ui/react-tw/edit-in-place.tsx
# 3. Do the same for the items it needs (registry/<name>.json):
#    core-edit-in-place, core-position, tw-i18n, tw-icon-button, tw-popover, tw-theme, tw-utils
```

npm gives you every component from the package. shadcn copies the source into your app instead: a copy pinned to this version that you can change. The shadcn commands need the `@kanok-ui` registry in your `components.json` once, see [Installation](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn).

## Use it

`label` is the field's accessible name; there is no visible label, so the text around the value has to say what it is.


HTML:

```html
<script type="module">import '@purpurabog/ui/edit-in-place';</script>

<ui-edit-in-place label="Contract title" value="Warehouse lease"></ui-edit-in-place>
```

React:

```tsx
import { UiEditInPlace } from '@purpurabog/ui/react';

<UiEditInPlace label="Contract title" value="Warehouse lease" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
import { EditInPlace } from '@/components/ui/react-tw/edit-in-place';

<EditInPlace label="Contract title" defaultValue="Warehouse lease" />
```

## Save and cancel

`ui-save` fires when a change is saved: with Save, with Enter, or when the focus leaves with a valid change. `ui-cancel` fires when the value is put back: with Cancel, with Escape, or when the focus leaves without a valid change. Both carry the value in `detail.value`. Save and Cancel are enabled only once the value has changed (spaces at the ends don't count).


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 360px">
  <ui-edit-in-place id="edit-in-place-po" label="Purchase order number" value="PO-2026-0815"></ui-edit-in-place>
</div>
<p>Last event: <output id="edit-in-place-po-out"></output></p>

<script type="module">
  const field = document.getElementById('edit-in-place-po');
  const out = document.getElementById('edit-in-place-po-out');
  field.addEventListener('ui-save', (event) => (out.value = `saved "${event.detail.value}"`));
  field.addEventListener('ui-cancel', (event) => (out.value = `put back "${event.detail.value}"`));
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const [last, setLast] = useState('');

<UiEditInPlace
  label="Purchase order number"
  value="PO-2026-0815"
  onUiSave={(e) => setLast(`saved "${e.detail.value}"`)}
  onUiCancel={(e) => setLast(`put back "${e.detail.value}"`)}
/>
<p>Last event: <output>{last}</output></p>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [last, setLast] = useState('');

<EditInPlace
  label="Purchase order number"
  defaultValue="PO-2026-0815"
  onSave={(value) => setLast(`saved "${value}"`)}
  onCancel={(value) => setLast(`put back "${value}"`)}
/>
<p>Last event: <output>{last}</output></p>
```

The `input` event fires on every keystroke, with `value` already updated. In React + Tailwind, `onChange` gets each new value, and the value put back on cancel.

## Save to your server

Saving is your app's: send the value to the server in `ui-save`. The element keeps the edited value meanwhile; Cancel and Escape go back to the value last saved. A `value` you set while it isn't being edited becomes the new starting point.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 360px">
  <ui-edit-in-place id="edit-in-place-ref" label="Reference" value="REF-104"></ui-edit-in-place>
</div>
<p>Saved on the server: <output id="edit-in-place-ref-out">REF-104</output></p>

<script type="module">
  const field = document.getElementById('edit-in-place-ref');
  const out = document.getElementById('edit-in-place-ref-out');
  field.addEventListener('ui-save', (event) => {
    const sent = event.detail.value.trim();
    setTimeout(() => (out.value = sent), 400); // the server's answer
  });
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const [reference, setReference] = useState('REF-104');

<UiEditInPlace
  label="Reference"
  value={reference}
  onUiSave={async (e) => setReference(await saveReference(e.detail.value))}
/>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [reference, setReference] = useState('REF-104');

<EditInPlace
  label="Reference"
  value={reference}
  onChange={setReference}
  onSave={async (value) => setReference(await saveReference(value))}
/>
```

`saveReference` stands for your own call to the server. React + Tailwind's `value` is controlled: pair it with `onChange`.

## Sizes

`size`: `sm` 40px (the default), `md` 48px, `lg` 64px. The buttons are squares of the same height.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 360px; display: grid; gap: 16px">
  <ui-edit-in-place label="Small" value="Small, 40px" edit-always-visible></ui-edit-in-place>
  <ui-edit-in-place label="Medium" value="Medium, 48px" size="md" edit-always-visible></ui-edit-in-place>
  <ui-edit-in-place label="Large" value="Large, 64px" size="lg" edit-always-visible></ui-edit-in-place>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiEditInPlace label="Small" value="Small, 40px" editAlwaysVisible />
<UiEditInPlace label="Medium" value="Medium, 48px" size="md" editAlwaysVisible />
<UiEditInPlace label="Large" value="Large, 64px" size="lg" editAlwaysVisible />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<EditInPlace label="Small" defaultValue="Small, 40px" editAlwaysVisible />
<EditInPlace label="Medium" defaultValue="Medium, 48px" size="md" editAlwaysVisible />
<EditInPlace label="Large" defaultValue="Large, 64px" size="lg" editAlwaysVisible />
```

## Show the Edit button all the time

By default the Edit button shows on hover only. `edit-always-visible` (`editAlwaysVisible`) keeps it visible, so people on touch screens, or who don't hover, can see the value is editable.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 360px">
  <ui-edit-in-place label="Cost center" value="CC-4410 Legal" edit-always-visible></ui-edit-in-place>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiEditInPlace label="Cost center" value="CC-4410 Legal" editAlwaysVisible />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<EditInPlace label="Cost center" defaultValue="CC-4410 Legal" editAlwaysVisible />
```

## Placeholder

`placeholder` shows in the empty field, for a value that hasn't been set yet.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 360px">
  <ui-edit-in-place label="Project code" placeholder="Add a project code" edit-always-visible></ui-edit-in-place>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiEditInPlace label="Project code" placeholder="Add a project code" editAlwaysVisible />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<EditInPlace label="Project code" placeholder="Add a project code" editAlwaysVisible />
```

## Invalid

`invalid` draws a red border and a warning icon, and blocks saving: Save stays disabled, Enter doesn't save, and leaving the field puts the value back. `invalid-text` (`invalidText`) shows under it and describes the field. Check the value on `input` and set `invalid` yourself.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 360px">
  <ui-edit-in-place id="edit-in-place-tax" label="Tax ID" value="0105556012345" invalid-text="A tax ID has 13 digits"></ui-edit-in-place>
</div>

<script type="module">
  const field = document.getElementById('edit-in-place-tax');
  const check = () => (field.invalid = !/^\d{13}$/.test(field.value));
  field.addEventListener('input', check);
  field.addEventListener('ui-cancel', check);
</script>
```

React:

```tsx
const [taxId, setTaxId] = useState('0105556012345');

<UiEditInPlace
  label="Tax ID"
  value={taxId}
  invalid={!/^\d{13}$/.test(taxId)}
  invalidText="A tax ID has 13 digits"
  onInput={(e) => setTaxId((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value)}
  onUiCancel={(e) => setTaxId(e.detail.value)}
/>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
const [taxId, setTaxId] = useState('0105556012345');

<EditInPlace label="Tax ID" value={taxId} onChange={setTaxId} invalid={!/^\d{13}$/.test(taxId)} invalidText="A tax ID has 13 digits" />
```

Delete a digit to see the error. A cancel puts the value back without an `input` event, so check again on `ui-cancel`; React + Tailwind's `onChange` gets the value put back.

## Read-only

`readonly` (`readOnly`) shows the value with an "Edit off" button instead of "Edit". A click on the field or the button opens a short note that it can't be edited. `readonly-text` (`readOnlyText`) says why, in your words.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 360px">
  <ui-edit-in-place label="Contract number" value="CT-2026-0142" readonly readonly-text="Contract numbers are set when the contract is signed"></ui-edit-in-place>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiEditInPlace label="Contract number" value="CT-2026-0142" readonly readonlyText="Contract numbers are set when the contract is signed" />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<EditInPlace label="Contract number" defaultValue="CT-2026-0142" readOnly readOnlyText="Contract numbers are set when the contract is signed" />
```

## A heading you can edit

`inherit-typography` (`inheritTypography`) makes the field take the size and weight of the text around it, so a page title can be edited as it is.


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 480px; font: var(--ui-font-heading-03)">
  <ui-edit-in-place label="Report name" value="Quarterly contract report" size="md" inherit-typography></ui-edit-in-place>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<div style={{ maxWidth: 480, font: 'var(--ui-font-heading-03)' }}>
  <UiEditInPlace label="Report name" value="Quarterly contract report" size="md" inheritTypography />
</div>
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<div className="max-w-120 type-heading-03">
  <EditInPlace label="Report name" defaultValue="Quarterly contract report" size="md" inheritTypography />
</div>
```

In a real page, put it inside the heading element itself (`<h2>`), so the heading keeps its level.

## Button names and tooltip places

The buttons' names come from the page language ("Edit", "Save", "Cancel", "Edit off"). Change them with `edit-label`, `save-label`, `cancel-label` and `readonly-label` (`editLabel`, `saveLabel`, `cancelLabel`, `readOnlyLabel` in React + Tailwind). `tooltip-placement` moves the buttons' tooltips (top by default) and `note-placement` the read-only note (bottom by default).


HTML:

```html
<div style="max-width: 360px">
  <ui-edit-in-place label="Supplier name" value="Siam Logistics" save-label="Save supplier name" cancel-label="Undo changes" tooltip-placement="bottom" edit-always-visible></ui-edit-in-place>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
<UiEditInPlace label="Supplier name" value="Siam Logistics" saveLabel="Save supplier name" cancelLabel="Undo changes" tooltipPlacement="bottom" editAlwaysVisible />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
<EditInPlace label="Supplier name" defaultValue="Siam Logistics" saveLabel="Save supplier name" cancelLabel="Undo changes" tooltipPlacement="bottom" editAlwaysVisible />
```

## Style it

The parts are `base` (the field box), `input`, `actions` (the buttons' box) and `invalid-text`. The host has `data-editing` while it is a field.


HTML:

```html
<style>
  .edit-in-place-styled::part(input) { font-weight: 600; }
  .edit-in-place-styled[data-editing]::part(base) { background: var(--ui-field-2); }
</style>
<div style="max-width: 360px">
  <ui-edit-in-place class="edit-in-place-styled" label="Owner" value="Malee S."></ui-edit-in-place>
</div>
```

React:

```tsx
// .edit-in-place-styled::part(input) { font-weight: 600; }
// .edit-in-place-styled[data-editing]::part(base) { background: var(--ui-field-2); }
<UiEditInPlace className="edit-in-place-styled" label="Owner" value="Malee S." />
```

React + Tailwind:

```tsx
// the look is in components/ui/react-tw/edit-in-place.tsx: change its classes there,
// or build your own on the Headless parts
<EditInPlace className="max-w-90" label="Owner" defaultValue="Malee S." />
```

`className` in React + Tailwind goes on the outer box, around the field and its error.

## Keyboard

| Key | While editing |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves into the field, which starts editing; then to Cancel and Save once they are enabled, then out (leaving saves a valid change, or puts the value back) |
| Enter | Saves a valid change and keeps editing. With nothing to save, stops editing; the focus stays in the field |
| Escape | Puts the value back and keeps editing |

## Accessibility

- The field is a text box named by `label`. Write a label that names the value ("Contract title"), since nothing visible does.
- `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`, and `invalid-text` is the field's description, so it is read with it.
- The buttons have names and tooltips. A press on Save or Cancel keeps the focus in the field.
- Leaving with a valid change saves it without a click. Tell people in your page's help if that could surprise them, or use a normal [text input](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/text-input/) and a Save button for values with consequences.

Unstyled React parts with the same behaviour: [Headless Edit in place](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-edit-in-place/).

## API

Generated from the package. In React, pass a property as a prop of the same name; events are props too (the React column).

### `<ui-edit-in-place>` · React `UiEditInPlace`

#### Attributes

| Attribute | Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `value` | `string` | `''` | The value (as `<input>.value`). |
| `label` | `label` | `string` | `''` | The field's accessible name (Carbon `labelText`; there is no visible label). |
| `placeholder` | `placeholder` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `size` | `size` | `EditInPlaceSize` | `'sm'` |  |
| `invalid` | `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `invalid-text` | `invalidText` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `readonly` | `readonly` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `edit-always-visible` | `editAlwaysVisible` | `boolean` | `false` | Show "Edit" without hovering. |
| `inherit-typography` | `inheritTypography` | `boolean` | `false` | The field takes the surrounding type (a heading made editable). |
| `tooltip-placement` | `tooltipPlacement` | `Placement` | `'top'` | Where the buttons' tooltips go (Carbon `tooltipAlignment`). |
| `note-placement` | `notePlacement` | `Placement` | `'bottom'` | Where the read-only note goes (Carbon `toggleTipAlignment`). |
| `edit-label` | `editLabel` | `string` | `''` | The buttons' names and the read-only note (defaults: the translation's "Edit", "Save", "Cancel", "Edit off", …). |
| `save-label` | `saveLabel` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `cancel-label` | `cancelLabel` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `readonly-label` | `readonlyLabel` | `string` | `''` |  |
| `readonly-text` | `readonlyText` | `string` | `''` |  |

#### Events

| Event | React | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | none (use a ref) |  |
| `input` | `onInput` | On every keystroke (`value` already updated) |
| `ui-save` | `onUiSave` | detail: { value } a change was saved (Save, Enter, leaving it) |
| `ui-cancel` | `onUiCancel` | detail: { value } the value was put back (Cancel, Escape, leaving it without a valid change) |

#### CSS parts

| Part | Description |
|---|---|
| `base` | The field box |
| `input` | The `<input>` |
| `actions` | The buttons' box |
| `invalid-text` | The error message |

# Headless

`@purpurabog/ui/headless` is the behaviour of the components without their look: React parts that bring Carbon's keyboard, focus, ARIA, popup placement and form submit, and render no class at all. The markup, the labels, the messages and every style are yours.

The React + Tailwind components are built on these parts, so both behave the same.

## Headless or React + Tailwind?

| Use | When |
|---|---|
| [React + Tailwind](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/installation/#react-tailwind-with-shadcn) | You want Carbon's look and to change it line by line. You start from a finished field: label, helper text, errors and sizes included. |
| Headless | You have your own design system, or a layout Carbon's components don't fit. You build the field around the parts. |

## Install

```bash
npm i @purpurabog/ui react react-dom
```

Import the parts from `@purpurabog/ui/headless`. Each component is a namespace of parts (`Dropdown.Root`, `Dropdown.Trigger`, …). There are no tokens to load: the parts have no colours of their own.

## Your first component


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Dropdown } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const types = [
  { value: 'sale', label: 'Sale' },
  { value: 'lease', label: 'Lease' },
];

export default function Example() {
  const [type, setType] = useState('');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      <Dropdown.Root items={types} name="type" onValueChange={setType}>
        <Dropdown.Label className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Contract type</Dropdown.Label>
        <Dropdown.Trigger className="group flex h-10 items-center justify-between border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-left text-sm text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-open:outline-2 data-open:-outline-offset-2 data-open:outline-focus">
          <Dropdown.Value placeholder="Choose a type" className="data-placeholder:text-ink-placeholder" />
          <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 fill-current group-data-open:rotate-180">
            <path d="M8 11 3 6l.7-.7L8 9.6l4.3-4.3.7.7z" />
          </svg>
        </Dropdown.Trigger>
        <Dropdown.Popup className="bg-layer-1 text-sm shadow-lg">
          {types.map((t) => (
            <Dropdown.Option
              key={t.value}
              value={t.value}
              className="flex h-10 cursor-pointer items-center px-4 text-ink-muted hover:bg-layer-hover-1 data-highlighted:bg-layer-hover-1 data-selected:bg-layer-selected-1 data-selected:text-ink"
            >
              {t.label}
            </Dropdown.Option>
          ))}
        </Dropdown.Popup>
      </Dropdown.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Value: {type}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`Root` holds the state and submits `name` with the form. `Trigger` gets the keys, roles and `aria-*`. `Popup` opens in the top layer and flips when there is no room.

Every popup, headless or not, is placed by one engine (`@purpurabog/ui/core`): it flips to the other side when there is no room and keeps that side while open (no jump back mid-scroll), shifts along its trigger to stay on screen but never leaves it, hides while its trigger is scrolled out of view, measures against the visible part of the screen (an on-screen keyboard, a zoom) and lands on whole pixels. A list or menu also gets `--ui-available-height`, the room left on its side. `setAnchorPositioning(true)` from `@purpurabog/ui/core` opts in to CSS anchor positioning where the browser has it: the popup's place is then written as `anchor()` offsets, so the browser itself keeps it on its trigger while a box around it scrolls. It is off by default, because inside a modal's scrolling body or a submenu Chromium still puts it a few pixels from the engine's place.

## Style on `data-*` attributes

Each part shows its state as a `data-*` attribute: present when true, absent when not. Style it with Tailwind's `data-*:` variants or with `[data-open]` in CSS:


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Dropdown } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const fruits = [
  { value: 'apple', label: 'Apple' },
  { value: 'mango', label: 'Mango' },
  { value: 'durian', label: 'Durian' },
];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      <Dropdown.Root items={fruits} name="fruit">
        <Dropdown.Label className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Fruit</Dropdown.Label>
        <Dropdown.Trigger className="flex h-10 items-center border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-left text-sm text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-open:outline-2 data-open:-outline-offset-2 data-open:outline-focus data-placeholder:text-ink-placeholder">
          <Dropdown.Value placeholder="Choose" />
        </Dropdown.Trigger>
        <Dropdown.Popup className="bg-layer-1 text-sm shadow-lg">
          {fruits.map((f) => (
            <Dropdown.Option
              key={f.value}
              value={f.value}
              className="flex h-10 cursor-pointer items-center px-4 text-ink-muted data-highlighted:bg-layer-hover-1 data-selected:font-semibold data-selected:text-ink"
            >
              {f.label}
            </Dropdown.Option>
          ))}
        </Dropdown.Popup>
      </Dropdown.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

| Attribute | Means |
|---|---|
| `data-open` | The popup, menu or panel is open (on the trigger and the popup) |
| `data-highlighted` | The row the keyboard points at in a list |
| `data-selected`, `data-checked`, `data-mixed` | Selected, checked, partly selected (Select all) |
| `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-invalid` | Field states |
| `data-placeholder` | No value chosen yet |
| `data-expanded`, `data-closing` | Expanded; sliding out (for a closing animation) |
| `data-side` | The side a popup ended up on after flipping: `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right` |

Each component's page lists the attributes of every part.

## Build your own theme switcher

There is no headless switcher. `useThemeMode` gives you what `<ui-theme-switcher>` keeps, so you can draw any control: it returns the mode (`light`, `dark` or `system`) and a function that shows, remembers and announces a new one. Every other switcher on the page, and in other tabs, follows. What it does is described in [Themes](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/themes/#let-people-pick-light-dark-or-system).


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useThemeMode } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function ThemeToggle() {
  const [mode, setMode] = useThemeMode();
  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      onClick={() => setMode(mode === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark')}
      className="h-10 bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
    >
      Theme: {mode}
    </button>
  );
}
```

| Option | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | `light`, `dark`, `system`: the mode your app owns (e.g. from a profile) | none |
| `defaultValue` | the mode to start on when nothing is remembered | what `<html data-theme>` shows, else `light` |
| `lightTheme` | `white`, `g10` | `white` |
| `darkTheme` | `g90`, `g100` | `g100` |
| `storageKey` | any key; `''` = don't remember | `ui-theme` |

To save the choice to a user's profile, pass the profile's mode as `value`: the hook shows it and remembers it.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { useThemeMode, type ThemeMode } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

interface Profile {
  theme: ThemeMode;
}

function ThemeToggle({ profile, saveProfile }: { profile: Profile | null; saveProfile: (profile: Profile) => void }) {
  // with value, the hook shows and remembers the profile's mode
  const [mode] = useThemeMode({ value: profile?.theme });
  return (
    <button
      type="button"
      onClick={() => saveProfile({ theme: mode === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark' })}
      className="h-10 bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
    >
      Theme: {mode}
    </button>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  // stands in for the profile on your server: nothing saved yet
  const [profile, setProfile] = useState<Profile | null>(null);
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
      <ThemeToggle profile={profile} saveProfile={setProfile} />
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Saved in the profile: {profile?.theme ?? 'nothing yet'}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

On a server the hook returns `defaultValue` (or light). Put `themeScript()` in `<head>` so the first paint already has the remembered theme ([Themes](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/themes/#paint-the-remembered-theme-on-the-first-frame)).

## Components

The pages in this section cover the form fields. The package has more parts than these pages yet: `Modal`, `Tabs`, `Accordion`, `ContentSwitcher`, `Menu`, `Popover`, `Tooltip`, `DefinitionTooltip`, `TreeView`, `StructuredList`, `SidePanel`, `Tearsheet`, `Notification`, `Toaster`, `Loading`, `Shell`, `Header`, `SideNav`, `DataTable`, `Pagination`, `PaginationNav`, `EditInPlace`, `Copy`, `CodeSnippet`, `TruncatedText`, `Tag`, `Card`, `ProductCard` and `ProgressIndicator`. Until they have a page, each part's props and `data-*` attributes are described in its types (your editor shows them on hover).

# Headless Text input

`TextInput` is the behaviour of the styled [Text input](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/text-input/) as unstyled React parts: an `<input>`, a button that shows or hides a password, and a mask that formats the value as the user types.

You own the markup: the label, the helper and error text, a prefix or suffix, sizes and every style. The parts set `data-*` attributes for you to style on.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { TextInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { TextInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [name, setName] = useState('');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      <TextInput.Root value={name}>
        <label htmlFor="name" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Full name</label>
        <TextInput.Input
          id="name"
          name="name"
          onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)}
          className="h-10 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
        />
      </TextInput.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Value: {name}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`type`, `value`, `defaultValue` and `disabled` go on `Root`, not on `Input`.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<TextInput.Root>
  <TextInput.Input />
  <TextInput.PasswordToggle />
</TextInput.Root>
```

## Label and helper text

The label and the message line are your own elements. Tie them to the input with `htmlFor` and `aria-describedby`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { TextInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      <TextInput.Root>
        <label htmlFor="full-name" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Full name</label>
        <TextInput.Input
          id="full-name"
          name="name"
          aria-describedby="full-name-help"
          className="h-10 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
        />
        <p id="full-name-help" className="text-xs text-ink-helper">As it appears on your ID card</p>
      </TextInput.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Passwords

With `type="password"`, `PasswordToggle` shows or hides the text. Name the button with what a press does next ("Show password", then "Hide password"); it has no `aria-pressed`. Read `visible` from `useTextInputContext()`. `onVisibleChange` runs on each press with the new state.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { TextInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

function PasswordToggle() {
  // name it with what a press does next
  const { visible } = TextInput.useTextInputContext();
  return (
    <TextInput.PasswordToggle className="shrink-0 px-4 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
      {visible ? 'Hide password' : 'Show password'}
    </TextInput.PasswordToggle>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  const [last, setLast] = useState('not pressed yet');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
      <TextInput.Root type="password" onVisibleChange={(visible) => setLast(visible ? 'shown' : 'hidden')}>
        <label htmlFor="password" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Password</label>
        <div className="flex border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1">
          <TextInput.Input
            id="password"
            name="password"
            autoComplete="current-password"
            className="h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
          />
          <PasswordToggle />
        </div>
      </TextInput.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">onVisibleChange: {last}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

For a controlled toggle, pass `visible` and update it in `onVisibleChange`.

## Masks

`mask` on `Root` formats the value as the user types: `0` is a digit, `a` a letter, `*` either, and any other character is a separator added for the user. `\` makes a pattern character a separator.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { TextInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [citizenId, setCitizenId] = useState('');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      {/* a prefix or suffix is your own markup next to the input */}
      <TextInput.Root mask="0-0000-00000-00-0">
        <label htmlFor="citizen-id" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Citizen ID</label>
        <TextInput.Input
          id="citizen-id"
          name="citizenId"
          aria-describedby="citizen-id-help"
          onChange={(_event, raw) => setCitizenId(raw)}
          className="h-10 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
        />
        <p id="citizen-id-help" className="text-xs text-ink-helper">13 digits: 0-0000-00000-00-0</p>
      </TextInput.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Raw value: {citizenId}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

- The input and the submitted form get the formatted text (`1-2345-67890-12-3`). `Input`'s `onChange` gets the value without separators (`1234567890123`) as its second argument, after the field has been reformatted.
- An edit is reformatted in place and the caret stays where it was. Nothing is reformatted while an input method is still composing.
- A `value` or `defaultValue` your code sets, raw or formatted, shows formatted.
- A mask of digits only sets `inputMode="numeric"`, unless you pass your own `inputMode`.

`TextInput` has no character counter. [Headless Text area](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-text-area/)'s `Counter` part is the one to borrow.

## Style it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { TextInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

function PasswordToggle({ className }: { className?: string }) {
  const { visible } = TextInput.useTextInputContext();
  return <TextInput.PasswordToggle className={className}>{visible ? 'Hide password' : 'Show password'}</TextInput.PasswordToggle>;
}

export default function Example() {
  const [disabled, setDisabled] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
      <TextInput.Root type="password" disabled={disabled}>
        <label htmlFor="style-password" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Password</label>
        <div className="flex border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1">
          <TextInput.Input
            id="style-password"
            className="h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled"
          />
          <PasswordToggle className="shrink-0 px-4 text-sm text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled data-visible:text-link" />
        </div>
      </TextInput.Root>
      <label className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm text-ink">
        <input type="checkbox" checked={disabled} onChange={(e) => setDisabled(e.target.checked)} />
        Disabled
      </label>
    </div>
  );
}
```
```css
input[data-disabled] { color: #a8a8a8; cursor: not-allowed; }
button[data-visible] { color: #0f62fe; }
button[data-disabled] { cursor: not-allowed; }
```

## Parts

### TextInput.Root

Renders no element; it holds the state for the other parts.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `string` | `'text'` | The input's type. `password` hides the text until `PasswordToggle` shows it. |
| `value` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` | — | The value (controlled). |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` | — | The starting value (uncontrolled). |
| `mask` | `string` | — | The format to type into. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Turns off the input and the toggle. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | — | Whether the password shows (controlled). |
| `defaultVisible` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the password shows at first. |
| `onVisibleChange` | `(visible: boolean, event) => void` | — | Each press of `PasswordToggle`, with the new state. |

### TextInput.Input

Renders an `<input>`. It takes every `<input>` prop except `type`, `value`, `defaultValue` and `disabled`, which come from `Root`.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `onChange` | `(event, raw: string) => void` | — | The change, after the mask reformatted it. `raw` is the value without separators (the value itself without a mask). |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-visible` | The type is `password` and the password shows |
| `data-disabled` | `Root` is disabled |

### TextInput.PasswordToggle

Renders a `<button type="button">`. It adds no props. It is off while `Root` is disabled or you pass `disabled`.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-visible` | The password shows |
| `data-disabled` | The button is off |

### TextInput.useTextInputContext()

Returns the state of the enclosing `Root`: `visible`, `value` (as shown, formatted), `type`, `mask` and `disabled`. Call it in a component inside `Root`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

- `Input` is a native `<input>`: Enter submits its form.
- `PasswordToggle` is a native button, so Enter and Space press it. It has `type="button"`, so it never submits the form.
- You add the `<label>`, the `aria-describedby` to the helper or error text, and `aria-invalid` when the value is wrong.
- Give the toggle a name that says what the next press does, as text or `aria-label`.
- Write the mask's format in the helper text, so people know it before they type.


---

# Headless Text area

`TextArea` is the behaviour of the styled [Text area](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/text-area/) as unstyled React parts: a `<textarea>` that can grow with its text, and a soft character or word counter. An uncontrolled area, and its counter, go back to `defaultValue` when its form resets.

You own the markup: the label, the helper and error text, the messages for a count that is near or over the limit, and every style. The parts set `data-*` attributes for you to style on.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { TextArea } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { TextArea } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [notes, setNotes] = useState('');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
      <TextArea.Root value={notes}>
        <label htmlFor="notes" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Notes</label>
        <TextArea.Input
          id="notes"
          name="notes"
          onChange={(e) => setNotes(e.target.value)}
          className="border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 py-3 text-sm leading-5 text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
        />
      </TextArea.Root>
      <p className="whitespace-pre-wrap text-xs text-ink-muted">Value: {notes}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`value` and `defaultValue` go on `Root`, not on `Input`.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<TextArea.Root>
  <TextArea.Counter />
  <TextArea.Input />
</TextArea.Root>
```

## Label and helper text

The label and the message line are your own elements. Tie them to the text area with `htmlFor` and `aria-describedby`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { TextArea } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
      <TextArea.Root>
        <label htmlFor="legal-notes" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Notes</label>
        <TextArea.Input
          id="legal-notes"
          name="notes"
          rows={4}
          aria-describedby="legal-notes-help"
          className="border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 py-3 text-sm leading-5 text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
        />
        <p id="legal-notes-help" className="text-xs text-ink-helper">Anything the legal team should know</p>
      </TextArea.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Height and auto-grow

`rows` is the native attribute: the starting height in lines. `autoGrow` on `Input` starts at `rows` and grows a line at a time with the text. `maxRows` caps it; past that, the text area scrolls. It is fitted again after each render and when its width changes.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { TextArea } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
      <TextArea.Root>
        <label htmlFor="description" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Description</label>
        <TextArea.Input
          id="description"
          name="description"
          rows={2}
          autoGrow
          maxRows={6}
          className="resize-none border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 py-3 text-sm leading-5 text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
        />
      </TextArea.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

- `autoGrow` sets the `height` and `overflow-y` inline styles. The resize handle is yours: set `resize: none` if you don't want it.
- `maxRows` is measured from the computed `line-height`, so give the text area a line-height other than `normal`.

## Count characters or words

`maxCount` on `Root` turns the counter on. It's a soft limit: typing past it isn't blocked. Past the limit, `Input` and `Counter` get `data-over`; in the last 10% before it, `Counter` gets `data-near`.

`counterMode="word"` counts words instead. Words are counted by the browser's word segmenter for `lang` (`en` by default), so Thai words count whole. Numbers don't count as words.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { TextArea } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
      {/* Counter shows "12/50"; data-near and data-over to style on */}
      <TextArea.Root maxCount={50} counterMode="word" lang="th">
        <div className="flex justify-between text-xs text-ink-muted">
          <label htmlFor="summary">Summary</label>
          <TextArea.Counter aria-hidden="true" className="data-near:font-semibold data-near:text-ink data-over:text-error-text" />
        </div>
        <TextArea.Input
          id="summary"
          name="summary"
          className="border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 py-3 text-sm leading-5 text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-over:outline-2 data-over:-outline-offset-2 data-over:outline-error"
        />
      </TextArea.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

The counter only counts: the near and over messages, and what screen readers hear, are yours. For a hard limit that stops typing, use the native `maxLength`.

## Style it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { TextArea } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
      <TextArea.Root maxCount={40}>
        <div className="flex justify-between text-xs text-ink-muted">
          <label htmlFor="style-notes">Notes</label>
          <TextArea.Counter aria-hidden="true" className="data-near:font-semibold data-near:text-ink data-over:text-error-text" />
        </div>
        <TextArea.Input
          id="style-notes"
          autoGrow
          maxRows={8}
          className="w-full resize-none border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 py-3 text-sm leading-5 text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-over:outline-2 data-over:-outline-offset-2 data-over:outline-error"
        />
      </TextArea.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```
```css
textarea { line-height: 1.25rem; resize: none; }
textarea[data-over] { outline: 2px solid #da1e28; }
.counter[data-near] { color: #8e6a00; }
.counter[data-over] { color: #da1e28; }
```

## Parts

### TextArea.Root

Renders no element; it holds the text for the counter.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` | — | The text (controlled). |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` | — | The starting text (uncontrolled). |
| `maxCount` | `number` | — | Soft limit of the counter. Without it, there is no counter. |
| `counterMode` | `'character' \| 'word'` | `'character'` | What `maxCount` counts. |
| `lang` | `string` | `'en'` | BCP 47 language the words are counted in. |

### TextArea.Input

Renders a `<textarea>`. It takes every `<textarea>` prop except `value` and `defaultValue`, which come from `Root`.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `autoGrow` | `boolean` | `false` | Grows with the text from `rows`. |
| `maxRows` | `number` | — (no cap) | The most lines `autoGrow` shows before it scrolls. |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-over` | The count is past `maxCount` |

### TextArea.Counter

Renders a `<span>` with `length/maxCount` (`12/100`), or your children instead. It renders nothing without `maxCount`. It adds no props.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-over` | The count is past `maxCount` |
| `data-near` | The count is in the last 10% before `maxCount`, and not past it |

### TextArea.useTextAreaContext()

Returns the state of the enclosing `Root`: `length`, `maxCount`, `over` and `near`. Use it to write your own counter text or message.

## Keyboard and accessibility

- `Input` is a native `<textarea>`: Enter types a new line and never submits the form.
- You add the `<label>`, the `aria-describedby` to the helper or error text, and `aria-invalid` when the text is too long.
- Hide the counter from screen readers (`aria-hidden="true"`) and announce the limit yourself, for example once in a live region when `near` or `over` turns on, not on every keystroke.


---

# Headless Number input

`NumberInput` is the behaviour of the styled [Number input](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/number-input/) as unstyled React parts: an `<input>` with − and + buttons. ↑ / ↓ step from the field. A step stays within `min` and `max` and is rounded, and each button turns off at its end of the range. With `type="text"`, the field shows the number in a locale's format while the value stays a plain number. An uncontrolled field goes back to `defaultValue` when its form resets.

You own the markup: the label, the button content and names, the helper and error text, a prefix or suffix, and every style. The parts set `data-*` attributes for you to style on.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { NumberInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { NumberInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [units, setUnits] = useState('1');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      <NumberInput.Root name="units" min={1} max={20} value={units} onValueChange={setUnits}>
        <label htmlFor="units" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Number of units</label>
        <div className="flex border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1">
          <NumberInput.Input
            id="units"
            className="h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink [appearance:textfield] focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus [&::-webkit-inner-spin-button]:appearance-none"
          />
          <NumberInput.Decrement aria-label="Decrease" className="size-10 text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled">−</NumberInput.Decrement>
          <NumberInput.Increment aria-label="Increase" className="size-10 text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled">+</NumberInput.Increment>
        </div>
      </NumberInput.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Value: {JSON.stringify(units)}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

- The value is text, so the field can be empty: `"12"`, `"0.5"`, or `""`.
- `onValueChange` gets the new value as text, not an event. It runs after typing, a step, or a blur that rounded the value.
- `name`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `disabled` and `readOnly` go on `Root`, not on `Input`.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<NumberInput.Root>
  <NumberInput.Input />
  <NumberInput.Decrement />
  <NumberInput.Increment />
  <NumberInput.HiddenInput />
</NumberInput.Root>
```

## Step, minimum and maximum

`step` (1 by default) is how far − / + and ↑ / ↓ move. A step stays within `min` and `max`, and the button at that end of the range turns off.

From an empty field, the first step goes to `stepStartValue` if you set one; otherwise to `min` when only a minimum is set, else to 1 or −1, as in Carbon.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { NumberInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [floor, setFloor] = useState('');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      <NumberInput.Root name="floor" min={1} stepStartValue={10} onValueChange={setFloor}>
        <label htmlFor="floor" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Floor</label>
        <div className="flex border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1">
          <NumberInput.Input
            id="floor"
            className="h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink [appearance:textfield] focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus [&::-webkit-inner-spin-button]:appearance-none"
          />
          <NumberInput.Decrement aria-label="Decrease" className="size-10 text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled">−</NumberInput.Decrement>
          <NumberInput.Increment aria-label="Increase" className="size-10 text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled">+</NumberInput.Increment>
        </div>
      </NumberInput.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Value: {JSON.stringify(floor)}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Decimals

A step rounds to the decimals of the value or of `step`, whichever has more, so 0.1 + 0.2 gives `0.3`. With the default `type="number"`, `step` is also the precision the browser accepts.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { NumberInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [rate, setRate] = useState('2.75');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      <NumberInput.Root name="rate" defaultValue="2.75" step={0.01} min={0} onValueChange={setRate}>
        <label htmlFor="rate" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Interest rate (% a year)</label>
        <NumberInput.Input
          id="rate"
          aria-describedby="rate-help"
          className="h-10 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
        />
        <p id="rate-help" className="text-xs text-ink-helper">↑ / ↓ step by 0.01</p>
      </NumberInput.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Value: {JSON.stringify(rate)}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Currency, units and number formats

`type="text"` with `formatOptions` formats the number with `Intl.NumberFormat`: thousands separators, currency, percent, units. The text is free while the user types and is formatted on blur; text that isn't a number stays, marked invalid, for the user to correct. The value stays a plain number: `฿1,234.50` is `1234.5`, and a percent style gives the fraction (`0.5` for 50%).


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { NumberInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [sent, setSent] = useState<Record<string, FormDataEntryValue>>();
  return (
    <form
      className="grid max-w-xs gap-2"
      onSubmit={(e) => {
        e.preventDefault();
        setSent(Object.fromEntries(new FormData(e.currentTarget)));
      }}
    >
      {/* type="text": HiddenInput submits the plain number; without locale it follows <html lang> */}
      <NumberInput.Root name="rent" type="text" locale="th-TH" defaultValue={18500} formatOptions={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'THB' }}>
        <label htmlFor="rent" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Monthly rent</label>
        <NumberInput.Input
          id="rent"
          className="h-10 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
        />
        <NumberInput.HiddenInput />
      </NumberInput.Root>
      <button
        type="submit"
        className="h-10 justify-self-start bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
      >
        Submit
      </button>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Sent: {sent ? JSON.stringify(sent) : 'nothing yet'}</p>
    </form>
  );
}
```

- Without `locale`, `type="text"` follows the page language (`<html lang>`, else the browser's).
- An invalid `locale` or `formatOptions` falls back to plain English and logs a console warning.
- A prefix or suffix (`฿`, `kg`) is your own markup next to the input.

## Empty fields and errors

There are no rules of their own for an empty field: check the value yourself. The browser's checks on the input (`required`, and `min`, `max` and `step` with `type="number"`) still run on submit, but its error bubble never shows. Instead the field gets `data-touched`, and the first invalid field of the form gets focus, so you can show your own message.

## Steppers and the mouse wheel

Leave out `Decrement` and `Increment` for a field without buttons; ↑ / ↓ still step. `disableWheel` on `Input` stops the mouse wheel from changing a focused field.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { NumberInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [year, setYear] = useState('2019');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      {/* leave out Decrement / Increment; disableWheel goes on the Input */}
      <NumberInput.Root name="year" defaultValue={2019} min={1900} max={2026} onValueChange={setYear}>
        <label htmlFor="year" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Year built</label>
        <NumberInput.Input
          id="year"
          disableWheel
          className="h-10 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
        />
      </NumberInput.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Value: {JSON.stringify(year)}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Style it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { NumberInput } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <form className="grid max-w-xs gap-2" onSubmit={(e) => e.preventDefault()}>
      <NumberInput.Root min={0} max={10}>
        <label htmlFor="qty" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Quantity</label>
        <div className="flex border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1">
          <NumberInput.Input
            id="qty"
            required
            className="h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink [appearance:textfield] focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-touched:invalid:outline-2 data-touched:invalid:-outline-offset-2 data-touched:invalid:outline-error [&::-webkit-inner-spin-button]:appearance-none"
          />
          <NumberInput.Decrement aria-label="Decrease" className="w-10 text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled">−</NumberInput.Decrement>
          <NumberInput.Increment aria-label="Increase" className="w-10 text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled">+</NumberInput.Increment>
        </div>
      </NumberInput.Root>
      <button
        type="submit"
        className="h-10 justify-self-start bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
      >
        Submit
      </button>
    </form>
  );
}
```
```css
input[data-touched]:invalid { outline: 2px solid #da1e28; }
button[data-disabled] { color: #a8a8a8; cursor: not-allowed; }
```

## Parts

### NumberInput.Root

Renders no element; it holds the value and the limits.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string \| number` | — | The value as plain number text (`''` is empty). Controlled. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| number` | — | The starting value (uncontrolled). |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | The new value after typing, a step, or a blur that rounded it. |
| `min` | `number` | — | Lowest value a step reaches. |
| `max` | `number` | — | Highest value a step reaches. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | Step of the buttons and ↑ / ↓; with `type="number"` also the precision. |
| `stepStartValue` | `number` | `0` | Where a step from an empty field starts. `0` means ±1, or `min` when only a minimum is set. |
| `type` | `'number' \| 'text'` | `'number'` | `text` formats the number for `locale`. |
| `locale` | `string` | `<html lang>`, else the browser's | BCP 47 locale of `type="text"`. |
| `formatOptions` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` | — | Format of `type="text"`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Turns off the field and the buttons. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps the value; the buttons and ↑ / ↓ do nothing. |
| `name` | `string` | — | Submitted name: on `Input` with `type="number"`, on `HiddenInput` with `type="text"`. |

### NumberInput.Input

Renders an `<input>` with `inputMode="decimal"`: a native number box with `type="number"`, a text box with `type="text"`. It takes every `<input>` prop except `type`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `min`, `max`, `step` and `name`, which come from `Root`. Your `onBlur` runs after the value settles. ↑ / ↓ don't step when your `onKeyDown` calls `preventDefault()`.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `disableWheel` | `boolean` | `false` | Ignore the mouse wheel while focused. |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-disabled` | `Root` is disabled |
| `data-readonly` | `Root` is read-only |
| `data-touched` | The field was left or stepped, or a submit found it invalid |

### NumberInput.Decrement and NumberInput.Increment

Each renders a `<button type="button">` that steps once down or up. They add no props. A button is off at its end of the range, while the field is disabled or read-only, and when you pass `disabled`. They are out of the Tab order unless you pass `tabIndex`.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-disabled` | The button is off |

### NumberInput.HiddenInput

Renders an `<input type="hidden">` with `Root`'s `name` and the plain value, only with `type="text"` and a `name`; otherwise nothing. It is disabled (not submitted) while `Root` is disabled.

### NumberInput.useNumberInputContext()

Returns the state of the enclosing `Root`, such as `value`, `number` (`NaN` while empty), `isEmpty`, `badText` (`type="text"` text that isn't a number), `touched`, `atMin`, `atMax` and `stepBy(1 | -1)`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| ↑ / ↓ | One step up or down, within `min` / `max` |
| Enter | Submits the form the field sits in, as a native input does |

- The − / + buttons are out of the Tab order, as in Carbon: the arrow keys do the same from the field. They are real buttons with `disabled` at the end of the range.
- You add the `<label>`, names for the buttons (`aria-label`), the `aria-describedby` to the helper or error text, and `aria-invalid` with your own error message.


---

# Headless Search

`Search` is the behaviour of the styled [Search](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/search/) as unstyled React parts: a `role="search"` landmark named by its label, an `<input type="search">`, a clear button, and the magnifier button of an expandable search. The parts handle Esc, where focus goes after a clear, open or close, and when the clear button is in the Tab order. An uncontrolled field goes back to `defaultValue` when its form resets.

You own the markup: the icons, how the label is hidden, the button names and every style. The parts set `data-*` attributes for you to style on.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { Search } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Search } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState('');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
      <Search.Root value={query}>
        <Search.Landmark className="grid gap-2">
          <Search.Label className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Search contracts</Search.Label>
          <div className="flex border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 hover:bg-field-hover-1">
            <Search.Input
              name="q"
              onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)}
              className="h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus [&::-webkit-search-cancel-button]:appearance-none"
            />
            <Search.Clear
              aria-label="Clear search input"
              className="size-10 text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-hidden:invisible"
            >
              ×
            </Search.Clear>
          </div>
        </Search.Landmark>
      </Search.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Value: {query}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

- `value`, `defaultValue`, `disabled` and `readOnly` go on `Root`, not on `Input`.
- Clearing empties the field with a real `input` event, so your `onChange` sees it; `onClear` runs after.
- Always render `Label`, even when you hide it: it names the landmark and the input.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Search.Root>
  <Search.Landmark>
    <Search.Label />
    <Search.Trigger /> {/* expandable only */}
    <Search.Input />
    <Search.Clear />
  </Search.Landmark>
</Search.Root>
```

## Clear the text

`Clear` empties the field and keeps focus in it. Esc in a filled field does the same. On an empty field Esc does nothing, so a dialog around the search can still close on Esc. While there is nothing to clear (the field is empty or read-only), `Clear` is out of the Tab order and has `data-hidden`; hide it with your CSS.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Search } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [cleared, setCleared] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
      <Search.Root defaultValue="Somchai" onClear={() => setCleared((n) => n + 1)}>
        <Search.Landmark className="flex border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 hover:bg-field-hover-1">
          <Search.Label className="sr-only">Search tenants</Search.Label>
          <Search.Input
            placeholder="Search tenants"
            className="h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink placeholder:text-ink-placeholder focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus [&::-webkit-search-cancel-button]:appearance-none"
          />
          {/* data-hidden while there is nothing to clear */}
          <Search.Clear
            aria-label="Clear tenant search"
            className="size-10 text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-hidden:invisible"
          >
            ×
          </Search.Clear>
        </Search.Landmark>
      </Search.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">onClear ran {cleared} times</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Expandable search

`expandable` (Carbon's `ExpandableSearch`) collapses the search to its `Trigger` until someone clicks it or presses Enter or Space; then it opens and focus moves to the field. When focus leaves an empty open search for anywhere outside its `Landmark`, it collapses. Esc on an empty open search collapses it and focuses the `Trigger`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Search } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
      <Search.Root expandable onExpandedChange={setOpen}>
        <Search.Landmark className="flex border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 data-collapsed:border-transparent data-collapsed:bg-transparent">
          <Search.Label className="sr-only">Search the table</Search.Label>
          <Search.Trigger
            aria-label="Search the table"
            className="grid size-10 shrink-0 place-items-center text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
          >
            <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 fill-current">
              <path d="m15 14.3-4.3-4.3a5.5 5.5 0 1 0-.7.7l4.3 4.3zM2 6.5a4.5 4.5 0 1 1 9 0 4.5 4.5 0 0 1-9 0" />
            </svg>
          </Search.Trigger>
          <Search.Input className="h-10 w-56 bg-transparent pe-4 text-sm text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-collapsed:w-0 data-collapsed:pe-0 [&::-webkit-search-cancel-button]:appearance-none" />
          <Search.Clear
            aria-label="Clear search input"
            className="size-10 text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-hidden:hidden"
          >
            ×
          </Search.Clear>
        </Search.Landmark>
      </Search.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Expanded: {String(open)}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

- `expanded` controls the state; `defaultExpanded` sets where it starts.
- While collapsed, `Landmark` and `Input` have `data-collapsed` and the input is out of the Tab order. Hiding or narrowing the input is your CSS.

## Style it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Search } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="max-w-sm">
      <Search.Root>
        <Search.Landmark className="group flex h-10 items-center border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 data-disabled:opacity-50">
          <Search.Label className="sr-only">Search</Search.Label>
          <Search.Input
            placeholder="Search"
            className="h-full min-w-0 flex-1 bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink placeholder:text-ink-placeholder focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus group-data-collapsed:w-0 group-data-collapsed:px-0 [&::-webkit-search-cancel-button]:appearance-none"
          />
          <Search.Clear
            aria-label="Clear search input"
            className="size-10 text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-hidden:invisible"
          >
            ×
          </Search.Clear>
        </Search.Landmark>
      </Search.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```
```css
[role="search"][data-collapsed] input { width: 0; padding: 0; }
button[data-hidden] { visibility: hidden; }
```

## Parts

### Search.Root

Renders no element; it holds the text and the open state.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inputId` | `string` | generated | The input's id. The label's id is `${inputId}-label`. |
| `value` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` | — | The text (controlled; follow the input's `onChange`). |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` | — | The starting text (uncontrolled). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Turns off the input and the buttons. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps the text: nothing to clear. |
| `onClear` | `() => void` | — | After `Clear` or Esc emptied the field. |
| `expandable` | `boolean` | `false` | Collapsed to its `Trigger` until opened. |
| `expanded` | `boolean` | — | Whether an expandable search is open (controlled). |
| `defaultExpanded` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether it starts open. |
| `onExpandedChange` | `(expanded: boolean) => void` | — | Each open or close. |

### Search.Landmark

Renders a `<div role="search">` named by `Label` (`aria-labelledby`). It adds no props.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-empty` | The field has no text |
| `data-collapsed` | An expandable search is collapsed |
| `data-disabled` | `Root` is disabled |
| `data-readonly` | `Root` is read-only |

### Search.Label

Renders a `<label>` for the input, with the id the landmark points to. You can't set its `htmlFor` or `id`.

### Search.Input

Renders an `<input type="search" autoComplete="off">`. It takes every `<input>` prop except `type`, `id`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `disabled` and `readOnly`, which come from `Root`. It has the same `data-*` attributes as `Landmark`.

### Search.Clear

Renders a `<button type="button">`. It adds no props, and takes no `disabled` (it follows `Root`). Its mousedown is cancelled, so focus stays in the field.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-hidden` | Nothing to clear: the field is empty or read-only |

### Search.Trigger

Renders a `<button type="button">` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the input. It adds no props, and takes no `disabled` (it follows `Root`). It is a Tab stop only while the search is collapsed.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-expanded` | The search is open (always, unless `expandable`) |

### Search.useSearchContext()

Returns the state of the enclosing `Root`, such as `empty`, `clearable`, `open`, `expandable`, `inputId` and `labelId`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| Esc | Clears the text and keeps focus in the field; on an empty open expandable search, collapses it and focuses the `Trigger` |
| Enter | Submits the form the search sits in, as a native input does |
| Enter or Space on the `Trigger` | Opens an expandable search; it doesn't submit the form |
| Tab | Moves to `Clear` only while there is text to clear |

- `Landmark` is a `role="search"` landmark named by `Label`, so screen reader users can jump to it.
- Carbon hides the label on screen. Hide it with a visually-hidden class, not `display: none`.
- You add names for `Clear` and `Trigger` (`aria-label`) and `aria-hidden="true"` on their icons.


---

# Headless Select

`Select` is the behaviour of the styled [Select](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/select/) as one unstyled React part: a native `<select>` with your `<option>` and `<optgroup>` children, so the browser gives the list, the keyboard and the form. On top, it adds a placeholder option, a read-only mode, `aria-invalid`, and `data-*` attributes to style on.

You own the markup: the label, the helper and error text, the arrow icon and every style. There are no sizes and no inline look: the height and layout are your CSS.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { Select } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Select } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      <label htmlFor="department" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Department</label>
      <Select.Root
        id="department"
        name="department"
        placeholder="Choose a department"
        className="h-10 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-ink data-placeholder:text-ink-placeholder"
      >
        <option value="sales">Sales</option>
        <option value="legal">Legal</option>
      </Select.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Select.Root>
  <option />
  <optgroup>
    <option />
  </optgroup>
</Select.Root>
```

## Label and helper text

The label and the message line are your own elements. Tie them to the select with `htmlFor` and `aria-describedby`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Select } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      <label htmlFor="filed-department" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Department</label>
      <Select.Root
        id="filed-department"
        name="department"
        placeholder="Choose a department"
        aria-describedby="filed-department-help"
        className="h-10 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-placeholder:text-ink-placeholder"
      >
        <option value="sales">Sales</option>
        <option value="legal">Legal</option>
        <option value="finance">Finance</option>
      </Select.Root>
      <p id="filed-department-help" className="text-xs text-ink-helper">Where the contract is filed</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Placeholder and starting value

`placeholder` adds a first, empty option (`value=""`). It is the uncontrolled choice until the user picks another, and `Root` has `data-placeholder` while it shows. With `required`, the user has to pick something else before the form submits.

Use `value` with `onChange` for a controlled select, or `defaultValue` for an uncontrolled one. `onChange` is React's own.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Select } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [currency, setCurrency] = useState('thb');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      <label htmlFor="currency" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Currency</label>
      <Select.Root
        id="currency"
        name="currency"
        value={currency}
        onChange={(e) => setCurrency(e.target.value)}
        className="h-10 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
      >
        <option value="usd">US dollar</option>
        <option value="thb">Thai baht</option>
      </Select.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Value: {currency}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Groups and disabled options

The children are plain `<option>` and `<optgroup>` elements, so `disabled` on either works as in HTML.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Select } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      <label htmlFor="office" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Office</label>
      <Select.Root
        id="office"
        name="office"
        placeholder="Choose an office"
        className="h-10 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-field-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-placeholder:text-ink-placeholder"
      >
        <optgroup label="Bangkok">
          <option value="silom">Silom</option>
          <option value="asok">Asok</option>
        </optgroup>
        <optgroup label="North">
          <option value="chiangmai">Chiang Mai</option>
          <option value="lampang" disabled>Lampang (closed)</option>
        </optgroup>
      </Select.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Read-only and disabled

`readOnly` keeps the value and sets `aria-readonly`: a press doesn't open the list, and no key changes or opens it, typed letters included. Tab and the ⌘ / Ctrl shortcuts still work. It still takes focus and submits. `disabled` is the native attribute: the select isn't submitted.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Select } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-4">
      <Select.Root
        aria-label="Department"
        defaultValue="legal"
        readOnly
        className="h-10 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-readonly:border-border-subtle-1 data-readonly:bg-transparent"
      >
        <option value="sales">Sales</option>
        <option value="legal">Legal</option>
      </Select.Root>
      <Select.Root
        aria-label="Department"
        disabled
        className="h-10 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:border-transparent data-disabled:text-ink-disabled"
      >
        <option value="sales">Sales</option>
        <option value="legal">Legal</option>
      </Select.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Style it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Select } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const states = ['invalid', 'readOnly', 'disabled'] as const;

export default function Example() {
  const [on, setOn] = useState<Record<string, boolean>>({});
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      <label htmlFor="dept" className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Department</label>
      <div className="relative">
        <Select.Root
          id="dept"
          placeholder="Choose"
          invalid={on.invalid}
          readOnly={on.readOnly}
          disabled={on.disabled}
          className="h-10 w-full appearance-none border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 pl-4 pr-10 text-sm text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-placeholder:text-ink-placeholder data-invalid:outline-2 data-invalid:-outline-offset-2 data-invalid:outline-error data-readonly:bg-transparent data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled"
        >
          <option value="hr">HR</option>
          <option value="it">IT</option>
        </Select.Root>
        <svg className="pointer-events-none absolute right-4 top-3 size-4 fill-ink" viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">
          <path d="M8 11 3 6l.7-.7L8 9.6l4.3-4.3.7.7z" />
        </svg>
      </div>
      <div className="flex gap-4 text-sm text-ink">
        {states.map((state) => (
          <label key={state} className="flex items-center gap-2">
            <input type="checkbox" checked={!!on[state]} onChange={(e) => setOn({ ...on, [state]: e.target.checked })} />
            {state}
          </label>
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```
```css
select { appearance: none; }
select[data-placeholder] { color: #6f6f6f; }
select[data-invalid] { outline: 2px solid #da1e28; }
select[data-readonly] { background: transparent; }
select[data-disabled] { color: #a8a8a8; }
```

## Parts

### Select.Root

Renders a `<select>`, with a first empty `<option>` when you set `placeholder`, then your children. It takes every `<select>` prop.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `placeholder` | `string` | — | The text of a first, empty option (`value=""`), chosen until the user picks another. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps the value: a press and the changing keys do nothing (`aria-readonly`). |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | — | Sets `aria-invalid`. Left out, there's no `aria-invalid`. |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-placeholder` | The empty placeholder option is the choice |
| `data-readonly` | `readOnly` is set |
| `data-disabled` | `disabled` is set |
| `data-invalid` | `invalid` is set |

## Keyboard and accessibility

- The control is a native `<select>`: the browser's own keys open and change it, and phones show the system picker.
