```css
nav button[data-current] { background: #0f62fe; color: #fff; font-weight: 600; }
nav :is(button, select)[data-disabled] { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }
nav select { appearance: none; color: transparent; }
nav select option { color: #161616; }
```

## Parts

### PaginationNav.Root

Renders a `<nav>`; name it with `aria-label` ("Pagination"). It takes every `<nav>` prop.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `totalItems` | `number` | — | The number of pages (Carbon's name; required) |
| `page` | `number` | — | The current page, 0-based (controlled) |
| `defaultPage` | `number` | `0` | The starting page (uncontrolled) |
| `onChange` | `(page: number) => void` | — | After the user chose a page (0-based) |
| `itemsShown` | `number` | `10` | Items in the row, the overflows included (at least 4) |
| `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | `Prev` on the first page goes to the last, `Next` on the last to the first |
| `disableOverflow` | `boolean` | `false` | The overflows can't be opened |
| `size` | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'lg'` | Only how many items fit on a window narrower than 320px (Carbon) |

### PaginationNav.Prev, PaginationNav.Next

Each renders a `<button type="button">` that moves one page back or forward; name it with `aria-label`. Disabled at the ends unless `loop`.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-disabled` | It can't move (or you set `disabled`) |

### PaginationNav.Page

Renders a `<button type="button">` that goes to its page, with `aria-current="page"` on the current one and `tabIndex={0}` (so Safari focuses it on click).

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | `number` | — | Its page, 0-based (required) |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-current` | It is the current page |
| `data-page` | Always: its page, 1-based |

### PaginationNav.Overflow

Renders a `<select>` of the hidden pages, with an empty, hidden first option, so it shows nothing: draw your "…" over it. Choosing an option goes to that page. Name it with `aria-label`.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | `number` | — | The first hidden page, 0-based (required) |
| `count` | `number` | — | How many pages it holds (required) |
| `renderPage` | `(page: number) => ReactNode` | the 1-based number | An option's text |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-disabled` | `disableOverflow` on `Root`, or you set `disabled` |

### PaginationNav.Status

Renders a `<div aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">`. Its text is yours: "Page 5 of 25", usually visually hidden.

### usePaginationNavContext()

Returns the state of the enclosing `Root`: `page` (0-based), `total`, `items`, `loop`, `disableOverflow`, `go(page)`, `step(-1 | 1)` and `stepDisabled(-1 | 1)`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

Every page, `Prev`, `Next` and overflow is a native button or select, so Tab moves through them and Enter, Space and the select's own keys work. The parts set `aria-current="page"`, `disabled` at the ends, and the polite live region.

You add:

- The landmark's name: `aria-label` on `Root`.
- Names for `Prev`, `Next` and each `Overflow` (`aria-label`), and the "…" drawn over each overflow with `aria-hidden="true"` and `pointer-events: none`.
- Words before each number for screen readers ("Page 4"), as the visually hidden text in the examples, and the `Status` text.


---

# Headless Content switcher

`ContentSwitcher` is the behaviour of the styled [Content switcher](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/content-switcher/) as unstyled React parts: a `tablist` where exactly one item is selected, one Tab stop on the selected item, the arrow keys (wrapping and skipping disabled items), Home and End, and automatic or manual selection. State shows as `data-*` attributes to style on.

You own the markup and every style: the track, the selected fill, the dividers, the icons and tooltips, and the content that changes.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { ContentSwitcher } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { ContentSwitcher } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const item =
  'flex h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center border-0 border-y border-solid border-border-inverse px-4 text-sm whitespace-nowrap text-ink-muted first:rounded-s-[4px] first:border-s last:rounded-e-[4px] last:border-e hover:bg-ghost-hover hover:text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-selected:rounded-[4px] data-selected:bg-layer-selected-inverse data-selected:text-inverse-ink data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:border-border-disabled data-disabled:text-ink-disabled';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ContentSwitcher.Root aria-label="Requests" className="flex max-w-xl">
      <ContentSwitcher.Item name="all" className={item}>All requests</ContentSwitcher.Item>
      <ContentSwitcher.Item name="mine" className={item}>Assigned to me</ContentSwitcher.Item>
      <ContentSwitcher.Item name="archived" className={item}>Archived</ContentSwitcher.Item>
    </ContentSwitcher.Root>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<ContentSwitcher.Root>
  <ContentSwitcher.Item />
  <ContentSwitcher.Item />
</ContentSwitcher.Root>
```

Each direct child of `Root` is one item, by position. `Root` reads the `name` and `disabled` props of its children, so a component of your own that wraps an `Item` must take those two props too.

## Switch the content

`onChange` gets `{ index, name }` of the item the user selected. Showing the matching content is yours; put it right after the switcher.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { ContentSwitcher } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const item =
  'flex h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center border-0 border-y border-solid border-border-inverse px-4 text-sm whitespace-nowrap text-ink-muted first:rounded-s-[4px] first:border-s last:rounded-e-[4px] last:border-e hover:bg-ghost-hover hover:text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-selected:rounded-[4px] data-selected:bg-layer-selected-inverse data-selected:text-inverse-ink';
const requests = [
  { title: 'Renew the server lease', mine: true, overdue: false },
  { title: 'Approve the catering contract', mine: false, overdue: true },
  { title: 'Sign the NDA with Siam Office Supplies', mine: true, overdue: true },
  { title: 'Review the car rental terms', mine: false, overdue: false },
];

export default function Example() {
  const [filter, setFilter] = useState('all');
  const shown = requests.filter((r) => filter === 'all' || r[filter as 'mine' | 'overdue']);
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xl gap-4">
      <ContentSwitcher.Root aria-label="Requests" onChange={({ name }) => setFilter(name)} className="flex">
        <ContentSwitcher.Item name="all" className={item}>All requests</ContentSwitcher.Item>
        <ContentSwitcher.Item name="mine" className={item}>Assigned to me</ContentSwitcher.Item>
        <ContentSwitcher.Item name="overdue" className={item}>Overdue</ContentSwitcher.Item>
      </ContentSwitcher.Root>
      <ul className="m-0 list-disc ps-6 text-sm text-ink">
        {shown.map((r) => (
          <li key={r.title}>{r.title}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled selection

Use `selectedIndex` with `onChange` for a controlled switcher, or `defaultSelectedIndex` (0 by default) for an uncontrolled one.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { ContentSwitcher } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const item =
  'flex h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center border-0 border-y border-solid border-border-inverse px-4 text-sm whitespace-nowrap text-ink-muted first:rounded-s-[4px] first:border-s last:rounded-e-[4px] last:border-e hover:bg-ghost-hover hover:text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-selected:rounded-[4px] data-selected:bg-layer-selected-inverse data-selected:text-inverse-ink';

export default function Example() {
  const [index, setIndex] = useState(1);
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xl gap-2">
      <ContentSwitcher.Root aria-label="Period" selectedIndex={index} onChange={(change) => setIndex(change.index)} className="flex">
        <ContentSwitcher.Item name="week" className={item}>This week</ContentSwitcher.Item>
        <ContentSwitcher.Item name="month" className={item}>This month</ContentSwitcher.Item>
        <ContentSwitcher.Item name="year" className={item}>This year</ContentSwitcher.Item>
      </ContentSwitcher.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Selected index: {index}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled items and manual selection

A `disabled` item gets `aria-disabled` and `data-disabled`: the arrow keys skip it, and a click does nothing. With `selectionMode="manual"` the arrow keys only move focus, and Enter or Space selects.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { ContentSwitcher } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const item =
  'flex h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center border-0 border-y border-solid border-border-inverse px-4 text-sm whitespace-nowrap text-ink-muted first:rounded-s-[4px] first:border-s last:rounded-e-[4px] last:border-e hover:bg-ghost-hover hover:text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-selected:rounded-[4px] data-selected:bg-layer-selected-inverse data-selected:text-inverse-ink data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:border-border-disabled data-disabled:text-ink-disabled data-disabled:hover:bg-transparent';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ContentSwitcher.Root aria-label="Report" selectionMode="manual" defaultSelectedIndex={1} className="flex max-w-xl">
      <ContentSwitcher.Item name="summary" className={item}>Summary</ContentSwitcher.Item>
      <ContentSwitcher.Item name="details" className={item}>Details</ContentSwitcher.Item>
      <ContentSwitcher.Item name="audit" disabled className={item}>Audit trail</ContentSwitcher.Item>
    </ContentSwitcher.Root>
  );
}
```

## Icon only

An item that shows only an icon needs a name: `aria-label` on the `Item`. Add a tooltip for sighted users; here `title` stands in for one.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { ContentSwitcher } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const item =
  'grid size-10 cursor-pointer place-items-center border-0 border-y border-solid border-border-inverse text-icon-secondary first:rounded-s-[4px] first:border-s last:rounded-e-[4px] last:border-e hover:bg-ghost-hover hover:text-icon-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-selected:rounded-[4px] data-selected:bg-layer-selected-inverse data-selected:text-icon-inverse';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ContentSwitcher.Root aria-label="Layout" className="flex">
      <ContentSwitcher.Item name="table" aria-label="Table" title="Table" className={item}>
        <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 fill-current"><path d="M13 2H3a1 1 0 0 0-1 1v10a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h10a1 1 0 0 0 1-1V3a1 1 0 0 0-1-1ZM3 7h4v2H3Zm5 0h5v2H8Zm5-4v3H3V3ZM3 10h4v3H3Zm5 3v-3h5v3Z" /></svg>
      </ContentSwitcher.Item>
      <ContentSwitcher.Item name="grid" aria-label="Grid" title="Grid" className={item}>
        <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 fill-current"><path d="M7 2H3a1 1 0 0 0-1 1v4a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h4a1 1 0 0 0 1-1V3a1 1 0 0 0-1-1Zm0 5H3V3h4Zm6-5H9a1 1 0 0 0-1 1v4a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h4a1 1 0 0 0 1-1V3a1 1 0 0 0-1-1Zm0 5H9V3h4ZM7 9H3a1 1 0 0 0-1 1v4a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h4a1 1 0 0 0 1-1v-4a1 1 0 0 0-1-1Zm0 5H3v-4h4Zm6-5H9a1 1 0 0 0-1 1v4a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h4a1 1 0 0 0 1-1v-4a1 1 0 0 0-1-1Zm0 5H9v-4h4Z" /></svg>
      </ContentSwitcher.Item>
      <ContentSwitcher.Item name="list" aria-label="List" title="List" className={item}>
        <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 fill-current"><path d="M2 4h12v1H2zm0 3.5h12v1H2zM2 11h12v1H2z" /></svg>
      </ContentSwitcher.Item>
    </ContentSwitcher.Root>
  );
}
```

## Style it

The low-contrast look: a grey track, and the selected item a light pill with bold text. The keyboard focus ring sits on the item with `focus-visible`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { ContentSwitcher } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const item =
  'flex h-8 min-w-0 flex-1 cursor-pointer items-center justify-center rounded-[4px] border-0 px-4 text-sm whitespace-nowrap text-ink-muted hover:bg-content-switcher-background-hover hover:text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-selected:bg-content-switcher-selected data-selected:font-semibold data-selected:text-ink data-selected:shadow-[inset_0_0_0_1px_var(--ui-border-inverse)] data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ContentSwitcher.Root aria-label="Requests" className="flex max-w-xl rounded-[4px] bg-content-switcher-background outline-1 -outline-offset-1 outline-hairline-strong">
      <ContentSwitcher.Item name="all" className={item}>All requests</ContentSwitcher.Item>
      <ContentSwitcher.Item name="mine" className={item}>Assigned to me</ContentSwitcher.Item>
      <ContentSwitcher.Item name="archived" disabled className={item}>Archived</ContentSwitcher.Item>
    </ContentSwitcher.Root>
  );
}
```
```css
[role='tablist'] { display: flex; border-radius: 4px; background: #e8e8e8; }
[role='tab'] { flex: 1; padding: 0 16px; color: #525252; cursor: pointer; }
[role='tab'][data-selected] { background: #fff; color: #161616; font-weight: 600; }
[role='tab'][data-disabled] { color: #a8a8a8; cursor: not-allowed; }
```

## Parts

### ContentSwitcher.Root

Renders a `<div role="tablist">` and wraps each child so it knows its position. It takes every `<div>` prop; name it with `aria-label`.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `selectedIndex` | `number` | — | The selected item's position (controlled) |
| `defaultSelectedIndex` | `number` | `0` | The starting item (uncontrolled) |
| `onChange` | `(change: { index: number; name: string }) => void` | — | After the user selects another item; `name` is the item's `name` prop, or `''` |
| `selectionMode` | `'automatic' \| 'manual'` | `'automatic'` | `automatic` selects as the arrows move; `manual` selects on Enter or Space |

### ContentSwitcher.Item

Renders a `<div role="tab">` with `aria-selected`. Only the Tab stop (the selected item, else the first enabled one) has `tabIndex={0}`. It takes every `<div>` prop.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | — | Reported in `onChange` (read by `Root`) |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | `aria-disabled`: stays visible and announced, but can't be selected or reached with the arrows |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-selected` | It is the selected item |
| `data-disabled` | `disabled` is set |

`ContentSwitcher.useContentSwitcherContext()` gives your own parts the state (`selected`, `focusable`, `count`, `selectionMode`, `select(index)`), and `ContentSwitcher.useItemIndex()` the position of the item it is called in.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| ← / → | Previous / next enabled item, wrapping (mirrored right-to-left); in automatic mode it also selects |
| Home / End | First / last enabled item |
| Enter, Space | Select the focused item |
| Tab | Leaves the switcher |

The parts set `role="tablist"`, `role="tab"`, `aria-selected`, `aria-disabled` and the roving `tabIndex`.

You add:

- A name for the group: `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on `Root`.
- `aria-label` on items that show only an icon, and a tooltip.
- The content that changes, right after the switcher. The items control no panel, so there is no `aria-controls`.


---

# Headless Tooltip

The `Tooltip` parts give you the behaviour of the styled [Tooltip](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tooltip/) with no styles: a popup in the top layer beside the element it explains, opened on hover after a short delay and on keyboard focus, closed on blur, on activation and on Esc. The pointer can move onto the popup (WCAG 1.4.13). The text describes the element, or names it with `label`.

You own the trigger element, the text, the caret and every style. The parts show their state as `data-*` attributes for you to style on.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { Tooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Tooltip.Root label="Edit contract">
      <Tooltip.Trigger className="inline-block">
        <button type="button" className="grid size-10 place-items-center text-ink hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 fill-current">
            <path d="m13.7 4.3-2-2a1 1 0 0 0-1.4 0L2 10.6V14h3.4l8.3-8.3a1 1 0 0 0 0-1.4ZM5 13H3v-2l6-6 2 2Zm7-7-2-2 1-1 2 2Z" />
          </svg>
        </button>
      </Tooltip.Trigger>
      <Tooltip.Popup className="w-max max-w-72 rounded-xs bg-inverse-surface-1 px-4 py-0.5 text-sm text-inverse-ink">Edit contract</Tooltip.Popup>
    </Tooltip.Root>
  );
}
```

`Trigger` is a `<span>` around exactly one focusable element: it watches hover, focus and activation inside it, and gives that element its name or description. The popup sits beside the element, not beside the span.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Tooltip.Root>
  <Tooltip.Trigger>
    <button type="button" />
  </Tooltip.Trigger>
  <Tooltip.Popup />
</Tooltip.Root>
```

## Describe or name

Without `label`, the popup's text is the element's accessible description (`aria-describedby`), added to any description it already has. Use it for a hint on a control that has a visible name. With `label`, the text becomes the element's `aria-label` and the popup is `aria-hidden`: use it for icon-only buttons, as in "Use it".


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Tooltip.Root placement="bottom">
      <Tooltip.Trigger className="inline-block">
        <button type="button" className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          Retention policy
        </button>
      </Tooltip.Trigger>
      <Tooltip.Popup className="w-max max-w-72 rounded-xs bg-inverse-surface-1 p-4 text-sm text-inverse-ink">Signed copies are kept for 10 years</Tooltip.Popup>
    </Tooltip.Root>
  );
}
```

## Placement and caret

`placement` takes `top` (the default), `bottom`, `left`, `right`, each with `-start` / `-end`. The popup flips when there is no room, and `data-side` says where it went. `gap` is the space to the element (8px by default).

With `caret`, the popup gets `--_caret-start`: where a caret `--_caret-w` wide (12px if unset) must start along the edge to point at the element's centre. Draw the caret yourself, as below.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const caret = [
  'pointer-events-none absolute h-1.5 w-3 bg-inherit',
  'group-data-[side=top]:top-full group-data-[side=top]:left-(--_caret-start) group-data-[side=top]:[clip-path:polygon(0_0,100%_0,50%_100%)]',
  'group-data-[side=bottom]:bottom-full group-data-[side=bottom]:left-(--_caret-start) group-data-[side=bottom]:[clip-path:polygon(50%_0,100%_100%,0_100%)]',
  'group-data-[side=left]:top-(--_caret-start) group-data-[side=left]:left-full group-data-[side=left]:h-3 group-data-[side=left]:w-1.5 group-data-[side=left]:[clip-path:polygon(0_0,100%_50%,0_100%)]',
  'group-data-[side=right]:top-(--_caret-start) group-data-[side=right]:right-full group-data-[side=right]:h-3 group-data-[side=right]:w-1.5 group-data-[side=right]:[clip-path:polygon(100%_0,0_50%,100%_100%)]',
].join(' ');

const sides = [
  { side: 'top', text: 'Opens above' },
  { side: 'bottom', text: 'Opens below' },
  { side: 'left', text: 'Opens on the left' },
  { side: 'right', text: 'Opens on the right' },
] as const;

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      {sides.map(({ side, text }) => (
        <Tooltip.Root key={side} placement={side} gap={12} caret>
          <Tooltip.Trigger className="inline-block">
            <button type="button" className="h-8 border border-interactive px-3 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
              {side}
            </button>
          </Tooltip.Trigger>
          <Tooltip.Popup className="group w-max max-w-72 overflow-visible rounded-xs bg-inverse-surface-1 p-4 text-sm text-inverse-ink">
            {text}
            <span aria-hidden="true" className={caret} />
          </Tooltip.Popup>
        </Tooltip.Root>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Delays

The popup opens 100ms after the pointer arrives (`delay`) and closes 300ms after it leaves both the element and the popup (`closeDelay`, Carbon's `leaveDelayMs`). Keyboard focus opens it at once. Raise `delay` in a dense toolbar, so tooltips don't flash while the pointer crosses it.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

function Tip({ text, delay }: { text: string; delay?: number }) {
  return (
    <Tooltip.Root delay={delay} placement="bottom">
      <Tooltip.Trigger className="inline-block">
        <button type="button" className="h-8 px-3 text-sm text-link hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          {text}
        </button>
      </Tooltip.Trigger>
      <Tooltip.Popup className="w-max rounded-xs bg-inverse-surface-1 px-4 py-0.5 text-sm text-inverse-ink">
        Opened after {delay ?? 100}ms
      </Tooltip.Popup>
    </Tooltip.Root>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      <Tip text="Default delay" />
      <Tip text="Slow (600ms)" delay={600} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Keep it open: "Copied"

Hold the state with `open` and `onOpenChange`. While your own flag is set the popup stays, whatever hover, focus, clicks and Esc report. Use it for a short confirmation. Click the number below.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { Tooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [hover, setHover] = useState(false);
  const [copied, setCopied] = useState(false);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!copied) return;
    const timer = setTimeout(() => setCopied(false), 2000);
    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  }, [copied]);
  const copy = async () => {
    await navigator.clipboard?.writeText('CN-2026-0142').catch(() => undefined);
    setCopied(true);
  };
  return (
    <Tooltip.Root open={hover || copied} onOpenChange={setHover}>
      <Tooltip.Trigger className="inline-block">
        <button type="button" onClick={copy} className="h-10 px-4 font-mono text-sm text-ink hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          CN-2026-0142
        </button>
      </Tooltip.Trigger>
      <Tooltip.Popup className="w-max rounded-xs bg-inverse-surface-1 px-4 py-0.5 text-sm text-inverse-ink">
        {copied ? 'Copied' : 'Copy contract number'}
      </Tooltip.Popup>
    </Tooltip.Root>
  );
}
```

`onOpenChange` reports changes only, so a click on a closed tooltip reports nothing. `disabled` on `Root` is the opposite case: the popup never shows (for example while the text is still loading), and hover and focus still report.

## Explain an unavailable action

A `disabled` button takes no focus, so keyboard users would never see its tooltip. Use `aria-disabled="true"` instead, ignore its clicks, and say why in the tooltip.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Tooltip.Root placement="right">
      <Tooltip.Trigger className="inline-block">
        <button
          type="button"
          aria-disabled="true"
          onClick={(e) => e.preventDefault()}
          className="h-10 cursor-not-allowed bg-button-disabled px-4 text-sm text-on-color-disabled focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus"
        >
          Sign contract
        </button>
      </Tooltip.Trigger>
      <Tooltip.Popup className="w-max max-w-72 rounded-xs bg-inverse-surface-1 p-4 text-sm text-inverse-ink">
        Only approvers can sign. Ask Ananya in Legal.
      </Tooltip.Popup>
    </Tooltip.Root>
  );
}
```

## Style it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Tooltip.Root placement="bottom" gap={12} caret>
      <Tooltip.Trigger className="group/trigger inline-block">
        <button type="button" className="h-10 border-b-2 border-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink group-data-open/trigger:border-interactive focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          Version 3
        </button>
      </Tooltip.Trigger>
      <Tooltip.Popup className="group w-max max-w-72 overflow-visible rounded-xs bg-inverse-surface-1 p-4 text-sm text-inverse-ink">
        Last changed 12 March 2026 by Somchai
        <span aria-hidden="true" className="pointer-events-none absolute bottom-full left-(--_caret-start) h-1.5 w-3 bg-inherit [clip-path:polygon(50%_0,100%_100%,0_100%)] group-data-[side=top]:top-full group-data-[side=top]:bottom-auto group-data-[side=top]:[clip-path:polygon(0_0,100%_0,50%_100%)]" />
      </Tooltip.Popup>
    </Tooltip.Root>
  );
}
```
```css
/* className="tip" on Trigger, "bubble" on Popup, "caret" on a span inside it */
.tip[data-open] button { border-bottom-color: #0f62fe; }
.bubble { width: max-content; max-width: 288px; padding: 16px; background: #393939; color: #f4f4f4; }
.caret { position: absolute; left: var(--_caret-start); width: 12px; height: 6px; background: inherit; }
.bubble[data-side='bottom'] .caret { bottom: 100%; clip-path: polygon(50% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%); }
.bubble[data-side='top'] .caret { top: 100%; clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 50% 100%); }
```

## Parts

### Tooltip.Root

Renders no element of its own: it holds the open state and the hover timer, places the popup and closes it on Esc.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | | Shown (controlled); hover and focus then only report through `onOpenChange` |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Shown at first (uncontrolled) |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | | After hover, focus, activation or Esc would change it (changes only) |
| `label` | `string` | | The text as the element's accessible name instead of its description; the popup is then `aria-hidden` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Never shows; hover and focus still report |
| `placement` | `Placement` | `'top'` | `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, each with `-start` / `-end` |
| `gap` | `number` | `8` | Space between the element and the popup, in px |
| `caret` | `boolean` | `false` | Writes `--_caret-start` on the popup |
| `delay` | `number` | `100` | Hover time before it opens, in ms |
| `closeDelay` | `number` | `300` | Time after the pointer leaves before it closes, in ms |

`Tooltip.useTooltipContext()` returns the `Root`'s state (`open`, `popupId`, `label` …) to any component inside it.

### Tooltip.Trigger

A `<span>` around the one element the tooltip explains (its first child). It watches hover, keyboard focus (`:focus-visible` only: a mouse click already had its hover), clicks and Enter / Space inside it. It adds `aria-describedby` (or with `label`, `aria-label`) to that element, and the popup is placed beside it. It takes every span prop.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-open` | The popup is showing |

### Tooltip.Popup

A `<span role="tooltip" popover="manual">` in the top layer, with the id the element's `aria-describedby` points to. Its content stays rendered while closed. The pointer can rest on it. It takes every span prop except `popover`, `id` and `role`.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-open` | Showing |
| `data-side` | `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right`: where it went |

With `caret` on `Root`, it also gets the CSS variable `--_caret-start`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus reaching the element opens the popup at once; focus leaving closes it |
| Esc | Closes the tooltip only (a surrounding dialog stays open); focus stays |
| Enter, Space | Activate the element and close the popup |

The parts set `role="tooltip"` on the popup and `aria-describedby` or `aria-label` on the element. A click closes the popup too, so it doesn't cover the result.

You add:

- A focusable element inside `Trigger`. A `<span>` or an icon on its own never gets keyboard focus.
- Nothing to click inside the popup: use [Headless Popover](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-popover/) for that.


---

# Headless Definition tooltip

The `DefinitionTooltip` parts give you the behaviour of the styled [Definition tooltip](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/definition-tooltip/) with no styles: a term that is a real button, and a popup in the top layer beside it. A click, Enter or Space toggle it; focus opens it; blur, the pointer leaving and Esc close it. The definition is also the term's description, so screen readers get it without opening.

You own the underline, the popup's look, the caret and every style. The parts show their state as `data-*` attributes for you to style on.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { DefinitionTooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { DefinitionTooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="max-w-xl text-sm text-ink">
      Choose{' '}
      <DefinitionTooltip.Root>
        <DefinitionTooltip.Trigger className="cursor-pointer border-b border-dotted border-hairline-strong hover:border-interactive focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          parallel signing
        </DefinitionTooltip.Trigger>
        <DefinitionTooltip.Popup className="max-w-44 rounded-xs bg-inverse-surface-1 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-inverse-ink">
          A signing round in which every signer receives the document at the same time.
        </DefinitionTooltip.Popup>
      </DefinitionTooltip.Root>{' '}
      when the order of signers does not matter.
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<DefinitionTooltip.Root>
  <DefinitionTooltip.Trigger />
  <DefinitionTooltip.Popup />
</DefinitionTooltip.Root>
```

## Open on hover

By default the pointer only opens the definition with a press. `openOnHover` opens it when the pointer rests on the term too. However it opened, it closes `closeDelay` (100ms) after the pointer leaves the term and the popup, so the pointer can move onto the popup.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { DefinitionTooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="max-w-xl text-sm text-ink">
      Every contract above 5 million baht needs a{' '}
      <DefinitionTooltip.Root openOnHover>
        <DefinitionTooltip.Trigger className="cursor-pointer border-b border-dotted border-hairline-strong hover:border-interactive focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          dual approval
        </DefinitionTooltip.Trigger>
        <DefinitionTooltip.Popup className="max-w-44 rounded-xs bg-inverse-surface-1 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-inverse-ink">
          A second approver from Finance, on top of the department head.
        </DefinitionTooltip.Popup>
      </DefinitionTooltip.Root>{' '}
      before it is sent.
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Placement and caret

`placement` takes `bottom` (the default), `top`, `left`, `right`, each with `-start` / `-end`. The popup flips when there is no room; `data-side` says where it went. `gap` is the space to the term (8px by default). With `caret`, the popup gets `--_caret-start`, where a caret `--_caret-w` wide (12px if unset) starts so it points at the term's centre. The styled one uses `gap={6}`, the caret's height.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { DefinitionTooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const caret = [
  'pointer-events-none absolute left-(--_caret-start) h-1.5 w-3 bg-inherit',
  'group-data-[side=bottom]:bottom-full group-data-[side=bottom]:[clip-path:polygon(50%_0,100%_100%,0_100%)]',
  'group-data-[side=top]:top-full group-data-[side=top]:[clip-path:polygon(0_0,100%_0,50%_100%)]',
].join(' ');

const terms = [
  { term: 'custodian', definition: 'The person who keeps the signed copy.', placement: 'top' },
  { term: 'reviewer', definition: 'The person who checks the terms before signing.', placement: 'bottom-start' },
] as const;

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="max-w-xl text-sm text-ink">
      {terms.map(({ term, definition, placement }) => (
        <span key={term}>
          A{' '}
          <DefinitionTooltip.Root placement={placement} gap={6} caret>
            <DefinitionTooltip.Trigger className="cursor-pointer border-b border-dotted border-hairline-strong hover:border-interactive focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
              {term}
            </DefinitionTooltip.Trigger>
            <DefinitionTooltip.Popup className="group max-w-44 overflow-visible rounded-xs bg-inverse-surface-1 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-inverse-ink">
              {definition}
              <span aria-hidden="true" className={caret} />
            </DefinitionTooltip.Popup>
          </DefinitionTooltip.Root>{' '}
          is named on every contract.{' '}
        </span>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Open state

Hold the state with `open` and `onOpenChange`, or give `defaultOpen`. `onOpenChange` reports changes only. Use it, for example, to count which terms people look up.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { DefinitionTooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2 text-sm text-ink">
      <div className="max-w-xl">
        An{' '}
        <DefinitionTooltip.Root
          open={open}
          onOpenChange={(next) => {
            setOpen(next);
            if (next) setCount((n) => n + 1);
          }}
        >
          <DefinitionTooltip.Trigger className="cursor-pointer border-b border-dotted border-hairline-strong hover:border-interactive focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
            escrow account
          </DefinitionTooltip.Trigger>
          <DefinitionTooltip.Popup className="max-w-44 rounded-xs bg-inverse-surface-1 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-inverse-ink">
            Money held by a third party until both sides meet the terms.
          </DefinitionTooltip.Popup>
        </DefinitionTooltip.Root>{' '}
        protects the deposit.
      </div>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Open: {String(open)}. Opened {count} times.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Style it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { DefinitionTooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {

          POA
        </DefinitionTooltip.Trigger>
        <DefinitionTooltip.Popup className="group max-w-44 overflow-visible rounded-xs bg-inverse-surface-1 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-inverse-ink">
          <strong>Power of attorney</strong>: who may sign on behalf of the company.
          <span aria-hidden="true" className="pointer-events-none absolute bottom-full left-(--_caret-start) h-1.5 w-3 bg-inherit [clip-path:polygon(50%_0,100%_100%,0_100%)] group-data-[side=top]:top-full group-data-[side=top]:bottom-auto group-data-[side=top]:[clip-path:polygon(0_0,100%_0,50%_100%)]" />
        </DefinitionTooltip.Popup>
      </DefinitionTooltip.Root>{' '}
      list comes from HR.
    </div>

```
```css
/* className="term" on Trigger, "definition" on Popup */
.term { border-bottom: 1px dotted #8d8d8d; cursor: pointer; }
.term:hover, .term[data-open] { border-bottom-color: #0f62fe; }
.definition { max-width: 176px; padding: 8px 16px; background: #393939; color: #f4f4f4; }
```

## Parts

### DefinitionTooltip.Root

Renders no element of its own: it holds the open state, places the popup and closes it on Esc.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | | Shown (controlled) |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Shown at first (uncontrolled) |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | | After it opens or closes (changes only) |
| `openOnHover` | `boolean` | `false` | The pointer resting on the term opens it too |
| `placement` | `Placement` | `'bottom'` | `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, each with `-start` / `-end` |
| `gap` | `number` | `8` | Space between the term and the popup, in px |
| `caret` | `boolean` | `false` | Writes `--_caret-start` on the popup |
| `closeDelay` | `number` | `100` | Time after the pointer leaves before it closes, in ms |

`DefinitionTooltip.useDefinitionTooltipContext()` returns the `Root`'s state (`open`, `popupId` …) to any component inside it.

### DefinitionTooltip.Trigger

A `<button type="button">` with `tabIndex={0}` (yours wins), `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-describedby` pointing at the popup next to any you pass. A press with the main button, Enter or Space toggle the popup; focus opens it, blur closes it. It takes every button prop except `type`.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-open` | The popup is showing |

### DefinitionTooltip.Popup

A `<span role="tooltip" popover="manual">` in the top layer (a `<span>`, as Carbon's, so the term can sit in a `<p>`). Its content stays rendered while closed, so the term's description is always there. It takes every span prop except `popover`, `id` and `role`.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-open` | Showing |
| `data-side` | `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right`: where it went |

With `caret` on `Root`, it also gets the CSS variable `--_caret-start`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Focus reaching the term opens the definition; focus leaving closes it |
| Enter, Space | Open or close the definition |
| Esc | Closes the definition only (a surrounding dialog stays open) |

The parts set `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-describedby` on the term and `role="tooltip"` on the popup.

You add:

- A look that tells the term apart from a link, such as a dotted underline.
- Nothing to click inside the popup: focus leaving the term closes it. Use [Headless Popover](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-popover/) for that.


---

# Headless Popover

The `Popover` parts give you the behaviour of the styled [Popover](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/popover/) and [Toggletip](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/toggletip/) with no styles: your own content in a popup in the top layer beside a trigger, flipped when it doesn't fit and placed again on scroll. The trigger gets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. Esc on the trigger or in the popup and a press outside close it, and after Esc focus goes back to the trigger.

You own the trigger's look, the content, the caret and every style. The parts show their state as `data-*` attributes for you to style on.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { Popover } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Popover } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const filters = ['Mine', 'Awaiting signature', 'Archived'];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Popover.Root>
      <Popover.Trigger className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus data-open:bg-interactive data-open:text-on-primary">
        Filters
      </Popover.Trigger>
      <Popover.Popup aria-label="Filter requests" className="w-60 bg-layer-1 p-4 text-sm text-ink shadow-lg">
        <p className="mb-2 font-semibold">Filter requests</p>
        {filters.map((filter) => (
          <label key={filter} className="flex items-center gap-2 py-1">
            <input type="checkbox" name="filter" value={filter} defaultChecked={filter === 'Mine'} className="size-4 accent-interactive" />
            {filter}
          </label>
        ))}
      </Popover.Popup>
    </Popover.Root>
  );
}
```

The popup's content stays rendered while it is closed, so the checkboxes keep their state. Name the popup with `aria-label`: it is a `role="group"`.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Popover.Root>
  <Popover.Trigger />
  <Popover.Popup>
    <Popover.Close />
  </Popover.Popup>
</Popover.Root>

// or with a trigger of your own
<Popover.Root>
  <Popover.Anchor>
    <YourTrigger />
    <Popover.Popup />
  </Popover.Anchor>
</Popover.Root>
```

## A form inside

`Close` is a button that closes the popup and gives focus back to the trigger. From your own code inside the popup, `dismiss('close')` from `Popover.usePopoverContext()` does the same: use it after a submit.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';
import { Popover } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

function RenameForm({ name, onSave }: { name: string; onSave: (name: string) => void }) {
  const { dismiss } = Popover.usePopoverContext();
  const save = (e: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    onSave(String(new FormData(e.currentTarget).get('name')));
    dismiss('close');
  };
  return (
    <form onSubmit={save} className="grid gap-4">
      <label className="grid gap-2 text-xs text-ink-muted">
        Contract name
        <input name="name" defaultValue={name} required className="h-10 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus" />
      </label>
      <div className="flex gap-2">
        <button type="submit" className="h-8 bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">Save</button>
        <Popover.Close className="h-8 bg-secondary px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-secondary-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">Cancel</Popover.Close>
      </div>
    </form>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  const [name, setName] = useState('Lease, Silom office');
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
      <Popover.Root placement="bottom-start">
        <Popover.Trigger className="h-8 px-3 text-sm text-link hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">Rename</Popover.Trigger>
        <Popover.Popup aria-label="Rename contract" className="w-72 bg-layer-1 p-4 shadow-lg">
          <RenameForm name={name} onSave={setName} />
        </Popover.Popup>
      </Popover.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Name: {name}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Placement and caret

`placement` takes `bottom` (the default), `top`, `left`, `right`, each with `-start` / `-end`. The popup flips when there is no room, and `data-side` says where it went. `gap` is the space to the trigger (8px by default; the styled one uses 10 with a caret, 0 without). With `caret`, the popup gets `--_caret-start`, where a caret `--_caret-w` wide (12px if unset) starts so it points at the trigger's centre.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Popover } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const caret = [
  'pointer-events-none absolute h-1.5 w-3 bg-inherit',
  'group-data-[side=top]:top-full group-data-[side=top]:left-(--_caret-start) group-data-[side=top]:[clip-path:polygon(0_0,100%_0,50%_100%)]',
  'group-data-[side=bottom]:bottom-full group-data-[side=bottom]:left-(--_caret-start) group-data-[side=bottom]:[clip-path:polygon(50%_0,100%_100%,0_100%)]',
  'group-data-[side=left]:top-(--_caret-start) group-data-[side=left]:left-full group-data-[side=left]:h-3 group-data-[side=left]:w-1.5 group-data-[side=left]:[clip-path:polygon(0_0,100%_50%,0_100%)]',
  'group-data-[side=right]:top-(--_caret-start) group-data-[side=right]:right-full group-data-[side=right]:h-3 group-data-[side=right]:w-1.5 group-data-[side=right]:[clip-path:polygon(100%_0,0_50%,100%_100%)]',
].join(' ');

const placements = [
  { placement: 'top', text: 'Opens above' },
  { placement: 'bottom-start', text: 'Lined up with the start edge' },
  { placement: 'right', text: 'Opens on the right' },
] as const;

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      {placements.map(({ placement, text }) => (
        <Popover.Root key={placement} placement={placement} gap={10} caret>
          <Popover.Trigger className="h-8 border border-interactive px-3 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
            {placement}
          </Popover.Trigger>
          <Popover.Popup aria-label={text} className="group w-max overflow-visible bg-layer-1 p-4 text-sm text-ink drop-shadow-md">
            {text}
            <span aria-hidden="true" className={caret} />
          </Popover.Popup>
        </Popover.Root>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## A trigger of your own

When the trigger is your own component, wrap it in `Anchor` instead of using `Trigger`. The popup sits beside the anchor's first element, and a press anywhere inside the anchor doesn't count as outside. Give your trigger `triggerProps` (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`) and toggle with `setOpen` from `Popover.usePopoverContext()`. `onOpenChange` tells you why it changed.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Popover } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

function AssigneeChip() {
  const { open, setOpen, triggerProps } = Popover.usePopoverContext();
  return (
    <button type="button" {...triggerProps} onClick={() => setOpen(!open, 'trigger')} className="flex h-8 items-center gap-2 rounded-full bg-layer-2 pe-3 ps-1 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-2 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
      <span aria-hidden="true" className="grid size-6 place-items-center rounded-full bg-interactive text-xs text-on-primary">AP</span>
      Ananya P.
    </button>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  const [last, setLast] = useState('none');
  const log = (open: boolean, reason: Popover.PopoverChangeReason) => setLast(`${open ? 'opened' : 'closed'} by ${reason}`);
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
      <Popover.Root onOpenChange={log}>
        <Popover.Anchor className="inline-block">
          <AssigneeChip />
          <Popover.Popup aria-label="Ananya P." className="w-64 bg-layer-1 p-4 text-sm text-ink shadow-lg">
            <p className="font-semibold">Ananya P.</p>
            <p className="text-ink-muted">Legal, Bangkok office</p>
            <p className="mt-2 text-ink-muted">3 contracts waiting for her signature</p>
          </Popover.Popup>
        </Popover.Anchor>
      </Popover.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Last change: {last}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`Popover.PopoverChangeReason` is `'trigger'`, `'escape'`, `'outside'`, `'focus-out'` or `'close'`.

## Close it yourself

`dismissible={false}` turns off Esc and the press outside: only the trigger, `Close` or your own `open` close the popup. Use it when the user must answer, such as a "what's new" hint.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Popover } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Popover.Root dismissible={false} placement="right">
      <Popover.Trigger className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Bulk signing
      </Popover.Trigger>
      <Popover.Popup aria-label="New feature" className="grid w-60 gap-2 bg-layer-1 p-4 text-sm text-ink shadow-lg">
        <p className="font-semibold">New: sign up to 50 contracts at once</p>
        <p className="text-ink-muted">Select the contracts in the list, then choose Sign.</p>
        <Popover.Close className="h-8 justify-self-start bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">Got it</Popover.Close>
      </Popover.Popup>
    </Popover.Root>
  );
}
```

## Toggletip

A toggletip is a popover behind an "i" button, closed as soon as focus moves away. `closeOnFocusOut` adds that rule: focus leaving both the trigger and the popup closes it (`focus-out`). Put the popup right after the trigger so the next Tab reaches its links. Name both the trigger and the popup.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Popover } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-1 text-sm text-ink">
      Retention period
      <Popover.Root closeOnFocusOut gap={10} caret>
        <Popover.Trigger aria-label="About the retention period" className="grid size-6 place-items-center text-ink-muted hover:text-ink aria-expanded:text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 fill-current">
            <path d="M8.5 11V6.5h-2v1h1V11H6v1h4v-1h-1.5ZM8 3.5a.75.75 0 1 0 0 1.5.75.75 0 0 0 0-1.5Z" />
            <path d="M8 15A7 7 0 1 1 8 1a7 7 0 0 1 0 14ZM8 2a6 6 0 1 0 0 12A6 6 0 0 0 8 2Z" />
          </svg>
        </Popover.Trigger>
        <Popover.Popup aria-label="About the retention period" className="group w-max max-w-72 overflow-visible bg-layer-1 p-4 text-sm text-ink drop-shadow-md">
          Signed copies are kept for 10 years.{' '}
          <a href="#toggletip" className="text-link underline focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">Read the policy</a>
          <span aria-hidden="true" className="pointer-events-none absolute bottom-full left-(--_caret-start) h-1.5 w-3 bg-inherit [clip-path:polygon(50%_0,100%_100%,0_100%)] group-data-[side=top]:top-full group-data-[side=top]:bottom-auto group-data-[side=top]:[clip-path:polygon(0_0,100%_0,50%_100%)]" />
        </Popover.Popup>
      </Popover.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Style it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Popover } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
```

```css
/* className="trigger" on Trigger, "box" on Popup */
.trigger[data-open] { background: #f4f4f4; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3); }
.box { width: 208px; padding: 16px; background: #f4f4f4; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3); }
```
