A `<section>` inside the panel, `hidden` while it is closed. Name it (`aria-label`) to make it a region landmark.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-open` | The panel is open |

### SideNav.Root

Renders no element: only its children. It holds the expanded, hover and breakpoint state.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expanded` | `boolean` | the shell's state, else `false` | Open (controlled) |
| `onToggle` | `(expanded: boolean) => void` | | Esc, the overlay or focus leaving asked for this state |
| `rail` | `boolean` | `false` | A strip of icons that opens on hover / focus |
| `fixed` | `boolean` | `false` | Always open beside the page |
| `collapsible` | `boolean` | `false` | Closed at every width until opened over the page |

`SideNav.useSideNavContext()` returns `{ expanded, hoverOpen, open, hidden, mode, rail, fixed, collapsible, large, … }`.

### SideNav.Overlay

A `<div aria-hidden="true">` that covers the page while the nav is expanded; a click on it asks to close. Show it below `lg` only.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-open` | The nav is expanded and not `fixed` |

### SideNav.Nav

A `<nav tabindex="-1">`: name it with `aria-label`. Its id is the shell's side nav id unless you pass one. Hover and focus open a rail; Esc asks to close and gives focus back to what opened it; over the page (below `lg`, or `collapsible`), focus leaving it asks to close. While neither shown nor a rail it is `inert`.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-ui-side-nav` | The mode: `default`, `rail`, `fixed` or `collapsible` |
| `data-open` | Shown at full width: expanded, a hovered rail, `fixed`, or the default nav from `lg` |
| `data-expanded` | Asked open, or a rail under the pointer or holding focus |
| `data-collapsed` | Hidden and `inert` |

### SideNav.Link

An `<a>`, out of the Tab order while the nav is hidden. It keeps `target` and `rel`.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `current` | `boolean` | `false` | The current page (`aria-current="page"`) |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-current` | `current` is set |

### SideNav.Menu, MenuTrigger, MenuPopup, MenuItem

`Menu` is an `<li>`; `MenuTrigger` a `<button type="button">` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; `MenuPopup` a `<ul>` to hide while `data-open` is absent; `MenuItem` an `<a>` with `current` (`aria-current="page"`, `data-current`).

| Prop of `Menu` | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expanded` | `boolean` | | Open (controlled) |
| `defaultExpanded` | `boolean` | `false` | Open on the first render |
| `onExpandedChange` | `(expanded: boolean) => void` | | The user opened or closed it |

| Attribute | On | When |
|---|---|---|
| `data-open` | `Menu`, `MenuTrigger`, `MenuPopup` | The menu is open |
| `data-current` | `Menu`, `MenuTrigger` | One of its items is `current` (open or closed) |

`SideNav.useMenuContext()` returns `{ expanded, current, menuId, toggle }`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | Where | Does |
|---|---|---|
| Enter, Space | `MenuButton` | Opens or closes the side nav |
| Enter, Space | `Header.MenuTrigger` | Opens or closes the menu |
| Esc | Open header menu | Closes it, focus back on its trigger |
| Esc | Open panel | Asks to close (`'escape'`), focus back on what opened it |
| Esc | Open side nav | Asks to close, focus back on what opened it |
| Tab | Out of a header menu, a panel, or a side nav over the page | Closes it (asks to) |
| Enter, Space | `SideNav.MenuTrigger` | Opens or closes the menu |

The parts set `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-pressed`, `aria-current="page"`, `inert` on a hidden nav and `tabindex="-1"` on its links, and `aria-hidden` on the overlay.

You add:

- The names: `aria-label` on `Header.Root`, the menu bar's `<nav>`, `SideNav.Nav`, `MenuButton`, each `GlobalAction` and `MenuPopup`.
- The skip link's text and a style that shows it on focus.
- The icons, with `aria-hidden="true"`.


---

# Headless Modal

The `Modal` parts give you the behaviour of the styled [Modal](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/modal/) with no styles: a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()` (the top layer, an inert page behind, Tab kept inside, focus back to the opener on close), Esc and a click outside that ask to close, Carbon's first focus, a body that becomes a focusable region when it overflows, and a page that doesn't scroll while it is open.

You own the markup, the heading text, the buttons and every style. `Root` is controlled: it reports why it wants to close, and closes only when you set `open` to false.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { Modal } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Modal } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const button = 'h-10 px-4 text-sm focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(true)} className={`${button} bg-interactive text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover`}>
        Open contract
      </button>
      <Modal.Root open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} className="m-auto w-[min(100%-2rem,42rem)] bg-layer-1 text-ink backdrop:bg-overlay open:flex open:flex-col">
        <header className="relative px-4 pt-4 pb-2 pe-12">
          <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">CT-2026-0142</p>
          <Modal.Title className="text-xl">Contract details</Modal.Title>
          <Modal.Close aria-label="Close" className="absolute end-0 top-0 grid size-12 place-items-center hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
              <path d="M24 9.4 22.6 8 16 14.6 9.4 8 8 9.4l6.6 6.6L8 22.6 9.4 24l6.6-6.6 6.6 6.6 1.4-1.4-6.6-6.6z" />
            </svg>
          </Modal.Close>
        </header>
        <Modal.Body className="px-4 pt-2 pb-12 text-sm">
          Master services agreement with Siam Logistics Co., Ltd., effective 2 October 2026.
        </Modal.Body>
        <Modal.Footer className="flex">
          <button type="button" data-kind="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)} className={`${button} h-16 flex-1 bg-secondary text-start text-on-primary hover:bg-secondary-hover`}>
            Cancel
          </button>
          <button type="button" data-kind="primary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)} className={`${button} h-16 flex-1 bg-interactive text-start text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover`}>
            Save
          </button>
        </Modal.Footer>
      </Modal.Root>
    </>
  );
}
```

`onClose(reason)` gets `'close-button'`, `'escape'`, `'backdrop'` or `'api'` (a `<form method="dialog">` inside closed the dialog). The preflight of most CSS resets removes the dialog's `margin: auto`, so put it back (`m-auto`) to centre it.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Modal.Root open={open} onClose={onClose}>
  <Modal.Title />
  <Modal.Close />
  <Modal.Body />
  <Modal.Footer />
</Modal.Root>
```

## Confirm before you delete

`alert` gives the dialog `role="alertdialog"` and makes `Body` its description. Focus then starts on the least destructive action in `Footer`: the first one whose `data-kind` is neither primary nor a danger kind. Put `data-kind` on every footer button.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Modal } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const button = 'h-10 px-4 text-sm focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [result, setResult] = useState('');
  const answer = (value: string) => {
    setResult(value);
    setOpen(false);
  };
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
      <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(true)} className={`${button} bg-button-danger text-on-primary hover:bg-error-hover`}>
        Delete contract
      </button>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Result: {result || '(none)'}</p>
      <Modal.Root open={open} alert closeOnOutsideClick={false} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} className="m-auto w-[min(100%-2rem,30rem)] bg-layer-1 text-ink backdrop:bg-overlay open:flex open:flex-col">
        <Modal.Title className="px-4 pt-4 pb-2 text-xl">Delete this contract?</Modal.Title>
        <Modal.Body className="px-4 pt-2 pb-12 text-sm">This removes CT-2026-0142 and its signatures for good.</Modal.Body>
        <Modal.Footer className="flex">
          <button type="button" data-kind="secondary" onClick={() => answer('kept')} className={`${button} h-16 flex-1 bg-secondary text-start text-on-primary hover:bg-secondary-hover`}>
            Cancel
          </button>
          <button type="button" data-kind="danger" onClick={() => answer('deleted')} className={`${button} h-16 flex-1 bg-button-danger text-start text-on-primary hover:bg-error-hover`}>
            Delete
          </button>
        </Modal.Footer>
      </Modal.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

There is no `Close` here, so Esc is the keyboard's way out.

## A form, and a click outside

On open, focus goes to an `autoFocus` control, else the first control in `Body`, else the first in `Footer`, else `Close`. A click on the backdrop asks to close (`'backdrop'`) by default; Carbon allows that only for a passive modal, so pass `closeOnOutsideClick={false}` when there are footer actions. A `<form method="dialog">` closes the dialog when it is submitted, after the browser has checked the required fields; `onClose` then gets `'api'`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Modal } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const button = 'h-16 flex-1 px-4 text-start text-sm text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus';
const field = 'h-10 w-full border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [sent, setSent] = useState<Record<string, FormDataEntryValue>>();
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
      <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(true)} className="h-10 bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Add a signer
      </button>
      {sent ? <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Added: {JSON.stringify(sent)}</p> : null}
      <Modal.Root open={open} closeOnOutsideClick={false} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} className="m-auto w-[min(100%-2rem,42rem)] bg-layer-1 text-ink backdrop:bg-overlay">
        <form method="dialog" onSubmit={(e) => setSent(Object.fromEntries(new FormData(e.currentTarget)))} className="flex flex-col">
          <Modal.Title className="px-4 pt-4 pb-2 text-xl">Add a signer</Modal.Title>
          <Modal.Body className="grid gap-4 px-4 pt-2 pb-12">
            <label className="grid gap-2 text-xs text-ink-muted">
              Full name
              <input name="name" required className={field} />
            </label>
            <label className="grid gap-2 text-xs text-ink-muted">
              Email
              <input name="email" type="email" required className={field} />
            </label>
          </Modal.Body>
          <Modal.Footer className="flex">
            <button type="button" data-kind="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)} className={`${button} bg-secondary hover:bg-secondary-hover`}>
              Cancel
            </button>
            <button type="submit" data-kind="primary" className={`${button} bg-interactive hover:bg-blue-hover`}>
              Add signer
            </button>
          </Modal.Footer>
        </form>
      </Modal.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Long content

When `Body` is taller than the room it has, it gets `tabIndex={0}` and `data-scrollable`, and the `Title` names it, so keyboard users can scroll it. Give the dialog a maximum height and let `Body` scroll.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Modal } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const clauses = Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, n) => `Clause ${n + 1}. The processor handles personal data only on the controller's written instructions and keeps it confidential.`);

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(true)} className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Read the agreement
      </button>
      <Modal.Root open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} className="m-auto max-h-[min(100%-6rem,30rem)] w-[min(100%-2rem,42rem)] bg-layer-1 text-ink backdrop:bg-overlay open:flex open:flex-col">
        <header className="relative px-4 pt-4 pb-2 pe-12">
          <Modal.Title className="text-xl">Data processing agreement</Modal.Title>
          <Modal.Close aria-label="Close" className="absolute end-0 top-0 grid size-12 place-items-center hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
              <path d="M24 9.4 22.6 8 16 14.6 9.4 8 8 9.4l6.6 6.6L8 22.6 9.4 24l6.6-6.6 6.6 6.6 1.4-1.4-6.6-6.6z" />
            </svg>
          </Modal.Close>
        </header>
        <Modal.Body className="min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto px-4 pb-8 text-sm data-scrollable:focus-visible:outline-2 data-scrollable:focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 data-scrollable:focus-visible:outline-focus">
          <div className="grid gap-4">
            {clauses.map((text) => (
              <p key={text}>{text}</p>
            ))}
          </div>
        </Modal.Body>
      </Modal.Root>
    </>
  );
}
```

`Body` watches its first child for size changes, so wrap the content in one element, as here.

## Ask before closing

`onClose` only reports. To keep the modal open, don't set `open` to false: here a first attempt with unsaved text shows a warning, and a second one closes.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Modal } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [note, setNote] = useState('');
  const [warned, setWarned] = useState(false);
  const [reason, setReason] = useState<Modal.ModalCloseReason>();
  const show = () => {
    setNote('');
    setWarned(false);
    setOpen(true);
  };
  const close = (why: Modal.ModalCloseReason) => {
    setReason(why);
    if (note && !warned) setWarned(true);
    else setOpen(false);
  };
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
      <button type="button" onClick={show} className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Edit note
      </button>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Asked to close by: {reason ?? '(nothing yet)'}</p>
      <Modal.Root open={open} onClose={close} className="m-auto w-[min(100%-2rem,42rem)] bg-layer-1 text-ink backdrop:bg-overlay open:flex open:flex-col">
        <header className="relative px-4 pt-4 pb-2 pe-12">
          <Modal.Title className="text-xl">Edit note</Modal.Title>
          <Modal.Close aria-label="Close" className="absolute end-0 top-0 grid size-12 place-items-center hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
              <path d="M24 9.4 22.6 8 16 14.6 9.4 8 8 9.4l6.6 6.6L8 22.6 9.4 24l6.6-6.6 6.6 6.6 1.4-1.4-6.6-6.6z" />
            </svg>
          </Modal.Close>
        </header>
        <Modal.Body className="grid gap-4 px-4 pt-2 pb-12">
          {warned ? (
            <p role="status" className="border-s-4 border-warning bg-notification-background-warning px-4 py-3 text-sm text-ink">
              Unsaved changes. Close again to discard them.
            </p>
          ) : null}
          <label className="grid gap-2 text-xs text-ink-muted">
            Note to the approver
            <textarea value={note} onChange={(e) => setNote(e.target.value)} rows={4} className="w-full border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 p-4 text-sm text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus" />
          </label>
        </Modal.Body>
      </Modal.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Style it

`ui-modal-motion` (React + Tailwind theme) gives it Carbon's motion: the box drops 24px in while it and the overlay fade, and fades back out after closing. A closing dialog stays on screen while it fades, so put the layout (`flex-col`) on the dialog itself and only `display` under `data-open`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Modal } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(true)} className="h-10 bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Open
      </button>
      <Modal.Root
        open={open}
        onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
        className="m-auto w-[min(100%-2rem,30rem)] bg-layer-1 text-ink backdrop:bg-overlay flex-col data-open:flex ui-modal-motion"
      >
        <header className="relative px-4 pt-4 pb-2 pe-12">
          <Modal.Title className="text-xl">Stamp duty rates</Modal.Title>
          <Modal.Close aria-label="Close" className="absolute end-0 top-0 grid size-12 place-items-center hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
              <path d="M24 9.4 22.6 8 16 14.6 9.4 8 8 9.4l6.6 6.6L8 22.6 9.4 24l6.6-6.6 6.6 6.6 1.4-1.4-6.6-6.6z" />
            </svg>
          </Modal.Close>
        </header>
        <Modal.Body className="px-4 pt-2 pb-12 text-sm">Lease contracts: 1 baht for every 1,000 baht of rent, or part of it, for the whole term.</Modal.Body>
      </Modal.Root>
    </>
  );
}
```
```css
/* className="modal" on Root, "body" on Body */
.modal[data-open] { display: flex; flex-direction: column; margin: auto; }
.modal::backdrop { background: rgb(22 22 22 / 0.5); }
.body[data-scrollable] { overflow-y: auto; }
.body[data-scrollable]:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0f62fe; outline-offset: -2px; }
```

## Parts

### Modal.Root

A `<dialog>`, opened with `showModal()` while `open` is true. It takes every dialog prop except `open`, `onClose` and `role`. While open, the page (`<html>`) doesn't scroll.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | | Shows the modal (required) |
| `onClose` | `(reason: Modal.ModalCloseReason) => void` | | Esc, `Close`, a click outside or a `<form method="dialog">` asked to close: `'escape'`, `'close-button'`, `'backdrop'`, `'api'` |
| `alert` | `boolean` | `false` | `role="alertdialog"`; `Body` describes it; focus starts on the least destructive footer action |
| `closeOnOutsideClick` | `boolean` | `true` | A press and release on the backdrop asks to close (`'backdrop'`) |

Its `aria-labelledby` is the `Title`'s id, and with `alert` its `aria-describedby` is the `Body`'s, unless you pass your own.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-open` | `open` is true |

### Modal.Title

An `<h2>` with an id (yours or `<id>-title`) that names the dialog.

### Modal.Body

A `<section>` for the content. While it overflows, it gets `tabIndex={0}` and an `aria-labelledby` pointing at the `Title`, so it is a named region the keyboard can scroll. First focus looks for a control in it first.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-scrollable` | The content is taller than the body |

### Modal.Footer

A `<footer>` for the action buttons. First focus looks here after `Body`; with `alert`, it reads the `data-kind` of its buttons (`primary`, `secondary`, `danger`, …) to start on the least destructive one.

### Modal.Close

A `<button type="button">` that asks to close (`'close-button'`). It is a Tab stop even in Safari (`tabIndex={0}`). Give it an `aria-label`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the controls inside the dialog only (the native modal dialog) |
| Esc | Calls `onClose('escape')`; the dialog stays open until you set `open` to false |

The native modal dialog makes the rest of the page inert and gives focus back to the element that had it when the dialog closes. The parts add the name from `Title`, `alertdialog` and its description, and the focusable scrolling `Body`.

You add:

- A `Title`, or an `aria-label` on `Root` when there is no visible heading.
- An `aria-label` on `Close`.
- `data-kind` on the footer buttons of an `alert` modal.


---

# Headless Side panel

The `SidePanel` parts give you the behaviour of the styled [Side panel](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/side-panel/) with no styles: a panel that slides in from the right or the left and slides out again before it unmounts, Tab kept inside it, Esc and a click on the overlay that ask to close, first focus inside and focus back on close, and a "slide-in" mode that pushes the page aside instead of covering it.

You own the markup, the heading, the buttons, where the panel sits and every style. `Root` is controlled: it reports why it wants to close, and closes only when you set `open` to false. The panel is yours to position: `fixed` under your app's header, or `absolute` inside a box, as in these examples.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { SidePanel } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { SidePanel } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const field = 'h-10 w-full border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-2 px-4 text-sm text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="relative h-96 overflow-hidden border border-hairline">
      <div className="p-4">
        <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(true)} className="h-10 bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          Edit incident
        </button>
      </div>
      <SidePanel.Root open={open} onRequestClose={() => setOpen(false)} selectorInitialFocus="#side-panel-use-title">
        <SidePanel.Overlay className="absolute inset-0 bg-overlay" />
        <SidePanel.Panel aria-labelledby="side-panel-use-heading" className="absolute inset-y-0 end-0 grid w-80 max-w-full grid-rows-[auto_1fr_auto] border-s border-border-subtle-2 bg-layer-1 text-ink shadow-lg">
          <header className="relative border-b border-border-subtle-2 p-4 pe-12">
            <h2 id="side-panel-use-heading" className="text-xl">Incident INC-2041</h2>
            <p className="text-sm text-ink-muted">Reported by the finance team.</p>
            <SidePanel.Close aria-label="Close" className="absolute end-0 top-0 grid size-10 place-items-center hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 fill-current">
                <path d="M12 4.7 11.3 4 8 7.3 4.7 4 4 4.7 7.3 8 4 11.3l.7.7L8 8.7l3.3 3.3.7-.7L8.7 8z" />
              </svg>
            </SidePanel.Close>
          </header>
          <div className="grid content-start gap-4 overflow-y-auto p-4">
            <label className="grid gap-2 text-xs text-ink-muted">
              Title
              <input id="side-panel-use-title" defaultValue="Invoice export fails" className={field} />
            </label>
            <label className="grid gap-2 text-xs text-ink-muted">
              Owner
              <input defaultValue="Ananya P." className={field} />
            </label>
          </div>
          <div className="flex border-t border-border-subtle-2">
            <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(false)} className="h-16 flex-1 bg-secondary px-4 text-start text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-secondary-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
              Cancel
            </button>
            <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(false)} className="h-16 flex-1 bg-interactive px-4 text-start text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
              Save
            </button>
          </div>
        </SidePanel.Panel>
      </SidePanel.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`onRequestClose(reason)` gets `'close-button'`, `'escape'` or `'overlay'`. On open, focus goes to `selectorInitialFocus` (a selector inside the panel), else to the panel's first control; on close it goes back to what had it. Name the panel with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<SidePanel.Root open={open} onRequestClose={onRequestClose}>
  <SidePanel.Overlay />
  <SidePanel.Panel>
    <SidePanel.Close />
  </SidePanel.Panel>
</SidePanel.Root>
```

## From the left

`placement="left"` makes the panel slide in from the left; `Panel` gets `data-placement="left"` for you to place it. Without an `Overlay` the page stays clickable beside the panel, but Tab still stays inside it.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { SidePanel } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const filters = ['Open', 'Waiting for approval', 'Closed'];

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="relative h-80 overflow-hidden border border-hairline">
      <div className="flex justify-end p-4">
        <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(true)} className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          Filters
        </button>
      </div>
      <SidePanel.Root open={open} placement="left" onRequestClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
        <SidePanel.Panel aria-label="Filters" className="absolute inset-y-0 w-64 bg-layer-1 p-4 text-ink shadow-lg data-[placement=left]:start-0 data-[placement=left]:border-e data-[placement=left]:border-border-subtle-2">
          <div className="flex items-center justify-between pb-4">
            <h2 className="text-lg">Filters</h2>
            <SidePanel.Close aria-label="Close" className="grid size-8 place-items-center hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 fill-current">
                <path d="M12 4.7 11.3 4 8 7.3 4.7 4 4 4.7 7.3 8 4 11.3l.7.7L8 8.7l3.3 3.3.7-.7L8.7 8z" />
              </svg>
            </SidePanel.Close>
          </div>
          <div className="grid gap-3">
            {filters.map((name) => (
              <label key={name} className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm">
                <input type="checkbox" className="size-4 accent-interactive" />
                {name}
              </label>
            ))}
          </div>
        </SidePanel.Panel>
      </SidePanel.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Push the page aside

`slideIn` gives the element that `selectorPageContent` points to a margin as wide as the panel, with a transition, instead of covering it. A slide-in panel takes no focus, doesn't keep Tab inside and ignores Esc, so the page stays usable beside it.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { SidePanel } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="relative h-72 overflow-hidden border border-hairline">
      <div id="side-panel-push-page" className="grid gap-4 p-4 text-sm">
        <p>Contract list: 24 contracts waiting for a signature.</p>
        <div>
          <button type="button" aria-expanded={open} onClick={() => setOpen(!open)} className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
            {open ? 'Hide summary' : 'Show summary'}
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>
      <SidePanel.Root open={open} slideIn selectorPageContent="#side-panel-push-page" onRequestClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
        <SidePanel.Panel aria-label="Summary" className="absolute inset-y-0 end-0 w-64 border-s border-border-subtle-2 bg-layer-1 p-4 text-sm text-ink">
          <h2 className="pb-2 text-lg">Summary</h2>
          <p>8 sale, 12 lease, 4 service contracts.</p>
        </SidePanel.Panel>
      </SidePanel.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Ask before closing

`onRequestClose` only reports: the panel closes when you set `open` to false. `closeOnOverlayClick={false}` stops a click on the overlay from asking at all. This panel only closes with its Done button and shows what asked.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { SidePanel } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [reason, setReason] = useState<SidePanel.SidePanelCloseReason>();
  return (
    <div className="relative h-72 overflow-hidden border border-hairline">
      <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2 p-4">
        <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(true)} className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          Open checklist
        </button>
        <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Asked to close by: {reason ?? '(nothing yet)'}</p>
      </div>
      <SidePanel.Root open={open} onRequestClose={setReason}>
        <SidePanel.Overlay className="absolute inset-0 bg-overlay" />
        <SidePanel.Panel aria-label="Signing checklist" className="absolute inset-y-0 end-0 grid w-72 grid-rows-[auto_1fr_auto] bg-layer-1 text-ink shadow-lg">
          <header className="relative p-4 pe-12">
            <h2 className="text-lg">Signing checklist</h2>
            <SidePanel.Close aria-label="Close" className="absolute end-0 top-0 grid size-10 place-items-center hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 fill-current">
                <path d="M12 4.7 11.3 4 8 7.3 4.7 4 4 4.7 7.3 8 4 11.3l.7.7L8 8.7l3.3 3.3.7-.7L8.7 8z" />
              </svg>
            </SidePanel.Close>
          </header>
          <p className="px-4 text-sm">Tick every item, then press Done.</p>
          <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(false)} className="h-16 bg-interactive px-4 text-start text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
            Done
          </button>
        </SidePanel.Panel>
      </SidePanel.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Style it

The panel slides 320px and fades with the Web Animations API (150ms in and out, as Carbon); there is nothing to animate in CSS. `data-closing` marks the panel and the overlay while they slide out, for example to stop clicks on them.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { SidePanel } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [placement, setPlacement] = useState<SidePanel.SidePanelPlacement>('right');
  const show = (side: SidePanel.SidePanelPlacement) => {
    setPlacement(side);
    setOpen(true);
  };
  return (
    <div className="relative h-72 overflow-hidden border border-hairline">
      <div className="flex justify-center gap-4 p-4">
        <button type="button" onClick={() => show('left')} className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          From the left
        </button>
        <button type="button" onClick={() => show('right')} className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          From the right
        </button>
      </div>
      <SidePanel.Root open={open} placement={placement} onRequestClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
        <SidePanel.Overlay className="absolute inset-0 bg-overlay data-closing:pointer-events-none" />
        <SidePanel.Panel
          aria-label="Vendor details"
          className="absolute inset-y-0 w-72 bg-layer-1 p-4 text-sm text-ink shadow-lg data-closing:pointer-events-none data-[placement=left]:start-0 data-[placement=left]:border-e data-[placement=right]:end-0 data-[placement=right]:border-s data-[placement=left]:border-border-subtle-2 data-[placement=right]:border-border-subtle-2"
        >
          <div className="flex items-center justify-between pb-4">
            <h2 className="text-lg">Vendor details</h2>
            <SidePanel.Close aria-label="Close" className="grid size-8 place-items-center hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 fill-current">
                <path d="M12 4.7 11.3 4 8 7.3 4.7 4 4 4.7 7.3 8 4 11.3l.7.7L8 8.7l3.3 3.3.7-.7L8.7 8z" />
              </svg>
            </SidePanel.Close>
          </div>
          <p>Siam Logistics Co., Ltd. Tax ID 0105556000000.</p>
        </SidePanel.Panel>
      </SidePanel.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```
```css
/* className="panel" on Panel, "overlay" on Overlay */
.panel { position: fixed; inset-block: 3rem 0; inline-size: 30rem; }
.panel[data-placement='right'] { inset-inline-end: 0; }
.panel[data-placement='left'] { inset-inline-start: 0; }
.panel[data-closing],
.overlay[data-closing] { pointer-events: none; }
.overlay { position: fixed; inset: 0; background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6); }
```

## Parts

### SidePanel.Root

Renders no element of its own: its children, while the panel is open and while it slides out.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | | Shows the panel (required) |
| `onRequestClose` | `(reason: SidePanel.SidePanelCloseReason) => void` | | Esc, `Close` or a click on the `Overlay` asked to close: `'escape'`, `'close-button'`, `'overlay'` |
| `placement` | `'right' \| 'left'` | `'right'` | The side it slides in from |
| `slideIn` | `boolean` | `false` | Push the page aside instead of covering it: no focus trap, no Esc, no first focus |
| `closeOnOverlayClick` | `boolean` | `true` | A click on the `Overlay` asks to close |
| `selectorInitialFocus` | `string` | | What takes focus on open (a selector inside the panel), else the first control |
| `selectorPageContent` | `string` | | The page element a `slideIn` panel pushes aside |
| `layerClassName` | `string` | | Class of the `<dialog>` the panel goes into when it opens from a modal (over it, in the top layer); give its `::backdrop` no colour (`backdrop:bg-transparent`) |

A slide-over panel joins the page's overlay stack with the modals and tearsheets: one Esc closes only the topmost (a modal opened from the panel closes first, and focus goes back into the panel), and a panel opened from a modal goes over it so it can be used.

`SidePanel.useSidePanelContext()` returns the `Root`'s state (`open`, `closing`, `placement`, `slideIn`, `requestClose` …) to any component inside it.

### SidePanel.Panel

An `<aside>` (a `complementary` landmark): what slides, and where Tab stays unless `slideIn`. Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-open` | `open` is true |
| `data-closing` | It is sliding out |
| `data-placement` | `right` or `left` |

### SidePanel.Overlay

A `<div aria-hidden="true">` that dims the page: while it is open, the page doesn't scroll (the one scroll lock the overlays share, on `<html>`: it lets go when the last overlay closes), and a click on it asks to close (`'overlay'`, unless `closeOnOverlayClick` is false). Leave it out for a panel that doesn't dim the page.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-open` | `open` is true |
| `data-closing` | It is fading out |

### SidePanel.Close

A `<button type="button">` that asks to close (`'close-button'`). Give it an `aria-label`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the panel's controls and wraps around inside it (not with `slideIn`) |
| Esc | Calls `onRequestClose('escape')` (not with `slideIn`) |

The parts move focus into the panel on open and back on close, and keep Tab inside a slide-over panel. The page behind is not made inert: screen reader users can still reach it.

You add:

- The panel's name (`aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at your heading).
- An `aria-label` on `Close`, and on any back button you add for steps.
- The panel's position and size, and a top offset under your header.


---

# Headless Tearsheet

The `Tearsheet` parts give you the behaviour of the styled [Tearsheet](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tearsheet/) with no styles: a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()` (the top layer, an inert page behind) whose sheet rises from below on open and sinks back before it unmounts, Tab kept inside the sheet, Esc, the close button and a click outside the sheet that ask to close, first focus and focus back, a page that doesn't scroll, and Carbon's stacking of tearsheets opened over each other.

You own the markup, the header, the action buttons and every style. `Root` is controlled: it reports why it wants to close, and closes only when you set `open` to false.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { Tearsheet } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Tearsheet } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const field = 'h-10 w-full border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus';
const action = 'h-20 flex-1 px-4 pt-4 text-start align-top text-sm text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(true)} className="h-10 bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        New contract
      </button>
      <Tearsheet.Root open={open} onRequestClose={() => setOpen(false)} selectorInitialFocus="#tearsheet-use-name">
        <Tearsheet.Dialog className="m-0 size-full max-h-none max-w-none bg-transparent backdrop:bg-overlay open:flex open:flex-col open:items-center open:justify-end">
          <Tearsheet.Sheet className="flex h-[calc(100%-5.5rem)] w-[calc(100%-2rem)] max-w-5xl flex-col border border-border-subtle-2 bg-layer-1 text-ink">
            <header className="relative border-b border-border-subtle-2 px-8 py-6 pe-20">
              <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Legal</p>
              <Tearsheet.Title className="text-2xl">New contract</Tearsheet.Title>
              <p className="pt-4 text-sm">Fill in the parties and the term.</p>
              <Tearsheet.Close aria-label="Close" className="absolute end-4 top-2 grid size-12 place-items-center hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
                <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
                  <path d="M24 9.4 22.6 8 16 14.6 9.4 8 8 9.4l6.6 6.6L8 22.6 9.4 24l6.6-6.6 6.6 6.6 1.4-1.4-6.6-6.6z" />
                </svg>
              </Tearsheet.Close>
            </header>
            <div className="grid flex-1 content-start gap-4 overflow-y-auto bg-canvas px-8 py-4">
              <label className="grid gap-2 text-xs text-ink-muted">
                Contract name
                <input id="tearsheet-use-name" className={field} />
              </label>
              <label className="grid gap-2 text-xs text-ink-muted">
                Counterparty
                <input className={field} />
              </label>
            </div>
            <div className="flex border-t border-border-subtle-2">
              <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(false)} className={`${action} bg-secondary hover:bg-secondary-hover`}>
                Cancel
              </button>
              <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(false)} className={`${action} bg-interactive hover:bg-blue-hover`}>
                Create
              </button>
            </div>
          </Tearsheet.Sheet>
        </Tearsheet.Dialog>
      </Tearsheet.Root>
    </>
  );
}
```

`onRequestClose(reason)` gets `'close-button'`, `'escape'` or `'outside'`. First focus goes to `selectorInitialFocus`, else `Close`, else the sheet's first control; on close it goes back to what had it. `Dialog` fills the screen and `Sheet` is the visible part: what rises, where Tab stays, and what a click counts as outside of.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Tearsheet.Root open={open} onRequestClose={onRequestClose}>
  <Tearsheet.Dialog>
    <Tearsheet.Sheet>
      <Tearsheet.Title />
      <Tearsheet.Close />
    </Tearsheet.Sheet>
  </Tearsheet.Dialog>
</Tearsheet.Root>
```

## Stacked tearsheets

A tearsheet opened over another one stacks on it. While more than one is open, `data-stack` on `Dialog` and `Sheet` says where each sits: `1-of-2`, `2-of-2`, `1-of-3` … up to three deep. Scale the ones underneath back and dim the page less, as Carbon does.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import { Tearsheet } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

function Sheet({ open, onClose, title, children }: { open: boolean; onClose: () => void; title: string; children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <Tearsheet.Root open={open} onRequestClose={onClose}>
      <Tearsheet.Dialog className="m-0 size-full max-h-none max-w-none bg-transparent backdrop:bg-overlay data-[stack=1-of-2]:backdrop:opacity-70 data-[stack=1-of-3]:backdrop:opacity-20 open:flex open:flex-col open:items-center open:justify-end">
        <Tearsheet.Sheet className="flex h-[calc(100%-5.5rem)] w-[calc(100%-2rem)] max-w-4xl flex-col border border-border-subtle-2 bg-layer-1 text-ink transition-transform data-[stack=1-of-2]:scale-95 data-[stack=1-of-3]:scale-90 data-[stack=2-of-3]:scale-95">
          <header className="relative border-b border-border-subtle-2 px-8 py-6 pe-20">
            <Tearsheet.Title className="text-2xl">{title}</Tearsheet.Title>
            <Tearsheet.Close aria-label="Close" className="absolute end-4 top-2 grid size-12 place-items-center hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
                <path d="M24 9.4 22.6 8 16 14.6 9.4 8 8 9.4l6.6 6.6L8 22.6 9.4 24l6.6-6.6 6.6 6.6 1.4-1.4-6.6-6.6z" />
              </svg>
            </Tearsheet.Close>
          </header>
          <div className="flex-1 px-8 py-4 text-sm">{children}</div>
        </Tearsheet.Sheet>
      </Tearsheet.Dialog>
    </Tearsheet.Root>
  );
}

const next = 'h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus';

export default function Example() {
  const [depth, setDepth] = useState(0);
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => setDepth(1)} className={next}>
        Open the contract
      </button>
      <Sheet open={depth >= 1} onClose={() => setDepth(0)} title="CT-2026-0142">
        <button type="button" onClick={() => setDepth(2)} className={next}>Add a party</button>
      </Sheet>
      <Sheet open={depth >= 2} onClose={() => setDepth(1)} title="Add a party">
        <button type="button" onClick={() => setDepth(3)} className={next}>Add a new company</button>
      </Sheet>
      <Sheet open={depth >= 3} onClose={() => setDepth(2)} title="New company">
        The top one. Esc closes it and shows the one below.
      </Sheet>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Ask before closing

`onRequestClose` only reports: the tearsheet closes when you set `open` to false. `closeOnOutsideClick={false}` stops a click outside the sheet from asking at all, which suits a form people type into. Type a memo, then press Esc.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Tearsheet } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [memo, setMemo] = useState('');
  const [warned, setWarned] = useState(false);
  const [reason, setReason] = useState<Tearsheet.TearsheetCloseReason>();
  const show = () => {
    setMemo('');
    setWarned(false);
    setOpen(true);
  };
  const close = (why: Tearsheet.TearsheetCloseReason) => {
    setReason(why);
    if (memo && !warned) setWarned(true);
    else setOpen(false);
  };
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
      <button type="button" onClick={show} className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Write a memo
      </button>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Asked to close by: {reason ?? '(nothing yet)'}</p>
      <Tearsheet.Root open={open} onRequestClose={close} closeOnOutsideClick={false}>
        <Tearsheet.Dialog className="m-0 size-full max-h-none max-w-none bg-transparent backdrop:bg-overlay open:flex open:flex-col open:items-center open:justify-end">
          <Tearsheet.Sheet className="flex h-[calc(100%-8rem)] w-[min(100%-2rem,40rem)] flex-col border border-border-subtle-2 bg-layer-1 text-ink">
            <header className="relative border-b border-border-subtle-2 p-4 pe-16">
              <Tearsheet.Title className="text-xl">New memo</Tearsheet.Title>
              <Tearsheet.Close aria-label="Close" className="absolute end-2 top-2 grid size-12 place-items-center hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
                <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
                  <path d="M24 9.4 22.6 8 16 14.6 9.4 8 8 9.4l6.6 6.6L8 22.6 9.4 24l6.6-6.6 6.6 6.6 1.4-1.4-6.6-6.6z" />
                </svg>
              </Tearsheet.Close>
            </header>
            <div className="grid flex-1 content-start gap-4 p-4">
              {warned ? (
                <p role="status" className="border-s-4 border-warning bg-notification-background-warning px-4 py-3 text-sm text-ink">
                  The memo isn't saved. Close again to discard it.
                </p>
              ) : null}
              <label className="grid gap-2 text-xs text-ink-muted">
                Memo
                <textarea value={memo} onChange={(e) => setMemo(e.target.value)} rows={5} className="w-full border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 p-4 text-sm text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus" />
              </label>
            </div>
          </Tearsheet.Sheet>
        </Tearsheet.Dialog>
      </Tearsheet.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Style it

The sheet rises with the Web Animations API (240ms) and sinks back on close; the backdrop fades with it. There is nothing to animate in CSS. Style the stack with `data-stack`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Tearsheet } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(true)} className="h-10 bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Signing log
      </button>
      <Tearsheet.Root open={open} onRequestClose={() => setOpen(false)}>
        <Tearsheet.Dialog className="m-0 size-full max-h-none max-w-none bg-transparent backdrop:bg-overlay data-open:flex data-open:flex-col data-open:items-center data-open:justify-end">
          <Tearsheet.Sheet className="h-[calc(100%-8rem)] w-[min(100%-2rem,36rem)] border border-border-subtle-2 bg-layer-1 text-ink data-closing:pointer-events-none">
            <header className="relative border-b border-border-subtle-2 p-4 pe-16">
              <Tearsheet.Title className="text-xl">Signing log</Tearsheet.Title>
              <Tearsheet.Close aria-label="Close" className="absolute end-2 top-2 grid size-12 place-items-center hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
                <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
                  <path d="M24 9.4 22.6 8 16 14.6 9.4 8 8 9.4l6.6 6.6L8 22.6 9.4 24l6.6-6.6 6.6 6.6 1.4-1.4-6.6-6.6z" />
                </svg>
              </Tearsheet.Close>
            </header>
            <ul className="grid gap-2 p-4 text-sm">
              <li>Ananya P. signed on 8 October 2026, 10:42.</li>
              <li>Boonmee S. signed on 9 October 2026, 14:05.</li>
            </ul>
          </Tearsheet.Sheet>
        </Tearsheet.Dialog>
      </Tearsheet.Root>
    </>
  );
}
```
```css
/* className="dialog" on Dialog, "sheet" on Sheet */
.dialog { inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%; max-inline-size: none; max-block-size: none; margin: 0; background: transparent; }
.dialog[data-open] { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: flex-end; }
.dialog::backdrop { background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6); }
.dialog[data-stack='1-of-2']::backdrop { opacity: 0.67; }
.sheet[data-stack='1-of-2'],
.sheet[data-stack='2-of-3'] { transform: scale(0.95); }
.sheet[data-stack='1-of-3'] { transform: scale(0.9); }
.sheet[data-closing] { pointer-events: none; }
```

## Parts

### Tearsheet.Root

Renders no element of its own: its children, while the tearsheet is open and while it sinks back.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | | Shows the tearsheet (required) |
| `onRequestClose` | `(reason: Tearsheet.TearsheetCloseReason) => void` | | Esc, `Close` or a click outside the sheet asked to close: `'escape'`, `'close-button'`, `'outside'` |
| `closeOnOutsideClick` | `boolean` | `true` | A press and release outside the `Sheet` asks to close |
| `selectorInitialFocus` | `string` | | What takes focus on open (a selector inside the dialog), else `Close`, else the sheet's first control |

`Tearsheet.useTearsheetContext()` returns the `Root`'s state (`open`, `closing`, `stackPlace`, `requestClose` …) to any component inside it.

### Tearsheet.Dialog

A `<dialog>`, opened with `showModal()`: style it to fill the screen, with the dim on its `::backdrop`. It takes every dialog prop except `open` and `onClose`. Its `aria-labelledby` is the `Title`'s id unless you pass your own. While a tearsheet is open, the page (`<html>`) doesn't scroll.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-open` | `open` is true |
| `data-closing` | It is sinking back |
| `data-stack` | `1-of-2`, `2-of-2`, `1-of-3`, `2-of-3` or `3-of-3` while more than one is open |

### Tearsheet.Sheet

A `<div>`: the visible sheet. It rises and sinks, Tab stays inside it, and a click outside it asks to close.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-open` | `open` is true |
| `data-closing` | It is sinking back |
| `data-stack` | As on `Dialog` |

### Tearsheet.Title

An `<h2>` with an id (yours or `<id>-title`) that names the dialog.

### Tearsheet.Close

A `<button type="button">` that asks to close (`'close-button'`). It takes first focus unless `selectorInitialFocus` says otherwise. Give it an `aria-label`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the sheet's controls and wraps around inside it |
| Esc | Calls `onRequestClose('escape')`; the tearsheet stays open until you set `open` to false |

The native modal dialog makes the rest of the page inert. The parts name it from `Title`, keep Tab inside the sheet, and move focus in on open and back on close.

You add:

- A `Title`, or an `aria-label` on `Dialog`.
- An `aria-label` on `Close`.
- The action buttons, header actions, tabs and any side pane: they are plain markup inside `Sheet`.


---

# Headless Notification

The `Notification` parts give you the behaviour of the styled [Notification](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/notification/) with no styles: the right role (`status`, none for a callout, `alertdialog` with an action), focus moved to the action of an actionable one and Tab kept going round it, Esc that closes it while focus is inside, a `timeout` that pauses while it is hovered or holds focus, and focus sent back when it closes itself.

You own the markup, the icon, the text and every style. `Root` renders nothing while the notification is closed.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { Notification } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Notification } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Notification.Root>
      <Notification.Box className="flex max-w-xl items-start gap-4 border-s-[3px] border-error bg-inverse-canvas ps-3 text-sm text-inverse-ink">
        <svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" role="img" aria-label="error icon" className="mt-3.5 size-5 shrink-0 fill-error">
          <path d="M10 1a9 9 0 1 0 0 18 9 9 0 0 0 0-18Zm3.5 13.5L10 11l-3.5 3.5L5 13l3.5-3.5L5 6l1.5-1.5L10 8l3.5-3.5L15 6l-3.5 3.5L15 13z" />
        </svg>
        <p className="flex-1 py-[15px]">
          <Notification.Title className="me-1 font-semibold">Upload failed</Notification.Title>
          <Notification.Subtitle>contract.pdf is larger than 25 MB.</Notification.Subtitle>
        </p>
        <Notification.Close aria-label="Close notification" className="grid size-12 shrink-0 place-items-center focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-inverse-ink">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
            <path d="M15 6.4 13.6 5 10 8.6 6.4 5 5 6.4 8.6 10 5 13.6 6.4 15l3.6-3.6 3.6 3.6 1.4-1.4-3.6-3.6z" />
          </svg>
        </Notification.Close>
      </Notification.Box>
    </Notification.Root>
  );
}
```

Without `open`, `Root` hides the notification itself when it closes. `Box` carries the role: `status` here, so screen readers read changes politely.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Notification.Root>
  <Notification.Box>
    <Notification.Title />
    <Notification.Subtitle />
    <Notification.Action />
    <Notification.Close />
  </Notification.Box>
</Notification.Root>
```

## With an action

`actionable` (with an `Action` inside) makes the `Box` an `alertdialog`, named by `Title` and described by `Subtitle`. When it appears, focus moves to `Action` (`autoFocus={false}` keeps it where it is); Tab and Shift+Tab go round its controls; Esc closes it while focus is inside it (`closeOnEscape={false}` turns that off). When it closes through `Close`, Esc, the timeout or `requestClose` with focus inside, focus goes back to where it was; setting `open` to false yourself doesn't move focus (nor does Carbon). `Action` doesn't close the notification: in its `onClick`, call `requestClose` from `Notification.useNotificationContext()`, which closes it the way `Close` does and sends focus back.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Notification } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

function UndoAction({ onUndo }: { onUndo: () => void }) {
  const { requestClose } = Notification.useNotificationContext();
  return (
    <Notification.Action
      onClick={() => {
        onUndo();
        requestClose('close-button');
      }}
      className="h-8 px-4 text-link-inverse hover:bg-inverse-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-inverse-ink"
    >
      Undo
    </Notification.Action>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(false);
  const [result, setResult] = useState('');
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
      <button type="button" onClick={() => { setShown(true); setResult(''); }} className="h-10 bg-button-danger px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-error-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Delete draft
      </button>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Result: {result || '(none)'}</p>
      <Notification.Root actionable open={shown} onClose={() => setShown(false)}>
        <Notification.Box className="flex max-w-xl flex-wrap items-center gap-x-4 border-s-[3px] border-info bg-inverse-canvas ps-3 text-sm text-inverse-ink">
          <p className="flex-1 py-[15px]">
            <Notification.Title className="me-1 font-semibold">Draft deleted</Notification.Title>
            <Notification.Subtitle>Lease draft for the 3rd floor.</Notification.Subtitle>
          </p>
          <UndoAction onUndo={() => setResult('restored')} />
          <Notification.Close aria-label="Close notification" className="grid size-12 place-items-center focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-inverse-ink">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
              <path d="M15 6.4 13.6 5 10 8.6 6.4 5 5 6.4 8.6 10 5 13.6 6.4 15l3.6-3.6 3.6 3.6 1.4-1.4-3.6-3.6z" />
            </svg>
          </Notification.Close>
        </Notification.Box>
      </Notification.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Callout

`variant="callout"` gives the `Box` no role: it is guidance that belongs to the page. Its `Action` is described by the `Title`. Leave out `Close` and `actionable`: a callout stays.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Notification } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Notification.Root variant="callout">
      <Notification.Box className="flex max-w-xl flex-wrap items-center gap-x-4 border border-s-[3px] border-info bg-notification-background-info ps-3 text-sm text-ink">
        <p className="flex-1 py-[15px]">
          <Notification.Title className="me-1 font-semibold">Signing closes on Friday</Notification.Title>
          <Notification.Subtitle>Two signers have not opened the document yet.</Notification.Subtitle>
        </p>
        <Notification.Action className="me-4 h-8 px-4 text-link hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          Send reminder
        </Notification.Action>
      </Notification.Box>
    </Notification.Root>
  );
}
```

## Close after a time

`timeout` closes it after that many milliseconds (`'timeout'`). The countdown pauses while the pointer is over the `Box` or focus is inside it, and an `actionable` one never closes by itself. Hover the card to hold it.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Notification } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(true);
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-4">
      <Notification.Root variant="toast" timeout={5000} open={shown} onClose={() => setShown(false)}>
        <Notification.Box className="relative w-72 border-s-[3px] border-success bg-inverse-canvas py-4 ps-3 pe-12 text-sm text-inverse-ink shadow-lg">
          <Notification.Title className="block font-semibold">Saved</Notification.Title>
          <Notification.Subtitle className="block">This closes after 5 seconds.</Notification.Subtitle>
          <Notification.Close aria-label="Close notification" className="absolute end-0 top-0 grid size-12 place-items-center focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-inverse-ink">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
              <path d="M15 6.4 13.6 5 10 8.6 6.4 5 5 6.4 8.6 10 5 13.6 6.4 15l3.6-3.6 3.6 3.6 1.4-1.4-3.6-3.6z" />
            </svg>
          </Notification.Close>
        </Notification.Box>
      </Notification.Root>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => setShown(true)} className="h-8 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Show again
      </button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Each time it shows again, the countdown starts afresh.

## Keep it open

`onClose(reason)` runs for `Close`, Esc and the timeout (`'close-button'`, `'escape'`, `'timeout'`). Return `false` to keep the notification open; with `open`, it closes only when you set `open` to false.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Notification } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [pinned, setPinned] = useState(true);
  const [reason, setReason] = useState<Notification.NotificationCloseReason>();
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
      <Notification.Root
        onClose={(why) => {
          setReason(why);
          return !pinned;
        }}
      >
        <Notification.Box className="flex max-w-xl items-start gap-4 border border-s-[3px] border-warning bg-notification-background-warning ps-3 text-sm text-ink">
          <p className="flex-1 py-[15px]">
            <Notification.Title className="me-1 font-semibold">Stamp duty unpaid</Notification.Title>
            <Notification.Subtitle>Pay it before the contract is filed.</Notification.Subtitle>
          </p>
          <Notification.Close aria-label="Close notification" className="grid size-12 shrink-0 place-items-center focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
              <path d="M15 6.4 13.6 5 10 8.6 6.4 5 5 6.4 8.6 10 5 13.6 6.4 15l3.6-3.6 3.6 3.6 1.4-1.4-3.6-3.6z" />
            </svg>
          </Notification.Close>
        </Notification.Box>
      </Notification.Root>
      <label className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm">
        <input type="checkbox" checked={pinned} onChange={(e) => setPinned(e.target.checked)} className="size-4 accent-interactive" />
        Keep it until the duty is paid
      </label>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Asked to close by: {reason ?? '(nothing yet)'}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Style it

The parts set no `data-*` attributes: the kind and the look are yours. Put the kind on the `Box` yourself, as `data-kind` here, and style on it.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Notification } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const kinds = [
  { kind: 'success', title: 'Contract signed', text: 'All parties have signed.' },
  { kind: 'info', title: 'New template', text: 'Lease 2026 is ready to use.' },
  { kind: 'warning', title: 'Expires soon', text: 'The lease ends on 31 October 2026.' },
  { kind: 'error', title: 'Payment failed', text: 'The bank declined the transfer.' },
];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      {kinds.map(({ kind, title, text }) => (
        <Notification.Root key={kind}>
          <Notification.Box
            data-kind={kind}
            className="flex max-w-xl items-start gap-4 border border-s-[3px] ps-3 text-sm text-ink data-[kind=error]:border-error data-[kind=error]:bg-notification-background-error data-[kind=info]:border-info data-[kind=info]:bg-notification-background-info data-[kind=success]:border-success data-[kind=success]:bg-notification-background-success data-[kind=warning]:border-warning data-[kind=warning]:bg-notification-background-warning"
          >
            <p className="flex-1 py-[15px]">
              <Notification.Title className="me-1 font-semibold">{title}</Notification.Title>
              <Notification.Subtitle>{text}</Notification.Subtitle>
            </p>
            <Notification.Close aria-label="Close notification" className="grid size-12 shrink-0 place-items-center focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
                <path d="M15 6.4 13.6 5 10 8.6 6.4 5 5 6.4 8.6 10 5 13.6 6.4 15l3.6-3.6 3.6 3.6 1.4-1.4-3.6-3.6z" />
              </svg>
            </Notification.Close>
          </Notification.Box>
        </Notification.Root>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```
```css
/* className="notification" and data-kind on Box */
.notification { display: flex; border-inline-start: 3px solid; }
.notification[data-kind='error'] { border-color: #da1e28; background: #fff1f1; }
.notification[data-kind='success'] { border-color: #24a148; background: #defbe6; }
.notification[role='alertdialog']:focus-within { outline: 2px solid #0f62fe; }
```

## Parts

### Notification.Root

Renders no element of its own: its children, while the notification is open. It holds the open state, moves focus, listens for Esc and runs the timeout.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | | Controlled visibility; without it the notification hides itself when it closes |
| `onClose` | `(reason: Notification.NotificationCloseReason) => boolean \| void` | | `Close`, Esc or the timeout: `'close-button'`, `'escape'`, `'timeout'`. Return `false` to keep it open |
| `variant` | `'inline' \| 'toast' \| 'callout'` | `'inline'` | A callout has no role |
| `role` | `'status' \| 'alert' \| 'log' \| 'alertdialog' \| 'none'` | | The `Box`'s role, in place of the one picked for you |
| `actionable` | `boolean` | `false` | It has an `Action`: an `alertdialog` that never closes by itself |
| `timeout` | `number` | `0` | Milliseconds before it closes itself; 0 = never |
| `closeOnEscape` | `boolean` | `true` | Esc closes an `alertdialog` one while focus is inside it |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `true` | An `alertdialog` one moves focus to its `Action` when it appears |

`Notification.useNotificationContext()` returns the `Root`'s state (`open`, `variant`, `role`, `requestClose` …) to any component inside it.

### Notification.Box

A `<div>` with the role: `status` by default, none for a callout, `alertdialog` when `actionable`, or the `role` you set (`none` gives no role). An `alertdialog` one is named by `Title`, described by `Subtitle`, and keeps Tab going round its links and buttons. The timeout pauses while it is hovered or holds focus.

### Notification.Title, Notification.Subtitle

`<span>`s with ids (yours or `<id>-title`, `<id>-subtitle`). `Title` names an `alertdialog` one and describes a callout's `Action`; `Subtitle` describes an `alertdialog` one.

### Notification.Action

A `<button type="button">`: the first focus of an `alertdialog` one, and a Tab stop even in Safari (`tabIndex={0}`). In a callout, the `Title` describes it. It doesn't close the notification.

### Notification.Close

A `<button type="button">` that asks to close (`'close-button'`). Give it an `aria-label`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift+Tab | In an `alertdialog` one, goes round its links and buttons; otherwise the page's normal order |
| Esc | Closes an `alertdialog` one while focus is inside it (`closeOnEscape`) |

The parts set the role and, for an `alertdialog`, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`.

You add:

- The status icon with a name (`role="img"` and `aria-label`, such as "error icon"), or text that says the kind.
- An `aria-label` on `Close`.
- A live region that exists before the message, for messages that must be announced: render the `Root` in the page and change its text, or use the [Toast](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-toast/) region.


---

# Headless Toast

The `Toaster` parts give you the behaviour of the styled [Toast](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/toast/) region with no styles: a queue of toasts (at most `max`, a new one closes the oldest, the same `id` replaces an open one), one polite live region that is in the page before any toast so each one is announced, placed in the top layer from the start and lifted above a modal dialog when a toast arrives while one is open.

You own the markup of each toast (usually the [Notification](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-notification/) parts), where the region sits and every style.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { Notification, Toaster } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Notification, Toaster } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

type Toast = { title: string; subtitle?: string };

// once per app: any code can add to it
const queue = new Toaster.ToastQueue<Toast>();

export default function Example() {
  const toasts = Toaster.useToasts(queue);
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => queue.add({ title: 'Contract saved', subtitle: 'CT-2026-0142' })} className="h-10 bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Save contract
      </button>
      <Toaster.Root queue={queue} aria-label="Notifications" className="pointer-events-none fixed inset-auto end-4 top-16 m-0 flex flex-col-reverse gap-2 overflow-visible bg-transparent p-0">
        {toasts.map(({ key, data }) => (
          <Notification.Root key={key} variant="toast" role="none" timeout={Toaster.toastTimeout('success')} onClose={() => queue.remove(key)}>
            <Notification.Box className="pointer-events-auto relative w-72 border-s-[3px] border-success bg-inverse-canvas py-4 ps-3 pe-12 text-sm text-inverse-ink shadow-lg">
              <Notification.Title className="block font-semibold">{data.title}</Notification.Title>
              <Notification.Subtitle className="block">{data.subtitle}</Notification.Subtitle>
              <Notification.Close aria-label="Close notification" className="absolute end-0 top-0 grid size-12 place-items-center focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-inverse-ink">
                <svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
                  <path d="M15 6.4 13.6 5 10 8.6 6.4 5 5 6.4 8.6 10 5 13.6 6.4 15l3.6-3.6 3.6 3.6 1.4-1.4-3.6-3.6z" />
                </svg>
              </Notification.Close>
            </Notification.Box>
          </Notification.Root>
        ))}
      </Toaster.Root>
    </>
  );
}
```

Each toast is a `Notification` with `role="none"`, because the region announces it; remove it from the queue in its `onClose`. `Root` is a `popover`, so it sits in the top layer: place it with `fixed` and reset the popover's `inset`, `margin` and background, as here.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Toaster.Root queue={queue} aria-label="Notifications">
  <Notification.Root>
    <Notification.Box>
      <Notification.Title />
      <Notification.Subtitle />
      <Notification.Close />
    </Notification.Box>
  </Notification.Root>
</Toaster.Root>
```

## Kinds and how long they stay

`Toaster.toastTimeout(kind, timeout?)` is the rule the styled toaster uses: the `timeout` you give, else 5 seconds for info and success and 0 (stays until closed) for error and warning.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Notification, Toaster } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

type Kind = 'success' | 'info' | 'warning' | 'error';
type Toast = { kind: Kind; title: string };

const queue = new Toaster.ToastQueue<Toast>();
const border: Record<Kind, string> = { success: 'border-success', info: 'border-info', warning: 'border-warning', error: 'border-error' };
const samples: Toast[] = [
  { kind: 'success', title: 'Approval sent' },
  { kind: 'info', title: 'New template ready' },
  { kind: 'warning', title: 'Stamp duty unpaid' },
  { kind: 'error', title: 'Could not save' },
];

export default function Example() {
  const toasts = Toaster.useToasts(queue);
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
      {samples.map((toast) => (
        <button key={toast.kind} type="button" onClick={() => queue.add(toast)} className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive capitalize hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          {toast.kind}
        </button>
      ))}
      <Toaster.Root queue={queue} aria-label="Notifications" className="pointer-events-none fixed inset-auto end-4 top-16 m-0 flex flex-col-reverse gap-2 overflow-visible bg-transparent p-0">
        {toasts.map(({ key, data }) => (
          <Notification.Root key={key} variant="toast" role="none" timeout={Toaster.toastTimeout(data.kind)} onClose={() => queue.remove(key)}>
            <Notification.Box className={`pointer-events-auto relative w-72 border-s-[3px] ${border[data.kind]} bg-inverse-canvas py-4 ps-3 pe-12 text-sm text-inverse-ink shadow-lg`}>
              <Notification.Title className="block font-semibold">{data.title}</Notification.Title>
              <Notification.Subtitle className="block text-inverse-ink-muted">{Toaster.toastTimeout(data.kind) ? 'Closes after 5 seconds.' : 'Stays until you close it.'}</Notification.Subtitle>
              <Notification.Close aria-label="Close notification" className="absolute end-0 top-0 grid size-12 place-items-center focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-inverse-ink">
                <svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
                  <path d="M15 6.4 13.6 5 10 8.6 6.4 5 5 6.4 8.6 10 5 13.6 6.4 15l3.6-3.6 3.6 3.6 1.4-1.4-3.6-3.6z" />
                </svg>
              </Notification.Close>
            </Notification.Box>
          </Notification.Root>
        ))}
      </Toaster.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Replace, and how many at once

`queue.add(data, id)` replaces an open toast with the same `id` instead of stacking another: "Syncing…", then "Synced". `queue.max` (3 by default) is how many show at once; a new toast drops the oldest. `queue.remove(key)` and `queue.clear()` take toasts away.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Notification, Toaster } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

type Toast = { title: string; done?: boolean };

const queue = new Toaster.ToastQueue<Toast>();
queue.max = 2;
let signers = 0;

export default function Example() {
  const toasts = Toaster.useToasts(queue);
  const sync = () => {
    queue.add({ title: 'Syncing…' }, 'sync');
    setTimeout(() => queue.add({ title: 'Synced', done: true }, 'sync'), 2000);
  };
  const addSigner = () => {
    signers += 1;
    queue.add({ title: `Signer ${signers} added`, done: true });
  };
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
      <button type="button" onClick={sync} className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Sync contracts
      </button>
      <button type="button" onClick={addSigner} className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Add a signer
      </button>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => queue.clear()} className="h-10 px-4 text-sm text-link hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Clear all
      </button>
      <Toaster.Root queue={queue} aria-label="Notifications" className="pointer-events-none fixed inset-auto end-4 top-16 m-0 flex flex-col-reverse gap-2 overflow-visible bg-transparent p-0">
        {toasts.map(({ key, data }) => (
          <Notification.Root key={key} variant="toast" role="none" timeout={data.done ? 5000 : 0} onClose={() => queue.remove(key)}>
            <Notification.Box className="pointer-events-auto relative w-72 border-s-[3px] border-info bg-inverse-canvas py-4 ps-3 pe-12 text-sm text-inverse-ink shadow-lg">
              <Notification.Title className="block font-semibold">{data.title}</Notification.Title>
              <Notification.Close aria-label="Close notification" className="absolute end-0 top-0 grid size-12 place-items-center focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-inverse-ink">
                <svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
                  <path d="M15 6.4 13.6 5 10 8.6 6.4 5 5 6.4 8.6 10 5 13.6 6.4 15l3.6-3.6 3.6 3.6 1.4-1.4-3.6-3.6z" />
                </svg>
              </Notification.Close>
            </Notification.Box>
          </Notification.Root>
        ))}
      </Toaster.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`queue.add` returns the toast's `key`. A new key each time also gives the `Notification` a fresh start, so a replaced toast's timeout starts again.

## With an action

Leave out `role="none"` and pass `actionable` for a toast with an action: it keeps its `alertdialog` role, takes focus, keeps Tab inside and never closes by itself. Use it only when the action is worth that interruption.


React (live React example):

