```tsx
import { Notification, Toaster } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

type Toast = { title: string; retry?: boolean };

const queue = new Toaster.ToastQueue<Toast>();

function RetryAction() {
  const { requestClose } = Notification.useNotificationContext();
  return (
    <Notification.Action
      onClick={() => {
        requestClose('close-button');
        queue.add({ title: 'Retrying…' });
      }}
      className="ms-0 mt-4 h-8 border border-notification-action-tertiary-inverse px-4 text-notification-action-tertiary-inverse hover:bg-notification-action-tertiary-inverse-hover hover:text-notification-action-tertiary-inverse-text focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-inverse-ink"
    >
      Retry
    </Notification.Action>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  const toasts = Toaster.useToasts(queue);
  return (
    <>
      <button type="button" onClick={() => queue.add({ title: 'Upload failed', retry: true })} className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Upload contract.pdf
      </button>
      <Toaster.Root queue={queue} aria-label="Notifications" className="pointer-events-none fixed inset-auto end-4 top-16 m-0 flex flex-col-reverse gap-2 overflow-visible bg-transparent p-0">
        {toasts.map(({ key, data }) => (
          <Notification.Root key={key} variant="toast" role={data.retry ? undefined : 'none'} actionable={data.retry} timeout={data.retry ? 0 : 5000} onClose={() => queue.remove(key)}>
            <Notification.Box className={`pointer-events-auto relative w-72 border-s-[3px] ${data.retry ? 'border-warning' : 'border-info'} bg-inverse-canvas py-4 ps-3 pe-12 text-sm text-inverse-ink shadow-lg`}>
              <Notification.Title className="block font-semibold">{data.title}</Notification.Title>
              <Notification.Subtitle className="block">contract.pdf</Notification.Subtitle>
              {data.retry ? <RetryAction /> : null}
              <Notification.Close aria-label="Close notification" className="absolute end-0 top-0 grid size-12 place-items-center focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-inverse-ink">
                <svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
                  <path d="M15 6.4 13.6 5 10 8.6 6.4 5 5 6.4 8.6 10 5 13.6 6.4 15l3.6-3.6 3.6 3.6 1.4-1.4-3.6-3.6z" />
                </svg>
              </Notification.Close>
            </Notification.Box>
          </Notification.Root>
        ))}
      </Toaster.Root>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Style it

Where the region sits is your CSS: the top end corner under the header (newest at the top, `flex-col-reverse`), or the bottom end corner (newest at the bottom). `Toaster.ToasterPlacement` (`'top-end' | 'bottom-end'`) is the type the styled toaster uses for it.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Notification, Toaster } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const queue = new Toaster.ToastQueue<{ title: string }>();
const corner: Record<Toaster.ToasterPlacement, string> = {
  'top-end': 'top-16 flex-col-reverse',
  'bottom-end': 'bottom-8 flex-col',
};

export default function Example() {
  const toasts = Toaster.useToasts(queue);
  const [placement, setPlacement] = useState<Toaster.ToasterPlacement>('bottom-end');
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
      {(['top-end', 'bottom-end'] as const).map((side) => (
        <button
          key={side}
          type="button"
          onClick={() => {
            setPlacement(side);
            queue.add({ title: `Link copied (${side})` });
          }}
          className="h-10 border border-interactive px-4 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus"
        >
          {side}
        </button>
      ))}
      <Toaster.Root queue={queue} aria-label="Notifications" className={`pointer-events-none fixed inset-auto end-4 m-0 flex gap-2 overflow-visible bg-transparent p-0 ${corner[placement]}`}>
        {toasts.map(({ key, data }) => (
          <Notification.Root key={key} variant="toast" role="none" timeout={5000} onClose={() => queue.remove(key)}>
            <Notification.Box className="pointer-events-auto relative w-72 border-s-[3px] border-info bg-inverse-canvas py-4 ps-3 pe-12 text-sm text-inverse-ink shadow-lg">
              <Notification.Title className="block font-semibold">{data.title}</Notification.Title>
              <Notification.Close aria-label="Close notification" className="absolute end-0 top-0 grid size-12 place-items-center focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-inverse-ink">
                <svg viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" className="size-5 fill-current">
                  <path d="M15 6.4 13.6 5 10 8.6 6.4 5 5 6.4 8.6 10 5 13.6 6.4 15l3.6-3.6 3.6 3.6 1.4-1.4-3.6-3.6z" />
                </svg>
              </Notification.Close>
            </Notification.Box>
          </Notification.Root>
        ))}
      </Toaster.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```
```css
/* className="toaster" on Root */
.toaster { position: fixed; inset: auto; inset-block-start: 64px; inset-inline-end: 16px; margin: 0; padding: 0; border: 0; background: transparent; overflow: visible; display: flex; flex-direction: column-reverse; gap: 8px; pointer-events: none; }
.toaster > * { pointer-events: auto; }
```

## Parts

### Toaster.Root

A `<section popover="manual" aria-live="polite" aria-relevant="additions">`, shown in the top layer as soon as it mounts. It takes every section prop except `popover`. When a toast is added while a modal dialog is open, it shows itself again so it is drawn above the modal.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `queue` | `Toaster.ToastQueue<T>` | | The toasts this region shows (required); render them as its children |

Give it an `aria-label`, such as "Notifications".

### Toaster.ToastQueue

A class: `new Toaster.ToastQueue<T>()` holds the open toasts, oldest first.

| Member | |
|---|---|
| `add(data, id?)` | Adds a toast and returns its `key`; replaces an open one with the same `id`; drops the oldest beyond `max` |
| `remove(key)` | Removes one toast |
| `clear()` | Removes every toast |
| `max` | How many toasts at once (default 3) |
| `toasts` | The open toasts: `{ key, id?, data }[]` |
| `subscribe(listener)` | Calls `listener` on every change; returns the unsubscribe function |

### Toaster.useToasts

`Toaster.useToasts(queue)` returns the queue's toasts and re-renders when they change.

### Toaster.toastTimeout

`Toaster.toastTimeout(kind, timeout?)` returns `timeout` when given, else 5000 for `info` and `success`, 0 for `error`, `warning` and `warning-alt`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

The region announces each toast politely. The toasts have no role of their own (`role="none"`), except an actionable one, which is an `alertdialog` that takes focus and keeps Tab inside until it closes. The keys inside a toast are the [Notification](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-notification/)'s.

You add:

- An `aria-label` on `Root`.
- `role="none"` on toasts without an action.
- Feedback inside a modal as an inline notification: the page outside a modal dialog is inert, so a toast drawn above it can't be clicked or read by screen readers.


---

# Headless Data table

`DataTable` is the behaviour of the styled [Data table](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/data-table/) without a single class, in the style of TanStack Table: the `useDataTable(options)` hook holds the state — sort, search, pages, selection, open rows, hidden columns, column widths and the editable grid — and hands back the rows to show, actions and prop getters. You write the `<table>`; the parts add the keyboard, focus and ARIA rules where they are needed.

You own the markup: every cell, the header, the toolbar, the icons, the empty state and every style. State shows as `data-*` attributes on the parts.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { DataTable } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { DataTable } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

interface Contract {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  party: string;
  status: string;
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

const headers = [
  { key: 'name', header: 'Contract' },
  { key: 'party', header: 'Counterparty' },
  { key: 'status', header: 'Status' },
];
const rows: Contract[] = [
  { id: '1', name: 'Service agreement', party: 'Acme Co., Ltd.', status: 'Signed' },
  { id: '2', name: 'NDA', party: 'Globex', status: 'Draft' },
  { id: '3', name: 'Lease renewal', party: 'Initech', status: 'In review' },
];
const arrows = { ascending: '↑', descending: '↓', none: '↕' } as const;
const head = 'h-12 bg-layer-accent text-start text-sm font-semibold text-ink';
const cell = 'h-12 border-b border-hairline px-4 text-sm text-ink-muted';

export default function Example() {
  const table = DataTable.useDataTable({ headers, rows, sortable: true, selectable: true });
  return (
    <DataTable.Root table={table}>
      <DataTable.Table aria-label="Contracts" className="w-full border-collapse">
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <td className={`${head} w-12 ps-4`}>
              <DataTable.SelectAll aria-label="Select all rows" />
            </td>
            {table.columns.map((column) => (
              <DataTable.ColumnHeader key={column.key} column={column.key} className={head}>
                <DataTable.SortButton className="flex h-12 w-full items-center justify-between px-4 font-semibold hover:bg-layer-selected-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
                  {column.header}
                  <span aria-hidden="true">{arrows[table.sortDirectionOf(column.key)]}</span>
                </DataTable.SortButton>
              </DataTable.ColumnHeader>
            ))}
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <DataTable.Body>
          {table.pageRows.map((row) => (
            <DataTable.Row key={row.id} rowId={row.id} className="hover:bg-ghost-hover data-selected:bg-layer-selected-1 data-selected:text-ink">
              <DataTable.Cell index={0} className={cell}>
                <DataTable.SelectRow aria-label={`Select row, ${row.name}`} />
              </DataTable.Cell>
              {table.columns.map((column, i) => (
                <DataTable.Cell key={column.key} index={i + 1} column={column.key} className={cell}>
                  {String(row[column.key])}
                </DataTable.Cell>
              ))}
            </DataTable.Row>
          ))}
        </DataTable.Body>
      </DataTable.Table>
      <p className="mt-2 text-xs text-ink-muted">Selected: {table.selectedIds.join(', ') || '(none)'}</p>
    </DataTable.Root>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
const table = DataTable.useDataTable({ headers, rows });

<DataTable.Root table={table}>
  <DataTable.EditHint />
  <DataTable.Table>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <td><DataTable.ExpandAll /></td>
        <td><DataTable.SelectAll /></td>
        <DataTable.ColumnHeader column="…">
          <DataTable.SortButton />
          <DataTable.ResizeHandle />
        </DataTable.ColumnHeader>
        <DataTable.Filler />
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <DataTable.Body>
      <DataTable.Row rowId="…">
        <DataTable.Cell index={0}><DataTable.ExpandToggle /></DataTable.Cell>
        <DataTable.Cell index={1}><DataTable.SelectRow /></DataTable.Cell>
        <DataTable.Cell index={2} column="…">
          <DataTable.CellValue />
          <DataTable.CellInput /> or <DataTable.CellSelect />
          <DataTable.CellError />
        </DataTable.Cell>
        <DataTable.Filler />
      </DataTable.Row>
      <DataTable.ExpandedRow rowId="…" />
    </DataTable.Body>
  </DataTable.Table>
</DataTable.Root>
```

Use only the parts you need: a read-only table is `Root`, `Table`, `Body`, `Row` and `Cell`, or even plain `<tr>` and `<td>` around `table.pageRows`.

## Search and pages

`table.setFilterText(text)` filters the rows (any cell shown contains the text, case-insensitive) and goes back to page 1. With `pageSize` (or `defaultPageSize`), `table.pageRows` is one page; drive it with the headless [Pagination](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-pagination/) or your own buttons through `table.setPagination`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { DataTable, Pagination } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

interface Contract {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  party: string;
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

const parties = ['Acme', 'Globex', 'Initech', 'Umbrella'];
const headers = [
  { key: 'name', header: 'Contract' },
  { key: 'party', header: 'Counterparty' },
];
const rows: Contract[] = Array.from({ length: 23 }, (_, i) => ({ id: `c${i + 1}`, name: `Contract ${String(i + 1).padStart(3, '0')}`, party: parties[i % 4] }));
const cell = 'h-10 border-b border-hairline px-4 text-sm text-ink-muted';
const arrow = 'size-8 text-ink hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-disabled:text-ink-disabled data-disabled:hover:bg-transparent';

export default function Example() {
  const table = DataTable.useDataTable({ headers, rows, defaultPageSize: 5 });
  return (
    <DataTable.Root table={table}>
      <div className="grid max-w-md gap-2">
        <input
          type="search"
          aria-label="Filter contracts"
          placeholder="Filter contracts"
          value={table.filterText}
          onChange={(e) => table.setFilterText(e.target.value)}
          className="h-10 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink placeholder:text-ink-placeholder focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
        />
        <DataTable.Table aria-label="Contracts" className="w-full border-collapse">
          <thead>
            <tr>
              {table.columns.map((column) => (
                <DataTable.ColumnHeader key={column.key} column={column.key} className="h-10 bg-layer-accent px-4 text-start text-sm font-semibold text-ink">
                  {column.header}
                </DataTable.ColumnHeader>
              ))}
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <DataTable.Body>
            {table.pageRows.map((row) => (
              <DataTable.Row key={row.id} rowId={row.id}>
                <DataTable.Cell index={0} className={cell}>{row.name}</DataTable.Cell>
                <DataTable.Cell index={1} className={cell}>{row.party}</DataTable.Cell>
              </DataTable.Row>
            ))}
          </DataTable.Body>
        </DataTable.Table>
        {table.filteredRows.length === 0 ? <p className="text-sm text-ink-muted">No results found.</p> : null}
        <Pagination.Root page={table.page} pageSize={table.pageSize} totalItems={table.filteredRows.length} onChange={table.setPagination} className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm text-ink">
          <span className="me-auto" role="status">
            {table.filteredRows.length} of {table.rows.length} rows · page {table.page} of {table.pageCount}
          </span>
          <Pagination.Prev aria-label="Previous page" className={arrow}>‹</Pagination.Prev>
          <Pagination.Next aria-label="Next page" className={arrow}>›</Pagination.Next>
        </Pagination.Root>
      </div>
    </DataTable.Root>
  );
}
```

`filterRows(row, text, headers)` replaces the test, and `manualFiltering` keeps every row while you filter on the server. `filterText` / `onFilterChange` and `page` / `onPageChange` make both controlled.

## Expandable rows

With `expandable`, each row's `ExpandToggle` opens it; render an `ExpandedRow` under every open row (`table.isExpanded(id)`). `ExpandAll` opens every row shown, or closes them all once all are open. The toggles get `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the open row.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { DataTable } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

interface Contract {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  party: string;
  owner: string;
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

const headers = [
  { key: 'name', header: 'Contract' },
  { key: 'party', header: 'Counterparty' },
];
const rows: Contract[] = [
  { id: '1', name: 'Service agreement', party: 'Acme Co., Ltd.', owner: 'Kanya S.' },
  { id: '2', name: 'NDA', party: 'Globex', owner: 'Anan P.' },
  { id: '3', name: 'Lease renewal', party: 'Initech', owner: 'Malee K.' },
];
const toggle = 'flex size-8 items-center justify-center text-ink hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus [&>svg]:transition-transform data-expanded:[&>svg]:rotate-90';
const chevron = (
  <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 fill-current">
    <path d="M11 8 6 13l-.7-.7L9.6 8 5.3 3.7 6 3z" />
  </svg>
);
const cell = 'h-12 border-b border-hairline px-4 text-sm text-ink-muted';

export default function Example() {
  const table = DataTable.useDataTable({ headers, rows, expandable: true, defaultExpandedIds: ['2'] });
  return (
    <DataTable.Root table={table}>
      <DataTable.Table aria-label="Contracts" className="w-full border-collapse">
        <thead>
          <tr className="bg-layer-accent text-start text-sm font-semibold text-ink">
            <td className="w-12 ps-2">
              <DataTable.ExpandAll aria-label={table.allExpanded ? 'Collapse all rows' : 'Expand all rows'} className={toggle}>{chevron}</DataTable.ExpandAll>
            </td>
            {table.columns.map((column) => (
              <DataTable.ColumnHeader key={column.key} column={column.key} className="h-12 px-4 text-start">
                {column.header}
              </DataTable.ColumnHeader>
            ))}
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <DataTable.Body>
          {table.pageRows.flatMap((row) => {
            const parent = (
              <DataTable.Row key={row.id} rowId={row.id} className="data-expanded:[&>td]:border-transparent">
                <DataTable.Cell index={0} className={`${cell} ps-2`}>
                  <DataTable.ExpandToggle aria-label={`Expand row, ${row.name}`} className={toggle}>{chevron}</DataTable.ExpandToggle>
                </DataTable.Cell>
                <DataTable.Cell index={1} className={cell}>{row.name}</DataTable.Cell>
                <DataTable.Cell index={2} className={cell}>{row.party}</DataTable.Cell>
              </DataTable.Row>
            );
            if (!table.isExpanded(row.id)) return [parent];
            return [
              parent,
              <DataTable.ExpandedRow key={`${row.id}-detail`} rowId={row.id}>
                <td colSpan={3} className="border-b border-hairline px-14 pb-6 pt-2 text-sm text-ink-muted">
                  Owner: {row.owner}
                </td>
              </DataTable.ExpandedRow>,
            ];
          })}
        </DataTable.Body>
      </DataTable.Table>
    </DataTable.Root>
  );
}
```

Return the rows as one flat list (as here with `flatMap`), so opening a row doesn't remount it.

## Pick one row

With `radio`, `SelectRow` is a radio: the radios are one Tab stop (the chosen row, else the first enabled one), and the arrow keys move to the next enabled row and select it, wrapping. `SelectAll` renders nothing. A row with `disabled: true` can't be chosen.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { DataTable } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

interface Template {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  type: string;
  disabled?: boolean;
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

const headers = [
  { key: 'name', header: 'Template' },
  { key: 'type', header: 'Type' },
];
const rows: Template[] = [
  { id: 'nda', name: 'Standard NDA', type: 'Confidentiality' },
  { id: 'lease', name: 'Office lease', type: 'Property' },
  { id: 'msa', name: 'Master services (being revised)', type: 'Services', disabled: true },
];
const cell = 'h-12 border-b border-hairline px-4 text-sm text-ink-muted';

export default function Example() {
  const table = DataTable.useDataTable({ headers, rows, radio: true });
  return (
    <DataTable.Root table={table}>
      <DataTable.Table aria-label="Pick a template" className="w-full border-collapse">
        <thead>
          <tr className="h-12 bg-layer-accent text-sm font-semibold text-ink">
            <th className="w-12">
              <span className="sr-only">Select</span>
            </th>
            {table.columns.map((column) => (
              <DataTable.ColumnHeader key={column.key} column={column.key} className="px-4 text-start">
                {column.header}
              </DataTable.ColumnHeader>
            ))}
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <DataTable.Body>
          {table.pageRows.map((row) => (
            <DataTable.Row key={row.id} rowId={row.id} className="data-selected:bg-layer-selected-1 data-selected:[&>td]:text-ink">
              <DataTable.Cell index={0} className={`${cell} ps-4`}>
                <DataTable.SelectRow aria-label={`Select row, ${row.name}`} className="accent-ink" />
              </DataTable.Cell>
              <DataTable.Cell index={1} className={cell}>{row.name}</DataTable.Cell>
              <DataTable.Cell index={2} className={cell}>{row.type}</DataTable.Cell>
            </DataTable.Row>
          ))}
        </DataTable.Body>
      </DataTable.Table>
      <p className="mt-2 text-xs text-ink-muted">Template: {table.selectedIds[0] ?? '(none)'}</p>
    </DataTable.Root>
  );
}
```

## Show and hide columns

`table.columns` is the columns shown; `table.headers` is all of them. `toggleColumn(key, show)` shows or hides one, `isColumnLocked(key)` says it can't be hidden (`hideable: false`, or the last one shown), and `resetColumns()` goes back to the headers' `hidden`. `columnsChanged` says the choice differs from that.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { DataTable } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

interface Contract {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  party: string;
  status: string;
  updated: string;
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

const headers = [
  { key: 'name', header: 'Contract', hideable: false },
  { key: 'party', header: 'Counterparty' },
  { key: 'status', header: 'Status' },
  { key: 'updated', header: 'Updated', hidden: true },
];
const rows: Contract[] = [
  { id: '1', name: 'Service agreement', party: 'Acme Co., Ltd.', status: 'Signed', updated: '2026-09-30' },
  { id: '2', name: 'NDA', party: 'Globex', status: 'Draft', updated: '2026-10-01' },
];
const cell = 'h-10 border-b border-hairline px-4 text-sm text-ink-muted';

export default function Example() {
  const table = DataTable.useDataTable({ headers, rows });
  return (
    <DataTable.Root table={table}>
      <fieldset className="mb-3 flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4 text-sm text-ink">
        <legend className="mb-1 text-xs text-ink-muted">Columns</legend>
        {table.headers.map((column) => (
          <label key={column.key} className="flex items-center gap-2 has-disabled:text-ink-disabled">
            <input
              type="checkbox"
              checked={!table.hiddenColumns.includes(column.key)}
              disabled={table.isColumnLocked(column.key)}
              onChange={(e) => table.toggleColumn(column.key, e.target.checked)}
            />
            {column.header}
          </label>
        ))}
        <button type="button" disabled={!table.columnsChanged} onClick={table.resetColumns} className="h-8 px-3 text-link hover:bg-ghost-hover disabled:text-ink-disabled focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          Reset
        </button>
      </fieldset>
      <DataTable.Table aria-label="Contracts" className="w-full border-collapse">
        <thead>
          <tr className="h-10 bg-layer-accent text-sm font-semibold text-ink">
            {table.columns.map((column) => (
              <DataTable.ColumnHeader key={column.key} column={column.key} className="px-4 text-start">
                {column.header}
              </DataTable.ColumnHeader>
            ))}
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <DataTable.Body>
          {table.pageRows.map((row) => (
            <DataTable.Row key={row.id} rowId={row.id}>
              {table.columns.map((column, i) => (
                <DataTable.Cell key={column.key} index={i} column={column.key} className={cell}>
                  {String(row[column.key])}
                </DataTable.Cell>
              ))}
            </DataTable.Row>
          ))}
        </DataTable.Body>
      </DataTable.Table>
    </DataTable.Root>
  );
}
```

Hidden columns leave the search too. `hiddenColumns` / `onColumnsChange` make the choice controlled, so you can save it.

## Edit cells in place

A column with `editable: 'text' | 'number' | 'select'` makes the table an APG grid: `Table` gets `role="grid"`, one body cell is the Tab stop, and the arrow keys, Home / End and Ctrl + Home / End move it. Enter, F2, a double click, a click on a `data-edit-icon` element or typing opens the editor. Render `CellInput` or `CellSelect` while the cell is edited (`useCellContext().editing`), and `CellError` for `validate`'s message. `onCellEdit` hands you the new `rows`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { DataTable } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

interface Contract {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  amount: number;
  status: string;
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

const headers: DataTable.DataTableColumn[] = [
  { key: 'name', header: 'Name', editable: 'text', validate: (value) => (String(value).trim() ? '' : 'Name is required') },
  { key: 'amount', header: 'Amount (THB)', editable: 'number' },
  { key: 'status', header: 'Status', editable: 'select', options: [
    { value: 'draft', label: 'Draft' },
    { value: 'signed', label: 'Signed' },
  ] },
];
const initialRows: Contract[] = [
  { id: '1', name: 'Office lease 2026', amount: 250000, status: 'draft' },
  { id: '2', name: 'NDA – Acme', amount: 0, status: 'signed' },
];
const editor = 'h-full w-full bg-surface-1 px-4 text-sm text-ink outline-2 -outline-offset-2 outline-focus aria-invalid:outline-error';

function CellContent({ column, value }: { column: DataTable.DataTableColumn; value: unknown }) {
  const { editing } = DataTable.useCellContext();
  if (editing) {
    return (
      <>
        {column.editable === 'select' ? <DataTable.CellSelect aria-label={column.header} className={editor} /> : <DataTable.CellInput aria-label={column.header} className={editor} />}
        <DataTable.CellError className="absolute start-0 top-full z-10 whitespace-nowrap bg-surface-1 px-2 py-1 text-xs text-error-text shadow" />
      </>
    );
  }
  const shown = column.options?.find((option) => option.value === value)?.label ?? String(value);
  return (
    <>
      <DataTable.CellValue>{shown}</DataTable.CellValue>
      {column.editable ? <span data-edit-icon="" aria-hidden="true" className="ms-2 cursor-pointer opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 group-focus:opacity-100">✎</span> : null}
    </>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  const [rows, setRows] = useState(initialRows);
  const [last, setLast] = useState('');
  const table = DataTable.useDataTable({
    headers,
    rows,
    onCellEdit: (edit) => {
      setRows(edit.rows);
      setLast(`${edit.key}: ${String(edit.previous)} → ${edit.value}`);
    },
  });
  return (
    <DataTable.Root table={table}>
      <DataTable.EditHint className="sr-only">Press Enter to edit</DataTable.EditHint>
      <DataTable.Table aria-label="Contracts" className="w-full border-collapse">
        <thead>
          <tr className="h-12 bg-layer-accent text-sm font-semibold text-ink">
            {table.columns.map((column) => (
              <DataTable.ColumnHeader key={column.key} column={column.key} className="px-4 text-start">
                {column.header}
              </DataTable.ColumnHeader>
            ))}
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <DataTable.Body>
          {table.pageRows.map((row) => (
            <DataTable.Row key={row.id} rowId={row.id}>
              {table.columns.map((column, i) => (
                <DataTable.Cell
                  key={column.key}
                  index={i}
                  column={column.key}
                  className="group relative h-12 border-b border-hairline px-4 text-sm text-ink-muted data-editing:p-0 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
                >
                  <CellContent column={column} value={row[column.key]} />
                </DataTable.Cell>
              ))}
            </DataTable.Row>
          ))}
        </DataTable.Body>
      </DataTable.Table>
      <p className="mt-2 text-xs text-ink-muted">Last edit: {last}</p>
    </DataTable.Root>
  );
}
```

In the editor, Enter saves, Escape cancels, Tab / Shift + Tab save and edit the next / previous editable cell, and leaving the cell saves. Controls inside cells (links, buttons) leave the Tab order in a grid; Enter or Space on their cell presses them.

## Resize columns

`resizable` (or a column's `resizable`) gives `ResizeHandle` something to do: a native range input on the header's edge — drag it, or arrows 2px, Shift / Page Up / Down 16px, Home / End narrowest / widest. The first resize freezes the automatic layout into fixed widths (`table.resize.fixed`); `Filler` then takes the rest of the row. Attach `table.boxRef` to the scroll box, so the widest a column gets is the box's width.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { DataTable } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

interface Contract {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  owner: string;
  amount: string;
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

const headers = [
  { key: 'name', header: 'Name', minWidth: 120 },
  { key: 'owner', header: 'Owner' },
  { key: 'amount', header: 'Amount (THB)', resizable: false },
];
const rows: Contract[] = [
  { id: '1', name: 'Office lease 2026', owner: 'Ananya', amount: '250,000' },
  { id: '2', name: 'Software licence', owner: 'Chai', amount: '48,000' },
];
const cell = 'h-10 border-b border-hairline px-4 text-sm text-ink-muted';

export default function Example() {
  const table = DataTable.useDataTable({ headers, rows, resizable: true });
  const { boxRef } = table;
  return (
    <DataTable.Root table={table}>
      <div ref={boxRef} className="overflow-x-auto">
        <DataTable.Table aria-label="Contracts" style={table.resize.tableStyle} className={`w-full border-collapse ${table.resize.fixed ? 'table-fixed' : ''}`}>
          <thead>
            <tr className="h-10 bg-layer-accent text-sm font-semibold text-ink">
              {table.columns.map((column) => (
                <DataTable.ColumnHeader key={column.key} column={column.key} className="group relative px-4 text-start">
                  {column.header}
                  <DataTable.ResizeHandle aria-label={`Resize ${column.header} column`} valueText={(px) => `${px} pixels`} className="peer absolute -end-3 top-0 z-10 m-0 h-full w-6 cursor-col-resize appearance-none bg-transparent opacity-0" />
                  <span aria-hidden="true" className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-y-0 end-0 w-0.5 group-hover:bg-border-strong-1 group-data-resizing:bg-interactive peer-focus-visible:bg-focus" />
                </DataTable.ColumnHeader>
              ))}
              <DataTable.Filler />
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <DataTable.Body>
            {table.pageRows.map((row) => (
              <DataTable.Row key={row.id} rowId={row.id}>
                {table.columns.map((column, i) => (
                  <DataTable.Cell key={column.key} index={i} column={column.key} className={cell}>
                    {String(row[column.key])}
                  </DataTable.Cell>
                ))}
                <DataTable.Filler className={cell} />
              </DataTable.Row>
            ))}
          </DataTable.Body>
        </DataTable.Table>
      </div>
      <p className="mt-2 text-xs text-ink-muted">Widths: {JSON.stringify(table.columnWidths)}</p>
    </DataTable.Root>
  );
}
```

`columnWidths` / `onColumnResize` make the widths controlled, so you can save and restore them. Columns take `width`, `minWidth` (default 50) and `maxWidth`.

## Style it

Draw the checkboxes yourself from `data-checked` and `data-indeterminate`, turn the sort arrow from `data-direction`, and shade selected and striped rows.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { DataTable } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

interface Signer {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  role: string;
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

const headers = [
  { key: 'name', header: 'Name' },
  { key: 'role', header: 'Role' },
];
const rows: Signer[] = [
  { id: '1', name: 'Anan P.', role: 'Managing director' },
  { id: '2', name: 'Kanya S.', role: 'Legal counsel' },
  { id: '3', name: 'Somchai D.', role: 'Witness' },
];
const cell = 'h-12 border-b border-hairline px-4 text-sm text-ink-muted';

function Box({ label, all = false }: { label: string; all?: boolean }) {
  const input = 'peer absolute inset-0 m-0 cursor-pointer opacity-0';
  return (
    <span className="relative inline-flex size-4">
      {all ? <DataTable.SelectAll aria-label={label} className={input} /> : <DataTable.SelectRow aria-label={label} className={input} />}
      <span aria-hidden="true" className="pointer-events-none flex size-4 items-center justify-center border border-icon-primary text-[11px] leading-none text-on-primary peer-focus-visible:outline-2 peer-focus-visible:outline-offset-1 peer-focus-visible:outline-focus peer-data-checked:bg-icon-primary peer-data-checked:after:content-['✓'] peer-data-indeterminate:bg-icon-primary peer-data-indeterminate:after:content-['–']" />
    </span>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  const table = DataTable.useDataTable({ headers, rows, sortable: true, selectable: true });
  return (
    <DataTable.Root table={table}>
      <DataTable.Table aria-label="Signers" className="w-full border-collapse">
        <thead>
          <tr className="bg-layer-accent text-sm text-ink">
            <td className="w-12 ps-4">
              <Box label="Select all rows" all />
            </td>
            {table.columns.map((column) => (
              <DataTable.ColumnHeader key={column.key} column={column.key} className="p-0 text-start font-semibold">
                <DataTable.SortButton className="group flex h-12 w-full items-center justify-between px-4 hover:bg-layer-selected-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-[direction=ascending]:bg-layer-selected-hover data-[direction=descending]:bg-layer-selected-hover">
                  {column.header}
                  <svg viewBox="0 0 32 32" aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 fill-icon-primary opacity-0 transition-transform group-hover:opacity-100 group-data-[direction=ascending]:opacity-100 group-data-[direction=descending]:rotate-180 group-data-[direction=descending]:opacity-100">
                    <path d="M16 4 6 14l1.41 1.41L15 7.83V28h2V7.83l7.59 7.58L26 14 16 4z" />
                  </svg>
                </DataTable.SortButton>
              </DataTable.ColumnHeader>
            ))}
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <DataTable.Body>
          {table.pageRows.map((row) => (
            <DataTable.Row key={row.id} rowId={row.id} className="even:bg-layer-accent hover:bg-ghost-hover data-selected:bg-layer-selected-1 data-selected:[&>td]:text-ink">
              <DataTable.Cell index={0} className={`${cell} ps-4`}>
                <Box label={`Select row, ${row.name}`} />
              </DataTable.Cell>
              {table.columns.map((column, i) => (
                <DataTable.Cell key={column.key} index={i + 1} column={column.key} className={cell}>
                  {String(row[column.key])}
                </DataTable.Cell>
              ))}
            </DataTable.Row>
          ))}
        </DataTable.Body>
      </DataTable.Table>
    </DataTable.Root>
  );
}
```
```css
th[data-sortable] button:hover { background: #d1d1d1; }
button[data-direction='ascending'] .arrow,
button[data-direction='descending'] .arrow { opacity: 1; }
button[data-direction='descending'] .arrow { transform: rotate(180deg); }
tr[data-row-id]:nth-child(even) { background: #e0e0e0; }
tr[data-selected] { background: #e0e0e0; color: #161616; }
input[data-checked] + .box,
input[data-indeterminate] + .box { background: #161616; }
td[data-editable]:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0f62fe; outline-offset: -2px; }
td[data-editing] { padding: 0; }
th[data-resizing] { background: #c6c6c6; }
```

## The hook

### DataTable.useDataTable(options)

Holds the state. Every piece of state can be controlled (`sortKey`, `selectedIds` …) or left to the hook (`default…`).

| Option | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `headers` | `DataTableColumn[]` | | The columns: `{ key, header }` plus the column options below (required) |
| `rows` | `R[]` | | The rows: `{ id, …cells }`, `disabled` to block selection (required) |
| `id` | `string` | generated | Base of the ids the parts give their elements |
| `sortable` | `boolean` | `false` | Every column sorts unless its header sets `sortable: false` |
| `sortKey`, `sortDirection` | `string`, `SortDirection` | | The sort (controlled) |
| `defaultSortKey`, `defaultSortDirection` | `string`, `SortDirection` | `''`, `'none'` | The starting sort |
| `onSortChange` | `(sort: { key, direction }) => void` | | After a sort button was pressed |
| `manualSorting` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep `rows` in your order (sort on the server); the headers still show the sort |
| `sortRow` | `(a, b, context) => number` | | Replaces the comparison |
| `locale` | `string` | `'en'` | Orders the sort |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | `false` | Checkboxes with select-all |
| `radio` | `boolean` | `false` | One choice with a radio per row |
| `selectedIds`, `defaultSelectedIds` | `string[]` | `[]` | The selected rows |
| `onSelectionChange` | `(ids: string[], rows: R[]) => void` | | After the selection changed |
| `filterText`, `defaultFilterText` | `string` | `''` | The search text |
| `onFilterChange` | `(value: string) => void` | | After `setFilterText` |
| `filterRows` | `(row, text, headers) => boolean` | | Replaces the search's row test |
| `manualFiltering` | `boolean` | `false` | Keep every row (filter on the server) |
| `expandable` | `boolean` | `false` | Rows open and close |
| `expandedIds`, `defaultExpandedIds` | `string[]` | `[]` | The open rows |
| `onExpandChange` | `(change: { expandedIds, expanded, id? }) => void` | | After a row (or, without `id`, every row) opened or closed |
| `pageSize`, `defaultPageSize` | `number` | `0` | Rows per page (0: one page of every row) |
| `page`, `defaultPage` | `number` | `1` | The page, from 1 |
| `onPageChange` | `(change: { page, pageSize }) => void` | | After `setPagination`, or a new search on a later page |
| `hiddenColumns`, `defaultHiddenColumns` | `string[]` | headers marked `hidden` | Keys of the columns not shown |
| `onColumnsChange` | `(change: { hiddenColumns, key, hidden }) => void` | | After a column was shown or hidden (`key` `''` after a reset) |
| `resizable` | `boolean` | `false` | Every column gets a resize handle |
| `columnWidths`, `defaultColumnWidths` | `Record<string, number>` | `{}` | Column widths in px by key |
| `onColumnResize` | `(change: { key, width, widths }) => void` | | After a resize (once per drag or key press) |
| `staticWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | A resized table is as wide as its columns, not its box |
| `onCellEdit` | `(edit: { rowId, key, value, previous, row, rows }) => void` | | An edited cell was saved: set `rows` to `edit.rows` |

Column options on each header: `sortable`, `editable` (`'text' \| 'number' \| 'select'`), `options` (`{ value, label }[]` for a select), `validate(value, row)`, `resizable`, `width`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth`, `hideable`, `hidden`, `pinned` (`'start' \| 'end'`).

What it returns, by topic:

| | |
|---|---|
| Rows | `rows`, `filteredRows` (search kept), `sortedRows`, `pageRows` (the rows to render), `rowById` |
| Columns | `headers` (all), `columns` (shown), `hiddenColumns`, `toggleColumn(key, show)`, `resetColumns()`, `isColumnLocked(key)`, `columnsChanged`, `pins` |
| Sort | `sortKey`, `sortDirection`, `sortDirectionOf(key)`, `isSortable(column)`, `sortBy(key)` |
| Search | `filterText`, `setFilterText(text)` |
| Pages | `paged`, `page`, `pageSize`, `pageCount`, `setPagination({ page, pageSize })` |
| Selection | `selectable`, `radio`, `selectedIds`, `isSelected(id)`, `setSelectedIds(ids)`, `toggleRow(row, checked)`, `toggleAll()`, `selectAll()`, `allSelected`, `someSelected`, `radioStop`, `getSelectAllProps()`, `getSelectRowProps(row)` |
| Open rows | `expandable`, `expandedIds`, `isExpanded(id)`, `allExpanded`, `toggleExpanded(id)`, `toggleAllExpanded()`, `expandedRowId(id)` |
| Widths and grid | `columnWidths`, `resize` (`fixed`, `hasFiller`, `tableStyle`, `widthOf(column)` …), `grid` (`enabled` …), `tableRef`, `boxRef`, `id` |

`DataTable.useDataTableContext()` returns the same object to any component inside `Root`.

## Parts

### DataTable.Root

Renders nothing of its own: it gives its children the hook's table.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `table` | what `useDataTable` returned | | Required |

### DataTable.Table

Renders a `<table>` with the hook's `tableRef`; `role="grid"` once a column is `editable`. It takes every `<table>` prop.

### DataTable.Body

Renders a `<tbody>`. In a grid it handles the cells' keys, clicks, double clicks and focus.

### DataTable.ColumnHeader

Renders a `<th scope="col">` with `aria-sort` on a sortable column, `data-key`, and its resized width. It takes every `<th>` prop.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `column` | `string` | | The column's key (required) |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-sortable` | The column sorts |
| `data-resizing` | Its handle is being dragged |

### DataTable.SortButton

Renders a `<button type="button">` that steps its column's sort: none → ascending → descending → none; a new column starts ascending. Describe the next step with `aria-describedby` if you like.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-direction` | Always: `none`, `ascending` or `descending` |

### DataTable.ResizeHandle

Renders an `<input type="range">` (nothing for a column that doesn't resize). Name it ("Resize Name column"). It takes every input prop except `type`, `value`, `min`, `max` and `step`.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `valueText` | `(width: number) => string` | | The width as words for assistive tech ("120 pixels") |

### DataTable.Row

Renders a `<tr>` with `data-row-id`, which the grid and the radios find it by.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rowId` | `string` | | The row's `id` (required) |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-selected` | The row is selected |
| `data-expanded` | The row is open |

### DataTable.Cell

Renders a `<td>`. In a grid one body cell is the Tab stop and the others are `tabIndex={-1}`; cells that can't be edited are `aria-readonly`.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | `number` | | The cell's place in its row, from 0, counting every cell (expand, select, data) (required) |
| `column` | `string` | | The column's key, for a data cell; an `editable` column makes the cell editable |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-editable` | The cell can be edited |
| `data-editing` | The cell is being edited |
| `data-key` | The column's key, on an editable cell |

`DataTable.useCellContext()` returns the cell's `rowId`, `column` and `editing` (`{ draft, error }` while edited, else `null`).

### DataTable.CellValue, DataTable.EditHint

`CellValue` renders a `<span>` around an editable cell's value: a click on it focuses the cell. `EditHint` renders a `<span>` with the text that describes every editable cell ("Press Enter to edit"); only in a grid. Hide it visually.

### DataTable.CellInput, DataTable.CellSelect, DataTable.CellError

The editor while a cell is edited: `CellInput` an `<input>` (text, or number with `inputMode="decimal"`), `CellSelect` a `<select>` of the column's `options` (or your own `<option>` children). Both are `aria-invalid` and described by the error while `validate` refuses the value. `CellError` renders a `<span role="alert">` with the message, and nothing while the value is valid.

### DataTable.SelectAll

Renders a native checkbox (the headless [Checkbox](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-checkbox/)): checked when every row in scope is selected, mixed when some are. A press clears the selection when any row is selected, else selects every enabled row shown (Carbon). Nothing in a `radio` table.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-checked` | Every row in scope is selected |
| `data-indeterminate` | Some are |

### DataTable.SelectRow

Renders a native checkbox for its row, or a radio in a `radio` table. A disabled row's box is disabled.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-checked` | The row is selected |

### DataTable.ExpandToggle, DataTable.ExpandAll

Each renders a `<button type="button">` with `aria-expanded`; `aria-controls` points at the open row(s). `ExpandToggle` opens or closes its row; `ExpandAll` opens every row shown, or closes them all once all are open. Name them with `aria-label`.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-expanded` | Its row is open (every row, for `ExpandAll`) |

### DataTable.ExpandedRow

Renders the `<tr>` under an open row, with the id its toggle controls.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rowId` | `string` | | The open row's `id` (required) |

### DataTable.Filler

Renders an empty `<td aria-hidden="true">` that takes the rest of a row of resized columns — only then.

## Keyboard and accessibility

- Without editable columns, the parts are native: sort buttons, checkboxes and expand buttons are each in the Tab order. A `radio` table's radios are one Tab stop, and the arrow keys move and select, wrapping.
- With an editable column, the table is a WAI-ARIA grid: one Tab stop among the body cells, the arrow keys, Home / End and Ctrl + Home / End move it, and Enter or Space press a control in a cell.
- You add the table's name (`aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` to your heading), names for the select and expand controls (say the row: "Select row, NDA"), a screen-reader name for the radio column, and the "Press Enter to edit" text.
- Announce what changed yourself: after a sort ("Sorted by Contract, ascending") and once typing in a search pauses ("3 of 12 rows"), with a polite status. Set `aria-busy` on the table while it reloads.


---

# Headless Structured list

`StructuredList` is the row selection of the styled [Structured list](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/structured-list/) as unstyled React parts. The rest of a structured list is plain table markup (`thead`, `tbody`, `th`, `td`), so the parts are only what selection needs: the `<table>` (`Root`), a selectable row (`Row` with a `value`: a click anywhere on it selects it) and its `Radio` (the keyboard: one Tab stop, the arrow keys move and select).

You own the markup: the cells, the header row, the radio icon and every style. State shows as `data-*` attributes to style on.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { StructuredList } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { StructuredList } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const plans = [
  { value: 'basic', name: 'Basic', price: 'Free' },
  { value: 'team', name: 'Team', price: '฿390 / user' },
  { value: 'enterprise', name: 'Enterprise', price: 'Contact us' },
];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <StructuredList.Root aria-label="Choose a plan" values={plans.map((p) => p.value)} defaultValue="team" className="w-full max-w-md border-collapse text-sm text-ink-muted">
      <thead>
        <tr className="text-start text-ink">
          <th className="w-10">
            <span className="sr-only">Select</span>
          </th>
          <th className="px-2 py-2 text-start font-semibold">Plan</th>
          <th className="px-2 py-2 text-start font-semibold">Price</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {plans.map((plan) => (
          <StructuredList.Row key={plan.value} value={plan.value} className="cursor-pointer border-t border-hairline hover:bg-ghost-hover data-selected:bg-surface-2 data-selected:text-ink focus-within:outline-2 focus-within:-outline-offset-2 focus-within:outline-focus">
            <td className="py-3 ps-4">
              <StructuredList.Radio aria-label={plan.name} className="accent-ink" />
            </td>
            <td className="px-2 py-3">{plan.name}</td>
            <td className="px-2 py-3">{plan.price}</td>
          </StructuredList.Row>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </StructuredList.Root>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<StructuredList.Root>
  <thead>
    <tr><th /></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <StructuredList.Row value="…">
      <td><StructuredList.Radio /></td>
      <td />
    </StructuredList.Row>
  </tbody>
</StructuredList.Root>
```

## A list without selection

Without selection you need no parts at all: write the table. `Root` and `Row` without a `value` render a plain `<table>` and `<tr>`, which helps when one list switches selection on and off.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { StructuredList } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const terms = [
  ['Counterparty', 'Acme Co., Ltd.'],
  ['Signed on', '30 September 2026'],
  ['Duration', '12 months'],
];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <StructuredList.Root aria-label="Contract summary" className="w-full max-w-md border-collapse text-sm">
      <tbody>
        {terms.map(([term, value]) => (
          <StructuredList.Row key={term} className="border-t border-hairline last:border-b">
            <th scope="row" className="whitespace-nowrap px-4 py-3 text-start font-normal text-ink-muted">{term}</th>
            <td className="px-2 py-3 text-ink">{value}</td>
          </StructuredList.Row>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </StructuredList.Root>
  );
}
```

## Controlled value

Pass `value` and `onValueChange` to hold the choice yourself, or `defaultValue` to let `Root` keep it. `values` lists the selectable rows in order: it sets the radios' "1 of 3" and which row takes Tab when none is selected. A `value` not in `values` selects nothing.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { StructuredList } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const methods = [
  { value: 'email', name: 'Signed PDF by email', arrives: 'Today' },
  { value: 'post', name: 'Registered post', arrives: '3–5 days' },
  { value: 'courier', name: 'Courier', arrives: 'Next day' },
];

export default function Example() {
  const [method, setMethod] = useState('');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-md gap-4">
      <StructuredList.Root aria-label="Delivery method" values={methods.map((m) => m.value)} value={method} onValueChange={setMethod} className="w-full border-collapse text-sm text-ink-muted">
        <tbody>
          {methods.map((m) => (
            <StructuredList.Row key={m.value} value={m.value} className="cursor-pointer border-t border-hairline last:border-b hover:bg-ghost-hover data-selected:bg-surface-2 data-selected:text-ink focus-within:outline-2 focus-within:-outline-offset-2 focus-within:outline-focus">
              <td className="py-2 ps-4">
                <StructuredList.Radio aria-label={m.name} className="accent-ink" />
              </td>
              <td className="px-2 py-2">{m.name}</td>
              <td className="px-2 py-2">{m.arrives}</td>
            </StructuredList.Row>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </StructuredList.Root>
      <div className="flex gap-2">
        <button type="button" onClick={() => setMethod('email')} className="h-8 border border-interactive px-3 text-sm text-interactive hover:bg-interactive hover:text-on-primary focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          Use the recommended method
        </button>
        <button type="button" onClick={() => setMethod('')} className="h-8 px-3 text-sm text-link hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          Clear
        </button>
      </div>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Value: {method || '(none)'}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`onValueChange` runs only when the user picks a row, not when you change `value`.

## Style it

Hide the native radio and draw Carbon's radio icon from the row's `data-selected`. A `group` class on the row lets the icon read it.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { StructuredList } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const plans = [
  { value: 'basic', name: 'Basic', users: 'Up to 5' },
  { value: 'team', name: 'Team', users: 'Up to 50' },
  { value: 'enterprise', name: 'Enterprise', users: 'Unlimited' },
];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <StructuredList.Root aria-label="Plans" values={plans.map((p) => p.value)} defaultValue="basic" className="w-full max-w-md border-collapse text-sm text-ink-muted">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th className="w-8 py-2 ps-4">
            <span className="sr-only">Select</span>
          </th>
          <th className="px-4 py-2 text-start font-semibold text-ink">Plan</th>
          <th className="px-4 py-2 text-start font-semibold text-ink">Users</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {plans.map((plan) => (
          <StructuredList.Row key={plan.value} value={plan.value} className="group cursor-pointer border-t border-hairline last:border-b hover:bg-ghost-hover hover:text-ink data-selected:bg-surface-2 data-selected:text-ink focus-within:outline-2 focus-within:-outline-offset-2 focus-within:outline-focus">
            <td className="py-3 ps-4 align-top">
              <StructuredList.Radio aria-label={plan.name} className="sr-only" />
              <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true" className="mt-0.5 size-4 fill-icon-primary">
                <circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.5" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" />
                <circle cx="8" cy="8" r="3" className="radio-dot hidden group-data-selected:block" />
              </svg>
            </td>
            <td className="px-4 py-3">{plan.name}</td>
            <td className="px-4 py-3">{plan.users}</td>
          </StructuredList.Row>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </StructuredList.Root>
  );
}
```
```css
tr[data-selectable] { cursor: pointer; }
tr[data-selectable]:hover { background: #e8e8e8; }
tr[data-selected] { background: #e0e0e0; color: #161616; }
tr[data-selectable]:focus-within { outline: 2px solid #0f62fe; outline-offset: -2px; }
tr .radio-dot { display: none; }
tr[data-selected] .radio-dot { display: block; }
```

## Parts

### StructuredList.Root

Renders a `<table>`. It takes every `<table>` prop.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `values` | `readonly string[]` | `[]` | The selectable rows' values, in order: the radio group's size and its first Tab stop |
| `value` | `string` | | The selected row's value (controlled); one not in `values` selects none |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | `''` | The starting value (uncontrolled) |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | | After the user selected another row |

`StructuredList.useStructuredListContext()` returns `value`, `focusValue` (the row whose radio takes Tab), `values` and `select(value)` to any component inside `Root`.

### StructuredList.Row

Renders a `<tr>`. With a `value` it is selectable: a click anywhere on it selects it, and it gets `aria-selected`. Without one it is a plain row (for the header or a read-only list).

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | | Makes the row selectable and identifies it in `Root`'s `value` |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-selectable` | The row has a `value` |
| `data-selected` | The row is the selected one |

`StructuredList.useRowContext()` returns the row's `value` and `selected` to any component inside a selectable `Row`.

### StructuredList.Radio

Renders an `<input type="radio">` checked when its row is selected. It goes inside a selectable `Row`. It takes every input prop except `type`, `value`, `checked` and `defaultChecked`; name it with `aria-label`.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-selected` | Its row is selected |

## Keyboard and accessibility

- The radios form one Tab stop: the selected row's radio, else the first row's.
- Up, Down, Left and Right move focus and the selection to the previous or next row, wrapping at the ends. Space selects the focused row.
- Each radio has `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` from `values`, so screen readers say "2 of 3".
- You add the table's name (`aria-label` on `Root`), a name for each radio (the row's main text) and a screen-reader name for the radio column's header cell.
- Keep the radio in the accessibility tree when you hide it: use `sr-only`, not `display: none`.


---

# Headless Pagination

`Pagination` is the behaviour of the styled [Pagination](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/pagination/) as unstyled React parts. `Root` holds the page, the page size and the total; inside it go a `PageSizeSelect` (a new size goes back to page 1, as in Carbon), a `PageSelect` (one option per page) and `Prev` / `Next` buttons that disable at the ends and hand focus to each other.

You own the markup: the labels, the range text ("1–10 of 95 items"), the icons and every style. `usePaginationContext()` gives you the numbers for the texts.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { Pagination } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Pagination } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

function Range() {
  const { min, max, totalItems } = Pagination.usePaginationContext();
  return <span className="px-4 text-ink">{min}–{max} of {totalItems} items</span>;
}

const select = 'h-10 cursor-pointer border-x border-hairline bg-transparent px-4 text-ink hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus';
const arrow = 'size-10 border-s border-hairline text-ink hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled data-disabled:hover:bg-transparent';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Pagination.Root totalItems={95} className="flex items-center justify-between border-t border-hairline bg-surface-1 text-sm">
      <div className="flex items-center">
        <label htmlFor="pagination-size" className="ps-4 pe-2 text-ink-muted">Items per page:</label>
        <Pagination.PageSizeSelect id="pagination-size" pageSizes={[10, 25, 50]} className={select} />
        <Range />
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center">
        <Pagination.PageSelect aria-label="Page number" className={select} />
        <Pagination.Prev aria-label="Previous page" className={arrow}>‹</Pagination.Prev>
        <Pagination.Next aria-label="Next page" className={arrow}>›</Pagination.Next>
      </div>
    </Pagination.Root>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Pagination.Root>
  <label />
  <Pagination.PageSizeSelect />
  <Pagination.PageSelect />
  <Pagination.Prev />
  <Pagination.Next />
</Pagination.Root>
```

Every part is optional: a bar with only `Prev` and `Next` works too.

## The texts

`usePaginationContext()` returns `min` and `max` (the first and last item the page shows), `totalItems`, `page`, `pageSize` and `pageCount`. Write them in your own words and language. `PageSelect` takes `renderPage` for the text of each option.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Pagination } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

function Status() {
  const { min, max, totalItems, page, pageCount } = Pagination.usePaginationContext();
  return (
    <p className="text-sm text-ink">
      Contracts {min}–{max} of {totalItems} · page {page} of {pageCount}
    </p>
  );
}

const button = 'h-8 border border-border-strong-1 px-3 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:border-border-disabled data-disabled:text-ink-disabled';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Pagination.Root totalItems={57} defaultPageSize={20} className="grid max-w-md gap-3">
      <Status />
      <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
        <Pagination.Prev className={button}>Previous</Pagination.Prev>
        <Pagination.PageSelect aria-label="Go to page" renderPage={(p) => `Page ${p}`} className="h-8 border-b border-border-strong-1 bg-field-1 px-2 text-sm text-ink focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-focus" />
        <Pagination.Next className={button}>Next</Pagination.Next>
      </div>
    </Pagination.Root>
  );
}
```

## Show the rows of the page

Hold `page` and `pageSize` yourself with `onChange`, and slice your rows with them (or ask the server for that page).


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Pagination } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const contracts = Array.from({ length: 23 }, (_, i) => `Contract ${String(i + 1).padStart(3, '0')}`);
const arrow = 'size-8 text-ink hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-disabled:text-ink-disabled data-disabled:hover:bg-transparent';

export default function Example() {
  const [paging, setPaging] = useState({ page: 1, pageSize: 5 });
  const start = (paging.page - 1) * paging.pageSize;
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-sm gap-2 text-sm text-ink">
      <ol start={start + 1} className="list-decimal ps-6">
        {contracts.slice(start, start + paging.pageSize).map((name) => (
          <li key={name}>{name}</li>
        ))}
      </ol>
      <Pagination.Root totalItems={contracts.length} page={paging.page} pageSize={paging.pageSize} onChange={setPaging} className="flex items-center gap-2 border-t border-hairline pt-2">
        <label htmlFor="pagination-rows-size" className="text-ink-muted">Per page</label>
        <Pagination.PageSizeSelect id="pagination-rows-size" pageSizes={[5, 10]} className="h-8 bg-field-1 px-2 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-focus" />
        <span className="ms-auto" />
        <Pagination.Prev aria-label="Previous page" className={arrow}>‹</Pagination.Prev>
        <Pagination.Next aria-label="Next page" className={arrow}>›</Pagination.Next>
      </Pagination.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Page {paging.page}, page size {paging.pageSize}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Total unknown

With `pagesUnknown`, `Root` doesn't need `totalItems` and has no last page: render no `PageSelect`, and set `isLastPage` when your cursor-based API says there is no next page.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Pagination } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const button = 'h-8 border border-border-strong-1 px-3 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:border-border-disabled data-disabled:text-ink-disabled';

function PageText() {
  const { page, min, max } = Pagination.usePaginationContext();
  return <span className="text-sm text-ink">Page {page} · items {min}–{max}</span>;
}

export default function Example() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
  return (
    <Pagination.Root pagesUnknown isLastPage={page >= 4} page={page} pageSize={25} onChange={(change) => setPage(change.page)} className="flex items-center gap-3">
      <Pagination.Prev className={button}>Previous</Pagination.Prev>
      <PageText />
      <Pagination.Next className={button}>Next</Pagination.Next>
    </Pagination.Root>
  );
}
```

Here the "server" has four pages: `isLastPage` turns true on page 4.

## Style it

Every part has `data-disabled` while it can't be used: `Prev` on the first page, `Next` on the last, and all of them when `Root` is `disabled`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Pagination } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const select = 'h-10 cursor-pointer border-x border-hairline bg-transparent px-4 text-ink hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled data-disabled:hover:bg-transparent';
const arrow = 'size-10 border-s border-hairline text-ink hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled data-disabled:hover:bg-transparent';

export default function Example() {
  const [disabled, setDisabled] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-3">
      <Pagination.Root totalItems={95} disabled={disabled} className="flex items-center justify-end border-t border-hairline bg-surface-1 text-sm data-disabled:opacity-75">
        <Pagination.PageSelect aria-label="Page number" className={select} />
        <Pagination.Prev aria-label="Previous page" className={arrow}>‹</Pagination.Prev>
        <Pagination.Next aria-label="Next page" className={arrow}>›</Pagination.Next>
      </Pagination.Root>
      <label className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm text-ink">
        <input type="checkbox" checked={disabled} onChange={(e) => setDisabled(e.target.checked)} />
        disabled
      </label>
    </div>
  );
}
```
```css
.pagination select:hover,
.pagination button:hover { background: #e8e8e8; }
.pagination [data-disabled] { color: #c6c6c6; cursor: not-allowed; }
.pagination [data-disabled]:hover { background: transparent; }
```

## Parts

### Pagination.Root

Renders a `<div>` around the parts and gives them its state. It takes every `<div>` prop.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | `number` | | The page, from 1 (controlled) |
| `defaultPage` | `number` | `1` | The starting page (uncontrolled) |
| `pageSize` | `number` | | Items per page (controlled) |
| `defaultPageSize` | `number` | `10` | The starting page size (uncontrolled) |
| `totalItems` | `number` | `0` | Items across every page |
| `pagesUnknown` | `boolean` | `false` | No page count: `Next` stops only with `isLastPage` |
| `isLastPage` | `boolean` | `false` | With `pagesUnknown`: this is the last page |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables every select and button |
| `onChange` | `(change: { page, pageSize }) => void` | | After the user changed the page or the page size |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-disabled` | `disabled` is set |

`Pagination.usePaginationContext()` returns `page`, `pageSize`, `totalItems`, `pageCount`, `min`, `max`, `atFirst`, `atLast`, `pagesUnknown`, `disabled`, and `goTo(page)`, `setPageSize(size)`, `step(1 | -1)` to any component inside `Root`.

### Pagination.PageSizeSelect

Renders a `<select>` of page sizes; give it a `<label>`. A new size goes back to page 1. It takes every `<select>` prop except `value` and `defaultValue`.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pageSizes` | `readonly number[]` | `[]` | The choices, one `<option>` each (unless you pass your own `<option>` children) |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-disabled` | `Root` or the select is disabled |

### Pagination.PageSelect

Renders a `<select>` with one option per page; name it with `aria-label`. It takes every `<select>` prop except `value`, `defaultValue` and `children`.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `renderPage` | `(page: number) => ReactNode` | `String` | The text of each page's option |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-disabled` | `Root` or the select is disabled |

### Pagination.Prev, Pagination.Next

Each renders a `<button type="button">` that steps one page. Name icon-only buttons with `aria-label`.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-disabled` | On the first page (`Prev`), on the last page (`Next`), or `Root` is disabled |

## Keyboard and accessibility

- The selects are native: the browser's keys and the phone's picker work.
- `Prev` and `Next` are buttons in the Tab order (`tabIndex={0}`, as Carbon, so Safari focuses them on click). When the pressed arrow disables at the first or last page, focus moves to the other arrow.
- You add the page-size `<label>`, the `aria-label` of the page select and of icon-only arrows, and the range text.
- Tell screen reader users that the rows changed, for example with a polite status line.


---

# Headless Tree view

`TreeView` is the behaviour of the styled [Tree view](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tree-view/) as unstyled React parts, following the WAI-ARIA tree pattern: a `role="tree"` of nested `Node`s, one Tab stop, the arrow keys, Home / End, typing to jump, single or multiple selection, an active node, and children loaded on demand.

You own the markup: each node's `Row` (caret, icon, label), the indent, and every style. State shows as `data-*` attributes on the node and its row; `useNodeContext()` gives a node's depth for the indent.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { TreeView } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { TreeView } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

interface Item {
  value: string;
  label: string;
  children?: Item[];
}

const folders: Item[] = [
  { value: 'contracts', label: 'Contracts', children: [
    { value: 'c1', label: 'Service agreement – Acme' },
    { value: 'c2', label: 'NDA – Globex' },
  ] },
  { value: 'templates', label: 'Templates', children: [{ value: 't1', label: 'Standard NDA' }] },
];

function Row({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const node = TreeView.useNodeContext();
  return (
    <TreeView.Row style={{ paddingInlineStart: 8 + node.depth * 24 }} className="flex h-8 cursor-pointer items-center gap-2 pe-4 text-sm text-ink-muted hover:bg-ghost-hover hover:text-ink data-selected:bg-layer-selected-1 data-selected:text-ink">
      {node.branch ? (
        <TreeView.Toggle className="flex size-4 items-center justify-center">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" className={`size-4 fill-current transition-transform ${node.expanded ? '' : '-rotate-90'}`}><path d="M8 11 3 6l.7-.7L8 9.6l4.3-4.3.7.7z" /></svg>
        </TreeView.Toggle>
      ) : (
        <span className="size-4" />
      )}
      {children}
    </TreeView.Row>
  );
}

function Branch({ item }: { item: Item }) {
  return (
    <TreeView.Node value={item.value} label={item.label} hasChildren={!!item.children} defaultExpanded className="outline-none [&:focus-visible>:first-child]:outline-2 [&:focus-visible>:first-child]:-outline-offset-2 [&:focus-visible>:first-child]:outline-focus">
      <Row>{item.label}</Row>
      {item.children ? (
        <TreeView.Group>
          {item.children.map((child) => <Branch key={child.value} item={child} />)}
        </TreeView.Group>
      ) : null}
    </TreeView.Node>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <TreeView.Root aria-label="Folders" className="max-w-xs bg-layer-1">
      {folders.map((item) => <Branch key={item.value} item={item} />)}
    </TreeView.Root>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<TreeView.Root>
  <TreeView.Node value="…" hasChildren>
    <TreeView.Row>
      <TreeView.Toggle />
      label
    </TreeView.Row>
    <TreeView.Group>
      <TreeView.Node value="…">
        <TreeView.Row>label</TreeView.Row>
      </TreeView.Node>
    </TreeView.Group>
  </TreeView.Node>
</TreeView.Root>
```

`hasChildren` tells a `Node` it is a branch. The tree finds the nodes in the DOM, so they can come from any component, at any depth.

## Selection and the active node

A click, Space or Enter selects a node and makes it the active one. Hold both with `selected` / `onSelect` and `active` / `onActivate`, or start them with `defaultSelected` / `defaultActive`. With `multiselect`, Ctrl / ⌘ + click and Space toggle a node, and Ctrl / ⌘ + A selects every enabled node.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import { TreeView } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

function Row({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const node = TreeView.useNodeContext();
  return (
    <TreeView.Row style={{ paddingInlineStart: 8 + node.depth * 24 }} className="flex h-8 cursor-pointer items-center gap-2 border-s-4 border-transparent pe-4 text-sm text-ink-muted hover:bg-ghost-hover data-active:border-interactive data-selected:bg-layer-selected-1 data-selected:text-ink data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled data-disabled:hover:bg-transparent">
      {node.branch ? <TreeView.Toggle className="w-4 text-center">{node.expanded ? '▾' : '▸'}</TreeView.Toggle> : <span className="w-4" />}
      {children}
    </TreeView.Row>
  );
}

const nodeClass = 'outline-none [&:focus-visible>:first-child]:outline-2 [&:focus-visible>:first-child]:-outline-offset-2 [&:focus-visible>:first-child]:outline-focus';

export default function Example() {
  const [multiselect, setMultiselect] = useState(true);
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string[]>(['contracts-team']);
  const [active, setActive] = useState('contracts-team');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-3">
      <label className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm text-ink">
        <input type="checkbox" checked={multiselect} onChange={(e) => setMultiselect(e.target.checked)} />
        multiselect
      </label>
      <TreeView.Root aria-label="Share with" multiselect={multiselect} selected={selected} onSelect={(next) => setSelected(next)} active={active} onActivate={setActive} className="bg-layer-1">
        <TreeView.Node value="legal" label="Legal" hasChildren defaultExpanded className={nodeClass}>
          <Row>Legal</Row>
          <TreeView.Group>
            <TreeView.Node value="contracts-team" label="Contracts team" className={nodeClass}><Row>Contracts team</Row></TreeView.Node>
            <TreeView.Node value="litigation" label="Litigation team" className={nodeClass}><Row>Litigation team</Row></TreeView.Node>
          </TreeView.Group>
        </TreeView.Node>
        <TreeView.Node value="finance" label="Finance" className={nodeClass}><Row>Finance</Row></TreeView.Node>
        <TreeView.Node value="archive" label="Archive (read only)" disabled className={nodeClass}><Row>Archive (read only)</Row></TreeView.Node>
      </TreeView.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Selected: {selected.join(', ') || '(none)'} · active: {active || '(none)'}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

A `disabled` node can't be selected or opened, and the arrow keys skip it.

## Open and close branches

Each `Node` keeps its own open state (`defaultExpanded`), or takes `expanded` with `onToggle` when you hold it, for example for an "Expand all" button. Right opens a branch and Left closes it; the `Toggle` caret does the same with the mouse.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import { TreeView } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const branches = ['hq', 'legal', 'branches'];

function Row({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const node = TreeView.useNodeContext();
  return (
    <TreeView.Row style={{ paddingInlineStart: 8 + node.depth * 24 }} className="flex h-8 cursor-pointer items-center gap-2 pe-4 text-sm text-ink-muted hover:bg-ghost-hover data-selected:bg-layer-selected-1 data-selected:text-ink">
      {node.branch ? <TreeView.Toggle className="w-4 text-center">{node.expanded ? '▾' : '▸'}</TreeView.Toggle> : <span className="w-4" />}
      {children}
    </TreeView.Row>
  );
}

const nodeClass = 'outline-none [&:focus-visible>:first-child]:outline-2 [&:focus-visible>:first-child]:-outline-offset-2 [&:focus-visible>:first-child]:outline-focus';
const button = 'h-8 px-3 text-sm text-link hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-focus';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState<string[]>(['hq']);
  const props = (value: string) => ({
    expanded: open.includes(value),
    onToggle: (expanded: boolean) => setOpen((now) => (expanded ? [...now, value] : now.filter((v) => v !== value))),
  });
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-xs gap-2">
      <div className="flex gap-2">
        <button type="button" className={button} onClick={() => setOpen(branches)}>Expand all</button>
        <button type="button" className={button} onClick={() => setOpen([])}>Collapse all</button>
      </div>
      <TreeView.Root aria-label="Organisation" className="bg-layer-1">
        <TreeView.Node value="hq" label="Head office" hasChildren {...props('hq')} className={nodeClass}>
          <Row>Head office</Row>
          <TreeView.Group>
            <TreeView.Node value="legal" label="Legal" hasChildren {...props('legal')} className={nodeClass}>
              <Row>Legal</Row>
              <TreeView.Group>
                <TreeView.Node value="contracts" label="Contracts team" className={nodeClass}><Row>Contracts team</Row></TreeView.Node>
              </TreeView.Group>
            </TreeView.Node>
            <TreeView.Node value="finance" label="Finance" className={nodeClass}><Row>Finance</Row></TreeView.Node>
          </TreeView.Group>
        </TreeView.Node>
        <TreeView.Node value="branches" label="Branches" hasChildren {...props('branches')} className={nodeClass}>
          <Row>Branches</Row>
          <TreeView.Group>
            <TreeView.Node value="cnx" label="Chiang Mai" className={nodeClass}><Row>Chiang Mai</Row></TreeView.Node>
          </TreeView.Group>
        </TreeView.Node>
      </TreeView.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Open: {open.join(', ') || '(none)'}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Load children on demand

`lazy` makes a node a branch before it has children. The first time it opens, it gets `data-loading` and `aria-busy` and calls `onLazyLoad(value)`: render the children when they arrive. A returned promise that resolves while there are still no children makes the node a leaf; one that rejects closes it, so opening it again retries.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import { TreeView } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

function Row({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const node = TreeView.useNodeContext();
  let caret: ReactNode = <span className="w-4" />;
  if (node.loading) caret = <span className="size-3 animate-spin rounded-full border-2 border-border-subtle-1 border-t-interactive" aria-hidden="true" />;
  else if (node.branch) caret = <TreeView.Toggle className="w-4 text-center">{node.expanded ? '▾' : '▸'}</TreeView.Toggle>;
  return (
```
