```css
/* className="copy" on Trigger */
.copy { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 40px; height: 40px; border: 0; background: #f4f4f4; cursor: pointer; }
.copy:hover { background: #e8e8e8; }
.copy:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0f62fe; outline-offset: -2px; }
.copy[data-copied] { color: #24a148; }
.copy[data-disabled] { color: #c6c6c6; cursor: not-allowed; }
```

## Parts

### Copy.Root

Renders only its children: it holds the text and the feedback timer, which stops with the component.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` | | What gets copied (required) |
| `onCopy` | `(text: string) => boolean \| void` | | Before copying; return `false` to copy it yourself (the feedback still shows) |
| `feedbackTimeout` | `number` | `2000` | How long `copied` stays true, in ms |

`Copy.useCopyContext()` returns `text`, `copied` and `copy()` to any component inside `Root`.

### Copy.Trigger

A `<button type="button">`; a press copies unless it is disabled. It takes every button prop except `type`.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Copies nothing; the native `disabled` unless `focusableWhenDisabled` |
| `focusableWhenDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disabled but still a Tab stop, with `aria-disabled` |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-copied` | In the feedback moment after a copy |
| `data-disabled` | Disabled |

### Copy.Status

A `<span role="status">`, a polite live region. Its children (your feedback) render only during the moment after a copy, so screen readers announce them once. Hide it with `sr-only`, or let it be the visible feedback.

### Copy.useCopy

`useCopy(text, { onCopy?, feedbackTimeout? })` returns `{ copied, copy }`: `copy()` copies (unless `onCopy` returns `false`) and sets `copied` for `feedbackTimeout` ms. `Root` uses it.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Enter, Space | On `Trigger`: copies |
| Tab | Moves to the next control (a `focusableWhenDisabled` trigger stays in the order) |

The parts give you a real button and a polite live region that speaks only after a successful copy. The copy falls back to `document.execCommand('copy')` where the Clipboard API isn't available (a plain-http intranet page).

You add:

- A name for an icon-only `Trigger`: `aria-label`, or the headless Tooltip's `label`.
- The feedback words inside `Status` ("Copied!", "Link copied").
- A visible feedback for sighted users: the `data-copied` style, a tooltip, or a visible `Status`.
- A visible focus style.


---

# Headless Truncated text

`TruncatedText` is the behaviour of the styled [Truncated text](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/truncated-text/) as unstyled React parts. `Root` measures whether the text in `Content` is cut at `lines` lines (again whenever the box resizes or the text changes), and `Toggle` ("View more / View less") opens the rest with a short height animation. `Content` gets a CSS variable for your line clamp, and the state shows as `data-*` attributes.

You own the clamp itself (one class), the ellipsis, the tooltip for cut text, the toggle's words and every style.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { TruncatedText } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { TruncatedText } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const note = 'Finance asks for two changes before signing: the payment term should be 30 days after delivery instead of 15, and the price review after six months needs a cap of 5%. Legal has no further comments.';

function ToggleText() {
  const { expanded } = TruncatedText.useTruncatedTextContext();
  return <>{expanded ? 'View less' : 'View more'}</>;
}

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <TruncatedText.Root value={note} lines={2} className="w-80 max-w-full text-sm text-ink">
      <TruncatedText.Content className="overflow-hidden line-clamp-(--truncated-text-lines)" />
      <TruncatedText.Toggle className="cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent px-0.5 text-link hover:text-link-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        <ToggleText />
      </TruncatedText.Toggle>
    </TruncatedText.Root>
  );
}
```

`Content` sets `--truncated-text-lines` to the lines to show, or `none` while open. Tailwind's `line-clamp-(--truncated-text-lines)` turns it into the clamp and the ellipsis.

## Anatomy

```tsx
<TruncatedText.Root value="…">
  <TruncatedText.Content />
  <TruncatedText.Toggle />
</TruncatedText.Root>
```

## Full text in a tooltip

Carbon's other choice: no toggle, and the whole text in a tooltip when it is cut. Read `overflowing` from the context and wrap the text in a button with the headless [Tooltip](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-tooltip/) only then; the tooltip's `label` names the button with the whole text.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { TruncatedText, Tooltip } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

function Text() {
  const { value, overflowing } = TruncatedText.useTruncatedTextContext();
  const content = <TruncatedText.Content className="overflow-hidden line-clamp-(--truncated-text-lines)" />;
  if (!overflowing) return content;
  return (
    <Tooltip.Root label={value}>
      <Tooltip.Trigger className="block">
        <button type="button" className="block w-full cursor-default border-0 bg-transparent p-0 text-start [font:inherit] text-inherit focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
          {content}
        </button>
      </Tooltip.Trigger>
      <Tooltip.Popup className="w-max max-w-72 rounded-xs bg-inverse-surface-1 px-4 py-0.5 text-sm text-inverse-ink">{value}</Tooltip.Popup>
    </Tooltip.Root>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-60 max-w-full gap-3 text-sm text-ink">
      <TruncatedText.Root value="CT-2026-0141: Cleaning" lines={1}>
        <Text />
      </TruncatedText.Root>
      <TruncatedText.Root value="CT-2026-0142: Office supplies for the head office and three regional branches" lines={1}>
        <Text />
      </TruncatedText.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Lines

`lines` (2) is how many lines show before the cut; `0` shows everything and never counts as cut. A text that fits isn't `overflowing`, and `Toggle` renders nothing.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { TruncatedText } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const scope = 'Supply of A4 paper, toner and stationery for the head office and the three regional branches, delivered monthly from January to December 2026, with a price review after six months.';

function Status() {
  const { overflowing } = TruncatedText.useTruncatedTextContext();
  return <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">{overflowing ? 'cut' : 'fits'}</p>;
}

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-80 max-w-full gap-4 text-sm text-ink">
      {[1, 3, 0].map((lines) => (
        <TruncatedText.Root key={lines} value={scope} lines={lines}>
          <TruncatedText.Content className="overflow-hidden line-clamp-(--truncated-text-lines)" />
          <Status />
        </TruncatedText.Root>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Hold the open state

`expanded` with `onExpandedChange` holds the state yourself; `defaultExpanded` only sets the start. `onExpandedChange` fires on a press of `Toggle`. Changing `expanded` yourself opens or closes without the animation, which plays only on a press.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { TruncatedText } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const notes = [
  { id: 'finance', text: 'Finance: the payment term should be 30 days after delivery instead of 15, and the price review after six months needs a cap of 5%. Everything else is fine.' },
  { id: 'legal', text: 'Legal: clause 7.2 (late delivery penalty) should refer to working days, not calendar days. Clause 9 (termination) is fine as written.' },
];

const toggle = 'cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent px-0.5 text-link hover:text-link-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus';
const button = 'h-8 cursor-pointer bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-link hover:bg-ghost-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState<Record<string, boolean>>({});
  const setAll = (value: boolean) => setOpen(Object.fromEntries(notes.map((n) => [n.id, value])));
  return (
    <div className="grid w-96 max-w-full gap-4 text-sm text-ink">
      <div className="flex gap-2">
        <button type="button" className={button} onClick={() => setAll(true)}>Open all notes</button>
        <button type="button" className={button} onClick={() => setAll(false)}>Close all notes</button>
      </div>
      {notes.map((note) => (
        <TruncatedText.Root key={note.id} value={note.text} expanded={!!open[note.id]} onExpandedChange={(value) => setOpen((o) => ({ ...o, [note.id]: value }))}>
          <TruncatedText.Content className="overflow-hidden line-clamp-(--truncated-text-lines)" />
          <TruncatedText.Toggle className={toggle}>{open[note.id] ? 'View less' : 'View more'}</TruncatedText.Toggle>
        </TruncatedText.Root>
      ))}
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Open: {JSON.stringify(open)}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Your own content

`Content` shows `value` unless you give it children. Give children to add markup (a bold label, a link) while `value` stays the plain text, for the tooltip and for measuring again when it changes.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { TruncatedText } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const text = 'Legal: clause 7.2 (late delivery penalty) should refer to working days, not calendar days. Clause 9 (termination) is fine as written. Please send the revised draft by Friday.';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <TruncatedText.Root value={text} lines={2} className="w-80 max-w-full text-sm text-ink">
      <TruncatedText.Content className="overflow-hidden line-clamp-(--truncated-text-lines)">
        <strong>Legal:</strong> clause 7.2 (late delivery penalty) should refer to working days, not calendar days. Clause 9 (termination) is fine as written. Please send the revised draft by Friday.
      </TruncatedText.Content>
      <TruncatedText.Toggle className="cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent px-0.5 text-link focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        Read the full note
      </TruncatedText.Toggle>
    </TruncatedText.Root>
  );
}
```

## Style it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { TruncatedText } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const notes = [
  'Approved by the department head.',
  'Approved with a condition: the vendor must send the delivery schedule before the first order, and finance must see it too.',
];

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-80 max-w-full gap-4 text-sm text-ink">
      {notes.map((note) => (
        <TruncatedText.Root key={note} value={note} lines={1} className="group data-overflowing:border-s-2 data-overflowing:border-border-interactive data-overflowing:ps-2">
          <TruncatedText.Content className="overflow-hidden line-clamp-(--truncated-text-lines)" />
          <TruncatedText.Toggle className="cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent px-0.5 text-link focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus">
            <span className="group-data-expanded:hidden">View more</span>
            <span className="hidden group-data-expanded:inline">View less</span>
          </TruncatedText.Toggle>
        </TruncatedText.Root>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```
```css
/* className="note" on Root, "text" on Content */
.text { display: -webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: var(--truncated-text-lines); overflow: hidden; }
.note[data-overflowing] { border-inline-start: 2px solid #0f62fe; padding-inline-start: 8px; }
```

## Parts

### TruncatedText.Root

A `<div>`: it holds the state and measures whether the text is cut as the box resizes. It takes every `<div>` prop.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | | The text (required; measured again when it changes) |
| `lines` | `number` | `2` | Lines shown before the cut; 0 = all |
| `expanded` | `boolean` | | Whether the text shows in full (controlled) |
| `defaultExpanded` | `boolean` | `false` | The start state (uncontrolled) |
| `onExpandedChange` | `(expanded: boolean) => void` | | On a press of `Toggle` |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-overflowing` | The text is cut (kept while open) |
| `data-expanded` | Open |

`TruncatedText.useTruncatedTextContext()` returns `value`, `overflowing`, `expanded`, `closing` (a collapse is animating), `clamp` and `toggle()` to any component inside `Root`.

### TruncatedText.Content

A `<div>` with the text: `value`, or your children. It gets the `id` that `Toggle` points at, and the style `--truncated-text-lines`: the lines, or `none` while open, while a collapse animates, or with `lines` 0. The height animation runs on it (`--ui-duration-moderate`, 110ms; none when that is 0, as with reduced motion).

### TruncatedText.Toggle

A `<button type="button">` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` (the `Content`), rendered only while the text is cut or open. A press opens or closes. It takes every button prop except `type`; give it the words.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-expanded` | Open |

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves to `Toggle` (or to your tooltip button) |
| Enter, Space | On `Toggle`: opens or closes the text |

The parts set `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` on `Toggle`, and keep the toggle out of the page while the text fits.

You add:

- The clamp on `Content` (`line-clamp-(--truncated-text-lines)` with `overflow-hidden`).
- The toggle's words ("View more" / "View less").
- For the tooltip pattern: a button named by the whole text, only while it is cut, so screen readers read all of it.
- A visible focus style.


---

# Headless Loading

`Loading` is the behaviour of the styled [Loading](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/loading/) without a single class. `Loading.Root` decides when the spinner shows: while `active`, after `delay` ms, and once shown for at least `minDuration` ms, so quick work never flashes a spinner. `Spinner` makes your graphic an assertive live region while it shows. `Indicator` holds focus: as a modal dialog over the page with `modal`, or as the waiting spot of a busy `Area`, and focus goes back where it was afterwards.

You own the spinner graphic, the overlay, hiding the parts while they don't show, and every style. Each part has `data-shown` while the spinner shows.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { Loading } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Loading } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Loading.Root>
      <Loading.Spinner className="size-[88px] animate-spin [animation-duration:690ms] motion-reduce:[animation-duration:2s]">
        <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" role="img" aria-label="Loading contracts" className="block size-full fill-transparent">
          <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="44" className="stroke-interactive [stroke-dasharray:276.46_276.46] [stroke-dashoffset:52.53] [stroke-width:10]" />
        </svg>
      </Loading.Spinner>
    </Loading.Root>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Loading.Root>
  <Loading.Area />
  <Loading.Indicator>
    <Loading.Spinner />
  </Loading.Indicator>
</Loading.Root>
```

`Area` and `Indicator` are optional: a plain spinner needs only `Root` and `Spinner`.

## Start, stop and wait

`active` starts and stops it (on by default). `delay` waits before showing, and `minDuration` keeps it up once shown. `useLoadingContext().shown` tells any component inside `Root` whether it shows now. The parts don't hide themselves: hide the spinner while it has no `data-shown`. Try the quick check: it ends before the 300 ms delay, so nothing shows.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Loading } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const button = 'h-10 bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus';

function Shown() {
  const { shown } = Loading.useLoadingContext();
  return <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Shown: {String(shown)}</p>;
}

export default function Example() {
  const [active, setActive] = useState(false);
  const run = (ms: number) => {
    setActive(true);
    setTimeout(() => setActive(false), ms);
  };
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-3">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
        <button type="button" className={button} onClick={() => run(200)}>Quick check (0.2 s)</button>
        <button type="button" className={button} onClick={() => run(2000)}>Full check (2 s)</button>
      </div>
      <Loading.Root active={active} delay={300} minDuration={500}>
        <div className="flex h-6 items-center gap-2">
          <Loading.Spinner className="hidden size-4 animate-spin [animation-duration:690ms] data-shown:block">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" role="img" aria-label="Checking vendor documents" className="block size-full fill-transparent">
              <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="42" className="stroke-layer-accent [stroke-width:16]" />
              <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="42" className="stroke-interactive [stroke-dasharray:276.46_276.46] [stroke-dashoffset:143.76] [stroke-width:16]" />
            </svg>
          </Loading.Spinner>
          <Shown />
        </div>
      </Loading.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Over one area

Wrap the content in `Area` and put the `Indicator` over it. While it shows, the area is inert and `aria-busy`, and the indicator is a group named by its `aria-label`. Focus that was inside the area waits on the indicator, then goes back: press Refresh with the keyboard and focus returns to it.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Loading } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const refresh = () => {
    setBusy(true);
    setTimeout(() => setBusy(false), 2000);
  };
  return (
    <Loading.Root active={busy}>
      <div className="relative max-w-md">
        <Loading.Area className="grid justify-items-start gap-3 border border-hairline bg-layer-1 p-4 text-ink">
          <h4 className="text-sm font-semibold">Contract CT-2026-118</h4>
          <p className="text-sm">Siam Logistics Co., Ltd. · ฿1,250,000</p>
          <button type="button" onClick={refresh} className="h-10 bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">Refresh (2 s)</button>
        </Loading.Area>
        <Loading.Indicator aria-label="Refreshing the contract" className="absolute inset-0 z-1 hidden items-center justify-center bg-overlay outline-none data-shown:flex">
          <Loading.Spinner className="size-[88px] animate-spin [animation-duration:690ms]">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" role="img" aria-label="Refreshing the contract" className="block size-full fill-transparent">
              <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="44" className="stroke-interactive [stroke-dasharray:276.46_276.46] [stroke-dashoffset:52.53] [stroke-width:10]" />
            </svg>
          </Loading.Spinner>
        </Loading.Indicator>
      </div>
    </Loading.Root>
  );
}
```

## Over the whole page

With `modal`, the `Indicator` is a modal dialog while it shows. It takes focus, and Tab and focus moving elsewhere come back to it; a modal dialog opened above it is left alone. When it stops, focus goes back where it was. It is no `<dialog>`, so Esc can't close it.

The overlay is `position: fixed`. In this demo it sits in a box with a `transform`, so it covers only the box.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Loading } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const generate = () => {
    setBusy(true);
    setTimeout(() => setBusy(false), 3000);
  };
  return (
    <div className="relative h-60 overflow-hidden border border-hairline bg-canvas text-ink [transform:translateZ(0)]">
      <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-4 p-4">
        <p className="text-sm">Quarterly purchasing report, 42 pages</p>
        <button type="button" onClick={generate} className="h-10 bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">Generate PDF (3 s)</button>
      </div>
      <Loading.Root active={busy} modal>
        <Loading.Indicator aria-label="Generating the PDF" className="fixed inset-0 z-10 hidden items-center justify-center bg-overlay outline-none data-shown:flex">
          <Loading.Spinner className="size-[88px] animate-spin [animation-duration:690ms]">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" role="img" aria-label="Generating the PDF" className="block size-full fill-transparent">
              <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="44" className="stroke-interactive [stroke-dasharray:276.46_276.46] [stroke-dashoffset:52.53] [stroke-width:10]" />
            </svg>
          </Loading.Spinner>
        </Loading.Indicator>
      </Loading.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Style it

Every part has `data-shown` while the spinner shows. Hide the indicator and the spinner without it, and fade or blur the area with it.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Loading } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-3">
      <button type="button" onClick={() => setBusy(!busy)} className="h-10 bg-interactive px-4 text-sm text-on-primary hover:bg-blue-hover focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus">
        {busy ? 'Stop' : 'Start'}
      </button>
      <Loading.Root active={busy} delay={200}>
        <div className="relative w-full max-w-md">
          <Loading.Area className="border border-hairline bg-layer-1 p-4 text-sm text-ink transition-opacity data-shown:opacity-40">
            Vendor documents: company certificate, VAT registration, bank book.
          </Loading.Area>
          <Loading.Indicator aria-label="Checking documents" className="absolute inset-0 hidden items-center justify-center outline-none data-shown:flex">
            <Loading.Spinner className="size-8 animate-spin [animation-duration:690ms] motion-reduce:[animation-duration:2s]">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" role="img" aria-label="Checking documents" className="block size-full fill-transparent">
                <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="42" className="stroke-layer-accent [stroke-width:12]" />
                <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="42" className="stroke-interactive [stroke-dasharray:276.46_276.46] [stroke-dashoffset:143.76] [stroke-width:12]" />
              </svg>
            </Loading.Spinner>
          </Loading.Indicator>
        </div>
      </Loading.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```
```css
/* className="area" on Area, "indicator" on Indicator, "spinner" on Spinner */
.area[data-shown] { opacity: 0.4; }
.indicator { position: absolute; inset: 0; display: none; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }
.indicator[data-shown] { display: flex; }
.spinner { width: 32px; height: 32px; animation: spin 690ms linear infinite; }
@keyframes spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } }
```

## Parts

### Loading.Root

Renders only its children. It holds whether the spinner shows and moves focus while it does.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `active` | `boolean` | `true` | Starts and stops it; false hides it |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | Milliseconds `active` must last before it shows |
| `minDuration` | `number` | `0` | Once shown, the least milliseconds it stays |
| `modal` | `boolean` | `false` | A page overlay: the `Indicator` is a modal dialog that holds focus while shown |

`Loading.useLoadingContext()` returns `shown` and `modal` (plus the refs of the area and the indicator) to any component inside `Root`.

### Loading.Area

A `<div>` around the content that a contained loading covers. While shown it is `inert` and has `aria-busy="true"`.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-shown` | The spinner shows |

### Loading.Indicator

A `<div>` that holds focus while it shows. It takes every div prop except `role` and `tabIndex`; name it with `aria-label`. While shown it has `tabIndex={-1}`, `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="true"` when `Root` is `modal`, or else `role="group"`, and its `aria-label`. While hidden it has no role and no name.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-shown` | The spinner shows |

### Loading.Spinner

A `<div>` around your spinner graphic, with `aria-atomic="true"`. While shown it is an assertive live region (`aria-live="assertive"`), so the graphic's name is announced; while hidden, `aria-live="off"`.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-shown` | The spinner shows |

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab | With `modal`: stays on the indicator while it shows |

The parts:

- move focus to the `Indicator` when a modal loading shows, or when focus was inside the `Area`, and give it back afterwards;
- set `role`, `aria-modal`, `aria-label` and `tabIndex` on the `Indicator` while it shows;
- make the `Area` inert and `aria-busy`;
- make the `Spinner` an assertive live region while it shows.

You add:

- The spinner graphic with an accessible name (`role="img"` and `aria-label` on the `<svg>`) and the `aria-label` of the `Indicator`. Say what is loading.
- Hiding the parts while they have no `data-shown`, and the overlay colour.
- A slower or still spinner under `prefers-reduced-motion`.


---

# Headless Tag

`Tag` is the behaviour of the styled [Tag](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/tag/) as three unstyled React parts. `Tag.Root` is a read-only or dismissible tag (a `<span>`). `Tag.Dismiss` is its close button: a press calls `onDismiss` and doesn't reach a click handler around the tag. `Tag.Toggle` is a selectable tag: a `<button aria-pressed>` that flips on a press, Space or Enter. An operational tag is a plain `<button>`, so it needs no part.

You own the markup and every style: the colours, the size, the icon, the ellipsis. The tag stays until you remove it from your state.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { Tag } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Tag } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Tag.Root className="inline-flex h-6 items-center rounded-full bg-tag-background-green px-2 text-xs text-tag-color-green">
      Signed
    </Tag.Root>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Tag.Root>
  <Tag.Dismiss />
</Tag.Root>

<Tag.Toggle />
```

## Dismissible

Put `Tag.Dismiss` inside `Tag.Root` and remove the tag in `onDismiss`. Name the button with `aria-label`, different for each tag. When the removed tag had focus, move focus to the next tag yourself.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { Tag } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [filters, setFilters] = useState(['Sales', 'Legal', 'Signed in 2026']);
  const row = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const remove = (index: number) => {
    setFilters(filters.filter((_, i) => i !== index));
    // after React removes it, focus the close button now at the same place (or the last one)
    requestAnimationFrame(() => {
      const buttons = row.current?.querySelectorAll('button');
      buttons?.[Math.min(index, buttons.length - 1)]?.focus();
    });
  };
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <div ref={row} className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
        {filters.map((filter, index) => (
          <Tag.Root key={filter} className="inline-flex h-6 items-center rounded-full bg-tag-background-blue ps-2 text-xs text-tag-color-blue">
            {filter}
            <Tag.Dismiss
              aria-label={`Remove filter ${filter}`}
              onDismiss={() => remove(index)}
              className="ms-0.5 flex size-6 items-center justify-center rounded-full hover:bg-tag-hover-blue focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
            >
              <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" className="size-4 fill-current" aria-hidden="true">
                <path d="m12 4.7-.7-.7L8 7.3 4.7 4l-.7.7L7.3 8 4 11.3l.7.7L8 8.7l3.3 3.3.7-.7L8.7 8z" />
              </svg>
            </Tag.Dismiss>
          </Tag.Root>
        ))}
      </div>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Filters: {filters.join(', ') || 'none'}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Selectable

`Tag.Toggle` keeps its own state with `defaultSelected`, or follows `selected` when you control it. `onSelectedChange` gets the new state after each press.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Tag } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const departments = ['Sales', 'Legal', 'Finance', 'Human resources'];

export default function Example() {
  const [shown, setShown] = useState<string[]>(['Sales']);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
        {departments.map((dept) => (
          <Tag.Toggle
            key={dept}
            selected={shown.includes(dept)}
            onSelectedChange={(on) => setShown(on ? [...shown, dept] : shown.filter((d) => d !== dept))}
            className="inline-flex h-6 items-center rounded-full border border-border-inverse bg-layer-1 px-2 text-xs text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus data-selected:bg-layer-selected-inverse data-selected:text-inverse-ink"
          >
            {dept}
          </Tag.Toggle>
        ))}
      </div>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Showing: {shown.join(', ') || 'every department'}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Operational

An operational tag is your own `<button type="button">` drawn as a tag. When it shows or hides something, give it `aria-expanded` (and `aria-controls`); when its text is only a number, name it with `aria-label`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useId, useState } from 'react';
import { Tag } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const listId = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
        <Tag.Root className="inline-flex h-6 items-center rounded-full bg-tag-background-blue px-2 text-xs text-tag-color-blue">Sales</Tag.Root>
        <Tag.Root className="inline-flex h-6 items-center rounded-full bg-tag-background-blue px-2 text-xs text-tag-color-blue">Legal</Tag.Root>
        <button
          type="button"
          aria-label="3 more departments"
          aria-expanded={open}
          aria-controls={listId}
          onClick={() => setOpen(!open)}
          className="inline-flex h-6 items-center rounded-full border border-tag-border-blue bg-tag-background-blue px-2 text-xs text-tag-color-blue hover:bg-tag-hover-blue focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus"
        >
          +3
        </button>
      </div>
      <p id={listId} hidden={!open} className="text-sm text-ink">
        Finance, Procurement, Human resources
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled

`disabled` on `Tag.Root` disables its `Tag.Dismiss` too (a `disabled` of its own on `Dismiss` wins). `Tag.Toggle` takes `disabled` like any button. Each part then has `data-disabled`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Tag } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
      <Tag.Root disabled className="inline-flex h-6 items-center rounded-full bg-tag-background-blue ps-2 text-xs text-tag-color-blue data-disabled:bg-layer-1 data-disabled:text-ink-disabled">
        Legal
        <Tag.Dismiss aria-label="Remove filter Legal" className="ms-0.5 flex size-6 items-center justify-center rounded-full data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" className="size-4 fill-current" aria-hidden="true">
            <path d="m12 4.7-.7-.7L8 7.3 4.7 4l-.7.7L7.3 8 4 11.3l.7.7L8 8.7l3.3 3.3.7-.7L8.7 8z" />
          </svg>
        </Tag.Dismiss>
      </Tag.Root>
      <Tag.Toggle disabled defaultSelected className="inline-flex h-6 items-center rounded-full border border-border-inverse px-2 text-xs data-selected:bg-layer-selected-inverse data-selected:text-inverse-ink data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:border-ink-disabled data-disabled:bg-layer-1 data-disabled:text-ink-disabled">
        Finance
      </Tag.Toggle>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Style it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Tag } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [disabled, setDisabled] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
        <Tag.Root disabled={disabled} className="inline-flex h-6 max-w-52 items-center rounded-full bg-tag-background-purple ps-2 text-xs text-tag-color-purple data-disabled:bg-layer-1 data-disabled:text-ink-disabled">
          <span className="truncate">Procurement and supplier management</span>
          <Tag.Dismiss aria-label="Remove Procurement" className="ms-0.5 flex size-6 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full hover:bg-tag-hover-purple focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:hover:bg-transparent">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" className="size-4 fill-current" aria-hidden="true">
              <path d="m12 4.7-.7-.7L8 7.3 4.7 4l-.7.7L7.3 8 4 11.3l.7.7L8 8.7l3.3 3.3.7-.7L8.7 8z" />
            </svg>
          </Tag.Dismiss>
        </Tag.Root>
        <Tag.Toggle disabled={disabled} className="inline-flex h-6 items-center rounded-full border border-border-inverse bg-layer-1 px-2 text-xs text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-1 focus-visible:outline-focus data-selected:bg-layer-selected-inverse data-selected:text-inverse-ink data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:border-ink-disabled data-disabled:text-ink-disabled">
          Selectable
        </Tag.Toggle>
      </div>
      <label className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm text-ink">
        <input type="checkbox" checked={disabled} onChange={(e) => setDisabled(e.target.checked)} />
        disabled
      </label>
    </div>
  );
}
```
```css
.tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 24px; border-radius: 16px; background: #d0e2ff; color: #0043ce; }
.tag[data-disabled] { background: #f4f4f4; color: #8d8d8d; }
.tag-toggle[data-selected] { background: #393939; color: #fff; }
.tag-toggle[data-disabled] { cursor: not-allowed; }
```

## Parts

### Tag.Root

A `<span>`, the tag itself. It takes every `<span>` prop.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables its `Tag.Dismiss` too |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-disabled` | `disabled` is set |

### Tag.Dismiss

A `<button type="button">`, the close button. It takes every button prop except `type`. Its press stops there: a click handler around the tag doesn't see it.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | — | After a press, not while disabled |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | the root's | Its own state; left out, it follows `Tag.Root` |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-disabled` | Disabled, by itself or through `Tag.Root` |

### Tag.Toggle

A `<button type="button">` with `aria-pressed`, the selectable tag. It takes every button prop except `type` and `aria-pressed`.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `selected` | `boolean` | — | The state (controlled) |
| `defaultSelected` | `boolean` | `false` | The starting state (uncontrolled) |
| `onSelectedChange` | `(selected: boolean, event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void` | — | After the user flips it |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-selected` | On |
| `data-disabled` | `disabled` is set |

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves to a close button or a selectable tag. `Tag.Root` itself isn't a tab stop. |
| Enter, Space | Presses the close button, or flips a selectable tag |

The parts set `type="button"`, `aria-pressed` on `Tag.Toggle`, and the native `disabled`.

You add:

- A name on each `Tag.Dismiss`, for example `aria-label="Remove filter Legal"`.
- Focus after a removal: the removed button takes the focus with it.
- `aria-label` on an operational tag whose text is only a number, and `aria-expanded` when it shows or hides something.
- The full text in `title` when you cut a long tag with an ellipsis.
- A visible focus style.


---

# Headless Card

`Card` is the behaviour of the styled [Card](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/card/) as two unstyled React parts. `Card.Root` is the card: with `href` one link (`<a>`), with `clickable` one button (a `<div role="button">`, since a card holds block content a `<button>` may not), else a plain box (`<div>`). A click, or Enter or Space on the card itself, calls `onClick`. `Card.Actions` marks the card's own small buttons: a click or key that starts inside it belongs to that button, not to the card.

You own everything else: the media, the header, the title, the body, the footer and every style. The styled card's other parts (media, header, title, body, footer) are layout, so here they are your own elements.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { Card } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Card } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Card.Root className="max-w-sm bg-layer-1 text-ink">
      <div className="p-4">
        <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Contract</p>
        <h3 className="text-base font-semibold">Office lease, Silom branch</h3>
      </div>
      <p className="p-4 pt-0 text-sm">Waiting for the landlord's signature.</p>
    </Card.Root>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<Card.Root>
  <Card.Actions />
</Card.Root>
```

## Linked card

With `href` the whole card is one `<a>` (with `tabIndex={0}`, so Safari focuses it on a click and stops on it with Tab). `target="_blank"` adds `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. `onClick` runs too, so a single-page app can route the click; the example prevents the navigation and shows the address. Name the link with `aria-label`, as its whole text would make a long name.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Card } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [opened, setOpened] = useState('');
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <Card.Root
        href="/policies/procurement"
        aria-label="Open the procurement policy"
        onClick={(event) => {
          event.preventDefault();
          setOpened('/policies/procurement');
        }}
        className="block max-w-sm border border-border-tile-1 bg-layer-1 p-4 text-ink no-underline hover:bg-layer-hover-1 focus:outline-2 focus:outline-focus"
      >
        <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Policy</p>
        <h3 className="mb-4 text-base font-semibold">Procurement policy</h3>
        <p className="text-sm">Who can approve purchases, and up to what amount.</p>
      </Card.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Router would open: {opened || 'nothing yet'}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Clickable card

With `clickable` the card is a `<div role="button" tabIndex={0}>`: a click, or Enter or Space while the card itself has focus, calls `onClick`. Name it with `aria-label`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Card } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const templates = [
  { id: 'sale', title: 'Sale contract', text: 'Goods, price and delivery.' },
  { id: 'lease', title: 'Lease contract', text: 'Property, rent and term.' },
];

export default function Example() {
  const [chosen, setChosen] = useState('');
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <div className="grid grid-cols-[repeat(auto-fill,minmax(200px,1fr))] gap-4">
        {templates.map((template) => (
          <Card.Root
            key={template.id}
            clickable
            aria-label={`Start a ${template.title.toLowerCase()}`}
            onClick={() => setChosen(template.title)}
            className="cursor-pointer border border-border-tile-1 bg-layer-1 p-4 text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-1 active:bg-layer-active-1 focus:outline-2 focus:outline-focus"
          >
            <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Template</p>
            <h3 className="mb-4 text-base font-semibold">{template.title}</h3>
            <p className="text-sm">{template.text}</p>
          </Card.Root>
        ))}
      </div>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Chosen: {chosen || 'nothing yet'}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Buttons inside a card

Carbon's guideline keeps other controls out of a link or clickable card: put buttons in a plain card, or use a [Headless Product card](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-product-card/) with click zones. If a button must sit inside one anyway, wrap it in `Card.Actions` (a `<div data-card-actions>`). A click inside it is that button's: the card's `onClick` doesn't run. Enter and Space on a focused button never press the card either, as the card only answers keys while it has focus itself. Screen readers handle controls inside a `role="button"` poorly, which is why Carbon advises against it.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Card } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [log, setLog] = useState('nothing yet');
  const [starred, setStarred] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <Card.Root
        clickable
        aria-label="Open the branch renovation project"
        onClick={() => setLog('card: open the project')}
        className="relative max-w-sm cursor-pointer border border-border-tile-1 bg-layer-1 p-4 text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-1 focus:outline-2 focus:outline-focus"
      >
        <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Project</p>
        <h3 className="mb-4 text-base font-semibold">Branch renovation</h3>
        <p className="text-sm">Silom branch, second floor.</p>
        <Card.Actions className="absolute end-2 top-2">
          <button
            type="button"
            aria-label="Star"
            aria-pressed={starred}
            onClick={() => {
              setStarred(!starred);
              setLog(starred ? 'star: off' : 'star: on');
            }}
            className="flex size-8 items-center justify-center text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
          >
            {starred ? '★' : '☆'}
          </button>
        </Card.Actions>
      </Card.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Last press: {log}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled

`disabled` stops `onClick`. A disabled linked card becomes a plain box (or the button, when it is also `clickable`); a disabled clickable card keeps its role, gets `aria-disabled` and leaves the tab order (`tabIndex={-1}`). The box and the button have `data-disabled`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { Card } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <Card.Root
      clickable
      disabled
      aria-label="Start a loan contract (unavailable)"
      onClick={() => alert('never runs')}
      className="max-w-sm border border-border-tile-1 bg-layer-1 p-4 text-ink data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:border-border-disabled data-disabled:text-ink-disabled"
    >
      <p className="text-xs">Template</p>
      <h3 className="mb-4 text-base font-semibold">Loan contract</h3>
      <p className="text-sm">Being revised by the legal department until 15 October.</p>
    </Card.Root>
  );
}
```

## Style it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Card } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [disabled, setDisabled] = useState(false);
  const [presses, setPresses] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <Card.Root
        clickable
        disabled={disabled}
        aria-label="Open the monthly summary"
        onClick={() => setPresses(presses + 1)}
        className="max-w-sm bg-layer-1 text-ink outline-transparent data-clickable:cursor-pointer data-clickable:border data-clickable:border-border-tile-1 data-clickable:hover:bg-layer-hover-1 focus:outline-2 focus:outline-focus data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:border-border-disabled data-disabled:text-ink-disabled data-disabled:hover:bg-layer-1"
      >
        <div className="p-4">
          <p className="text-xs">Report</p>
          <h3 className="text-base font-semibold">Monthly contract summary</h3>
        </div>
        <div className="flex justify-end p-4" aria-hidden="true">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" className="size-4 fill-current">
            <path d="M9.3 3.7 13.1 7.5H1v1h12.1l-3.8 3.8.7.7 5-5-5-5z" />
          </svg>
        </div>
      </Card.Root>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-4 text-sm text-ink">
        <label className="flex items-center gap-2">
          <input type="checkbox" checked={disabled} onChange={(e) => setDisabled(e.target.checked)} />
          disabled
        </label>
        <span className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Presses: {presses}</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```
```css
.card { background: #f4f4f4; }
.card[data-link],
.card[data-clickable] { border: 1px solid #c6c6c6; cursor: pointer; }
.card[data-link]:hover,
.card[data-clickable]:hover { background: #e8e8e8; }
.card[data-disabled] { color: #8d8d8d; cursor: not-allowed; }
```

## Parts

### Card.Root

An `<a>` with `href` (unless disabled), a `<div role="button">` with `clickable`, else a `<div>`. It takes every `<div>` prop; `ref` points at whichever element it renders.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `href` | `string` | — | Makes the whole card one link |
| `target` | `'_self' \| '_blank'` | `'_self'` | `_blank` adds `rel="noopener noreferrer"` |
| `clickable` | `boolean` | `false` | Makes the whole card one button (`tabIndex` 0, Enter and Space) |
| `onClick` | `(event: MouseEvent<HTMLElement> \| KeyboardEvent<HTMLElement>) => void` | — | The card was pressed: a linked or clickable card only, not from inside `Card.Actions`, not while disabled |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | No `onClick`; a link falls back to the box or the button |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-link` | It renders the link |
| `data-clickable` | It renders the button |
| `data-disabled` | `disabled` is set, on the box or the button |

### Card.Actions

A `<div data-card-actions>` for a button that must sit inside a link or clickable card (Carbon advises against it). It takes every `<div>` prop. A click that starts inside it doesn't call the card's `onClick`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves to a linked or clickable card, then to the buttons inside it |
| Enter | Follows a linked card; presses a clickable card that has focus itself |
| Space | Presses a clickable card that has focus itself |

The part sets `role="button"`, `tabIndex`, `aria-disabled` and `rel`.

You add:

- A name on a linked or clickable card: `aria-label`, since its whole text would be read as the name.
- Headings for the titles, at the level the page needs.
- `alt` text for media that carries information, `alt=""` for decoration.
- A visible focus style on the card and its buttons.
- A sentence in a disabled card saying why it can't be used.


---

# Headless Product card

`ProductCard` is the behaviour of the styled [Product card](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/product-card/) (Carbon for IBM Products' legacy `ProductiveCard` and `ExpressiveCard`) as unstyled React parts. For new work, use [Headless Card](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-card/) instead.

What the parts give you is a clickable zone that never swallows the card's own controls. `ProductCard.ClickZone` is an empty `<button>` that you lay over the zone (`position: absolute; inset: 0`), with the card's buttons stacked above it. The buttons stay siblings of the zone's button: separate tab stops whose clicks never press the card. The zone's button is named by `ProductCard.Title` (else `Label`, else `Body`) and described by `Description`; a click, Enter or Space on it calls the root's `onClick`. You own the layout, the buttons and every style.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { ProductCard } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { ProductCard } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ProductCard.Root className="max-w-sm bg-layer-1 p-4 text-ink">
      <ProductCard.Label className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Department</ProductCard.Label>
      <ProductCard.Title className="text-base font-semibold">Legal</ProductCard.Title>
      <ProductCard.Description className="text-xs text-ink-muted">6 people</ProductCard.Description>
      <ProductCard.Body className="pt-2 text-sm">14 contracts in review, 2 overdue.</ProductCard.Body>
    </ProductCard.Root>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<ProductCard.Root>
  <ProductCard.ClickZone />
  <ProductCard.Label />
  <ProductCard.Title />
  <ProductCard.Description />
  <ProductCard.Body />
</ProductCard.Root>
```

## Clickable card

Give `Root` an `onClick` and `position: relative`, put `ClickZone` in it with `position: absolute; inset: 0`, and lift the card's own buttons above it with `position: relative; z-index: 1`. Here a click on the card opens the project, and the edit button only edits.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { ProductCard } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [log, setLog] = useState('nothing yet');
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <ProductCard.Root
        onClick={() => setLog('card: open the project')}
        className="relative max-w-sm border border-border-tile-1 bg-layer-1 p-4 text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-1"
      >
        <ProductCard.ClickZone className="absolute inset-0 cursor-pointer focus:outline-2 focus:-outline-offset-2 focus:outline-focus" />
        <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-2">
          <div>
            <ProductCard.Title className="text-base font-semibold">Branch renovation</ProductCard.Title>
            <ProductCard.Description className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Due in 3 days</ProductCard.Description>
          </div>
          <button
            type="button"
            aria-label="Edit"
            onClick={() => setLog('edit button')}
            className="relative z-1 flex size-8 items-center justify-center hover:bg-layer-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
          >
            <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" className="size-4 fill-current" aria-hidden="true">
              <path d="M1 13h14v1H1zM12.7 4.5 10.5 2.3a1 1 0 0 0-1.4 0L3 8.4V11h2.6l6.1-6.1a1 1 0 0 0 0-1.4zM5.2 10H4V8.8l4-4 1.2 1.2zm4.7-4.7L8.7 4.1l1.1-1.1L11 4.2z" />
            </svg>
          </button>
        </div>
        <ProductCard.Body className="pt-2 text-sm">Silom branch, second floor.</ProductCard.Body>
      </ProductCard.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Last press: {log}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## A smaller zone

Carbon's productive card can make only part of the card clickable: the header with the body, or the body alone. Put `ClickZone` inside that part and make the part `position: relative`. The footer button below stays outside the zone.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { ProductCard } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [log, setLog] = useState('nothing yet');
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <ProductCard.Root onClick={() => setLog('zone: open the request')} className="max-w-sm bg-layer-1 text-ink">
        <div className="p-4 pb-2">
          <ProductCard.Title className="text-base font-semibold">Approval request</ProductCard.Title>
          <ProductCard.Description className="text-xs text-ink-muted">From Malee S.</ProductCard.Description>
        </div>
        <ProductCard.Body className="relative p-4 pt-0 text-sm hover:bg-layer-hover-1">
          <ProductCard.ClickZone className="absolute inset-0 cursor-pointer focus:outline-2 focus:-outline-offset-2 focus:outline-focus" />
          Purchase of 20 laptops for the Finance department, 640,000 baht.
        </ProductCard.Body>
        <div className="border-t border-hairline">
          <button
            type="button"
            onClick={() => setLog('Approve button')}
            className="h-10 px-4 text-sm text-link hover:bg-layer-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus"
          >
            Approve
          </button>
        </div>
      </ProductCard.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Last press: {log}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## What names the zone

`ClickZone` points `aria-labelledby` at the `Title`, or at the `Label` when there is no title, or at the `Body` when there is neither. `aria-describedby` points at the `Description`. Pass your own `aria-labelledby` or `aria-describedby` on `ClickZone` to change them. The parts make their own ids; an `id` you pass is used instead.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { ProductCard } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [pressed, setPressed] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <ProductCard.Root onClick={() => setPressed(pressed + 1)} className="relative max-w-sm bg-layer-1 p-4 text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-1">
        <ProductCard.ClickZone className="absolute inset-0 cursor-pointer focus:outline-2 focus:-outline-offset-2 focus:outline-focus" />
        <ProductCard.Label className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Only a label: it names the zone</ProductCard.Label>
        <ProductCard.Body className="pt-2 text-sm">The body would name it if there were no label either.</ProductCard.Body>
      </ProductCard.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Presses: {pressed}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Disabled

`disabled` on `Root` stops `onClick` and sets `aria-disabled` on the card and the zone's button, as Carbon does. The button stays focusable, so screen readers still find it and hear that it's disabled. Nothing else changes: grey it out yourself with `data-disabled`, and say why.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { ProductCard } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ProductCard.Root disabled onClick={() => alert('never runs')} className="relative max-w-sm bg-layer-1 p-4 text-ink data-disabled:text-ink-disabled">
      <ProductCard.ClickZone className="absolute inset-0 data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed focus:outline-2 focus:-outline-offset-2 focus:outline-focus" />
      <ProductCard.Title className="text-base font-semibold">Loan contract template</ProductCard.Title>
      <ProductCard.Description className="text-xs">Being revised until 15 October</ProductCard.Description>
    </ProductCard.Root>
  );
}
```

## Style it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { ProductCard } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

export default function Example() {
  const [disabled, setDisabled] = useState(false);
  const [presses, setPresses] = useState(0);
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-4">
      <ProductCard.Root
        disabled={disabled}
        onClick={() => setPresses(presses + 1)}
        className="relative max-w-sm border border-border-tile-1 bg-layer-1 p-4 text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-1 data-disabled:text-ink-disabled data-disabled:hover:bg-layer-1"
      >
        <ProductCard.ClickZone className="absolute inset-0 cursor-pointer outline-transparent focus:outline-2 focus:-outline-offset-2 focus:outline-focus data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed" />
        <ProductCard.Label className="text-xs text-ink-muted data-disabled:text-ink-disabled">Report</ProductCard.Label>
        <ProductCard.Title className="text-base font-semibold">Monthly contract summary</ProductCard.Title>
        <ProductCard.Body className="pt-2 text-sm">48 contracts signed in September.</ProductCard.Body>
      </ProductCard.Root>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-4 text-sm text-ink">
        <label className="flex items-center gap-2">
          <input type="checkbox" checked={disabled} onChange={(e) => setDisabled(e.target.checked)} />
          disabled
        </label>
        <span className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Presses: {presses}</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```
```css
.product-card { position: relative; background: #f4f4f4; }
.product-card [data-click-zone] { position: absolute; inset: 0; cursor: pointer; }
.product-card > :is(a, button):not([data-click-zone]) { position: relative; z-index: 1; }
.product-card[data-disabled] { color: #8d8d8d; }
[data-click-zone][data-disabled] { cursor: not-allowed; }
```

## Parts

### ProductCard.Root

A `<div>`, the card. It takes every `<div>` prop except `onClick`, which here means the click zone.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `onClick` | `(event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void` | — | The click zone was pressed (a click, Enter or Space on `ClickZone`); never while `disabled` |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Sets `aria-disabled`; the zone then calls no `onClick` |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-disabled` | `disabled` is set |

### ProductCard.ClickZone

An empty `<button type="button">` with `tabIndex={0}`, to lay over the zone. It takes every button prop except `type` and `children`; your own `onClick` runs before the root's.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-click-zone` | Always (to leave it out of rules such as `[&>button]:relative`) |
| `data-disabled` | The root is disabled |

### ProductCard.Title

A heading, `<h2>` by default. It takes every heading prop. It names the click zone.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `as` | `'h1' \| 'h2' \| 'h3' \| 'h4' \| 'h5' \| 'h6'` | `'h2'` | The heading level |

### ProductCard.Label

A `<p>`, the text above the title. It names the click zone when there is no title.

### ProductCard.Description

A `<p>`, the text below the title. It describes the click zone.

### ProductCard.Body

A `<div>`, the content. It names the click zone when there is neither title nor label.

Every part except `Root` throws when it isn't inside a `ProductCard.Root`.

## Keyboard and accessibility

| Key | Does |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves to the zone's button and, separately, to each of the card's own controls |
| Enter, Space | Presses the zone's button (calls `onClick`) or the focused control |

The parts set the zone's `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby` and `aria-disabled`, and give each named part an id.

You add:

- The positioning: the zone's button over its part, the card's own controls above it.
- A visible focus style on the zone's button; it covers the zone, so an outline on it outlines the zone.
- Names for icon-only buttons.
- A disabled look, if you want one; the parts only announce it.


---

# Headless Edit in place

`EditInPlace` is the behaviour of the styled [Edit in place](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/edit-in-place/) as unstyled React parts: a value shown in a text field that is edited where it is, with Edit, Cancel and Save buttons. The parts hold the value and the value editing started from, start editing on focus or typing, save on Enter, put the value back on Escape, and save or put back when the focus leaves. Each button shows only when it applies, and a press on one keeps the focus in the field.

You own the markup and every style: the icons, the hover fill, the focus line, the error text and the read-only note. State shows as `data-*` attributes to style on.

## Installation

The headless parts come with the package (there is no shadcn item; the React + Tailwind items are built on them):

```bash
npm install @purpurabog/ui
```
```tsx
import { EditInPlace } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';
```

## Use it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { EditInPlace } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const button = 'inline-flex size-10 items-center justify-center text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:text-ink-disabled disabled:hover:bg-transparent';

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="max-w-sm">
      <EditInPlace.Root defaultValue="Warehouse lease, Bang Na">
        <EditInPlace.Group className="group flex items-center hover:bg-field-1 data-editing:bg-field-1 has-[input:focus]:outline-2 has-[input:focus]:outline-focus">
          <EditInPlace.Input aria-label="Contract title" className="h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 cursor-pointer bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink outline-none" />
          <EditInPlace.Action action="edit" aria-label="Edit" className={`${button} invisible group-hover:visible`}>✎</EditInPlace.Action>
          <EditInPlace.Action action="cancel" aria-label="Cancel" className={button}>✕</EditInPlace.Action>
          <EditInPlace.Action action="save" aria-label="Save" className={button}>✓</EditInPlace.Action>
        </EditInPlace.Group>
      </EditInPlace.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
<EditInPlace.Root>
  <EditInPlace.Group>
    <EditInPlace.Input />
    <EditInPlace.Action action="edit" />
    <EditInPlace.Action action="cancel" />
    <EditInPlace.Action action="save" />
  </EditInPlace.Group>
  <EditInPlace.InvalidText />
</EditInPlace.Root>
```

`Root` renders nothing of its own. `Group` is the box that hears the focus move between the field and its buttons; put every part that takes focus inside it.

## Save and cancel

`onSave` gets the value when a change is saved: with Save, with Enter, or when the focus leaves the group with a valid change. `onCancel` gets the value put back: with Cancel, with Escape, or when the focus leaves without a valid change. Save and Cancel are enabled only once the value has changed (spaces at the ends don't count).


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { EditInPlace } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const button = 'inline-flex size-10 items-center justify-center text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:text-ink-disabled disabled:hover:bg-transparent';

export default function Example() {
  const [last, setLast] = useState('');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
      <EditInPlace.Root
        defaultValue="PO-2026-0815"
        onSave={(value) => setLast(`saved "${value}"`)}
        onCancel={(value) => setLast(`put back "${value}"`)}
      >
        <EditInPlace.Group className="group flex items-center hover:bg-field-1 data-editing:bg-field-1 has-[input:focus]:outline-2 has-[input:focus]:outline-focus">
          <EditInPlace.Input aria-label="Purchase order number" className="h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 cursor-pointer bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink outline-none" />
          <EditInPlace.Action action="edit" aria-label="Edit" className={`${button} invisible group-hover:visible`}>✎</EditInPlace.Action>
          <EditInPlace.Action action="cancel" aria-label="Cancel" className={button}>✕</EditInPlace.Action>
          <EditInPlace.Action action="save" aria-label="Save" className={button}>✓</EditInPlace.Action>
        </EditInPlace.Group>
      </EditInPlace.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Last event: {last}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Controlled value

Hold the value with `value` and `onValueChange`. `onValueChange` gets every keystroke, and the value put back on cancel. Send the value to your server in `onSave`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { EditInPlace } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const button = 'inline-flex size-10 items-center justify-center text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:text-ink-disabled disabled:hover:bg-transparent';

export default function Example() {
  const [reference, setReference] = useState('REF-104');
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState('REF-104');
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-sm gap-2">
      <EditInPlace.Root value={reference} onValueChange={setReference} onSave={(value) => setTimeout(() => setSaved(value.trim()), 400)}>
        <EditInPlace.Group className="group flex items-center hover:bg-field-1 data-editing:bg-field-1 has-[input:focus]:outline-2 has-[input:focus]:outline-focus">
          <EditInPlace.Input aria-label="Reference" className="h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 cursor-pointer bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink outline-none" />
          <EditInPlace.Action action="edit" aria-label="Edit" className={`${button} invisible group-hover:visible`}>✎</EditInPlace.Action>
          <EditInPlace.Action action="cancel" aria-label="Cancel" className={button}>✕</EditInPlace.Action>
          <EditInPlace.Action action="save" aria-label="Save" className={button}>✓</EditInPlace.Action>
        </EditInPlace.Group>
      </EditInPlace.Root>
      <p className="text-xs text-ink-muted">Value: {reference} · Saved on the server: {saved}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Invalid, with an error text

`invalid` blocks saving: Save is disabled, Enter doesn't save, and leaving puts the value back. It sets `aria-invalid` on the field and `data-invalid` on the group and the field. Put the error text in `InvalidText`: it shows only while `invalid` and describes the field (`aria-describedby`).


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { EditInPlace } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const button = 'inline-flex size-10 items-center justify-center text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:text-ink-disabled disabled:hover:bg-transparent';

export default function Example() {
  const [taxId, setTaxId] = useState('0105556012345');
  return (
    <div className="max-w-sm">
      <EditInPlace.Root value={taxId} onValueChange={setTaxId} invalid={!/^\d{13}$/.test(taxId)}>
        <EditInPlace.Group className="group flex items-center hover:bg-field-1 data-editing:bg-field-1 has-[input:focus]:outline-2 has-[input:focus]:outline-focus data-invalid:outline-2 data-invalid:-outline-offset-2 data-invalid:outline-error">
          <EditInPlace.Input aria-label="Tax ID" className="h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 cursor-pointer bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink outline-none" />
          <EditInPlace.Action action="edit" aria-label="Edit" className={`${button} invisible group-hover:visible`}>✎</EditInPlace.Action>
          <EditInPlace.Action action="cancel" aria-label="Cancel" className={button}>✕</EditInPlace.Action>
          <EditInPlace.Action action="save" aria-label="Save" className={button}>✓</EditInPlace.Action>
        </EditInPlace.Group>
        <EditInPlace.InvalidText className="mt-2 text-xs text-error-text">A tax ID has 13 digits</EditInPlace.InvalidText>
      </EditInPlace.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Read-only

`readOnly` keeps the value: the field is `readonly`, no button shows, and a click on the field sets `noteOpen` in the context. Show your note with it, for example in a [Headless Popover](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/headless-popover/), and close it with `setNoteOpen(false)`.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { EditInPlace } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

function ReadOnlyNote() {
  const { noteOpen, setNoteOpen } = EditInPlace.useEditInPlaceContext();
  if (!noteOpen) return null;
  return (
    <div role="status" className="mt-2 flex items-start justify-between gap-4 bg-inverse-surface-1 p-4 text-sm text-inverse-ink">
      Contract numbers are set when the contract is signed.
      <button type="button" onClick={() => setNoteOpen(false)} className="underline focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-focus-inverse">Close</button>
    </div>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="max-w-sm">
      <EditInPlace.Root defaultValue="CT-2026-0142" readOnly>
        <EditInPlace.Group className="flex items-center data-readonly:cursor-not-allowed">
          <EditInPlace.Input aria-label="Contract number" className="h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink outline-none focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus" />
        </EditInPlace.Group>
        <ReadOnlyNote />
      </EditInPlace.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

The `Action`s show in their own mode only: `edit` at rest, `cancel` and `save` while editing, none when read-only. For an "Edit off" button beside a read-only field, render your own button that calls `setNoteOpen`.

## Your own buttons

`render` on an `Action` renders your component with the action's props (`type`, `disabled`, `data-disabled`, `onMouseDown`, `onClick` and your own), for example a styled icon button with a tooltip. Spread them all onto your button, so the press keeps the focus in the field.


React (live React example):

```tsx
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react';
import { EditInPlace } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

function IconButton({ label, children, className, ...props }: ComponentProps<'button'> & { label: string }) {
  return (
    <button {...props} aria-label={label} title={label} className={`inline-flex size-12 items-center justify-center text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled ${className ?? ''}`}>
      {children}
    </button>
  );
}

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <div className="max-w-sm">
      <EditInPlace.Root defaultValue="Siam Logistics">
        <EditInPlace.Group className="group flex items-center hover:bg-field-1 data-editing:bg-field-1 has-[input:focus]:outline-2 has-[input:focus]:outline-focus">
          <EditInPlace.Input aria-label="Supplier name" className="h-12 min-w-0 flex-1 cursor-pointer bg-transparent px-4 text-sm text-ink outline-none" />
          <EditInPlace.Action action="edit" render={(props) => <IconButton {...props} label="Edit supplier name">✎</IconButton>} />
          <EditInPlace.Action action="cancel" render={(props) => <IconButton {...props} label="Undo changes">✕</IconButton>} />
          <EditInPlace.Action action="save" render={(props) => <IconButton {...props} label="Save supplier name">✓</IconButton>} />
        </EditInPlace.Group>
      </EditInPlace.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Style it


React (live React example):

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { EditInPlace } from '@purpurabog/ui/headless';

const button = 'inline-flex size-10 items-center justify-center text-ink hover:bg-layer-hover-1 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:-outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus data-disabled:cursor-not-allowed data-disabled:text-ink-disabled data-disabled:hover:bg-transparent';

export default function Example() {
  const [invalid, setInvalid] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-sm gap-4">
      <EditInPlace.Root defaultValue="Malee S." invalid={invalid}>
        <EditInPlace.Group className="group flex items-center border-b border-transparent hover:bg-field-1 data-editing:border-border-strong-1 data-editing:bg-field-1 has-[input:focus]:outline-2 has-[input:focus]:outline-focus data-invalid:outline-2 data-invalid:-outline-offset-2 data-invalid:outline-error">
          <EditInPlace.Input aria-label="Owner" className="h-10 min-w-0 flex-1 cursor-pointer bg-transparent px-4 text-sm font-semibold text-ink outline-none data-editing:cursor-text data-editing:font-normal" />
          <EditInPlace.Action action="edit" aria-label="Edit" className={`${button} invisible group-hover:visible`}>✎</EditInPlace.Action>
          <EditInPlace.Action action="cancel" aria-label="Cancel" className={button}>✕</EditInPlace.Action>
          <EditInPlace.Action action="save" aria-label="Save" className={button}>✓</EditInPlace.Action>
        </EditInPlace.Group>
      </EditInPlace.Root>
      <label className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm text-ink">
        <input type="checkbox" checked={invalid} onChange={(e) => setInvalid(e.target.checked)} />
        invalid
      </label>
    </div>
  );
}
```
The same in plain CSS, with your own class names on the parts:

```css
.eip-group:hover,
.eip-group[data-editing] { background: #f4f4f4; }
.eip-group:has(input:focus) { outline: 2px solid #0f62fe; }
.eip-group[data-invalid] { outline: 2px solid #da1e28; outline-offset: -2px; }
.eip-input[data-editing] { cursor: text; }
.eip-action[data-disabled] { color: #c6c6c6; cursor: not-allowed; }
```

## Parts

### EditInPlace.Root

Holds the value, the editing state and the value editing started from. Renders only its children.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | — | The value, controlled (pair with `onValueChange`) |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | `''` | The first value, uncontrolled |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | Every keystroke, and the value put back on cancel |
| `onSave` | `(value: string) => void` | — | A change was saved (Save, Enter, leaving the group) |
| `onCancel` | `(value: string) => void` | — | The value was put back (Cancel, Escape, leaving without a valid change) |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | `false` | Blocks saving; `aria-invalid` on the field |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Shown, not edited |

### EditInPlace.Group

Renders a `<div>`. A focus coming in starts editing; a focus leaving all of it saves a valid change or puts the value back. It takes every `<div>` prop.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-editing` | While editing |
| `data-invalid` | `invalid` is set |
| `data-readonly` | `readOnly` is set |

### EditInPlace.Input

Renders an `<input type="text">` with the value. Enter saves, or stops editing when there is nothing to save (the focus stays); Escape puts the value back. A click starts editing, or opens the note when read-only. It takes every `<input>` prop except `value`, `defaultValue`, `type` and `readOnly`, which come from `Root`. Its id is yours when you give one, else `${id}input`; its `aria-describedby` is yours when you give one, else the `InvalidText` shown.

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-editing` | While editing |
| `data-invalid` | `invalid` is set |
| `data-readonly` | `readOnly` is set |

### EditInPlace.InvalidText

Renders a `<p>` with your error text while `Root` is `invalid`, and nothing otherwise; while it shows, it describes the field. Its id is yours when you give one, else `${id}error`. It takes every `<p>` prop.

### EditInPlace.Action

Renders a `<button type="button">`, only in its mode. Its mousedown is cancelled, so a press keeps the focus in the field. It takes every `<button>` prop except `type`.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | `'edit' \| 'cancel' \| 'save'` | — | `edit` at rest: focuses the field. `cancel` while editing, once the value changed: puts it back. `save` while editing, once it changed and is valid: saves |
| `render` | `(props) => ReactElement` | — | Renders your own button with these props |

| Attribute | When |
|---|---|
| `data-disabled` | `disabled` is set, or the action can't run yet (`cancel` without a change, `save` without a valid change) |

### EditInPlace.useEditInPlaceContext()

Reads the state of the enclosing `Root` from any component inside it: `id` (the field is `${id}input` and the error text `${id}error` unless you give them ids), `value`, `editing`, `mode` (`'rest'`, `'editing'` or `'readonly'`), `canSave`, `canCancel`, `invalid`, `readOnly`, `noteOpen` and `setNoteOpen`, and the actions `begin`, `save`, `cancel` and `refocus`. Outside a `Root` it throws.

## Keyboard and accessibility

- Tab into the field starts editing. Tab then reaches Cancel and Save once they are enabled; leaving the group saves a valid change or puts the value back.
- Enter saves a valid change and keeps editing; with nothing to save it stops editing, the focus staying in the field. Escape puts the value back and keeps editing.
- After Save, Cancel or Escape, the focus goes back to the field with the caret at the end.
- The field sets `aria-invalid` when `invalid`. `InvalidText` describes it while it shows. You add its name (`aria-label`, or a `<label>` for its id) and names for the buttons, whose content is often only an icon.
- A read-only field is `readonly`: it still takes focus and is read. Your note should say why it can't be edited.

The styled [Edit in place](https://parntengza.github.io/kanok-ui-docs/en/edit-in-place/) is built on these parts.
